belview/62df06329425d658.text: Wood for the wards. Wood for the wards. The cold ones in the cells are always cold. We bring them wood and they eat it.

belview/6e5ae382f4f74c76.text: Wine. Clovin says. Wine and no more gifts. And the loud ones in the cells fed. The Abbot forgets them. He forgets things in rooms. He locks the rooms so he can forget them better.

belview/7c18b3933d597eff.text: Belview. We're all Belview. Mother is Belview, Clovin is Belview, the ones in the cells are Belview, only louder.

belview/8201ba8ab455b433.text: Clean for the Abbot. Clean for the Abbot. The bride must not get her feet wet. That's what he says. That's what he says.

belview/85220df58a9fcaa3.text: Ourselves. Ourselves. That's a lot of selves. We'll practise.

belview/a9ff45bd9e599022.text: Nobody's improving us now. Nobody. We're stopping where we are. Clovin says that's all right. Is it all right?

belview/b3c09f611886fffe.text: Hello. Hello. Who are you? Who are you? That's what you were going to say. I heard you think it.

belview/f123301bef88b6bc.text: Visitors! Visitors! Mother, visitors! Mother doesn't come out. Mother has had nine gifts.

belview/f4d3c28e6c99f340.text: This one is yours. You're a good one. The grey ones are for the bad ones. I have a lot of grey ones.

belview_mother/252383360a5d1e81.text: Not while he's improving. Come back when he's done improving. Go on. He listens at the walls.

belview_mother/45d115d457ecada6.text: I'm ready now. Only I don't want heaven. I want Krezk. I was born there, two doors down from the burgomaster's. I want to see the door.

belview_mother/5e469f8b7c044c58.text: My boys in the cells. They're dead. I heard it. (She is quiet for a long time.) They were never going to get better. I'll still go. There's nothing to stay for now but the fire.

belview_mother/622b9a76091ef195.text: He said they'd work if I believed. I've never believed anything he said.

belview_mother/869e93ab691ef312.text: My boys in the cells. Somebody let them out, gently, and they ran up the mountain. Was it you? Thank you. They'll come back for the winter, or they won't. That's what boys do.

belview_mother/956b9885d0137af7.text: Nine gifts. The eyes, to see in the dark. The legs, to wade. The wings, to go up to heaven when I'm ready, he said. He'd finish them when I was ready. He sewed them shut so I wouldn't go early.

belview_mother/bc21cf6defbe58ad.text: My boys first. The loud ones, in the cells along the corridor. He forgets them. I don't. I won't go and leave them behind bars. Let them out, and gently. They bite when they're frightened, and they're always frightened.

belview_mother/cb2c2e5e0dd6c6f7.text: Never mind. Never mind. They're mine now. They can hurt if they like.

belview_mother/d314c03feee173fb.text: And my uncle Pavel's asked me to Sunday soup. I've never had an uncle. I've never had soup I didn't have to fight for.

bildrath/00bad157f0730049.text: Grigore sold me a load of firewood at a price I could not refuse, being very nearly nothing. Beautiful wood. White. It's in the back.

bildrath/0dcdcbc9cce484e0.text: For you, the special price. Nine times. I'll never recover.

bildrath/1802f0c2ec2f0176.text: Ismark says it's grief. I've sold rope to grieving men. They don't howl at walls.

bildrath/227ac5ce221c28ef.text: Ah. Yes. The firewood. I would consider it a kindness if the village went on believing that this shop sells rope and candles and nothing that walks.

bildrath/23da5158d4f18907.text: For you, the rude price. The dear things carry ten percent for the tone of voice. Menace is itemized.

bildrath/2409863728cde356.text: I did not stand it on its end.

bildrath/2e80e2e2754bb47f.text: Back again. The prices haven't changed. They never change. That's what makes them prices.

bildrath/2e9b63a01859ea99.text: It creaks at night. Wood creaks; I've told Parriwimple so. Parriwimple tells me it doesn't usually creak toward the door.

bildrath/5226bfbeae109635.text: Haggling is a form of theft that takes longer.

bildrath/54b6e784ac27b4c5.text: Father Donavich stopped buying candles. A priest who prays in the dark is either very holy or very ashamed. I don't extend credit to either.

bildrath/57496290386039d0.text: No. The prices are posted. They will stay posted. You may look at them as long as you like; looking is free, for now.

bildrath/576560a64cadb261.text: Lower them? No. I'll raise them. Ten percent on the dear things, for menacing the proprietor. Parriwimple, the ledger. Under "Customers, Rude".

bildrath/5922a29baf2ac592.text: Everything is on the shelf, and every price is on its tag. The tags are correct. I wrote them.

bildrath/614a653d21498f55.text: The burgomaster's dog. Big grey wolfhound, Lupu. He sits under the mansion's study window every night and howls at the wall. Not at the wolves. At the wall.

bildrath/711507c3f678ec4b.text: And ten percent off, from now on. For discretion. Do not tell Parriwimple why.

bildrath/71f69fb69ef5baba.text: Thirty gold. I'll note that you returned it. I'll also note that you took it. My ledger has two columns for a reason.

bildrath/81cbd2affeb2f69f.text: I pay a tenth of what a thing is worth. That is not greed; that is arithmetic. Everyone in this valley already owns a sword, and none of them helped.

bildrath/8228c08befc18bed.text: Out. Thieves aren't customers. They're weather.

bildrath/96ea6e3539afe493.text: Parriwimple's time is five gold an hour. A coffin takes an hour. A grave takes two. Fifteen gold, and he brings his own shovel, which is also mine.

bildrath/9e33d4f29978a9be.text: My strongbox is thirty gold lighter than it ought to be, and you are the only new faces in the valley. Parriwimple! Stand by the door.

bildrath/adcab676bc090bb6.text: Hm. Perhaps. Perhaps it was the wolves. I shall be counting the spoons when you leave.

bildrath/ae4426e24755c6b5.text: A monk left these as surety six years ago, against a debt of four silver, and never came back for them. They have been on my books for six years. I am writing them off. Into your hands. Today only.

bildrath/b3f35b9f1ae7c667.text: You have coin in your purse that has my thumbprint on it. Out. Come back with thirty gold and an apology, in that order, or don't come back.

bildrath/c3031882ae10585e.text: No. Out. You know the price of coming back in.

bildrath/c95a7d1acf3ada63.text: Ismark Kolyanovich owes this shop eleven gold and four silver. I mention it only because you appear to be his friends.

bildrath/cc667a382e2b3127.text: He offered. For free. Parriwimple, we will be having a talk about the concept of value. Go, then. Go! Bring the shovel back clean.

bildrath/ccc6ed1bc3422dfb.text: Take it. Take all of it. Parriwimple! Carry it to Grigore's for these people, and then wash your hands. Twice.

bildrath/cfd82cd10db950c6.text: Parriwimple, sit down. Sit. They're... customers. Valued customers. Buy something, and then leave.

bildrath/d03b71f86ce58233.text: Welcome to Bildrath's Mercantile. Prices are posted. They are ten times what you're used to. You are used to the wrong place.

bildrath/d0f206ecba2867b7.text: Blight. In my storeroom. I'll have to write it off. Do you know what writing it off does to a ledger? It weeps.

bildrath/d31a1e3081a96260.text: Parriwimple! The customers have purchased three hours of you. Take the good shovel. Bring it back clean.

bildrath/d50e85db289b00d4.text: She bakes at the old windmill on the Vallaki road, up on the crag. Nobody I'd lend money to has gone up there to check.

bildrath/e4b3308982ef4fe9.text: Ten percent. Ten! You have robbed me in broad daylight, and I let you. Parriwimple, write it down. No. Don't. I don't want a record of this.

bildrath/e8ae16a1bde86483.text: That is not a feature of firewood. I would know. I sell firewood.

bildrath/eff40f523d7749f7.text: Mary bought three locks from me this year. Good locks. Her daughter went out of the window. You can't sell a lock for a window. Believe me, I've tried.

bildrath/f0577d4a35c22c76.text: Morgantha. Comes through every few weeks with that cart. I don't sell pastries; I have standards. Folk who can't pay her settle up some other way. I don't ask how. I don't give credit, and I suspect neither does she.

bildrath/f4ff00f8501546aa.text: Thirty gold, and an apology. The gold, I accept. The apology I'll take under advisement. Browse. Touch nothing you haven't paid for.

bildrath/fa3a37cfa25935d3.text: News costs nothing, which is what it's worth. Ask.

blinsky/0180daaf254fc879.text: You came back. Nobody comes back. Piccolo, put the kettle on. No, the other kettle. The one without the frog in it.

blinsky/0405d499f627b057.text: And for you. I have been making this for twenty years and never finished it, because I could not get the knees right. Now I have seen his knees.

blinsky/04eac43cfcb3fff6.text: Thank you. It will not help, but thank you.

blinsky/0736a4d60c3dd4cd.text: Customers. Real ones. Welcome to Blinsky Toys, where every toy is a small sadness, beautifully made. Do not sit on the horse. The horse bites.

blinsky/08450272e3282ca8.text: Blinsky. The first. The only, sadly. Would you like some tea? I have two kettles. One of them has a frog in it.

blinsky/1af07a3996ddef9e.text: After. Yes. Everything good in this valley is after. I will keep the kettle on. The one without the frog.

blinsky/265750ab22fabf30.text: Never. I would want to shake its hand. Then, perhaps, if it permitted, to look at the knees.

blinsky/2bb8464193543ae8.text: The Baron, for his festivals: puppets of the Baron, mostly. The children, sometimes; they cry and are carried out. And one man, who only buys dolls.

blinsky/303649dd75c00d3f.text: That was nearly funny. Here. A whistle. For when the toys come for you. I joke. Mostly.

blinsky/55fe008c6d2df0e9.text: That was very brave. It was not funny, but it was brave. Most things here are one or the other.

blinsky/5a2d542e8253d4ec.text: Oh. Oh. Von Weerg's jester. You are real. You are real, and you are so much smaller than I imagined, and so much better.

blinsky/5ffce797d77873c1.text: Eleven dolls. One lady, red hair, always the same face. He tells me her face from his dreams, every line of it. He has dreamed it since he was a boy, he says, since the night the wolves took his arm in the woods.

blinsky/6d8e339e21721b3b.text: Say the word to it, and it is a horse. A real one, a black one, very fast. Do not ask me how. I am not sure I know.

blinsky/7bf0b7f43b8a16c1.text: Can he stay? He is asking me if he can stay. Piccolo. Piccolo, he is asking.

blinsky/87d377bd512b9cc8.text: Izek. Izek Strazni. He describes you from his dreams, and I carve, and he pays. Once I asked who you were. He held me against that wall with the arm. So I carve and I do not ask.

blinsky/8833eaef59ebe7e8.text: I would give everything in this shop to see it. Once. To see how he did the knees. Nobody knows how he did the knees.

blinsky/8b49c708f1aa6a11.text: Goodbye. Come back. Or don't. The toys will be here either way. They are very patient.

blinsky/99ecb5d09d11f529.text: Everything is for sale. Dice for gamblers. Whistles for lost children. Marbles, very good for slipping on. A little drum, for marching to your doom in time.

blinsky/9f8a3410e1cf75c3.text: He keeps them in a chest at the foot of his bed in the Baron's house. He talks to them, the maids say. I do not want to know what he says.

blinsky/a7c857b8a49783f6.text: I will build a ramp. Piccolo, we are getting rid of the stairs.

blinsky/c29ef91d77eda8a9.text: So. He was jealous, and he was lonely, and he was made too well. I know about all three of those.

blinsky/daa88a3a89f91620.text: A toy that walks? Ha. No. Nobody makes a toy that walks. Except once. Once, somebody did.

blinsky/f1e21a5b5993d19f.text: Piccolo is a critic. He has never once paid to see anything, and he charges for everything. Like all critics.

blinsky/f34bce823225ac59.text: He has written me an order on his slate: one hour of happiness a day, by decree. He signed it. I am obeying it. The Baron would be so proud.

blinsky/fd8959f420614004.text: I should not have said that. Forget I said that. There is no man who buys dolls. Buy a whistle.

blinsky/fe1ca92665a8d758.text: The doll lady. You are the doll lady. I have carved your face eleven times. Green dress, grey cloak, once smiling, he was very particular about the smiling.

blinsky/fe886d63c21bbde3.text: My master's master, Fritz von Weerg. He made a jester for the count's children, up the hill, long ago. It walked. It juggled. It bowed. They say it is still up there, in the castle, walking the stairs.

bluto/2ed683ab78d49569.text: No. No, no, I paid. I paid you. I paid you every month!

bluto/300270198393fcb2.text: The boat's yours whenever you want it. I'll row, if you'll have me. The north shore is where the wolves come down to drink; there's a trail up from there into the hills, to their den.

bluto/3809d2fb9f14a404.text: No! She told me! She told me in the dark!

bluto/3a0bd5d4bc18dc2f.text: You. You're the ones who took her back. The lake was so angry after. A whole year of empty nets, and then you took her supper away. So she told me in the dark that it's my turn instead.

bluto/3f375a5d22c724f9.text: And west, up the stream, there's a little cold lake under the mountain with a tower in it. A lamp burns there some nights. A Vistani woman has her wagon by it, and she shoots at anything that moves.

bluto/5769347b3ac11cbd.text: Every day. Yes. Every day. Take the boat, I can't look at it. Take it and go.

bluto/5f8e76527cd68060.text: The north shore's a long pull. I'll want my coat lighter for it.

bluto/625b75eb8f7cab59.text: Don't look at me, little one. Please don't look at me.

bluto/7156e7fc4580124c.text: Stay back! Stay back! The lake's hungry. A whole year without a fish. She wants something better than worms, she does, and then the nets'll fill!

bluto/792cb03a43025ced.text: No. No more talking. She's been talking for a year and I'm tired.

bluto/9175eae72ffc14ff.text: I haven't eaten in four days. Maybe that's what she was. Maybe she was only hunger, talking in my own voice.

bluto/a32c442a929e10a5.text: Fed, dry and nobody's dinner. That's a better week than I've had in a year. The boat's ready when you are.

bluto/b8e09acb9301d93c.text: You can't scare me worse than she does!

bluto/dff2cce20b23ec72.text: Take the boat. Go on. Take it.

bluto/f617c6713434162b.text: She paid. You see? She paid. A whole year of nothing, and the morning after, this. The lake keeps her bargains.

bogdan/001c190a6b54d714.text: Lady Ireena? Out here? My condolences, lady. Your father dug our well with his own hands, once. Wouldn't take a copper for it.

bogdan/04da647ad273dad2.text: That's... thank you. That's a priest's fee and a candle besides. Mother would have made you take soup for it.

bogdan/0eb1cfe38eb426e2.text: The church. Before dark. Come on, Petru, pull, pull!

bogdan/1356319634aa1827.text: She said a gentleman came to the window. Said he was lonely. She was always kind to the lonely. Oh, Mother.

bogdan/28e415a6c50ea440.text: Morning. Or what passes for it. My mother, in the box. We're taking her to the church in the village. I won't put her in the ground unblessed, not with things the way they are.

bogdan/7d06f4516d396f78.text: They say the priest won't open his doors any more. We'll knock anyway. What else is there?

bogdan/98b87601a7a74b39.text: Thank you. I won't say it again, so hear it now. Thank you.

bogdan/b859d0e5e174c601.text: Heard the burgomaster went into the ground proper, at last. Good. Then somebody still remembers how.

bogdan/f97cbffd475f24be.text: And to you. Keep off the road after dark. Everybody knows that, but people forget.

bonegrinder_mouse/1aacb402fab44fe3.text: A lady comes up from the village every morning and buys one. I always give her the best in the basket. I don't know why I do that.

bonegrinder_mouse/22a097c2e51af3e0.text: Mouse. I'm Mother's fourth. Mother Morgantha. You can't be a sister till you're thirteen, so I live in the hut down by the millrace, out from under feet.

bonegrinder_mouse/38c7ec43d4a8d3c1.text: Granny's Mother's mother. She's very old and very big, and her teeth are iron. Mine are coming in. Look.

bonegrinder_mouse/394f4c79feeeb4f9.text: Bella says I'm her problem now. Bella doesn't like problems. She says I can sell plain ones till Granny comes.

bonegrinder_mouse/3da5419e533f6192.text: Pastries! Still plain. Still a copper.

bonegrinder_mouse/4557e2be9ea46dd8.text: Mother's gone. Somebody killed her. (She looks at you, and you can't tell how much she knows.) Granny says that's how it goes with hags. Somebody always does, in the end.

bonegrinder_mouse/515ff083f9fcf6c6.text: Interesting? Granny's coming! For my birthday. I'm thirteen the next dark night, and Granny comes out of the deep wood to make me a sister, and then I'll never be hungry again.

bonegrinder_mouse/714e9581a3c94551.text: (She takes a step toward the trees, and looks back at you.) It only hurts a bit, Granny says. Then I'll never be hungry again.

bonegrinder_mouse/84a43b3b88823626.text: I make the pastries for Bildrath's now. Plain ones. People buy them. Nobody's dreamed anything yet.

bonegrinder_mouse/9740a85f5cb81016.text: It's very long. Mouse is shorter. (She pulls the sleeve back down.) It tastes like soup, though. The good kind.

bonegrinder_mouse/9815dac1ef3120bf.text: Zamfira. I've been practising. Can I go and see her now? The lady who buys the plain ones?

bonegrinder_mouse/9a02594f7ca52121.text: Pastries! Plain ones. A copper. Mother said I mustn't put the dreams in till I'm a sister.

bonegrinder_mouse/a30608bcd4783cdd.text: You came! Granny's coming. I can smell her. She smells like the inside of a kettle.

bonegrinder_mouse/b2ee9049af4fea00.text: Granny comes the next dark night. So I sort of do.

bonegrinder_mouse/c275cfa95cfe4fae.text: (She steps behind you.) My name's Zamfira. My mother kissed my wrist. I'm not a mouse.

bonegrinder_mouse/f47b06a3914585fc.text: I chose. Didn't I? I chose you.

bray_martikov/25275dadac2e1916.text: Brom says I was brave. Mama says I was an idiot. Papa says both, and that it's a family tradition.

bray_martikov/987ba974cc7c3573.text: I only wanted to see it. Brom said I wouldn't. I did. It's very big.

brother_anatol/2a1c8e2cad5a2293.text: Weeks. I count the days by the cook's visits. He brings bread. I pray over it and give it back.

brother_anatol/2c88c4f3a172b4cc.text: Pity. The Master so enjoys it when the rescuers walk me to his table themselves.

brother_anatol/644c4698dda56eed.text: I fast. It is a discipline.

brother_anatol/800b701d0d57055f.text: Brother Anatol, of St. Andral's in Vallaki. I came to pray for the lord of this house. He did not care for it.

brother_anatol/8029f7b898d20ffe.text: Lucian. Yes. Of course. Lucian and I... It was a long time ago.

brother_anatol/92d941f217dde445.text: Back with that stake? Or did you only come to look at me?

brother_anatol/99d4dc4962771332.text: Friends. Bless the dawn, you came back.

brother_anatol/a8657e464fcab82b.text: Bless the dawn. Visitors, and not the cook. The Morninglord heard me after all.

brother_anatol/c8f33232d4e6bea9.text: Bless you. Truly. Now hold still.

camp_cook/310b389ee0656dad.text: No horn in the woods. Three cold nights now, and nothing. Gavril's taken to sleeping outside the wagon just to hear the quiet.

camp_cook/68dcfb423592125e.text: The count gives his huntsman a scent, and the huntsman runs it down. He has to blow three nights first, so the quarry can say its prayers. He's particular. They say the count likes rules he thinks can't be kept.

camp_cook/856bae785cd4996c.text: The hunt ends under the crossroads gallows at moonrise. The rule is, if the quarry is standing there and turns and faces him, he has to fight it out, fair. If the quarry wins, it's done. Nobody has ever stood.

camp_cook/a8da5d5067bcf5dc.text: And the hounds. Every one of them was quarry once. Their names are on the stones by the crossroads, the ones we put up. A dog knows its name. Even that kind.

camp_cook/b271a160d9140946.text: Interesting? There's a horn in the Svalich woods on cold nights. Three notes, and then the hounds. In the morning somebody's lying under the gallows at the crossroads, run to death. Boots worn through. Not a mark on them.

camp_cook/d0b450d923640a31.text: It blew three times last night, on the road you came in by. (She looks at you over the pot for a long moment.) Three notes is for strangers. You've made somebody up at the castle very angry.

camp_cook/ec6309c63896ee55.text: And it blew for Gavril, our groom. He sold the castle's stable master a horse with a painted blaze, the fool. He hasn't slept for two nights.

camp_cook/f549bc6299571a24.text: You know what I know. The crossroads, moonrise, and stand when you get there. And learn their names first, the ones under the stones.

camp_cook/f9f779412d12e717.text: Sit if you want to eat, stand if you want to be looked at. Luvash's wine is for Luvash, and for me when he isn't looking.

camp_fisher/68c99771b2d4663c.text: Don't wade in past your knees. The bottom drops away, and nothing that goes down there comes back up the same.

camp_fisher/ef9b2336e0db18da.text: Nets tear. You mend them. The lake's the same. It takes a little and you mend what's left.

camp_groom/1cfd2dbddc144d32.text: This one bites, that one kicks, and the black one is Arrigal's, so don't touch it at all. The others are good horses. They know the way out of the valley. They just can't take it.

camp_groom/b3d679034f317d33.text: If I run, I die tired. Paraschiva says stand. So I'm standing. Next to you, if it's all the same.

camp_groom/e252f61e78c76165.text: I stood. I actually stood. (He sits down in the road very suddenly.) Don't tell Paraschiva I'm sitting.

camp_groom/e9d7201a34a1ef49.text: You came. You actually came. I've got a knife and a horseshoe, and I'm not sure what either of them is for.

camp_lookout/d6565abd9726a895.text: Keep to the fire, stranger. I watch the road so you don't have to. And so I see who comes down it.

clovin_belview/0bc6d48454990d53.text: A hood, then. Monks go down sometimes, to the shrine. Nobody looks under a monk's hood. They're afraid of what's under there, and they're right.

clovin_belview/180f71f838d74a6c.text: Great-uncle Pavel comes up on Sundays with soup. Mother came out to meet him. She hasn't come out in eleven years. They sat on the step and didn't say much, and he held the hand with the claws on it.

clovin_belview/1e969f09f8611c9b.text: Well. Well, now. Clovin Belview, of the Abbey of St. Markovia, up over Krezk. If you're ever that way, I'll pour you something. If there's ever anything to pour.

clovin_belview/1f574cba44ff7bcb.text: Krezk! Lovely town. Big wall. I've seen a great deal of the outside of it.

clovin_belview/1f60daef828efe21.text: I've changed my mind. I'd like to go home. Which way's home? Up? It's always up.

clovin_belview/2b3631f392cdc037.text: Good evening. I've come down from the abbey. Yes. That one. I won't keep you. I know you've all got gates to get behind.

clovin_belview/2fd819bc408a8355.text: Good evening. I'm Clovin. I'm a Belview. I know. You can tell by the ear. If you can't tell by the ear, I'll show you the hand.

clovin_belview/30d45580d951e101.text: This? Found it under a loose board in the saint's old room, when I was a lad. Pretty writing. Nobody's ever read it to me. The Abbot says it's nothing. He said it very quickly.

clovin_belview/34d21c9fba730902.text: Great-uncle Pavel's asked her to Sunday soup. He can't stay up here for ever, and she can't walk down. She sits by the kitchen fire and looks at the door.

clovin_belview/4884c1ea727a848c.text: Leave it. I'll carry it. I carry everything else.

clovin_belview/48f401bae359c582.text: Chapel. North door, the big one. He's in the chapel or he's over in the wards, with her. He doesn't sleep. I've checked. I've checked a lot.

clovin_belview/48f77744cd3d90d1.text: Keep it. No. Read it to him. Read it to him when he's happy. I want to see his face.

clovin_belview/4ae5d321e8dc7c52.text: There's money in the hat. Not a lot. More than the Abbot ever paid. Take it. You got me through the gate.

clovin_belview/4db6bbd001e48e3c.text: You again. Gate's open. Everything's open. The Abbot doesn't believe in locks, except on the wards. He believes in those a great deal.

clovin_belview/4e5faa7f2751b229.text: She said to give you these. Her eighth gift. Before the wings he tried boots. She floated about on the ceiling for a year, and we used her to fetch things off the top shelf. She said you'd know what to do with them. She said you'd been very kind about the wire.

clovin_belview/51e891ba54ed660a.text: He walked up the mountain at dawn and didn't stop at the top. We all watched. Mother came out to watch. Nobody's going to improve us any more. I keep waiting to be sad.

clovin_belview/5b483eb02625e2c4.text: I've still got the letter. I've learned three of the words. "Light", "candle" and "go". They're good words.

clovin_belview/6158a178a5cb0665.text: Visitors. He said there'd be visitors today. He's always right. It's exhausting. Clovin Belview. I open the gate and I carry things.

clovin_belview/6b369b7125c5b08f.text: She went to kill him. The saint. She didn't go to make friends with him. He told us she went to make friends.

clovin_belview/6c5e062754e1ec05.text: (From somewhere in the hood, very quietly.) If this goes badly, I was never here. I'm a rumour. Nobody throws a bucket at a rumour.

clovin_belview/75d6d30cffa5755f.text: I drove her down to the castle. Vasilka. She sat up straight the whole way and asked me what the weather was like at weddings. I said lovely. I'm a liar now. I'm a lot of things.

clovin_belview/76a89fd5977a8189.text: I'm writing new material. It's all about soup now. The cells think it's hilarious. The cells think everything's hilarious.

clovin_belview/773e7c937d224d89.text: There's money in the hat. Real money. Krezk paid to laugh. Nobody up there's going to believe me. Take it. You got me through the gate.

clovin_belview/77ad4dcb526f4cdb.text: He's gone. He's gone. Mother, he's gone.

clovin_belview/77ebb366ae779a9c.text: A dress? Up here? The nuns left in a hurry; they left everything. The matron's room, in the wards, past the cots. It's locked. He locked it. He locks the things he doesn't want to think about.

clovin_belview/7e30703ba181e347.text: I will, sir. I'll go back up. Only I've got one joke left, and it's yours. It's a Krezk joke. Let me give it back and I'll go.

clovin_belview/7f1bc4a01bcec43c.text: The bucket. Yes. That was me. It was a very good bucket. Krezk has excellent buckets. I said so at the time.

clovin_belview/82ff0234057edd10.text: No. But he says it with such a kind face.

clovin_belview/8731475a223d44c6.text: Forty years I've written jokes on the backs of his letters. I want to tell them once to people who could choose not to laugh. Real people. Krezk.

clovin_belview/89736f91e28848e4.text: The door sticks. Low down, by the hinge. A good kick and it'd remember it's a door. I didn't tell you that.

clovin_belview/8a04a382497bab06.text: She's very beautiful. That's the worst part. He's very good at it. She'll be the most beautiful thing that ever went down that road, and he'll send her to the castle like a ham.

clovin_belview/90312b77f7f32652.text: The Abbot will be disappointed. He doesn't shout when he's disappointed. He just gets very kind. You don't want him kind.

clovin_belview/9354c21a27e41118.text: Would you? The burgomaster's the one who says yes. He's never said yes to anything. I've watched.

clovin_belview/939f3fdf6903e73c.text: Don't. Don't say it. I know what I look like. I look like a man who walked two days to a winery and found nobody to sell him wine. That's what I look like.

clovin_belview/a8ebca793fbb8242.text: Vasilka. That's her name; he picked it. I carried half of her up the mountain myself, in a sack, at night, from the graves by the pool. Don't ask which half.

clovin_belview/b86b499f834f9a1e.text: A great-uncle. I've got a great-uncle. Mother will want to meet you. She doesn't come out much. She's had nine improvements.

clovin_belview/b9d2b2764186ef8d.text: No? No. Well. That's the burgomaster. He's very consistent. It's his best quality.

clovin_belview/bc12232840d1eb40.text: We were Krezk folk once. Grandmother says. Then we all got sick and came up here and got better. Then he made us better again. And again. He calls it improving.

clovin_belview/bcc3c88978b5e4c3.text: Maybe keep your hood up, miss. In the chapel. He likes red. He likes it too much.

clovin_belview/c839ffaf37cee36d.text: I've had three improvements. You can see two of them. Don't ask about the third. Mother's had nine. She doesn't come out much.

clovin_belview/c9c8c270ab155600.text: And they're both still standing there.

clovin_belview/cab451551e305eeb.text: So the Abbot says to me, Clovin, every creature can be improved. And I say, Father, what about the wine? And he says: especially the wine.

clovin_belview/cb825d340665a1db.text: Then it's a very short show, and you carry me home.

clovin_belview/d4341cc40cc02549.text: Interesting? Mother's talking about Krezk again. She doesn't talk about Krezk while he's improving. She thinks he listens at the walls. He does.

clovin_belview/dc8f67107b3130a9.text: Mother comes down to Krezk on Sundays now. Lands on Great-uncle Pavel's roof. He's had it mended twice and he says he's never been happier. The roof says otherwise.

clovin_belview/dce965d1827331b7.text: Interesting? Mother's been talking about Krezk. She was born there, before she was carried up here in a basket. She says she'll go down if somebody can tell her how, and nobody can, because of the legs. And the other thing.

clovin_belview/e5385cd8e8191da1.text: My grandmother taught me this one. Floarea. She said it was a Krezk joke. She said it was the only thing she brought up the mountain, apart from the cough.

clovin_belview/e7df1386885592f1.text: Trouble, they said. Didn't open the gate, didn't sell me a drop. Somebody shouted from a window to go home, there was trouble, and to tell everyone. So. I'm telling everyone. You're everyone.

clovin_belview/e91f9cd722ba4597.text: A Krezker dies and goes up to the gate of the morning. The saint on the gate says, "Who's there?" And the Krezker says, "Who's asking?"

clovin_belview/e9f3c89cfdccb524.text: Can I tell you something? I'm funny. I think I'm funny. Mother laughs at everything, but that's the improvements. The loud ones in the cells laugh at nothing. The Abbot says I'm not funny. He says it kindly.

clovin_belview/eb5c2a167a4e37ac.text: My grandmother. Floarea Belview, two doors down from the burgomaster's. She went up the mountain with the cough when she was a girl.

clovin_belview/f279f463e2ca0b33.text: You! The people from the road. With the wheel. Well. Well, now. Come in out of the wind; it gets up here before anyone else does.

clovin_belview/f714489ff17b29b8.text: Krezk won't open its gate for a Belview. We were Krezk folk once, Grandmother said. She taught me a Krezk joke. I've never told it to anyone from Krezk.

clovin_belview/fa22b8e2f634799f.text: You killed him. In his own chapel. I swept up after. There wasn't much; it went to light. Mother says we'll go down to Krezk. Krezk won't have us. We'll go anyway.

clovin_belview/fc28a315c1b1a159.text: I've had three improvements. You can see two of them. The third, I'll be honest, I'm not sure about either. Some mornings I wake up and I bark. Mother says that isn't an improvement. That's just me.

clovin_belview/fd677d41fd2748a5.text: The last of the Martikovs'. Go on. Nobody drinks with me. Mother says it's because of the ear. I say it's because of the wine.

clovin_belview/fff95a61019d8b45.text: He sits. In the chapel. He doesn't talk. I bring him water and he doesn't drink it, and I take it away and bring more. Somebody has to carry things.

corvina/69065b4fe65d0aea.text: (Very slowly, as if she's reading it off a page.) Corvina. That's mine. I'd put it down somewhere. (She looks at you properly.) He sent you. He remembered.

corvina/940dc4a62c69147f.text: Tell him it's all right. Tell him I'd do it again. And then stand back, because I can't stop. I hold the master's doors. The new master's. I've held them so long I'm made of it.

corvina/f303b317219fa3eb.text: Corvina. Put it on the box. Everybody has a name on their box.

corvina/f822dcad285c2314.text: You're in the wrong part of the house. This door is held. They're all held. That's what I'm for.

count_fowler/44f415f37d529fab.text: (Pleasantly, from the branches.) Ah. We wondered who the birds would bring us. The master will be so pleased to know your faces.

count_huntsman/21b1c97b688c8fa1.text: Toader. I took a deer out of his woods, his first winter, when the valley was still new to him. He ran me down himself, for the sport of it, and I got as far as here, and I turned round.

count_huntsman/d583ed79e6ecb2d6.text: Quarry. You stood. Nobody stands. (He looks at you, and there's something in it you weren't expecting. It looks like relief.) Well. Rules are rules. He made them.

count_huntsman/ea5fabd1a4819b9d.text: Run if you like. It's better sport. (He doesn't wait to see if you will.)

count_huntsman/ecdacec6523125f4.text: He laughed. He said, you run well. Now you'll run them. And every one I've run since is in the pack. That one was a tinker. That one, a girl who said no to him at a dance.

cult_shades/51cd446083782875.text: One must die. We will wait. We are very good at waiting.

cult_shades/51fbfadf617e373b.text: You came for the child. The child was ours first. One must die.

cult_shades/538ab7ce5cde72b5.text: Then the house will have all of you.

cult_shades/5efb6b933756761b.text: One has died. The house is satisfied.

cult_shades/7271814bb60cc0f0.text: We fed the house. The house fed the one below. The one below waits for the lord to remember us. One must die.

cult_shades/b273cbaa8f8f6815.text: One must die. One must die. One must die.

cult_shades/c4bf044b927bb0db.text: A spirit does not die. It only goes home. One must die.

cyrus_belview/001239b15aa72155.text: At first light Cyrus takes the scraps down the cliff path for the crows, in the big barrel. A girl fits in a barrel. Cyrus has checked.

cyrus_belview/032bf3aed0b261bd.text: Not the pot! Cyrus will help. Cyrus always helps. Please put that down.

cyrus_belview/048c69279683e087.text: Out? Guests don't go out. Guests go down. To the table.

cyrus_belview/05e72bdc94d10eb6.text: Someone has been in Cyrus's box. The buttons were counted. Cyrus counts them every night.

cyrus_belview/0649bf2d4e99bcd1.text: Wine, mostly. And the wine man. He sold the Master vinegar in good bottles.

cyrus_belview/09bacd4cf5ab3ad9.text: The Master is very old, and very tired, and very particular about gravy.

cyrus_belview/10127921337b92c8.text: The girl with the lamp-soot hands. She cries. Cyrus gives her extra bread, so she won't be ripe for the table yet.

cyrus_belview/129ca01de3c67cb1.text: Everything is for the table, in the end. That's what a kitchen is.

cyrus_belview/12c863d285dd4644.text: Cyrus Belview, cook to the Master. Thirty years at this fire. Or three hundred. The fire never says.

cyrus_belview/1324234cae2f24ee.text: You've met him? Then you know. He looks at you as if you were already on a plate. It's a compliment.

cyrus_belview/1aeeea7eb804e897.text: He's never once thanked Cyrus for a meal. But he's never once sent one back.

cyrus_belview/2a5209d2fb18a3e5.text: Bring her to the kitchen with her chain off. She goes down with the scraps. At the bottom, the road. After that, legs.

cyrus_belview/2e2f2cdbfe5935ef.text: A bride came up the mountain? Father's bride? Then Father is happy, and Cyrus will bake a cake. A tall one.

cyrus_belview/37b1a5f92ad66e01.text: Soup, for the guests downstairs. The guests in the cells. They must be kept fresh for the Master's table.

cyrus_belview/426b214bb81b8ab0.text: Then Father sent Cyrus here, a present for the Master's wedding. There wasn't a wedding in the end. Cyrus stayed anyway. Somebody has to cook.

cyrus_belview/43ca20635558b657.text: And this. A little stone. Master gave it so Cyrus would never stop cooking to eat. But Cyrus likes eating. You take it.

cyrus_belview/49981e3b4b2115e2.text: She does cry a great deal, though. It gets in the bread.

cyrus_belview/4bbb2faa36d65461.text: The new wine comes up on a cart again now, with ravens on the casks. Good wine. Nobody bricks up a Martikov.

cyrus_belview/4ea5fcbccc47306d.text: Father walked somewhere to be judged? Father doesn't walk. Father doesn't get judged. Father does the judging.

cyrus_belview/4edec5c09cf0d093.text: Cyrus has forgotten her already. Who? Exactly.

cyrus_belview/4f484268dd984c5a.text: Father sits and says nothing? Father always says something. Usually about improvements.

cyrus_belview/5a4d4bc7df92d57a.text: The Belviews! Is Clovin still carrying everything? He carries everything. Does he still drink?

cyrus_belview/63af9dd0f50cdeb0.text: The crying girl went up the stairs. The Master was very pleased. Cyrus is not pleased. Cyrus doesn't know why.

cyrus_belview/7e87238e981e85cd.text: The holy brother in the other row. He never eats Cyrus's soup. Not once. The Master says leave his door alone.

cyrus_belview/84fb55f5f9ffe851.text: Clovin would. Clovin carries everything, even things he shouldn't.

cyrus_belview/84ff6c581a51a81d.text: The scrap barrel went down the cliff path this morning. Very heavy. Cyrus didn't look inside. Cyrus never looks inside.

cyrus_belview/861ac9e9b26a0bab.text: Down below, past the guests. The Master keeps a table for special company. It is all made of his old enemies. Very sturdy.

cyrus_belview/86a4dd91b08aeb60.text: Back again! Wipe your feet. No, don't. Nobody wipes their feet down here. Why start now?

cyrus_belview/8d57dac5814465af.text: Mind the stairs down. They eat people. Only sometimes.

cyrus_belview/a27b6aed63822dfa.text: Words are cheap. Cyrus knows cheap. It will cost more than words now.

cyrus_belview/a31f8ec3af65bb0d.text: Go away. Go away! Cyrus told the Master nothing. Nothing!

cyrus_belview/a32e160b03337099.text: Shiny. Cyrus collects shiny. Very well.

cyrus_belview/a80129784c51e010.text: He never sent love in his life. You are a kind liar. Cyrus likes kind liars.

cyrus_belview/a9ba3db3cc58aefd.text: One fewer. Nobody counts. That's true, nobody counts. The Master never counts the spoons either.

cyrus_belview/a9cc8a6b28e9d471.text: No! Not in the kitchen! Never in the kitchen!

cyrus_belview/aa7eabfc2b3be83f.text: Somebody built everything. Then they went in the soup.

cyrus_belview/af7eedd3bf3ca43a.text: When the lamp over it burns green, never sit. The lamp drinks from the furnace. Turn the furnace's water wheel and the lamp goes to sleep.

cyrus_belview/b5b8178c74fbdde0.text: Guests! Nobody told Cyrus there were guests up here. Sit, sit. Not that stool. That stool bites.

cyrus_belview/bba5733b26551f6e.text: If he is sorry now, maybe he is sorry about Cyrus too. That would be nice. Cyrus would like that.

cyrus_belview/c221ca6339d25431.text: The Master laughed and laughed. Then Cyrus laid the bricks. Last rack at the very back. Cyrus is good with bricks.

cyrus_belview/c7d56f91035a828f.text: Cyrus was a Belview, up at the abbey. Father made Cyrus. Father makes all of us, a little at a time.

cyrus_belview/cf5accda470bed1f.text: And the priest's boy, who came home with nothing. Cyrus is not to feed him at all. The Master is cross with him.

cyrus_belview/dc9490781737084a.text: Cyrus doesn't know if that is good news. Cyrus will think about it while the bread rises.

cyrus_belview/dfb91331da7d7b8f.text: They are. That's why Cyrus counts them.

cyrus_belview/ecea568bcb4c4767.text: Good. Good! Tell him Cyrus has a whole cellar. Tell him Cyrus is the lucky one.

cyrus_belview/fa0bdbf33bf27856.text: Father is dead. Then nobody will improve the Belviews any more.

danika_martikov/0e3a0e0278dc90df.text: (She doesn't stop kneading. She is kneading very hard.) Bring him home. Then I'll kill him. Then I'll feed him. In that order.

danika_martikov/34af58d1d7d7a6bd.text: Then it's not just us. Then something's wrong at the vineyard. I'll tell Urwin. He'll want to know where you heard it.

danika_martikov/47f616ee554b211a.text: He listens at the cellar door. He's never once cared about the cellar. Somebody's listening through him, aren't they.

danika_martikov/5b9860d8788e61c4.text: Stew. It's always stew. What's in it depends what Urwin found. Don't ask him, and don't ask the stew.

danika_martikov/6116781dcf617129.direction: [brisk, warm, then shouting at the boys]
danika_martikov/6116781dcf617129.text: Guests. Wipe your feet. Brom! Bray! Get away from that window. Sorry. Two boys and an inn. You'd think one would cancel out the other.

danika_martikov/82f8594740a7079c.text: You did this. I know you did; the whole town watched you do it. You'll get a bed, because I won't turn anyone into the night. Don't expect breakfast.

danika_martikov/cb699b0589d3d827.text: Safe as anyone in this valley. Safer than most. Our windows have very good locks, and better neighbours.

danika_martikov/d140abc1e42d6fc6.text: Thin? It's the last cask. The wine comes from Urwin's father's vineyard, the Wizard of Wines, south of the lake road. Every month, a cart. Three months now, no cart, and no word.

davian_martikov/04bdad0bddfbb706.text: To starve us, first. A winery without wine is a farm with airs. And on Yester Hill, west of here, they're building a great figure of earth shaped like the lord in the castle. They mean to wake it with my stone for a heart.

davian_martikov/09885e7b26566722.text: I'll be counting the spoons, mind.

davian_martikov/1528b1ed336d0b3b.text: He's home. That's the thing. Whatever else is true, he's home.

davian_martikov/1d9ae58e27c2b7dd.text: Someone has been in my strongbox. It was a good lock. It was a good lock for forty years.

davian_martikov/202e8be18e0dce58.text: To Krezk. They keep their gate shut to strangers and open it for my carts. If you're going that way, walk beside the casks. A gate that opens for wine might open for you.

davian_martikov/22072ef1e254e3c9.text: Go on. The house won't empty itself.

davian_martikov/22c0cefb472c4e7c.text: From the witch. From Berez. You went into that drowned place for my vines. ...Three. I didn't think I'd see three again before I died. I find I'm in less of a hurry now.

davian_martikov/28bcdec5fdddc375.text: Now come and do the same to the ones sleeping in my house.

davian_martikov/2b972daa8bca7e8e.text: Then here are the terms. Drive them out of the winery and out of the press house. Bring up my stone from the founder's cask: cellar, foot of the stair, third hoop, pull. Then we'll talk about the hill.

davian_martikov/2e561dd67d2df5f9.text: To Urwin, then. He'll pretend he isn't pleased. He gets that from me.

davian_martikov/3777b0e2913650af.text: The first bottles of a free harvest. You'll pay what they cost me to make and not a copper more, and you'll drink the Champagne slowly, or I'll know.

davian_martikov/3b8479070333e8b1.text: Gone up into the mountains, last I heard, forty years back. If he's alive, he's somewhere high and cold, being rude to it.

davian_martikov/3cc035f43c2eb270.text: ...I sent them. I sent them to that hill. And I couldn't look at the one who came home, because then I'd have to look at the one who sent them.

davian_martikov/3e6d620a0659bde1.text: A hat a night, for a dream. You could have told me. I'd have sat in the row with you. I dream of him too, boy. I don't need grapes.

davian_martikov/425880c667ec1953.text: Your fee. My father paid men to clear wolves from these rows, and they charged less, and they were also thieves. Fine. It's paid.

davian_martikov/441260068c83c52c.text: And one thing I can't account for. The ravens say a cold light shows in my house some nights, where no lamp is. If you find it, it isn't mine.

davian_martikov/4540aa248de7ea06.text: Then the press runs again. Not this week; the grapes need a month to remember themselves. But the cellar still holds what we pressed before they came, and the cart in the yard has three good wheels.

davian_martikov/45f43798b7b71c3e.text: To the village. The shopkeeper there will try to charge them double for it. The ravens will see that he doesn't.

davian_martikov/468fcccd31bbb157.text: One was stolen last autumn. The ravens followed the thief to Berez, the drowned village by the river, to the witch who lives there. One the druids carried off to their hill. The last I hid the night we fled.

davian_martikov/4df6d5640f3dd541.text: Hm. Say "ravens" more quietly in my yard, priestess. The castle keeps ears in its eaves.

davian_martikov/4fb5a58643bd8552.text: Then why didn't he say so? He's had a year. A year of me looking through him at supper.

davian_martikov/52d18762d2e55b42.text: Even you. My son says you're not as bad as your aim. Ravens have long memories, but we're not unreasonable.

davian_martikov/59ede29d685f4250.text: The druids sleep in the fermenting hall and feed my vats to their creatures. Their leader, a boy called Kostin, keeps to the press house with something he grew in my best vat. Some nights it sings to him.

davian_martikov/5d3a4576e5431408.text: The Seventh Row's in again. Young vines. Adrian waters them himself and won't let anyone else hold the can. It's a family failing.

davian_martikov/5e055893fd771cf1.text: It's named for a wizard, if that helps. My grandfather named the house for the man who paid us the stones, to annoy him. He stayed a whole winter. A rude old man with a long nose, played dragonchess against himself every night and lost his temper with the black king.

davian_martikov/61fd1d1f90c91ac6.text: You're sitting on his doorstep. That's his lane, with the druids on it. That's his vines. I'm the master of the Wizard of Wines, for my sins.

davian_martikov/6286b12e37972198.text: My family pressed wine on this hill before the valley had its lord. The man on the sign is the wizard who paid us in stones. We set by a cask for him every year. He's never come for it. Wizards are poor at visiting.

davian_martikov/64a9818c69a9f9b1.text: It was carried, once, by a woman who should have lived to be old. It came back without her. My family has been waiting a long while for someone else to ask after it.

davian_martikov/66116f83e084ebc7.text: A vine in winter has no leaves, no fruit, and no warmth you can feel with your hand. You prune it anyway, and you wait. That is faith, priestess. The rest is weather.

davian_martikov/6a2161fca8ab3566.text: My grandfather's row, and you cut it out by the roots. Good. It wasn't his any more.

davian_martikov/6c86fde58ecaf410.text: Somebody picks it in the dark. My pickers won't go near it. Find out who. If it's druids, I want them. If it isn't, I want to know what it is before I burn my grandfather's vines.

davian_martikov/72c8f059be314d06.text: The first cart goes where you say. You've earned that much.

davian_martikov/72e38efe441343df.text: The Keepers of the Feather owe you two stones and a house, and ravens don't forget a debt. Wherever you go in this valley, look up. If you need word carried or eyes on a place, say so out loud.

davian_martikov/76086d5d5b8a8327.text: Adrian. The press is yours. My knees are finished with it.

davian_martikov/797674be2f94d1e5.text: Hello, old friend. You hid well. Better than I did.

davian_martikov/7ee8dc21c668eb56.text: Urwin's friends. The birds have talked of nothing else for a week. Sit. You're shorter than they said.

davian_martikov/8298993ef7419b23.text: The druids. Of course. Filthy creatures, druids. No respect for a good lock.

davian_martikov/82be96bf7ad8ef09.text: My son Elvir went to watch that hill last spring. Don't ask me about it.

davian_martikov/8997baf4dc2b8a0f.text: Adrian has the press. Stefania has the house. I have nothing left to do here but get in the way. Better I get in his way.

davian_martikov/8f615f8ae8811e4d.text: You took my son up that hill and brought him back down it. I'll not forget that.

davian_martikov/902f1a22c3f612e7.text: The boy Kostin ran west, the ravens say, toward the hill. He'll warn them you're coming. Expect to be expected.

davian_martikov/90e037efa83533db.text: Hm. You have honest faces, or faces that have practised. In the cellar, at the foot of the stair, stands the founder's cask, older than the house. It has a false end. Turn the third hoop and pull.

davian_martikov/934bd45451438a99.text: The figure broken and the druids scattered. And the tree? Still standing, the ravens say. Hm. Trees are patient. So are ravens.

davian_martikov/9663837b68445e83.text: Interesting. Hm. The Seventh Row. My grandfather planted it, and Elvir pruned it from the day he could hold the knife. It's coming up black. Black grapes every night, and every morning, bare.

davian_martikov/9735213fc88d9874.text: The Wizard of Wines is a winery, boy. It's a sign over a gate. It's a house that makes wine.

davian_martikov/a293478e7fc6964d.text: No. You don't. Neither do I.

davian_martikov/a8844ce231f80cc9.text: Then we'll find out when I count it, won't we. I'll count it later, alone, like a miser. It's a family tradition.

davian_martikov/a9021a11974952e4.text: The Seventh Row. You know as much as I do. Go and sit in it after dark.

davian_martikov/ab6bc8bfa8d12887.text: "I sent him." ...Elvir. You stubborn, stupid boy. You always did think you were the eldest.

davian_martikov/ac6554596f34ce2d.text: Because a raven sees a great deal and repeats it in the right ears. My family has watched the lord in the castle for longer than he has known he was being watched. He knows now. This is his answer.

davian_martikov/afa2cc7f0b32405b.text: Someone in Vallaki misses my wine, then. Good. So do I. Sit.

davian_martikov/b153146082bb74f8.text: He told me. Some of it. Enough. We'll talk about the rest when we've both drunk enough to manage it.

davian_martikov/b23c9a6aa58d7411.text: No vine should live in this valley; there's no sun worth the name. Ours do because three stones lie in their soil, green as new leaves, each the size of a plum. A wizard paid them to my family, long ago, for a winter's lodging.

davian_martikov/b3ac8e7e818840f9.text: To the hill, broken. To the house, ours. And to strangers, who it turns out are good for something.

davian_martikov/b69f5eca980e1e64.text: Ilinca Vrana says you pulled two children out of a hag's oven. Ilinca doesn't say good things about anyone, so I expect it's true. Sit.

davian_martikov/bacefd1b4bdc2e95.text: Hm. A thief who brings it back is either a fool or an honest man having a bad week. I'll assume the second. Keep ten for the lock.

davian_martikov/bb707eb29cee8445.text: I'll pay in the only coin I trust. Wine, when there's wine again. Until then, my gratitude, which is rarer.

davian_martikov/bc615c5aa10812aa.text: And Ruxandra is dead. I knew her when she was a girl who picked my grapes for a copper a basket. I'll drink to who she was. Not to what she became.

davian_martikov/bcd096b25d42202a.text: The ravens saw the smoke from here: one black column, straight up, as if the hill were being emptied. Good. Let it burn to the roots.

davian_martikov/beece6da2670e83b.text: Don't tell me what my son meant. I know what my son meant. I knew him before you knew this valley had a name.

davian_martikov/bfa4ddc3022716d8.text: Stefania will mind the house. Adrian will mind the vines. He's good at being left behind.

davian_martikov/c13b291b499f258c.text: Stefania! Bring the children. We're going home.

davian_martikov/c3f41c9dba707a5e.text: It's been near that tree. Good soil will draw it out, in time. Most things wash out, in time.

davian_martikov/c46a3c183e9d8d6d.text: And Ruxandra lives, somewhere out there. Mercy's a fine thing. Remember that you chose it, if she comes back.

davian_martikov/c718193e22f5214e.text: You asked before. My house is mine again. Ask me now.

davian_martikov/cc05af62cd12ef3e.text: The ravens saw the boy Kostin walk west, slowly, like a man who isn't sure where he's going anymore. Interesting.

davian_martikov/d1fbd1f564d0d6eb.text: Three helpings. I don't take three helpings of anything. Ask my wife. Ask my dead wife; she'll tell you.

davian_martikov/d3485ae57dbc6745.text: You're the ones who struck my son out of the air on the Svalich road. Sit down. I can't afford to throw you out, and I hate that more than I hate you.

davian_martikov/d45085ae41a49497.text: My house smells of druid. It will smell of wine again by spring or I'll know the reason. Speak.

davian_martikov/db79474244be5812.text: Druids don't pick locks. They don't need to; they grow through them. Don't lie to me in my own house. You're not good enough at it yet.

davian_martikov/de2d01219cde5cc6.text: Eva. Of course it was Eva. She bought wine from my father and haggled him to tears. If her cards say the old raven flies with you, then the old raven flies with you.

davian_martikov/df7e02a91ded3b9e.text: Fewer than yesterday, if you start now.

davian_martikov/e19e3896b40a87b8.text: They're tearing my house apart to find it. So far my house is winning.

davian_martikov/e6a16f2ad3e15da4.text: My grandmother told it so. At the first dawn the sun was given a raven to carry it, because the sun cannot walk. Long after, when this valley went dark, a raven carried a little of that dawn down here, in silver, for anyone fool enough to carry it back up into the night for somebody else.

davian_martikov/e88ed32b191335d4.text: Strangers, at my fire. Either you've come to rob me, and you're three months late, or you've come to help, and you're very welcome. Sit.

davian_martikov/f0e193c4db4cc43c.text: I am Davian Martikov. That was my winery up there until the druids of Yester Hill walked up my lane with the forest at their backs. Now my family lives under the trees like birds. Which, in fairness, we are.

davian_martikov/f25fe283265ca1f6.text: I've drunk to both, in alternate years.

davian_martikov/f5a398517b1daae9.text: A Vistani crone shuffled her deck and my name fell out. Hm. I'll go where her cards say, and gladly, once there are no druids asleep in my bed. Not before. A man doesn't leave his house to squatters.

davian_martikov/fea6eab5c80fd098.text: Two. Two in the ground. My grandfather had only two for a while, when he was a boy, and he swore the wine was better for having to try.

davian_martikov/ffb205836f61f052.text: The wizard who gave us the stones left this in the press-house rack a hundred years ago, against the day something in the vines needed burning. I always thought it was a joke. It turns out he was a better farmer than he looked.

dmitri_krezkov/064e7686dee8c1a1.text: Nobody has talked their way past that gate in eleven years. I'll let you in to see what that kind of tongue looks like. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/066b13afb09e2425.text: Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. The Martikovs' wine has come up this road every autumn since my grandfather's time. This year: nothing. No cart, no word.

dmitri_krezkov/0a83253979c1c6f4.text: The road ends here. The mountains don't. Everything that comes down out of them, or up the road at us, meets the wall first. That's what a wall is for.

dmitri_krezkov/11ddf6131e28e94a.text: Sorin. Sorin. I told her not to take you up there. I was right, and I'd give every year of being right to have been wrong.

dmitri_krezkov/1422e26e643dd494.text: Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. You're a priest. A real one, with a god that answers?

dmitri_krezkov/160b361d3384ea83.text: Or very loud. Come in, then. You'd climb it otherwise, and I'd lose men stopping you. Don't make me sorry I counted.

dmitri_krezkov/1f71e18d2b910050.text: Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. You bled on our doorstep for us. That's a reason. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/21600fa05176489b.text: Jokes. A Belview wants to come down the mountain and tell Krezk jokes.

dmitri_krezkov/21dc533ccc1b0be3.text: Might. He might. And then I'd owe him my son, and he'd come down for the debt one day with that kind face of his, asking nicely.

dmitri_krezkov/2466c58c24dc6ee8.text: No. I'm sorry. If I open the gate for one Belview, I open it for the Abbot's errands, and then for the Abbot. No.

dmitri_krezkov/2b33d6a6ea5b5810.text: The Abbot cured them. He keeps them up there still, and he's been improving them ever since. That's his word for it. Go and look at them, and then tell me what word you'd use.

dmitri_krezkov/2b97d402555e6ec4.text: The devil wants you. Every soul in the valley knows it. You ask me to open my gate and let his want in after you.

dmitri_krezkov/2f259b2a33087fd4.text: He looks like a boy carved out of honey and he talks like your grandmother. Folk go up that mountain sick and come down well. Or they don't come down.

dmitri_krezkov/302b516373d59e27.text: The Martikovs. Their cart came up every autumn since my grandfather's time. Wine for the shrine, wine for weddings, wine for the long nights. This year nothing.

dmitri_krezkov/36a612706228dff3.text: Dead. An angel, or whatever he was, dead in his own chapel. I'll have the bell rung. Somebody should, and nobody up there will.

dmitri_krezkov/38acb2926434d1ae.text: He's out of bed. Thin as a candle, but out of bed. Anna says the White Sun did it. I say you did. We've agreed to both be right.

dmitri_krezkov/3c425ff957a29b03.text: You came to my gate with threats, and now you want me to take in the one woman in the valley he'd burn a village to reach? No. Find her another wall.

dmitri_krezkov/47bef3e5bcdce1a0.text: Two doors down. Yes. I said that. I hate it when people listen.

dmitri_krezkov/4965ea1543af43bf.text: Dmitri Krezkov. Burgomaster. My watchman tells me you're very persuasive.

dmitri_krezkov/528bcc695f9ffd05.text: That isn't my son. That's one of his... things. Belviews. Get it out of my yard.

dmitri_krezkov/59a7aab62b1f5a5b.text: A village that can't drink can still pray, but it does it with less conviction. Come in. Drink our water. Tell me what you know.

dmitri_krezkov/5a598402f396f04d.text: Five of our children are in the churchyard by the pool. I can walk to their stones with my eyes shut. I am not going to learn the way to a sixth.

dmitri_krezkov/60ee23441f1fbd8b.text: And this. My grandfather's mail. I kept it for my eldest son to wear. It seems he'll never fit it now, so you'd better.

dmitri_krezkov/612e7751c91ac03e.text: Inside. Quickly. We don't hold it open for weather. My house is the big one past the well, if you've business with Krezk.

dmitri_krezkov/62d86336f10f5e68.text: That's more than mine does. My son is sick. My last son. If your god answers you in my house, you can have anything Krezk owns. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/657f879bde92433f.text: No. No. I buried my son. I'll not have the Abbot's leavings at my table to remind me how.

dmitri_krezkov/692b5f67242f6aeb.text: One evening. Dusk, in the square by the shrine, and he's back up the mountain before the gate's barred. And if anyone throws a bucket, it isn't on my word.

dmitri_krezkov/6ccc3b719fd38d6f.text: You gave me back a son. I suppose I can give a Belview an evening.

dmitri_krezkov/78fa5c2941ac8e2e.text: If you pass that way, find out what's become of them. Krezk would owe you, and Krezk pays in things you can't buy anywhere else. Goat cheese, mostly. And honesty.

dmitri_krezkov/8070d6130682800c.text: Ireena Kolyana. I knew your father. I am Dmitri Krezkov, and Krezk is mine to keep.

dmitri_krezkov/8498c8a389d54235.text: Our healer died two winters back. Anna sits with him. She sings. When she stops singing, I go up and check he's breathing.

dmitri_krezkov/853b4e9b595337f3.text: He's never once raised his voice, or a hand, to anyone in Krezk. That frightens me more than if he had.

dmitri_krezkov/8b72b93cb9d04565.text: Back again. Sit, if you like. The chairs are older than the both of us and they've held worse.

dmitri_krezkov/8d209f282b1cd354.text: My son is well, and the thing on the mountain is dead, and I didn't have to choose which I wanted more. You did that. Krezk keeps its debts.

dmitri_krezkov/90f7c95fb7f48697.text: The little room off the hall. It was my eldest's. It's had nobody in it for six years, and it'll be glad of the company. Lock the shutters. Krezk does.

dmitri_krezkov/9380ab0a2d32ecc5.text: If he says you're harmless, you're harmless or you're his. Either way, he'd find another road for you. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/94d1b9ff94a54ccc.text: The Belviews were a Krezk family. Farmers, two doors from here. A sickness took the whole house, and they went up to the abbey for the cure.

dmitri_krezkov/a36d24971ea7bf71.text: Your father sent us salt, the winter the passes closed and we had none. Krezk doesn't forget salt. Open it.

dmitri_krezkov/a7d2785074e86e38.text: The town armory. Every family gave something to it once, when we still thought walls were enough. Blades, bows, mail, a suit of plate that nobody has fitted in thirty years. Pay what it's worth, and use it on the things outside.

dmitri_krezkov/b21af8c0cbe042aa.text: The Abbot came down at dawn and put his hand on the boy's head, and walked back up without a word. I owe him. I hate owing him. Both of those are true.

dmitri_krezkov/b37fcbe836083619.text: One thing. Word came up from Vallaki that Fiona Wachter sits in the burgomaster's chair now, and that strangers put her there. If that was you, keep it to yourselves inside my wall.

dmitri_krezkov/b40bf8522bee23af.text: The Belviews say he walked up the mountain and didn't stop at the top. I've hated him for twenty years. I find I'm not sure who to hate now. It's restful.

dmitri_krezkov/b4e23f3514246c34.text: And she wants me to go up the mountain and ask the Abbot. On my knees, I expect, the way the Belviews asked.

dmitri_krezkov/b578123498ced975.text: If he comes to my door on his own, I won't bar it. That's as far as I can bend. Don't ask me to bend further. I'll break, and Anna needs one of us whole.

dmitri_krezkov/b86ac6e36a3f4e92.text: Word came from Vallaki that the town threw out its Baron and put a priest and an innkeeper in charge. If you had a hand in it, I'd shake it. Once.

dmitri_krezkov/bff4743d94643dab.text: In Anna's dress. I haven't told her yet what it was for. I don't know if I will.

dmitri_krezkov/c0c37e4a36a5e616.text: I'm Dmitri Krezkov, burgomaster. You've been up the mountain. And he sent you down to me with his blessing.

dmitri_krezkov/c7327af817520444.text: I made nothing of him while he lived, because I was afraid. Now he's dead and I find I'm still afraid. Perhaps that was never about him.

dmitri_krezkov/cbe8e76b41c2eb67.text: You gave him his bride. A dead girl sewn out of our dead girls, sent down the road to the castle in a wedding dress. Krezk will pray about that for a long time.

dmitri_krezkov/cded5316c9518776.text: Our wall, our roof, our bread. It's not much and he'll know where it is within a week. But it's yours, Ireena Kolyana. Your father sent us salt once.

dmitri_krezkov/ce7f0215d34e7280.text: He's out at the well, shouting at goats. My son. I keep going to the window to check it's true.

dmitri_krezkov/dd80bf03df15c41a.text: Every stranger who knocked in my lifetime wanted something. Twice, it was him, wearing a stranger's face, asking nicely. So now we ask for a reason, and we decide what a reason is.

dmitri_krezkov/e31270f96ab95cb3.text: And you're the ones who offered to test my wall. My bowman remembers your faces. So will I. Behave inside it.

dmitri_krezkov/e55916f319bc899f.text: Dmitri Krezkov. This is my house, and that's my table, and you're welcome at both while you mind the wall's rules.

dmitri_krezkov/e5dbe48ad14ee09e.text: Stones. I carried stones. I dug the hole myself, and I carried stones.

dmitri_krezkov/f2f26a8aa67397ac.text: You. The ones who threatened my watchman. Say your business and don't get comfortable.

dmitri_krezkov/f4c3c703e80b40a4.text: My son Ilya. Eight years old. A fever came up the road in the autumn with the last carter, and it found him. It's been burning a month.

dmitri_krezkov/f5ea8dda7ec2c3d1.text: He sits in his chapel, the Belviews say, and won't speak. A thing like that, broken. I thought I'd be glad. I'm only tired.

dmitri_krezkov/f68dc12f06131757.text: You were. Don't spend it all at once.

dmitri_krezkov/fa9def900ca6af90.text: Sent by who? No. Don't answer that. I'd rather not have to pray to whoever it was.

dmitri_krezkov/fce93394c15894e9.text: Upstairs. Anna won't let go of his hand, so you'll have to work around her.

donavich/053e692327b64cbc.text: It's still quiet below. I keep waking to listen for him. Habit, I suppose. Grief is mostly habit.

donavich/09c8fd642f507493.text: There's nothing to tell. Nothing. Please.

donavich/14ff4b0c7dd936df.text: Please. Whatever you are, don't hurt him. There may be a way back. There must be.

donavich/1a3f7c948a5ad59e.text: The rest is in the vestry, for the burial of the dead. Ask me again when I know you better.

donavich/2290855b8c982567.text: You've been below. You've seen him. Then there's no use lying, is there.

donavich/273ba3923b9e1b1a.text: And Morninglord forgive me, the moment he was gone I slept, the first time in weeks. What kind of father sleeps?

donavich/35f027b0a2824b70.text: If anyone alive knows where it lies, it's the old Vistani seer at Tser Pool. Or him. He keeps what frightens him.

donavich/36b98c50e734102b.text: You still feel Him? Here? I haven't, not for a year. I say "Dawn will come" every night, to keep my mouth from saying other things.

donavich/38d77e067fd1f8b3.text: Get out of my church. Bury your burgomaster yourselves. I have a son to bury, and no one to say the words over him either.

donavich/3e2f13bfacd0d52c.text: Ah, but you've found the vestry chest already. Keep what you took. It does no good in a box.

donavich/3e39a663631605b4.text: There's nothing for you here. Not anymore. Go.

donavich/3e3c9c15c8463e35.text: My own hand. Yes. I've held it every night for months, from this side. First let me pray. An hour. Forgive me; I need the hour more than he does.

donavich/44a392f65e32d166.text: It's quiet. For the first time in weeks, it's quiet below. Thank you. I think. Ask me again in a year.

donavich/46b9eebcc87f0201.text: The Durst children. Rose and Thorn. Folk saw them in the road for years. If they are at rest now, then you've done more for this village in a night than I have in a year.

donavich/4d4f70818680fba5.text: The Holy Symbol of Ravenkind. Older than this church. A giant raven brought it to a paladin of the dawn, the stories say, and it was turned against the devil once, and lost after. Lost, mind. Not destroyed.

donavich/4fcb1d49ec7cd93d.text: Then he's farther from the castle than any of us. Go. Bury your dead. I'll bury mine.

donavich/510a40441a61dce2.text: Months later Doru came home, at night, wearing his own face. I lured him below and barred the door. I pray. He screams. Neither of us has stopped since.

donavich/539ab017640b6d79.text: You've come back. He's still below. You left him to me, and I'm grateful, and some nights I wish you hadn't. Both of those are prayers, I think.

donavich/53a0c144b2542ccf.text: You've come back. He hasn't. I leave the side door unbarred at night now. I don't know if that's faith or foolishness.

donavich/6233819e2ad9964c.text: The bell rang by itself when that house at the end of the lane began to groan. You were inside it, weren't you, children? And you came out. The Morninglord keeps odd company these days.

donavich/67cc6f3665fd04fe.text: No. I'm sorry. I can't. If he gets past you, he gets past me, and then the village. The bar stays.

donavich/70b16faca21bb9a9.text: Do it, then. Gently, if there's any gentle way. I've lifted the bar. I can't watch. I'm sorry, my boy. I'm so sorry.

donavich/72bcc122dabeb539.text: No. No! He's my son. You'll not touch him. The bar stays where it is, and you'll stay away from it.

donavich/795a613178f81655.text: You went down there. You killed my boy. I begged you. I begged you.

donavich/7a9a52b918dc86cd.text: You've come back, children. Forgive me if I don't rise; my knees have taken the shape of the floor.

donavich/7ac52eedc1a77796.text: Talk? Oh, he'll talk. He'll talk you all the way to the door and through it. He was always good at talking.

donavich/7add3eb5f9df0e72.text: Forgive me. Pay it no mind, children, please. It's nothing that concerns you.

donavich/7bfe148e14559072.text: You ask me that? After what you did below? No.

donavich/7f0522b8de65b2cf.text: I'll keep him fed on prayer until you come back. It's all I have to feed him on.

donavich/7f11e8a1fc10b9f5.text: My son. Doru. He went with the other young men to storm the castle and kill the devil in his bed. They had torches and a song. The devil gave them dinner.

donavich/8f7e7efc60d1c245.text: Need? Food. Sleep. My son back. You can't give me those, children. Holy water is all I have left to give, and precious little of that.

donavich/9cafebe75706fe58.text: Forgive me. Forgive... I've lost the words.

donavich/a9484897955c9eb3.text: We give Kolyan Indirovich to the earth he kept, in the light he trusted. Morninglord, you who come back every morning though no one thanks you for it, come back for him.

donavich/a9ea6c32240cdfc7.text: Forgive me, children. You've been in the house at the end of the lane; there's a smell on you I know from funerals that went wrong. That house wanted an offering. I won't ask what you gave it. The Morninglord already knows.

donavich/afeb363c4dbf64ea.text: The church sold healing once, when there were people to heal. There's a little left in the vestry: draughts the sisters brewed, prayers written out on good paper. Take what you need. Leave what you can. I'll buy bread with it, and candles.

donavich/b07d60b1ecd1b344.text: End it. You mean kill him. Kill my boy.

donavich/bfd171e410046db3.text: Take these. Holy water. It will burn him. I blessed it for him weeks ago, and could never throw it.

donavich/cb4f4e3311c7654a.text: Wait. Take this. A shard of the old dawn window, from before it cracked. It still holds a little of the morning. I can't look at it anymore.

donavich/d392551f4c51d7e0.text: Here. Two flasks. Throw them hard; the dead don't flinch the way the living do.

donavich/ddc46aed171f2bb8.text: The bar is up. The undercroft is empty. You let him out. He'll go to the castle. He'll go to him.

donavich/e6a09acb84391b4e.text: Rest, Kolyan. Nobody will call you up again. Not while I have breath to forbid it.

donavich/e89ff3d79983fbd3.text: Your word. In Barovia that's a strange coin. Very well; the bar is up. Don't open your hand to him. Don't let him see your throat.

donavich/ec0ac84afa5e05f9.text: I've given you all I had. The well's dry, and so am I.

donavich/f186972a6db0642d.text: A madman. A poor soul I shelter, out of charity. He's loud. Please, don't go near the undercroft door.

donavich/f4f880796e6cc8d4.text: You would? There are old stories. Saints' bones that turn the dead. Relics of the Morninglord. The sun itself, once. If anything in this valley could bring him back, it's one of those.

donavich/f59eab40f9247a58.text: Forgive me. You've sat through it now. There's no use lying to people who've sat through it.

donavich/f706681d48fd2b91.text: Who... forgive me. Visitors. We have so few. The doors are open; I can't remember why I stopped barring them. Perhaps I hoped someone would come.

donavich/f75ea70729aa651f.text: Kolyan. He came every holy day until there were no holy days left. Yes. Yes, I'll say the words over him. It's the one thing I still know how to do.

donavich/ff607d5632fe1e5c.text: Bring him to the grave behind the church; I'll meet you there. And if my boy cries out during the rites, keep singing. Please. Keep singing.

doru/186b2e0d5dcaaabb.text: You came back. Nobody comes back. Did you bring Father, or just your throats?

doru/2633bf933b768a92.text: He fed us. He let us talk about killing him all through the meal, smiling. Then the candles went out. I was dessert, he said. The others weren't so lucky. Or they were.

doru/36dbfbc447f3b194.text: You would? Oh, you would. I'll go far away. To the castle; the master will take me in. I'll never trouble Father again. I swear it on the Morninglord. On my mother. On anything.

doru/4909a05251994079.text: Doru. The priest's son. I rang the bell on holy days, before. I was going to be a hero. Everyone was going to sing about it.

doru/4bf25d56a2b62f5e.text: Does he? Still? Even now? Tell him... no. Don't tell him where I am. Tell him I went far away.

doru/54c9badd83f8545f.text: He sent you. Didn't he. He finally said yes. Tell him I'm sorry about the cake on his name day. Tell him... quickly. Before I stop being sorry.

doru/7208cefeb30ed682.text: Still here. Still hungry. Have you come to watch?

doru/734c769a8a1b7a88.text: I'll tell him. He'll smile. He smiled at us too, all through dinner. He sent a gift, in case you said it.

doru/8536d13d64a39aad.text: You. You opened the door under the church. I remember how you smelled. Rain and roads.

doru/8b7e93e8a5b6011e.text: Yes. Please. Before he wants me again.

doru/9c9c0299f8b4407c.text: Thank you. Thank you. Oh, you're warm. You're all so warm.

doru/9ee2ed3865d2b96f.text: Stop. Stop it, it burns. No, keep going. Father used to... stop! Stop!

doru/b2fe66ea26a527b0.text: We went up the road with torches, singing. The gates were open. He met us in the hall in a beautiful coat and said we must be hungry after such a climb.

doru/cc3774ccb6f2a292.text: There isn't one. There's the hunger and there's the stake. I've asked the dark every night. That's all it says.

doru/d39fe9e90b2ddf4e.text: Then come up here and do it.

doru/da2cda4de1875412.text: Don't stop. I like funerals now. My master sends his regrets; he's dining elsewhere tonight. He says Ireena should leave her window open. It's stuffy, waiting.

doru/db8f3a4228a846ed.text: Father? No. You smell like outside. Like rain and roads. I'd forgotten roads. Come closer; I can't see you properly.

doru/df08d4ec011540ff.text: Is he. Is he still. Tell him... no. Tell him nothing. Tell him I was never here.

doru/eaa1d794abda75e4.text: No. No! Come back! I'm better now! I'm better!

doru/eede6669c4ff8b7b.text: Go, then! Go! I'll be here. I'm always here. Tell Father I'm hungry. Tell him every night!

doru/f57aa5bf47526c70.text: Come a little closer while you think it over. Just a little.

doru/f85ac20ab10a0a4f.text: I went home to him, to the castle. I thought he'd give me a seat at the table. He gave me this, for coming back with nothing.

durst_nursemaid/3f688642df16de11.text: Liars. You're with them. You're wearing their faces!

durst_nursemaid/475a41be2343b6f3.text: He's under the house. He's been under the house so long. If you go down, sing it to him. Someone should.

durst_nursemaid/6f63aaf020b50c00.text: Gone. Yes. I knew. I knew when they stopped him crying. They stopped me too, at the bottom of the stairs.

durst_nursemaid/7a60fba2052cd40d.text: He was mine. The master's and mine. The mistress gave him to the robed ones the night he was born, and they carried him down, and I followed them.

durst_nursemaid/f06fdd0abb77cc7c.text: Have you brought him? Have you brought my Walter back up?

elisabeth_durst/114280b8a69c12e9.text: One must die, so the rest may live forever. We only got the second half wrong.

elisabeth_durst/3401308dfbde8e12.text: Upstairs. Safe. We locked them in so they wouldn't see.

elisabeth_durst/5daba77263063c8b.text: That one was never mine. He was the first gift. The finest gift we had.

elisabeth_durst/ed9e599aae00c894.text: They came down the children's way. Didn't you, dears.

emil_toranescu/16c9f6a5130098d7.text: The Vistani grandmother and her cards. She told me once I'd die in chains. Funny, how close she came.

emil_toranescu/19af3d13928d64b3.text: You freed me to kill me? Zuleika said you were honest. She was right. You're honest butchers.

emil_toranescu/2bbb4e5b8e044aa8.text: I'll be here. The jewellery makes sure of it.

emil_toranescu/2e40a729202e2ebd.text: Zuleika has one; Kiril trusted her with it so she could watch. Kiril keeps the other on a peg in his lair, north of the great cave, because he likes to look at it.

emil_toranescu/2e7641ddbdf175d1.text: It's done. By the old law the pack is mine again. Kiril's favourites are dead or running down the Krezk road with their tails tucked. The rest are listening.

emil_toranescu/3386e728dd21b226.text: I know it. That's why I'm the one in chains.

emil_toranescu/3396ba1fa8e695d5.text: He's not far. He never was, from his supper. Wait for him in the great cave, where he can see us.

emil_toranescu/3df98278ec1ca216.text: Hear me, then. We hunt deer. We keep to the high hills. We don't come when the castle whistles. And the children go home.

emil_toranescu/4632d4881a479bc3.text: The Vistani grandmother's cards. She told me once I'd die in chains, and she was nearly right. Now they say I'm to walk with you to the old man's door.

emil_toranescu/4d0626087f781649.text: Thank you. Now I have to do something you won't like. A chained wolf who walks free without howling his challenge is a thief, and anyone may kill a thief.

emil_toranescu/5615c80d7e7e2f11.text: Emil Toranescu. I led this pack nineteen winters. We hunted deer and the odd careless shepherd, kept to the high hills, and left the villages alone. The castle left us alone in return. Then Kiril came home.

emil_toranescu/5c401a16c13bd2ce.text: Get me out of these, and let's see what else she got wrong.

emil_toranescu/66177b81b06c4a8a.text: But if it ever comes to the end with the old man on the hill, and you need teeth at his gates, send word up this hill.

emil_toranescu/73bf612faee3a92e.text: Not mine. I wasn't leader then. But I was in those woods that night, and so were wolves that weren't ours: the castle's, big and silent.

emil_toranescu/833538e3db13b101.text: Kiril will hear it. He'll come. When he does, you'll want to be standing next to me.

emil_toranescu/8911897212e1778d.text: You smell of Zuleika's herbs. She sent you. That woman. I told her not to.

emil_toranescu/8a7f672c50eb9b79.text: Visitors. Kiril's? No. Kiril's visitors don't look at the chains like that.

emil_toranescu/8b8127f092beb4af.text: The pack is quieter without Kiril. Hungrier, too. Deer it is, for a while.

emil_toranescu/9a57b5f0ce4437e0.text: I know. I told you not to.

emil_toranescu/9bfa58a62c87504a.text: And the huntress. You killed two of Kiril's on the Krezk road. Good shooting. I'd have done it myself, with my hands free.

emil_toranescu/9d131a9030519fe8.text: You've given me back my pack. I can't follow you to the castle; they'd be at each other's throats in a week without me, and at Zuleika's in two.

emil_toranescu/9f7165706077f504.text: The ones who loved Kiril are dead or gone down the Krezk road. The rest are tired and glad to be. Zuleika has them mending things. Wolves hate mending things.

emil_toranescu/a0b0399868178833.text: She means she never needed me.

emil_toranescu/a59ea0516707b3a4.text: Then stand close, and don't let them get behind you.

emil_toranescu/a5d875f61384023d.text: Go well. Keep to the trail; my wolves know your smell now.

emil_toranescu/a860dea8819a3662.text: I misjudged you. That's my fault, not yours. I always was too quick to like people.

emil_toranescu/ac7b481977bf8cd0.text: And be hunted through the hills by a pack that knows every stone, with five children who can't run? No. We do it the old way, here, with rock at our backs.

emil_toranescu/bdfc834112dbd6b5.text: Watch, then, huntress. From a respectful distance.

emil_toranescu/c131c78eac2038b5.text: I told him the old law: we don't take pups that aren't ours. He said the old law was dead. Then his favourites held me down.
