emil_toranescu/d78fcc34cf16889d.text: There was a boy screaming and a girl with red hair, and a rider in black at the treeline. We ran. I've been ashamed of running for twenty years.

emil_toranescu/d9771e68eda034d7.text: Not come. Let the old man on the hill whistle for his dogs. If it ever comes to the end with him, and you need teeth at his gates, send word up the hill.

emil_toranescu/db1482a64381ce5b.text: The key would be kinder. To both of us.

emil_toranescu/e35afea0ed4afaba.text: Still here. Still chained. Neither of us is enjoying it.

emil_toranescu/e7677a143b700f6c.text: I howled the challenge, Kiril. By the old law, you answer it.

emil_toranescu/eb6d5a7315c95cd2.text: I always mind the bite. That was the whole argument.

emil_toranescu/ef556c51dc16fde1.text: You found Kiril's chest. Good. Half of it came off the Krezk road; if you pass anyone who looks robbed, you know what to do.

emil_toranescu/f188ca634dc58544.text: Kiril went up to the castle and came back with a new law. The master wants an army that runs on four legs. And where do new wolves come from? He came back from the Krezk road with a sack of children.

escher/0bc41bf080b1e51b.text: He'll feel it the moment it breaks, of course. I'd be somewhere else when it does, if I were you.

escher/0e9f9579c66c69b7.text: He collects people, you see. He just doesn't play with them for very long.

escher/187322801dc3143b.text: He got bored of everyone. I was simply the most recent.

escher/20c1d240913cacc1.text: Get out. Go and threaten somebody with a pulse.

escher/291d7cb6ced3172f.text: Well. Visitors. Has our host sent you up to look at me? I'm not on display today. Come back when I've been dusted.

escher/3d7589d6bfa75d00.text: I was a guest here, once. Then a favourite. Then this. Then the favourite part ended, and here I am, locked in with my coats.

escher/41255941b6654ddd.text: Do shut the door on your way out. The draught is dreadful, and I can't even die of it.

escher/457eb1820e99a174.text: Back again. I'm flattered. I'd offer you a chair, but you'd only sit in it.

escher/4ec2781955f71a6b.text: Oh, don't. Flattery from the living. It smells of soup. Now it will cost you double.

escher/62dbbd471317efe3.text: Double. I did warn you. I always warn people; it's the only manners I have left.

escher/6a335426ed6513eb.text: At the top of the high tower there is a heart. Not his own; that stopped centuries ago. A glass one, big as a man, and it beats for him.

escher/7c3d9df4bd114503.text: With you? Into a fight with him? I've seen what he does to people who leave. I've seen what he does to people who stay, which is worse, only slower.

escher/95629e86dd782e55.text: There is something. I've seen it. He took me up to see it once, the way you'd show a lover a scar. What's it worth to you?

escher/981be99a3cdf4fdc.text: One of Strahd's former. Do keep up.

escher/9b30016dd28ba371.text: Customers. Come for something else? Everything here has a price, darlings, including the conversation.

escher/9d6b2a9232e7c943.text: ...Yes. Yes, I do. Oh, very well. It's been so long since anyone asked me anything.

escher/b2fa1857ffe452c2.text: My jailbreakers. Is he dust yet? No? Then I can't think why you're bothering me.

escher/b3bd031066199fe6.text: A promise. How quaint. Nobody has made me one of those in a hundred years. Here, something to remember it by.

escher/b86d5ae7450d97ce.text: That little clockwork thing? It was built to amuse the children of the house in place of their jester, a little man called Pidlwick. The children went on preferring the real one.

escher/c205e84d297cf50e.text: Behind my wardrobe there's a stair the servants used, up into the roof where the ravens live. I'd use it myself, but he'd know. He always knows.

escher/fc1f685c4e71a752.text: You think I'm afraid of the sun? I'm afraid of him. You're merely rude.

escher/fd034711d4aafcc7.text: Keep your promise. Leave my door open. That is all the help I can stand.

escher/feb763d0a0304575.text: Then one night the real one went down the high tower stair the quick way, and the toy was standing at the top. Draw your own conclusions.

escher/fef8563d0b1940f2.text: Cut him, and the glass bleeds instead. That's why your swords never seem to take. Break it, and he bleeds like the rest of us.

exethanter/055dd0501cc44a2f.text: Not so loud! Someone might hear, and then they'd know where it isn't.

exethanter/0888e9573f2ddcc4.text: Please. I'd like to forget this again now. Would you mind very much if I did?

exethanter/0cf77f9d0b804d6f.text: How thoughtful! I'll read it every time I see you. If I remember to read it. I generally do read my sleeve.

exethanter/16e619a29eab21cd.text: Oh, no. Oh, my dears. We had one rule. One. We carved it over the door so we wouldn't forget, and even I...

exethanter/1a6eaec0d78d37ee.text: I took him down to the one with no name. I told myself the rule was for wardens, and he wasn't one. The jackal was there, I think. I think he was smiling.

exethanter/1c0f95cc87825869.text: We gathered up the vestiges, you see: the last scraps of dead gods and worse, things the world was right to forget. Amber holds them. Nothing else does. And then we sat down to guard them forever.

exethanter/22995ceb480c89a5.text: This? The Amber Temple. We built it. Well. They built it, and I helped, and then they all died and I didn't, which I gather is the usual arrangement with liches.

exethanter/23f4f75b52175424.text: Need? Oh, there is something, now you mention it. I've lost a... thing. Small. It has a lid, I'm nearly sure. A box, or a jar. Something with a lid.

exethanter/31a02403206ecb05.text: Ah. Well. You live a few centuries, things slip. Names. Faces. Most of my spells. I used to know one that made a sort of wall out of... no. It's gone. It had a lovely name.

exethanter/3ad1ca803d5fd080.text: Goodbye! Do come again. I'll be delighted to meet you.

exethanter/3b39ae87a28c1a61.text: One by one. They were very persuasive scraps. I believe I listened too. I can't remember to which.

exethanter/3baac9570d68b5ae.text: Goodbye, friends! It says friends. Mind the duck.

exethanter/3ef1405d6e17d4fc.text: The jackal's gone. I felt him go, like a draught shutting off. I've been cold for three hundred years and never noticed.

exethanter/3f74c60a3d4f0548.text: Here! I wrote it down. Clever me. You say it like a door closing. There. Now you know it, and I've already half forgotten I told you, so we're both quite safe.

exethanter/44ed5b7a58f17fbd.text: The word! Yes. The wardens' word. It quiets the colossus and it opens the honey doors, and it's... it's...

exethanter/4fbfb0a6c972b3fc.text: Where else would I keep it? In my head? Have you met my head?

exethanter/5f3c5fa72dcd5aad.text: Oh! The robe. I remember this robe. I sewed the stars on it myself, the year I could still see them. Take it; I appear to be wearing another.

exethanter/6724f56ee3e7e871.text: Vosk? Is that his name this time? Pleasant fellow. Reads a great deal. He's been in my library for... I want to say a week. I said that last time too. It may have been a century.

exethanter/68c8f97a27da9a67.text: I'm sorting. Deciding what to forget on purpose, for once. It's quite pleasant. Did you want something?

exethanter/68ff43e4dbf5d0f5.text: NOT THE... oh, that's good. That's very clever. Nobody would ever look there. I didn't, for a hundred and twelve years.

exethanter/69925a40f1ff48a2.text: ...Yes. All right. A warden's whole job is to remember. I'll write it on the back of my hand, where I'll see it every time I reach for something.

exethanter/6c6cc6df2404d99e.text: It's in here somewhere. I'd look harder if I weren't so distracted. I've lost something, you see. Something with a lid.

exethanter/7662d589362f0a67.text: The word for the doors, at least, you shall have, written out large. And there's a note about the jackal somewhere. Ask me about him; I'll find it now. I feel much less distracted.

exethanter/7665abf90a0ef477.text: Thank you. ...Thank you for what? Never mind. I'm sure it was kind.

exethanter/77fe8d294cd66f06.text: Visitors! How unusual. We almost never get visitors. Have we met? You have the look of people I've met. Everyone does, lately.

exethanter/8394884a3ee1d039.text: "These are friends. Do not freeze them." Friends! Of course. I knew that. Sit, sit. What can I fail to remember for you today?

exethanter/89dfed95d05b6b32.text: Norganas? I don't... oh dear. Oh, dear. The eraser.

exethanter/8b5d1541108894a3.text: I think I've been waiting for that for a very long time. Thank you. I think. Would you go away now, please? Gently.

exethanter/8ce883556cb81fcf.text: Visitors! I feel as though I ought to be grateful to you for something. I am, whatever it was. Hello!

exethanter/8d5d74d116d5856f.text: Have you got it? Might I... could I have it back?

exethanter/8f18deb53f8d23f5.text: I write things down. That's what the notes are for. The difficulty is remembering to read them, and which ones are still true. One just says DUCK, underlined, and I have no idea at all.

exethanter/950bb7e23fe540f5.text: That's my hand. That's... yes. That's my hand.

exethanter/98aeb1df5b6e94ba.text: And the colossus won't let you out with it, you know. It was built for nothing else. Say the word to it on your way out, if you have the word.

exethanter/9cff5c27cc6f3052.text: There. Done. I think I'll sit down now. I think I'll sit down for a very long time.

exethanter/9db7cea31bb56661.text: It was very kind about it. It kept on taking. It's still taking. That's why everything goes, isn't it? It isn't age at all. It's interest.

exethanter/a0c11dba24eb2dc4.text: If the jackal is in my temple, he's waiting at the bottom, where it happened. And when he's gone, there's a rite. The last one we had. Find me after.

exethanter/a36c2917ea50392e.text: Yes. I remember remembering. The voices were so loud, those first years. I asked it to take the whispering out of my head. Only the whispering.

exethanter/a36eccbe075805bb.text: Oh, must we? I was enjoying the company. I can't remember the last time I enjoyed company.

exethanter/b2821931acac4286.text: Then this is the third time, and the third time is when one finally gets to know a person. Splendid.

exethanter/b416906da016c3bd.text: Do they? I'll write that down. I'll write it down this minute and pin it somewhere I'll see it.

exethanter/bc2240267692d782.text: The jackal's gone, and he left smiling. He's never left smiling before. What did you give him?

exethanter/bdbbfd8f331f1e0c.text: Oh! Living people. Hello! Don't be alarmed, I'm a lich. Was a lich. Am a lich; one doesn't really stop. Exethanter, Warden of the Amber, at your service, if I can remember what the service involves.

exethanter/bed5895133e2c113.text: Well. It's done; it never comes undone. Don't take another. They're like stairs: each one is only a small step down.

exethanter/c22bd5cefc9216d7.text: It's on the back of my hand, see? "He showed the prince the way down." I've read it nine times since you left. It doesn't get easier. It isn't supposed to.

exethanter/c477725ab8bb2a66.text: Here. Take the note. I won't be needing it.

exethanter/c5b8598334b79841.text: He was so polite. Young, angry, grieving something he hadn't lost yet. He wanted time. He said he had a war to finish, a woman to win, and a brother who would always be younger than him.

exethanter/c68565214c9c72a0.text: Still here? So am I. It's what I do.

exethanter/d3c156a0123d6c5b.text: Of course. Practical. We said that too, the first year. I'll just... sweep.

exethanter/d7c7bd2b69f77fff.text: It wants a warden, which I am, and a reason, which I think you've given me. Shall I?

exethanter/ddbb2a3dc30fec75.text: It's rather important. If anything happened to this body, the thing with the lid is how I'd come back. And I hid it so cleverly that now I can't find it.

exethanter/de708f57f1cfff1f.text: Was there a fight? There's always a fight down here, sooner or later. I come down afterward to sweep. Oh. Is that... was that a jackal?

exethanter/e044652ec648d9a0.text: The thing with the lid! You remembered. Did you find it? No? It'll be somewhere sensible. I'm a very sensible person. That's what worries me.

exethanter/e047e19625620b6d.text: Very well. I'll be... cooperative. That's the word, isn't it? You'll have the doors' word, and anything else I can find.

exethanter/e1a0da1362d1414f.text: Ask away! I'll answer the ones I recall. It won't take long.

exethanter/e612ad276a865279.text: I don't like him. I can't remember why. There's a note somewhere.

exethanter/e66fd829a0ee31c5.text: Thank you. Truly. I'd give you something, if I could remember what I own.

exethanter/eb093a453e6e3fde.text: There's a rite. The wardens' last one, the one we were meant to use if it ever came to this. It seals every sarcophagus at once. Nobody would ever hear them again. Nobody could ever bargain here again.

exethanter/f235cc05236ed7a1.text: Jackal? I don't recall a jackal. But I recall that I don't trust him, and that will have to do.

exethanter/fb0560f147812ea3.text: The trouble with forever is that the things you're guarding can talk.

exethanter/fc0d652f1e40c5ad.text: Ah. Yes. I see. I've held a few things over people myself, in my time. I just can't remember how it turned out for them.

ezmerelda/005d978c5ff939fa.text: Somebody has been in my wagon. Don't. Don't say anything. I know who's been up and down this shore this week, and it's a very short list.

ezmerelda/034d813733368223.text: And the children are going home. Good. That's a better day than this valley usually allows.

ezmerelda/0545627be7ab614b.text: Eva. Of course it's Eva. That old woman has been dealing me into other people's games since I was six.

ezmerelda/05f0a9ffbac3f1be.text: Four. The fourth is his handwriting.

ezmerelda/078ec7a045f3c2dd.text: Everyone does, at first. Ask Rudolph.

ezmerelda/0928fe3d145c3574.text: That's no monk. Look at his feet. He's standing a finger's breadth off the floor.

ezmerelda/0980f5cae2115f15.text: Kiril. Big, black, laughs with his mouth open?

ezmerelda/09fbced0f2f576c3.text: Feathers? Tell me there are feathers. No, don't. I'll see for myself. I'm leaving tonight.

ezmerelda/0c17a9dde2b25d5c.text: I've been taking them back two at a time ever since. Lately they've been carrying children up there, from the farms under Krezk. I'd go in after them, if Rudolph would let me into his armoury.

ezmerelda/0f1d986cc90c285b.text: The abbey. The locals call the man in charge an angel. Angels don't stitch, and somebody up there stitches a great deal. I've seen a sack carried in at night that was shaped like a woman.

ezmerelda/12fb2b58cfcfa3db.text: That sounded like you meant it, and nothing came off you in smoke. Good enough.

ezmerelda/13fd7fb3b44eaacf.text: And this. My second-best armour. It can look like a ball gown or a beggar's coat when you need it to, and it has turned more claws than I can count.

ezmerelda/151472af42bd7b94.text: In a taproom, pretending to be loud. I trained under that man for six years and never once heard him raise his voice. Did he do the lute? Please say he did the lute.

ezmerelda/173f4db7f71eec28.text: Kiril. Big, black, laughs with his mouth open? You left that one on top? With the children?

ezmerelda/18106db41217be4e.text: "If you are reading this, I am dead, or you are more stubborn than I hoped." I am more stubborn. I am always more stubborn. He knows that. He wrote it anyway.

ezmerelda/1b1cb32a7e3e4156.text: Stop there. Say something a vampire wouldn't say.

ezmerelda/25f5c13fb5193318.text: Back again. Has the tower spoken to you yet? It won't speak to me.

ezmerelda/2730342751aa7168.text: Then I'll tell him I wrung it out of you. He'll believe it. He knows me.

ezmerelda/2761dcaf96d0a6cd.text: He's in there. He came home. He's been in there the whole time, listening to me shout.

ezmerelda/2f6b2d7e9e7b70e3.text: A vampire would have said something about my eyes. Fine. Sit down before you fall in the lake.

ezmerelda/30db28a2aebd4cc9.text: A pack that leaves people alone. I'll believe it when I've watched it for a year.

ezmerelda/3653db5af7e8dd21.text: It won't know you. Go in for me. Find out where he's gone, and bring me anything with his handwriting on it.

ezmerelda/382d7df69e575f0c.text: Says someone who still has both feet.

ezmerelda/38a1dbb8e528e984.text: You're stitching a corpse a wedding for Strahd. I've hunted a lot of madmen. You're the calmest.

ezmerelda/390d69a7f25f7639.text: Rictavio. Rudolph is calling himself Rictavio. In a taproom.

ezmerelda/3d00f83234a550de.text: Ha. All right. A vampire would have said something charming. That was the least charming thing I've heard all month.

ezmerelda/3f14aee6bd0b0bdb.text: A werewolf in the hills above the lake, when I was young and quick and stupid. I kept the rest of me. Fair trade. The brace was Rudolph's work; it kicks harder than the old one did.

ezmerelda/3f9a6b0c775dd787.text: Then you should have stayed alive near me, so you could keep an eye on me. That was always the deal.

ezmerelda/45588df5ad8d1c63.text: Go carefully. If anything in these hills hums, growls or compliments you, shoot it.

ezmerelda/4795d83d09ae3cb0.text: You'd have done the same. You taught me.

ezmerelda/4904794cce3aad39.text: Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Of the Vistani, when they'll have me. I hunt the things that hunt people. I'm very good at it, as you can tell from all the bits of me that are left.

ezmerelda/4e1ffff193850cd4.text: Keep what you took. You'll need it. And then stay out of my way.

ezmerelda/508bc9c788225f28.text: He was always thorough about the wrong things.

ezmerelda/516ff1a8f3ec4c8f.text: A pack that leaves children alone. I'll believe it when I've watched it for a year.

ezmerelda/59055ddbddfab085.text: Peace. From him. I've heard monsters plan a great many things. That's the first time one's planned a honeymoon.

ezmerelda/5a849a10edf551c9.text: Wait. If he'd left Vallaki, where would he go to lick his wounds? Where would he go that I couldn't follow?

ezmerelda/5ccb31286cd7d955.text: Now go away. I have a wagon to hitch and an old man to shout at.

ezmerelda/652541fe80c5d360.text: Back. Good. I've counted the Belviews twice more and got two different numbers. Are we going in, or are you going to make me admire the view?

ezmerelda/656e5375ec9871b5.text: Nobody with fangs has ever asked to buy silver. Not twice, anyway. Sit.

ezmerelda/686aacd960666b3b.text: Then keep it. From everyone but me. I'm not everyone; I'm the reason he needs a secret.

ezmerelda/687eabe75e71df71.text: You're a terrible liar. He made you promise, didn't he. He always makes people promise.

ezmerelda/6b20f19af2c7698f.text: She would. Tell her I ate a whole sausage last week. Don't tell her it was the only thing I ate. Fine. Fine, you've got honest faces, and she sent you.

ezmerelda/6e1c969898073421.text: The cards said I'd find friends on this road. I told Eva the cards had never met me. Fine. I'll come. I go first through doors, I take the silver, and nobody calls me "girl".

ezmerelda/75ca530b83bcee6e.text: I hunt alone. Usually. But you've done more for me in a week than the whole valley has in a year. All right. Until it's done.

ezmerelda/76de3227db45cce7.text: He's making tea. He's terrible at tea. Don't tell him; he thinks it's the only thing he's good at besides killing.

ezmerelda/7ccbc137ce55c437.text: Eva's cards, I suppose. They've been dealing me into other people's games since I was six. Fine.

ezmerelda/824b39ba4a3920e6.text: ...Fine. Keep his secret. You're the first people in this valley who've kept anything. I'll keep looking. I'm good at looking.

ezmerelda/94341c516677c5de.text: I'm going to pretend I didn't watch that. I'm a very good pretender.

ezmerelda/98c25c3c1d89bd83.text: Then I'll keep waiting. I'm good at waiting. No, I'm not. I'm terrible at it.

ezmerelda/9c1e33ccad81a535.text: Two of Kiril's. Tell me I chose badly.

ezmerelda/9da1397c7c7d181d.text: Remind me to kill him. After I've hugged him.

ezmerelda/9e10bd1e2297dd18.text: That's the one who took my leg. Thank you. I wanted to do it myself. I find I don't mind that much, now.

ezmerelda/9e9954cc8d77e1fc.text: The ward. It knows my name; it also knows my temper. We had words. It won.

ezmerelda/9f055c96b4244552.text: I could go in on my own. I've decided I'm not that brave. Which, for me, is new.

ezmerelda/a5f5ea5d5dedfbc0.text: You let that happen. I'll remember who let that happen.

ezmerelda/a7de8a63d8bc7620.text: Whatever he's left lying about that isn't his notes. He'll be appalled. That's a reward in itself.

ezmerelda/a90f32d3aa31d0a3.text: That's done, then. I thought it would feel like more.

ezmerelda/ab0a88c7b6b50092.text: A pack dens two hours east along the ridge, in a cave above Lake Zarovich. One of them took my leg below the knee, years ago, when I was young and quick and stupid. Big, black, and laughing while it did it.

ezmerelda/ac8ff90a61ce558d.text: Ezmerelda d'Avenir. Vistani, when the wagons will have me. I hunt the things that hunt people. Right now I'm hunting one stubborn old man who taught me how, and who has locked me out of his house.

ezmerelda/b11d4fe5ad05701a.text: Save them for the walk. It's a long walk, and he wrote very long books.

ezmerelda/b3d382a77a4c0c2e.text: I came up here to kill you. I'm still not sure I shouldn't.

ezmerelda/b6261334bc43f3c7.text: I hunt alone. Usually. But this valley's too big for one pair of eyes, and too dark. All right. Until it's done.

ezmerelda/bde7766e517e6bc3.text: Did she say anything else? About me?

ezmerelda/bfe743087d832f03.text: Here. You've earned better than thanks. Silver-headed bolts, holy water and my last good potion. Don't waste them on anything that doesn't deserve them.

ezmerelda/c38e4b18966f6f9c.text: I go first through doors, I take the silver, and nobody calls me "girl".

ezmerelda/c8f1c5e95047c8d4.text: He's agreed. He just doesn't know it yet.

ezmerelda/c994115c9f7013d4.text: He made you promise. Of course he did. He's very good at making people promise things that keep them away from him.

ezmerelda/cb9a9f43bd6e8cdb.text: It's a terrible costume. You look like a chicken that's been to a wedding. You keyed your ward to me.

ezmerelda/ccf3991adf711fdb.text: If you see a man who looks too tired for the face he's wearing, tell me before you tell him.

ezmerelda/d199657c944d659c.text: Then I'll come and fetch it, dog.

ezmerelda/d9575e7830c3796b.text: Stopping's the one thing I'm bad at.

ezmerelda/dc1f752ddf5e8b09.text: An old man with burned hands and a head full of monsters. Rudolph van Richten. He taught me everything, then went off into the mists to die heroically without me. I'd like a word with him first.

ezmerelda/dd860914ad8bd38a.text: Yes, yes. I know. I love you too.

ezmerelda/e253dbe176179a95.text: You got the children out, at least. I'll give you that. I'll give you that and nothing else.

ezmerelda/e6abbeb081029ab1.text: He'll have got my good side wrong.

ezmerelda/e6f1bf3b7be9a48c.text: Then Rudolph's own ward threw me twenty feet into the lake. He wove my name into it. Mine. Nobody else's. Months of work, to keep out one person.

ezmerelda/e75d4b51dae5107a.text: Good. Say the name, mind your feet, and don't touch anything that hums. He likes things that hum.

ezmerelda/f0861d3aa596faa1.text: Of course I trapped it. There's a werewolf pack two hours up the ridge, and a castle that reads over everyone's shoulder. You found it. Good eyes. Most people find it with their faces.

ezmerelda/f3680ef16e2120ff.text: It's Rudolph's. Rudolph van Richten. An archmage built it centuries ago, and the old lock still opens to that wizard's name. I found the name under the moss in an hour: KHAZAN.

ezmerelda/f5269b9946f345d9.text: And he's left Vallaki already. Of course he has. He never stays where people might start to depend on him. It's his only real flaw, and he has it in bulk.

ezmerelda/febaa65324ff0e11.text: And there's a strongbox in his lantern room he never let me near. He called what was in it "the thing the cards keep moving". Eva would know what that means. So, I suspect, do you.

father_lucian/047836bf58b37326.text: The town should hear this, from my mouth, in the square. Not as a weapon. As a warning.

father_lucian/07ebd4816303a3a4.text: And Fiona will try to step into his shoes the moment they're empty. If there's proof of what she is, the town should hear it.

father_lucian/0a0047bc4cc8a4c8.text: Vargas has asked me to preach on gratitude at the next festival. I'm going to preach on mercy instead. We'll see whether he notices.

father_lucian/103f8f9617241e0f.text: Tonight, or any night now. If whoever took the saint means the church harm, they'll come after dark, when the doors are shut and I'm alone with a few candles. Come back at dusk, if you're willing, and keep the vigil with me.

father_lucian/10e6ba471659c478.text: You know your saints. Andral stood in a doorway here against the dead, the old stories say, until they stopped coming. Whatever was in him stayed in his bones. While they rest under the altar, this whole building is a doorway he's still standing in.

father_lucian/12c6f25c09169f58.text: Never mind. I can see in your faces it isn't a happy answer.

father_lucian/15d9f460376c71e8.text: Councillor work. I have spent the whole morning settling a dispute about a goat. It was wonderful. Nobody was put in the stocks.

father_lucian/1c3672d01ab5497b.text: Three nights ago, someone opened the saint's sarcophagus in the crypt and took his bones. St. Andral has lain under this altar for two hundred years. While he did, nothing dead could set foot in this church.

father_lucian/1ce928a234d8e52e.text: Take this; it's the church's last one. Read it over whatever holds her, and bring her to me afterwards. She'll need somewhere her mother can't tie a bow.

father_lucian/208003e5e38035b1.text: Then God bless you, and God help us. Urwin Martikov feels the same, and he's quieter about it than I am, which is wiser.

father_lucian/20b21256fba048fd.text: Nobody seize anybody! Please! These are your neighbours!

father_lucian/284a0a5fcb3c35d6.text: And Milivoj. I'll speak to him. Hunger is a sin, they tell me, but I don't think it was his.

father_lucian/28c774c0ed92aa5a.text: Take these, and my blessing with them. It's not much, but it's what the church has.

father_lucian/2be0603b9bada453.text: Doru, destroyed, and against his father's wishes. I understand why. I'll pray that Donavich comes to, one day.

father_lucian/325e5425925b4312.text: You let Doru out? Then Donavich has lost him twice. And something hungry is walking the roads with a priest's son's face.

father_lucian/44309e0ad5ac08a9.text: Welcome back to St. Andral's. It feels like a church again. I keep stopping in the doorway just to feel it.

father_lucian/4bb971e2edc08f27.text: Welcome to St. Andral's. Forgive the bare altar; we've had a loss. I'm Father Lucian. Are you hurt, or hungry, or in trouble? Those are the three reasons people come here now.

father_lucian/4f25adf455a9a75c.text: He let his son go. That's the hardest prayer there is. Thank you for being there to say amen.

father_lucian/5bd060b9ac3ad10d.text: Only two people knew where the bones lay and how the lid comes away: myself, and my gravedigger, Milivoj. I haven't accused him. I would very much like never to have to.

father_lucian/5f42736f3cfe6cb7.text: Not yet. Without the saint this is only a big wooden room, and he knows where it is. Try the Blue Water Inn. The Martikovs keep a very good door, and Urwin sleeps less than any man I know.

father_lucian/5fb7435c68e871ed.text: It was, my dear. Until three nights ago. I'd take you in tonight if I could promise you anything. I can't. Not until the saint is home.

father_lucian/67cac5fa0961f659.text: The poor souls in the lockup, too. Every festival he drags them out to make an example. I'd sleep better if there were nobody in there to drag.

father_lucian/692158fe10a48b15.text: Only stories. That it was carried against the castle once, and didn't come back. Stories are what we have instead of relics, these days.

father_lucian/791c57b31e5e9dbf.text: Fiona. I baptised her children. She sat in the third pew every holy day for twenty years. And she was writing to him the whole time.

father_lucian/7cfe918543b6283c.text: Whatever happens, they don't reach the altar. Not while I'm breathing.

father_lucian/7ddb4620e63d9f66.text: I can't work miracles of my own; I was never that kind of priest. But the church keeps scrolls for the days that need them, written by better men than me. I can read them. The church asks a gift in return, so it can buy more.

father_lucian/9070b6e184bb8b01.text: Vargas. It's over. Go home to Lydia. Nobody is going to hurt you.

father_lucian/90ef9c68f3dd95c4.text: Someone who wants this church to be ordinary ground again. And there's only one creature in this valley who'd want that, and he has many hands.

father_lucian/9255bb192854e93f.text: The sisters brew healing draughts, and I copy out prayers onto scrolls in the evenings, when the lamps are lit and the town is quiet. What we sell keeps the roof on. What the roof keeps out, you know as well as I do.

father_lucian/92a2a1ee87b21163.text: Welcome home. Welcome home, old man.

father_lucian/adc24e3c82584bd4.text: No. No, Vargas. Not today, and not again.

father_lucian/ade4aa512ac73712.text: Take her to the lockup. Gently. Lock it well.

father_lucian/b5a5eb18d488f6be.text: Then go with God, my dear. The door is open if you ever need it.

father_lucian/bc3b336d09c34438.text: My dear, this is holy ground again. You may stay as long as you like. Nothing dead comes through those doors now, and nothing living will while I'm here.

father_lucian/c6cc9c30d58a0655.text: Stay near me, if you would. When Vargas is frightened, he shouts. When he shouts, Izek moves. I would like someone between Izek and the crowd.

father_lucian/c8bc7d9f1ce0d22f.text: You held. All night, you held. I've lit a candle for each of you, and one for the windows, which did not.

father_lucian/cb5228f48dba4d2b.text: Vargas loses his temper when the sun won't burn. It rains, it always rains. When he does, he'll want someone punished, and Izek will want to do it. Stand near me. If someone has to be between Izek and the crowd, I'd rather it were people who can hit back.

father_lucian/d5bbdee6c7b26c54.text: You've come from the village of Barovia? Then you've met Donavich. We were novices together. How is he?

father_lucian/d94258eceee88b19.text: I won't ask who took them. I find I don't want to know. I've decided that's a mercy, and not cowardice.

father_lucian/d9489a1e34dc2a96.text: Thank you. I mean it more than I can say without sounding like a sermon. Start with Milivoj, if you must. He digs in the churchyard most days. Be gentle with him. He has three young ones at home and no parents for them.

father_lucian/dc10d4663cb183da.text: Go with God, and come back to us. People keep forgetting that second part.

father_lucian/dcfbe84f2959fea6.text: Stella. Poor child. I married her parents. I baptised her. I've prayed outside that door.

father_lucian/e153a81dabf22c43.text: You've come to church. Good. I've been preaching to Lydia and Victor and a great many empty pews. Lady Wachter's men sit at the back and take notes.

father_lucian/e22c1815631e903c.text: And you, my friends, if you'll stay a while. There's a bed at the church and a seat on any bench in this town.

father_lucian/e8ac433a31433c86.text: He was a holy man, and he died here, and his bones kept the dead away. That's all most of us know. It was always enough.

father_lucian/e938e65444f20298.text: Blessed this morning. Throw it, don't drink it, and don't miss.

father_lucian/f5bf8b78908b57ab.text: Still locked under the church, still screaming. And Donavich still feeding him. God help them both.

father_lucian/f650fff6e21d2107.text: No. It's a hope. I'm a priest in Barovia; hope is the only tool they let me keep.

father_lucian/fab8f5eb2da5c6b2.text: Vargas is a frightened child with a whip. Fiona is a patient woman with a much worse master. If you're asking me to choose between them, I won't. I'll choose the people in the pews.

fen_burley/04fa9d5ffd2c624c.text: Get me out, if you can. Out of the chains, anyway. What's in me doesn't come out with a key.

fen_burley/17723c0b30b16efd.text: Still here, lass. Still me. Mostly.

fen_burley/1c7b9a5045eaa4aa.text: Aye. Well. You smell like a town.

fen_burley/2ab363af2fe5ebd3.text: Some nights it nearly does, lass. I'll not lie to you. Some nights I'm more of it than me.

fen_burley/339a5f3854d87f4a.text: The big one keeps the key. Or Emil knows. Ask Emil.

fen_burley/462a32fca921e193.text: Or, if the moon's close and you can't do better, do the other thing. Quick, the way I taught you with the hares. I'd rather that than wake up with you in my mouth.

fen_burley/47e72d0141396ee0.text: Wanted me to track bairns. Out of farmhouses. I said no. So I hang here till the moon changes my mind.

fen_burley/48062739896bcfdc.text: Wolf came out of the fog. Followed it in. Its brothers were waiting. They bit me and brought me home like a sack of meal, because the big one wanted the best tracker in two worlds running with his pack.

fen_burley/4e5f0d5a8e004f61.text: Don't follow my blazes this time. Make your own.

fen_burley/52168524c44881c6.text: I'll go down to Krezk. They've walls there, but you can climb them, and they keep goats. I'll wait. You come and find me after. You're good at that.

fen_burley/665f3b65450fc30a.text: Aye. Took me a week. Wanted it to be the right one.

fen_burley/706f2987ed9d6725.text: Aye. I know. I'm only telling you it's allowed.

fen_burley/a5bc3604622590b6.text: Leave it. Find the key, lass.

fen_burley/bf0de5f04605192b.text: Aye. Mind the big one. He grins before he bites.

fen_burley/d4a9068611182184.text: Don't look at me like that, lass. I'm not coming out of this. Not all the way. But I'll not hunt bairns, and I'll not hunt you, and the high woods are wide.

fen_burley/f571e83ef2b5d369.text: And on the full moon I'm the best tracker in two worlds with teeth. No.

gertruda/0247ee63cf822a9e.text: Mother wants me to learn the woods. Just the edges, by day. I went as far as the well yesterday. It was wonderful. It was only a well.

gertruda/0712c0d323c05ccd.text: She said that? She isn't angry? All three locks. She'd never. She must have been so frightened.

gertruda/239f17d2d09bce7f.text: You came back! I hoped you would. Nobody here talks, not properly. Rahadin only counts things.

gertruda/350c2fed0bc712cd.text: I want to go home. I want to go home, and I don't know the way. It was dark in the carriage.

gertruda/367268fff6785f5b.text: I'm not... I hum. Mother says I hum when I'm frightened. I've been humming since the carriage.

gertruda/3af478d781bfb3db.text: He wasn't angry. He said I'd been frightened, and that it was natural. He said everyone is frightened before a wedding.

gertruda/3d40f288653b66de.text: An account. In a book. Like a horse. Like buying a horse.

gertruda/3e2f70611c7b0523.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry, I'm sorry.

gertruda/3f399a0251d3ab63.text: The lady downstairs, at the window? She was in this room? These were...

gertruda/4797ae7f657fc190.text: He sang under my window. Old songs, the ones Mother never let me hear. Then a black carriage came with nobody driving it, and the door opened by itself, just like in the stories.

gertruda/4b754e5084787d8e.text: Oh! You're guests too? Isn't it wonderful? I never saw a room this big. I never saw a room I wasn't locked into.

gertruda/5f75033334bc224e.text: He says I'm to be a lady. He says soon.

gertruda/67c44cbd6952accc.text: You're jealous. Everyone is jealous of the girl in the story. I'm going to tell him what you said!

gertruda/795636d5b805622a.text: I'll be quiet. I'm good at quiet. I've had practice.

gertruda/8e74e2481a8a47dd.text: Why did I... I don't even like blue.

gertruda/91c9ee358937dc66.text: I want to go home. I'm allowed to want that. Aren't I?

gertruda/ad30859572a2f87d.text: Gertruda. From the village, the house with the shutters; maybe you passed it. My mother is careful. Very careful. I'd never been out at night before. I'd never been out.

gertruda/b0accbba3398d89d.text: My mother is going to be angry too. I don't mind. I want her to be.

gertruda/ba5a419343a0c699.text: He did say I was the prettiest one yet. Yet. I didn't think about that word.

gertruda/c1fbba8a32f7607c.text: You'll come back? Yes. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting.

gertruda/d37f95c8096992b0.text: Oh. Yes. Of course. I'll go up.

ghakis_doina/7c1e34d3214e3722.text: You killed them. You actually did. Petrache, look.

ghakis_doina/a037e5c52c16e846.text: You're going in to it, aren't you. (She looks at your faces.) Then we'll go down slowly and tell the soldiers at the pass you were here, so somebody knows.

ghakis_doina/ce83c0860b86b8fb.text: We burn charcoal below Krezk. We owed the castle a tithe we couldn't pay, so the castle took it in us. They said we were going up the mountain to keep something warm.

ghakis_petrache/2c6f8f3fec84a5bb.text: And there's salt. Sacks of grey salt, for the meat. "Keeps her slow," he said. Her. Whatever it is, it's a her.

ghakis_petrache/864d00200f524aa5.text: Keep it fed, he meant. It breathes in there. All night, through the rock, like a forge's bellows.

ghakis_petrache/d852e0aec3ceec30.text: Not much to us. To each other, plenty. One of them said "open the sluice before you go down, or you'll cook like Andrei did." The other said Andrei was an idiot. They both laughed.

godrick_pendlebrook/0108621bb7375c90.text: I'm scared of something. Not monsters. Monsters are easy; you hit them.

godrick_pendlebrook/021ff505f3ffbd8b.text: And then at the very end he says, "Kneel, lad," and he can't lift the sword, so he picks up the ladle off his soup tray and does it with that. And then he says, "Now take the sword to the Order and have them do it proper." And then he died.

godrick_pendlebrook/037eff9bcfdf2e6b.text: Hello again, little lady! You're much drier than last time. Well done.

godrick_pendlebrook/04e9f03f7ec7afa5.text: He rode for help, my lord. The dragon sent him. Sir Godfrey wrote it on his wall four hundred years ago, so he'd remember. He wrote that you'd say otherwise.

godrick_pendlebrook/05123c4c97774a70.text: Can I tell you something? You won't laugh? You can laugh a bit. Not a lot.

godrick_pendlebrook/0515f564f5539806.text: You'll be wondering about the ladle.

godrick_pendlebrook/05c5338c77cea073.text: I know. I'd stand a watch with them anyway, and be proud to.

godrick_pendlebrook/062744b993b2b4ae.text: My master died before my last lesson. I asked him what it was and he said it was in a letter I'm not allowed to read. I make jokes all day so nobody notices I'm not finished.

godrick_pendlebrook/06f4109ae1ac674a.text: K. N. I. G. H. T. Knight. ...I read that. That was me reading.

godrick_pendlebrook/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

godrick_pendlebrook/0bbf805abaf1ba13.text: ...Yes. Yes! Is this, are we... yes. Right then. Yes.

godrick_pendlebrook/0dd2f8470901bbe6.text: Good for something! That's the nicest thing anyone's said about me in this whole valley.

godrick_pendlebrook/0f1570fbe40416dd.text: Maybe he's keeping it for a rainy day.

godrick_pendlebrook/0f8bc879a6e7be5d.text: The Lesser, they call him. I was the youngest of six. I know that name, even when nobody says it.

godrick_pendlebrook/123873c7d5351aa3.text: You told us she was brave and mistaken. She wasn't mistaken. She knew what he was, and she went anyway.

godrick_pendlebrook/1282f2af88c55522.text: I'm also tall. ...That was a joke. I make jokes now. Wren's a bad influence.

godrick_pendlebrook/14106a5ae6dc1ba1.text: Right then! Back to the stairs, everyone past me. I'll be the door. Go!

godrick_pendlebrook/14c3ecbc02b33a53.text: None of it was your fault. Not one bit. You remember that part too.

godrick_pendlebrook/152d71bf3269304c.text: Then we walk soft. And we walk together.

godrick_pendlebrook/1831dc0979667636.text: Sir Pellam said there'd be flowers. There weren't any flowers. This was better than flowers.

godrick_pendlebrook/1914fa8db7cd5520.text: Right then! I'll carry it. It'll be heavy, a dragon's head.

godrick_pendlebrook/1941b839e41bc9d5.text: What's it say at the bottom? My eyes are tired.

godrick_pendlebrook/1aa0a4745cbb31c1.text: Right. Read it. I can do that. I'll read it tonight. I'll read it tomorrow. I'll definitely read it.

godrick_pendlebrook/1ae0e372ec8142f5.text: He's shorter than me. Everyone is. But he talks like he's taller. How does he do that?

godrick_pendlebrook/1bf64c6472c83b37.text: Maybe. You're cleverer than me; maybe you can see a way it had to be. I can't. I'll keep looking for it.

godrick_pendlebrook/1cb95fcff4220362.text: Both of them, Thistle. Here, have my hat. It'll come down past your nose, but it's warm.

godrick_pendlebrook/1ce2f799d766c5be.text: I've never said that out loud. It sounds worse out loud.

godrick_pendlebrook/1dd1ff2f41301ff4.text: Then I'll carry it. I've carried it this far.

godrick_pendlebrook/20440e69962c5137.text: Two lads went up that hill. One came home. And the old man can't forgive the one who did.

godrick_pendlebrook/20c8aa3d64cdf93d.text: Maybe he's being polite. Sir Pellam always said, assume good manners until you're bitten.

godrick_pendlebrook/210f2eb25aa98496.text: You're not walking it alone, Mirela. Ana can ride on my shoulders. Everybody else, single file behind me.

godrick_pendlebrook/21dd394c752e6cae.text: She didn't. She's sad, and she thinks sad means guilty. Somebody should keep telling her it doesn't.

godrick_pendlebrook/220c47cc75acbee8.text: We let one of us take a gift from a thing in a box. A devil's gift. Kip's told us what those cost.

godrick_pendlebrook/23507c528a53af9f.text: "I told him fly." The lad sent his brother away and stayed to face them. Sir Pellam would call that a knight's death.

godrick_pendlebrook/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

godrick_pendlebrook/24798854f0786c29.text: I'm never going to get tired of that. You'll get tired first. I promise you'll get tired first.

godrick_pendlebrook/27e29e09466a8230.text: Bells don't ring underwater. Do they? Is that a riddle? I'm bad at riddles.

godrick_pendlebrook/2857c56ef52bc6ce.text: And now there's an Order, and they'll have books, and oaths written down, and I'll stand there like a great big post.

godrick_pendlebrook/293ed4a3febb70b3.text: You've gone quiet, Thistle. You're never quiet.

godrick_pendlebrook/29554ad720bb752e.text: I just did, madam. Sorry. Step away, please.

godrick_pendlebrook/29f45e5be1dd0b5b.text: That lady's in every room. Over the fire, in the hall, by his bed. Who is she?

godrick_pendlebrook/2c742587c1964635.text: You read his letter out nicely. We should send it on to his college. Somebody there's waiting.

godrick_pendlebrook/2e917bcfc201dde2.text: Four hundred years. Master Sorrel always did take his time with the post.

godrick_pendlebrook/2f06c048ceb7c943.text: Your da said no so you'd not have to. You said yes so he'd not have to. That's a family, that.

godrick_pendlebrook/31fc247339eb5051.text: Right. So we break the heart. Then we hit him. Then it hurts. Is that it?

godrick_pendlebrook/353a3303d4d112f6.text: Things taken from the dead should go back to their families.

godrick_pendlebrook/35830421e27dac29.text: You're not large. You're loud. Sir Pellam was large. No.

godrick_pendlebrook/367dc4e04c2a8218.text: Not today, my lord, if it's all the same to you.

godrick_pendlebrook/36b5618504b819b8.text: Can I say something? I'm no good at hard things, so I'll say it plain and then I'll stop.

godrick_pendlebrook/373a75c74aec8a9f.text: They were waiting for somebody to come. Somebody came. It's us. We're late, but we came.

godrick_pendlebrook/375990e5e8588ad3.text: Shield the sleeper and the stranger. Lift the fallen. I've been riding with people who don't, lately, and standing by while it's done. I can't kneel and say those words with that on me.

godrick_pendlebrook/375a750239ae2107.text: I'm not slowing down. I'm savouring. Sir Pellam said a knight savours.

godrick_pendlebrook/389f8720ecc93abb.text: The lad didn't watch. Good. I watched for him. Better I keep that than him.

godrick_pendlebrook/3a066bcc41e85bbb.text: I like towns. Bit. Beds. The little cakes. People singing in the big room at the inn. And I don't fit in them, and I don't fit in the woods any more either. I don't fit anywhere.

godrick_pendlebrook/3acd16867a766dab.text: Next time he comes, I'll fight him. Is he the fighting sort? He looked like the fighting sort. Thin ones are.

godrick_pendlebrook/3b0041596f14ee07.text: A bully in a good coat, then. Sir Pellam always said they fall over like anybody else.

godrick_pendlebrook/3f301a1a755004a0.text: I won't. I'll just walk on this side of you. The windy side.

godrick_pendlebrook/3f8467ad6d1167a1.text: I'll pray with you tomorrow, if you like. I don't know any of the words. I'll hum.

godrick_pendlebrook/3fc431f1a5ddcab2.text: Your feet are never tired. You walked forty miles yesterday and climbed a tower for fun.

godrick_pendlebrook/3fed41e8e2b03e7c.text: He gives her extra bread so she won't be ready yet. That's kind. And it's horrible. I can't make it be just one.

godrick_pendlebrook/40a3b54721e0f022.text: Sir Pellam's grandad didn't run. Sir Pellam carried that his whole life. He never even knew he didn't have to.

godrick_pendlebrook/413b7686b389a163.text: ...Right. Yes. You're cleverer than me about these things. Friends is good. Friends is the best thing I've got.

godrick_pendlebrook/41e12a363d6a29d7.text: I'll... my eyes are tired too, my lord. Somebody else'd do it better. You do the voices.

godrick_pendlebrook/4283308d82b16e69.text: We left one of ours on a table in the dark. I'll not forget it. I don't want to.

godrick_pendlebrook/437bd381954ee36d.text: No, madam. I'm sorry. He didn't.

godrick_pendlebrook/4433f67e1396bb1e.text: Ha! Now you're just being kind. ...Keep being kind. I like it.

godrick_pendlebrook/445cb7297cc84e39.text: Two more for the party, then. Welcome, both of you. Hold on tight; I'm very tall.

godrick_pendlebrook/448312b28b88a9ad.text: Right then. We don't fight three hags. We fight one hag, three times.

godrick_pendlebrook/44ffd6f856f377f2.text: Sir Pellam died before he'd finished with me, too. I think they leave us to finish ourselves.

godrick_pendlebrook/45598eff57b2ae42.text: Right. Then we stop at the windmill on the way. And we don't knock.

godrick_pendlebrook/45826291da557539.text: Sorry. I had a whole speech. It's gone. Thank you, my lord. Thank you.

godrick_pendlebrook/45937a77f90aaf74.text: We'll bring it back to you, my lady, if there's any way at all. I swear it.

godrick_pendlebrook/45cdb9bd736a264f.text: My dad sent the devil away from our gate. Told him we'd manage. I went after him down the lane and signed behind Dad's back. I came home and said the orchard came back on its own. He went to temple and gave thanks for it. I've been lying to him for two years.

godrick_pendlebrook/45d2da253af31a9c.text: I'd rather cook than cast. I always would. I learned magic so people would sit with me, and I'm good at it, and I'd still rather be in a kitchen. That's a terrible thing for a wizard to say.

godrick_pendlebrook/45e6c424a573496e.text: He isn't here. I know. That is what faith is for. You need none; you are right here. That is how I know you are not him.

godrick_pendlebrook/46044378ddebf5d0.text: No ally? That's all right. We've got us. Us is loads.

godrick_pendlebrook/474702a862deb12d.text: Them, my lord. All of them. They're the ones I won't leave behind.

godrick_pendlebrook/475ec0e428b4edcf.text: Ha! They didn't like that! They remember the dawn, then. Good.

godrick_pendlebrook/4793950faa4f6277.text: Evening, my lady. ...I've just bowed to a painting. But that's Ireena's face. That's her exactly.

godrick_pendlebrook/49d7efffdcad47af.text: Thank you for not making a thing of it. That's a kindness. I'm keeping a list of kindnesses. Well. Somebody else is writing it down.

godrick_pendlebrook/4a78edf43e691a85.text: I'll fight beside you. I'll not leave you. But when it comes to the Order and the oath, I can't kneel and say those words with this on me.

godrick_pendlebrook/4b339e8ed500cb4c.text: We told Mary we'd look. So we look. Every house, every road.

godrick_pendlebrook/4c24d5ae98d1e7ee.text: That was the left one. The right one's been feeling left out.

godrick_pendlebrook/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

godrick_pendlebrook/4c93e8e98a6fccff.text: Can I tell you something daft? Back home I was the youngest of six. The others were clever, or quick, or good with money, and I was large. That was my whole job. Being large, and carrying things.

godrick_pendlebrook/4cd75c07371d623b.text: I thought we were doing quite well.

godrick_pendlebrook/4d90036dabba55b5.text: Myself. Right. I can do that. I'm very good at being myself. It's the only thing I've had much practice at.

godrick_pendlebrook/4debf9d1137b1bcc.text: If the devil comes for you, I'll fight him. That's three times I've offered now.

godrick_pendlebrook/4e44b44dafb6848f.text: Right then. That's done. Now there's only the vampire.

godrick_pendlebrook/4eeabd8a1cee4e7f.text: I can do that. I'm good at saying when things are wrong. I'm loud. It's one of my gifts.

godrick_pendlebrook/501b592feabf8859.text: Sir Pellam went to three wars. He said they all end the same way: somebody digging.

godrick_pendlebrook/5020a66e3255aefd.text: Everybody here? Shout if you're not. ...Right. Nobody's shouted. Good.

godrick_pendlebrook/54605c031c672f8f.text: They didn't, though! Look. Boots. Both of them.

godrick_pendlebrook/54c647843cb6b969.text: You lot ask me what I think. In a fight, in a town. You wait for the answer, even when it's slow coming. Nobody's waited for my answer before.

godrick_pendlebrook/54c708a0f2632042.text: Something that forgot what it was for. Sir Pellam prayed for everything he ever had to kill. I'll pray for this one.

godrick_pendlebrook/55aa50566030e01e.text: Right then. Bed. Big day tomorrow. All the days are big here. Have you noticed? It's very tiring.

godrick_pendlebrook/5616f7139464fbc5.text: Then let's give them something good to report. I'll wave.

godrick_pendlebrook/5a9f6040fe99fc96.text: Sir Pellam knighted me with it. On his deathbed. In an inn called the Wheatsheaf, which did a very good mutton soup, hence the ladle.

godrick_pendlebrook/5abb6fb802da075d.text: I've been thinking about your devil, Kip.

godrick_pendlebrook/5e5f6294569cdc9a.text: We'll find him, Thistle. That's what the feather means now. That we're coming.

godrick_pendlebrook/5f3dbe6b6a971aff.text: ...You would, wouldn't you. I can tell. I'm good at telling. It's the one clever thing I've got.

godrick_pendlebrook/61189baeb0a4a295.text: Every week? Oh, that's splendid! Is there cake every week?

godrick_pendlebrook/619db972fcdd89ff.text: So we just need the vampire to write his name on something. That's easy! People write their names on things all the time. I can do it now. Nearly.

godrick_pendlebrook/62809f3f9a74a72d.text: I can't read. Not properly. My name, and "ale", and "danger", because Sir Pellam said those were the three a knight needs. The rest of it swims about.

godrick_pendlebrook/62ba231ba3089bd7.text: Then I'll take the door off its hinges. No hinges, no lock. Just a plank.

godrick_pendlebrook/63191a4ecb0228c6.text: Maybe you're just very good at stairs, my lady. Some people are.

godrick_pendlebrook/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

godrick_pendlebrook/6a22902138aa59df.text: Commander. My lord. I've brought Sir Aldric Ashgrove's sword home to the Order, and I'd be honoured to be knighted with it. Properly. There was a ladle before, but.

godrick_pendlebrook/6fbc6702c76e9e5d.text: Tonight? Right now? I've got the page here. I've been holding it for an hour hoping it'd give in.

godrick_pendlebrook/700d09d71f25b44c.text: He'd like you. He'd argue with every one of you, and then he'd like you. That's how you knew he liked you; he argued.

godrick_pendlebrook/70c97c87dd5783b9.text: I noticed. I'll ask about it at the house. Politely.

godrick_pendlebrook/710bd57185d1beab.text: He looked sad, though. Not hurt. Sad. Like we'd broken the last thing he had.

godrick_pendlebrook/736147a1c7912b04.text: My lady. I'll keep the lantern lit every night. I'm the tallest, so it'll light more.

godrick_pendlebrook/741f9c9d75089489.text: We told a little girl her mother sold her. I keep thinking we ought to have lied.

godrick_pendlebrook/749ad33145e91a88.text: I left my sword in the grass. A knight doesn't leave his sword. A knight doesn't kneel to... I knelt.

godrick_pendlebrook/75d91cbe61ccbf5e.text: I'm frightened of the dark. I have been since I was small. A priestess of the dawn, and I sleep with a light on, and tell everyone it's devotion. And I've come to the darkest place in the world.

godrick_pendlebrook/771cfbea72a0dd93.text: Knights of the Silver Dragon! The real Order. I've carried Sir Aldric's sword all this way, Wren, and there they were.

godrick_pendlebrook/7abee0fbc5ea050e.text: What if I challenged him? Honourably. To single combat. Devils must have honour. They've got contracts.

godrick_pendlebrook/7afcd2468adc1afc.text: I'm going to say this once, and then I'll carry on, because I said I would.

godrick_pendlebrook/7c432acb03b8bb15.text: Sorry, my lady. I'll do it again.

godrick_pendlebrook/7d0036df32f632b0.text: No. I won't stand here for that. Sir Pellam wouldn't have, and I won't.

godrick_pendlebrook/7e7690257c64a380.text: Would you? I'd like that. I'd like that very much.

godrick_pendlebrook/7f39a73d9d490439.text: Oh. Oh, that's the sun. I'd forgotten it was that colour.

godrick_pendlebrook/7f5801b1887ceb60.text: I'm not saying I'm better than anybody. I'm not clever enough to be sure what's right. But I'm sure about some things, and that's one of them.

godrick_pendlebrook/80ff31669950fb6f.text: Liriel, would you bless us? Thistle and me. Together, I mean. Not like the boots.

godrick_pendlebrook/8163a21908def44b.text: He wanted his father to know. Then his father will know. I swear it.

godrick_pendlebrook/81fd62ff3066c23d.text: I do, though. That's the thing about an oath. I swore I'd see this through. I never swore I'd like how.

godrick_pendlebrook/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

godrick_pendlebrook/85a907a5011d212a.text: Oh, we don't mind wolves, sir. Thank you kindly.

godrick_pendlebrook/861377174da00d79.text: It's daft. I know it's daft. Next time he calls me, he can have the sword too, and see how he likes the end of it.

godrick_pendlebrook/87dd41cf319691ef.text: We sent a frightened girl back up the stairs to him. I promised her mother. I promised.

godrick_pendlebrook/8869e025097d2e7c.text: Whatever's up at that castle, I'm not afraid of it. I never was, much; I'm not clever enough. But now I've got a better reason. I've got you lot to walk back down with.

godrick_pendlebrook/88b157c6ddf7f40c.text: Right then. Bed. That's going on the list of kindnesses. I'll write it down myself. I can do that now. Badly.

godrick_pendlebrook/891bb1cca841eddf.text: My lady. Sir Godrick Pendlebrook, at your service. Fear not.

godrick_pendlebrook/892da1ecfe25a492.text: Liriel, would you bless my boots? They've been through a lot.

godrick_pendlebrook/89c4ee80eab68b7f.text: That's what I think too, most days. Then I think, it's a ladle. Then I think, it was his ladle. Round and round.

godrick_pendlebrook/8a052db3295be704.text: Right. Yes. Find the Order, hand over the sword, kneel. Simple. I'm good at simple.

godrick_pendlebrook/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

godrick_pendlebrook/8c67e4a1494d9bc5.text: A challenge! Yes. Arm-wrestling. Loser has to say something nice. I'll lose on purpose. No. She'd smell it. I'll lose properly.

godrick_pendlebrook/8f2905b5fbb7d3d9.text: We've met him. He's kind, madam. He means every bit of it. That's what frightened me.

godrick_pendlebrook/8f37fe2414f29168.text: Wolves on two legs, a den in the hills, and a mother they pray to. That's not a pack. That's a parish.

godrick_pendlebrook/9065f58820907dbb.text: Brilliant. I could do that. I can point.

godrick_pendlebrook/9077a07f9c91cb35.text: I keep thinking, I should hang it up somewhere. Over a fireplace. That's what knights do with things. But I haven't got a fireplace. I've got a log.

godrick_pendlebrook/9201a9685d641c9d.text: He didn't say that. I just made it up. I think it's true, though.

godrick_pendlebrook/924351754ac2e0f0.text: Right then. Bed. That's going on the list of kindnesses. Somebody'll have to write it down for me.

godrick_pendlebrook/930e1343cf7b0fba.text: I've been thinking what Sir Pellam would make of you lot. He was very particular about company. He sent a bishop away once for slurping.

godrick_pendlebrook/954513ab194a262f.text: I came here to be a knight. A proper one. And I've been standing next to things a knight doesn't stand next to.

godrick_pendlebrook/959c9e0e46ea747b.text: Out in the scrap barrel! Clever girl. When she tells it in Vallaki, she'll leave the barrel out.

godrick_pendlebrook/980adfb7cb12a0cf.text: I think that was a letter. From a bird. Do we write back?

godrick_pendlebrook/98b72f5716d11c67.text: Sir Pellam said a knight's only as good as the people he won't leave behind. Lately I keep looking back, and I keep seeing people we left.

godrick_pendlebrook/990a2c27f7583873.text: We did that this morning. You won.

godrick_pendlebrook/9af5d2abe4a6b294.text: That's a long time to be dressed for nowhere.

godrick_pendlebrook/9b384445df064b09.text: You've gone quiet, Thistle. You're never quiet. It's like the sea going quiet.

godrick_pendlebrook/9c1b169c6c78d14c.text: We gave him our word. And now we've broken it. I don't like that, madam. Not one bit.

godrick_pendlebrook/9d4e292f7fbe51bf.text: Only it's Thistle. She'd eat the flowers. She'd laugh at the poem, and then she'd bite me for the respectful distance. And I don't know what day it is.

godrick_pendlebrook/9e00ac58790a85ca.text: A wall that big, and they still look at every face on the road. Fair enough. I'd look at us twice.

godrick_pendlebrook/9f9d6452b5a96ec1.text: I'm scared people only like me because I'm big and I smile a lot. Like a good dog. And if I stopped smiling, or got hurt and couldn't carry things, they'd find somebody else to like.

godrick_pendlebrook/a065afc7234b6395.text: I don't know what you mean. It's a very important buckle.

godrick_pendlebrook/a06689f7c867c7a4.text: A cellar. A mountain. Right. I'll take notes. I'm writing this down. Somebody hold my skillet.

godrick_pendlebrook/a104da6560b198e7.text: A sword made of daylight. Now that's a proper knight's sword. Right. Good. I understand swords.

godrick_pendlebrook/a1583830a322c9ca.text: I'll come with you. I'm good at standing quiet in doorways.

godrick_pendlebrook/a1a7c90bc7b0e61d.text: Right. We start again tomorrow. Everybody gets to start again tomorrow. That's what tomorrow's for.

godrick_pendlebrook/a4d4a642ae2366b8.text: A spoon! I meant a spoon. I definitely meant a spoon the whole time.

godrick_pendlebrook/a6e9b768f0813a7a.text: Then we find it. Leave it to me.

godrick_pendlebrook/a79d0a05bec0cb43.text: Thistle. You belong with us. That's a somewhere. It's got a cook and everything.

godrick_pendlebrook/a892717493c17735.text: Toma waved at me. I waved back, a big one. He sat down in the mud, laughing.

godrick_pendlebrook/a9c57d75ade735a5.text: Children. We walked away from children in a cage. I keep hearing it.

godrick_pendlebrook/aa3717c675756663.text: I can't read. Not proper. My name, and "ale", and "danger". Every letter we've had, I've said my eyes were tired and given it to someone else. My eyes are fine. I'm just slow.

godrick_pendlebrook/aadf2baedd9beef7.text: Walter was the nurse's baby. Hers and the master's. That's what the lady knew. Isn't it.

godrick_pendlebrook/acbe32ee4653d3ad.text: So that's the lord of this place. He looks like a bully in a good coat.

godrick_pendlebrook/ad6fb43460ac6bd1.text: It's quite long. Sir Pellam added bits.

godrick_pendlebrook/afb48038f6640843.text: Here. Rat. You have it. You'll use it right. Sir Pellam liked soup more than he liked honour, he told me once, and he liked honour more than anyone I ever met.

godrick_pendlebrook/b1c55d9bc2e0955c.text: There's nothing wrong with a house cat. House cats are brilliant. They live in houses AND they can kill things.

godrick_pendlebrook/b1cfff2371c18c27.text: He swore he'd go to the castle. On his mother. A lad doesn't lie on his mother.

godrick_pendlebrook/b20552dc959c3f40.text: She answered me sideways about the Order. Seers do that, don't they?

godrick_pendlebrook/b20a9a6407887050.text: I'd still like to sit at that table with them. Just once. Is that daft?

godrick_pendlebrook/b3b8466d224e0b8d.text: My lady, stand by me. Closer than that. He'll have to go round me, and I'm a long way round.

godrick_pendlebrook/b3bd647e97bf4259.text: Did one of them just wink at me? I winked back. Was that right?

godrick_pendlebrook/b49d97c0265c3810.text: Then somebody ought to tell him. The castle man. He drowned a whole village over a lie. That's not fair, even to him.

godrick_pendlebrook/b4b294e6762e7a41.text: We were polite to him. Sir Pellam always said be polite to a man before you hit him.

godrick_pendlebrook/b691f88982df54f0.text: Right then. That's all I wanted. Well, no. I wanted it not to have happened. But that's the next best thing.

godrick_pendlebrook/b6eb4ac737c5e2fc.text: Right then. That's settled. I'll tell Mum. She'll cry. She cries at everything; it's where I get it.

godrick_pendlebrook/b73d5059ae1fe60b.text: Sorry's a start. Sir Pellam said sorry's the door and not the house. We'll see about the house.

godrick_pendlebrook/b7488c5ae70ac5ed.text: I asked after the Order, and she answered in a riddle. I'm bad at riddles. Was that a yes?

godrick_pendlebrook/b8254e1156035a20.text: I'll carry them. Gently. They'll not feel a single bump, I promise.

godrick_pendlebrook/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.

godrick_pendlebrook/b96017d13d449ed4.text: There, there. It's a good farm, Rat. Look at it. That's a lot of grapes.

godrick_pendlebrook/ba80665148d220ae.text: Angry first, then tidy after. I've met that sort. They smile at you in church.

godrick_pendlebrook/bc55c12126fc8778.text: Smiling! I can do that. Look. I'm very good at it.

godrick_pendlebrook/bd1aabef6b25a6e3.text: Thank you, my lord. I think. Lovely table.

godrick_pendlebrook/bd3c14ae59ad3883.text: Rest easy, sir. We'll look after her. On my oath.

godrick_pendlebrook/bdc1233f6d951f64.text: Oh. Well. When you say it like that, it doesn't sound so bad.

godrick_pendlebrook/bf8dd3fb852c505f.text: Then we'll be our own ally. I'll be the big one.

godrick_pendlebrook/c2e0479bd97380a4.text: Then we go back and cut him down. Nobody gets left behind. Not even the dead ones.

godrick_pendlebrook/c36b1fc33df867d9.text: A land of mists. This is it. Sir Pellam, I'm here. I've got your sword. I've not dropped it once. Well. Once.

godrick_pendlebrook/c49fccf69ccd5b39.text: Sir Godrick Pendlebrook, my lord. More or less. I've brought the Order a sword. It was Sir Aldric Ashgrove's. His grandson asked me to say an Ashgrove kept faith.

godrick_pendlebrook/c76eba8b36c9b9ce.text: Rat, how does the fire one work? The short way.

godrick_pendlebrook/c7e60e1ccd4e4c2d.text: So here's my question, and I want a straight answer, because I'm not clever and I can't work it out on my own. Does a ladle count?

godrick_pendlebrook/c9a5ca77365d00ae.text: I need advice. Courting advice. Sir Pellam was very clear about courting: flowers, a poem, a respectful distance, and never on a Tuesday.

godrick_pendlebrook/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

godrick_pendlebrook/cec0458bb9a51d0e.text: Thank you! Thank you. I'd make a speech, but I think she'd bite me.

godrick_pendlebrook/cf88ba52d27cb2a3.text: It's a horse. Was a horse. It's a dog now. It'll be a spoon by the end.

godrick_pendlebrook/d08d835564c9b8d4.text: Low on the wall. Right. Is that a riddle? I'm bad at riddles.

godrick_pendlebrook/d19bdcb4f44c6ae5.text: And they're the ones who wouldn't leave me behind, either. That's the bit I never expected.

godrick_pendlebrook/d1b2b86a82385741.text: Right then. They sleep in the day. So we go in the day, while they're asleep. Simple.

godrick_pendlebrook/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

godrick_pendlebrook/d4b20ad4fd12029f.text: We are, aren't we? Best friends inside a day. I've never had that. I've had friends, but they took weeks.

godrick_pendlebrook/d5d880782d804b01.text: Are they? Even Wren? Even Liriel? Huh. That's a comfort, and a bit sad. Mostly a comfort.

godrick_pendlebrook/d6a259a0e10cf111.text: Five of them, sergeant and all. Posts kept, mail oiled. Nobody came to relieve them, and they stayed. That's how the Order does it.

godrick_pendlebrook/d79f3bd65664ecf7.text: Every letter we've had, I've handed to someone and said my eyes are tired. My eyes are fine. They're the best eyes in the party.

godrick_pendlebrook/d989e1732e5be9e5.text: The knights on the ridge have waited four hundred years for him. He goes home. After we've dealt with the one who hung him there.

godrick_pendlebrook/da2ab3f5460f604b.text: Morning. I had almost forgotten the word.

godrick_pendlebrook/da566303ff2d3940.text: We're not running. Any of us. I'll carry you up that hill if I have to. I've carried heavier. I once carried a pony.

godrick_pendlebrook/dae175d9af1b07df.text: Easy, madam. Easy now. We're not the ones who took him. We'd never.

godrick_pendlebrook/db7d3c84df3c8987.text: Wren. Why does Thistle keep looking at you like you're a pie on a windowsill?

godrick_pendlebrook/dd1fdd8a4cd88bc2.text: Sir Godfrey gave me the oath on a bit of paper, after. I can read most of it. Not "sleeper". Sleeper's got two Es together, that's showing off.

godrick_pendlebrook/df287921248a57df.text: Right then! I'll be ready by the time we find them.

godrick_pendlebrook/e0b8fbbb2d368e2e.text: I'll take your word for it. My eyes are tired. But a man who writes to everybody wants something from everybody.

godrick_pendlebrook/e135c6d809e21192.text: Fear not. I'll do your smiling for you. I've got plenty spare.

godrick_pendlebrook/e189d914b9533256.text: Why is it there? What's it doing? It's not doing anything! Who let it in?

godrick_pendlebrook/e18d683956d4d2a9.text: We put one of our own on a table in the dark. I still see it when I shut my eyes.

godrick_pendlebrook/e1f9c7f881b1447a.text: You fit with us. You fit right next to me. Mostly because nobody else will arm-wrestle me.

godrick_pendlebrook/e2ce2df37089731d.text: Oh. Oh, that's lovely. That's the best thing I've had since the mutton soup at the Wheatsheaf, and I cried at the Wheatsheaf.

godrick_pendlebrook/e378c3caa4846a24.text: A king and a queen and their boys, all in stone. And one face scratched clean off. That's sad, that is.

godrick_pendlebrook/e421c45c2ffa3132.text: Fair. Sorry. That was the last of the good sausages, wasn't it. Sorry, Rat.

godrick_pendlebrook/e67d7c070d19e6e6.text: Welcome aboard, little fellow! You walk beside me. Nobody walks behind anybody on a stair. New rule.

godrick_pendlebrook/e8132e0bd3f69c72.text: He called me squire, and I got up. Just like that. Like it was Sir Pellam calling.

godrick_pendlebrook/e9c6da1bbbd3b4c1.text: Fear not, little lady. Nobody's going back in there alone. Which house is it?

godrick_pendlebrook/eb69d1748d0e7be1.text: Right. Well. That's harder than I'd planned for. Still. A knight's a knight. Sir Pellam always said it's the posts that matter, not the pulse.

godrick_pendlebrook/ec4c0b726b2d0113.text: No blade? I'll hold it anyway. Somebody ought to.

godrick_pendlebrook/ecb702c0d6b67316.text: You've got a bit of sausage on your nose.

godrick_pendlebrook/ecb98e79d0fa0708.text: There'll be soup. I'll make it myself, with the ladle. Ha! It'd finally be doing two things at once.

godrick_pendlebrook/ed33ce09ff116e73.text: Sir Pellam used to say that. I always thought he was being kind. Maybe he was being right. He could be both. He was good at both.

godrick_pendlebrook/ee2b6e42ae5556a8.text: Good. Huh. Sir Pellam said that once, on his last day. I thought he was rambling.

godrick_pendlebrook/ee4070bbba1925d9.text: Behind me, Baron. Fear not. Leave it to me.

godrick_pendlebrook/ef34b9fe6ed547a8.text: With respect, my lord, I don't think he did. I don't know how I know. I just know Ashgroves, and they don't.

godrick_pendlebrook/ef44b2d45b858fc8.text: Then I'll say it every night, out loud, so it's the last thing in my head when I sleep. You'll have to put up with that.

godrick_pendlebrook/ef6b388552bbd1ce.text: Sir Pellam Ashgrove, my lord. On his deathbed. With a soup ladle. His arms were too weak for the sword.

godrick_pendlebrook/f1085b104485efa2.text: I'm going to have to sit with that one a while. I'm slow with the big ones. I get there.

godrick_pendlebrook/f15826c0a658003e.text: One road out, and it goes through him. Good. I like a plan with one road.

godrick_pendlebrook/f1ff33f98fd407b8.text: I like him. He's a lich, and I like him. He called me young man. Nobody's called me that since I was nine.

godrick_pendlebrook/f3bf332dfc4d05d7.text: I'll sit up with you. I'm big. The dark has to get past me first. I've never lost a staring contest with the dark.

godrick_pendlebrook/f4a90b8c0c9af899.text: The Order. It's... all of you are dead, aren't you, my lord. Sir Pellam never said. I don't think he knew.

godrick_pendlebrook/f53b903d9c857a60.text: Twelve years I carried his shield and mucked out his horse and listened to him talk about honour. He never knighted me. I asked him why once. He said I wasn't ready. I asked when I'd be ready. He said he'd know.

godrick_pendlebrook/f5e5e386d685b52f.text: Right. Stairs. Coffin. Stake. In that order, and nobody stops for anything.

godrick_pendlebrook/f60ef0a14837d726.text: Then nobody's giving him a friend. Not her. Not anyone.

godrick_pendlebrook/f6a91b4e448ca04d.text: He does, my lord. All of them true, I reckon. He's that sort.

godrick_pendlebrook/f8877620fe003c23.text: When the old man gave Adrian the press. His face. I'm crying, and I don't care who sees. Knights are allowed.

godrick_pendlebrook/f8bc3950ad1eee33.text: I'll keep it. Somebody'll need soup one day. A knight's for people who need things.

godrick_pendlebrook/fb3d87c0fd2e04e0.text: When this is done, if we're alive, you're coming to the manor. All of you. There's more sheep than tenants and the roof leaks in the good bedroom, but there's room. There's always been more room than people.

goodwife_sarnov/04598ecc522ff691.text: In the morning she was cold in the cradle, already wrapped. Morgantha said not to look; it was a mercy not to look. So I didn't. We buried the bundle by the church.

goodwife_sarnov/202d3b3bb8d31b14.text: The plain ones. Yes. I go up every morning. I stopped buying the other kind, after. But I go up for a plain one, and she gives me the best in the basket. I don't know why.

goodwife_sarnov/3b3a54e3eeb04cbc.text: I know who you are. You found my children. They're in Vallaki, at the inn. It's better. I'd sell them again; that's what I am.

goodwife_sarnov/403ec8ff30e90f4d.text: Three. I've three again. I don't deserve one of them. I'm going to try to, every day, till I do.

goodwife_sarnov/8071ac6fd53d2ad7.text: She has my husband's eyes. That's a foolish thing to say. He had the ordinary kind.

goodwife_sarnov/91f60b2194b3c39e.text: You're the ones who brought them down. Ilka told me what I did. She said somebody told her the truth. I'm glad somebody did.

goodwife_sarnov/aac08bc2aab1331f.text: She had a mark on her left wrist like a thumbprint of jam. I used to kiss it.

goodwife_sarnov/e3d012783d6bd2b7.text: My first. A girl. Zamfira, for my mother. She was eight days old and fretful, and the old pastry woman came down from the mill to sit up with her so I could sleep. Everybody said Morgantha was kind.

goodwife_sarnov/e4c178526f6250fb.text: Then you bring her home. Whatever she is by then. Whatever they've made of her. Bring her home.

goodwife_sarnov/f129f572da0e5547.text: Nothing. You'll say nothing. (She picks up one bean, and then another.) I've had twelve years of nothing. I can manage a few more days.

goodwife_sarnov/f5e0fa4791a432b4.text: Why do you want to know about her wrist?

granny_ash/1b84f7b2ca47128b.text: (She sighs, like a kettle coming off the boil.) Heroes. Mousie, dear, stand back by the hut. Granny's going to be a while.

granny_ash/712456e80c728dd9.text: Clever ones. Granny likes clever ones. Here's Granny's offer. The girl comes with Granny, and you have this. (She shakes the basket, and it clinks.) And Granny goes back to the deep wood and never comes to this valley again. Never ever. Granny's word.

granny_ash/9a99aee5e464f4c9.text: Names! Names are for eating, dearie. Granny ate that one twelve years ago, and it was delicious.

granny_ash/9f63707f341749bc.text: Mousie. Mousie, dear. Granny's come to make you a sister.

grigor/18b1dd4dbcc4d675.text: The wolves took my brother off this road a month back. We've been taking them back since, one pelt at a time.

grigor/23ea9ac1c217c8da.text: Kolyan's girl? Out here? Then the world's ended and nobody told me.

grigor/519c7fe7fab05ecd.text: And the big wolves, the ones that walk on two legs when it suits them, den in the hills above the lake. They pray to some mother of theirs. Keep clear.

grigor/56f697794f8e3aad.text: That's close enough. Strangers on this road, this near dark, are mostly his. Give me a reason to think you're not.

grigor/80ccc1256b4709cd.text: Fine. Go on, then. And may the wolves find you before you find us again.

grigor/b1bc060a8daceb19.text: That's what his things say too. Walk past, slow, hands where I can see them.

grigor/ef1af5c9d1bd9788.text: Two things, for free. There's an old windmill on a crag on the way to Vallaki. Don't knock. Crows on the sails, and some nights a child crying inside, and nobody in this valley has a child to spare.

gunther_arasek/04368764494c3045.text: Back for more? Good. Steel doesn't sell itself. It mostly sits there being heavy.

gunther_arasek/3a8ced6be3153d1f.text: Pleasure. Bring it back dented and I'll buy it for half. Bring it back bloody and I'll buy it for less.

gunther_arasek/45b900b23f11530e.text: Twice what you'd pay over the mountains. Every cart that reaches us loses a horse or a driver on the way, some months both. My sister Yelena keeps the books, and the books say twice.

gunther_arasek/49477ea56252a10f.text: You came over the pass and the wolves let you by? Huh. They don't let my carts by.

gunther_arasek/67d952cf4166f7de.text: West road to Krezk: wolves, and worse past the river. The lake road: fishermen who've stopped catching anything and gone strange with it. East road, the way you came: an old windmill nobody sane stops at.

gunther_arasek/7c7653a9bbd89810.text: Then you heard right. My carters won't water their horses within sight of it. Horses go in. Horses don't come out.

gunther_arasek/9abb08590b7cea83.text: Arasek Stockyard. Steel, leather, rope, grain. Everything that comes into Vallaki on a cart comes past me first, and the wolves get a look at it on the way.

gunther_arasek/a9ac349bb96ec112.text: You've come from the village, eh? Bildrath's prices? Ten times. And I hear somebody helped themselves to his strongbox. Not that I'd ever think it of you.

gunther_arasek/c991f2adc54ba877.text: It's up on a crag above the road, between Tser Pool and the village. If you must see it, see it by day.

gunther_arasek/ed66e7615c3901ba.text: You can ask Yelena. I'd sell you a helmet first.

gustav_durst/12790cc4ae672d87.text: Go down and see. The altar will ask you too. Everyone gets asked.

gustav_durst/6b6ca485c84ae6be.text: We wanted what he has. Forever. So we fed the house, and the house fed the thing below, and we waited for him to notice.

gustav_durst/6d88cdcdbb741d80.text: And the gift was refused. He wanted nothing from us. Not even that.

gustav_durst/708375940383990b.text: We meant to go back up for them. And then we were so very hungry.

gustav_durst/ecad08f5bea780ea.text: Gustav Durst, and my wife, Elisabeth. This is our house, you understand. All of it. Even the parts that never appeared on the plans.

gustav_durst/f3b4df070b5b9791.text: Guests. Elisabeth, guests. Do sit. We so rarely have anyone down.

hedda_ironvow/045c987aafee7637.text: You want the last light out. I carry one. We have nothing to discuss.

hedda_ironvow/065e4c9ea15a1722.text: Then let's be late. Rudely, unforgivably late.

hedda_ironvow/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

hedda_ironvow/12b1c2bddcc9fb22.text: She thanked us. In his name. I can still hear it.

hedda_ironvow/12c8281370df8cdb.text: I've ground a lot of things in my time. Ore. Grudges. Never that.

hedda_ironvow/132903772db2e1ea.text: Whoever kept this crib made never stopped hoping. That's the saddest kind of housekeeping.

ireena/64838d2dc83d2dad.text: Then I'll stay. But you'll come back. I'm not a parcel to be left at the church door and forgotten.

ireena/65286d6c1412d7a5.text: Let's begin. Before the light goes.

ireena/69ff9ce8b8c0cf88.text: Finished looking? Twice. He's come to my window twice, and twice I woke with these and no memory of opening the shutters. That's the part I can't forgive. Not him. Me.

ireena/6b8df6c0d391f760.text: Ismark said you'd come. He also said you were "probably not monsters". From him, that's a glowing reference. I'm Ireena.

ireena/6cd3d8725db19f58.text: My father and my brother never said it either. Not once, before the end. I'm glad somebody did.

ireena/6e96631d0277d23e.text: He can't come in. He can't. I'm going to tell myself that all night.

ireena/6ebfceca4ad487af.text: And I know your voice. You're the one who told my door to open. Now. Keep that voice down in this house.

ireena/6f82a126dcbe3c47.text: Not for you. Never once for you.

ireena/7157d2580e0bafac.text: I don't know whose it ought to be. Hers. Mine. I'll keep it until I know.

ireena/72634da58edeb691.text: I see. No, I do. It's a long road, and he's very patient. Go on, then.
