ireena/72b3ea523036b645.text: It's only water now. I keep checking. I'd hoped it would hurt less, choosing. It doesn't hurt less. It hurts properly, which is different.

ireena/72d001c23b1a7683.text: You'd do that? Then listen: the parlor window is the weakest, the front door the most stubborn. If he comes himself, he won't break in. He'll ask. Whatever you do, don't answer.

ireena/75900f7dc9ee162e.text: Then I'll stay. For now. Don't get yourselves killed while I'm safe; I'd never forgive you, and I'd say so at every one of your funerals.

ireena/75bf9d5dffbf9239.text: Changed your minds? Or just checking the shutters for us?

ireena/79b3860ad7ee9b61.text: Then come back soon. And next time, knock louder.

ireena/7a5dd42251ddedd6.text: I've decided. Get away from us.

ireena/7bf4c8fc76308b18.text: Vallaki first, then Krezk. Farther than anyone in my family has ever walked.

ireena/810cecbe64eb77ca.text: I'm sorry. I loved you. She loved you. I can't be her and still be anyone at all.

ireena/84c7b13d5e14f525.text: Let him write. I've had his letters before. I burn them.

ireena/84de9f4d452cf200.text: The Vistani women say there's a seer at Tser Pool, on the way. If anyone can tell me what he wants with me, perhaps she can.

ireena/854210746c7d7079.text: My eyes are up here. So is my sword.

ireena/862e587fcce80a89.text: I know this. Not this place. A height, and white cloth, and somebody shouting a name that isn't mine, and then I stepped...

ireena/871bab8545eda7d4.text: The Martikovs are kind. Urwin sits up all night watching the windows. I've never met a man so interested in birds.

ireena/877da13d891f70bb.text: Someone has been in my father's strongbox. If it was you, I'd rather you had asked. He would have given it to you. That was the sort of fool he was.

ireena/87aa0cb53c40704f.text: I'd sooner sleep in the lake.

ireena/88cae0b691269aff.text: No. I've heard sweeter voices than yours at this door, and they had claws. Find Ismark at the tavern.

ireena/8c411815bda7efcb.text: Kolyan Indirovich. Burgomaster for twenty years. Loud, stubborn, and kind to everyone, even the people he was shouting at. He found me on a road when I was a girl and never once made me feel found.

ireena/8ca4f6f6df8a9b4d.text: First, he dies. The one upstairs. After that I'll find that pool, and I'll decide there. Not in a cellar, with all of you watching.

ireena/8d231dfbbf864fdf.text: I'm not asking you to fight him. I'm asking for a roof he hasn't been under.

ireena/8dc72b5f3c852e08.text: If I go now, he waits. A hundred years, two hundred, for the next one of me, in some village, with my face. Some girl who doesn't know what's coming to her window.

ireena/8e83fdef5b2ec052.text: I'm fine. I'm not made of glass. I just wasn't sure, for a moment, that I'm not.

ireena/909d44fb7643aa02.text: A wall that's never let him in. A burgomaster who remembers my father. I came all this way for something like that.

ireena/9110bf694eada617.text: Izek comes to the church door at dusk. He doesn't come in. He can't, or he won't. He just stands there.

ireena/93b8a00104790220.text: He keeps finding us. Doesn't he. Over and over, he keeps finding us, and it never ends well for the girl.

ireena/992e9f91b4e750f4.text: ...I remember a chapel full of white flowers. I'll keep that one.

ireena/99f9ad5bd1bcf45a.text: Then I'll go on. Walls never kept him out of my father's house. I'd rather be moving.

ireena/9b6bdfb27e0f92bf.text: I came to watch you die.

ireena/9c99f1b147d6454d.text: Where did you get this? I've never sat for a painter. I've never owned a dress like that. Who is she?

ireena/9cb1fc29c0e69664.text: Then you know it's a cage.

ireena/9f592b40e4c1f51b.text: And you went for him with steel. He laughed, but you did it. I've wanted to do that for a month.

ireena/9fb080b569894928.text: I don't remember anything before Kolyan's house. Only trees, and being cold, and a boy shouting a name. I always thought the name was mine.

ireena/a1327d06bad2c4fa.text: Father always said I was the daughter he got back. I never once asked him what he'd lost.

ireena/a145cbf093c9d4f6.text: I've been offered rides by strangers before. I walked.

ireena/a275f017368ca46a.text: I'm not visiting. I'm hiding. Tell him that, if you have to tell him anything.

ireena/a27cf3394d5802ea.text: Good. I was going mad sitting still. Walls didn't keep him out of my father's house; I'd rather take my chances with you.

ireena/a2e31ca9c5e8ad05.text: I don't know what he means. I don't. Don't look at me like that.

ireena/a3930a65216a42cd.text: The company in here is a saint. Go home.

ireena/a3cdb5ad99d23005.text: Vallaki. Where we were going anyway. At least the cards are economical.

ireena/a4d0dae7c5eb2dc5.text: I've never been here. I know I've never been here. So why do I know there are nine steps under that plinth?

ireena/a55d3d03557de0da.text: A wall, very high, and a gorge under it. A wedding. No: after a wedding. I was running from someone who said he loved me. Isn't that a stupid thing to be afraid of?

ireena/a7dd09fa939091cc.text: I'm fine. I'll tell you when I'm not. Right now I'd like to go and kill someone.

ireena/abcc4b7701e0fc3a.text: Ismark says you'll help with Father. Then he needs a priest. Father Donavich, at the church on the hill. He hasn't left it in weeks, but he owes Father that much.

ireena/abdc1d0f9f5ac34d.text: Before Kolyan? Nothing. Trees. Being cold. A boy shouting a name through the trees, over and over. I always thought the name must have been mine.

ireena/ad43242d4878fc7b.text: And that was Donavich's boy on the wall. You let him out. You'll have to live with that, and so will the rest of us.

ireena/af227a8982f72046.text: Father used to ride out and cut them down himself. He said a crossroads is no place to be left; the dead get confused about which road leads home.

ireena/b25905477d903713.text: I don't remember you. I'm sorry. I don't remember anything from before.

ireena/b27b4c2f4368ab33.text: Not a priest's words. Honest ones. He'd have taken honest over pretty, most days.

ireena/b33b5dfa18e603ee.text: I dream about falling. Every time I close my eyes near a window.

ireena/b346998ac3eed71c.text: Krezk, then. I've never seen it. For once I'd like to go somewhere I've never been, on purpose. Through Vallaki, and on.

ireena/b4164aeabef61641.text: Ireena Kolyana. This is my father's house. It's still his, until he's in the ground.

ireena/b4774f5014bf51bb.text: Then I'll fetch my sword and my good boots. I'm not made of glass; I'll walk, I'll fight, and I'll take a watch. Don't argue about the watch.

ireena/b51f769ad86c8f2a.text: That's the first time you've called me that.

ireena/b706c3c6f4417252.text: Stay in Krezk? Beside the pool. Beside him. I'd sit by that water every morning and every morning I'd want to walk in.

ireena/b7ba9652abe7bebe.text: Good. I've made forty cheeses. That's enough cheese for a lifetime, and I'm not sure how long mine is.

ireena/b9ca0453693439fe.text: Then you'll have to go through me as well.

ireena/ba893d1ecbbad855.text: No. When he's dead, I'll come back. I swear it on my father. Wait for me a little longer, Sergei. You're good at it.

ireena/bb0e390f24ab432d.text: I know the end of that story. I've dreamed it. The wall, and the wind, and somebody calling a name that isn't mine.

ireena/bb605e44cf728db9.text: Father said there was nothing past the crossroads but more Barovia. He was right. It's the same mud. I still want to see it.

ireena/bc915309ed3abca0.text: I was going to go. I wanted to. That's the worst of it.

ireena/c018a979025ae2b3.text: He hasn't come inside since Father died. He used to sleep under the study desk. He'd never go near that corner, though. The cold corner, we called it.

ireena/c0af52bd1d26cb87.text: Ismark would want me to stay. Father would have. And I'm very tired of sleeping with a sword in the bed.

ireena/c0ce4775e7b8ca1d.text: Don't. Whatever you're about to say. Later. By a fire.

ireena/c4023de052e46bf9.text: No. Not yet. I made a promise, and I can only keep it if the devil's dead. That means I go where you go.

ireena/c464b1151ee4c61b.text: Donavich won't come. Then he'll go into the ground without the church's words. I hope one of you knows some others.

ireena/c5bedce470e935f4.text: I'm... Ireena. Ireena Kolyana. My father was the burgomaster. I buried him myself.

ireena/c628ac6afba2408d.text: You're the brother. The one on the lid. I've dreamed your face for years and never known whose it was.

ireena/c91bfbae2238f482.text: My brother sent me to you. He said this church was the one place in the valley the devil can't walk into.

ireena/ce7487cdfa1deea9.text: He made me beg him for my brother's breath, and I did. I'd do it again, and he knows it. That was the lesson.

ireena/ce8cf1676ecda5b1.text: Ireena. Yes. That's me. That's who I am.

ireena/cecdabd6a01f3089.text: No. Yes. Later. Ask me again when we're somewhere with a fire and no water anywhere.

ireena/cfe4968cbd34ea0b.text: Thank you. That's the kindest wrong thing anyone's said to me in a month.

ireena/cfed50b18e8264b1.text: Anna's teaching me to make cheese. I'm terrible at it. Dmitri says it builds character. I have character. I'd like a sword drill.

ireena/d088d913ebd0a549.text: I said goodbye to you at the pool. I'm saying it again here, to your bones, so that it's done properly. Father would want it done properly.

ireena/d19c5ba3df650ef4.text: There's no such custom. I lived in that village all my life.

ireena/d204b5e4824f34f4.text: He was buried properly. With words said over him. That's all he'd have wanted.

ireena/d2a8baeedf722f52.text: Then tell him I said no. He's heard it before.

ireena/d40321fb7b5a9403.text: You're the ones who came out of the house at the end of the lane. People don't come out of that house. Come in, quickly, before the dark notices the door is open.

ireena/d4dd0ef8fab36c78.text: Thank you. Then he needs a priest. Father Donavich, at the church on the hill. Ask him to say the words. Then we carry Father over together, before dark.

ireena/d6d7438001334751.text: Your god didn't know him. Your god does now. Thank you for that.

ireena/d70e4e2717020846.text: You put our dead back where they belong, too. Buried twice. Father always said this village did nothing by halves.

ireena/d84776560e44fe78.text: I said I'd come back to you when he's dead. I'm close now. He's somewhere under our feet.

ireena/da1556d5b0b4ff00.text: He's in the ground. No words, no prayer. I'll go, because staying is worse. But I won't pretend I liked how.

ireena/dad1aa2098b40ee6.text: Krezk, then. It's farther, and it has an abbey, and nobody in it has ever served him tea. Take me there, or I'll walk it alone.

ireena/dc34e3292e314934.text: Ireena. I'm Ireena Kolyana. Kolyan found me in the woods and taught me to hold a sword, and I'd like to find out what I do next.

ireena/de56bfbf4b514d0e.text: Say it again if I ever forget.

ireena/df7dc4986e2ea5ba.text: Wolves, most nights. Dead things on others: neighbors we buried, back to scratch at the boards. And once, him. He doesn't scratch. He knocks, and asks, very politely, to be let in.

ireena/e1c447d5578479fe.text: Last night you stood in my father's house, and nobody ran. I've watched a lot of people run. I won't forget it.

ireena/e57774004dda9288.text: I'm not made of glass. But I'm not a fool either. I'll be by the well. Shout if you need a sword.

ireena/e7015008560f4a18.text: Donavich said the words. Father would have corrected his grammar. He'd have been pleased, though. He liked things done properly.

ireena/e93a17293a8d77d8.text: Don't talk. Don't wake him. Just do it.

ireena/eb4bfd5443179abc.text: I am standing right here, and I am not a sack of flour to be handed over a counter.

ireena/ec13e4eee1a5901b.text: Bring him back in one piece. He's the only brother I have.

ireena/ec262933970b9bb8.text: Back again. Good. The house is quieter with more swords in it.

ireena/ed268219258f9602.text: She had my hair. Didn't she. Whoever she was.

ireena/f18221a21b34732a.text: I could have told you that for free.

ireena/f39271a4a02421e6.text: Why are you all looking at me like that?

ireena/f4eb4a29af125655.text: Krezk. All that road, and it's a wall with a man in front of it.

ireena/f55a8a3e0b127fab.text: I remember a chapel full of white flowers. I remember Sergei. I don't remember loving you. I've looked.

ireena/f60f433325f0fbc3.text: He's still down there. I can feel it, like a door left open somewhere in the house. When this is over, I'm coming back here. Don't let me forget I said it.

ireena/f6a4140195454a3f.text: He dreams about me. A man I've never met dreams about me, and pays for dolls.

ireena/f6ecc73a01a92191.text: Fine. Come in. Slowly, and with your hands where I can see them. I've opened this door to worse than you, and I'm still standing.

ireena/f85499811a1ee145.text: Thank you. He'd have liked you. He'd have argued with you about everything, and liked you.

ireena/f88a9813292e6cef.text: I've never been here in my life.

ireena/f8a1614c8b69ce91.text: I don't remember him. I don't remember anything. And he's dreamed of me every night since he was nine.

ireena/f8c49b65da6347a3.text: Tser Pool first, then. If this Madam Eva reads cards for strangers, she can read a few for me.

ireena/fb82ad34d66f23d9.text: I'd sooner walk off a cliff.

ireena/fec5c736bcda575f.text: I remember you. I remember a chapel full of white flowers, and being happy for one whole morning. And then the wall. And your brother at the top of the stair.

ismark/01f21b9723fdb4e7.text: Do you know, I'd never been to Tser Pool? Twenty years, half a day's walk. Father always said the Vistani would steal my boots.

ismark/073ecb13cffc9f64.text: The house. Of course. Somebody has to argue with the wolves. Get her there. I'll walk you to the west road and wave like a fool.

ismark/08b31cc7e8eb2b18.text: And I'll go and sit by a different door. I'm getting very good at doors.

ismark/0daaf664e938d165.text: The house with the iron fence, north-west of the square. Follow the claw marks. I'll go ahead and tell Ireena not to stab you.

ismark/0eccf7486cf3da0c.text: No. No, no. I was awake. I was awake the whole time.

ismark/109393cee928305f.text: She's packed. She's been packed since the funeral. Every hour she sits by that window is an hour I don't sleep.

ismark/166d5068266f2d4b.text: Where she goes, I go. I'd rather argue with wolves than drink to his health.

ismark/1b9655fa0d80e085.text: What... Ireena? Why is everybody standing at the window?

ismark/1bf420b41b55a619.text: We'll manage. We always do. Badly, mostly, but we manage.

ismark/1c3ba6cf552b9695.text: Ismark the Lesser, off to see the world. Someone tell the tavern. Actually, don't; they'll only throw a party.

ismark/1c969f9f368ea321.text: You gave her to him. After everything. Get out of my sight, and out of my village.

ismark/1d26f1d644c04181.text: Strangers. In Barovia. And you came out of the house at the end of the lane; you've still got its dust on you. Sit. I'm buying. It won't help, but I'm buying.

ismark/21c6db89c76af6c6.text: Then I'll sit by the door and glare at it. I'm good at that. Ask any door in Barovia.

ismark/25ef38cbee395558.text: Then he invited you. You're his guests, or his game. Let's make you the third thing: his problem.

ismark/265225d5d64efcf4.text: You're the ones my sister let in. She doesn't let anyone in. Sit down, before I decide that's suspicious.

ismark/26ca23d01a36f8d1.text: Me? The cards want me? Somebody tell the tavern. No, don't. They'll only laugh, and then they'll stop, and that will be worse.

ismark/283795b41a5e4723.text: Where she goes, I go. Don't make me say anything sentimental about it.

ismark/28a70e0b80fb2e21.text: Donavich isn't coming. After what happened under his church, I can't say I blame him.

ismark/2e5ede49fcd07254.text: This is as far as I go. Get her there. Bring her back one day, if there's anything to bring her back to.

ismark/3089b0261ae2e0c1.text: Strahd von Zarovich. Our lord. Our landlord. The thing in the castle on the cliff. He collects his rent at night, and the coin he likes best is us.

ismark/320243b272b02663.text: And he made Ireena beg him for my breath. That's what he came for. Not me. Her, begging. I won't forget it.

ismark/39e91ec7e63841eb.text: Changed your minds. Good. I'd stopped hoping, which in Barovia is usually when things happen. Talk to Ireena; she has opinions about how it's done.

ismark/3a87ed6a22504477.text: I have spent my whole life afraid of this place. It is only a house now. A cold, ugly house.

ismark/3d459ebc23bb87e5.text: Wolves, most nights, big ones. Some nights, the dead: people we buried, back to scratch at the boards. Once, the devil himself, knocking politely. Father answered with a lamp in his face. That was the last good night.

ismark/3f6c90c404be1651.text: Of course I'll stay. There's a wall. I'll stand next to it. It's the one thing in Barovia I'm reliably good at.

ismark/45413dc141122928.text: No. Of course not. Why would you. If you change your minds, I'll be at the house, waiting for something to come through the door. It may as well be you.

ismark/469f7dfd8fc8ca9b.text: I'm coming with you. Don't argue. We go up that mountain and we bring her down.

ismark/4d13a4f93594b954.text: Fine. I'll sit in the taproom and drink Urwin's wine and glare at the door. It's a sacrifice, but I'm prepared to make it.

ismark/531fa67a33f2ccb8.text: Ireena. Father took her in when she was a girl; she's my sister in every way that counts. The devil has been at her window. Twice. You'll see the marks on her neck, and she'll hate you for looking.

ismark/54af7cbb9b2f59a8.text: Strangers. In Barovia. Either a miracle or a mistake, and I've stopped believing in miracles. Sit. I'm buying. It won't help, but I'm buying.

ismark/55e0629ddd0f21ac.text: About time. She's safe here, and I'm going soft. Lead on.

ismark/575c6d823d9e9b4a.text: The Durst children used to stand in the east road, where the cottages begin. Folk saw them for years. If they're gone now, if you did that, then thank you. I think.

ismark/5c94c9adb510dce0.text: He's lying in his coffin at the house, and not one man in this village will help me carry him to the church. They think the devil is watching. They're right. He is.

ismark/5dbbf32f8eff2fb5.text: No priest, then. Someone say something. Father would hate a silent funeral; he never let a silence pass without a speech.

ismark/602f524707a9c90c.text: Someone's been in Father's strongbox. I'll assume it was the wolves. Wolves with remarkably good fingers.

ismark/6155b9eb0693e8d7.text: Go on, little sister. I will tell the village you were happy. It will even be true.

ismark/67b7367a6a5486b2.text: He wants her. I don't know why her. I don't think he'd tell me if I asked nicely, which I haven't.

ismark/69455b0236b8d03c.text: Go carefully. Be indoors by dark. And if something knocks on your door and says it's me, it isn't.

ismark/74183516e7b4c934.text: Vistani, by the earring. Whoever did this was proud of their lettering.

ismark/744fbc7b3aceb6fe.text: He did. He made it deeper "for the wolves". Bildrath will charge me for every inch. Worth it.

ismark/76630c0490fc3993.text: And if it helps, I'm her brother, and I'll be doing all the fighting anyway.

ismark/8126363b8d48f35c.text: Ireena, behind me! Into the church porch, go!

ismark/824283e19cba58d5.text: You found the place. Ireena hasn't stabbed anyone yet today; you're in luck.

ismark/82911b8c33ff36d4.text: Last night. You held the door and the windows, and nobody ran. I've been the only one not running for a month. It was good to have company.

ismark/892c597486a9eb84.text: Thank you. I mean that, and I don't say it often, mostly because nobody gives me cause.

ismark/8b4514abc0e2c4c9.text: And I'll... well. Somebody should stay with her. Somebody should also keep you lot alive. I can't do both.

ismark/8be800dda7085a1e.text: Second: once he's in the ground, take Ireena west to Vallaki. It has walls, a church with old relics under the altar, and a baron who's a fool, but a careful fool. And it's farther from the castle.

ismark/9039fc17417b1099.text: I'm coming too. Don't argue either. It's the only family business I have left.

ismark/95779c870f9e2d82.text: Ismark Kolyanovich. My father was burgomaster here until three nights ago. Now I'm the burgomaster's son with no burgomaster: all of the work, none of the chair.

ismark/9592f49bc56bc172.text: Right. She's safer here than she's been in a month, and I've never been much use sitting still. I'm with you.

ismark/95dbc370a3cd22e8.text: My father was the Greater, and his heart burst at his own front door. I'll take the Lesser, and breathing.

ismark/96c90e0a6897ad32.text: My throat still feels like there's a hand on it. He never touched me. He never had to. Father faced that every night, alone, with a lamp.

ismark/96d22901c86ecd2a.text: She has a wall and a burgomaster with an axe. You have me. I'll come. Ireena, if anything happens, scream; I'll hear it from the castle.

ismark/98804d50121f3552.text: Two things. First: help me carry my father to the church and see him buried properly, with Father Donavich's words over him. Ireena won't leave until it's done.

ismark/99a055ea8b3649dd.text: Rest, old man. I'll look after her. I'll do better than I did.

ismark/99df10a77b67d631.text: That's not my father's hand. Father wrote letters too, begging for help. The Vistani carried them out of the valley. Nobody ever answered. Except, it seems, him.

ismark/9a60b25baaaa77a0.text: Holy ground. I keep feeling I should take my boots off. Lucian says I needn't. I've taken them off anyway.

ismark/a311f89a2d7c100f.text: A long day west on the old road, past the crossroads and Tser Pool. A stockade, and a baron who throws festivals to prove everyone's happy. The devil goes where he likes, but there, at least, he has to knock.

ismark/a886d999ef441736.text: I'm guarding. This is what guarding looks like. It involves a great deal of wine and a lot of looking at doors.

ismark/a8fa484df8c27e2a.text: One more thing. After dark the square isn't ours. If you can wait for morning, wait. If you can't, keep together.

ismark/b0d6744d736c9fbe.text: Father kept a strongbox in his study. Take what's in it. Oh. You've already found it. Efficient. Call it payment in advance, then, and don't make me regret the bookkeeping.

ismark/b16647002a192c2a.text: For a month, things have come at our house every night. Wolves. Worse than wolves. Father stood at the door with a lamp and his old sword, shouting at them. Three nights ago his heart stopped mid-shout.

ismark/b29e2858f45a3e53.text: And I'm her brother, before anyone in this town gets ideas.

ismark/b55f2d157651c8f2.text: What can I pay? My gratitude, which in this valley is a figure of speech, and my company, which you've seen. I have nothing. That's why I'm asking.

ismark/bca66de26b224cba.text: Do they. Good. It means they still talk about me.

ismark/bfbbc1bf6514f80e.text: The whole lane heard that house: bricks grinding, glass going. Nobody gets out of it at all. You got out through a window, by the look of your sleeves.

ismark/c453079bb5b3c16f.text: It's a good wall. I've been looking at it. I've been looking at walls a great deal lately.

ismark/c6b0b3765d9ae3d3.text: I've been put on the wall. They gave me a spear. It's a terrible spear. I'm having the time of my life.

ismark/c8c9b57307f74b10.text: Here. This was his. He had it blessed in Vallaki when he was young and foolish, and it never once let him down. I'm keeping her. You keep this.

ismark/cc7afca751b97b9b.text: I'll pretend I did, and come back anyway.

ismark/ccac9c488326b8e4.text: Right. Urwin, if anything so much as looks at her...

ismark/dbb3493ab5e7e9a5.text: Stop that. I can feel you reading me. Yes, I should have saved him. No, I couldn't have. I have that argument with myself every night. I'm winning on points.

ismark/dfe54c79032b9999.text: Call him what you like. He answers to all of it.

ismark/e17dc9a1ae14252e.text: About time. The goats were starting to look up to me.

ismark/e258325fb6177d4f.text: It's very good mud. Westward mud. I'm told the gentry prefer it.

ismark/ea0d4b6d7ae2e9af.text: Fair. Father kept a strongbox in his study. Whatever's left in it is yours once he's in the ground. It isn't much. Nothing is, here.

ismark/ecbe2fc2f479d143.text: He's in the ground. Properly or not, he's in it, and nobody's digging him up tonight. Now there's only her.

ismark/ee1f0ff83a4e0e5d.text: Madam Eva said Father would ride with us. I thought she meant his memory. She didn't, did she.

ismark/f0df24bf6998a113.text: Where she goes. You know the rest. Don't make me say it in front of the goats.

ismark/f5c620f45a8ce597.text: Still here, then. Still not taking her. I don't blame you. I blame the valley. It's easier.

ismark/fe1107da427d12d8.text: Krezk? That's days past Vallaki, up in the hills, behind a wall and an abbey. Farther from him, I'll grant you. Farther from everything.

ismark/fed0efea4a080158.text: Well. The Lesser goes adventuring. If I'm killed, tell the tavern I was the Greater. They won't check.

izek/02a44f237a3b808a.text: I woke up with this one. Nobody knows where it came from. The Baron doesn't ask. That's why I work for him.

izek/0d9858b161709c86.text: I won't touch her. I won't let anyone touch her. And I won't break any more heads for that fat fool in the sash. I'm done.

izek/0db2337074c840b5.text: Then you know I'm not mad. She's real. I'll find her and keep her, and she'll never be cold in the woods again.

izek/22f1e796710d2913.text: I feel the same. I've felt the same since I was nine. I'll take her myself.

izek/23f3d21ed5dec1fd.text: He said no. In front of everyone. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting.

izek/24885cea6c70a45f.text: Good. I've wanted to since the gate.

izek/2eac614fbebfeee2.text: I remember enough for both of us.

izek/3546d2cc66f1c2ad.text: Where did you come from? Who are you?

izek/41d0e7ec2cc74546.text: If it's true, she can tell me herself. Not you. Never you.

izek/4a7d522ad7ab0831.text: I've seen you. Every night since I was nine years old. I didn't know your name. Now I do.

izek/6cd3716cdfe79541.text: She's here. In Vallaki. I've seen her. Tell me why I shouldn't go and get her now.

izek/6ff7cc2c559445ac.text: You think you frighten me? Something took my arm when I was nine and gave me this one. Nothing's frightened me since.

izek/83389f4d6fef143d.text: Wolves. When I was nine. My little sister and me, in the woods past the lake, gathering sticks. They came out of the trees and took her, and took my arm with her.

izek/a1f65f95d0cb607e.text: Never found. They found my arm. Not her.

izek/a224cec45cb8bdfe.text: My sister. My sister had red hair.

izek/a2b8c853268e1275.text: She's real. I dream her every night. Her face, her hair. When I find her, I'll keep her safe. Nobody will ever take her into the trees again.

izek/a562c4be4437b803.text: Everything in this town is the Baron's business. And the Baron's business is mine.

izek/aa51a93c2117883e.text: Kill me? In the Baron's house? Go on, then. Try.

izek/acc00ace42afd22d.text: I do. I remember all of it.

izek/ae233d280e54ba95.text: You again. You stood between us in the square. I remember where everyone stands.

izek/b0b84ddd5f6180b4.text: The Baron's happy. That makes one of us.

izek/b89b2330485b8b80.text: Bring her, then. If she says it, I'll listen. If you say it again without her, I'll break your jaw.

izek/bac716db1dc856c8.text: Her. The red-haired one. Ireena. Give her to me.

izek/bccdb8bf21aad211.text: My lord. I want my reward.

izek/c4d792ade2607d88.text: Blinsky talks too much. One day I'll take the rest of his teeth for it.

izek/c677386cea663ed8.text: Liar. You saw the dolls and you made up a story to go with them. Get out of my sight before I forget the Baron likes you.

izek/d0f257a335a96017.text: Not here. Not in front of the town.

izek/e2173d8868a4e2ad.text: I'm done, my lord. I'm done.

izek/ef02d0f590b28841.text: Strangers. The Baron says be polite to strangers. I'm being polite.

kasha_varo/08414428901f8649.text: Lighter than it should be. I said. I've always said. Put it back, now. Put it back gently.

kasha_varo/1069a1943872439c.text: The shrine of the White Sun. The morning lord, in Vallaki they'd say, but we're older than Vallaki and we call him what our grandmothers did. Krezk was built round this pool, not the other way.

kasha_varo/198e5a2ce78711eb.text: Somebody's been in the pool after the wishes. Sixty years of wishes. I hope it was worth nine gold to be the sort of person who does that. No, don't tell me. The pool knows, and the pool doesn't gossip. I do.

kasha_varo/3bd66e5ce5e885e7.text: It remembers, you see. The sun used to come here properly. The water's been holding onto it ever since, the way you'd keep a letter.

kasha_varo/408c4f92ceb33d0f.text: Sitting in his chapel, the Belviews say, not speaking. Well. I've sat by this pool not speaking for sixty years, and it's done me no harm. Maybe he'll come to something.

kasha_varo/45d826b262897cfe.text: And somebody's been leaving toys on the Krezkov stones. Every morning this month. Carved. I leave them be. Toys aren't my business; graves are.

kasha_varo/49bdc186920bb7ea.text: It doesn't freeze. Never has. Snow falls in and stops being snow. And when the sun goes behind the clouds, look in it quick, and you'll see the sun stays in the water a breath longer than it stays in the sky.

kasha_varo/4b636f90e25d15b4.text: Fill a flask and find out. It doesn't do anything for people who ask what it does. That's my experience. Sixty years of it.

kasha_varo/51b7ab8e574f84a1.text: A light went up off the mountain at dawn. I stood here and watched it go and I didn't know whether to cheer or cry, so I swept. It's what I do with things I don't understand.

kasha_varo/540b312895d3b51c.text: And some of them are lighter than they should be, if you take my meaning. I've found earth turned that I didn't turn. I put it back. I say a prayer. It's all I can do.

kasha_varo/7627215f3d4a0376.text: The toys? Still coming. I've stopped sweeping round them. The eldest stone's always had the most. The eldest was always lighter than it should be, if you ask me. Nobody asks me.

kasha_varo/7a239d3842320980.text: The wall's for the wolves. The pool's for us.

kasha_varo/7ce96f75b43a3672.text: You've been here before, girl. Long before me. Don't ask me how I know; my knees know things, and I've stopped arguing with them.

kasha_varo/a2893c88d797debf.text: Back again. The pool remembers you. It remembers everybody, but it's polite about it.

kasha_varo/a5221e710a8d90a2.text: A cart went by in the night, they say, with a bride in it. I don't want to hear about it. I'll pray for her. She's ours, whatever she's made of.

kasha_varo/acd4c3b3c73719d7.text: Some. The pool's water goes into the draughts, and the prayers I write out on the long nights. They're not free. The shrine needs a new roof, and I need new knees, and only one of those can be bought.

kasha_varo/b9fddd9f01e5ff53.text: I don't go in after it. My knees are the oldest residents of Krezk and they've earned their rest. You've young knees. Wade in, if you want it.

kasha_varo/c7ba3eec38089639.text: Mind the edge. The pool doesn't like boots. Kasha Varo, if you're asking. You weren't, but people ought to, so I tell them anyway.

kasha_varo/c814b8bace3bdcff.text: Best groundskeeper I ever had. Doesn't talk back. Talks in my voice sometimes, which is a bit much, but I've heard worse voices.

kasha_varo/c823c9c8a237610a.text: Since the autumn there's something down in the middle that shines when the sun's gone in. Not a coin. Coins don't shine like that.

kasha_varo/de02c42e707814cf.text: I didn't say that. I'd never say that. Not out loud, where the mountain can hear.

kasha_varo/e18662731268debe.text: Dead, they say. Something that was sent here to look after us, and went wrong, and you put it right the only way you could. I'll light it a candle. Somebody ought to.

kasha_varo/f805efa6144b21b8.text: I thought he was a saint. Now I've seen your red-haired girl look at him, I think he's only someone waiting. Which is holier, in the end.

kasha_varo/fbfe00dbb2d52916.text: Once. When I was a girl, and once again the winter my husband died. A young man in old clothes, looking up out of the water as if he'd lost something.

kasha_varo/fd81f6b941b88dda.text: Krezk's. All of us end up round the pool, sooner or later. The little stones by the pavilion are the burgomaster's. Five of them. Anna comes and sits with them on Tuesdays.

kasimir_velikov/0289a7d97edd718b.text: Then I will be brave once, and late. Take it.

kasimir_velikov/0893692f1946d036.text: Long ago a Vistana I had never met fell sick with a fever on the road, and I sat with her three nights until it broke. Her grandchildren still bring me soup. The Vistani forget nothing: not a kindness, not an insult.

kasimir_velikov/1b85e45a5940de11.text: You are patient. The young rarely are. Very well; you have paid for it.

kasimir_velikov/1fb546cb5e2b42ca.text: I write them out at night, when I can't sleep, which is every night. Lesser spells; the ones that matter I keep. Take what you can pay for. Gold buys passage, and I have a long way to go.

kasimir_velikov/22e4faf6ee15f1c9.text: My sister asked for far less than this, once. Look what it made of her.

kasimir_velikov/28804e166c6393f9.text: Beyond the pass to the north, in the ice. I have read of it, and dreamed of it, and been too much of a coward to climb to it. If ever you go that way, I would like very much to go with you.

kasimir_velikov/30f526670ef15662.text: "Kasimir. You stayed, and I ran, and neither of us saved her. I have had a long time to decide which of us was the coward, and the answer is both, and it does not matter any more."

kasimir_velikov/32a055f1d4b09dbb.text: "The boy who brings you this is the best thing I did with the time I stole. Feed him. He will say he isn't hungry. He is lying. S."

kasimir_velikov/374d831acb6c9ed1.text: I will come. Somewhere along your road is the castle, and beneath it, my sister. And past it, perhaps, the temple. It is time I stopped mending nets.

kasimir_velikov/3e5b1a5938f6abfe.text: My sister, Patrina. Cleverer than me, prouder than me. She went up to the castle of her own will, to learn what its lord knew. Our own people stoned her for it, and I stood at the back and did not stop them.

kasimir_velikov/4ac1daf646b797eb.text: Which is why, if I were you, I would not linger by their fire. They have heard what happened at Tser Pool.

kasimir_velikov/4de4af30055168a2.text: Back again, to the saddest wagon in the camp. People will start to talk.

kasimir_velikov/52f9526ec3250b26.text: "I hear you mean to go to the temple in the mountains, where death can be argued with. Do not. Whatever answers there will want more than either of us has, and it will not give her back as she was. Let her rest, brother."

kasimir_velikov/5873ae668a382d5f.text: The songs were written before the ending. They usually are.

kasimir_velikov/5b1a822636f0c532.text: I know. I have stood behind one for a very long time.

kasimir_velikov/5b350f174bc52bbd.text: Walk in the light while there is any. It goes quickly here.

kasimir_velikov/5d075b00025495a9.text: ...She's right. She was always right. That was the whole trouble with her.

kasimir_velikov/6d23261d03a546f9.text: I have read about these. They were made to keep something in, not to keep us out. I wish I had not read that part.

kasimir_velikov/6eddfe7bdeaa8ad4.text: Kasimir Velikov. My people came to this valley long ago, the elves of the dusk, as guests of its lord. We stayed as his tenants. Now there are only a handful of us, none of us young, and there will never be another. That was his doing. And, I am afraid, a little of ours.

kasimir_velikov/838a484be330adf0.text: We do not say it. We are what is left of a people who said yes to the lord of this valley once. Our sister said yes to him too. Patrina. Our own people stoned her for it, and I stood at the back.

kasimir_velikov/8ef61e95a9b59743.text: She told me to be brave somewhere she can't see me. I think she meant the castle. I think she meant you.

kasimir_velikov/9f7928bac2268bba.text: My sister. Patrina. Her bones lie under the castle and her voice is in this temple. Can you put them together again?

kasimir_velikov/a1ac801d1a296e95.text: One year. I have wasted three hundred.

kasimir_velikov/a785bc5fbd689336.text: ...Yes. You're right. I know you're right. It is a terrible thing, to be talked out of the only brave thing I nearly did.

kasimir_velikov/a9d8c6642c1555e7.text: I was afraid of them, and I was afraid of you, and I let them do it so that I would never have to be as brave as you were. I'm sorry. I have been sorry every day.

kasimir_velikov/b5ba36fb05918de7.text: Eva named me? Then the cards have a sense of humour, or a sense of justice. I have never been able to tell those apart.

kasimir_velikov/b738e5d468cdd5ec.text: The strangers. The camp talks of nothing else. Sit, if you like. I am poor company. I have been poor company for a very long time.

kasimir_velikov/c67237f9f28f8077.text: I let them, Patrina. Because I was afraid of being you.

kasimir_velikov/ca3b3102ee6dc474.text: It knows. Of course it knows. It was built for nothing else.

kasimir_velikov/d1a39dddf5af5b34.text: He did. He's dead, sister. He lived a long time, a long way away, and he taught a halfling to fight, and he wanted you to rest.

kasimir_velikov/d658f55c4448881d.text: Sorrel went over the mountains before the mists came. I thought him dead four hundred years. I thought him dead every day of them.

kasimir_velikov/d88ae0a549de70a9.text: One year. It is strange, how much longer a year feels when you can count it.

kasimir_velikov/dc2be83d7ca61789.text: The road's open. She walked this. I can feel it.

kasimir_velikov/dcfd22d135b00d17.text: She didn't wait. Of course she didn't wait. She never once waited for me.

kasimir_velikov/eb7526d015abd872.text: My sister came this way. If they stopped her, they'll remember. If they didn't, they let her through to that place, and I don't know which I'd rather hear.

kasimir_velikov/f56907da6e122ef6.text: Her bones lie under his castle now. They say there is a temple high in the mountains, sealed in amber, where death itself can be argued with. One day I will go there and argue.

kasimir_velikov/f6b98f4ff4351ce3.text: I did. I do. I don't know. He says let her rest. He was always the wise one. He was always the one who left.

kasimir_velikov/fccf787709dde00a.text: I stood at the back. I have stood at the back for three hundred years. I came up here to stop.

kip_smudgewick/062744b993b2b4ae.text: My master died before my last lesson. I asked him what it was and he said it was in a letter I'm not allowed to read. I make jokes all day so nobody notices I'm not finished.

kip_smudgewick/072684fc0cca75a0.text: His diary and his contract, side by side. He read every term, and he signed anyway. That's the part I can't stop looking at.

kip_smudgewick/07af2364aa48859f.text: A land of mists. Right. Lord of a land of mists. One signature. That's all. How hard can one signature be?

kip_smudgewick/0a41e9353029be06.text: I've drawn something up for the two of you. Purely as a precaution. Standard terms. Who gets the good bedroll, and so on.

kip_smudgewick/0ad21dbaa13ae23a.text: Can I raise a matter? Under any other business. It's a bit awkward. I'll be brief. I'm never brief.

kip_smudgewick/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

kip_smudgewick/0bfcf880e6ca2869.text: That's a merchant's hand. Neat columns, every line tallied. They kept people like stock.

kip_smudgewick/0ddb49464c3599e2.text: We know something about his own nursemaid that he doesn't. In trade, that's leverage. In Barovia, I think it's a lit fuse.

kip_smudgewick/0e89f8d4b759ec50.text: You haven't, have you. I'd have noticed. I always notice.

kip_smudgewick/0f1142ac774a85a6.text: Bring coin. Seers always want coin. I'll bring apricots too, in case she barters.

kip_smudgewick/103e40b7d054eac7.text: Will he send someone down to look? I'd like to be somewhere else when they look.

kip_smudgewick/124ccd9eaf2ee93e.text: Is that... is that it? Is it done? I don't feel any different. I thought I'd feel different. I thought there'd be a noise.

kip_smudgewick/12f17893a3c66633.text: Mister Quillon. If you'd be so kind. I'd like to settle my account.

kip_smudgewick/13b7b2de35b889f2.text: Me. Huh. That's a frightening amount of responsibility. I'll need it in writing. No, I won't. I'll need it said again sometime, that's all.

kip_smudgewick/16691ba74a4cac12.text: I can do that. I'm very good at accounts. I'll keep a ledger. Two columns. The second one's for putting things right.

kip_smudgewick/190368c6bbf481b5.text: So I've always been honest. Stupidly honest. Change counted out loud. Weights on the table where you can see them. Because if I wasn't, I'd only be what they thought I was.

kip_smudgewick/1a4bb4dd6e6d6d8d.text: I asked if there's a way out. She answered like a solicitor. That's either very good or very bad.

kip_smudgewick/1aa0a4745cbb31c1.text: Right. Read it. I can do that. I'll read it tonight. I'll read it tomorrow. I'll definitely read it.

kip_smudgewick/1bc0b3992a7fe586.text: It is. That's true. Mum says you weigh the risk on one hand and the fruit on the other, and you never put your soul on the scale. I did. I'm saying don't.

kip_smudgewick/1c037bf6f3c517d3.text: I did. I did do that. I keep forgetting that part. I'm going to put it in the letter. "I'm sorry, and also I saved everyone." That's a good sentence. That's a sentence a person can live with.

kip_smudgewick/1cdbdf362756e274.text: That's not medicine. I've paid for medicine. It comes in a little bottle, and nobody grows an ear.

kip_smudgewick/1dd1ff2f41301ff4.text: Then I'll carry it. I've carried it this far.

kip_smudgewick/1eed21bf1f8435cd.text: They're still scared, though. Whatever they are. That part's real.

kip_smudgewick/1f48d5ffbddd1280.text: Apricot tarts. You bake, I sell. After. If there's an after.

kip_smudgewick/22a90b95af1c4935.text: Never sell to a collector, Mum says. They pay beautifully, and then one day you're in the cabinet.

kip_smudgewick/22e3cb0cdf0eaeeb.text: Is that in my favour, or against? Sorry. Professional habit.

kip_smudgewick/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

kip_smudgewick/24e78214d6b932ea.text: Please don't fight the devil, Godrick. It's in the contract. I think. I haven't read that bit.

kip_smudgewick/26b1ec772543d40d.text: A real angel, sewing dead girls together. I always thought if I met one, I'd ask for help with a paperwork matter.

kip_smudgewick/26e5e327901343ea.text: I'll be walking in the very middle of the bridges, then. If nobody minds.

kip_smudgewick/277e53c30f538b42.text: A signature of the lord of the land of mists. Freely given. In his own hand. At the bottom of a letter he wrote us, to say hello.

kip_smudgewick/278a91571e0e0160.text: Oh, lovely. I was hoping they'd be careless.

kip_smudgewick/27f141dcaebc8142.text: I'd like it on the record, please, that I've been very patient. I'm a patient man. You have to be, with trees.

kip_smudgewick/29c195488d19e9dc.text: Hang on. Hang on. "A signature of the lord of the land of mists, freely given, in his own hand." That's it. That's the whole clause.

kip_smudgewick/2ba2122f92be3133.text: Hello, miss. We're very glad you're not drowned. Apricot? No charge. You must be starving.

kip_smudgewick/2c9d3115a805979a.text: I'm not saying anything. I'm just saying it. Notwithstanding.

kip_smudgewick/2cddc5aaecd09887.text: For what it's worth, you'd do well in a market town. People trust a loud voice.

kip_smudgewick/2e376a7603630352.text: Thank you, sir. I think. I'll think about whether I think.

kip_smudgewick/2e917bcfc201dde2.text: Four hundred years. Master Sorrel always did take his time with the post.

kip_smudgewick/2e941eb89322ac0a.text: Apricot-pit charm. Finest in three counties. I've sold hundreds, and not one of them ever worked, because the orchard was cursed.

kip_smudgewick/2ebdcf83da033957.text: The children aren't in the road anymore. I keep looking for them anyway. I'd saved them each an apricot.

kip_smudgewick/2f46319458361243.text: Better sad than eaten. Sad folk bolt their doors. Dreamers leave them on the latch.

kip_smudgewick/313227a78b4d074a.text: Now that is a hiding place. I'd have looked under the floor. So did the druids, by the state of it.

kip_smudgewick/3587052576ba0c48.text: She answered like a solicitor. Notwithstanding, I think there was a door in it somewhere.

kip_smudgewick/37877e48b6fb89b3.text: I know that sort. Polite, patient, and he's already got your name written down somewhere.

kip_smudgewick/3808db455821461b.text: Two of them, alive, walking down a hill on their own feet. I gave them an apricot each. No obligation.

kip_smudgewick/3a066bcc41e85bbb.text: I like towns. Bit. Beds. The little cakes. People singing in the big room at the inn. And I don't fit in them, and I don't fit in the woods any more either. I don't fit anywhere.

kip_smudgewick/3a08dba5a775316a.text: It says "run". That's... that's the whole thing. Just "run".

kip_smudgewick/3bdd0e9d2589a0a3.text: With respect, sir, that's not what her letter says. I read it. Small print and all.

kip_smudgewick/3c8404d9f299f76c.text: Sold the wrong man vinegar and got bricked up with his stock. That's every merchant's nightmare. I've had that exact dream.

kip_smudgewick/3d3b196cca79649b.text: Smudgewick and Company. Apricots and adventuring. I've put all your names in. I've left the small print blank on purpose. No small print. Just the big print.

kip_smudgewick/3d3e7d0eb3b0cc27.text: So we break into a vampire's castle and take a dragon's head off his wall. Recovery of property. Strictly legal. Mostly.

kip_smudgewick/3e9d428f46dd36aa.text: I gave him an apricot after. It was all I had.

kip_smudgewick/40845c7b21a2912a.text: A creditor who never collects. Either very generous or very dead. I wish mine were either.

kip_smudgewick/423ec8992b7feabe.text: When I settle with Mister Quillon, I'll do it on my own, if it comes to that. I'll not have him see me standing with people like this. He'd only take notes.

kip_smudgewick/431493b3ed20ef15.text: Congratulations, Sir Godrick. Apricot? On the house. Well. On the cart.

kip_smudgewick/434af0d4676d5d10.text: That's your worry? Not the vampire? The weight?

kip_smudgewick/4379f08f1cadaf71.text: Good dog. Nice dog. Apricot? No? No. Very sensible.

kip_smudgewick/45cdb9bd736a264f.text: My dad sent the devil away from our gate. Told him we'd manage. I went after him down the lane and signed behind Dad's back. I came home and said the orchard came back on its own. He went to temple and gave thanks for it. I've been lying to him for two years.

kip_smudgewick/45d2da253af31a9c.text: I'd rather cook than cast. I always would. I learned magic so people would sit with me, and I'm good at it, and I'd still rather be in a kitchen. That's a terrible thing for a wizard to say.

kip_smudgewick/45e6c424a573496e.text: He isn't here. I know. That is what faith is for. You need none; you are right here. That is how I know you are not him.

kip_smudgewick/47b06dea5fc1bb37.text: Sorry. Sorry about that. He does that. He's very polite. That's the worst part. He's so polite.

kip_smudgewick/496774ec61d3ac28.text: And the one party who most needs telling is the one who did the drowning. I don't like that clause one bit.

kip_smudgewick/4ab3a60a44e86d70.text: Before anyone burns that, er. Could I have it? It's signed. I collect signatures. It's a hobby. Since about a minute ago.

kip_smudgewick/4b7d4db9acbeeb5c.text: Who steals a saint? Who would you even sell one to? I sold jam to a bishop once, and he haggled.

kip_smudgewick/4c248ede2b2e96ef.text: I'll just take this. The letter. Nobody needs it. Nobody needs it but me.

kip_smudgewick/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

kip_smudgewick/4d66206db97560d4.text: Tell that to the paperwork. But... thank you. I'll write it in the margin. In ink.

kip_smudgewick/4df98a09f638b41d.text: Right. Good. Lovely. I'm putting my hat back on now, because it's cold, not for any emotional reason. Apricot? They're all free tonight.

kip_smudgewick/514b723a4d57c3b0.text: Will they let me in? With the... with the horns and the whole... situation?

kip_smudgewick/51b130d090363bd6.text: Pip used to sit with me and choose the faces. She liked them sad. Said a sad one would understand you better. She's little. She's very wise. Gets it from her grandmother. Not from me.

kip_smudgewick/526decc56928edba.text: We shook on it with a hag. I know what a handshake like that's worth. I've got one in my pocket.

kip_smudgewick/52d49d5bd35adf1b.text: I don't think it works like that.

kip_smudgewick/585c674e8ee0a509.text: I've done a lot of deals in my life, and only one bad one. And lately, watching us, I keep getting the feeling I had in the lane that night. The polite feeling. The "sign here, it's all perfectly fair" feeling.

kip_smudgewick/58fbc0f2ed39922e.text: Then his father hears it. Today. Some news you don't leave sitting in a pocket.

kip_smudgewick/59f95f4174816c16.text: Somebody who reads contracts for a living. A lawyer. A scholar. Somebody who isn't scared of it. Somebody very boring.

kip_smudgewick/5d103838f725e383.text: That one. I did that one in the Svalich woods, the first night. I didn't mean to. My hands just did it.

kip_smudgewick/5d872a7c1c753d63.text: He wrote it sloppy. Mister Quillon wrote it sloppy because he never thought I'd get anywhere near a vampire lord. Or read.

kip_smudgewick/5e91446b19f8552a.text: Agreed. Hereinafter, all hanged persons shall be cut down. I'm writing it in. In ink.

kip_smudgewick/609d44fd7654ab97.text: It keeps... the words keep moving. Every time I get to the end of a line it's a different line. I can't. I can't read it on my own.

kip_smudgewick/611adffb471077d3.text: I know that sum. I did it myself, once, for my family. You don't stop doing it after.

kip_smudgewick/6195399d9ad98655.text: We're very sorry. Truly. Have an apricot as well. No obligation.

kip_smudgewick/61c26e6356db6ba7.text: He sent Mister Quillon away from the gate. That winter. Told him we'd manage. And I went after him down the lane, and signed, and came home and said the trees had come back on their own. A miracle. He went to the temple and gave thanks for it.

kip_smudgewick/63f5b0f632937aa3.text: I'll go, if she has one living. I'll take something with me. You don't go to a mother empty-handed.

kip_smudgewick/643b6233e7cc8a0f.text: Look. Look at this one. Mouldy. Proper mould. Green and everything.

kip_smudgewick/647d44536e6f8cf4.text: Clause one: nobody signs anything without reading it. Clause two: nobody goes into the dark alone. Clause three: I bring the apricots. There isn't a clause four. Three's a good number for clauses.

kip_smudgewick/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

kip_smudgewick/68e529bcec015f8c.text: When I get home. Yes. When I get home I'll tell him, and he'll be furious, and then he'll make me dig the whole bottom field on my own, and I'll be so happy I'll cry into the soil.

kip_smudgewick/693859a4fb9f7922.text: Mister Mordenkainen, sir. An honour. I've got questions, if you've a minute. Contractual ones. No rush.

kip_smudgewick/69770335ac27b579.text: We let her go up alone. I said it would be fine. I'm always saying it'll be fine.

kip_smudgewick/69c4f51f59f6c5a0.text: That wasn't a bat. Or it was, but it was also somebody.

kip_smudgewick/6b4f821d43410e86.text: Mum always says read the small print. I never have. I signed it in the lane in the dark, crying. I'm going to read it now. Will somebody help? Some of the words are in a language that hurts.

kip_smudgewick/713cc56e7cab01cc.text: It doesn't say that. It doesn't say soul. It doesn't say contract. It says signature. Any signature.

kip_smudgewick/7371fe0c5cb1aea5.text: Not one promise in it. Mum says read the small print. There isn't any. That's worse.

kip_smudgewick/75d91cbe61ccbf5e.text: I'm frightened of the dark. I have been since I was small. A priestess of the dawn, and I sleep with a light on, and tell everyone it's devotion. And I've come to the darkest place in the world.

kip_smudgewick/7659324dae0f54ff.text: He said he wanted to inspect the goods. I know that voice. Mister Quillon uses it. Now two of them have looked me over.

kip_smudgewick/76bb067c6084defa.text: Somebody's son. I keep thinking that. He was somebody's son.

kip_smudgewick/77953cec90a99f7e.text: Miss, the boat. The boat's drifting into deep water. Could we do the fish later? I'm sure it's fine. It isn't fine.

kip_smudgewick/787a130dadee00ba.text: We got the boy healed. That was the bargain. I've made worse ones, and I still sleep. Mostly.

kip_smudgewick/78a7b2abd50a7ed6.text: No! No. Friends. Of the family, sort of. Would you like an apricot? Can you... no. Sorry. Hello.

kip_smudgewick/7922a334007b0437.text: Am I? Even after? ...You'd know. You've seen me at it. You've seen me give back the change people didn't notice.

kip_smudgewick/7a6c5fe8b90e3aaa.text: We did, um, agree to keep his secret. Verbally. Verbal agreements count. Mum says.

kip_smudgewick/7ca0b19f319377e3.text: Cooks, grooms, a steward. All in rows, all labelled. He keeps his servants like a ledger.

kip_smudgewick/7e3b4fe7ac9f88bd.text: And then I signed that paper in the lane. And now I don't know if I'm the honest one or the horns.

kip_smudgewick/7e6943195b653653.text: It's warm. It's actually warm. I'm going to cry on a vampire's floor and I don't care who knows.

kip_smudgewick/7e898ca09e311751.text: It's written. In her face. People remember who leaned on them, and they remember the price.

kip_smudgewick/80bebe04fe0237f6.text: She sells better than me. She stands on a crate at market and tells people the apricots are sad to be left behind. They buy two. She's going to run the stall one day, and I'll just carry the boxes. That's my whole retirement plan.

kip_smudgewick/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

kip_smudgewick/85516146045095bb.text: Those are my apricots. You got them out of my cart. ...They're beautiful. Keep going.

kip_smudgewick/866f9a96fda08328.text: Course. One apricot. No. No charge. Don't tell my mum; she says I give the stock away.

kip_smudgewick/883d059dc6454a94.text: Nobody happens to be passing here. There's no here to pass. It's surrounded by fog.

kip_smudgewick/8af6e9fc244c3eca.text: Lovely. Thank you. That's all I wanted. Apricot? I've got loads. I always have loads. That's sort of the problem.

kip_smudgewick/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

kip_smudgewick/8baf268f18c67398.text: Read it first, whatever it is. Read the small print, that's what Mum says.

kip_smudgewick/8c4497a34663c6e0.text: Right. His soul. On a contract. Which he's never going to...

kip_smudgewick/8cbfbc7890e81909.text: That is the most frightening kind thing anyone has ever offered me. Apricot?

kip_smudgewick/8f038a7b8ab26313.text: Is it all right if I come in? With the horns, I mean. I can wait at the back.

kip_smudgewick/9135eb1170c153e3.text: Said. Only, we did shake on it. A bargain's a bargain, even a bad one. Especially a bad one.

kip_smudgewick/9365fec9ea11a9e3.text: It's going off. It's going off! LOOK. It's going brown! Oh, thank every god there is, it's ROTTING.

kip_smudgewick/940b1755bea2d063.text: She kept it in a chest behind her chair. For years. I'd have sold it inside a week.

kip_smudgewick/9535d90506be9a49.text: Odd coin, she said. I'll take odd coin. Better than apricots. Don't tell the apricots.

kip_smudgewick/96108375bbd54859.text: Not one bottle left whole, and the vines are sick. I know a blighted row when I see one. You don't forget it.

kip_smudgewick/9657e8760c830de1.text: Right. Yes. Sorry. I'll mind it. ...I'll mind it very carefully.

kip_smudgewick/967d4d41fa2ffc01.text: Freely given. In his own hand. Right. Right. I can do that. I'm a salesman. Getting people to sign things is the entire job.

kip_smudgewick/96c14799500f30b9.text: That gem. The vineyard at the crossroads lost three like it, and their vines are dying. I know what that looks like.

kip_smudgewick/977f38fc8813bfb6.text: Apricot? They, er. They don't go off. Ever. You'll know why.

kip_smudgewick/97be789aae7c3c59.text: Will you open Sorrel's letter before you hand it over? Just a peek. For the paperwork.

kip_smudgewick/9a1e687631c3a0df.text: This one might. First pit off a free tree. No charge. Partners don't charge each other.

kip_smudgewick/9a7837d0a5fb58e6.text: We've put a werewolf in charge of the werewolves. I had concerns. I've brought him apricots anyway.

kip_smudgewick/9b0475037617c492.text: Just there. Freely given, in your own hand. ...I've wanted to say that to someone and mean it nicely for two years.

kip_smudgewick/9d7b7678f31f9fa2.text: They're counting us. Don't let them count us.

kip_smudgewick/9db8b1e9734bc505.text: Legally inadvisable. Deeply appreciated. Please keep offering.

kip_smudgewick/9dd6639754943078.text: Off my road, he says. I looked. No toll house, no milestones with his name. No paperwork at all.

kip_smudgewick/9e147c71a14ba93a.text: A ward keyed to one named party? That's a very specific clause. Somebody wrote that very carefully.

kip_smudgewick/9e28dcc6aad8b75b.text: He took three. Very politely. I think it's going to be fine.

kip_smudgewick/a06689f7c867c7a4.text: A cellar. A mountain. Right. I'll take notes. I'm writing this down. Somebody hold my skillet.

kip_smudgewick/a1ffa5953ef11a52.text: Terms agreed, then, madam. I do hope you're worth it. I really do.

kip_smudgewick/a297a400b16470aa.text: We said we'd stand with you, Baron. A Smudgewick keeps his word.

kip_smudgewick/a400a824c1b11282.text: It might have been his. His bird, I mean. Possibly.

kip_smudgewick/a5dbbc9daaaa4ce3.text: Keep moving. Don't touch anything. Please.

kip_smudgewick/a63d8277675cb1b4.text: His letter treats worship like a debt. I know that kind of letter. I've had that kind of letter.

kip_smudgewick/a6d20f4685774a00.text: He signed it. Like a receipt. So he does sign things. Good to know. No reason.

kip_smudgewick/aa3717c675756663.text: I can't read. Not proper. My name, and "ale", and "danger". Every letter we've had, I've said my eyes were tired and given it to someone else. My eyes are fine. I'm just slow.

kip_smudgewick/ac110112dd954c7d.text: Your lordship. Sir. Your Excellency. Would you sign something for me? It's, er. It's a receipt. For the apricots.

kip_smudgewick/ad9318f4629d344d.text: Could the books say once and a half, neighbour? Trade rate? One merchant to another?

kip_smudgewick/ae2ed25140060884.text: Company. That's all. That's the whole consideration. It's a very good deal. Best I ever made.

kip_smudgewick/ae5cca6bd2163dd0.text: Delivered six casks, got marked paid, got bricked in. I'm never delivering to a castle again. Poor fellow.

kip_smudgewick/af3d2ded67c256a6.text: It's, er. It's a small business matter. Lovely to meet you, sir.

kip_smudgewick/b155443c93bfab49.text: Said. Witnessed. No small print, which is what worries me. Trust me. I'd know.

kip_smudgewick/b2c799c8abe99365.text: I've been lying to my dad for two years, every day, every time an apricot didn't rot.

kip_smudgewick/b440def22aa3a7d5.text: I don't like this house. I'd like that in writing. Signed, and witnessed.

kip_smudgewick/b78183b19dffc04a.text: Forty-one years chained to a desk, and the first thing he did when he was free was tidy it. I understood him completely.

kip_smudgewick/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.

kip_smudgewick/becf7aa23c432abc.text: No rail. Five hundred feet of stairs and not one rail. Whoever built this has never once been taken to court.

kip_smudgewick/bf27abd037394979.text: Most days. Apricot? They don't help. Have one anyway.

kip_smudgewick/bfa53bf660e4ecf4.text: "Must" is a very strong word. Is there a clause? There's always a clause.

kip_smudgewick/c16061934876c596.text: A signature of the lord of the land of mists. Freely given. In his own hand. At the bottom of a dinner invitation.

kip_smudgewick/c2d8d0e65991d085.text: Next time, could we get it in writing? For my nerves, Miss Liriel. Not for his.

kip_smudgewick/c4740a84073c3fe1.text: A werewolf. On our side. Lovely. I'll draw up a little agreement. Terms of non-biting. Nothing formal.

kip_smudgewick/c59a5f2290d3e865.text: You saw that desk. It needed doing.

kip_smudgewick/c5d1f53fad2faedd.text: Pairs. Yes. Two signatures on everything. Very sound practice.

kip_smudgewick/c81b15f3e12709c9.text: A signature. He said "a signature". I thought he meant... I thought it meant his soul. On a contract. Signed over. I thought it was impossible. That's why he offered it.

kip_smudgewick/ca4a19d9b24b5e11.text: That's how they sell, Miss Liriel. Mister Quillon came the week our trees died. They always come in the quiet.

kip_smudgewick/ca622b601d5e95e1.text: It's to my dad. I'm not going to be able to send it. There's no post out of here. I'm writing it anyway.

kip_smudgewick/ca9830a57ffd46a9.text: Six of them carrying one coffin, and they'd measured us for it. I don't like being measured.

kip_smudgewick/cba3b585c31755db.text: Because it's MINE, Thistle. Nobody owns it but me and the mould.

kip_smudgewick/cbc2e6d5bc11f295.text: Master Vosk. Sir. You said you read contracts. I've got a contract. Would you, er. Would you have a look. I can pay. I've got apricots. And money. Mostly apricots.

kip_smudgewick/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

kip_smudgewick/cd6bf24c35e5de2a.text: Two of them, and they've laid the table. I'm sure it's... no. Don't let them get behind us.

kip_smudgewick/ce0f729287b259b8.text: Thank you. I'll keep it somewhere safe. Somewhere very safe. My hat.

kip_smudgewick/ce923b9d925932fb.text: Does it do anything? Heal? Bless? Could it be bottled? Asking professionally.

kip_smudgewick/d08d835564c9b8d4.text: Low on the wall. Right. Is that a riddle? I'm bad at riddles.

kip_smudgewick/d16be1f1a99f6e06.text: But I've sat across a table from a devil, and I know what it looks like when somebody stops counting what things cost other people. I've seen it in a mirror. I don't want to see it in you.

kip_smudgewick/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

kip_smudgewick/d2d5f4f4d2ac059b.text: We robbed the only friendly fire in the valley, then paid it back. With interest. I added interest. I felt I should.

kip_smudgewick/d384561eb8ba6716.text: We bowed to him. I'd like it on record that I bowed ironically.

kip_smudgewick/d69abc7bb8ce328b.text: Mine's very honest. It's the horns that let it down. Do you think they'd take an apricot?

kip_smudgewick/da880d272f7646b1.text: Drawbridge down, gate up, doors wide open. Nobody leaves a door open like that unless they're selling something.

kip_smudgewick/daa75ebacae6948b.text: Not one orchard, though. The whole valley, and not one orchard. How do people live?

kip_smudgewick/dad9287879fa4ff7.text: Apricot? I need to be doing something with my hands.

kip_smudgewick/dc65af2a98071889.text: Accepted. Provisionally. Subject to terms. I'm sorry, I can't help it. Accepted.

kip_smudgewick/df9c57750c2f190b.text: I've carried a lot of things to market. Never anything this light. Or this heavy.

kip_smudgewick/e1277d9bdd542645.text: I know that one. You sign, it's done, and after that you carry it about in your chest.

kip_smudgewick/e21c7a54edf77e06.text: I keep hearing it. The noise it made when it caught. Trees aren't meant to make a noise like that.

kip_smudgewick/e3053c5cc25958d7.text: Respectfully, no. Notwithstanding the excellent company, absolutely not.

kip_smudgewick/e7c96befafadcf8b.text: I looked down. Don't look down. I sell ladders, and I have never wanted one more.

kip_smudgewick/e8271db1cda1b39e.text: If you ever want to sell it... no. No, sorry. Force of habit. Never sell that.

kip_smudgewick/e887a7ee64663f7d.text: ...Apricot? No reason. I just need to hand you something.

kip_smudgewick/e9d8373acc466974.text: People see the horns and count their change twice. All my life. I don't blame them. I'd count mine, if I were them and I saw me.

kip_smudgewick/eb361ecbc3f65860.text: A signature of the lord of the land of mists. Freely given. In his own hand. On the back of a bill for one apricot.

kip_smudgewick/effaf3c64629199e.text: I'd leave something in exchange, all the same. Only all I've got is apricots.

kip_smudgewick/f03c79a5ea5bdeb2.text: Finest apricot-pit charms in three counties. I'd say four, but there's a woman in the next valley who does a very good rabbit.

kip_smudgewick/f122f47716319bf9.text: For what it's worth, my... the people I'm in business with... they're very loud. All the time. I'd take quiet.

kip_smudgewick/f14d331047bb4e4b.text: And I was smiling. Pip says my smile's the only honest thing about me. It wasn't mine.

kip_smudgewick/f159bd18c752844d.text: It says signature, Mister Quillon. Not soul. Not contract. I read it. Mum always says read the small print.

kip_smudgewick/f4d18c7d39cd481f.text: It's warm. Warm like a hand. I don't love that. Here, somebody else hold it.

kip_smudgewick/f6261b3ab17f62bb.text: Did anyone else... has anyone else seen a man? In a grey coat? Just there? At the edge of the light?

kip_smudgewick/f6eef62574a85ee1.text: That's not a custom, madam. That's a contract. A crooked one, with the terms hidden in the honey.

kip_smudgewick/f9f1b1422bc9aad9.text: We let something in the amber give one of us a gift. Do you know what they call a gift, where Mister Quillon comes from? An advance.

kip_smudgewick/fbdfa1e2ce96f8c1.text: She gave him the horse to sell. Now she thinks she tied the rope herself.

kip_smudgewick/fc7aa82712766280.text: Apricot jam on everything. Straw hats on a hook by the door. A sign. A painted sign.

kip_smudgewick/fe64fa46bbf9836b.text: Can I sell these? I'm not going to. I just want to know if I can.

kip_smudgewick/fef49dbbcbcad085.text: "Ratatoille and Smudgewick." Alphabetical, Rat. You'd want it done properly.

kip_smudgewick/ff8d914aab72d077.text: Every market day. I'll show you the good stalls. No obligation.

kiril_stoyanovich/0999aa35a50ea709.text: A wolf can be bought. A wolf just can't stay bought. Take the pups before I remember I'm hungry.

kiril_stoyanovich/1408e8a182cea5f6.text: And you. Yes, you. I smelled you at the bottom of the hill. Pine and smoke and nobody's dog. You weren't raised by people, were you, girl?

kiril_stoyanovich/16ef75b5725cfa00.text: Here's the new law, guests. Stand aside, and you walk out of my hills alive. The master likes his guests unchewed. I'd hate to disappoint him.

kiril_stoyanovich/1d995950bb2fba05.text: No. You've had my generosity. Don't push your luck up my hill.

kiril_stoyanovich/22789b5f45b268f9.text: And the Vistani huntress. How's the leg? I kept the boot. It's on my wall.

kiril_stoyanovich/2a47e0e745ff2de8.text: A hundred for the pups, fifty for the arithmetic. Take them before I remember I'm hungry.

kiril_stoyanovich/396e1bf06dec3ff8.text: Mind your tongue, meat. I've a good memory for tongues.

kiril_stoyanovich/4d4b60a1ff531f31.text: Pity. You'd have made good company at the master's table. As the dinner.

kiril_stoyanovich/532c92971a663d30.text: Don't come back without a present.

kiril_stoyanovich/5b0890d1e5aec867.text: Back again? You're starting to smell like the den. Careful. It sticks.

kiril_stoyanovich/5d9fa3d0aa54c5b6.text: There it is. I knew there was a wolf in you somewhere.

kiril_stoyanovich/6a97ed28b0621083.text: Run along. Tell the valley Kiril Stoyanovich keeps his word. Tell them what else I keep, too.

kiril_stoyanovich/6cdf0071e2225b77.text: Everything in these hills is mine to raise. Ask the deer.

kiril_stoyanovich/707541d8ff8aab3b.text: Now. Get out of my hills, guests, and give the master my regards.

kiril_stoyanovich/7c5e1c9102997694.text: Serve? The old man on the hill feeds us and looks the other way. One day he'll look the other way for too long.

kiril_stoyanovich/83e79cefec7aaa22.text: My favourite customers. Brought another purse? The pups were cheap. Everything else costs more.

kiril_stoyanovich/84c5efa7827eae58.text: The old law kept us thin and hiding in the rocks. The new law eats.

kiril_stoyanovich/8847a5e64507b786.text: Sensible meat. I like sensible meat. The silver's too good for him now. He'll go to the moon at dawn.

kiril_stoyanovich/9ad06216623b5711.text: Then what are you doing walking on a lead with these? Run with us. No walls, no forks, no bowing to burgomasters. The night belongs to you and you belong to nobody. You'd be good at it. You'd be the best of us.

kiril_stoyanovich/a488e0be548f8e27.text: Ha! I like these ones. Shame.

kiril_stoyanovich/aa9dafff080d2715.text: Back for the pups? They're getting fat. Not fat enough. Eleven days.

kiril_stoyanovich/b97283e5ba69408e.text: The pups? They're pack now, or they will be after the moon. Don't fret. I'll raise them right. Strong and hungry, like me.

kiril_stoyanovich/c26d52c016abedc3.text: ...Ha. You've got some wolf in you. Fine. Take the pups. They whine all night anyway, and the master can wait for his army till next moon.

kiril_stoyanovich/d15c62ab59ce29ca.text: Emil! Out of your jewellery. And you've made friends. Meat with swords. The master's guests, if I'm not mistaken.

kiril_stoyanovich/e17d4383428c5bba.text: And the master's red-haired lady, in my den. Oh, he'll want to hear about this. He'll want to hear about it from me.

kiril_stoyanovich/f2010216681c5505.text: I counted. Fewer of you than of us, and I've teeth left over. Now the pups cost a hundred and fifty. Fifty for making me do sums in my own den.

kolyan_indirovich/4d3c6e0cef3550a9.text: My heart gave out the last time he came knocking. Let's see if it does better the second time. Give me a sword I can lift.

kolyan_indirovich/683c4ce40554a8b9.text: Then I'll sit on my own grave and frighten the gravedigger. Don't be long. I've lost enough time.

kolyan_indirovich/6b6a82af892af32f.text: Twenty years I kept this village. Two weeks dead and you lot are digging me up. Is the church still standing?

kolyan_indirovich/b011f113e8933eae.text: Back, are you? I'm ready when you are.

kolyan_indirovich/b02c4ef5fbf863aa.text: I know who you are, girl. I'm dead, not blind. Help an old man up.

kostin/044bb4e362959a35.text: Visitors. The bird-man sent you. He'll send anyone now; he's run out of birds.

kostin/04c4600aa27b02d7.text: Our Mother. Our tree. And the Lord-in-the-Land, lying in the earth, waiting for a heart. When it beats he'll stand up and walk east, and these vines will be the first thing he treads on.

kostin/12696e055102d468.text: A tenant. You sound like the bird-man. He said the same, and look where he sleeps now.

kostin/2d93efadb98de9d6.text: Home. I'll have to find out where that is. Somewhere the trees only drink rain.

kostin/6150adc6af25b0ff.text: The black-eyed one. I took him water in the cage. He wasn't afraid of Mother, and it made her furious. He said he'd ordered his brother to fly, and it was the best order he ever gave. He told the tree so, at the end.

kostin/75accb237a7d4702.text: Because you said the land was older than him, and I can't stop hearing it. I'd like to be wrong about everything. It would be restful.

kostin/b6ba5e9fabdddd20.text: You killed my brothers in the hall. They were singing to the vats. They were happy, for once.

kostin/bcab235c256a3af9.text: Mother will know you're coming! She'll be ready for you!

kostin/c3ac174a55041d83.text: This house belongs to the land, and the land belongs to its lord. You are standing in his press house with mud on your boots.

kostin/cfd5544d53910886.text: I couldn't go up. Two days I've sat here, trying. Every time I stand I hear roots, and nothing else.

kostin/d3ef628918e51120.text: It doesn't know me anymore. It's yours.

kostin/d710155d3de9cc23.text: Listen. There's a gully on the west side; the wardens never watch it. And Mother has your stone in the effigy's chest. When the chant ends, the thing wakes.

kostin/d875fa55ba25ced7.text: I've stood on that hill at midnight with the tree singing. You don't frighten me. You don't even interest me.

kostin/ff9bed8136867fbc.text: ...She says the land and the lord are one. She says if I listen I'll hear his heart in the roots. I've listened. I never heard anything but roots.

krezk_bucket_wife/cb9f4b0d23280019.text: Water to the south row, a word at the shrine, and back. Thirty times a day. My arms are as strong as Cezar's and my knees are holier than the abbot's.

krezk_carver/1d00eb93b945d51b.text: A sun a day, still. And on Sundays my niece comes down off the mountain and lands on my roof. I've had it mended twice. I'd have it mended every week.

krezk_carver/1e56cb8e3a2171fa.text: A sun for the shrine every day since. Sixty years. I thought I was asking for the morning. I think I was asking for the gate.

krezk_carver/1ff0e9d6896afbaa.text: A sun a day, still. But on Sundays I go up the mountain with soup, so on Saturdays I carve two.

krezk_carver/62f4a98e13c3b5e6.text: The toys on the Krezkov stones? Not mine. Mine are suns, all of them, every one for the shrine. Whoever makes those works fast and doesn't care for his fingers.

krezk_carver/7884d8addfafc106.text: A sun for the shrine. One every day. When the shrine is full, I start on the windows. Somebody has to keep asking for the morning.

krezk_carver/819966d1c15b3c88.text: Or he hasn't got fingers. I've looked at the cuts. That's not a knife. That's a thumbnail, and a hard one.

krezk_carver/8c6df0a455cf8315.text: And this. It was our father's. He found it in the high pasture the year Floarea was born and swore it butted back if you were rude to it. I kept it for the day the gate opened. You opened it.

krezk_carver/8dd8089a19a49b00.text: That's my father's joke. Where did you get my father's joke?

krezk_carver/9f5b2d2ac721e68b.text: Floarea was my sister. The whole house took the cough the winter I was twelve, all but me. They went up to the abbey for the cure, and the burgomaster told the watch to bar the gate behind them.

krezk_carver/c84af2a3f7a1c606.text: Then I'll go up. I'm old. I don't frighten.

krezk_carver/ee07dbb273aab999.text: I was the boy on the gate that night. I barred it. My mother told me to, through the boards. She said it was a good gate and I should mind it. I went to the neighbours and took their name, and never said Belview again.

krezk_dragos/01c2fc8ad294b1b1.text: Everything in that thing's stuffing was a bride's. The dowries, the rings, all of it. I've no right to it and neither did she. Take it; she'd want it spent on the living.

krezk_dragos/4d8bff1582894525.text: The field by the stump, in Berez. It's tall as a house. It hates fire. That's all I know that helps.

krezk_dragos/58028921baeb6191.text: Stelian says I'm good with goats. I tell him I have an understanding with them.

krezk_dragos/737e5f701796b4d9.text: You burned it. You let her out. I felt it, here, in the scar, the night you did it, like a hand taking hold of mine and then letting go.

krezk_dragos/808e6d485a7a48fb.text: The old woman came to the landing in her hut and wanted rowing across to the castle side. I said I didn't row her sort. She laughed, and I was a goat. I swam the river. A goat can swim. I didn't know that.

krezk_dragos/b0079f303eaf8547.text: It walks the field by the old woman's stump. Whether she's there or not. Burn it. Please. Let my wife out of it.

krezk_dragos/b86a46dce9054d1c.text: And this was in it too. Not a bride's. Something the old woman stole off a knight who rowed across with me once, years back. It moves when you let go of it.

krezk_dragos/d759f559f16ab67c.text: Vera she kept. Lysaga takes the brides of Berez, the ones the river drowned, and she sews them into something. A queen, she calls it. A scarecrow queen in a dress made of every wedding dress in Berez, and my Vera's in it. I saw her face in the stitching, the night I swam.

krezk_dragos/f73f1631f1ebeffc.text: Berez. The old woman. I wouldn't row her. Vera. Vera's still there. Please.

krezk_dragos/fc1b9bb3ef90b9a1.text: Dragos. My name. Dragos, the ferryman of Berez. Somebody give me a blanket and I'll tell you what she did with my wife.

krezk_fence_mender/f8377c07217d7dc6.text: The billy breaks a rail, I mend a rail. He breaks another. I think he likes the company.

krezk_gate_boy/14a08375f3880984.text: Nobody comes up the road. Except you. Did you see wolves? Did you see the castle? Is it true it has a thousand windows?

krezk_gate_boy/ebac213a6861ca7d.text: Ilya's out of the house! Everybody says it was you. Is it true you've been past Vallaki? Is it true there's a lake?

krezk_goatherd/9f6b06a40bc831cf.text: My best billy turned into a ferryman. I've lost a goat and gained a man who's very good with goats. I'm calling it even.

krezk_goatherd/a9b199ce4228f24a.text: Turned up last spring, already grown, with a woman's ring jammed down on his horn. Nobody's been brave enough to take it off him. He looks at you like he's waiting for something.

krezk_goatherd/db5e1700b5f7edc6.text: That one's Rodica's, and that one's the Burgomaster's, and the one with the horn is nobody's, because nobody's brave enough. Mind your fingers by the rails.

krezk_guard/0046292684ec4004.text: The Belviews come down for bread now. They say the Abbot doesn't. Doesn't eat, doesn't speak, just sits. They seem to think that's our fault. Maybe it is.

krezk_guard/12c21386ed5b35db.text: Back again. The gate's the same as you left it. Shut. Have you found a reason yet, or just more road?

krezk_guard/24db376d4d42af01.text: Fine. Go. And if the Abbot asks, I never saw you. I'd rather he didn't ask.

krezk_guard/2f134c9582c66ff4.text: Gate's barred for the night. If you're inside, stay inside. If you're out here with me, keep talking. It helps.

krezk_guard/312c0d5358c752f3.text: That's far enough. This is Krezk. The road stops here, and so do you.

krezk_guard/3180b839011852a9.text: You put a spell on one of ours. Inside our walls. The Burgomaster will hear of it, and he doesn't like hearing things.

krezk_guard/3b04a0d69e133723.text: You were told that house isn't yours. In Krezk we knock, and we leave when we're asked.

krezk_guard/3c7f29aac052b66b.text: And an angel came down off the mountain and landed on Old Pavel's roof. It was a Belview. Krezk has decided to be very calm about it.
