krezk_guard/40d5fb78b6ae639d.text: Everyone who's ever said that to me wanted to be the door. No.

krezk_guard/40fd5b4a7ea170b1.text: The burgomaster's got a son home who went up the mountain twenty years ago. I don't understand it and I'm not asking. Anna's singing again. All day.

krezk_guard/4f24320a17e7bf62.text: And it's dark, which means I'd not open that gate for my own mother. She knows. She sleeps inside early.

krezk_guard/556172d271c5e674.text: The Abbot came after the nuns were gone. Looks younger than me. Looked younger than my grandmother, too, when she was alive. Folk go up sick and come down well, or they don't come down.

krezk_guard/5aa874c7813fa9ff.text: Saw a light go up the mountain at dawn. Not a lamp. Walked off the top of the peak, the Belviews say, and kept going. The burgomaster went up to the shrine and sat there an hour.

krezk_guard/5e52aba1a5887ece.text: Bats. A cloud of them came down off the abbey at dusk and went east, toward the castle, like they were carrying a letter. The burgomaster's had the gate doubled.

krezk_guard/61c73a2ea85cdd44.text: The wall's very good. Thank you for asking. And now nobody up there will believe a sweet word out of you, so don't waste one.

krezk_guard/6393782adb0c9072.text: And something big has been circling the farms below the wall these three nights. Bigger than a wolf. It isn't one of ours, whatever that means now.

krezk_guard/6b0cb1765da87309.text: The burgomaster's boy is no better. People go quiet passing that house. You can hear Anna singing through the shutters, and you can hear her stop.

krezk_guard/6ba5fd2a6c0b4e77.text: Twice now. Twenty-five gold for the people you took from, or out of the gate, and you can explain yourselves to the wolves.

krezk_guard/6d23ae9a735ea27e.text: We don't take strangers. Not for coin, not for pity, not for stories. The burgomaster opens that gate when there's a reason, and he decides what a reason is.

krezk_guard/6ebbf5eb35ab597f.text: No more children gone from the farms. Not one. Nobody talks about Petru. Nobody talks about why.

krezk_guard/71c3bebc0077d5a9.text: Up there? Holy house, once. My grandmother went up to the nuns when her chest was bad and came back singing. Nobody goes up singing now.

krezk_guard/72d28924a0f1be79.text: All right. All right! I'm fetching the burgomaster. Stand back from the wall and keep your hands where my friends can see them.

krezk_guard/76f2a4094ef5624c.text: Kolyan's girl? Wait here. Don't move. I mean that in the friendliest way.

krezk_guard/770ec8558d2f7a43.text: Ask him about the Belviews. Or don't. I'd rather you didn't, in the end; you might get an answer.

krezk_guard/790a150e84d5502b.text: And the wine's stopped. The Martikovs' cart came every autumn. Not this one.

krezk_guard/7cf025ea14d63d28.text: The burgomaster's boy is sick. A fever since the spring. His last son, Dmitri says. You can hear Anna singing to him through the shutters every night, and you can hear her stop.

krezk_guard/86c969cffdc4570b.text: I'm told the Belview comedian's to be let in on feast days now. I'm told to laugh, as well. I'm practising.

krezk_guard/88724a250762b2a9.text: I saw. Half the wall saw. Wait.

krezk_guard/89b67e4408457b01.text: Up the mountain. The Abbey of St. Markovia. The track leaves the road just there, by the cairn, and climbs till your knees complain.

krezk_guard/9016554849f215ca.text: The smallest of the five children who came home from the hills, Petru, eight years old. He sleeps in the goat pens at night now. The goats don't mind him. That's the part that frightens his mother.

krezk_guard/93d7e7048bcda96f.text: Then whatever's in your purse. Out with it. All of it. Shelter's for Krezk, and so is that, now.

krezk_guard/9cb4c892c0e9e88f.text: That's far enough. Put it back. We let you in, and this is how you thank us? Krezk is a village. Everybody saw.

krezk_guard/9fdc937d7c677a56.text: The abbey's quiet. First time in my life I've looked up at it and not felt looked back at. I don't know if I like it.

krezk_guard/a9d24981f6686000.text: Paid. Next time it's the gate, and the gate doesn't take coin.

krezk_guard/b46c0f76c29f40a7.text: Then I'll do it the hard way. Up on the wall! To me!

krezk_guard/b8280a929cd1cb8a.text: Nothing circling the farms these nights. Petru sleeps in a bed. The goats are said to be very hurt about it.

krezk_guard/b856a76ea9a6889f.text: The burgomaster's boy is out of bed. Pale as milk, but out of bed. Anna carries him to the well and back every morning so he can see the sky.

krezk_guard/b97587fab831f79d.text: The Abbot. Of course it's the Abbot. Wait.

krezk_guard/bb7080d4b401340a.text: Shelter's for Krezk. You're not Krezk. There's a ledge under the pines a mile back that keeps the snow off, if you don't mind the wolves minding you.

krezk_guard/c2c3ef2936f5158c.text: No. I know everyone in Krezk by their cough, and none of them would believe that either.

krezk_guard/ca4c4bc6b819fb2f.text: Back again. My friend on the wall has kept an arrow out for you. He's sentimental that way. Found a reason yet, or just a louder voice?

krezk_guard/d5f881730427ba2b.text: And a Belview came down from the abbey at midsummer with a bell sewn on his hood, and asked could he tell us a joke. Lazar threw a bucket of water over him from the wall. He said thank you, it was a very good bucket, and went back up.

krezk_guard/d783f451756534b3.text: The Abbot takes in anyone. That's the trouble with him. But the burgomaster listens to what he says about people, much as he hates to.

krezk_guard/d981ac372dcd5859.text: Five children gone from the farms below the wall this year. Wolves, they say. Wolves don't lift latches. There's a den up in the hills over the lake, the shepherds say, and the shepherds don't go up there any more.

krezk_guard/e049c7629017bdf9.text: Good. That's done, then. Don't make me do it again; I've got sheep.

krezk_guard/e1ecb5a65768db83.text: There's Belviews on the mountainside. Not the usual ones; worse ones, thin and wild, digging in the snow for roots. The Abbot's let them out, or someone has.

krezk_guard/e8aa2e0c621799a7.text: And there are toys on the Krezkov graves at the pool every morning. Carved ones: horses, wolves. Nobody in Krezk carves like that. Dmitri smashes them. Anna keeps them.

krezk_guard/e8efb0274b00db84.text: The burgomaster's boy is up and about. Running, even. First thing he did was try to climb the wall. We let him. Nobody's had the heart to tell him off.

krezk_guard/fc1194403498d28c.text: Ten gold, for the trouble. The burgomaster would want more. I'm not the burgomaster.

krezk_guard/fedd66bc47971d8f.text: A cart went down the road last night, with something in a white dress sitting up very straight in the back. Nobody here waved.

krezk_guard/ff0b7e8347c5e710.text: The wine? Wait there. Don't go anywhere. Don't let the wine go anywhere.

krezk_guard/ff199f2a53589086.text: Still in one piece? Good. Krezk likes visitors who stay that way. Fewer graves.

krezk_petru/07e873f2ced08c40.text: The big old one, the Grandsire, licked my face after. He said I was his now. He said Kiril was his once, and look how well Kiril turned out. He said he'd come for me at the next full moon. That's tonight. Or tomorrow. It's very close; I can feel it.

krezk_petru/115f8e1bf645cc6d.text: Mirela said you'd come. Mirela says I'm not to be frightened. I'm frightened anyway. I do it quietly.

krezk_petru/2d5751628f04fa52.text: The moon came while we were in there. Before you came. I was the only one it came for. It hurt, and then it didn't, and then I was very fast.

krezk_petru/3282bff40dad69e3.text: It's gone. (He sniffs.) I can't smell the rain any more.

krezk_petru/eb759d22e6ff008c.text: I'm a boy all month now. Except I can still smell when it's going to rain. Mama says that's useful. Stelian says it's cheating.

krezk_petru/eee85352467602d1.text: (He's asleep against a goat, and wakes when the basket goes down.) Is he gone? The big one? (He sniffs.) He's gone. I can still smell the rain. I don't mind.

krezk_wall_watch/8463bf04b51b8772.text: A Belview. In the square. Who opened the gate to a Belview?

krezk_wall_watch/fc2bb6c8050a1ad4.text: (From the back, by the wall.) Go back up your mountain, dog-ear. We've had enough of what comes down it.

krezk_wall_watch/fc57aa45ff2a308d.text: The gate's watched, the wall's watched, and the road is watched most of all. Walk where you like inside. Just walk where I can see you.

krezk_well_wife/cfdd4758f012793f.text: One bucket for the Burgomaster, one for the widow at the end of the row, one for me, and a prayer for each. The well's never frozen. Not once. We don't ask why, we just say thank you.

krezk_woodcutter/2fef8668149d4fe9.text: Ilya's up and about. Took a cord of wood off me this morning to prove it. You did that, I hear. Thank you.

krezk_woodcutter/950c560e08db514c.text: The Burgomaster let you in, so I'll say good day. Wood for the winter. It's always winter for the wood.

lady_wachter/06685818278b04da.text: And don't kill Izek before the festival, however tempting. Today it would look like murder. On the day it will look like justice.

lady_wachter/07923b9b90773cfd.text: A hundred and fifty, as agreed, and the thanks of the burgomistress of Vallaki. My lord will have heard by nightfall; he hears everything in this valley sooner or later. I expect he'll be very pleased with you.

lady_wachter/0bf4c04044996bde.text: Go and tell Vargas, if you haven't. Go and tell the priest. And when you watch that wicker sun tomorrow, remember: the night is longer than any fire anyone has ever lit.

lady_wachter/11292c0b40137a83.text: Your sun burns, Vargas. Look around you. Is anyone warmer?

lady_wachter/117e4185af9e222b.text: You took my sons from me in my own cellar. My purse you left alone. Gentlemen, you have been paid.

lady_wachter/121c5acdc227f7ed.text: The strangers the whole town is pretending not to talk about. Sit. The chairs belong to my book club; they won't mind.

lady_wachter/16c6b7f1b6553dac.text: Come to gloat? Please do. There's so little else to look at.

lady_wachter/19c166ae1d37ed62.text: You killed my sons in my own cellar, and now you come to my parlour. I'd offer you a cup, but I don't think you'd drink it, and you'd be right.

lady_wachter/1e4a7c756782445d.text: Someone has been through my desk. Forty-five gold and a bottle of scent. I mention it only so you know that I know.

lady_wachter/2168c11ca08c4c81.text: No more festivals. No more stocks for a sour face. A town that stops pretending its lord isn't there, and stops annoying him. A vassal who pays her rent sleeps soundly, my dears. Ask Vargas how he sleeps.

lady_wachter/2534002e7fc27f2f.text: Quiet. Curfew. Courtesy. When a black carriage stops at the gate, the gate opens. When a guest of the castle passes, the town bows. In return, the wolves keep to the woods and nobody vanishes without a reason.

lady_wachter/2cb4a71e62ba050b.text: I hear you were civil to our lord, at your burgomaster's graveside. Good manners are so rare in this valley. I knew we'd get on.

lady_wachter/350116afb1b97e70.text: And my new friends at his side. You drank my tea. I hope he gave you something better than biscuits.

lady_wachter/358808503137c464.text: By a fat man who moves his lips. Very well, Vargas. We'll do it now, then.

lady_wachter/3fbef3ff9524ea0d.text: Vargas, you sad little man. Your people don't love you, they fear your watch, and your watch is very small. Now, my dears.

lady_wachter/4bc4b120dde639d4.text: And when he does, I will step up and offer the town something better. The watch will have to choose. I'd like them to see you standing behind me when they do.

lady_wachter/4f1bf5eeaa97aa69.text: You've earned a say in it, my friends. What shall we do with our Baron?

lady_wachter/4fce973cbf70bc7c.text: Vargas? Vargas is a frightened man who has discovered that if you make everyone else frightened, nobody notices you are. He thinks a wicker sun keeps the night out. It doesn't. Nothing does. One simply has to come to terms with the night.

lady_wachter/527348918a3fbf96.text: Vargas. Enough. Your sun won't burn and your people won't smile. They're done pretending, and so am I.

lady_wachter/55a766bab2cc24c2.text: Then go to the square at noon and tell that dreadful herald you're ready.

lady_wachter/58ca11362c1b5267.text: The stocks, then. He built them. It seems only fair that he should try them.

lady_wachter/5dc897874c93cd39.text: Kolyan's girl is welcome to stay, of course. More than welcome. I'd see her very well looked after, and so would my lord.

lady_wachter/5fb10d7bb6d13b5e.text: Oh, the classics. History, mostly. The history of this valley, and who it has always belonged to. We're very well read on that subject.

lady_wachter/6c18725b2a6f4a32.text: Merciful. How unfashionable. Very well: he leaves at dawn with what he can carry, which, knowing Vargas, will be bunting.

lady_wachter/6ea384a69c9c87b0.text: Mice. Old houses have mice. Old families too. More tea?

lady_wachter/70ae9fbf591289ce.text: You've been to Vargas. Or to the priest. It doesn't matter which; the tea tastes the same either way. Sit, if you like. I don't hold grudges. I collect them.

lady_wachter/7ae8f5ac59150c1e.text: Do come again. Bring an appetite and an open mind; I can supply everything else.

lady_wachter/8b1c0da3bb6d6aaa.text: People have, my dear. Ask the fishermen.

lady_wachter/8d6dc9b73abd1d03.text: And Kolyan's girl. You have a face people remember, my dear.

lady_wachter/8ea5206055c4f78e.text: It's more than Vargas ever got.

lady_wachter/8ed21d465f542318.text: No, I didn't. Very well, plainly: at the festival, the Baron's sun will fail. It has rained for a week, and suns are made of straw. When it fails, Vargas will lose his temper in front of the whole town, the way he always does.

lady_wachter/9594b0d7d561a25e.text: Enjoy it, Vargas. He won't let you keep it.

lady_wachter/98090a393f1296af.text: Then I shall do as I like. Take him to the lockup. Tonight, quietly. There's no need to spoil the afternoon.

lady_wachter/99c87740a5c938e9.text: Watch closely, my dears. The best part of any festival is the end.

lady_wachter/9b18d7871da1226d.text: For him? With him. It's his valley; it always has been. I'd simply stop pretending otherwise. Do you know what he does to towns that pretend? Look at your village. Look at its graveyard.

lady_wachter/9fb915ccd07aff63.text: Fools. Very well. Lock me up, if it makes you feel brave. He'll be along.

lady_wachter/9fe3e5ba7be39350.text: Then let him sing at your funeral.

lady_wachter/aa9c8e459f17f9b1.text: I hear you told our lord no, at a funeral, to his face. How brave. I do hope you've grown out of it.

lady_wachter/ac49221a8c89f0d1.text: People of Vallaki. You may stop smiling now.

lady_wachter/adf73e920969615e.text: Wonderful. Then a small task first. The night before the festival, it would be a great shame if that wicker sun got wet. A very great deal of water. The watchman by it will be asleep after midnight. I've seen to it.

lady_wachter/c470f6094b0fdd08.text: And on the day, stand where the watch can see you. When I speak, don't let Izek reach me. That's all. The town will do the rest; it has been waiting years to.

lady_wachter/cbb3da18b7e2f51e.text: My daughter, Stella. She was a clever, wilful girl, and she made a promise to someone she shouldn't have, and he took it very literally. Now she believes she's a cat. She's quite happy. Happier than most of us. Leave her be.

lady_wachter/d28840fac1af3493.text: People of Vallaki: no more festivals. No more stocks for a sour face. Peace, with the lord who has always really ruled us, and an end to this fool's shouting.

lady_wachter/d29b3ad97d810aa8.text: Ask me again in a year, when Vargas is still holding festivals and his lord has stopped finding them amusing.

lady_wachter/d3d81d76adab7cc4.text: Such a shame. Do give my regards to the abbot.

lady_wachter/d53c5bfa1735ddb2.text: I hear you drew steel on our lord. How exciting for you. How very brief.

lady_wachter/d87114e56e759a71.text: And? I'm not ashamed of my correspondents. I'm only sorry you read it before I showed you. I'd have liked to see your faces.

lady_wachter/d9fbf83f4a76d4b5.text: The sun, my dears. Water. After midnight, when the square is empty.

lady_wachter/dc86e1766f695c03.text: No? Another time, then. There's always another festival.

lady_wachter/e27fbb927c20b821.text: Well. The town needs a steady hand, now that it has shaken off a foolish one. I am happy to offer...

lady_wachter/ed7a71e9e38546cc.text: So you've been in my cellar. How bold. Do what you like with it. Vargas reads with his lips moving, and the priest won't believe evil of anyone until it bites him.

lady_wachter/ee7b2fed93b95e96.text: My friends. I believe this is where you come in.

lady_wachter/f1dac3ad9f068ec7.text: There's a word for most things in temples. Very few of them keep the wolves off.

lady_wachter/f29a27a48b315c4d.text: Vargas. Enough. Look at them. Look at your happy town.

lady_wachter/f33e7cf5f2621235.text: You have no idea what you've done. He was going to be kind to you.

lady_wachter/fa61236febd354fb.text: Back for more tea? I'll ring for a fresh pot. Sit.

lady_wachter/fcf7aae160003fff.text: My friends. Sit. You've done this town a great service, whatever the priest says from his pulpit.

lady_wachter/ff9b818c9febf64d.text: You again. Come to see how the losers live? Very comfortably, as it happens. Enjoy your council. It will talk you all to death long before he gets round to it.

lief_lipsiege/02933f601699be1e.text: Lief Lipsiege. Accountant to the count, by appointment, since the year they rebuilt the bridge at Vallaki. The second time they rebuilt it.

lief_lipsiege/087422d10073ad27.text: Everything. Vallaki's tithe. Wine from the vineyard, when there is wine. Rents from Krezk. Candles. Gowns. He is a very poor spender and a very good collector. It makes for dull books.

lief_lipsiege/3c1f47a4c33b4067.text: Behind the lady in the long hall, of course. The alcove. Push the left side of the frame. He likes her to keep an eye on it.

lief_lipsiege/3f796c8bcdff561b.text: Vallaki. Their tithe books are a disgrace; I have seen them. Yes. Yes, I could do something with Vallaki.

lief_lipsiege/4cb7b2286fcc7684.text: I left once. I got as far as the gate. Rahadin brought me back, and the next morning the smith came up with this. That was forty-one years ago.

lief_lipsiege/5058db8a373b53ab.text: If you are from the treasury, you are late. If you are not from the treasury, you are interrupting. Which?

lief_lipsiege/5ccfb715a51397fe.text: You again. A visit from you costs me eleven minutes on average. I have opened a column for it.

lief_lipsiege/689e89536027ed48.text: Wherever I like. I shall have to make a list. I have never had to make that list.

lief_lipsiege/68be2f6398a236a9.text: Behind the lady in the long hall. Push the left side of the frame. There. Now I have stolen from him too. How very modern of me.

lief_lipsiege/6d81173763fc370a.text: Don't tell Rahadin I told you. And don't take more than you can carry. It unbalances everything.

lief_lipsiege/8075fa99104f9406.text: There was an "A." before her. Same size. That account is closed. I closed it myself. Neat hand. I always have a neat hand.

lief_lipsiege/83d160e80c6b92b2.text: Forty-one years, three months and a week. I shall have to close the column.

lief_lipsiege/844463d468278316.text: Seven. Wood is cheaper than stone and the river is patient. I have the figures.

lief_lipsiege/86a1311893a030e1.text: The yellow room, third floor. The account is open: "G., sixteen, three gowns, all one size. Pending."

lief_lipsiege/8af387e3684f2aa3.text: I have not tried again. I find the arithmetic discourages it.

lief_lipsiege/c5ac966fdd0ce0a8.text: He is very good at his work. I keep the count's accounts. He keeps the count's other accounts. His have more names in them.

lief_lipsiege/da65623ed9274e63.text: Don't. Don't touch the chain. The rug. The count had it woven for this office. It does not like things to leave.

liriel_dawnsong/013821663c0f2fed.text: So I'll carry it. All the way up to the castle, if I have to, and I'll sing it in his chapel.

liriel_dawnsong/0149c3391840d6f9.text: Gold first, then white. The snow went pink, as if it were embarrassed to be seen. You told me that. You were sent to keep the morning for these people. Keep it.

liriel_dawnsong/01605e6b7ca92b37.text: Kip. Thank you for telling us. We'll get you home to tell him yourself.

liriel_dawnsong/035c19db0acd11ed.text: The dawn comes, my lady. Even here. I'll sit with you until it does.

liriel_dawnsong/045c987aafee7637.text: You want the last light out. I carry one. We have nothing to discuss.

liriel_dawnsong/062744b993b2b4ae.text: My master died before my last lesson. I asked him what it was and he said it was in a letter I'm not allowed to read. I make jokes all day so nobody notices I'm not finished.

liriel_dawnsong/065e4c9ea15a1722.text: Then let's be late. Rudely, unforgivably late.

liriel_dawnsong/073fc209345038a9.text: Then I'll pray for the next soul who would have climbed that hill, and will never know to thank us.

liriel_dawnsong/07e0fe479efbe8cf.text: Everyone says that. I've never understood why it surprises them.

liriel_dawnsong/09748db1c66829d7.text: Every voice around that man is someone he killed. He's carrying a graveyard about with him.

liriel_dawnsong/09bdc187b6e71cad.text: And you? What do you think happened?

liriel_dawnsong/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

liriel_dawnsong/0d4f42b600edac1e.text: Every one of them was somebody's child. I'll say their names as we pass.

liriel_dawnsong/0e145d4df4dee989.text: He is of the heavens. My Lord's own heavens, I think. And underneath, something has soured, the way milk sours.

liriel_dawnsong/0e85833d95a0a0c7.text: The village never harmed her. Her nurse did, and all of Berez drowned for it. Oh, those poor people.

liriel_dawnsong/10401d74d4be9f98.text: Thank you for asking. Asking is the first step of every road I know.

liriel_dawnsong/108f18acdc4a1858.text: Wherever that light went, it was going home.

liriel_dawnsong/11252994aa5a8f0f.text: You carried it too, you know. All the way up here. I could never have got it up those stairs on my own.

liriel_dawnsong/11f024ce5a98b9ad.text: The Morninglord made bread before he made kings. There's a reason.

liriel_dawnsong/12b1c2bddcc9fb22.text: She thanked us. In his name. I can still hear it.

liriel_dawnsong/132903772db2e1ea.text: Whoever kept this crib made never stopped hoping. That's the saddest kind of housekeeping.

liriel_dawnsong/13c2d3f0389c18f1.text: We put a man in the ground without a word said over him. That's not a burial. That's tidying.

liriel_dawnsong/13c4c24dcd31119d.text: Fire is a kind of dawn. The small kind. It will do, for now.

liriel_dawnsong/13e8bed3db6f666f.text: I knew the answer before I asked. I only wanted to hear it in someone else's mouth.

liriel_dawnsong/1466fccae76ffa48.text: They answer, every one of them, the moment you speak. My god has been quiet all week.

liriel_dawnsong/15066ba39d1eab61.text: Never eat a stranger's pie in a cursed valley, Ratatoille. We teach it to novices.

liriel_dawnsong/17a00c30662db447.text: Don't. Whatever this buys us, we'll be paying for it forever.

liriel_dawnsong/17aa92e3b843e585.text: I've never done that. It feels terribly vain. ...It feels rather nice. Don't tell the Morninglord.

liriel_dawnsong/18c6bdaa91827140.text: I've never prayed into a silence before. It's very loud.

liriel_dawnsong/18d360375ee97fb8.text: I've never told anyone this. Not my abbess. Not the Morninglord, though He knows, of course. He knows everything. It's very inconvenient.

liriel_dawnsong/1aa0a4745cbb31c1.text: Right. Read it. I can do that. I'll read it tonight. I'll read it tomorrow. I'll definitely read it.

liriel_dawnsong/1c10d65c013a71a3.text: Is that how it is for you, Kip?

liriel_dawnsong/1dd1ff2f41301ff4.text: Then I'll carry it. I've carried it this far.

liriel_dawnsong/1e14fb995627e827.text: "Cared for." I've read that phrase on too many graves.

liriel_dawnsong/1eafe6d668666ca9.text: He's celestial. An angel, or the next thing to one. And something in him has turned, the way milk turns.

liriel_dawnsong/1ef4d2e15e644c8e.text: He'd filled his pockets with stones. A man doesn't do that in a hurry. He'd been thinking about it for days.

liriel_dawnsong/1fc0e71bd0bfaf44.text: For her son. She knew what she was doing. That's what makes it hard to carry.

liriel_dawnsong/205745a51f540ea7.text: Not yet. I'm sorry. Not like this.

liriel_dawnsong/2237a812c71f84d2.text: I'm not angry. I'm frightened, a little, and I'd rather be frightened out loud than in the dark. You know how I feel about the dark.

liriel_dawnsong/2273825068b77321.text: There's no shame in a wound you didn't choose.

liriel_dawnsong/235cb466d45d37e8.text: A dead man for an ally. Calling a soul back is no small mercy, and no cheap one.

liriel_dawnsong/238bd3b22a2bbbd6.text: ...It does work. That's the trouble with you. You're always right in the wrong way.

liriel_dawnsong/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

liriel_dawnsong/250418619cd19143.text: Brother Kesten came up this hill alone with a cudgel and a prayer. I'll wear his symbol a while, so that someone finishes the walk.

liriel_dawnsong/256f160d4b68ac0f.text: There. Did you feel that? Like a window opened in winter. He's here. Wherever somebody carries Him, He's here.

liriel_dawnsong/27310d8ff4779566.text: You'll stand at the front, Kip. With me.

liriel_dawnsong/2798d5c862e21128.text: We took the old man's strongbox in a war he was losing. I'd like that remembered when we're being proud of ourselves.

liriel_dawnsong/27e859764aa4dbec.text: Someone who wants a church to be just a room. Which tells you who.

liriel_dawnsong/287265aa11e6d6ea.text: That's a hard sum. I won't pretend it isn't.

liriel_dawnsong/2a0923a78c34bb25.text: Everyone knew, my dear. Even Thistle knew, and Thistle thinks a carriage is a box on wheels.

liriel_dawnsong/2b47b3ec897eeff0.text: Morning's grace. ...It's still dark. I'll say it anyway. That's rather the point of me.

liriel_dawnsong/2bed4ec2e9a497a1.text: Oh. Don't mind me. It's a devotional light. The Morninglord likes a lamp lit.

liriel_dawnsong/2c41010a80e6dae7.text: It won't keep him from coming home. It will make sure he hates the bed when he gets here.

liriel_dawnsong/2c6c1289900589b3.text: We left that child up there. With him. I won't pretend otherwise.

liriel_dawnsong/2d109500003e6356.text: You never had your last lesson, you said. Perhaps you're having it now, Wren. Slowly.

liriel_dawnsong/2de50cbeb03c32b8.text: He walked out of the square like a man going to bury someone. I suppose he was. Himself, the one he'd been.

liriel_dawnsong/2df029566fec9449.text: I was sent here to carry a light. I didn't know it would be a borrowed one. I'll carry it carefully.

liriel_dawnsong/2e446bca7348c754.text: He has kept every promise he's made us. I'm watching him too, Wren. Kindly, and with both eyes.

liriel_dawnsong/2e917bcfc201dde2.text: Four hundred years. Master Sorrel always did take his time with the post.

liriel_dawnsong/2f3c1ff808a3c61c.text: Earth to earth, and the dark to the dawn. Rest, Kolyan Indirovich. Let no voice call you up again.

liriel_dawnsong/2f5fc22c60866e77.text: Nothing. A man with forever doesn't save, Wren. He only keeps.

liriel_dawnsong/2ff792540eb8f3d9.text: Would you? Into this? ...Yes. I think you would. That's either very brave or very foolish, and I find I don't mind which.

liriel_dawnsong/3110e4b812d66a8d.text: Holy ground again. You can feel it in your teeth.

liriel_dawnsong/315030aede5da1ec.text: A shrine to a lord, not a god. They knelt to the wrong one.

liriel_dawnsong/3277a8230e209d51.text: You're elven. Or you were. What are you now?

liriel_dawnsong/327cbb5980001819.text: I won't weep for her, dear heart. I won't call it clean, either.

liriel_dawnsong/32f80d945f1b328d.text: That is the kindest bad theology I have ever heard. Thank you.

liriel_dawnsong/33a9d013a1b4ad2f.text: I always thought heaven was... finished. Perfect. That the messengers were the safe part. And here's one who stayed too long in the dark and forgot what he was for.

liriel_dawnsong/33c7ab885f8ff131.text: That isn't a tree. That's a grave that learned to stand up.

liriel_dawnsong/358ead387511d47c.text: Go gently. Nobody will lock that door again.

liriel_dawnsong/3770c0f3c0d28ffd.text: Wolves don't keep ranks. Not on their own.

liriel_dawnsong/37f2d0c2b26d6143.text: We'll keep her behind us, always. Always.

liriel_dawnsong/389e88fb3ec7f5c7.text: Morning's grace on you, Sir Godrick. Truly, now.

liriel_dawnsong/38c5bd305da8d8fb.text: There's a law older than both of yours about children.

liriel_dawnsong/38df7ecad3ca1bf6.text: He's at rest, Wren. Words help. So does a straight grave, and someone who stays to dig it.

liriel_dawnsong/395dfeaf49d7444b.text: We've sworn ourselves to a man who jails widows for laughing. Someone should say that out loud.

liriel_dawnsong/3a066bcc41e85bbb.text: I like towns. Bit. Beds. The little cakes. People singing in the big room at the inn. And I don't fit in them, and I don't fit in the woods any more either. I don't fit anywhere.

liriel_dawnsong/3a9a1747f0c2ace0.text: She was his nursemaid. Once he was only a baby in someone's arms, and somebody sang to him.

liriel_dawnsong/3ad9140569ab6f70.text: He's lovely when he's flustered, isn't he? Oh. Did I say that aloud?

liriel_dawnsong/3c25ba91e37d73df.text: That is not a choice I will carry for her. Remember that I said so.

liriel_dawnsong/3d2a8e7837866807.text: Morning's grace upon you, stranger. The Morninglord keep you, and the dark keep its distance.

liriel_dawnsong/3d5a94fd55999798.text: I know which I'd rather have nowhere near a child. They're the same answer, which is a mercy.

liriel_dawnsong/3e670914c069cd99.text: Sorry for a very long time. That is a long penance, little one. Be at peace.

liriel_dawnsong/417b649a6609dca7.text: The novices write down whoever they pray for, so nobody is forgotten at the morning hymn. I started this in Death House. I've never had to cross anyone out. I mean to keep it that way.

liriel_dawnsong/41e2a0eb223cfd36.text: That's either very wise or very silly, and I can't tell which, and I think that means it's wise. Thank you.

liriel_dawnsong/421ecc27a5f2ffbe.text: Dawn keep you, stranger, and the dark keep its distance.

liriel_dawnsong/42c33af581acebb8.text: Of course. The Morninglord made bread before he made kings. You're the nearest thing to a temple we have out here.

liriel_dawnsong/435fa12409ed468b.text: Did you see his face when it all came back? He looked round for people who weren't there any more.

liriel_dawnsong/4503a76638b93b89.text: I knelt to him. I kneel every morning of my life, and last night my knees didn't know the difference.

liriel_dawnsong/45cdb9bd736a264f.text: My dad sent the devil away from our gate. Told him we'd manage. I went after him down the lane and signed behind Dad's back. I came home and said the orchard came back on its own. He went to temple and gave thanks for it. I've been lying to him for two years.

liriel_dawnsong/45d2da253af31a9c.text: I'd rather cook than cast. I always would. I learned magic so people would sit with me, and I'm good at it, and I'd still rather be in a kitchen. That's a terrible thing for a wizard to say.

liriel_dawnsong/45e2b74c7273c5bd.text: I shall say grace at his table. Aloud. I should like to see his face.

liriel_dawnsong/45e6c424a573496e.text: He isn't here. I know. That is what faith is for. You need none; you are right here. That is how I know you are not him.

liriel_dawnsong/471a0aa9d01b715b.text: He wore the dawn like a coat, to lure decent people close. I find I am very angry, and I don't mind it at all.

liriel_dawnsong/477efd740fdc95eb.text: I've tried to find a kind way to say this, and there isn't one, so I'll say it as plainly as Thistle would.

liriel_dawnsong/48886956a5eaf3e4.text: We promised that poor creature his door, and I mean to keep it. I want it said that I noticed, all the same.

liriel_dawnsong/49318802a797ae7c.text: I didn't truly need her answer. I only wanted to hear someone else say the dawn comes.

liriel_dawnsong/49424b1399bf72be.text: We stood and watched an angel give a dead girl to the devil. I keep seeing the dress.

liriel_dawnsong/4aa98ff158ae0e21.text: Night hags. Fiends who ride sleepers' dreams and keep the souls they steal in little bags. I'd hoped those were stories for novices.

liriel_dawnsong/4adb05d57763c397.text: The dawn comes, little ones. Go on ahead of us. We'll follow one day, though not too soon.

liriel_dawnsong/4b55ccd64aec9909.text: Forgive me, sir knight. You're dead.

liriel_dawnsong/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

liriel_dawnsong/4c86341ba6be616f.text: Then we keep looking. Or we keep our word another way.

liriel_dawnsong/4ce70c1beef1ab7b.text: Ireena. The man in the water. Would you like to speak of him?

liriel_dawnsong/4d4aa20e8f242e93.text: A valley in a ring of mountains, and no sun. I've seen this sky before. I saw it on the morning of my vows.

liriel_dawnsong/4d8455c78fc689a3.text: Not while the wood that sent it is still standing.

liriel_dawnsong/4d92b34b624cee79.text: That isn't how lanterns work, Godrick. Thank you. It helps more than you know.

liriel_dawnsong/4fcfb1713e367875.text: We'll see him buried right. You have my word on it.

liriel_dawnsong/51288554aba60917.text: We frightened an old woman into reading for us. Let it be written that I was against it.

liriel_dawnsong/52141d398ce2067a.text: That isn't how grace works, my dear.

liriel_dawnsong/535cde9b3924f38f.text: The bones. The children in the house. The little lights. ...Yes. Those weren't dreams. I was there for those. So were you.

liriel_dawnsong/53fdb183e1d49dd0.text: A cradle song, sung every night by someone who loved him. Keep it close. Someone in this house will know it.

liriel_dawnsong/54622bed5129c701.text: Rest. You kept it long enough.

liriel_dawnsong/5469ce173a29119e.text: Then let it be so. I'll watch, and I'll hope. I'm very good at both; I've had practice.

liriel_dawnsong/5886263dc38e6d16.text: He came up the well himself. Not his wolves. Not his brides. We have hurt him, and he knows it.

liriel_dawnsong/593746aa6b32ea3f.text: I'm going to pretend I didn't see that, and then I'm going to pray about it anyway.

liriel_dawnsong/59780cdbf45b5070.text: He does answer. Not always quickly. Never like that.

liriel_dawnsong/5a173abccbaf6825.text: Lycanthropes who worship nothing but keeping watch. I was taught they were all cursed. She seems more tired than cursed.

liriel_dawnsong/5a7d3dfcc43434f7.text: We killed an angel. I helped. I'd do it again. I don't know what that makes me, and I'm not going to pretend I don't mind.

liriel_dawnsong/5a9b31fe7608a1e1.text: Go with the dawn, old dragon.

liriel_dawnsong/5ae4b73d85ed6be4.text: Some birds in old places carry more than seeds. I'd follow it, one day.

liriel_dawnsong/5b0af5068a778239.text: You've carried it this far, Wren. You'll carry it the rest.

liriel_dawnsong/5b0e42d044c40b87.text: It's carrying his wounds for him. Every one. A reliquary that keeps the hurt instead of the saint.

liriel_dawnsong/5ee0f6e181a39df1.text: I was wrong. It isn't something one person carries. It's heavier than that, and lighter. Do you understand? I'm not certain I do.

liriel_dawnsong/5ef4474454be083c.text: Whatever holds them is still in that house. Nobody has let them go.

liriel_dawnsong/5f1636c31eceecbf.text: He went out to the yard to cry, I think. Let's give him a minute. The Morninglord made bread before he made kings, you know. There's a reason.

liriel_dawnsong/5f299574b9b453d9.text: Whatever brought us here went to some trouble. That's worth remembering.

liriel_dawnsong/6018911870612fdd.text: We passed a hanged boy at the crossroads and left him to the crows. I prayed as we walked. It wasn't enough.

liriel_dawnsong/602a8af3ef9c0b79.text: Then they have been waiting in that road a very long time. Poor lambs.

liriel_dawnsong/609581a62ea52359.text: Sisters needn't agree to share a house. Good night to you, lady. He sends his regards.

liriel_dawnsong/60c433c7c1b23b5a.text: Morning's grace. I'm sorry. I didn't mean to wake anyone.

liriel_dawnsong/6243477b5611229c.text: My faith has never once been asked to bend. He didn't ask. He just bent it, and handed it back.

liriel_dawnsong/626781f7e5bbb839.text: Mind the bite, and we'll get along.

liriel_dawnsong/62da417bc2bcef8f.text: You can belong to the woods and the town both, dear heart. Most of us belong to more than one place. It's how we know we're not lost.

liriel_dawnsong/6308abb798cbb589.text: Two bites on her throat, and she still keeps her own counsel. Most people would be raving by now.

liriel_dawnsong/6487bd509530e9f7.text: It shook it. I could feel it go, like a bell. And then it rang.

liriel_dawnsong/64d52b7304ae73b0.text: That wasn't justice. That was only the end of something.

liriel_dawnsong/6612b1b5fdc9de17.text: Yes. He always knows. That's the comfort of him. It's also, I'm learning, the difficulty.

liriel_dawnsong/668e2cbbd0c84ec3.text: Be at peace, sister. The dawn comes, even for you. Especially for you.

liriel_dawnsong/eb3e157975b849db.text: May I ask you something? You needn't answer tonight.

liriel_dawnsong/eb78bfc297cc3b35.text: He filled this valley with graves, and we swore to leave him living. The words sat in my mouth like stones.

liriel_dawnsong/eb870c36caaeca8d.text: There. Do you feel it? Out it goes, little one. Be at peace.

liriel_dawnsong/ec196c18fd457dfd.text: No. He isn't in charge of anyone. That was never the point of Him. ...I thought you knew that.

liriel_dawnsong/f0c647870abbf00a.text: We'll answer for it. Not to you, Father. But we'll answer.

liriel_dawnsong/f18f9517dcaf8f16.text: They were. Be at peace, all of you.

liriel_dawnsong/f2db427da5dcbafa.text: Let it be quick, then, and let nobody in the crowd be hurt.

liriel_dawnsong/f3553784fd44677c.text: Wren, you've made eleven jokes since breakfast.

liriel_dawnsong/f48d02d429d572d2.text: We just helped dress a corpse for the devil and called it a wedding. I'll be praying about this for the rest of my life. However long that is.

liriel_dawnsong/f523288dde5bc66a.text: It sounds better at dawn. Everything does. That's rather the point of dawn.

liriel_dawnsong/f79c6fb07ce6977a.text: For the bread, and the fire, and the hands that made them. Especially the hands.

liriel_dawnsong/f8805f87aded2058.text: Made by people who believed the sun would come back. Then I'm not the first. Oh, I'm so glad I'm not the first.

liriel_dawnsong/f8a427fdd31c0462.text: Dear heart, in a town, one doesn't sniff people to see if they're lying.

liriel_dawnsong/f90cb9f73783ab94.text: There. Now there are two of us facing east. That's a congregation, technically.

liriel_dawnsong/f9f0abe0d7fc33dd.text: Perhaps not. But it won't come by being cruel, either. I've looked. It isn't down that road.

liriel_dawnsong/fa16148b640e050b.text: Bless this table, and the one who made it.

liriel_dawnsong/fa7f1e48e2ed6f56.text: That's very kind, dear heart. Please don't bite anything near my face.

liriel_dawnsong/fe3606d80807b137.text: He sits in his church and won't speak. An angel. In the dark, with nobody to pray to. I'd have thought that couldn't happen to one of them.

liriel_dawnsong/ff972b3b212e721f.text: So Kasimir is a real man, somewhere in this valley. Not only a name on a letter.

ludmilla_vilisevic/2734ad73504fe617.text: Poetry. A man loved a woman who did not love him back, and wrote four hundred pages about it. I find it restful.

ludmilla_vilisevic/353123d5449e809b.text: Yes? Be brief. I am at a good part.

ludmilla_vilisevic/bd521799203f4cc2.text: Of course not. That is the poem.

ludmilla_vilisevic/e7fc2d735b1f2cb6.text: They are his guests, Volenta. You may look. You may not touch.

ludmilla_vilisevic/ec4117f3a32b3484.text: It swings open, you know, onto his money. Push the left side of the frame. He thinks I don't know. I know everything in this house that hurts.

ludmilla_vilisevic/fc84af068f79630c.text: He has had her painted forty times. I counted. There is one in the long hall he visits more often than he visits me.

luminita/0d2878bcf2224c6a.text: Then he's still in Vallaki, drinking the money. Good. I hope he drinks all of it and comes home with a headache.

luminita/20d1e887bfc46c70.text: Our cousins camp by the lake outside Vallaki. Arrigal runs it. He smiles more than I do and means it less. Tell him Luminita says the horse was mine. Watch his face.

luminita/274bf636856e2c98.text: She was Nicu's favourite. He used to ride her bareback in the river and pretend he couldn't hear Radu shouting.

luminita/43ef21b885f6a106.text: Nicu. My brother. He rode to Vallaki four days ago to sell a mare, and said he'd be back the next night with a sack of flour and a new song. He always comes back with a new song.

luminita/57a0999cc89f2417.text: Still no rider on the road? No. You'd have said.

luminita/8217c5a5435ca2a7.text: Huh. He doesn't do that for anyone but Nicu. Fine. You can stay.

luminita/87cf0b6cc8b65d90.text: And you left him hanging there. For the crows. Go away. I'll ride out to him myself.

luminita/8ad676299a32f7d4.text: You again. I'm still brushing the same horse. It's very clean now.

luminita/9c3fbaf875e96ca0.text: You came along the road. Did you pass a rider? Black hair, silver earring, a laugh you can hear across a field. Too handsome, and he knows it.

luminita/b67ae2e384cb8fe6.text: Thank you. I'll keep her far away from the road.

luminita/c0310e89a8ec5303.text: And he got up again, and you put him down. Good. Good. He'd have hated walking around for somebody else.

luminita/c1dfc8db0a3b14c0.text: You're the ones who found Nicu. Stanimir told me. I don't want to talk about it. Ask me something else.

luminita/cb552ff197b2a1e4.text: You cut him down. Strangers, and you cut him down and put him in the ground.

luminita/d04f8fb389ca65dc.text: Grandmother's remedy. It tastes like plums and regret. Take it, before I change my mind.

luminita/d13babef1224884c.text: The mare was mine. I found her loose in the woods with a Vallaki brand on her rump and a broken halter, and I said, sell her, Nicu, sell her back to them, nobody will know. I said nobody will know.

luminita/e61ab5542a48f667.text: Walls, bells, banners, and a burgomaster who throws a festival every week and calls you a traitor if you don't smile at it. They hanged my brother for a horse. Smile at the gate.

luminita/eab8e8a56d430473.text: He doesn't like strangers. Neither do I. It's nothing personal; we just have taste.

luminita/eeea6649f9ca30fb.text: You again. The ones who cut him down. Sit with the horses if you like. They're better company than people.

luvash/64a572c9d3c7ff2b.text: Take this. It's not enough. Nothing would be enough.

luvash/66767035b732cf69.text: Go away! Unless you've come to find my girl. Have you come to find my girl? Arabelle. Seven years old. Black hair. Gone from her bed since last night, and my brother says she wandered!

luvash/7c1bc14cb90f215b.text: My friends. My friends! Every Vistani wagon in Barovia is your wagon now. Every fire is your fire. I've told them. I've told them all.

luvash/9f3fc92e33ce7f3b.text: You tried. They tell me you tried. Go away now. Please.

luvash/a0397bb660d3b605.text: You will? Strangers? None of my own people will, because Arrigal says not to. Find her and I'll owe you more than I have. Ask at the fire. Somebody saw something. Somebody always sees something.

luvash/abf47bbbf26a4f39.text: She was in her bed when I went to sleep. In the morning, the bed was cold and the wagon door was open. She never opens the door. She's afraid of the lake.

luvash/aea24ecdab977b7c.text: On your lives. I'll hold you to every one of them.

luvash/affcdc5968d28e75.text: And this. My grandmother swam the Luna in it, all the way to the falls and back. In the water it makes you a fish. The lake took my girl once; let it never take you.

luvash/b27b96bbd42702f6.text: No. No! I only just got you back!

lydia_petrovna/09e2cb7a7b005777.text: My marshals! I've started your sashes. Gold thread. It's taking forever, but forever is what we've got, Vargas says.

lydia_petrovna/1d97f75ff6809e03.text: Isn't it wonderful? I stitched every ray myself. Vargas says it's the best sun yet. He says that every week, but this week I believe him.

lydia_petrovna/22d357d37e0ae1b9.text: We leave at dawn. Lucian has found us a cart. I've packed the bunting. I don't know why. Habit.

lydia_petrovna/2a93651e241f9b0b.text: Vargas says if we're happy enough, nothing bad can get in. I used to think that was silly. Then I thought: what if it isn't? What if we stopped and that's the night it gets in? So I sew.

lydia_petrovna/43177859a30b9455.text: Oh, you were marvellous. Vargas was so frightened. He's always frightened. He's never once been right before.

lydia_petrovna/4770cd63d2e150c7.text: I'll sew you sashes. Proper ones. With your names on.

lydia_petrovna/4eecf033c3feaca6.text: They say he's not the Baron any more. He was so proud of being the Baron. I'll have to find him something else to be.

lydia_petrovna/5a5216aad616c158.text: Oh! Guests! Vargas didn't say. Vargas never says. Do you like the bunting? I did the bunting. I did all of it.

lydia_petrovna/630c92071e8e42b2.text: Izek is dead. I know I should be sad. I'm trying very hard to be sad. It's like sewing in the dark.

lydia_petrovna/6a71f2598703839c.text: I take him soup in the stocks twice a day. He tells everyone who passes that it's a new festival. Some of them laugh. I'm glad. Someone should.

lydia_petrovna/78fde7f372b2d85a.text: Come to the festival! Wear something yellow, if you have it. If you haven't, I've got bunting.

lydia_petrovna/877e0fd03257697b.text: Back again! Sit, sit. Mind the pins.

lydia_petrovna/95a924c0adf4fbd4.text: We're to grow turnips, Vargas and I. He doesn't know yet. I'm going to tell him it's a festival.

lydia_petrovna/96e5c781688d238c.text: Isn't it? Forty yards for the Blazing Sun. Sixty for the Swallows, but the swallows didn't come, so I've unpicked it for the sun. Nothing's ever wasted in this house. Except the swallows.

lydia_petrovna/9a6ebbab2ac394cb.text: Only he hasn't come down in four days. And the maids who took up his trays haven't come down either. Vargas says they went to Krezk. Would you look in on him? He won't let me up.

lydia_petrovna/cf047d4c393e1bdf.text: Please don't let her hurt him. He isn't clever and he isn't kind, but he's mine, and he only wanted everyone to be happy.

lydia_petrovna/d4c2301c580fd368.text: Victor? He's studying. In the attic. He's terribly clever; he gets it from me, Vargas says, which is the kindest thing Vargas says.

lydia_petrovna/d52b790edefd4f80.text: Please. Please, Fiona. He's a silly man. He only wanted everyone to be happy. Don't hurt him.

lydia_petrovna/e24b4b2825773428.text: He only wanted everyone to be happy.

lydia_petrovna/ec64bc7a6cdca193.text: And Victor's gone. There was a light in the attic, and then there wasn't any Victor. I keep laying a place for him.

lz_old_fisher/2e1aa45ebdd58527.text: Forty years I fished this water. Then the fish went deep and the men went to Vallaki, and here I am, mending nets for a lake that's stopped answering.

lz_old_fisher/30019da825a70812.text: You stood on my step between me and the lake. Forty years I've been waiting for it to come up that shore. I never once thought anybody would stand there.

lz_old_fisher/32a7f1aa83a4a971.text: Before the count put the dam on the Luna there was a village where the lake is. Pescari. My grandmother was from there. When the water came up, the folk came up the hill, mostly. The ones who wouldn't leave the chapel stayed in the chapel. The bell's still down there.

lz_old_fisher/3887869cedad08ec.text: You stood on my landing between the lake and a man who'd put a child in a sack. I've been thinking about that. I don't know what I think yet.

lz_old_fisher/38fc71ffcb7c1826.text: You want to know why the fish went deep? Nobody's asked me that in forty years. Sit down, then.

lz_old_fisher/3aa66b6cf38b19b7.text: Well. It was always going to be one of us.

lz_old_fisher/424bf74602238405.text: After moonrise. Stand on the landing and you'll hear it. Then you'll see them. Then you decide what to do about Bluto. I've had forty years and I haven't decided.

lz_old_fisher/6baca514721b5024.text: It rings when they want company. That's what my grandmother said. A sack of something every month and they'd stay down, and the fish would come up to see what was in it.

lz_old_fisher/7280b45849958245.text: Bluto's shack is empty. I don't go in. Some nights I think I hear him singing, out on the water, the way he used to when he'd had a catch.

lz_old_fisher/d87b59855e04a239.text: A pike this morning. A pike, the length of my arm. First fish in a year that wasn't too small to bother. I nearly wept on it.

lz_old_fisher/e9374aa7508b549a.text: Listen. There. Every night now, after the moon's up. Under the water. You'd think water would stop a bell.

lz_old_fisher/eac4d438d7ecfc5c.text: Bluto's sacks. You know what he put in them. He wasn't mad. That's the worst of it. He was paying the bell. Now he's stopped paying, and it rings every night, and it's coming up the shore a little further every time.

lz_old_fisher/f95ce1fe61fdf85c.text: Keep away from the big fellow in the shack. He drinks, and he cries, and he goes out in his boat at night with something in a sack. I don't ask. Nobody asks.

lzt_hunter/04e6d492bc8b9cc0.text: Hares, grouse, the odd fox. The wolves take the deer before I get near them. They're bold this year, bold as dogs. They watch the trail in the daytime now.

lzt_hunter/d9c6bddd15bc02a0.text: The lake's below, if that's where you're going. Don't drink from the near shore. Bluto's been sick in it.

mad_mage/0799847bf1f24e59.text: This rock is an excellent listener. Better than you, I expect.

mad_mage/20f5a4e36bace942.text: You said it before, and it hurt. It doesn't hurt now. It fits, like an old boot.

mad_mage/2fd9bb5410849bbf.text: I went down to the castle with a plan. The plan was excellent. I remember the plan was excellent. The plan went in, and I came out, and some time after that a little old woman with a jar said "hush now" and everything went quiet.

mad_mage/4176cb9fd5b67da2.text: You again. Or someone wearing you. Sit. Don't touch the black king; he bites.

mad_mage/46870eece5e97fb2.text: Stop it. Stop poking at the hole. It's MY hole.

mad_mage/56f232040dcf6b20.text: Mordenkainen. That's... that's my hand. That's how I make a capital M, with the little hook. Nobody else makes it like that. It's a terrible M. It's mine.

mad_mage/5c3760d732362f9b.text: Am I? How interesting. I wonder what I'm practising for.

mad_mage/5fedeec9aae48a3f.text: Don't. Don't say it like that, as if it were somebody's. It hurts. Why does that hurt?

mad_mage/68ed30870b056c13.text: There's more. I can feel there's more. Read me the end. Not the spells. The last page. I wrote something there for myself, I'm sure of it.

mad_mage/714b67bacb8ebc2b.text: Lost? It was taken. One doesn't simply lose a name like that. One would hear it fall.

mad_mage/9bdef57f60a76228.text: That is exactly what the persuasive one said.

mad_mage/9c7fc3955d87cb87.text: Goodbye! Mind the birds. Don't believe a word they say.

mad_mage/b328bf23f63abd24.text: I'm sorry. Have we met? Are you real?

mad_mage/b7aed4eb40863307.text: I am not rude. I am occasionally correct at people.

mad_mage/c9494af8a083f107.text: I am... Osric. No. Osric was a goat. I am Marvellous Something. I had a name like a staircase, long, with a landing in the middle. I have looked for it under every stone on this mountain.

mad_mage/d63fb7d5f1748a2e.text: Did you see my storm on the ridge? I made it to tell me something every evening. I can't remember what. It's very punctual.

mad_mage/d843c40716433037.text: Cards! I love cards. Yes, certainly, I'll come, where are we going? We'll need provisions, and a plan, and a...

mad_mage/e8acd3a85e5ac97b.text: A jar. Yes. A little woman with a jar, saying hush now. I remember the jar more than I remember anything else. Bring me the jar. No: don't. She'll want something for it. They always want something.

mad_mage/f8c8ff03e596b080.text: Ah. Are you real? Be honest. The last three visitors were birds, and one of them was extremely persuasive.

mad_mage/feb63825dc54ccc9.text: I play the other fellow every day. He's very good. He was always very good. I just can't remember who he is.

mad_mary/179c247692b53c1e.text: You came back. Nobody comes back. Have you come to look at the mad woman?

mad_mary/21732d31f8b344c6.text: Sixteen years. Yes. That's something. That's something, isn't it. Thank you.

mad_mary/31829011b88af69b.text: My daughter. Sixteen this spring. Dark hair, like her father. She hums when she's frightened. I kept her in, you see. Sixteen years safe. She never saw the woods, or the castle. She never saw anything.

mad_mary/3df2b838214c8c65.text: You brought her home. I said nobody listens. I was wrong, and I'm glad to be wrong. Sit. Let me mend something for you. Let me do something.

mad_mary/59a290369cefc927.text: These were my mother's beads. I said a prayer on every one, every night she was gone. Take them. I've no more prayers left to say, only thank-yous.

mad_mary/5c832e58b07b4ba7.text: Do they work, here? Prayers? No, don't answer. Say another one.

mad_mary/65103b245b1dca8f.text: Hush. The door's unlocked. It's staying unlocked. We'll learn how, the two of us.

mad_mary/86fbf76853d95d2a.text: Gertruda? Gertruda, is that... no. No, you're not her. Forgive me. You're taller. She's not so tall. She's a good girl.

mad_mary/8769f44e413331db.text: You will? You'll look? Dark hair, a blue dress with a mended hem, she hums when she's afraid. She'll be afraid. Tell her I'm not angry. Tell her the door is unlocked now. All three locks.

mad_mary/87d035c04455615b.text: Of course. Of course you can't. Thank you for listening. Nobody listens. Mind the step on your way out; it sticks.

mad_mary/97da70d3dd1e22a5.text: They call me mad because mad is easier to walk past.

mad_mary/befad26b62c4b23d.text: You're cold. You're so cold. Where are your good shoes? Never mind. Never mind the shoes.

mad_mary/db7f0f0a52b89415.text: She sleeps late now. I let her. I sit and listen to her breathing and I don't weep at all. The neighbours think I've gone madder.

mad_mary/e663aaafbdb0c5f9.text: There was singing, some nights. Under her window. A man's voice, old songs. I told myself it was the wind. I pulled my own shutters closed.

mad_mary/e931efd8c0c6e164.text: Kind of you. It's not true, but it's kind. She'd say the same. She's kinder than me, my Gertruda.

mad_mary/ecd04908e3d160ea.text: From the inside. Then nobody took her. She went to him. Whoever he was, with his old songs. I made a house so safe that a girl had to escape it.

mad_mary/f8802ab514b76298.text: Have you found her? No. No, you'd have said. You'd have said first thing. Sit, sit. Your sleeve's torn at the seam; leave it with me. I mend things. Everything but the one thing.

mad_mary/fd7a931293f3b5b7.text: Four nights ago. I went to wake her, and the bed was cold, and the window was open. No blood. The wolves didn't take her; I'd have heard wolves.

madam_eva/0018ac7df17a2422.text: You did not pay what the cards asked. They will tell you anyway. They are not kind, and neither am I.

madam_eva/01fdca2312b6448e.text: The mist lies over this card; it will not show me. He will be wherever he chooses, and he will choose well.

madam_eva/0650e7ff89df5612.text: Then you are like everyone else in this valley. A true thing, then. Barovia has not found a way to tax those yet.

madam_eva/0880b70a33de9281.text: You sold yourself to save a man who would not let you. That is a terrible bargain and a very good son. The cards will take it. They like a good son.

madam_eva/0c55a0c56668e3dd.text: Somewhere in his pits, his old enemies were made into furniture. Sit at their table, and mind the lamp.

madam_eva/0ca9eeeb1b24a9e7.text: Brave. Stupid, but brave. Fine. The cards will speak to you, and you will wish you had paid them.

madam_eva/0cd78673cd483ec1.text: A scholar who came for a friend, and was ashamed of it. The cards like you better already.

madam_eva/0defab9ba8dfdbdc.text: The Morninglord's light is a long way from here, priestess. It still reaches you. Ask why it reaches, not why it's cold.

madam_eva/0e37c5f63ec72ec4.text: Go. Stanimir will feed you if you let him. And when you meet the devil on the road, as you will, be polite. He forgives rudeness least of all, and he forgives nothing.

madam_eva/0f41f1d8ec1b60e3.text: You lied to Stanimir about his strongbox. He believed you; he is a kind man. I am not, but I will let it pass. Once.

madam_eva/11bef8b65b3c0334.text: And you have been counting heads ever since, so that nobody is ever missing again. Yes. That will do. That is worth more than gold.

madam_eva/1243a6922446c35b.text: You came into my tent and showed me your teeth. Now my family is showing you theirs. Choose again.

madam_eva/163899baff438cb1.text: It lies in the room where he sleeps the day away, beneath everything, guarded by the oldest dark in the valley.

madam_eva/174a56cb5d88ea40.text: He receives you the way a lord receives petitioners: seated high in his great hall, with all the time in the world.

madam_eva/1df0a20d0c451ba6.text: Beyond the last gate in the valley, where the walls keep out everything but snow, there is water that remembers the sun. Wade in.

madam_eva/1f70242dba474489.text: Because he was bored, and he called. Because the cards wanted players. Because each of you was already walking toward the mist before you ever saw it. Pick whichever answer lets you sleep.

madam_eva/1fac0f23f7021b7a.text: Better. The price has doubled. Twenty gold, or the true thing. The true thing has not doubled; the truth is never on sale.

madam_eva/2124266ef14d925a.text: You have already shaken his hand. A village measured him against his father and found him short. The cards measure differently.

madam_eva/21d78cdc95990044.text: The dragon's knights keep their watch still, big one, on a hill where the house is burned and the dead lay the table every night. Their master will not knight you. One of them will. Look low on the wall.

madam_eva/2221a0668b4da3ef.text: Where the river ate a village whole, an old woman keeps house on the wreck, singing to the child she raised long ago. Take it from her kitchen.

madam_eva/2434bfbff4d184c8.text: Then it is yours, and so is what comes with it. Remember that I said so. Sit. The cards will speak to thieves; they have spoken to worse.

madam_eva/24b59c718c8add66.text: In his house a lady made of paint and varnish keeps her place above the hearth. She has watched it burn for centuries. Look where she looks.

madam_eva/2537cdf226c80f0d.text: One question more, and then the cards sleep. Only one. Choose it well; I am old, and I don't repeat myself for free.

madam_eva/273697b223892e78.text: There you are. I turned up a card for you three nights ago, and it has been tapping its foot ever since. Sit.

madam_eva/28072ffc8f31e64c.text: You need not walk far. It has been under my own canvas all along, waiting for the hands the cards would send.

madam_eva/280c8cd778f8de6d.text: No? Keep the road you have, then. The cards are patient.

madam_eva/29cacbcfc0c9302e.text: Yes. That will do. Keep the rest of it; you will need something to carry.

madam_eva/2eecb7bdaa9e1d33.text: In his house there is a room built for kneeling, and nobody has knelt there in centuries. Look under the dust of its last prayer.

madam_eva/3101ae0569746bce.text: He keeps vigil by the queen who bore him, in the cold beneath his house.

madam_eva/32dbda4e233d8325.text: Find the hearth in his keep that is always burning, and ask why a dead man needs a fire. Behind it is something he keeps and never spends.

madam_eva/339698852faf4216.text: Slow. Ha. The cards have read for kings who could recite a library and could not read a face. You read faces, big one. That is the harder alphabet.

madam_eva/34fc4d1a1c3e5216.text: The fourth card is a friend. One who will stand beside you when the others run.

madam_eva/37ac89b4213f9cd4.text: The cards don't change. Only the people carrying them.

madam_eva/391a4a2ba4b4f8df.text: The things the cards named, in the hands the cards named, in the room the cards named. He has been hurt before. He has never been hurt by all of it at once. And sunlight. Always sunlight.

madam_eva/3b9c30c0217d2f5f.text: He stands at the castle's lookout, high over the valley, admiring his property. He will turn around when you arrive.

madam_eva/3c14895dc7ecffa8.text: Behind the walled town's finest door, a widow raises a glass to the castle every night. Her strongbox holds it, and an old enemy's bones keep it company.

madam_eva/3e04ff3674b4827a.text: Some of your forty went into his house as guests and never came out as anything. Some walk his roads still, in colours that are not their own. You will see one before the end, sergeant. Count carefully.

madam_eva/4105d794994b9cec.text: Find the painting of the woman he lost. Behind her lies his hoard, and he will be sitting on it like a dragon, counting what it never bought him.

madam_eva/42195eab315cdce3.text: Something clockwork walks the castle's stairs on its own: a jester with a wound-down smile. It knows every passage in that house, and it is lonely.

madam_eva/424e4d350f2b9372.text: The mists open for my people and for the dead. When the devil is truly ended, they will open for you. There is no other door. People have looked. You walked past some of them in the village churchyard.

madam_eva/42cc0cc93ac9320f.text: Two brothers: one walked into the dark, the other was put into the ground. Look where the good one sleeps.

madam_eva/4510b034acdef30a.text: He wants what he has always wanted: a woman who told him no, long ago, and keeps being born to tell him again. Keep her away from high places and still water. She has fallen before.

madam_eva/46066d03cc8e3301.text: You again. The camp is empty because of you, and the cards still haven't changed their minds. What do you want?

madam_eva/4945ea2a304b5bfc.text: No. Not in this one. Sit by the brazier; you are cold all the way through, and it isn't the weather.

madam_eva/4a21867e3a3ae820.text: Back again. The cards haven't changed their minds. I might have.

madam_eva/4b499985c0baf09c.text: West of the vines the old dead are heaped into a hill, and from them grows one tree that drinks wrongly. Those who go there in green worship it. Go anyway.

madam_eva/4fc40ed73175bd37.text: Who pays? Not something clever. Something that costs you to say out loud.

madam_eva/4ffa36fd03f1d8b6.text: Keep that stolen face in your pocket, little thief. Some faces belong to the dead, and the dead want them back.

madam_eva/4fffa764fdaa6c06.text: He will be in the room where his own coffin lies, deep below, where the night is oldest and he is strongest.

madam_eva/50e577bb95aa520d.text: The dragon's house has a lamp at its crown that nobody lights any more. Climb to where the light should be.

madam_eva/519c374832ebc6f1.text: You came back. They always come back. The cards waited; they are better at it than you.

madam_eva/52ecc787c79c14d8.text: No hand reaches for yours. The cards set no friend at your side: you will face him with only what you carry.

madam_eva/533595004393499b.text: Among the wagons outside the walled town sits an elf with dusk-dark skin who mourns a sister. He keeps it, and he will trade it for a road into the mountains.

madam_eva/54f8482eee19aebe.text: Under the castle, past the cells, there is a room furnished with the dead. He likes to entertain there.

madam_eva/56ee5380ffe823ff.text: Go to the woman who bore him. She sleeps beneath his house, and she has kept this for her son's enemies.

madam_eva/5b1e4c30a8b97aae.text: So yes, some of us carry tales up the hill. Be careful what you say at our fires. Be more careful what you say at other people's.

madam_eva/5e2ba9d9f3d149cd.text: It rides in a wagon of my cousins by the lake town, in a chest whose owner has lost a daughter. Bring the girl home, and the lid will open for you.

madam_eva/61c2fb7adb7fe188.text: The third card is a blade. Not steel: daylight with an edge, once carried by the one he hated most. He cannot bear to look at it.

madam_eva/6280a36a5657d35c.text: Climb until you can hear the castle's pulse, a great glass heart that bleeds for him. He will be standing beside it.

madam_eva/653b22a046cd254b.text: Follow the howling into the high hills above the cold lake. The wolves keep a mother there who never bore them.

madam_eva/65a9e34a43e7019e.text: Earth is a door, child. Most doors open both ways, if someone pays the toll.

madam_eva/65ecdb79cd86bf0c.text: Gold. Honest, at least. The cards will take it. Sit closer.

madam_eva/6882e2561b981222.text: Nobody sent you? No. The road sent you. It sends everyone to my table in the end; most of them simply don't stop.

madam_eva/6922cc68d2a1a3fb.text: Many things here are not possible. Sit in enough of them and you stop counting.

madam_eva/6a05ac169d5c12c9.text: A child of ours. Don't sit here listening to me. When we're done, go.

madam_eva/6ab65269cd1a607d.text: A gentle giant of a boy sweeps a shop floor for an uncle who doesn't deserve him. He is stronger than anyone has ever told him.

madam_eva/6ae7d1121384a4ed.text: Everybody is not finished, little acrobat. The ones who think they are, they are the ones the cards worry about.

madam_eva/6c8f02150ff5f529.text: Ask him, child. He will tell you at great length, and every word will be a lie except her name.

madam_eva/6ca7b843243ed8f4.text: There. You are who you are now. Try not to waste it.

madam_eva/6ca9b59dc1915da2.text: You brought our Nicu home, and then you lied to me at my own table. The one cancels the other. Pay like a stranger.

madam_eva/6df30b21d00ac525.text: Among the vines lives an old man whose family wears feathers by night. He is tired, and proud, and he would like very much to be asked.

madam_eva/70e49428d5d75677.text: A seat made for one, in a hall made for the many who were meant to kneel before it.

madam_eva/755e9249a4318faa.text: Somewhere in his house a famous killer is laid out on a stone slab, with winged stone guardians crouched at his head and his feet. He won't miss it.

madam_eva/7746fd09c8ea8770.text: So. You have come round again, child. Further along the road than last time.

madam_eva/799ac90a489a49f5.text: Somebody did. And now you have said it aloud, you can stop pretending you are only a thief. Good.

madam_eva/7ced0aaaabe057b2.text: Where a silver dragon once kept his hall, a captain with no heartbeat keeps a grudge instead. It lies within reach of that grudge.

madam_eva/7e8ff7f9bf2d93e5.text: He waits in the room where his family prayed, among the broken pews, under a window that has not let in morning for centuries.

madam_eva/7f12a0eea5d4a703.text: The last card. Where the darkness will be waiting when you come for him. And you will come for him; the cards are very sure of that part.

madam_eva/807df4214bf9081b.text: Follow the birds that will not leave his roofs. Where they sleep, a clever hand tucked something bright among the twigs.

madam_eva/81c84ff7956f63d8.text: Climb his highest tower until your knees shake, and mind the carvings on the parapet. Not all of them are carvings.

madam_eva/83828659920e21fc.text: No. Put your purse away. You brought our Nicu home to his people, as much of him as the road left. That is paid already, and more.

madam_eva/843dc9c81e82eae8.text: Beside the walled town, among my cousins' wagons, sits an elf who lost his sister and won't stop trying to buy her back. Walk his road with him a little way, and he will walk yours.

madam_eva/84ffd19491fdf1c6.text: The Vistani have no house and no country and we fit everywhere the road goes. Belonging is not a place, wolf-girl. It is the people who save you a seat.

madam_eva/86542efcf81b7f53.text: Climb to where the snow never melts and the air won't fill your lungs. There is a temple there, and a great statue whose sculptor never finished the face. Look at its feet.

madam_eva/8780dc9008c780c7.text: Before we begin. One of you has forty of my nephew's gold pieces about you. The cards will not speak over the clink of them.

madam_eva/89d2d233081c4db6.text: Then go and do it. I will be here when you are finished. I always am.

madam_eva/8e63c00154ef42e5.text: Sit. We were in the middle of something.

madam_eva/8f2777cc11cfc74d.text: Go back the way you came, to the village, and dig where the mourners stand. It sleeps under somebody else's name.

madam_eva/8fb18a1061bfdba4.text: Your friend with the ink to his elbows went up to the castle to read. He is reading still. Whether he is still alive is a question even the cards find rude.

madam_eva/91664ab02d0008bf.text: The valley has needed things for four hundred years, and still the candles cost money. Pay, or tell me something true.

madam_eva/91fa82fba96cfc14.text: Liar. A bad one, which is almost to your credit. Give it back, or keep it and listen to what it costs you.

madam_eva/92aec909706f598c.text: Her name was Tatyana. She is dead, and she is not. Whoever put her in your hand wanted you to carry her face home, and you have.

madam_eva/93e3edf474af1847.text: He will be among his books, by a fire that warms nothing, reading old letters he should have burned.

madam_eva/93fd52694ae86543.text: Down where his wine sleeps in racks, one rack holds no wine. A tradesman was walled in among the bottles, and it is with him.

madam_eva/97b099f8feaf9a36.text: There you are. The house at the end of the village let you go. It doesn't, as a rule. Sit.

madam_eva/98c68cbc443c6337.text: A windmill leans on a crag above the road with its sails stopped. Something in it bakes, and something in it cries.

madam_eva/9a3af6066bf80837.text: Above the walled village stands a holy house that has become a kennel for madness. Look in the rooms where the young were once kept.

madam_eva/9c90ee152e0c68f5.text: Far up the mountain road a door is cut into the rock, and two great figures the colour of old resin stand on either side of it. It waits just past them.

madam_eva/9cfb5cc2626481d5.text: Up the mountain lives a mage who has forgotten who he is. What he has not forgotten is how to bring down a sky. Help him find himself.

madam_eva/9ee88aaa0b09f0f1.text: Then you came on purpose to the thing you fear most, carrying a candle. Child, that is not a weakness. That is the whole of courage, in one sentence.

madam_eva/a02b6a99fda0cf75.text: A hunter of my blood left the wagons to chase what chases us, and the man who taught her. Catch her if you can; lately she has been seen on the road up to the abbey above the walled village.

madam_eva/a0f08af1ff1fe48b.text: Five cards. Three for what was lost, one for who will help you, one for where he waits. Don't touch them. Don't breathe on them. Listen.

madam_eva/a4b0884c2ba2ad75.text: A man of standing lies cold, and a daughter who was never his by blood still keeps his memory. Give breath back to that body and he will stand with you.

madam_eva/a5eb737a6e9ac7d0.text: And one of the three, you need not walk a step for. The cards put it in my keeping long ago, and told me to wait for the right hands. My hands are tired.

madam_eva/a77f3bc0e063a9af.text: High where the road climbs over the mountain's shoulder, a pale tower keeps a gate that nobody uses. Its sentries have not blinked in years.

madam_eva/ae00369bb694fa88.text: The wizard you want pays his debts in green stones and plays games against nobody, up where the snow is. You will find his name in a cellar before you find him on a mountain. And you will not like either.

madam_eva/b0012c1b2237773a.text: One of you is walking a road that doesn't fit their feet. I can read them another. It costs nothing you will miss; not today. Choose who sits.

madam_eva/b3942a3f0f5baad5.text: The first card is the past: a book in his own hand, the story of how he became what he is. Knowing it is a weapon. This one cuts him.

madam_eva/b3cb1792a410babc.text: In the den in the hills, one wolf has started to look at his pack the way you look at the castle. When they turn on him, be there.

madam_eva/b3ce92af02753cc8.text: Stanimir has told the castle you went east. He thinks I don't know. Let him think it.

madam_eva/b5890d59171b3506.text: Your old trapper is alive, wolf-girl. He walks on more legs than he left home with, some nights. He is waiting where the wolves wait, above the lake. He told you to run. Don't.

madam_eva/c0b1f714fd72ea4f.text: Good. The cards prefer clean hands. Cleaner hands. They are not fussy.

madam_eva/c1408cb74ee2ef3e.text: That one is my people's own. She left the wagons to hunt the things that hunt us. If you find her, tell her the old woman says to eat something.

madam_eva/c1e5ea103b172f81.text: The second card is a holy thing, made by people who believed the sun would come back. In the right hands it makes the dead remember they are dead.

madam_eva/c2ab6fee12a17bb6.text: Among the endless crypts below, where his house keeps its dead in rows, he walks between the names.

madam_eva/c426145414895b8d.text: There. Expensive manners are still manners. Sit.

madam_eva/c682dbdb98baf9fe.text: Dawn comes to this valley every day, priestess. It simply never arrives. Somebody has to carry it the last of the way, into his house.

madam_eva/c6ddc16fcda2b762.text: As you like. The cards are patient. They have outlived everyone who walked away from them.

madam_eva/c7ce6b6d0ec2672d.text: Among his honoured dead lies a general whose own men called him a mad hound. It is in his tomb, under him.

madam_eva/c7e60c197ffa803f.text: For the valley. Ha! Nobody has said that to me in sixty years. Very well. The valley can owe me. It already owes me a great deal.

madam_eva/ca4f951be512df0d.text: Behind a town's bright banners stands a house where something has gone wrong, and in it a room crowded with small, still faces. Every one of them is hers.

madam_eva/cac253802a045176.text: Then you know more than he would like. Good. Hold on to that.

madam_eva/cb4419e14ee02f9d.text: Hm. Then perhaps the cards are mistaken. They are not. But perhaps.

madam_eva/cc462687661e588f.text: He keeps company with the brother he murdered for a woman. He talks to him, sometimes. The brother never answers.

madam_eva/d2b83fb10fd36958.text: A small magician sleeps among the castle's grand dead, remembered by nothing but his name on a stone. What he carried in his hand unlocks what he guards.

madam_eva/d371a11eead0db7b.text: Where frost lies on the beds of a walled garden, a man of straw stands sentry with a stitched mouth. He holds it closer than any gardener would.

madam_eva/d38dfbeaeaee2125.text: Is it? The best wizard I ever read for burned his own beard making me an omelette. He was happier holding that pan than any staff.

madam_eva/d7b1aca6d7f6722e.text: I mean what the cards mean. Put it away, now.

madam_eva/d8795af26f8e0a34.text: In a village the river swallowed, the mud remembers a girl he loved once, and keeps her in stone. Ask the hag who rules the reeds.

madam_eva/d9357c26bd4ea9bd.text: Somewhere a barrel that held the best vintage in the valley stands as dry as a skull. Knock on it.

madam_eva/d9a2ece81a424659.text: A holy woman's house stands above the walled village, and its brightest symbol hides a hollow. Look behind the light.

madam_eva/da3a95bf1deabbef.text: There. That is the shape of it. Three things lost, a friend, and the room at the end. Everything else, you will have to do yourselves.

madam_eva/da58eea1338fba57.text: You have bloodied my family and driven the rest into the trees. And still you come to my table. Sit. The cards do not care who deserves them.

madam_eva/dc2950079d63536e.text: It lies where a lord counts what he has never needed, buried under coin heaped like snowdrifts.

madam_eva/dfa92ee92d896259.text: Wise. Most people ask. Most people wish they hadn't.

madam_eva/e091440da7e4c3c6.text: The man you carry a letter for mends nets he will never cast, at a fire that is not his, outside the walled town. He has waited four hundred years for word from over the mountains. Don't make him wait longer.

madam_eva/e24326a589a1158c.text: In the walled town's grandest house, a clever young man has made his attic into a cell and a workshop. Free his mind from that house, and he will lend it to you.

madam_eva/e6401d2459c554bb.text: Now get out of my tent.

madam_eva/eb580deba95f2f8a.text: The dragon's house is full of dead knights who have forgotten their oath. One of them still remembers, a little. Find him, and make him remember the rest.

madam_eva/ebc01ad3ca8f52e9.text: The cards are free. The one who turns them is not. Ten gold, or one true thing that one of you has told nobody. The cards take either. They prefer the second.

madam_eva/eed7087167f2a077.text: I am old. Older than the walled town on the lake, older than the inn in the village, older than some of his walls. I knew him when he was young and only ambitious. That much you get for free.

madam_eva/f55b007a354eeb58.text: Follow the vines to the house that pressed the valley's last good wine. A bargain was struck there that nobody has paid.

madam_eva/f6a37fd4ddc2f878.text: My people come and go through the mists, and he lets us. Long ago one of us did him a kindness. He has a long memory for kindness, and a longer one for the other thing.

madam_eva/f6e84097931b2c9b.text: A ringmaster has rolled into the walled town with a painted wagon he lets nobody near. Ask yourself what a showman keeps locked up that he never shows.

madam_eva/f8c59dd4ace36593.text: A ringmaster with a menagerie of one has come to the walled town, laughing too loudly. Under the laugh is a hunter who has buried everyone he ever loved. Earn his trust.

madam_eva/f9a80b49e26db9ad.text: He goes down to stand over his brother's coffin, over the man he could never be. He goes there often.

madam_eva/fa8ea2bbc34c8376.text: In the mountain's golden halls, behind a door that glows like honey held to a candle, the gifts of forgotten gods lie heaped up. It is among them.

madam_eva/fa92a4199d68d4cf.text: Read it, merchant. Every word. Devils write in a hurry and expect their clients to sign in tears. The way out of a cage is very often written on the cage.

madam_eva/fbb1b1cff0e89b80.text: A tower stands in a cold mountain lake, and the mage who built it is long dead. Its door still answers to him, and to the one who served him. Find out who they were.

madam_eva/fecd5a677028a1db.text: One of our little ones has wandered where she shouldn't, out onto the big water by the walled town. Someone has her who should not. Go quickly.

madam_eva/ffbfb8f7486b02c2.text: He has gone down to visit the king who made him. Father and son, both of them stone now.

marshal_dragomir/05b0c0794c46d275.text: Lies are a scout's work. I have heard them all.
