marshal_dragomir/0c03348346e9ecd8.text: They are relieved. I am not. An officer is relieved by his commander, or by defeat. My commander will not come.

marshal_dragomir/36c10f1edd82b0eb.text: So. Beat me. Fairly, at the gate I was told to hold. Then I can tell him, when I see him, that I held it until I couldn't.

marshal_dragomir/561342017ba7aef2.text: You again. The gate is still held.

marshal_dragomir/605cb0162236fd27.text: Halt. This gate is held. No one passes in, no one passes out, until the count returns to relieve us.

marshal_dragomir/66ab199b1b962f26.text: Tomorrow night, then. We have time. We have had nothing but.

marshal_dragomir/8ecdb66d33577dd9.text: You came back. Good. My men are relieved and I am not. On guard, then, when you're ready.

marshal_dragomir/a202eaae2e204b89.text: An order is an order until it is countermanded. Four hundred years. We hold.

marshal_dragomir/a549b198f8dfbc40.text: Done. The war is done. ...Then what have my men been holding?

marshal_dragomir/ab413ac7487b3978.text: My men will stand down when I am relieved, and not one hour before. Who are you to relieve me?

marshal_dragomir/de450bb3d934d81d.text: State your names and your lord.

marshal_dragomir/e10bea200cc64fee.text: The count is in his castle. Yes. We see its lights from the gate, some nights. He has never once sent a rider down to relieve us.

milivoj/030796c029e50baa.text: Council's paying me to dig a ditch for the new latrines. First honest money in a year. Smells worse, pays better.

milivoj/081e5bf1a1f00b6b.text: ...Twenty. Same as him. Funny how that's what everything in this town costs.

milivoj/141fc70e54cc73b9.text: The saint's home, they say. I went down and looked. I put a candle by him. I didn't know what else to do.

milivoj/1fbf75ac7e7c1883.text: Did you go to Henrik's? Go in daylight.

milivoj/3f0e7692997985aa.text: He does. He always does. Tell him I'm sorry. Tell him I'll dig for nothing till it's paid back.

milivoj/45f558fbbf8a8da0.text: I sold them. Henrik. The coffin maker. Twenty gold. He came to me at night, shaking all over, and asked for the saint by name. Said someone made him ask. I didn't ask who.

milivoj/64ef6b1c7871c233.text: You. My collar's still creased. Grave's still not for you, but I've started measuring.

milivoj/6a283a9a0f2e1102.text: You again. Still digging. Still not for you.

milivoj/6b855f7cda29a1b3.text: Grave's not for you. Unless you keep standing on the edge of it.

milivoj/6d479d18eaa1e2a0.text: Old Bogdana, from the lane by the lockup. Fever. That's what the priest wrote down, anyway. It's always fever, or wolves, or nobody knows. I dig the same size hole for all three.

milivoj/844716510ffa79f9.text: All right! All right. Let go. I'll tell you.

milivoj/8702a8c20a238c61.text: Says who? The priest? He'd never say that. He wouldn't.

milivoj/9387caa5a1e89c1a.text: Twenty gold is a winter. I've got two brothers and a sister and a roof that leaks onto all of them. The saint's dead. They're not. That's how I did the sum.

milivoj/b98a30f751f01aa7.text: It pays. Barely. Nothing else in this town pays at all.

milivoj/c04cf8ed312c1d9e.text: Go on, then. Hit me. You'll have to dig your own hole after; I'm not doing it for free.

milivoj/d37435e22a7e4421.text: Nobody hangs in Vallaki. They go in the stocks and then they go hungry. I've done hungry. I'm not going back.

milivoj/e692c2f22f2de6b4.text: I don't... nobody gives anybody anything here. Thanks. Go and see Henrik. Go in daylight. Whatever's in his shop, it doesn't like daylight.

milivoj/feadbbeba0c93e5f.text: Henrik. Of course Henrik. He couldn't keep a secret in a coffin.

mirabel/8e103bbfd534c640.text: And for strangers who don't, she reads them anyway. It's worse.

mirabel/95a7c666688c3342.text: Or don't. We'll guess. Our guesses are always better than the truth.

mirabel/a361ea2735f3f28e.text: Ismark the Lesser. His father was loud, and brave, and dead. Ismark is quiet, and brave, and not dead yet. Give him time.

mirela/080fafe8c058c8c7.text: You came back. You left, and you came back. I counted the days you were gone.

mirela/1bc5eb0de43deaa4.text: Is it over? Are they all...?

mirela/4789adfea4428f9b.text: That's Ana's! She dropped it when they carried us up. She's been crying for it every night.

mirela/6f2af3fc6e5fac3c.text: If you're here to look at us, look and go. If you're here to eat us, you'll have to start with me. I'm the stringiest.

mirela/70f1ef12e15dd8da.text: Come back. You have to come back. You promised, or your friend did.

mirela/718623e3472a88d4.text: Don't tell the little ones. Is it going to make me one of them?

mirela/7abc32a2d9ab0330.text: Now? With all of them out there?

mirela/884bcfeb5dc4f802.text: Krezk is down the stream path, then west on the road. We can find it. We're not little. Except Ana. Ana's little.

mirela/8860815d0c64da4b.text: Emil's loose? I heard him howl. Then hurry up and win. We'll be here. We're always here.

mirela/9abb8d733af95629.text: Mirela. From the Vadu farm under Krezk. That's Ana, she's six, and Petru, and the twins, Ilie and Ioana. They came in the night with sacks. They took my dog first so he wouldn't bark.

mirela/a37f36786dbc8bba.text: Thirty-one days. I scratch them on the wall. The big one says the moon comes in eleven more, and then we'll find out which of us are wolves and which of us are supper.

mirela/ae976ad836d8d6d9.text: We can't run. They'd smell us on the hill before we got to the trees, and they're faster than horses. Zuleika says wait for Emil. Zuleika says a lot of things, but she brings bread.

mirela/bcb143189acfa5f9.text: Still here. We're always still here.

mirela/f24c6f0c505c0618.text: It doesn't itch any more. It always itched.

mirela/f88094accf22e979.text: The priest in Krezk is old and his hands shake. But he's kind. I'll make him do it right.

mister_quillon/005b37de2db4a27e.text: The terms are met. The account is closed. Good evening, Mister Smudgewick. I do hope we never meet again. I will make sure we don't.

mister_quillon/5985cd570b8a00e1.text: Mister Smudgewick. You've been busy. I can smell the castle on you.

mister_quillon/5f20996d02d7ce2b.text: Our agreement runs to the end of the final harvest. I merely mention it. And the way out I so generously offered, a signature from the lord of this land, remains on the table. I do hope you're making progress. Truly. I hate a default. The paperwork.

mister_quillon/629d7bf0f9ec08fc.text: Of course. I can't do anything else here, you understand; my jurisdiction ends at the mists. I can only talk. You'd be amazed what talking does.

mister_quillon/6a65a1bc92167f80.text: Completion. The consideration is collected, the orchard continues to flourish, and his family never learns why. Everybody keeps something. It's a very fair contract. I drafted it myself.

mister_quillon/b86a69896a4ce042.text: Your mother is a very tiresome woman.

mister_quillon/d06a4fe74db607c9.text: Good evening. Please, nobody get up. Mister Smudgewick. I happened to be passing.

mister_quillon/f98230b62c65bd3c.text: Quite so. I travel on a pass. The lord of this land is very particular about his border, and I am very particular about manners, so I shan't stay. I only called to see how you were getting on.

mordenkainen/118fa3e7ce0b5eab.text: Eva. That woman read my cards forty years ago and told me I'd be broken, and here I am, with the pieces in a heap. If her cards say I mend in your company, I'm not going to argue with them. Not twice.

mordenkainen/13e98db11da162fd.text: Go on. And stay out of jars.

mordenkainen/271c430769a22da9.text: I paid that family three stones for a winter's lodging and some decent food, forty years ago. Is that what I'm famous for now? Gods help us all.

mordenkainen/30e3fb667d218623.text: Interesting. The witch's jar gave me back almost everything. Almost. There are pages missing. Not from the book. From me.

mordenkainen/3135cf3405f63f8b.text: Everyone has questions. Very few have the right ones. Ask later.

mordenkainen/3e4776c0771db2ed.text: No. You're right. I'd go up there as exactly the man who ran. I need to be someone else first, and that takes longer than a night.

mordenkainen/493f773ae43fc076.text: You found her. (He doesn't ask how it went. He looks at your faces and doesn't need to.) Did she have ink on her fingers still? She always did. Thank you. Now go away for a while. I'd like to be old in private.

mordenkainen/4df1cb73c1b61922.text: But you'll be in that castle before I am. If you find her, and you will, he'll have seen to that, say her name to her. Corvina. Names matter to the dead in this valley. They're very nearly all the dead have left.

mordenkainen/56086bdec4d7f055.text: The witch. Lysaga. She held my eyes open while she did it, and sang. I'll remember that now, too. Thank you, I suppose.

mordenkainen/56531bff07ff1e3c.text: A hand I know better than my own. Small, slanted, impatient, always running out of margin. Letters, written to me. I can see the handwriting when I close my eyes, and I can't see the name.

mordenkainen/5935756e75c9946a.text: You crossed the mists for me? Nobody's done that on purpose.

mordenkainen/606ac0fb7ba9e610.text: Not like this. If I go down that mountain today, I'll be a clever old man with half his spells and all his pride, which is exactly how I lost the first time.

mordenkainen/635df20005b5e20d.text: Status is a coat. Anyone can wear it, and it keeps nobody warm. What are you good at? Not magic. I can see what you're good at with magic. What are you good at?

mordenkainen/65b87e4ae39a50e4.text: They were in my coat the night the witch took me. Since then this hut has been blown inside out by a storm I forgot I'd ordered, for forty years. They'll be in the snow somewhere. In the ice. Bring them to me.

mordenkainen/6689274c263564ea.text: The Tsolenka watch. Dead sergeant, very correct, wants the word. I went up that road the year I came here, looking for a weapon in the temple. I didn't find one, and I'm glad.

mordenkainen/671f02d0f4807f02.text: And take this. She made it, her first year, to fetch my books down without asking. I took it off her desk the night we went up, because I thought I'd need it more. I didn't. I needed her.

mordenkainen/67fea953e056f8f3.text: Take nothing that's offered. Anything they give you, they keep a hand on. I've seen what that looks like after forty years. It looks like him.

mordenkainen/6851466c491e9043.text: "She holds my doors still." He wrote that for me to find. He knew I'd come looking one day. He's been waiting forty years for me to read it.

mordenkainen/6a285a0085625cd2.text: If I knew that, they wouldn't be missing, would they?

mordenkainen/6fa1a4ba6a60db7a.text: The word is "cold hearth, shut door". Their old officers' joke, I think: keep the fire out and the door shut. Say it like you're bored. Sergeants trust bored people.

mordenkainen/79aa4bba7ad413d1.text: Stop looking at me as if I might wander off. I have my wits back. Most of them. The useful ones.

mordenkainen/7acf851bea72f67c.text: Amber. Rooms of it, and things sleeping in the amber, very old and very hungry, that will offer you whatever you've always wanted for the small price of the rest of you.

mordenkainen/8cf20a6650bf9565.text: I'll come. My spells are rusty and my pride is worse. Keep me away from mirrors and from anyone who says "hush".

mordenkainen/9b8c61be49a53a21.text: Corvina. I say it every morning, so I don't lose it again. If you find her before I do, say it to her. Names matter to the dead in this valley. They're very nearly all the dead have left.

mordenkainen/9c17ddd77a421782.text: Look at me, boy. The greatest wizard alive spent a year on this rock eating raw turnips and arguing with a cat that wasn't there. I had every title in the West. They were no use to me at all up here.

mordenkainen/9e16897fb3bf9713.text: I told everyone he beat me. I told myself. He didn't. I was beaten, and I knew it on the stair, and she said go, and I went. I left a girl of twenty-two holding a door against him so that I could be ashamed of losing instead of ashamed of running.

mordenkainen/9f50816524148bb8.text: Then cook. Cook for the people you're walking into the dark with, and they'll walk out again. You'll be a better wizard for it. Divination is mostly knowing when a thing is done, and you already know that.

mordenkainen/a1212da00ddc2d25.text: I came to this valley to kill him, and he beat me, and then he had his witch take everything I was and put it on her shelf, so I would live up here forever and not even know enough to be ashamed. He thought that was funny. He was right.

mordenkainen/aadfb61cb42cdd6a.text: No apprentice. You don't need a master; you need a kitchen. Come back when this is over and make me something that isn't a turnip.

mordenkainen/dffb877c0f19c47c.text: And he cheats. Not with magic. With people. He'll put somebody you care about between you and him, and smile.

mordenkainen/ea4f69a7cc8b911d.text: You again. Good. I've been rebuilding my spells from the bottom up; it's like learning to walk after a fall, if walking could set things on fire. What do you need?

mordenkainen/f249036fae21249c.text: He is not the strongest thing I've fought. He is the most patient. He doesn't win the battle; he wins the week after it, when you're tired and he isn't. Don't fight him on the day he chooses. He chooses every day.

mordenkainen/fcfea92e84679f35.text: Give me time to mend. When you go up to the castle, send a raven to this mountain, and I will come. That's a promise, and I remember how to keep those now.

mordenkainen/fd148b18de8835b2.text: Here. I've been wearing this for forty years without knowing what it was for. It holds a spell or two for whoever wears it. Put something nasty in it before you meet him.

morgantha/0a20853a07dc0937.text: And you gave Morgantha your word. Morgantha remembers.

morgantha/0d2d8ffb640afd5d.text: So soon? Take a pastry for the road. No? Ah, well. Everybody comes back to Morgantha in the end.

morgantha/0f3d8aa1a1a05761.text: Off you go, ducklings. Mind the stairs. Give your mother Morgantha's love; she'll be wanting another basket soon.

morgantha/107ffdb9111984eb.text: My heroes! No more children today, dearies. There's always pastries.

morgantha/15986dc938a55bf8.text: Two hundred. A hundred and fifty for the ducklings, and fifty for the shouting. Morgantha did say manners keep you fresh, pet.

morgantha/1c83c38d01c962c9.text: Back for a pastry, my sensible dearies? The little ones are keeping nicely.

morgantha/23c9274e64a17c66.text: Well, well. The brave one from the village square. Morgantha said she'd remember you, duckling. Out here there's nobody to watch you be brave.

morgantha/250a54cb90b4bb54.text: Gold is dull, pet. Here's a better price. One dream: your sweetest, the one you save for bad nights. Morgantha draws it out like a splinter, and after that she visits now and then while you sleep. Only to sit.

morgantha/28d88fc5743dad88.text: Taking a poor old woman's grandchildren, in her own home. Shame on you. Girls! Mother needs you!

morgantha/2cc9eba7e9e8df28.text: Then you never ran short, did you, pet? Lucky girl. He'd pay more for you than for any pastry.

morgantha/30a2e683f5a7254a.text: Peace, from heroes. That's worth something: you're the sort who keeps a promise and hates yourselves for it. Very well. The children, for your word. Morgantha will hold you to it.

morgantha/3206ee2c2b178eb0.text: But Morgantha is fair. Ask anybody. You may buy them back.

morgantha/370e7b6cb79ad8b3.text: Vallaki, dearie. Lady Wachter orders two dozen a week for her book club. Such a refined lady. Such deep sleepers, her friends.

morgantha/39af81953efe6ec0.text: Back again, dearies? Morgantha knew you would be. Everybody comes back.

morgantha/3cad612fc06ad5e1.text: Let them go? But they're paid for, dearie. Their mother had a basket a week all season and dreamed of her little lost one every night. A child for a season. That's the custom. Everybody knows the custom.

morgantha/3d7deab26e1443bb.text: Read the family receipts, did you? Then you know about the special flour. Every family has a secret ingredient, duckling. Ours is just more honest about it.

morgantha/3de9e03442bb9f96.text: Well. Aren't you brave. Morgantha's going, duckling. But Morgantha remembers every face. Every single one.

morgantha/4b1a230d5a872a8b.text: Back again, dearies. I knew you would be. They always come back to Morgantha.

morgantha/4ca123486283d494.text: Peace? From you? Morgantha has peace. She has a mill, and a hill, and a valley full of hungry people. What she hasn't got is a reason.

morgantha/4fc1b2929f36506f.text: And somebody's had their fingers in my cart. Morgantha counts her pastries, pet. She counts everything.

morgantha/53cc13fa6580e434.text: Visitors! Up all those stairs and not one of you carrying a basket. Never mind. Morgantha has plenty.

morgantha/549fbcc753317d32.text: Pastries! Fresh dream pastries! Oh, look at you. New faces. Lovely, plump new faces. Come, come, my ducklings. One bite and all your troubles go to sleep.

morgantha/54c0af5cb4949eab.text: My customers! All those stairs, just to see where the pastries come from. How are the dreams, dearies? Sweet? Of course they are.

morgantha/582120bae15daa24.text: Then you can't afford them, can you? Morgantha doesn't give credit. Credit is how folk end up owing children.

morgantha/5d109fcae21ddd05.text: And you broke my Offalia. She was the slow one, dearies, but she was mine. Morgantha is adding that to your account.

morgantha/614e0d6218cd1735.text: My windmill, pet, on the road to Vallaki. Me and my two daughters, baking day and night. Do visit. Bring the little ones. Bring everyone you love.

morgantha/61816b6f28de3057.text: My ducklings from the village, out on Morgantha's lane! She's on her way home to bake. You must visit. Up the hill, past the dead oak. Bring an appetite.

morgantha/640fa1e2e1e397a2.text: And my girls tell me you fib, dearies. Morgantha has written it in her book. Fibbers' promises aren't worth the flour they're dusted with.

morgantha/6bb2410dc1a14d11.text: There. Warm as a kiss. Eat it tonight, pet, and dream of whoever you've lost. Morgantha will know if you don't.

morgantha/75dc16b4eb2c313c.text: Vallaki, dearie. All those festivals make everybody so terribly cheerful. Folk need a good long sleep afterwards.

morgantha/785bebb608a3d5ec.text: All on her own, then. Bella's sulking somewhere and Offalia's gone somewhere, and it's only Morgantha and you. Well. Morgantha has managed alone before.

morgantha/78a0521ab06df067.text: Sent my Offalia trotting down the hill after nobody. She'll stop at every hedge from here to Vallaki. Never mind. Morgantha can see to her own visitors.

morgantha/78b4bf8b9b9d8d73.text: Three! Oh, you've a family to feed, I can tell. Do bring them by sometime. Bring the little ones especially.

morgantha/8277fbc9a3cf144d.text: There. Wasn't that lovely? You'll want another one tonight. Morgantha will be back. You'll be waiting.

morgantha/8351308967951774.text: The brave one who chased Morgantha's cart out of the village! Morgantha told you, duckling: she remembers every face. And here's yours, come all this way to be remembered properly.

morgantha/8f8a6406d487a651.text: Back again, my ducklings! And how were the dreams? Sweet? Of course they were. Morgantha's dreams always are.

morgantha/9541ed6b3ea7144c.text: Flour, honey, butter, a pinch of this and a pinch of that. Family recipe, dearie. Very old family.

morgantha/95d2ebd704ac9191.text: My plump little hero! You told Morgantha to take her cart out of the village, and she didn't, and now here you are in her house. Isn't that funny? Morgantha thinks it's funny.

morgantha/9bf5a7206c42a352.text: Out on the open road, dearie, with all these ravens watching? Come up to the mill. We'll do it properly there.

morgantha/a62492249d61da58.text: Pastries! Fresh dream pastries! Oh, new faces on my lane. Lovely. Come and visit Morgantha's mill, dearies. Up the hill, past the dead oak. Bring an appetite.

morgantha/a64d2465817009b2.text: Out? Oh, I'll go when I've sold out, my plump little hero. Mind your manners. Manners keep you fresh.

morgantha/a75b1583951cdc19.text: Not you at the old price, though, my plump little hero. You shouted at Morgantha in the square. Shouting is fifty gold extra.

morgantha/b316583254ce14bd.text: And who doesn't need a good night's sleep, in a place like this?

morgantha/b4449f7cced4bf21.text: A wise choice. Wrap it up warm, dearie. And remember: Morgantha remembers every customer. Every one.

morgantha/b5672ec3f4133018.text: Sweet dreams, pet. Dreams of whoever you've lost: mothers, sweethearts, little brothers. One bite, and you're with them all night. Two bites, and you're with them all week.

morgantha/b7a8ea306026ade3.text: The new faces! Still lovely. A little leaner. The road does that to people.

morgantha/c14640dfec8a9140.text: A hundred and fifty. Their mother let them go for less, if you don't count the honey. Pleasure doing business, dearies.

morgantha/c1dfce400a0238f6.text: No? Ah, well. Everyone comes round to Morgantha eventually. Everyone.

morgantha/c57647aa8f4787a2.text: Everybody, dearie. The farms, the village, Vallaki. Folk who've lost somebody. In this valley that's everybody.

morgantha/c76459e5a4cd46be.text: Just an old baker, dearie, and her two girls, doing an honest trade in a hard country. Folk want sweet dreams. Morgantha sells them. Is it Morgantha's fault the dreams are better than waking?

morgantha/ca493a060873becf.text: All three of us, dearies? Together? Oh, you are brave. Bella, pet, put down the mirror. Offalia! Visitors!

morgantha/ccaa3b98743547d8.text: And you had the free sample, pet. Morgantha has looked in on your dreams since. You were smiling.

morgantha/cd33591b74a3b2d4.text: Then Morgantha will have you for the oven, and your bones for the stone, and your dreams for supper. Waste not, dearies.

morgantha/d41bbab09e84d654.text: Off you go. Everybody comes up the hill in the end.

morgantha/d79c734f3a26d7d3.text: My plump little hero from the village square! Still shouting at old women? Out here, dearie, there's nobody to hear you do it.

morgantha/e42b22bfb6b3b000.text: Fed my own girl my own baking. Oh, that's clever. Morgantha likes clever. Clever keeps.

morgantha/e57df6828597badd.text: Such words, from such a pretty mouth. Morgantha will sit a little further off from your sun-trinket, pet, if it's all the same.

morgantha/e722d6fda51d7bfc.text: Secret ingredient, dearie. Every family has one.

morgantha/eaee8a1ff5961005.text: Delicious. Morgantha will be seeing you, duckling. Now and again. Don't wake.

morgantha/f6d264ed9d649917.text: Sensible. You'll go far, dearies. Not very far; it's a small valley. But far.

morgantha/ff7c96e890c851ea.text: And keep your fingers out of Morgantha's oven. There's something at the back of it that won't burn, and Morgantha doesn't care for things that won't burn.

mother_ecaterina/0829ac497eef668e.text: (Her voice comes through the ice, very small and very slow, a word at a time.) Yes. Ecaterina. From Vallaki. We had a winter. It took the little ones. All of them.

mother_ecaterina/815017c952ba9806.text: (She's wrapped in somebody's cloak by the shrine, holding her hands over the lamp.) It's out. They're out. I felt them go, one at a time, like coins out of a purse.

mother_ecaterina/9141f82e33d28a74.text: To stop. All of us. Or to see the valley in spring once, from the bottom. I'd take either. I've had a long time to decide, and I can't.

mother_ecaterina/9d6761110cb54553.text: Don't break the ice. If you wake me, they wake. And they'll want to be warm, and you're warm.

mother_ecaterina/aa46447fbe783116.text: (Very faintly.) I'm sorry. They were so cold.

mother_ecaterina/b14498c255a8e83e.text: Take it. It's the cold. All of it. The amber put it in there when it took us. Better in your hands than mine.

mother_ecaterina/b21994c64e5408e9.text: We asked the amber never to be cold again. It said yes. It said the price was to be the cold. So we are. They're all in here with me. They're so cold. Forty years and they're still so cold.

mother_ecaterina/b89b7f35a8b28414.text: I'll go down. Slowly. I'll see the valley in spring once, from the bottom, and then I'll see about the rest.

nadia_boteanu/0f0c0b1d752d91e6.text: Nadia. Nadia Boteanu. I light the lamps in Vallaki. Lit them. I don't know which, any more.

nadia_boteanu/142105069a4af000.text: A carriage stopped beside me on the road at dusk. Black, no driver. The door swung open by itself.

nadia_boteanu/3a97d6519ce4ad93.text: Once. The cook walked me down the passage, past the other cells, to a long hall at the end.

nadia_boteanu/40aa9c9ff3d1661e.text: A chain went up into the dark toward the noise. There's a noise down here like something breathing, all the time.

nadia_boteanu/415da946a71e1db2.text: Don't. Please. Oh. You're not him. You're not the cook either.

nadia_boteanu/449eca996cf8fec0.text: I thought, well, it's going toward Vallaki, and my feet hurt. It was not going toward Vallaki.

nadia_boteanu/4c4f5f212a047e37.text: Shut the gate behind you. It's worse when it's open and I can't go anywhere.

nadia_boteanu/730d824f10d7ca3e.text: He asked me about Vallaki's lamps, very politely, as if he cared. Then he sent me back. He said I wasn't ripe.

nadia_boteanu/91cd841821786396.text: Is it over? Is he gone?

nadia_boteanu/92154a61b5b2cb10.text: In a barrel. With the scraps. Of course. Why would anything here be easy.

nadia_boteanu/9ab99c832e2e49fd.text: Up there? Through his house? On my own?

nadia_boteanu/9b0b9ad55a8781f2.text: It should have been a rule already.

nadia_boteanu/bdd818738dfce05a.text: Out. Yes. Which way is out? I came in asleep.

nadia_boteanu/be21741bf4d09463.text: A man sat at the head of a table made of bones. The chairs were bones. The lamp over it burned green.

nadia_boteanu/f634606a060c822e.text: Hide. In the cell. Like a guest who's very good at being a guest. All right. Shut the gate. Come back.

nadia_boteanu/fe6007572ece5c98.text: You came back. Nobody comes back down here. Except the cook, and he doesn't count.

narrator/0006cf46805d499c.text: The stocks hold someone who used to matter in this town. Passers-by have been very careful not to throw anything, in case it's held against them later.

narrator/0006ec5a88ec5f5e.text: A cold stream runs down the slope in a cut of grey rock. On the far bank, purple flowers grow thick, and nothing has drunk on that side for a long time.

narrator/0009991945a802e6.text: Ileana keeps her eyes on the grave and doesn't answer you.

narrator/000a859f74367b89.text: Most of the inscription has been clawed away, from the inside. That tells you more than the words would have.

narrator/000c415d229013cf.text: The holy water hits the flames. They flinch, hiss, and are gone. Along the hall, the carved faces look somewhere else.

narrator/001735ee13cb5f7f.text: Somewhere in the walls a board creaks, slow and satisfied, like a fisherman reeling in a line.

narrator/001a17128dcb84d9.text: The crown goes quiet. Somewhere below, on the moor, a bird starts to sing, and stops as if surprised at itself.

narrator/003a2298aae38aa7.text: Vasilka. She is beautiful, the way a thing made very carefully is beautiful, and the seams at her wrists and throat are so fine you could take them for lace. The dress fits her as though it had always been waiting.

narrator/0053a5f9abaeca76.text: Empty niches, cold stone, and a heap of rags in the corner. Whatever lived here doesn't any longer, in either sense.

narrator/0064e3d43d0abe52.text: The sun's ashes have been swept into a tidy pile with a sign on a stick: KEEP FOR THE NEXT FESTIVAL.

narrator/006eaf8105ea6c4b.text: The furnace room is black and wet and steaming. The gears stand still.

narrator/007e3851ede34c4a.text: When you come up over the lip with her in your arms, she is already standing behind you.

narrator/007fdd36a6d31922.text: Where the Penitent fell there's only meltwater running off the landing into the gorge, and nine small heaps of grey cloth, and the lamp, which somebody has stood upright.

narrator/0088455b111c05d2.text: Grey stone three men high. At its foot, the snow is trampled and stained where the wolves came for you and you didn't let them reach the wall.

narrator/008f8ee72fd7f230.text: He lays two fingers on the pulse in their neck, the way a buyer feels a horse's leg, and takes his hand away. They wake on their knees on the cold ground with a hand at their throat, and scramble back to the fire.

narrator/00a2c53fcd9126f0.text: One flagstone sits a finger's width proud of the others. Under it, your footstep echoes too long.

narrator/00abfc39cf880753.text: The mirror in the corner is cracked clean across. Morgantha doesn't look at it.

narrator/00b4cdb648dce4f1.text: The earth heaves. The Seventh Row stands up out of the ground: every vine of it one plant, one great dark mass of root and vine-wood, rising twice the height of the house, dripping black wine from every branch.

narrator/00b8233055edd7a0.text: Silvain has Aurel's note spread on one knee and a stub of candle at their elbow, and has been reading the same sheet for an hour.

narrator/00bda4eb17b314ce.text: The rows nearest the house have turned green, a green so loud after the rest of the valley that it almost hurts. Somewhere up in the yard, a man is singing badly in a cellar.

narrator/00cb71d85d700b90.text: A narrow passage, its stones cracked and stained red, the floor strewn with old bones. They are laid out too neatly.

narrator/00dcbd8da9a1da38.text: Every panel in the hall stands open. Four of Kestrel Company come out of the walls in step, and their captain draws his sword.

narrator/00f531e1d2853b50.text: Sheet music stands open on the rack: a lullaby, copied out in a careful, loving hand. Across the top someone has written a single letter, W.

narrator/01006548dc38ef7a.text: You've done what you can for it. It will burn, if anything in Barovia still does.

narrator/010db587f70441ee.text: A tall clock stopped at a quarter past three. Its pendulum swings anyway, very slowly, keeping some other time.

narrator/011999b700c2e6b1.text: A reading hall: rows of desks, books open on every one, everything furred with frost. One desk is clear, and someone is weeping at it in a voice that doesn't stop for breath.

narrator/0128d1bf8b2cee6c.text: He doesn't pick the spear up. He looks at it as if it belongs to somebody braver.

narrator/01367b02da06fc3e.text: Inside the hood is a skull with a little parchment skin left on it, and two cold sparks where the eyes were.

narrator/0139c35ddf073836.text: The lake lies flat and black all the way to the far shore, where the wolf hills climb into cloud. On the landing the drying racks stand empty, and only one hut has smoke at its chimney.

narrator/013f01e60f43c63b.text: Far above, in the hall of echoes, the wailing stops. Later you'll find footprints in the frost: bare, narrow, walking out through the doors and down the mountain, toward the castle.

narrator/014e2658f3312a19.text: Soup: barley, onions, carrots, and something that might have been mutton once. It smells better than anything in Barovia has a right to.

narrator/0155d14725280ac7.text: How do you tell a child she is dead?

narrator/01564ff9e99cef54.text: Grave-salt in every carcass, a scoop to the leg, worked deep. It keeps her slow. Don't skimp it, or she'll be at the chain again like the spring of the bad year.

narrator/01566d1e3f2e1c6f.text: In the carved paneling, among the vines and flowers and dancing nymphs, serpents wind through every leaf, and the blossoms are skulls when you look at them straight.

narrator/015d72a64d8bfc0b.text: Strahd takes Kip's pen, dips it in the wine, and signs the back of the bill for the apricot: a single tall letter, a Z, crossed with a flourish.

narrator/0179db935f219ab7.text: The bar is oak, polished by three generations of elbows. Carved under the lip, where only the bar-keeper would see it, is a tiny raven.

narrator/017c23af4cf5db4a.text: The cold corner of the study. The wallpaper here is newer than the rest, and under it the plaster is newer, and under that, where the plaster has cracked, there is brick, laid in a hurry. Garlic has been pushed into the cracks, dried to paper.

narrator/01962ffc192be00d.text: A thin girl of twelve or so sits on an upturned bucket by the lane with a basket of pastries on her knees. She has flour on her nose, and her sleeves pulled down over her hands.

narrator/01a6afbb7d0f2276.text: When the last stitch is out the wings open by themselves, slowly, the way a hand does when you stop making a fist. They fill the kitchen. Every Belview in the room goes quiet.

narrator/01ace6cdc529fe5a.text: A narrow vestry: robes on pegs, a chest, a cot where the priest has clearly been sleeping since the theft.

narrator/01adb5f9f1a538f4.text: Everything in the shop is dusted, labeled and squared to the edge of its shelf. Behind the counter, a narrow man in a spotless apron is already reaching for a pencil.

narrator/01b1273de7f2c4dd.text: Behind the field wall, under a flat stone, a farmer hid what he valued most: a pair of heavy iron gauntlets that make your arms feel like a bull's.

narrator/01b7dc2280b945e4.text: A fire in an iron basket, banked high. The watchmen keep a pot of something on the edge of it that smells mostly of turnips and partly of hope.

narrator/01ce3b07501a7ffb.text: The red amber is colder than ever, and under the floor something very large has turned its head toward whoever carries its gift.

narrator/01d7b374af2b3adf.text: The attic is lit by candles and by a chalk circle on the boards, which glows faintly with a light of its own. The air tastes of struck iron.

narrator/01e7a809b23f82d1.text: The burgomaster's house is the biggest in Krezk, which is to say it has two chimneys. Only one of them is smoking. In an upper window, a candle burns in the middle of the day.

narrator/01f0422ac20a7ea9.text: Mounds with no markers. The rope's work, buried where the rope left it. Somebody once tried to plant a little cross on one of them; it is lying in the grass.

narrator/01fa5f11447a8515.text: Vladimir rises from the winged chair for the first time, and all down the table dead heads turn to watch. He draws a greatsword as long as a man is tall and salutes you with it, properly, as if there were a crowd.

narrator/01ffad3bb7cc845d.text: You sleep in shifts in a locked room off the long hall. Twice in the night footsteps stop outside the door, and wait, and go away.

narrator/0200f52c7b5f5202.text: The cuffs give one after the other with two small clicks. Fen drops to four feet in the straw and stays there a long moment, head down, shaking.

narrator/020e24ca068892e1.text: A narrow bed, neatly made, with a rag doll propped on the pillow. Under the pillow, when you lift it, is a pressed wildflower of a kind that doesn't grow in town.

narrator/0214d1e3e3985fe3.text: The fire's lit and the stew's on, but the Martikovs look at you across the taproom the way you'd look at someone who tracked mud through a church.

narrator/021a1d45cfedef2d.text: You sit with him. The chapter is long, and the young lord in it is very sure of himself, and Aurel reads every word as if it matters. Silvain doesn't leave his side.

narrator/021ed95a39d4953d.text: For a long time she says nothing. Then she closes the book on her desk, gently, and it doesn't crumble.

narrator/022a96aceed7fa33.text: The slate roof of the keep, with chimneys like broken teeth. Ravens watch you from the ridge.

narrator/0241b2b1ee4cf15d.text: The switchback track arrives at the abbey gate. Inside: the courtyard with its well and a statue of Markovia, the church doors to the north, the wards to the east and the garden door to the west.

narrator/024559b862474e47.text: The ice of the gorge wall above the landing is clear as a window, and there are people in it. Nine of them, kneeling in a row, facing up the pass toward the temple, frozen in the middle of a prayer.

narrator/024e23c591915dec.text: On the side of an old ash facing away from the fire, at the height of a soldier's shoulder: the swept-wing bird again, and three rows of ten strokes, and one more.

narrator/0259d72f7541797e.text: You go easy. She stops pushing at once and looks at you, deeply offended.

narrator/026a105b45091f35.text: Davian takes his son's hands and turns them over in his own. The dark veins are fading already, back to plain blue.

narrator/02784ad3a8aed606.text: The mist that was Strahd slides away like water finding a drain. Wherever his coffin is, deep under the castle, he is going there now, and he will lie helpless in it for a while.

narrator/028019fa3b5dd7b8.text: Behind the armour stands, a sword still in its scabbard. Draw an inch of it and the blade catches light from nowhere, a flicker of fire along the steel.

narrator/02865917b416c09e.text: Bildrath takes you through to the storeroom with a candle and an air of grievance. The white logs are stacked by the back door, very neatly. One of them is standing on its end.

narrator/0294a3e336b274ac.text: The doorframe is gouged at knee height, from the floor side, as if something lay down against it and dug. The bar across the door is newer than the frame.

narrator/02971187f673d4f4.text: The paper is old and soft as cloth. The hand is firm, a little hurried, signed with a single M.

narrator/02a38fc14be004dc.text: The chain lies slack off the drum and into the rock, moving very slightly. She knows the sound of that capstan now. She won't let it take her twice.

narrator/02afc82bf01df458.text: The top of the south tower: battlements, the hatch you came up through, and the wind.

narrator/02b53c56c83b3d63.text: The crown of the hill is flat and bare inside its ring of stones. In the middle stands a tree with bark like a burnt hand and roots that go into the ground the way fingers go into a wound. Beside it lies a man made of earth and timber, forty feet long, cloaked, with a face you have seen before.

narrator/02b557d60286a10b.text: Out of the wolf, his wrists are thin enough to work out of the cuffs. Thistle catches him before he hits the straw.

narrator/02d6c11c5a3a7e5e.text: Godrick gets up at once, the way he would for Sir Pellam, and walks to him across the camp with his sword left lying in the grass. His eyes are open. Nobody is behind them.

narrator/02f74107542eda66.text: Wagons in a ring around a fire, horses on a line, the lake at the camp's back with a rotten jetty and reeds. The road runs back east to Vallaki's gate.

narrator/02fcf4d1387b8878.text: He sets down a sack of flour, very gently, as if it might wake.

narrator/0319fda60545c908.text: The rider unfolds it, holds it to the lamp, and turns it over. Then he looks at Dobre for a long time, and Dobre stops smiling.

narrator/032ca3f989d9a956.text: You read him the two entries: the courteous prince who asked to read, and the line underneath in different ink. "He asked for the deep vault. God help us, I showed him."

narrator/032cb137785ebd02.text: Behind the wayside shrine, someone left a tin of salve for whoever needed it next. It smells of mint and clean linen.

narrator/033ab38cdc2d4abc.text: In a hollow of the dead oak the ravens keep their treasures: buttons, a spoon, a ring of keys and, at the bottom, a raven carved from silver, warm as a living bird.

narrator/0343f3197e96e09c.text: In the lamp-keeper's niche, a hooded lantern under a skin of soot. Light it and the room shows you more than it did a moment ago.

narrator/035b3a374618063c.text: Small stones, hand-cut, each with a first name and nothing else. Whoever cut the last few was running out of time and was careful anyway.

narrator/037782b61e033ae3.text: People turn to look at Ireena as she passes, and then look quickly away, as if her red hair were a lamp left burning after curfew.

narrator/0377aad30df8e291.text: The planks are slick and you are a stride short. Your fingers close on the hem of his coat as it goes over, and the hem tears.

narrator/038c7acee5319181.text: Under the ledge, where they left their bundles for the climb, there are nine purses of temple offerings nobody ever made.

narrator/03c2ef6b1be9de3d.text: A black bird sits on a fence post and watches you pass. It is not one of the Keepers' ravens; those look away when you meet their eyes. This one doesn't.

narrator/03cadb6ce9a83d1a.text: The bar groans up out of its brackets and the gate opens a body's width, exactly. Krezk doesn't do anything wider than it has to.

narrator/03cbdc4e6134f449.text: Black armour lies in pieces on the floor of the guard post.

narrator/03d20cb1e3fac6a6.text: You say the words over the bricks, and push fresh garlic into every crack, and plaster over all of it. The scratching stops. Outside, for the first time in a long while, the dog stops howling.

narrator/03ee9b7a384fb548.text: Two doors of solid amber, lit from within like honey held up to a candle. There's no handle, no lock and no hinge you can see: only a ring of carved glyphs on the floor in front of them.

narrator/040203b5e40bb0f2.text: Nothing is left inside but heat, ash and the smell of it.

narrator/040bc5d8738b6698.text: Every window in the castle is dark but one. It is directly over the great doors, and it is lit for you.

narrator/04230ecebd80f33e.text: Thistle is braiding crow feathers into a cord in the firelight, fast and neat, and humming something tuneless and happy under her breath.

narrator/0425655c5646e82a.text: Whoever carries a gift sleeps soundly, and wakes rested. Nobody else does, and nobody mentions it.

narrator/042f84c89c467726.text: Under the crocheted blanket lies a marsh root trimmed into the shape of a swaddled infant, and tucked under its chin like a rattle, a green gem the size of a hen's egg, glowing softly.

narrator/0445ac14dd6f86fb.text: It fits like a key in a lock. A little sister lost in the woods by the lake, about the age Ireena was when Kolyan Indirovich found her wandering, with no memory of where she came from. The red hair.

narrator/044a038f33e400f2.text: Behind the festival ledger, a velvet case the Baron must have been saving for the big night: a necklace of small glowing beads, each one hot to the touch.

narrator/044bd2a6488d9eb4.text: He is on the throne, one leg over the arm of it, as if he has been waiting a long time and enjoyed every minute. Two great wolves rise from the dais steps.

narrator/048363a1f3ce6ddd.text: The old words come right, every one, and on the last the sill seems to harden like ice on a pond. His hand stops a finger's width from it.

narrator/04853ea0fe4a8c0b.text: Bluto keeps the fire going all night and talks about fish, quietly, to nobody. It's the most restful thing you've heard in Barovia.

narrator/04864904e5bf2716.text: The road east runs back the way you came, toward the gates and the mist beyond them. The mist has not moved; it doesn't need to.

narrator/049d79558627706a.text: Books in neat stacks, a coffin with a reading lamp beside it, and no mirror anywhere.

narrator/04b0c6cd60c549f2.text: A big man in a watch captain's coat stops dead in the middle of the square. His right arm is wrong: scaled red-black to the shoulder, with claws where the nails should be. He is staring at Ireena as if she were a ghost he'd been expecting for years.

narrator/04b6695f9a7312ec.text: The cook's work. He did say he was good with bricks.

narrator/04babc0c1da00c29.text: A lean figure in the amber holds a fistful of chains, and every chain ends in the snarling head of a hound. The amber around the hounds is clouded, like smoke.

narrator/04c7b80a3cfd44d8.text: She says it again, slowly, as if she's tasting it.

narrator/04d5f948d5c4c7d4.text: The hoop turns with a grudging click, and the whole end of the cask swings out on hidden pins. Inside, wrapped in a wine-stained shirt, lies a stone as green as a leaf held up to the sun, and faintly warm.

narrator/04f4646d7820d192.text: From the rock you can see the whole lake: the far north shore where the pines come down to drink, and the hills above, and a rock face high up with a dark mouth in it.

narrator/04f61b8d9be04a56.text: She fades the way breath fades from a window. The frost on the other desks melts, just a little, and doesn't come back.

narrator/04fcea55f15b744e.text: The frost scar in the courtyard has gone. There is only a long, clean stretch of flagstones, as if someone had swept it.

narrator/0505378ef79cbee9.text: The last of Lady Wachter's people are down or running. The watch hauls Lady Wachter to the foot of the dais by the elbows. She walks between them as if they were seeing her in to dinner.

narrator/0510ca3e49b88e83.text: The well is dry, the rope still tied, the bucket somewhere down in the dark. Someone has carved a sunburst into the lip, and someone else has tried to scrape it off.

narrator/051cfc35c097f4f2.text: The rowboat rides at the foot of the jetty, bailed and ready, oars shipped. The north shore is a long pull, and the wolf hills are waiting on the far side of it.

narrator/052853444c2cd1b0.text: It looks at the leaf, then toward the vineyards south of the lake road, then back at you, as if you were being slow on purpose.

narrator/0532932a49c3037d.text: Thistle drops out of a tree beside you with no warning at all, which she seems to think is a greeting.

narrator/053e4aa4c50b1d33.text: Silver dragon scales, shed and gathered and made into a knight's coat. The silver's own. The count put it under her so she'd lie on her enemy forever and never know it.

narrator/05434a5e1464d41f.text: Shelves of sealed jars and cheeses under cloth, every label in the same neat hand. Nothing has spoiled, and nothing is fresh.

narrator/056fd71b0aae3230.text: The lakebed goes out from under your feet. By the time you're up again, spluttering, Bluto has thrown the sack into the deep water.

narrator/057c970c0aea974e.text: You leave her to it. Behind you, the letter crackles in her hands for a long time before the fire is the only sound.

narrator/0582bc35d98df10c.text: A domed oven of fired brick, cold to the touch. The kettle on the hob beside it is warm.

narrator/059e897051fd2aab.text: The yellow room is empty, and the wardrobe door hangs open on gowns that will never fit anyone again.

narrator/05afeec2a250873b.text: The wolves that have been pacing you through the fields all morning stop pretending to be shy.

narrator/05b7c21606eb4ce5.text: She pulls her lip down with one finger. Behind her milk teeth the gums are dark, and something hard and grey is pushing through.

narrator/05bc5ee734882029.text: The clothes are a generation out of date and the paint has crazed like an old plate. These children would be grown by now, if anyone had let them grow.

narrator/05c9d77620bdc4a1.text: The split halves shift on the block, slowly, toward the yard where the boy is lying.

narrator/05d4db21bb1bfb2a.text: The coffin rests on trestles between two new candles. Someone replaces them every few hours, and doesn't sleep in between.

narrator/05e08b02c2d87a9b.text: The house is quiet now. Somewhere far above, someone is walking about.

narrator/05e1e94b02253715.text: You climb out of the dark by the long stair. Torches gutter as you pass, like servants who no longer know whom they serve.

narrator/05ea13314612a4a2.text: Vladimir draws, and his knights come down the black stair behind him with their swords already out.

narrator/05eae3f7a32e5ef1.text: Pidlwick II pats the stone bench as you pass, the way you'd pat a dog.

narrator/05efd11d13c03752.text: Lucian reads the letter once, slowly, and folds it along its creases as if it might break.

narrator/05f4ea5d77ab839c.text: From somewhere in his habit he produces a bottle with an inch of wine left in it, and looks at the inch, and at you, and makes a terrible decision.

narrator/05fdd421b60a9739.text: Shuttered cottages, mud, and woodsmoke from chimneys that are trying not to be noticed. A village, at last, holding its breath.

narrator/05fea0b634f7393d.text: Tall white candles in iron stands. They burn, and they don't get any shorter. He wants it always to be the first night.

narrator/060332afbe4838f3.text: Bray sits at the kitchen window with a blanket round him and watches the castle road. Danika sits beside him and watches Bray.

narrator/061a140be9076375.text: You sit with Grigore by the pallet while the light goes. Nobody talks. When the sun is down, a door bangs open along the street on its own: Bildrath's.

narrator/063c06fa30b3130e.text: The ribbon smokes. The bow crawls, trying to tie itself tighter, and comes apart in your fingers like wet ash. The bell rings once.

narrator/0644f745746629d2.text: Then they're gone down the corridor and out through the kitchen, and the Belviews in the kitchen are wailing and laughing at once, and the mountain has some new and strange residents.

narrator/0646110c3b5d0d57.text: A family portrait in a heavy gilt frame, hung over the mantel where every guest would see it first.

narrator/06491b768c76d186.text: Under the portrait over the fireplace someone keeps a stand of candles lit. The painted woman has red hair and Ireena's eyes.

narrator/06494772b7316028.text: Where were we? Ah, yes. Barovia, and you, still in it.

narrator/0659e4d030dc2977.text: The sigils are good work, copied by a careful hand. But the destination glyph doesn't name a place. It reaches for anywhere beyond the mists and finds nothing at all. Whatever stands in that circle isn't sent away. It's simply sent.

narrator/067b9829f66ea1fc.text: Shapes climb up over the edge of the shelf in the moonlight, roped together, frost in their beards. They have been climbing toward the temple for a very long time.

narrator/067c30da14fb617d.text: The abbey gate stands open. It looks as if it's never been shut, and has rusted that way on purpose.

narrator/067d9395fd5677fd.text: The tent flap opens behind you. Stanimir fills it, and he is not holding his fiddle. Outside, the music has stopped.

narrator/0680653cfce39d9a.text: A handcart heaped with glazed pastries under a white cloth. They smell of honey and warm butter and something else, faint and sleepy, underneath.

narrator/06899fe0f4da1def.text: You unfold Markovia's letter and read it to him, all of it, slowly, in the candlelight. The Belviews stop humming. Clovin, at the back, mouths the words he knows.

narrator/069774c0a0f482d1.text: The thing in the coffin goes still, and stays still. Far above you, stone groans, as if the whole castle has let out a breath.

narrator/069b8dcd3116b219.text: For a long time Vladimir says nothing at all.

narrator/06a440b5dae4d87a.text: He reads over you, louder, the way a man talks over a noise in the next room. The words don't reach him.

narrator/06b185f4d7397bd0.text: The lower town is where the smiles get thinner: leaning houses, a coffin maker's sign, and a hovel by the palisade with three small faces in its one window.

narrator/06b903bce141e00a.text: A roof beam above the hall hangs loose in its socket, swaying, aimed.

narrator/06c0aae52ca8f033.text: Two uniforms, pressed and hung, ready for the morning. The morning has been a long time coming.

narrator/06c77778e873b40c.text: A rough mound of earth, no marker yet, no candle. The burgomaster's grave looks like what it was: a hurry.

narrator/06cd4487339acbcc.text: Someone sits down beside her and stays until morning, and nobody mentions it the next day.

narrator/06cf478075f81905.text: A rocking chair polished by long use. The bowl beside it is full of something small, white and shelled. You decide they are almonds.

narrator/06d87db47828c628.text: A small fire, a worn settee, a sword leaning against the hearth within easy reach. Whoever sits in this room has been sitting up nights.

narrator/06f1618cade88494.text: The crypt is cold and quiet, the sarcophagus lid set square again. Someone has left a candle on it, and it burns perfectly straight, though there's a draught.

narrator/06f2bee412e3df38.text: The knight's head turns toward you with a sound like a door on a cold morning. Behind the visor, nothing blinks.

narrator/06fe2a2658ba7e5d.text: The pool is perfectly round and perfectly still, and the snow along its rim has melted back a hand's breadth all the way round. In the water, the sky is a little brighter than the sky above it.

narrator/07144e62882575a7.text: A boulder heaped with little offerings: buttons, a wooden doll, a rusted spoon, ribbons gone grey with spray. Barovians bring the falls something for the ones it took.

narrator/07484b8e47eee0a7.text: The pillars are carved with the wardens at work: carrying sarcophagi, sealing lids, standing guard. In the highest carvings the wardens are leaning close to the amber, listening.

narrator/07787907fc8af541.text: The great hall goes up into the dark further than your light can follow. At its centre stands a colossal robed figure in a warden's hood, and under the hood there is no face, only smooth stone.

narrator/07b7d399df8eb171.text: A long gallery lined with carved stone faces, and at the far end a fire burning in a great hearth.

narrator/07c08e2659c16d46.text: The camp outside is empty and the fire has burned low. Madam Eva has not moved from her table.

narrator/07e0903985cdf289.text: She steps down, smiling, and the crowd lets her through, because nobody can say exactly what she has done. Yet.

narrator/07f81db7f3cd3990.text: An old standing stone, carved long ago with spirals worn almost smooth. Somebody newer has daubed a crude castle over the spirals in red clay.

narrator/07facd000a35db4e.text: She falls the way his spawn fall, all at once, into dust and an old scholar's coat. In the coat there's a slip of paper with a few lines of small, slanted handwriting and a name at the bottom: Corvina.

narrator/080df9420473340f.text: Chalk, scorch marks and ash. The circle tells you only that Victor practises, and that it goes badly.

narrator/081c46e4e8f5fad6.text: The fever is the kind that sits in the blood and won't be sweated out. Willow bark won't touch it. Prayer with a real answer behind it might, or a hand that has healed before.

narrator/08299e943b98f960.text: The tower is quieter than it was. You hadn't noticed the slow beat in the stones until it stopped.

narrator/082dc45a5b9df745.text: From the crag's edge the whole valley lies open under the cloud: the road, the dark pines, and far off on its pillar of rock, the castle, which you could swear is looking back.

narrator/083e0c857e051c25.text: Above the altar hangs a sunburst of gilded oak as wide as a cart wheel, the brightest thing in the abbey. It hangs a little away from the wall, on two iron hooks.

narrator/085583f25630af8c.text: You tell them. At the head of the table, Vladimir has gone completely still.

narrator/085ade50dc9f6bb7.text: You bury him by the road. This time he stays where he is put.

narrator/086b4fa82800c526.text: Then there is only a brushed coat on the step, and the carriage lamp coming closer, and Ileana's door is a door like any other.

narrator/087607ea546c3ac1.text: He scrambles up and is gone up the cellar stair, or round the corner, or wherever frightened men go in Vallaki.

narrator/088e97e6a7789887.text: Every dead head at the long table turns, at once, with a sound like a door in a storm.

narrator/088f47d5ad4fbc4f.text: The village sits in the valley like something left out in the rain: grey roofs, nailed shutters, mud to the ankle. Smoke rises from a few chimneys, and from none of them in a hurry.

narrator/0892829bb28aaff1.text: Somewhere in a farmhouse below the road, a shutter opens, and stays open.

narrator/089c23797805ab4c.text: Heads turn as Ireena comes into the firelight, and the music falters for half a bar. Then the fiddler plays louder, as if to make up for it.

narrator/089f6619c7fc8d98.text: At the head of the bier there is a hollow in the stone, smooth and round, made for something that isn't here. Someone has laid a single dried flower in it.

narrator/08a2590e2992f30c.text: The Huntsman sets the pack on you with one note of the horn, and the hounds come up the road in silence.

narrator/08abd1627e33bf5e.text: Thistle comes up out of sleep on all fours and goes to him low and quick, the way a dog goes to its master. Her eyes are open and empty.

narrator/08c0a9e1a8acf984.text: When the marshal falls, the column falls with him: every rider, every horse, a long rattle of bones going down together in the mud, and then nothing but harness and rust.

narrator/08d7b9237af81a68.text: You bail it out and ship the oars. It sits low and steady in the water: a good boat. Across the lake, the hills wait.

narrator/090e0ba81628ede1.text: It says nothing at all about leaving.

narrator/09111514946482de.text: The raven in her hands grows warm, then hot, then too bright to look at. The black window over the altar turns grey, and then gold.

narrator/0914e7df28524bd5.text: At the very back of the cellar, one rack has been bricked over. The bricks are newer than the wall around them, and someone has pressed a row of corks into the mortar like buttons.

narrator/091c2a5feb9a8605.text: The offer is sincere in one way only: he'd carry her somewhere, gladly, and very quickly. You've seen that look on men selling horses they've already sold to someone else.

narrator/092281967231b288.text: He comes over the north wall the way goats come down a cliff: all at once, without looking. He's very big and very bent, with a goat's legs and a man's shoulders, and a carved wolf held carefully in both hands.

narrator/0956eb763d496c55.text: The first blow cracks the ice from top to bottom. Mother Ecaterina falls out of it into your arms, light as a bundle of sticks and burning hot to the touch, and the lamp rolls away across the landing.

narrator/095d9cd086306e0f.text: In the storage room, the bare nook in the corner is not bare anymore. A stair waits behind it, going down.

narrator/097f4654af7df55e.text: The Old Svalich Road runs past a clearing on the edge of the Svalich Woods. In it, painted wagons stand in a loose ring around a bonfire, horses doze in a rail pen by the water, and a tent the size of a small house glows from inside.

narrator/0985c3b236e980ea.text: A little roadside shrine, its sun-disk chipped away to bare stone. Someone still leaves candle stubs here, though none of them are lit.

narrator/09a7ccfd65b7644a.text: Bunks made up tight enough to bounce a coin, and none of them slept in for a very long time.

narrator/09a98dcd2a517b27.text: Bluto's shack is dark, his boat still tied at the jetty's foot. The lake is calm in the way a full stomach is calm.

narrator/09be35303f42959d.text: A big young man in a sheepskin is digging a grave with a good deal more force than the earth requires. He doesn't look up.

narrator/09c2bb2499009b44.text: Incense, candle smoke, and the dry smell of very old paper. Charms hang from every rope, turning slowly, though the air in the tent is still.

narrator/09c6897add587216.text: The roost goes up all at once: a black storm of wings and beaks and shrieking, pouring down off the beams.

narrator/09c7e544f7179d4a.text: Somewhere around the tenth "Silvain" the reading slows. Around the twelfth it stops, in the middle of a word.

narrator/09e58078783ebec5.text: Rows of pews under a sunburst window gone grey with soot. Your footsteps carry all the way to the altar and come back slower.

narrator/09e634fab48324f8.text: A spreading slick of rot. Lorghoth the Decayer has decayed.

narrator/09f25dcd0e9164d8.text: The capstan groans, then turns. The chain comes up out of the rock link by link, slowly, then all at once, fighting you, and you hold it, and the pawl drops into its notch with a clang.

narrator/0a0528ceed6d0730.text: The back lanes are narrow, muddy and full of collapsed fences. A cat watches you from a rain barrel with the calm of something that has outlived several owners.

narrator/0a099d619b72118a.text: The fiddle is playing something slow tonight. When you come into the firelight, a few of the Vistani nod to you as if you were cousins.

narrator/0a42204d72a2b94b.text: Zamfira sits on the step beside her mother, shelling beans much faster than her mother does, with grey-rooted nails.

narrator/0a46c184b3fb5044.text: The cold takes the breath out of you before you're a body's length down. You come up gasping, and the rope swings, and somewhere under you something patient waits for you to try again.

narrator/0a4aa550cf3492c0.text: Granny takes the girl by the hand. Mouse looks back once, over her shoulder, and doesn't say anything, and then the trees close behind them both.

narrator/0a68f7f9efa24ff5.text: She is very beautiful. She does not breathe. Every so often, slowly, the fingers of her right hand close, as if around another hand, and then open again.

narrator/0a8f02d81d87c1c3.text: Ireena stops at the foot of the mound. The statue has her face. Not a likeness: her face, the set of the jaw, the small frown.

narrator/0a92651f151af6da.text: The crowd cheers again, slightly less than before. Vallaki is saved, and it is going to be very, very happy about it.

narrator/0aa05e8eb1bbdb87.text: The servants' hall is the only room with its table still laid: plates, cups, a loaf gone to stone. Nobody in this house has needed to eat for a long time, and nobody has cleared up either.

narrator/0ab8b9dc21f5d2c7.text: He looks at Ireena. He looks for a long time. The smoke goes out of his arm the way breath goes out of a body.

narrator/0ad0f2cf87f2110b.text: Armour on the black stair. Vladimir Horngaard comes down into the tomb with his knights at his back and stops at the foot of the dais.

narrator/0ad9c25c2905701d.text: And among the offerings, something no wolf would think to give: a bundle in oiled cloth, too square and too carefully wrapped. Somebody hid it here, among things nobody would steal.

narrator/0adecb459413190d.text: The gate is a pair of iron-strapped log doors under a walkway where the watch stamps its feet. Every face on the walkway is turned outward, toward the road. One or two turn back to look at you.

narrator/0aedac48dece4356.text: One servant bolts. The other is slower, and fat with Lady Wachter's dinners. He sits in the mud, bucket in his lap, and tells you everything he knows, which is that he was told to make the sun wet and not to ask why.

narrator/0aef14ee95e5e8c5.text: In the morning the watch finds Ilie at the lake gate, sitting against the post, smiling, white as milk. Nobody finds Ana at all. Mila Petrova wakes up and eats her breakfast.

narrator/0afe4b6f76b6d7d4.text: The boards of the gallery give way under you with a long tearing groan.

narrator/0afe525202923c1b.text: The round room is cold and bright now. Red glass crunches underfoot, and nothing beats.

narrator/0b3a2efdf7bcde34.text: Ireena lifts the spoon, stops, and sniffs.

narrator/0b4b73dafd02f01c.text: Up in the hills a wolf howls, long and rising. Another answers it from the north, and then a third, and then the whole ridge is singing.

narrator/0b4c73020ef55f65.text: The carvings on the parapet turn their heads. Stone grinds on stone as wings unfold that were never meant to be carved.

narrator/0b6bcb354749d540.text: Sorin crouches, and takes a stick of firewood from the pile, and starts to carve with his thumbnail. Dmitri watches him make a wolf for his son, and the anger goes out of him all at once, like water out of a split cask.

narrator/0b8b3ec4d3bd4c43.text: Vladimir comes off the last step with his greatsword already moving. Behind him on the stair, dead knights in black plate, climbing.

narrator/0b8d9b55e59e1901.text: The humming breaks into a shout. The effigy's chest splits like a log in frost, and out of it, unfolding, comes a tree that walks.

narrator/0b95c7a318736927.text: His eyes go to the empty place at the end of the pen and come back quickly.

narrator/0bcb420be5a991c9.text: Goat bones, a horse's skull, and a long thin bone that might be a man's. All of it scorched, all of it cracked open.

narrator/0bccbda653c056b5.text: A tiny old woman in three shawls is sweeping snow off the stones around the pool with a broom taller than she is. She is singing to the water, tunelessly and with great affection.

narrator/0bea93e8cb55063d.text: Wren rolls out of his blanket and walks to him, perfectly balanced, perfectly silent, his face as blank as a fresh page.

narrator/0bf3b84e10aa9e77.text: The sky over the road comes apart into wings. Under it, from the ditches, the dead sit up.

narrator/0bfd9f57ae06f1a5.text: The crowd scatters like pigeons, and the square is suddenly very large.

narrator/0c0a4ed2aa116541.text: Ratatoille is doing something complicated to tonight's rations with a pinch of salt, a pinch of something from a twist of paper, and a great deal of concentration. It smells unreasonably good.

narrator/0c10bcef2112a64f.text: The boy is thin and flushed, his hair stuck to his forehead. His eyes open when you lean over him, and fix on you with the frank interest of a child who has met very few new people.

narrator/0c12957b0550cdbc.text: The painted woman's eyes are lowered, as if to something just below her frame.

narrator/0c2a92d9c293cefb.text: The heart rings like a struck bell. Below, armour comes clanking up the last turn of the stair, and something in a great helm floats up the well behind it.

narrator/0c40b31f55d33e90.text: A pillar carved with dragons climbing toward the dark. Their eyes have been picked out with something that catches the light.

narrator/0c4514c8cdebd5c0.text: Fifty paces in, the marks end at a pine scored with claw marks higher than a tall man can reach. Whatever took the peddler stood up on two legs to do it.

narrator/0c45d37a6dd11814.text: There is a place in front of the statue where the blank face seems to look straight down. You'd rather not stand in it.

narrator/0c668d1323d0776b.text: And all that cold will have to go somewhere.

narrator/0c6a5eb09596d621.text: The smell reaches you first, sweet and wrong. Then the things that died on these hills and didn't stay down come crawling out of the bracken, grinning.

narrator/0c70d84948c29c45.text: She beams at you and offers you a pincushion shaped like a sun. Whatever's behind the smile, the smile is winning.

narrator/0c8649b62b971e5e.text: The mists part again, and the story picks up where you set it down.

narrator/0c86f6c1b3c05d0b.text: You light a stub from the box at the statue's feet and say what you have to say, or say nothing. The flame stands perfectly straight in a wind that bends the pines on the wall.

narrator/0ca84fc955aaeff9.text: Every hearth on the floor exhales at once, and the air turns to black wool in your throat.

narrator/0cad84d5d6da4912.text: The roots of the ribbon tree have been dug under and packed back. In the hollow, wrapped in a Vistani shawl, a pair of boots with springs worked into the heels.

narrator/0cba25c11446e9d7.text: The woman at the front holds a tin lamp in both hands. The lamp is lit. As you look at her, her eyes move, slowly, and find you.

narrator/0cbf325db43d63db.text: Closed doors on both sides, and a long carpet that swallows your footsteps. The crying is always one door further on.

narrator/0cc217e57f934c12.text: The vault behind the honey-glow doors is heaped with offerings: coins, rings, swords, crowns, children's toys. Everything anyone ever brought down here to bargain with, and left.

narrator/0cca31496737e5bc.text: Two wards, one nested inside the other. The outer one is ancient and simple: it is waiting to hear a name. The inner one is new, neat and spiteful, and it is listening for one particular person. It isn't listening for you.

narrator/0ceab9b0982005e7.text: He can't hold your eyes. His hands go white on the spade handle, and there's dirt under his nails that didn't come from this grave: it's pale and dry, like dust from a stone box.

narrator/0cfcd936986b410e.text: A big fire, well banked, ringed with stones painted green. A haunch of something turns on a spit. You decide not to identify it.

narrator/0d46b59ed1bb0055.text: It is quick, which is the only kind thing about it. Afterwards Kiril stands up a man again, licking his teeth, and nobody in the cave looks at you.

narrator/0d48e797031be812.text: They pass so close you could touch the coffin. The one at the front stops beside your ditch, lifts his face, breathes in where breathing does no good, and walks on.

narrator/0d4b941de2f73520.text: He glares at you over the spade, and either he's honest or he's angrier than he is guilty. You can't tell which.

narrator/0d575fb7f490e5b6.text: Horses in a rail pen, sleek and well fed, the best-cared-for living things you have seen in Barovia. They watch you the way the Vistani do: politely, and counting.

narrator/0daf81a7c8457296.text: A shop so tidy it feels like a reprimand. Behind the counter, each shelf is labeled, and each label has a price, and each price has been written in ink so it can't be argued with.

narrator/0dbb7b8d994bf757.text: The ward slides through your understanding like meltwater, and the colossus is already stepping down off its plinth.

narrator/0dc22d1d4704d026.text: The Tenant comes up the little stair on all fours, and the servants who starved with him come up behind.

narrator/0dc34889531c8635.text: Not trophies of hunting: trophies of hunters. A row of small things on nails: a scarf, a brass compass, a girl's hair ribbon, a pair of spectacles. Each has a name written under it and a date. All the dates are a long time ago.

narrator/0dd31ee105be4184.text: The black stair goes down a long way, and the cold at the bottom is a different cold, older, with a smell of turned earth in it.

narrator/0de3d82863d2a230.text: She kisses him on the nose, which is all she can reach, and lets go. He stays bent over for a moment, as though he's forgotten how to stand up straight.

narrator/0e180e5415ef1cb0.text: You sleep under the beacon's light, and for the first time since the mists closed behind you, nobody has a dream worth mentioning.

narrator/0e2bdf0755609553.text: Somewhere far off in the hills a single wolf howls, long and low, and stops. Thistle, at the fire, lifts her head.

narrator/0e2dbffe365b4cb8.text: The latch was lifted from the inside, carefully, so it wouldn't squeak, and her good shoes are gone from under the bed. Nobody carried Gertruda off; she went.

narrator/0e43b75ff3791d65.text: Warmth, peat smoke and the smell of vinegar from upstairs. It's a good house, and a careful one, and every room in it is listening for a cough.

narrator/0e4889154123c6c0.text: Every door on this floor stands open, like a host showing guests the way out.

narrator/0e6e2ccc99847988.text: She isn't mad. Every few breaths her hand goes up to the ribbon at her throat and stops short, the way a hand stops at a pane of glass. Her eyes, under the cat, are a person's eyes, and they are frightened.

narrator/0e835e401dbc732f.text: Under the menace there is something almost like grief, worn down to a point. Whatever he wants, he has wanted it every day of his life, and nothing he's done for the Baron has come close to it.

narrator/0e92d43328436785.text: On the third verse the dawn comes. Real dawn, gold first and then white, pouring through the stained glass, laying coloured light over the dust and the pews and the altar, warm on your faces. Things in the walls cry out and go quiet.

narrator/0e974b42f6c43633.text: One word is cut deep into the plinth: MARINA. Below it, smaller, in the same fine and patient hand: Berez took her. I took Berez.

narrator/0ea81b16df25636a.text: You are inside Castle Ravenloft. Its master is a gracious host, which is the worst thing about him.

narrator/0eace5e0a707c77e.text: Letters in an old, beautiful hand, all to the same woman, none of them sent. The desk keeps its other secrets.

narrator/0eae02f8533f3fee.text: The board snaps and a leg plunges through into the dark between floors. Something down there brushes the boot.

narrator/0eae5db869fc461f.text: Your knuckles hit the log hard enough to hurt. She whoops loud enough to wake the camp.

narrator/0ec3b7e94c8ae0db.text: Among the knucklebones and teeth, one relic has been carved: a set of bone pipes. Even unplayed, they make the room colder.

narrator/0ed19cabcd86d7c9.text: The saint's bones are home, and the niche below his sarcophagus stands open, as if it had been waiting. In it lies a mace with a sunburst head, polished by old hands.

narrator/0ede502d2f392df3.text: Wren comes and sits next to you on watch, which he never does; he hates watch. He's quiet for a long while.

narrator/0ee9ea638c219cd3.text: He holds it up to the light as if it were a jewel.

narrator/0f024c90a51b1a19.text: Bundles of cut willow and straw, stacked for the wicker sun. Somebody has tucked a little straw doll into the top bundle, with a yellow ribbon round its neck.

narrator/0f1856422a26e620.text: Among Kiril's trophies hangs a sword he took from someone who hurt him. The blade is notched and still somehow wet.

narrator/0f1b03e74a886bff.text: A bed of wolf furs. The wolves, you notice, died of cold.

narrator/0f39788ab8f5340f.text: The lord of the house in marble, seated, a wolf at his feet. The sculptor made him kinder than he is, and the stone has not forgiven either of them.

narrator/0f4f295f6baaff81.text: A long slope of gold under her belly: coins, cups, crowns, plate. Enough to buy Vallaki twice.

narrator/0f5678abc90fd019.text: Wren has gone very still. Not the stillness of a fighter waiting. The other kind.

narrator/0f655616daa310c9.text: At the foot of the bone cairn, under the last stones, a pair of archer's bracers on a forearm that no longer needs them.

narrator/0f73df3f703dfee6.text: A workshop of coffins on trestles, lids leaning against the walls like doors to nowhere.

narrator/0f8a1c5c88d09ca8.text: Guests of the house, painted one by one. The newest frames are empty, and the brass plates under them are blank.

narrator/0f8ab24c90ce7f1d.text: The great hall is quiet. Not empty, never that, but quiet, the way a held breath is quiet.

narrator/0f9b218c46bdd080.text: You knock on it, and it answers hollow. Inside, where wine should be, something cold is waiting.

narrator/0fa63600ced6fe3f.text: Behind you, a single lamp burns in an upstairs window of the burgomaster's house.

narrator/0faa58ee2a647250.text: Ghost-light moves along the broken wall: men-at-arms in grey, shields up, running toward a gate that isn't there any more.

narrator/0fb09f096f9fd735.text: The gorge is dark and loud and empty. Nothing down there knows your name.

narrator/0fb615e5e622518a.text: He looks like a frightened young man, and nothing in his face says otherwise.

narrator/0fbaddb32a06cd88.text: He doesn't fight. He leaves the fish where they lie and walks ahead of you along the shore to the painted wagons, and when Luvash sees who you have brought, the whole camp goes silent.

narrator/0fd0d6e63fda3d43.text: You dream of two children walking down a hill in the rain, holding an old woman's hands. They don't look back. You decide that's a good sign.

narrator/0fd8ac5dd79771cc.text: A broad shelf of rock under the crags, scattered with bones too big to be sheep's. Up on the crag at its edge sits a nest built of whole pine trunks.

narrator/0fe260f944e6a1ba.text: Green fire with no fuel under it and no smoke over it. It gives heat like any fire. It gives light like nothing natural.

narrator/0fef437bd5f5d09e.text: A lean-to shed for the cart and the firewood. Everything in it is neat, swept and labelled in a careful hand. Whoever lives here is very, very tidy.

narrator/1013a52bfac68007.text: The slates ahead are dark with damp and tilted toward the edge. Go round.

narrator/102f0208ffdf291f.text: The howls come from everywhere and nowhere, the way they do in hills. By the time they stop, you have lost track of all of them.

narrator/104308db364b2847.text: It is quick. It is not justice, and everyone here knows it.

narrator/10455ca0f573dc64.text: It takes two of you on the handles. The cage comes up out of the dark, rattling, and something small with a great many legs leaves it in a hurry.

narrator/1045fa4c9fcc7263.text: Old bones in old blankets. Whatever happened to them, it happened a long time ago.

narrator/1049ef72aef148bc.text: You cover the jetty in four long strides and have him by the collar as his weight goes forward. For a moment you are both leaning out over the black water. Then you aren't.

narrator/104e43fec283860f.text: The lad on the pallet is nineteen or so, broad in the shoulder, his mouth a little open. His right hand is clenched shut, the knuckles white.

narrator/105487f7fdd053e5.text: A stone bridge carries the road over the Ivlis. East lies the village of Barovia, west Tser Pool and Vallaki, north the river track to the falls; south, a steeper road climbs toward the castle on its cliff. A gallows stands beside the signpost, and behind it a field of unmarked mounds.

narrator/106921b08e66e6c2.text: A straw bed under a patched quilt, a painted box tucked beneath it, and a little shelf of pretty stones, buttons and broken spoons.

narrator/10714e920f393524.text: The Baron as a hunter. The Baron as a scholar. The Baron as a general, which he has never been. In every one he is smiling, and in every one the painter has given him very anxious eyes.

narrator/1092939b5752b10f.text: The watch takes them in irons, and a sergeant counts a few coins into your palm for the trouble you have saved the town.

narrator/1097740d2616ab2d.text: The gates stand open now. Neither of the headless knights looks pleased about it.

narrator/1098f901f5fe9b67.text: Goat pens, a hay rick, and a great many goats, all of whom look at you with the same yellow, unimpressed expression as the village.

narrator/10af696093a8cb21.text: Yevgeni said not to stand where his father told you to. The rise behind the shacks is the only good shot at the shore; the shore is the only place a horse-sized wolf can come at you from three sides.

narrator/10bd4ce7ad84e7d5.text: At a bend stands a waist-high stone with a sunburst cut into it, so old the rays are just dents. A candle burns in a niche at its foot, though there's no one in sight.

narrator/10c5cc4c2943832c.text: Master. The mists are thick here and the people thicker. I've started a list of the count's servants and what they're afraid of. It's a long list and a short one at the same time. C.

narrator/10d160503a0ab3cc.text: On the dead tree by the signpost, at a tall man's shoulder height: three neat notches cut with a knife, and in the middle one a crow feather, weathered down to a bare quill.

narrator/10d6b70da347d025.text: One has a journal open on his knee. The last page reads: "Tomorrow the temple. Petra says she can hear it already. She says it knows our names."

narrator/10dcf96d4719b1e9.text: She doesn't have to go far. Goodwife Sarnov is already coming up the lane at a run, in the dark, with her shawl falling off.

narrator/10e29798d3dbde65.text: Coins, teeth, candle stubs, and under them a bundle in oiled cloth that no wolf ever brought here.

narrator/10faadc6fa561fc5.text: He bangs on the gate. A broad, grey-bearded man in a sheepskin steps out through the wicket and looks at the bodies in the road before he looks at you.

narrator/10fb502825d9a7e0.text: He says it gently, and a little too quickly, and doesn't look at you while he does.

narrator/110bb9e3961ab261.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Drizlash, who spins between the walls. Its priests lived in the dark, and were glad of it, and never came out."

narrator/1114cc5051aaa67e.text: Rusted blades slide out of the paneling like teeth.
