narrator/1117825600113cbd.text: Kip is doing his accounts tonight. You can tell because he keeps sighing at a little book and licking his pencil. Eventually he shuts it.

narrator/11196bd58c9aa5f6.text: You are in the Amber Temple, where the things sealed in the walls have not stopped talking.

narrator/112fc9ce7c212971.text: An empty lectern. The book it held is gone; the chain that held the book is still here.

narrator/113f4db6625004b3.text: Oak, iron hoops and a century of wine soaked into both. The founder's cask is just a cask, as far as you can tell.

narrator/11651c9e2912ba78.text: Sarkhaza comes up off the gold all at once, faster than anything that size should, and the chain goes taut across the cavern with a crack like a bell.

narrator/119240a2464cfde5.text: NOTHING LEAVES, says the colossus, and steps down to make sure of it.

narrator/119dfd09aedee4f0.text: She lies down on the bier and smooths her dress and closes her eyes, and does not open them again.

narrator/11b7cf5a2f52a039.text: Heavy curtains, a heavier silence. Under the pillow on the dented side lies a black hood, folded small.

narrator/11b9039b6a07c9d3.text: The wheel shrieks, the sluice opens, and black water floods the firebox. The green fire screams like a kettle and goes out. All through the dungeon, the green lamps go out with it.

narrator/11c6536744901780.text: When you let go, he puts his forehead against your chest and leaves it there, the way a man leans on a wall when he can't stand up any more.

narrator/11f4858eed20e397.text: Scratches on the wall in groups of twelve: a year of new moons to a group. You stop counting at thirty groups, and there are more.

narrator/11f74107c02174eb.text: Three women enjoying an evening out. If they're anything more, the wine hides it.

narrator/1202a3eb5c617dce.text: The edge of the world, as far as you can tell. Cloud fills the valley from wall to wall, and somewhere under it a castle is waiting for you to come down.

narrator/1203ce1806a06185.text: You say the name. For the first time since you met him, Vosk stops smiling. His spectacles fall and break on the floor, and the face behind them is a jackal's, its ears flat.

narrator/120671322a8d4e4a.text: The woman by the wagon looks up from her bolts, sees who is walking behind you, and goes completely still.

narrator/1227282ff7446827.text: A ledger, swollen with damp heat, kept in three hands over forty years. Most of it is the same line, month after month: Fed her. Salted. Checked the wing-pins.

narrator/122e631a159b63da.text: You set to the chain. Behind you, the rug ripples like a pond someone has dropped a stone in.

narrator/123b282df23f600e.text: The church is quiet now, and the candles are lit. Someone has swept the floor, badly, as if with shaking hands.

narrator/1243c86d1dfc0f7a.text: A great hall hung with yellow bunting. The Baron's chair stands on a little platform of its own, so that even indoors he can be looked up to.

narrator/12463bbae7302bc5.text: The altar stands bare on its step, its cloth folded on a chair beside it as if for a funeral.

narrator/1247b6461c3cf937.text: A marble hearth, swept and cold. Above the mantel a longsword hangs on brass pegs, oiled as if someone means to take it down tonight.

narrator/125099313bf98cfb.text: Wren is juggling three stones, then four, then a stone, an apple and somebody's boot. It isn't clear whose boot.

narrator/12556ef3c34d0ba0.text: From the rock, the far shore is a black line and the hills are a blacker one. Up there, very small, a fire is burning in the mouth of a cave.

narrator/125e4f6b8347beba.text: Slush, and stones, and more slush.

narrator/1275433daf9b17d9.text: It takes a while, and a good deal of effort, and a hat. But somewhere around the third verse, Blinsky's mouth twitches, and Piccolo falls off his shoulder with shock.

narrator/12839506592090a3.text: Nine gold, give or take, dripping. When you look back at the water, the sky in it is exactly as grey as the sky above it now.

narrator/12881c0e628f3391.text: Fog rolls across the road, and he is inside it, and then there is only fog. His voice comes from everywhere at once.

narrator/128c5436d190b013.text: It looks like weather. It smells like weather. It is far too punctual to be weather.

narrator/1296aea4db568ac4.text: It doesn't show Escher either, though he is sitting right in front of it, watching you look.

narrator/129e026d5b5792c4.text: Among Ludmilla's books is a grimoire bound in grey leather, its margins full of her notes. The spells in it feel stronger just for being read.

narrator/12a23229611950b3.text: The oven door swings open on a breath of heat that smells of bread and of bone. You rake through the ashes at arm's length, and try not to recognise anything.

narrator/12a9b8fb968509cf.text: Under the notches, scratched into the bark in a hurry, there is a word.

narrator/12cc91e565b10159.text: Copper, soot, a cold hearth. If it means something, it is keeping it between itself and the chimney.

narrator/12d28ce280b09b31.text: She puts the letter away. It's the first time tonight her hands have been still.

narrator/12d9d049d691024f.text: Notes cover the wall behind Exethanter's desk, pinned three and four deep: lists, warnings, recipes, and one that just says DUCK?, underlined twice.

narrator/12e329f0ece60284.text: Nobody cheers. But nobody stops her, either, and a few faces in the crowd look as if they've put down something heavy.

narrator/24321e4d89897510.text: Something cracks deep in the amber, and the doors grind inward on hinges nobody has used in three hundred years. In the alcove beside them, the guardian steps out of the dark.

narrator/2436dbfe7f8dea95.text: Thistle hasn't spoken all day. Tonight she sits by the fire with her knees up and her knife in her hands, cleaning a blade that is already clean.

narrator/244273b5c70fe1ad.text: A teleportation circle chalked with great care: rings within rings, glyphs at the quarters, a destination sigil at the heart. The chalk is warm, and slightly sticky, like a wound.

narrator/2458311d476cc649.text: Master Vosk waits beside the hollow sarcophagus, his books stacked neatly on the floor, his hands folded.

narrator/24706a3e6eed72ea.text: Ratatoille has been unusually quiet for an hour, which means he's planning something. Eventually he presents you, very formally, with a page torn out of his spellbook.

narrator/247fb8ab4f01f067.text: The jar bursts on the flagstones. Among the wax and the shards, a dull grey stone cracks in two, and something like a sigh passes through the whole library.

narrator/248339daf9121bd3.text: Izek vaults off the dais with his strange arm already smoking. The Baron's watch closes ranks behind him.

narrator/2489d2d934a48930.text: A rag doll face down in the mud of the ruts. Its stitched smile has been unpicked and sewn back on upside down.

narrator/2499e9473e8318b9.text: The candles lean all one way, toward the broken windows.

narrator/24afed501d593c15.text: A Belview crouches by the well, picking at the ice on the rope. Her face is a girl's, mostly, with a goat's slotted eyes, and when she speaks it's in your own voice, a beat behind you.

narrator/24b3ae08234ca35e.text: Upstairs, the rocking chair creaks once, and stops, and starts again. Nobody comes down.

narrator/24b5d0010bbbd913.text: He holds out Sir Aldric's sword, hilt first. It seems heavier than it was a moment ago, as if it had made up its mind about something.

narrator/24c2814b0a15be56.text: When it's over, Lupu goes down the little stair alone and lies down on the floor of the swept room with his head on his paws, for a long while. Then he comes back up, and out, and lies down on the mansion's step in the daylight, and goes to sleep.

narrator/24d1d4e581e47c07.text: The seam runs in a neat rectangle. Pressed, the plaster swings inward on a breath of warm air, onto a stair that winds down inside the walls.

narrator/24e814c4a30be04b.text: Behind the dais, an attic window in the Baron's mansion flashes white, once, like lightning that forgot the thunder. Lady Lydia turns toward it and screams her son's name.

narrator/24ec12100be935af.text: Someone has dragged the fallen banner poles upright in the courtyard. From inside the house comes the long, patient sound of whetstones on old steel.

narrator/24f08b0640a45a6e.text: Your heel finds black ice instead of stone, and the stair hurries you down the rest of the way.

narrator/24f6bf476bad9697.text: The lockup is a squat log house with one barred window. Three faces look out of it at you, without much hope.

narrator/251e3833118356b8.text: The floor of this passage slopes toward a channel, and the channel runs one way only.

narrator/25215d4fca48a0df.text: A rutted track climbs north beside the river. You can hear the falls long before you could ever hope to see them.

narrator/253be794875e2e9d.text: He steps back from the dais, and his knights step back with him.

narrator/2542916e7a10b02c.text: The scarecrows come down off their poles in silence. They have no breath to shout with.

narrator/25538e93b2265855.text: Liriel hasn't said much since the abbey. Tonight she sits with her holy symbol in her lap, not praying, just turning it so the firelight runs round the rim.

narrator/2554d2b9b06247c5.text: Inside the sarcophagus, a long oak box with its lid off, lined with old silk, and nothing in it but the dent where something lay for two hundred years.

narrator/255871ccf4020ad7.text: It hops to the next post, and the next, and looks back each time. Following it, you skirt three pools that would have had you up to the neck, and a patch of reeds where something large turns over and goes back to sleep.

narrator/25699062f62885db.text: On the seat lies a letter sealed in black wax.

narrator/25a128ebe83941a1.text: A ledger kept in a neat merchant's hand: dates, names, and beside each one the word given. Vagrants, a tinker, two pilgrims, a girl from Vallaki.

narrator/25abe2861140e8ef.text: The letters are cut so shallow that the stone seems to have healed over them. Of course it has.

narrator/25b15e77321ea4ca.text: His hands are open in his lap, holding the shape of a book that isn't there. He turns a page of nothing. He has it by heart.

narrator/25b21ae4c543be67.text: At first there is nothing in this sarcophagus. Then your eyes adjust, and the nothing has a shape: a figure-shaped absence in the amber, darker than the dark around it.

narrator/25b43675a6c0db49.text: Names are scratched into the parapet, hundreds of them, by people waiting for someone to come along the road. Some of the newest have dates. None of the dates are recent.

narrator/25ca120caefccf99.text: Stab wounds, many of them, the blade turned on the ribs again and again. Someone did this in a fury, and then folded her neatly into a trunk.

narrator/25d3a72f2c2c89fc.text: Under the Abbot's cot, one stone lifts. In the hollow, a dusty blue stone that rises from your hand and settles into a slow orbit round your head.

narrator/25e30e60671605d7.text: Tamsin snaps the locket shut and puts it back inside his shirt, where it sits over his heart like a stone that's been in the sun.

narrator/2605a64f2940cc95.text: A cellar made into a chapel: benches, candles, and a shrine at the far end draped in black, with a silver S worked into the cloth.

narrator/26112c0252ca16b1.text: The lace is soft and cold. When you step back, it lies a little straighter than he left it. You suspect he'll notice.

narrator/261a48d9729d6b4b.text: It's quiet in the wards. You'd forgotten they could be.

narrator/261d8428677e5afa.text: What you offer comes out too smooth, a speech for a stage. Kasimir shakes his head at you, kindly, and finds his own.

narrator/262881d8508cfc12.text: The Martikovs bind them with vine-cord and lock them in an empty vat to wait for a cart to Vallaki. The ravens on the press-house roof watch with interest.

narrator/2643e227298b33b3.text: Behind the tool shed's door, in a pouch of heavy cloth, a handful of dry beans. They are warm, and one of them is trying to sprout.

narrator/264be6f017c42ceb.text: The panels along the walls swing open. They come out in file, grey under crimson, each taking a coat from a chair in passing, and follow their captain out toward the courtyard to wait for the sun.

narrator/264f182cedfe9dfc.text: She looks at the page a long moment. Then, at the very bottom, she writes her own name, in a hand much less steady than the others.

narrator/265177526d5fed7c.text: The yard is trampled mud and flour. The mill door stands ajar, letting out warmth and a long, slow creak from somewhere upstairs, like a chair rocking.

narrator/265915bda513c800.text: The hearth room takes most of the hut; the kitchen and the nursery corner open off it. The floor tilts a little when the hut shifts its weight.

narrator/265942b0827caa07.text: You sleep in the lee of the gatehouse. The castle's one lit window never goes out.

narrator/2673f935b4269eb6.text: Gertruda keeps a hand on somebody's sleeve all the way along the hall, and hums under her breath.

narrator/2686b0b9f816c932.text: He looks at you, then past you, at something just over your shoulder. His lips move: two small names, said like a blessing.

narrator/26935f000daa770d.text: He rises, thanking you in a low voice, and steps out into the passage behind you.

narrator/269b31fef234e27b.text: Deep ruts from a cart that comes this way every week, regular as a heartbeat.

narrator/26a285ad75d4541c.text: She shuffles once, twice, and the cards whisper together like dry leaves. Then she deals five face down in the shape of a cross, and lays her hand flat beside them.

narrator/26aa3d042f140be6.text: Izek steps down off the dais, flexing the arm that isn't his. A few of the watch step down with him.

narrator/26af2a581b8636db.text: A mountain of gilt lead, a fortune to look at and worth nothing, and the long dark shape lying across it.

narrator/26b080ab5702dbb3.text: The air around the cairn claps shut like two great hands.

narrator/26b8c6fcb059abda.text: The stair lets you out into cold so still that your breath hangs where you leave it. Aisles of iron gates run away into the dark, each with a name over it.

narrator/26c59dacc5691cf4.text: A raven lands on the nearest post with a scroll tied to its leg in black ribbon. It waits, head cocked, for someone to take it, then flies off toward the mountains.

narrator/26cf6f547c87940e.text: A hunter's pack, torn open, with the bow still in it. Whoever carried it didn't get the chance to string it.

narrator/26e4bb5b23e7c6c5.text: The green fire is out. The pot hangs over cold ash, and what's in it has set like glue.

narrator/26e8172f8a3290e8.text: A big grey wolfhound lies across the mansion's side step with his chin on his paws, watching the study window. Grey at the muzzle. A good collar, too good for a dog, with a name burned into the leather: LUPU.

narrator/26eda9fc27600692.text: He says "the Abbot" the way people say the name of a river that has drowned someone they knew.

narrator/2710ba6f1d891d41.text: Hedda prays at the end of every day, aloud, the way her chapel taught her. Tonight she stops halfway through and sits back on her heels, and stays there.

narrator/272c0e721a56e69e.text: A round room at the top of the world, windows on every side. In the middle hangs a heart of red crystal as big as a man, and it beats.

narrator/2735b0116331b4dc.text: Hundreds of empty bottles, every one washed and stoppered with a cork against the dust. The Martikovs expected to fill them this autumn. The druids expected otherwise.

narrator/273d5981e4b89901.text: The trail vanishes into pine needles and rock. Whatever carried the child knew this slope better than you do.

narrator/27410b2881786992.text: A narrow bed with a crucifix over it, another under the pillow, and a third, small one, clutched in the shape of a fist in the blanket.

narrator/2743a68b086019d8.text: Every blade on the floor has woken up.

narrator/274ac76ff9ceeb77.text: He looks at Vasilka for a long time. She looks back, politely, waiting to be told what to feel.

narrator/274f7c7348a825cf.text: Under it, two marks: a warden's signature, Exethanter, and a small, neat sketch of a jackal's head.

narrator/275c5b4bd153b79d.text: East, the road runs back to the village. From here you can see the smoke of a few chimneys, and above them, on its cliff, the castle.

narrator/2762b30936ba449a.text: The ring comes out of the rock in a spray of grit, and the other with it. Fen drops to four feet in the straw and stays there a long moment, head down, shaking.

narrator/276894978cc9a957.text: The mirror shows the room behind you, perfectly: the bed, the chair, the dust. It doesn't show you.

narrator/2776aceca62c2302.text: Candlelight, a long table laid for guests, and organ music filling the room to the rafters.

narrator/278b93f555aa53f5.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Norganas, the eraser. It has been forgotten twice already." Below, in a newer, shakier hand: "Warden, if you can't remember why you carved this: you asked it to take the voices. It took you."

narrator/27b97f7a037e8252.text: The black, sodden sun still stands on its pole over an empty dais. Nobody lingers in the square now. Nobody needs to.

narrator/27c2b4e47775ce44.text: The last few steps, and above them an arch. Through it comes a slow red light that brightens and fades, brightens and fades.

narrator/27ee07c04746155a.text: Iron, black and new-looking in a way nothing in Barovia is new-looking, as if it's oiled every month. The count's crest is worked into it, and under the crest, in letters as long as your hand: WHAT I KEEP, I KEEP.

narrator/27f11bd22d31cc9f.text: A small, too-hot room. A boy in the bed, a woman beside it, and on the sill a row of willow-bark cups, all of them full.

narrator/27f159fd9b35c430.text: A woman in a plain habit, a mace in one hand, the other held out palm up as if asking you to come with her. The face was carved with great care. Much later, someone very gently chiselled away the eyes.

narrator/27f50dab3cd25901.text: Stone faces, dozens of them, men and women, all carved with their eyes open. Some have been chiselled away.

narrator/2800c7f498e747fc.text: A plain black coffin with a reading lamp on its lid and a ribbon marking somebody's place in a book.

narrator/280384798f8e9e8c.text: The wolves fan out without a sound. On the wall above, someone has started praying, very fast.

narrator/2805b067409dcb68.text: Between the two cages, in a rocking chair worn smooth, a little old woman in a flour-dusted shawl is shelling something small and white into a bowl in her lap. She doesn't get up. The chair keeps rocking.

narrator/280bd11ec7892862.text: Silver light goes up out of the cradle and over the parapet, over the treetops and the whole dark valley, all the way to the castle on its rock.

narrator/2810e79331816239.text: A cairn of black stones with a goat's skull on top, its horns painted red. A herdsman's warning, very old: don't bring the flock up here.

narrator/28350a7b4eea627d.text: The door gives. Inside, a young woman crouches on the bed with her knees drawn up and looks at you with enormous, unblinking eyes. Then she hisses.

narrator/283bc89fd7bdc944.text: In Dobre's satchel there are three copies of tonight's list, not one. Each is marked in the corner in his hand: a crown for the Baron's clerk, a W, and a little black horse.

narrator/284154353a2f6d35.text: In a crack of the lych-gate post, a stoppered vial of holy water, the wax on its stopper stamped with the morninglord's sun. Someone left it here for whoever needs it most.

narrator/284a75ae03743f02.text: Two dark shapes scorched into the boards beside the circle, each about the length of a person lying down. Someone has tried to scrub them out, and failed.

narrator/28580f28d9d9e112.text: Glass bursts outward and the soft brick crumbles with it, leaving a ragged gap onto grey daylight and the weeds of the lot. Behind you, every door in the house slams at once, like applause.

narrator/28746c3ade9f62b1.text: You sleep under the Krezkovs' roof. Nobody sings in the night. Somebody small snores like a bear instead, and the house sleeps round it.

narrator/287831e8755fe6e5.text: Past the gate the road goes on, steep and narrow, into cloud so thick you can hear it. Somewhere up there, something golden is catching a light that isn't the sun's.

narrator/289f31af11610ad8.text: From somewhere inside one of you, a small voice says: that's ours, but we're not in there. We're upstairs, in the toy chest.

narrator/28bf56f831f04a5d.text: The collar falls off onto the gold. Sarkhaza rises, all of her, and the cavern is too small for her, and she doesn't care.

narrator/28c98862070d4af6.text: Sacks of flour, stacked neatly, each stamped with a little drawing of a smiling old woman. Some are flour. Some are labelled SPECIAL, and you leave those alone.

narrator/28cf356ead0ff741.text: Goodwife Sarnov looks up at you. The bowl tips off her lap, and she doesn't pick it up.

narrator/28da292c32a44d1c.text: On the rise behind the shacks, a bow creaks. Pointed at the hill, not at you.

narrator/28dbbc1bf9b665d0.text: Warmth, at last: a real fire, a long bar, and a taproom that smells of stew and woodsmoke. Above the door, a carved raven watches everyone who comes in, and seems to approve of you.

narrator/28ff31180308e6ac.text: For the first time since you met her, Baba Lysaga looks her age, which is very great.

narrator/2902c6e975e2dc11.text: What you took for knobs of rock on the cliff above unfold their wings and drop.

narrator/2909519259b2e66e.text: An iron-bound sea chest with three locks, scratched all over as if something has tried to open it from outside, more than once, with claws.

narrator/291b3b17037c2bac.text: Grey shapes slip between the trunks on both sides of the road, keeping pace.

narrator/2922a5f36408cc54.text: Thistle is between you and him before the first word, low and fast, the way she goes between a hound and a snare.

narrator/292a3be044e90c82.text: Two of you dream of a locked door and a long wait, and wake with wet faces.

narrator/292c6efce5d3bef6.text: Wind, and nothing between you and the valley but a parapet. Slate roofs fall away on every side, and beyond them a long, long drop.

narrator/29316b8a46dc7e31.text: North, the mountains, white at the top. Somewhere out there a ruined house on a ridge.

narrator/295ae35d11b35316.text: In the darkest corner of the kitchen something very large sits under a blanket of sewn-together habits. The blanket moves. It comes off.

narrator/2982caf9c96536f4.text: Something in the milky amber is blurred, as though the sculptor kept rubbing it out and starting again. The longer you look, the less you could say what shape it is.

narrator/2990e720cfed9bfe.text: A little perch with a little cushion and a little cup of nuts. Piccolo the monkey sits on it and watches you shell one, with the expression of a moneylender.

narrator/2994c3f915872505.text: The satchel's lining was slit and sewn shut again. Inside: a pair of crystal lenses in a wire frame, a scholar's best tool and best-kept secret.

narrator/29bcf8c96c4f54b6.text: Castle Ravenloft stands on its pillar of rock above the valley, its towers lost in cloud. One window high up is lit, as it always is.

narrator/29d17de1824e65f0.text: He turns to his men and says something you don't catch. They stand easier. One of them, very quietly, sits down for the first time in a very long time.

narrator/29d55a214ed29491.text: She opens her mouth to answer, and the answer is in her face before she can stop it: pride, and something like devotion. The crowd sees it. A woman spits at her feet. Then another.

narrator/29e61160f31fddc3.text: The wire comes out, but not cleanly; there's blood on the grey feathers, and Mother hisses like a cat through her teeth, and says nothing. When the last stitch is out the wings open by themselves, slowly, and she winces every time they move.

narrator/29efe77d89f6fcfb.text: The path switchbacks up the bare slope between cairns of skulls the size of turnips. Every cairn faces the crown, the way a congregation faces an altar.

narrator/2a03afb9da5d9b49.text: The lid grinds aside on a general laid out in rusted armour, his teeth bared even now.

narrator/2a051cf2d51d2ddc.text: The summit is bare rock and wind. A cairn of flat stones stands at the very top, and the frost around it lies in a perfect ring.

narrator/2a0a0d1e9593348d.text: Later, when the others are asleep, Kip sits up by the fire with his little knife and the stone of the bruised apricot, carving. In the morning there's a charm on a string, tied to the pack of whoever slept nearest.

narrator/2a3c432649ed9cad.text: A cairn of flat grey stones, waist-high, stacked with a care nobody spends on a trail marker. The stones are warm. Snow melts on them as it lands.

narrator/2a468a2e88c7180d.text: Across the courtyard in the wards, the stitched bride he never finished lies under her linen. She will not wake now. There's nobody left who knows how.

narrator/2a539c4b1f3ca006.text: Godrick has the old sword across his knees and is polishing a part of it that is already very clean. Beside him on the log, also being polished, is a soup ladle.

narrator/2a61f0904e464f1f.text: For one moment Kiril and Emil look at each other across the cave, and agree on something for the first time in a month.

narrator/2a628f55300b5872.text: The attic hall is quiet now: no humming, just the roof and the wind.

narrator/2a66d797e50c8ac5.text: The flagstone tips, and the dark under it is ten feet deep, bristling with spikes and floored with older bones.

narrator/2a6d54085c700c80.text: As Ezmerelda follows you in, blue fire crawls over the frame and snaps at her. She swears in three languages, shoulders through it with her hair standing on end, and doesn't look back.

narrator/2a9c148b313eb4d2.text: You lay a hand on the coffin lid and speak the old words. Ireena stands very straight and doesn't cry, though it costs her something.

narrator/2aa3da15e3dde67d.text: He gets up gladly. You haven't gone a dozen steps when the fog behind you opens like a mouth, and out of it, low and quick and silent, come the count's wolves.

narrator/2aa5262512ea0e37.text: You walk them down to the road and as far as the first milestone, where Mirela takes over, counting heads every twenty paces like a sergeant on a march.

narrator/2ab1829fd8643fac.text: At the bottom, under a foot of black water, the silt gives up a bundle wrapped in what was once a veil. Bones, small and light, and a necklace of little silver coins.

narrator/2ab39d0e63e5cef8.text: A yellow room with a curtained bed, a dressing table and a wardrobe of gowns. Everything in it is very pretty and none of it is hers.

narrator/2ac1e4bba0cbcfcc.text: Coins, ribbons, buttons and a child's tooth. Every token here was somebody's whole heart, and none of them is yours.

narrator/2ad4f1a9c5dd3dea.text: The water goes into the earth with a hiss like a cat, a curl of steam and a smell of struck matches. The earth will remember.

narrator/2ad6c4d4e9471ff6.text: A small pipe organ with half its pipes missing. The keys that are left are worn down to the wood in the middle, where someone has played the same few notes for years.

narrator/2aeea9beff54c511.text: The floor under the bench by the door is warmer than the rest, and it gives, very slightly, like a tongue.

narrator/2aef19385834b680.text: The glyphs light as you cross them, and for a moment every voice in the amber is inside your head at once.

narrator/2af3a224fe6c77e7.text: The stone under the front pew rocks when you press it. Beneath it, a small silver sunburst on a chain, hidden from someone a long time ago.

narrator/2af6c5252d4fbcce.text: A small portrait of a girl with red hair in a plain dress, a candle in her hand, painted by someone who loved her and couldn't paint. Someone else, much better, has painted over the eyes.

narrator/2b04502997903634.text: The magic is too old and too tangled to read. All you can tell is that it matters very much to someone.

narrator/2b1a928b57904308.text: The old woman straightens slowly from the effigy, wiping earth off her hands. Her face is kind. It's the kindest face you've seen in Barovia, and it doesn't change in the least when she looks at your weapons.

narrator/2b1ecb1c80843754.text: She says it the way a music box plays its tune: exactly the same, every time it's wound.

narrator/2b2b0713be03c8be.text: Somebody wakes in the night certain that a little old woman was sitting at the foot of their bedroll, counting on her fingers. There's flour on the blanket.

narrator/2b3c03669a73be74.text: You tell him what you know. He listens with his head on one side and his bells quite still. Then he writes, small:

narrator/2b451f7d03cceeba.text: You sleep while dead knights stand guard at your door. It is very safe. It is not very restful.

narrator/2b4683528fe1c487.text: Then it lifts its head, and the face is half an old man's: white stubble, a broken nose, and two fingers missing from the left hand.

narrator/2b46a6dc98800f0b.text: Ismark drags in a breath like a man pulled out of a river. Before he can get up off his knees, all around the churchyard the earth begins to split.

narrator/2b5b96cfaddd435f.text: A man in a clean grey habit kneels in the straw with his hands folded. A sun is scratched into the wall above him. Beside him sits a tray of bread nobody has touched.

narrator/2b61a8dcc25215dd.text: On a ridge above the trail, a big wolf stands outlined against the sky, watching you. When it sees you looking, it turns and lopes away north, unhurried, toward the rock face above the lake.

narrator/2b722c85d2719ef2.text: He doesn't. Not really. He's asking you to bring something back so there's something to bury, and he hates himself for it.

narrator/2b8006d4a69c7e7b.text: He starts to answer, and stops. You watch the argument go into him like a splinter, and watch him try to close round it, and fail.

narrator/2b859647b3ba3b28.text: Halfway up the first stretch a stone goes out from under a boot and bounces all the way down, loudly, the way stones do when it matters. Up on the crown the humming stops for one breath, and then goes on.

narrator/2b8acb7477c33c02.text: Bones on bones, stacked with care. The druids built this for someone. Not you.

narrator/2b9df065eacd338f.text: Somewhere below, a black carriage is being made ready. The castle opens its doors from the inside.

narrator/2b9e60fbb403f494.text: You read it to him from the bottom up: his own name, a sister who laughed like a goose, the light, the oath.

narrator/2baca96003c3edf4.text: The bundles weigh almost nothing. Whoever carries them will feel them all the way down.

narrator/2be0e741a33d9c1b.text: The end of the road. Ireena stops and looks at the wall for a long moment, the way you'd look at the far shore after a long swim.

narrator/2beda762f7a04598.text: He turns three cartwheels down the landing, bells going like a sleigh, and stops in front of you at attention.

narrator/2bf3e65298e1875a.text: Wine casks branded with a wizard's hat and a bunch of grapes. Most ring hollow when you knock; one sloshes, sadly, about a quarter full.

narrator/2bf5b2255fe82c1b.text: A black stump of a mill on a black crag. The ravens have the hill to themselves now, and they seem to like it that way.

narrator/2bf65bdfde95ba5b.text: A half-elf in a scarlet coat and a hat with a whole pheasant's worth of feathers is standing on a chair, addressing a taproom that isn't listening.

narrator/2bfc75312616cf39.text: The ceiling is alive. Hundreds of bats hang up there in their sleep, and the floor is thick with what they leave behind.

narrator/2c0c50daab632a3f.text: The step crumbles under your boot and you go over the edge, onto the turn of the stair below.

narrator/2c1800fd175414a3.text: A dead knight stands where the gate used to be, facing down the drive toward the castle, as still as the trees.

narrator/2c1cf352ff109e0f.text: Ruxandra presses her forehead to the effigy and shouts one word into the earth. The chest splits like a log in frost, and out of it, unfolding, comes a tree that walks.

narrator/2c22b668a2883268.text: Somebody gets a cloak round him. He keeps looking past you, up the valley, toward the castle on its rock.

narrator/2c24cb09cf4e4bee.text: For a moment Thistle doesn't answer, and her nostrils flare, and you can see her hearing it: the whole wide dark of the hills, and no one ever telling her to sit still again.

narrator/2c2f2078f6d431ee.text: Grey coats hang over the chairs all down the long table, forty of them, a little bird stitched on every shoulder. Dust on all of them, and not one moth. Someone has been keeping them.

narrator/2c46875bbdeb4457.text: An ivory hairbrush with silver bristles, a few long hairs still caught in it. Twenty-five gold, to someone who doesn't ask.

narrator/2c591270037046f8.text: Things that were people once come scuttling from behind the sarcophagi, each with one great eye where a face should be. The wardens' dead drift up through the floor behind them.

narrator/2c5c227a5f08ea0b.text: Warmth, peat smoke and somebody small running along the upper floor in boots, being told off for it, and running anyway.

narrator/2c882a7f830b5a97.text: Pack law has rules, and Kiril keeps them to the letter. A ring of wolves; two men stripping off their shirts; then two wolves, one grey and slow from a month in silver, one black and fresh from the hunt.

narrator/2c97c30f36d9c70a.text: It's her own voice, from twenty years ago, saying her son's name to him, and then it's a small boy's. Anna doesn't scream. She sits down on the step as if her legs have been taken away, and holds out both arms.

narrator/2cb8073128ffe667.text: The square goes quiet. Somewhere at the back of the crowd, very hesitantly, somebody claps.

narrator/2cbedc91c519d7f7.text: The alcove beside the doors was not empty. Something tall and golden steps out of it, and the hall's light shifts as it moves.

narrator/2cd4598006602734.text: Tiny bones, picked clean: mice, sparrows, a bat. The ravens are keeping the castle tidy in their own way.

narrator/2cd9b3625a4dd052.text: When you climb out, Vosk is closing his book with a soft, satisfied clap.

narrator/2ce919a2aa61e31c.text: That evening the festival bunting comes down all over Vallaki, and nothing goes up in its place. The town is quieter than it has been in years. It is not the same thing as peace.

narrator/2d1e0da22ab2cbed.text: You wake in the small hours and know at once you are not alone. Just past the last of the light, a tall man stands watching the others sleep.

narrator/2d34f1f8cd1b8f61.text: The wind hits you the moment your head clears the hatch. The whole valley is laid out below, grey and green and endless.

narrator/2d50d9e6f23514e3.text: He looks at your faces and does the sum. He drops the sack in the shallows and runs, splashing, into the reeds.

narrator/2d580fed430ab4ef.text: A hunter's pack, torn open. The quiver is stitched with the same running-deer mark as Grigor's sons wore on their sleeves. You've found his brother, or what the wolves left.

narrator/2d5cdfa3eb172834.text: He looks at the net in his hands, and his hands keep working. Whatever he is mourning, he has worn it smooth.

narrator/2d5fc3502342cfb5.text: Powder, combs and a mirror that shows you looking tired. Nothing else worth the trouble.

narrator/2d859df2a0a9e96f.text: It hops out of reach, plainly offended, and flies off west.

narrator/2d862c708a2837fb.text: Candle stubs crowd the statue's feet, dozens of them, burnt down to puddles. Someone keeps lighting new ones. The wax has run into the shapes of hands.

narrator/2dab710622ec3d1f.text: He holds your gaze with the steadiness of a man who has rehearsed this every night. It may even be true; you can't tell.

narrator/2dc162a0afea1bd6.text: You sleep in the pews. Twice in the night someone walks the length of the aisle, and both times there is no one there.

narrator/2dc7c38554305ec0.text: The nursery is warmer than the rest of the floor. The candle by the crib burns straight and steady.

narrator/2dcaf9eee553831d.text: The drive runs between dead trees planted in two straight rows, as straight as the day someone set them out to make an approach worth approaching.

narrator/2dcd0129e89fd82e.text: The boards are nailed three deep, and the outermost layer is splintered by claws. Light comes through the gaps in thin grey blades.

narrator/2df2ccaf33203108.text: A landing wide enough for a carriage, and two suits of black armour with wolf-headed helms standing guard over nothing.

narrator/2e1458c930b7538f.text: A grave half dug, neatly squared. The spoil heap beside it is still damp, and the spade has been left standing in it like a flag.

narrator/2e14634f2a498bbc.text: The jaw moves, stiffly, and a voice comes out of the dark between the bones: young, furious and very tired.

narrator/2e178b01a33cd9b9.text: The tall black door swings open without a sound, the way a good servant opens a door for a guest.

narrator/2e25a81c01209d19.text: Below, the cloud glows faintly in one place, the way a sheet glows over a candle. You know what that light is.

narrator/2e2ccb85cf3052df.text: The road climbs from the south along the cliff, crosses the gorge on a narrow bridge to the roc's shelf, then turns north up to the tower. The road goes on through the tower's gate passage and up into cloud.

narrator/2e2f4d4fd62e9f9f.text: A square vault, green fire in iron braziers, and on a stepped dais in the middle a plain wooden coffin on trestles. It is the humblest thing in the whole castle.

narrator/2e34d614f6bef1e9.text: A cart on its side, one wheel gone. Its owner left in a hurry, and not on the cart.

narrator/2e4a445e1ac3f0b4.text: Brick is climbing the tall window from the sill up, row by row. There is still a gap at the top, though not for long.

narrator/2e55bb1f8551687c.text: A stone bench facing the view, its seat worn hollow by someone who sat here a great deal.

narrator/2e7a8fa4a935cad9.text: A soldier's cot, tightly made. Under the pillow, a child's hair ribbon, faded to no colour at all.

narrator/2e86e2cae49e3e81.text: The lock is excellent, and it was made to keep out people with less time than you.

narrator/2e959f294f438217.text: Kip is carving tonight: an apricot-pit charm, turning it under his thumb as the little knife goes round. There's a row of them on the log beside him, each face slightly different.

narrator/2eade02578965635.text: An oil lamp on the side table, wick trimmed, reservoir full. You check again later, and it is still full.

narrator/2edfe2a8ecf48cc3.text: An entry hall of cold marble. Ahead, through an archway, the dark opens out into something much bigger.

narrator/2f10f8abba0448f5.text: A coil of good rope on a peg, labelled ROPE. Whoever lives here labels everything, and takes nothing for granted.

narrator/2f356f29a59b64e8.text: Cyrus snatches up a cleaver in one hand and a ladle in the other, weeping.

narrator/2f5f347782780eb1.text: The splinter is still going in. Whatever drew it there has to be dealt with before it can come out.

narrator/2f6a15cff8528825.text: A huge jaw fills the amber, lined with row on row of teeth: a man's, a horse's, a child's milk teeth, a wolf's fang. No two come from the same mouth.

narrator/2f9d0f56afd228c9.text: Kip is sitting by the fire with his contract unrolled across his knees, not reading it. He has been holding the same corner for an hour.

narrator/2f9e971337f29054.text: Cottages huddle in the lee of the wall here, shutters closed, a ladder against every eave so the roofs can be cleared of snow before they come down. One ladder has a boy's coat hung on it, not taken in.

narrator/2f9ee3bd08c25538.text: His hand closes on the nearest throat, and two more shapes drop from the vault above the passage.

narrator/2f9f789fea206065.text: A raven lands on the road ahead, drops something at your feet and waits. It's a vine leaf, fresh and green, the first leaf you've seen in this valley that isn't half dead.

narrator/2f9f9385e3a2c1f0.text: A notice board, every notice on it the same notice: curfew, by order of the burgomaster. The newest copy is three weeks old, and someone has added a line underneath.

narrator/2fac574dab9e58af.text: Plates set for a meal four centuries cold. A child's wooden cup sits among them, with a name burned into it that you can almost read.

narrator/2fb28011a7ac81bd.text: Tamsin opens the silver locket and holds it out. The tiny painted woman inside has Ireena's face: the same eyes, the same red hair, in a gown a few centuries out of fashion.

narrator/2fb7b37344ae91ee.text: Straw, cobwebs and the creak of the sails. Nothing up there but the dark.

narrator/2fbd3993d23b9697.text: The cells on this side are colder, as if something in them takes the warmth.

narrator/2fc1682807652f5a.text: Chain armor on a stand, a visored helm shaped like a wolf's head, a spear grounded at its side. It doesn't move. You check twice.

narrator/2fcf776335537108.text: Tamsin takes out the locket and holds it a moment, the way he held it over the pool. Then he puts it in the long white hand.

narrator/2fd3a10bfe85a25f.text: A pine that grew up here once when the snow lay. It's been cooked from the roots up, standing, its needles still on it and all of them brown.

narrator/2ffb6d942a2f91dc.text: Down among the bones, where the rain hasn't reached, your hand closes on a chain, and on the chain a holy symbol, and on the symbol a name scratched small: Kesten.

narrator/2ffcc6de24a5af71.text: A harpsichord with its lid raised and a page of music on the rack.

narrator/30062f5256cbf0da.text: The foot of the lane, where the cart road from the lake turns off. A sign on a post says WIZARD OF WINES, and somebody has scratched NO under it with a knife.

narrator/3006918b74950a0d.text: Every other window in the house is brick now, and this one is closing, wet brick climbing the glass row by row. At the top there is a gap the width of a person, for now.

narrator/3010beb98ad864d6.text: A worktable scored by a thousand cleavers. One of the knives laid out on it is very small and very sharp, for fine work.

narrator/3017755e1bcae2e9.text: The ruts are deep and the cart that made them was heavy going down the hill and heavier coming back. Small footprints run beside them, once, going up.

narrator/301cc9975477c8f2.text: The founder's cask is older than the house: black oak, bound in iron gone brown, so big a man could stand up inside it. The druids have chopped at every cask in the cellar except this one, because it was too much trouble.

narrator/3039fc2197c4472d.text: You catch it as he glances past you at the mountains: the look of a man at a window that will not open. Then it's gone.

narrator/304babc5e07b81c6.text: A basin, a cloth, and a row of needles laid out in order of size. The thread on the smallest one is so fine you can only see it when it catches the candle.

narrator/3070ba56b77453da.text: A thin young man with a long pole and a pocket of tapers, very tired, very polite. Whatever he isn't saying, he's had a year to practise not saying it.

narrator/30765ba26b35cc8f.text: Izek lies at the foot of the dais where he fell, his strange arm cooling in the drizzle.

narrator/3090459be5779ca0.text: You have a moment to choose your ground before it reaches you. Use it.

narrator/30b1ddf2679a8352.text: His hand has stopped halfway to his cup. Slowly, he puts the cup down.

narrator/30bd93fa38752521.text: A weathered marker stone with a carving of a woman in a long dress, falling. Someone has chipped away the face.

narrator/30dcf4ad3ce575ea.text: He holds one up. It's a very small face with its mouth turned down and its eyebrows up, the way a person looks when they've been told bad news kindly.

narrator/30e8b23a57a018dc.text: They get up one after another and go to stand behind Godfrey, until the commander sits alone at the head of an empty table.

narrator/30f3868e891125db.text: The chain runs taut across the cavern to a collar of black iron at the base of a long red neck. The neck strains against it, and the head at the end of it, the size of a cart, is turned toward you.

narrator/30f53cb9bf007be2.text: Paper, ink and a pen chewed at the end. Whatever else the scholar carried, he took it with him.

narrator/31024cb6f1bde3ad.text: No wounds, no breaks: just bones too light for their size, curled the way children curl when they fall asleep hungry and cold. Nobody killed them; somebody forgot them.

narrator/3104bc715e8698bc.text: Lupu is asleep on the mansion step in the middle of the day, like an ordinary dog, with one ear turned toward the house. He thumps his tail twice when he hears you.

narrator/3104fdeadc6ba4fe.text: He sits very still. The snow stops. Something comes back into his face, one piece at a time, like furniture being carried into an empty house: a hard mouth, a scholar's frown, an old and specific anger.

narrator/310ad23245086483.text: The stable yard, where a carnival wagon painted red and gold takes up most of the space. Every horse in the stable stands at the far end of its stall, away from it.

narrator/313f0a270ba67978.text: He breaks against a will that won't let him in and falls back, sobbing, into his sister's arms.

narrator/314ba7b3405807d4.text: Behind the milestone, a hollow packed with moss. In it lies a stubby wand of grey wood wound with something like spider silk.

narrator/31522a81843ba33a.text: Bones, teeth and the dust of both. If any of these relics is more than it seems, it isn't telling you.

narrator/31582d516639d3fc.text: Ezmerelda doesn't say anything. She just looks at him, with her hair still standing up from his ward, until he looks away first.

narrator/3166c126d29dae0a.text: The fire dies, and every face in the hall turns toward you. Two portraits lean out of their frames; helmed armour marches in from the dark.

narrator/3171f31a03b460ab.text: Under the tarpaulin, iron bars, and behind them a striped flank rising and falling. A golden eye opens, regards you, and decides not to bother yet.

narrator/317407965855233d.text: The weeping is quieter than it was. Mary is mending something by the stove, and keeps glancing at the door.

narrator/3175a9deb941734b.text: You walk out of the village of Barovia with the burgomaster's daughter between you. Behind you, a shutter opens a crack, and closes again.

narrator/319488a8c2e3d9b5.text: The red amber flares. Kasimir staggers, and when he straightens, his white hair has gone the grey of old ash and there are lines at his eyes that weren't there a breath ago.

narrator/319c38792077ad6b.text: He doesn't stop you. He doesn't need to. As you go, he calls after you, gently, the way you'd call after children leaving a party early.

narrator/319f22cec6a51cbf.text: Old graves lean in the long grass, and the church watches them from its rise like a tired shepherd. The lych-gate creaks shut behind you on its own.

narrator/31acdcbe5ba341ad.text: The Huntsman's coat lies in the road with nothing in it. His saddlebag holds four hundred years of quarry's purses, and a plain iron ring he called the pack with.

narrator/31b93412b5e25e38.text: For a moment he leans toward the amber. You see exactly how much he wants it.

narrator/31bdaeb459d766d9.text: Lazar has an answer, and it's better than yours. Nobody laughs. Nobody leaves, either, which in Krezk counts as manners.

narrator/31cb71233ca93311.text: The beacon burns silver in its cradle, without heat and without smoke. From up here its light lies on the treetops all the way to the castle.

narrator/31cf06c3a648a937.text: Kip is sitting a little way from the fire with his hat off. Without it his horns look very large and very red in the firelight, and he keeps touching one of them, the way some people touch a scar.

narrator/31d1bfcce4ca4774.text: The hut lies on its side in the mud below the stump, its root legs snapped like kindling. Someone did this with his hands.

narrator/31f388e6ded2ecd1.text: The whole crown lies before you: druids swaying in a ring round the black tree, an old woman with both hands pressed to the effigy's chest, and nobody, nobody at all, looking your way.

narrator/31fe9a6eb7c2347c.text: Bunks, a table, a stove nobody has needed to light in forty years. Wet hoods hang on pegs. The keepers lived here between new moons, and it smells like it.

narrator/3211a73cb4809e1a.text: While he talks, his eyes go to the door and the windows every few seconds, the way a soldier checks his flanks. His hands are old, much older than his face, and seamed with burn scars. Those are a hunter's hands, and he's been hunting a long time.

narrator/3213c6cda4eb2a50.text: Every mound in the field has been opened from the inside. The grass lies flat around them, as if something very heavy got up and walked.

narrator/322acc5b17b85551.text: There's something here, a pattern in the woods and the wolves and the red hair, but it slips away before you can hold it.

narrator/32738dab226f279e.text: You stand at the bottom of the temple, beside the hollow where the devil's bargain was struck. For the first time since the stair, none of the voices in the amber are talking. They're listening.

narrator/327b8b4a481721b6.text: The ground floor waits exactly as you left it, every chair squared to its table. Houses are not supposed to be this patient.

narrator/328e319e3e53c837.text: The rider wheels his horse in the gateway and comes back in, drawing a sabre. Dobre's lads come running up the street from the guardhouse.

narrator/32b1fb6ac53304e6.text: The locket is warm inside Tamsin's shirt. It has been warm since the castle gate.

narrator/32cb87cbcea6a3bc.text: Nobody says the number aloud anymore. Nobody needs to.

narrator/32cdf7fc0d49c6b5.text: West, the lake like a dropped mirror, and the walls of a town beside it.

narrator/32e26a7a7f98392d.text: Crates, stacked to the beams, and the smell of cold earth. The crates are too heavy to be empty, and too quiet to be anything you want.

narrator/32eef24ee63707a0.text: Kasimir stops at the top of the stair and looks up at the doors for a long time. His breath smokes. He doesn't seem to notice the cold at all.

narrator/32f04bf7e28ef96d.text: The east wing smells of straw, wet fur and boiled bones. Somewhere further in, something is calling for its mother in a voice it learned from someone else.

narrator/32f076d8befbe3f7.text: A small room, too warm, smelling of vinegar and willow bark. A woman sits by the bed holding a boy's hand in both of hers. She is singing under her breath, and she doesn't stop when you come in, only looks up.

narrator/32f7deb222b00979.text: He meets your eye, shrugs, and goes back to the cask he's scraping. Whatever else there is, he has kept it a year, and he's had the practice.

narrator/32fd0f039cb88ae7.text: A bowl of yellow bone comes skimming over the reeds, low and fast, with a tiny furious woman standing in it. Behind her the whole marsh rises in a cloud of wings.

narrator/331f455549c891a3.text: Wren is sitting on the same boulder as always, not doing a handstand. He looks up as you come over.

narrator/3328450382cdb853.text: Under the shrine of Mother Night, an offering nobody came back for: a silver sickle shaped like the new moon.

narrator/33334efaf91b3bd6.text: The Seventh Row is young vines on new stakes, and a long scar of turned earth where something was dug out by the roots. Somebody has planted rosemary at the end of it.

narrator/3343480972c5d8bd.text: The ravens in the dead oak bob their heads at you as you pass, all together, like a choir taking a bow.

narrator/334f1119d914ff4f.text: She does not hear it. Not on the stair, not in the hall, not ever again.

narrator/33607d59030081e9.text: Pidlwick puts one hand on the banister, and takes it off again. Then he writes on his slate and holds it up so only you can see.

narrator/336c87d1ce6efccd.text: Old ruts, full of rainwater. Frogs have moved in.

narrator/3372cb54e3eacc47.text: In her chair, Morgantha rocks, and listens, and smiles.

narrator/3374a79faf044fa3.text: Nobody answers, and the humming stops. Then, very quietly, someone giggles.

narrator/337e903a96315fc6.text: He doesn't wait for dusk. He says the dark up here is close enough. The Belviews carry her in on a bier, a dozen of them in their best rags, humming something with no words in it.

narrator/3380717979c5fe57.text: She held it very well. She holds my doors still. S.

narrator/3389422f2765ff98.text: He sweats and stammers and fusses with a coffin lid. He's frightened of something. He might be frightened of you.

narrator/33933d77e38a6bc5.text: Just glass now, cloudy and ordinary. The chains overhead swing a little in the wind, holding nothing.

narrator/33953dbdd1f8ae59.text: The empty hut's hearthstone lifts away. Under it, a small wooden box with a fisherman's knot carved on the lid. Say the right word and it will be a boat.

narrator/33b106ebeba4b48e.text: After a long, judging moment it takes the crust, and then leads you round the worst of the pools before it flies off east, toward the drowned village.

narrator/33b4c5ac9336d9b0.text: Luvash sits on the step of his wagon with an empty bottle and doesn't look up when you come.

narrator/33c08e19d8d0a869.text: The bridge is two strides wide with a parapet to the knee, and the gorge under it goes down into cloud. The wind pushes at you, like a hand testing a door.

narrator/33c593559df69c23.text: Cards, glasses and dust. If Gustav cheated at cards, he hid it better than this.

narrator/33f6e0e0c6155984.text: The silver raven flares in your fist, and the tomb fills with morning, real morning, the first this room has ever held.

narrator/34293020968bf6e9.text: The refectory. Nobody has cleared the table, and nobody ever will.

narrator/342f9c312f4cbd2b.text: You give Sir Godfrey's name. The warden is silent so long you think he hasn't heard.

narrator/343336bdbc07fff8.text: A black carriage waits on the road ahead, drawn by two black horses with embers for eyes. It has no driver. Its door stands open.

narrator/343f398c63608c3a.text: He says it as if tasting it.

narrator/3445822096735095.text: Coins and little silver things left in a niche in the wall, the offerings of somebody who had no one to give them to.

narrator/34661871e7fdef69.text: The woods fill with eyes. The howling comes from everywhere at once, which is the point of it.

narrator/3469456828595e04.text: The left shin is pierced clean through, an old wound that never knitted. The fingertips are worn to the knuckle, as if he spent a long time scratching at something hard.

narrator/34c62c5d7ccf9996.text: At the one desk not furred with frost sits a dusk elf woman, as translucent as breath on glass, her white hair floating as if she were under water. Her face is beautiful and ruined, scored with the marks of stones.

narrator/34d6d3cfaf2c76f4.text: The candles stand up straight again, one by one, as if they'd been hiding.

narrator/34da2e8a67737533.text: She skips away up the lit side of the street toward her father's, humming. You let her go.

narrator/34da8626e86cc650.text: The knights still sit at the long table, but their heads are bowed, and the hall feels like a church after the last hymn.

narrator/34dfb0b72a120828.text: Scree, roots and old fire-scars. If the druids hid anything up here, they hid it from you too.

narrator/34e1b626ca0f554f.text: Among the names scratched on the cairn's stones hangs a necklace of glass beads, each one with a bubble of air trapped inside.

narrator/34ec08e7ef94686e.text: Nests, feathers and droppings. A hundred ravens watch you look, and none of them helps.

narrator/350931be5a87bcec.text: She takes out her knife and cuts a small mark into the stock of her sword, beside the hilt, where she'll see it every time she draws. One.

narrator/3509abe3665a8c99.text: You sleep in shifts in a house full of the dead. Every watch hears armour in the corridors and every watch hears it stop outside the door, politely, and move on.

narrator/350d58187424ad8d.text: The island is bare rock, moss and a few stunted thorns, and the tower takes up most of it. Close to, the stone hums very faintly, like a bell long after it has been struck.

narrator/35282f5c47004d97.text: The axe goes in and the log bleeds. The sap is red and slow, and inside, the rings of the grain run the wrong way round, tightening toward the heart instead of growing out of it.

narrator/352c9add0b19c119.text: Six thin pillars of white stone hold up a round roof over a statue whose face has been worn away by hands. The floor round its feet is scattered with candle stubs and wax.

narrator/354460b5d680bde5.text: In the still water, beside her reflection, there is a second face: a young man with kind eyes and a sunburst at his throat. You look up. Nobody kneels beside her.

narrator/3550971298b1c429.text: Adrian walks into the yard ahead of you and stops in front of his father. Neither of them says a word. Then Davian takes his son by the shoulder, once, hard, and lets go.

narrator/3558cb169fea40a1.text: The cairns by the crossroads have a new stone at the end of the row, with no name on it, only a horn scratched into the face.

narrator/355ddd06db693967.text: The ice stair ends on a shelf of wind-scoured snow, and the mountain opens a door in front of you. Two colossi of amber stand on either side of it, and the air is so thin that your heart has to work twice as hard for each step.

narrator/358aa30ea4a8c2ca.text: A cairn, built carefully, with a frozen glove on top to mark the way. Someone was kind up here, once.

narrator/358e0677064b9b09.text: A wide stair cut down into the rock. The chanting comes up it like heat from an oven.

narrator/358ea338cd39fa39.text: Two children sit on the floor beside a dollhouse, pale as frost on a window. The girl looks up first, with a hope that has had a long time to get thin.

narrator/3597af9e63313b1e.text: The water along the shore stands up in the shape of people: the drowned of Pescari, grey and swollen, in their Sunday clothes, and behind them a tall shape in a priest's black lifting a hand like a man ringing a bell.

narrator/359cbaa843a3b5e6.text: A big stooped man stirs a cauldron with a paddle. He has a boar's tusk on one side of his mouth, one long hare's ear, and a goat's hoof that clicks on the flagstones.

narrator/35ad29c9d5867467.text: The guardian's base is hollow, packed with old coins and dead leaves.

narrator/35c235507a88dd28.text: At the workroom table, under a lamp, sits the showman from the Blue Water Inn without his feathers or his voice: a thin old man in shirtsleeves, burn-scarred hands spread flat on a map of the valley.

narrator/35dc81ab102c92d9.text: The needle-things straighten up out of their holes all at once, like dogs who've heard the gate.

narrator/35de7f76666c8c15.text: Rahadin rises from his cot as if he has been expecting this, and the screaming rises with him.

narrator/35e80b236779e6e6.text: This one is split from end to end, and silent. Whatever was in it is gone, or dead. Up here, you have learned not to assume which.

narrator/35e84c93e224a450.text: It's empty amber. It's the emptiest thing you have ever seen, and you can't say why.

narrator/35ecf4e48ac0076c.text: Clean floors, aired sheets. Danika keeps a good house, and it keeps its secrets.

narrator/35f31d266c38b184.text: She comes down in Krezk's goat pens, all at once, in a burst of goats. When the shouting stops you can hear Stelian saying that he's seen worse, and that he has, in fact, seen worse, this year.

narrator/362d8a072c7c872f.text: A cold stream comes down from the north, from Tser Falls, and slides into the pool without a ripple.

narrator/3636405af8ac60b8.text: Wind comes up out of the chasm and smells of wet stone. You don't hear anything land.

narrator/363abdc8253d2e84.text: The letters slide away from your attention like fish. The fire leans out to lick your sleeve, and the ring knots itself tighter. You won't unpick it now.

narrator/363c126337d93c0a.text: He holds his hands like a man holding something that isn't there anymore. It isn't his son he can't forgive. He sent two boys to watch that hill, and one came back.

narrator/3645963430df7155.text: Grief, yes, but older and sharper than grief: the kind of guilt that has had centuries to settle into the bones.

narrator/365b8261ad4fcffe.text: You stumble through the old prayer, half-remembered from church doors in other countries, and Ireena mouths the parts you miss. Between you, it's whole.

narrator/3667212c7e50ba1b.text: In the bark at the heart of it there's a face, almost a young man's, almost a Martikov's. It isn't. It has only been drinking from one.

narrator/368fc38f45cd1875.text: Notes, in a hand that gets smaller and smaller down the page. Nothing you can use.

narrator/36903b98272e2845.text: Iron jaws snap shut in the fog.

narrator/36a996752d76b5b0.text: He doesn't lift a hand. He only turns his face up, the way a flower turns to the window.

narrator/36f21c98822dec27.text: The ground under the cave mouth is still beaten bare, but the clay pot is gone and the knife with it.

narrator/37089851a3e2a205.text: You walk her home along the churchyard wall. Her cottage is two rooms and a fire, and the shutter by the hearth stands open the width of a hand.

narrator/370e7dcd89117761.text: The frozen birds hang in the frost garden where they've always hung. One has a gap in the ice beside it where a letter used to be.

narrator/3711db4df0ad4147.text: Getting her up the stair to the courtyard takes six Belviews and most of the afternoon. At the top of the abbey wall she stands on her long legs with the whole valley under her, the wings half open, and doesn't move.

narrator/3719609ecaab5e11.text: The Baron is a round man in a velvet coat with a festival ribbon pinned to every button. He crosses the whole hall to meet you with both hands out, as though you might escape if he walked any slower.

narrator/37261a8ccef8cdfc.text: A narrow bed, made tight. Whatever she kept close, she kept it close.

narrator/37286468a954d277.text: The end of the balcony: an empty armor stand, and beside it a suit of black plate standing on its own, as if it got tired and stepped down. The oak paneling behind it is carved with trees and falling leaves.

narrator/373096819175d6a8.text: Escher watches you go through his things with a face like a slammed door.

narrator/3737ab9938d87a35.text: A crater where the heap was, wet and deep, in the shape of something that got up.

narrator/3788c4666d85f0f3.text: Polished floors, good candles, and the particular hush of a house whose servants have been trained not to hear things. Somewhere upstairs, slow and patient, something is scratching at a door.

narrator/379aa3424bc51c2d.text: Krezk lets one more monk through the gate at dusk without much interest: a stooped one in a deep hood, carrying a bell. A few dozen people drift into the square to see what a monk could possibly have to say.

narrator/37a2a43930682f25.text: A grand hall paneled in dark carved wood, a red marble staircase sweeping up its far side, a longsword hung over a cold marble hearth, and a lamp burning low on a side table. Nobody here lit that lamp, and it burns anyway.

narrator/37b8f78f51085d89.text: A wire, a finger's width above the wagon step, running to a clay jar wedged under the footboard. Somebody here is very good at this.

narrator/37bbff159a9c23db.text: Old, says the brushwork. How old, it won't say.

narrator/37c44461aac3d8c7.text: He says one word to the walls, and every panel in the hall bangs open at once.

narrator/37c692be355f99bd.text: You slip the black halter. She doesn't wait to be thanked: she's a pale streak down the west road toward the camp before the cord hits the ground.

narrator/37c6caf587ed7988.text: The desk is empty. A broken shackle lies on the floor beside a neat stack of ledgers, squared off at the corners.

narrator/37cb3e7746195bf8.text: When the hour is up he lifts the bar, and sits at the head of the stair with it across his knees, lips moving, ready to drop it back.

narrator/37cd9e1b1acc1d14.text: The crowned figure no longer looks at the room. It looks only at whoever carries its gift, the way a proud parent watches a child on a stage.

narrator/380380c2f7eb53a0.text: It doesn't sink. A hand comes up out of the reflection, not out of the water, and closes round it, and it is gone.

narrator/3814ff858e9ce998.text: Empty huts with their doors open, as if their owners only stepped out. One has a notice nailed to it, in careful letters, for whoever comes next.

narrator/381bca0c2b2ebdd8.text: In Ireena's room the candles are out. She stands at the open window in her nightdress, and outside it, standing on nothing, is Strahd.

narrator/3825dd1ed6fde7f4.text: The mound is dry. Everything in Berez is wet except this, and the statue on top of it, and the grass around her feet, which someone keeps cut.

narrator/38285feab93e064c.text: The roots give him up slowly, one at a time. You wrap what's left of him in a cloak. He weighs almost nothing.

narrator/383a23479fe820ca.text: He's a raven before you can answer, going away over the vines toward the house.

narrator/38507f476e554479.text: Dead men in the castle's livery sit up on their pallets. Two suits of armour by the door turn their empty helms toward you. The watch was never relieved.

narrator/3858ad0b9cf4cd96.text: Behind the statue's alcove a slab swings aside onto a narrow clay stair going up. The air on it smells of rain.

narrator/38744d7a6b5dd4b8.text: A long gallery runs the width of the crypts, its ceiling carved with mourners whose faces have worn away to smooth stone.

narrator/387af3ae9b641b0e.text: Kiril's favourites take Emil by the arms and walk him back toward the dark. Kiril doesn't watch. He's looking at you, and grinning.

narrator/387c076a2513f710.text: Five heads on five thick necks crowd the amber, every mouth open. You can't tell whether they are roaring or laughing. The inside of the lid is scored with claw marks.

narrator/38898c514cee1310.text: You sleep in turns at the edge of the pines. All night something walks the slope above you, round and round, never quite close enough to see.

narrator/3890ba40bfd02581.text: The Mash goes still in a spreading stain. The great press stands over it like a judge who has heard enough.

narrator/389c1248279ab494.text: A flagstone sinks, and a blade swings out of the wall at knee height.

narrator/389dfb30f7c4eadf.text: Bluto's shack: one room, one cot, one pot, one patched net hung up to dry over the door. Everything a man needs, if he has given up needing anything else.

narrator/38ab64c81f39ecb4.text: The wicket opens. A broad, grey-bearded man in a sheepskin steps out and looks you over the way a farmer looks at weather.

narrator/38b0b47b05a02dcd.text: A crack in the floor breathes out, and the frost around it is feathered in a fan. The mountain is exhaling through it.

narrator/38b69562a5b066d9.text: Radu's smile arrives a moment late, like a man coming back from somewhere else.

narrator/38d01480a690982c.text: The table is half empty; the rest of the knights are on their feet, buckling on things that have not been buckled in centuries.

narrator/38d156b45c7125b3.text: The cracks in the floor are dark and wet, and steam rises off them. It's hot in here, but only hot.

narrator/38d442a296b8a16c.text: The carved paneling swings inward on a narrow stair going up into the dark.

narrator/38dc85d944f19b34.text: A promise is a heavy thing to set down. You feel the weight of this one as you do it.

narrator/38f44c5a148c98b9.text: The black water is running back toward the altar, as if the whole house is draining toward its stomach.

narrator/38f97ef57864d9d2.text: A green painted wagon stands by the signpost, hung all over with pots and ladles and strings of little bells, with no horse in the shafts. On the board at the front sits a thin Vistani man with a big smile and a blanket over his knees.

narrator/3901c4dfbfedeb7e.text: He's silent so long the candles gutter. When he speaks, his voice is very small.

narrator/390a85d1a2cee6a3.text: Bricks are climbing the window row by row. There is still a gap at the top. Break through it, or stay forever.

narrator/390e72e51f4c0baf.text: Under the torn sleeve, a bite: half healed, ringed in angry red, the marks of long teeth. She glares at you as if you'd made it yourself.

narrator/3917092c0ad48f11.text: The boy flings himself at the nearest of you before anyone can move.

narrator/391f140de2957172.text: The screaming around the chamberlain rises, all at once, as if every voice in it has turned to look. One of them, very clearly, is a woman calling a name. It is Sorrel's name.

narrator/392fd42860d5f1b2.text: The column forms up across the gate again, as it has every night for four hundred years. The marshal rides forward.

narrator/3936157775a39da1.text: The words go out over the water. The bell rings once more, softer, and stops, and does not start again. The marsh feels less crowded afterwards.

narrator/3942c3a69fd29611.text: You say it the way it's cut in the stone: keep the watch, shield the sleeper and the stranger, lift the fallen, take nothing not given, and when the light goes out, be the light. Halfway through, his lips start moving with yours.

narrator/3945762117c447ee.text: He sits down again, very fast, and goes very pink, and starts serving before anyone can say anything.

narrator/394a1caf1ec686f2.text: Old script runs across the stone over the doors, cut deep by someone who expected to be obeyed. Most of it is a list. The last line is a single word.

narrator/394c5be5f7157589.text: The silver is real, the plates are old, and the food is very good. Nobody carries it in, and nobody takes it out.

narrator/3955458668f3641d.text: A ragged flock of bats lifts off the ridge and beats away south, toward the castle. Nobody is up there now.

narrator/396b4ba10acf3eec.text: The weeping from the shuttered house has softened to something nearer to humming. It is not a happy tune.

narrator/3974741ad38eb894.text: A shortsword with a silvered blade, wrapped in oilcloth. Someone came down here expecting monsters.

narrator/3976d385ba60afb2.text: The old woman lies by her own hearth. All around you the hut groans, long and low, and its timbers settle like an animal lying down for the last time. The green fire gutters out.

narrator/3987fe9cab1a352c.text: The oldest crypts, names worn soft by damp: Durst, Durst, Durst. This family kept its dead close, closer than most.

narrator/398af36013ed6709.text: One of the sleepers rises and walks to him across the camp with open, empty eyes.

narrator/399288afd33732f7.text: The silver flame leans toward the cradle on its own. You swore an oath over Vladimir's table that this house would go on watching.

narrator/39bc5d50ba175037.text: The words go into him and something goes out, the way a fever breaks. The ruff at his neck is only hair. When he looks up his eyes are a boy's eyes, brown and wet, and the goats on either side of him wake up and edge away, offended.

narrator/39c1eb8308bf204b.text: Knives come out of sleeves all over the square. Lady Wachter's people were never here to watch the sun.

narrator/39c636ff1087d2db.text: The showman goes out of him like air out of a bladder. What's left is an old man, very tired and very alert, who sits down and lowers his voice.

narrator/39da9c093a5ace1f.text: Four arms on a leaning post, the paint long gone and the names cut deep with a knife: BAROVIA east, VALLAKI and TSER POOL west, TSER FALLS north. The south arm has been sawn off, and someone has nailed a dead crow in its place.

narrator/39e015c85e402bd4.text: Banners so rotted they hang like grey cobweb. The one over the head of the table has been mended, badly, with the stitches of someone who had never sewn before and had a very long time to learn.

narrator/39e6b66fb282f743.text: A hooded figure sits with its mouth sewn shut and its hands folded over a small closed box. The voice, when it comes, comes from inside the box.

narrator/39e826faa5b4378b.text: All down the slope, every blight on the hill folds up where it stands and falls into a heap of dry brush.

narrator/3a0a9130c0babdba.text: A guardroom: bunks, a cold brazier, a rack of halberds furred with frost. Whoever stood watch here left in good order, and didn't come back.

narrator/3a1a02937c2b2f9a.text: On the lid's edge, two clean scrapes where it was lifted with a lever, carefully, in exactly the two places that wouldn't crack the stone. Whoever did this knew the trick of it.

narrator/3a264205c5372693.text: The stair is narrow enough that two people can't pass, and it goes up and up with no window, as if the tower meant to keep its secret until the top.

narrator/3a4336284340dba5.text: The slab grinds aside, and the coffin's lid lifts by itself, raised from beneath by a pouring black tide of legs.

narrator/3a43e4578b08f042.text: Somebody's hand closes on his collar and pulls, and he comes away from the amber blinking, as if out of a warm bath into the cold.

narrator/3a46f5aa29c2057a.text: You make your case, and Krezk listens to it with its arms folded, which is how Krezk listens to everything.

narrator/3a4f545be9beb37b.text: You tell him: the nails never drawn, the stones from the abbey track, the child's blanket wrapped round them to make the shape.

narrator/3a6b3e12782f9f7b.text: She goes into the wagon behind her and comes back with a small corked bottle, which she pushes into the nearest hand without looking at whose it is.

narrator/3a6f52ed6a11306f.text: HENRIK VAN DER VOORT, COFFINS, ALL SIZES. Underneath, newer and smaller: CLOSED AFTER DARK.

narrator/3a7d71c939e8f700.text: The trail climbs out of the pines onto a bare slope under a rock face. High up in the rock is a cave mouth, and the warm air coming out of it smells of wet dog and old meat.

narrator/3a7e5c7385d83ce3.text: Behind the wall, bones are stacked to the ceiling in careful patterns, skulls in rows, long bones in bundles. Somebody had a great deal of time and nobody to stop them.

narrator/3a8d8f71c3fe2972.text: A small den: a table set for supper, two high-backed chairs, iron candlesticks, one candle burning. Somebody down here still keeps up appearances.

narrator/3a8df6851d94e7fc.text: The letters are worn soft and written in a script that went out of fashion centuries ago. They might say anything. They might be a name.

narrator/3aa25855c362283b.text: You stack Bildrath's load on top of Grigore's and set the lot alight. For a moment it burns like any wood. Then the logs begin to scream.

narrator/3ad37612c1dda15b.text: A huge grey-bearded man in a red sash rises from beside the fire with a fiddle in one hand and a cup in the other, and spreads both arms as if you were family come home late.

narrator/3ae6f8916a770b44.text: The lid is scored all over with claw marks and scorches. If there were words, the dogs have had them.

narrator/3aee4ed0a401fc48.text: The great wooden gear of the sails fills this end of the loft, its teeth as long as your forearm, braked still with a timber wedge. In the floor beside it, the chute down to the millstone.

narrator/3af71da0d1553c51.text: The carved lid slides back off a giant in old mail, a greatsword laid down his length.

narrator/3b22bc9dc40f74b5.text: A crooked hut of black timber with one shuttered window and a door that doesn't sit straight. It's breathing. The shutters lift and settle, very slightly, in time.

narrator/3b2484d5c3d66215.text: The shore is churned to mud, and the reeds are flattened in a track as wide as a cart where something huge came down to drink for the last time.

narrator/3b374f5bc1edad82.text: Cyrus's shriek goes down the guards' run like a bell. Boots answer it, and some of them are not boots.

narrator/3b3c8ad309b4eee8.text: Among the jars and bottles, one flask has no label. The oil inside is grey, and your hand looks faintly see-through behind the glass.

narrator/3b4441162cf10370.text: Grey shapes come out of the dark in a line, too orderly for a hunting pack. Somebody sent them, and they know whom they were sent for.

narrator/3b5df2869e171f47.text: He sits down on the top step with his back to the wall and his face to the light, and is still.

narrator/3b6211436fc09e1c.text: Ireena puts her hand in his. He lifts her over the sill as lightly as a dancer, and she does not look back.

narrator/3b6fff2c1732e2e3.text: A square shaft drops away into the dark beside a great iron winch. A cage hangs in the shaft on a chain, turning a little in a draught you can't feel.

narrator/3b7035b452d1b0e4.text: Clear glass now, and behind it the dragon and his lamp, the lamp bright enough that you look twice.

narrator/3b7107bf6d8a43e9.text: Both helmets turn south toward the castle together, like two compass needles.

narrator/3b82bbe313480d94.text: He beams at you with total, impenetrable cheer. It's either the most sincere face in Barovia or the most practised. Possibly both.

narrator/3b8b4883cca0aa91.text: Behind the winch, on its hook, the watch horn. Its mouth is cracked from the last time someone blew it too hard.

narrator/3b94633aefc752f6.text: A heap of burned straw and wet silk the size of a haystack, and a ring of black ground around it where nothing will grow back.

narrator/3ba12255bf0a36f4.text: He says it to you, but he's looking at Ireena, and she's looking at the ground.

narrator/3bc30b716b910dfe.text: The upper hall is longer than it was, or you are more frightened. Possibly both.

narrator/3bdf23effa55c3e3.text: Kip unrolls the contract on the table. It's longer than it should be when it's rolled up, and the ink moves a little, like something breathing in its sleep. Vosk's nose lifts.

narrator/3bdf5b774e356e0d.text: Each time a word slips away from him, his eyes go up and to the left, out of the window, to the summit where a cairn of stones stands against the sky. As if he left something there and can't remember why he keeps checking on it.

narrator/3c1a9b1f8aa3f43e.text: Tamsin gets up with the silver locket already open in his hand. He walks to Strahd and holds it up on his flat palm, the way you'd offer a horse a sugar lump, and his eyes are empty.

narrator/3c2b183eebd93ad7.text: The wardens' word is the last line of the carving. Now that you know it, you can't stop seeing it.

narrator/3c466d9a3593e0fc.text: He shivers once, all over, and gets up from the window for the first time in a day, and goes and hits his brother.

narrator/3c4be6137e042db2.text: Thistle's on her knees in the straw in front of him before anyone can stop her, both hands on his face, fur and stubble and all, and he lets her, and closes his eyes.

narrator/3c61c45843162e6e.text: A carriage house with one carriage in it, black and polished, and two black horses that do not look round.

narrator/3c693431dd4346e9.text: Lucian reads them at the church door the next morning, slowly, name by name. Urwin stands beside him with his arms folded. By noon the stocks are empty, and nobody in Vallaki wears a ribbon.

narrator/3c821ec382623162.text: It starts, as most things between them start, with Wren saying something he shouldn't.

narrator/3c9332370af6bbb8.text: The board snaps under you and you drop to the waist, legs kicking in the air of the room below.

narrator/3c948ae0ef65b272.text: Gertruda sits on the bed in a new gown, a green one. She smiles at you politely, the way you smile at strangers.

narrator/3c970c0e3a018530.text: Shapes in rusted helmets of an old pattern come up the road in a ragged column, still marching on a house they burned four hundred years ago. Two at the back sniff the air and break into a run.
