narrator/3c9d6b3bb7867671.text: The stacks run the length of the hall. Most of the books have been chained in place, as if they might otherwise wander.

narrator/3c9f68a0fa6750db.text: SERGEI VON ZAROVICH, and under the name, smaller: BELOVED. Under that, scratched much later by a less steady hand: FORGIVE ME.

narrator/3c9fe7bc6d983196.text: A room that has been locked for a long time and smells like it: lavender gone to dust, a narrow bed, a trunk, a hairbrush with grey hair still in it.

narrator/3cace754ec692f61.text: Two figures on the road ahead, walking upright. Then one of them drops to all fours, and the other one laughs with far too many teeth.

narrator/3cb000018405274b.text: A marble hearth under a mahogany-framed painting of an alpine valley, green meadows under white peaks. Barovia has no valley like it; perhaps that is why someone painted it.

narrator/3cb9e25cd28f9d6e.text: She goes back to eating whatever it was. You don't think she's hungry.

narrator/3cc1c955031ac9f2.text: At the bottom of the stair the silence has a shape, the way a house is quiet when someone in it is asleep.

narrator/3cda38ce325d3539.text: The wainscot along the hall bristles. Something metal is pushing through the paneling from inside.

narrator/3cea237b0f8c5526.text: You kneel beside her. The step is so cold it aches.

narrator/3cf4520c1003d93b.text: A bare little room with a coffin in it, and on the coffin's lid a child's drawing of a town on a hill, pinned flat with a hairpin.

narrator/3d0c630300fe78d8.text: He talks about the dawn the way a man describes a country he has only read about. And he hasn't blinked once.

narrator/3d10de41cd260d73.text: The straw drops away under you into a shaft, and the shaft has a bottom.

narrator/3d12be87a1e38be4.text: It comes over the wall on all fours and stands up in the square: a wolf the size of a cart horse, grey to white with age, scarred, missing an ear, with old wolves at its heels.

narrator/3d1e076e46472d0b.text: The voices in the walls go quiet. Merrow doesn't answer.

narrator/3d29587d61cebb90.text: Your blade goes into the black wood at the foot of the row, and the whole row flinches, from one end to the other.

narrator/3d59335aed308cb1.text: A mound of rot and rushes taller than a man, steaming faintly. It rises and falls, and rises, and falls.

narrator/3d59cf5be4893b85.text: He goes slowly, holding the pen. Behind him, for the first time in a year, the lamp in the window goes out.

narrator/3d6515e4d3d4ebcc.text: The vines lie down again. Some of them, you're nearly sure, look relieved.

narrator/3d6d160ebc876605.text: Bells. The watch goes door to door with clubs and ribbons, and Vallaki comes out to be happy. Within the hour the square is full, shoulder to shoulder, nobody speaking much above a murmur.

narrator/3d8a7f4a14cf2176.text: Thistle isn't up a tree tonight. She's on the ground, right across the fire, staring at you. She's been doing it for some time.

narrator/3d9ecbcc1b512c29.text: You go for him. Ireena cries out and stumbles back from the sill, and Strahd laughs, delighted, and steps into the room.

narrator/3daba32220b7b3f0.text: Crate lids lift on their own, slowly, the nails squealing out one by one. What climbs out has been waiting in the dark for a reason to.

narrator/3dc0059edd6cae89.text: A narrow closet that smells of lamp oil. Lamps hang in rows on hooks, every one of them cold.

narrator/3de0b65b7eaa5fe2.text: Silvain is writing by the last of the firelight, small and fast, crossing out almost as much as they keep.

narrator/3de24e4f3abab904.text: The hut lies sprawled across the stump with its roots in the air, like a beetle on its back. Its door hangs open on nothing.

narrator/3de9108521cfca27.text: The ravens barely look up. A few of them make room on the beams.

narrator/3deb7ce0cbc4cc0a.text: A good fire, banked with stones and burning hot and smokeless. Silver-headed crossbow bolts lie in a neat row beside it, drying.

narrator/3df9d9d599e0b7eb.text: The slope under the cave mouth is beaten bare. A clay pot of water sits by the rock, and a knife, and a basket of cut stalks: someone has been working here and only just stopped.

narrator/3dfccad7eec8822a.text: Druids look up from the vats, where they have been feeding something green and pulpy into the wine. Around them the floor heaves, and things of twig and needle unfold from the mash.

narrator/3e0958bcaeae14ea.text: White, clean, dry. Excellent firewood, by every sign you know. Bildrath watches you put it down as if you've insulted his stock.

narrator/3e16111f9ef2f5e4.text: It takes longer than it should, and somebody's knuckles pay for it, but the bricks go in the end.

narrator/3e2e2140463fb50a.text: A plain clay jar on the highest shelf, sealed with wax and labelled in a careful, shaky hand: NOT THE PHYLACTERY.

narrator/3e349da923b09b04.text: The second suit of wolf-helmed armor, its spear a little crooked, as if it leaned to listen and straightened when you looked.

narrator/3e4b1bc0dc8ec0d1.text: A child's drawing on the lid: a walled town on a hill, a pool, a tree. Underneath, in a careful round hand, "Krezk".

narrator/3e7e19ddf51b2752.text: A drive between dead trees climbs past the footings of a gatehouse into a courtyard of cracked flagstones. The mansion's black front fills the north side, its beacon tower above the east wing. A stone mausoleum stands apart to the east; the stables and the squires' graves are going back to the forest on the west.

narrator/3e823791793a28b2.text: Three mornings later the sun is still rising, and Ireena asks to be taken to Krezk.

narrator/3e8408f2db0fb6e0.text: Ireena leans out over the water until her breath clouds its surface. Then she stops.

narrator/3e87654af98a9c4c.text: The rock is slick with spray and the rope burns through your hands. You come back up empty and bleeding, and the boy's voice says: it's all right. It's all right. Try again.

narrator/3e87e8bec5eed484.text: A long hall round a long table, scarred by a hundred years of elbows, with a hearth at one end and a spinning wheel at the other.

narrator/3e930af42bc8781e.text: Every jar on the shelf hums, except one. Inside the silent jar, a potion that fizzes like shaken wine and makes your heartbeat hurry just looking at it.

narrator/3e95a4dc6b1397da.text: Bats. Hundreds, hanging in the dead pine in black bunches. And in the crook of the trunk, very still, two pale shapes in good coats that are not asleep, with their eyes open, watching the trail.

narrator/3e9e9190d8dea260.text: The only room in Barovia where people still talk, if quietly. The wine is Purple Grapemash No. 3, and there isn't much of it left.

narrator/3eb8b37dc02dbd7d.text: A dry well. A stone dropped in takes a long time to hit anything.

narrator/3eb9d8fcae22cc99.text: A small room with a narrow bed, a peg with nothing on it, and a carved wooden sword on the sill. It's been kept clean. It hasn't been slept in for a long time.

narrator/3ebf8c943abb6c62.text: Something has been sitting at the edge of the trees, listening to the water with you. It stands up on two legs.

narrator/3ee981310e974d3b.text: The great doors swing inward before you touch them, and close behind you just as quietly.

narrator/3eeedffed884b449.text: A girl comes down the lane barefoot, in a white nightgown, with an armful of black roses. She walks on the lit side of the street, the way she was taught.

narrator/3ef3bef81e5f7de4.text: The ring groans, cracks and comes out of the rock in a shower of grit, then the other. The silver goes slack.

narrator/3ef5b4f9741a7261.text: Liriel takes one step toward him and goes down on both knees on the cold flags, her hands over her mouth. When she looks up her face is wet and shining.

narrator/3f0c70149b9ed5c9.text: Liriel has been writing something in the back of her prayer book, very small. When she sees you looking, she turns the book round so you can read it. It's a list of your names.

narrator/3f53a4b2e4fc7bd5.text: She climbs the stairs alone and doesn't look back. Rahadin bows to you, very correctly.

narrator/3f6a92274dcad48d.text: Stella screams, and it is a girl's scream, all of it. But her shadow on the wall doesn't scream with her. Her shadow stands up, and so do all the others in the room.

narrator/3f8b4c8d3cbd29e7.text: His face is a beautiful closed door.

narrator/3f907ec898b71939.text: You know the house. You have heard the woman weeping in it.

narrator/3fa528e5f144882f.text: She doesn't answer him. She takes the locket from her collar and opens it, so he can see whose it is now.

narrator/3fa88fa27c86fd42.text: A man of packed earth and split timber, forty feet long, lying on his back with a cloak of turf. The face is crude but you'd know it anywhere. In the chest, under the turf, something green beats like a heart.

narrator/3fd3ed244274e38e.text: A long hall lined with stone knights on plinths, swords grounded, visors down, facing each other across the aisle.

narrator/3fd55b663bd2b8e4.text: Small graves in a neat row, each with a small stone. The squires buried the knights' horses and the dragon, and then somebody buried the squires.

narrator/3fe1cb4fef14bb71.text: Under a servant's bed, wrapped in a clean rag, a pair of thick leather gloves. Whoever owned them caught things that were thrown at them, by the look of the palms.

narrator/3fe493a4b0494446.text: Back on the family's floor. A door that was shut is now open.

narrator/3fe640dac403ea56.text: The paper is stiff with frost and the ink has run, but the hand is the one he described: small, slanted, running out of margin.

narrator/3fe8c12ad4dff0fb.text: She doesn't lower the spyglass. She raises a small crossbow in her other hand instead, and points it at you without looking.

narrator/40023dc46d1c4ffc.text: A saint carved in white stone, hands open. Her face has been cut away with care, the way you'd peel fruit.

narrator/400971a1fc859421.text: His fingers twitch. It could be the wind. There is no wind.

narrator/400f53b7a4573f58.text: A cradle on rockers, under a crocheted blanket. Something green glows under the blanket, softly. When you lean over it, the old woman stops rocking and watches your hands until you straighten up again.

narrator/401203d47c3f26de.text: Howling, close and getting closer, from voices that sound almost like men's.

narrator/404b14a4cdbea9da.text: Red light pours out of it and is gone. The pieces that hit the floor are only glass.

narrator/4063c92afd94304d.text: A small room: a large bed under a faded coverlet, a writing table, an empty wardrobe with its doors ajar, and a full-length mirror that doesn't quite sit flush with the wall.

narrator/4067d605d8ba3609.text: Ratatoille is cooking breakfast with tremendous concentration, though there's very little to cook and nobody is hungry.

narrator/407073a70fe7542e.text: The stables lost their roof long ago. The stalls still have their names painted over them, and their bones in them.

narrator/407b3539e7341c04.text: She rises from the bier in one smooth movement, like a dancer, and the Belviews reach under their rags for cleavers and pruning hooks.

narrator/40a966c1bd56a416.text: The oven is going cold. Without anyone to tend it, the bakery smells only of flour and old ash, and it is very quiet upstairs.

narrator/40cb86362ad8bd71.text: The woman at the bricked-up window doesn't turn round. Her reflection would, if she had one.

narrator/40d11d57ef5df46e.text: You ask Lazar whether he guards the wall from the outside or the inside, and whether the wall knows. It's not much, but Krezk has been waiting years for somebody to say something to Lazar, and the square laughs at him instead of at Clovin.

narrator/40e0b7b1d129296a.text: A painted sign of blue water under a black bird. Somebody has repainted the bird recently, with real care.

narrator/40e87570c1c7fc41.text: You lift the lid. A young woman lies in the crypt with her eyes open, grey to the lips, in the rags of a scholar's coat, with ink still on her fingers. She sits up as if she's been waiting.

narrator/40f8ab28e4d3e062.text: For a heartbeat the tea stops halfway to her mouth.

narrator/4109af1ea9c8011c.text: The last steps of the black stair are worn into hollows. Not by many feet. By one pair, over a very long time.

narrator/410b4e35c76222cf.text: He listens. He doesn't want to, but he listens, and halfway through he starts crying, and the sack slides off his shoulder into your arms.

narrator/4129c0ba3995b110.text: You let him lead you to the amber, and at the last moment you aren't there. His hands close on air, and the hollow takes the only thing within reach: his own shadow, with its two tall ears.

narrator/4146fc1d92297172.text: Ilarion stands by the well and looks at the blue door, which is grey, and at the old woman coming across the square with two buckets, who stops dead when she sees him and lets them both go.

narrator/414b79432434798a.text: Bundles of herbs and feathers and little knotted cords hanging from every beam. Several of the knots are tied around teeth.

narrator/415c99ac29012e48.text: The pines over the road are hung with grey sheets of web, and the sheets are moving.

narrator/4164b091c9f92c70.text: A long rug with the family crest woven into it, worn through where the boots go.

narrator/41661ce7d05a3327.text: His lips have drawn back from his teeth, and he doesn't seem to know. The two behind him stopped breathing some time ago and haven't missed it.

narrator/416b9ec6c5bb20a1.text: A rotten jetty running out into the Luna, with a mooring ring and no boat. The last plank has been gnawed through, by something that wanted it.

narrator/41777ab32482c1c0.text: Neither of them seems to notice they're still holding each other's sleeves.

narrator/417a9eccf77e3bf6.text: A great iron winch, its drum wound with chain that runs down a square shaft into the dark. Beside it a brake lever stands thrown off, and the cage hangs a foot below the landing.

narrator/4182ce554838a0df.text: The ground has told you all it's going to.

narrator/4184968984354e70.text: The straw in the open cell lies too flat and too fresh, and the satchel on it was put there to be seen.

narrator/41b38fdaa4450b05.text: He rubs his face with both hands, for a long time.

narrator/41d6a84977d7b96f.text: You say the word the wardens chose. The colossus lowers its head, and the light in its eyes sinks to an ember. Somewhere deep in the amber, something settles.

narrator/41dae0bfd8d53cf1.text: Cold ash underfoot and the smell of a fire that went out four hundred years ago. Somewhere ahead, beyond tall doors, armour creaks as something turns its head.

narrator/41e20ed056efa5eb.text: Bones in the reeds, picked clean and laid out in a neat row by size, the way a child lines up toys. Someone in Berez likes things tidy.

narrator/41e74c7dc89cfe82.text: You tell her about the board round his neck, and the two words written on it.

narrator/41ed0ab8e8900c0d.text: A narrow court in the lee of the church, sheltered from the wind. The snow here is untrodden, except for one line of bare footprints that walks to the wall and stops.

narrator/420628c9bd2f54c7.text: Sacks stacked by size, each labelled in a careful, loopy hand: FLOUR, MORE FLOUR, DREAMS (BEST), DREAMS (SECONDS). The last sack is labelled with a name.

narrator/421a5f6f2d7e76a1.text: The stair is so narrow your shoulders brush both walls. At the bottom, something glitters.

narrator/422bb3f98a9b7187.text: The crowd parts to let him through. A few people don't look away. Most do.

narrator/4231f1a188df2998.text: The portrait stands a little open on its hinge. Behind it, narrow steps go down into the dark.

narrator/4245b381ed66b42e.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Khirad, who reads the stars backward. Everything it foretold came true. Its readers wished it hadn't."

narrator/4253b0b5775cebcb.text: On the wall, somebody bangs a spear on the stones, once, twice. In Krezk, apparently, that's applause.

narrator/426601ed63898b28.text: With the chant ended, the tree is only a tree, and somehow that's worse: a crooked black thing with its roots deep in a hill of old graves, waiting for the next person to feed it.

narrator/426a52ff09784012.text: A gallery of pillars at the head of the stair. Every sound you make comes back to you a moment later, slightly changed, as if repeated by someone who didn't quite catch it.

narrator/426a66d7bf9441fb.text: The pews are worn smooth. On the backs of some, small hands have carved small names, the way children do in church when the sermon is long.

narrator/4273238490a96a1f.text: You are at Argynvostholt, a cold house of a fallen order whose armour still stands to attention.

narrator/4288c08d191037da.text: A portrait of a stern man in armour. Its eyes are not painted on. They follow you.

narrator/428d1d9efc1d0331.text: It's quick. The roots that were reaching toward her draw back, as if they'd lost interest.

narrator/42934930d6a45f23.text: The wind turns, and the mountain disappears. Snow comes sideways, thick as wool, and the person in front of you becomes a grey shape, then a voice, then nothing.

narrator/42a6adaf96a17ac1.text: Down here the amber in the walls glows, faintly, like honey held up to a candle. It is the only warm colour for a mile in any direction, and it is not warm.

narrator/42b26b11ca54bc33.text: The last row before the camp. The leaves are veined dark, like the back of an old hand, and the grapes hang in heavy black clusters, far too many and far too ripe for this valley.

narrator/42bab163ba982d70.text: Davian lets the blanket fall and walks up the lane without a word. At the top he lays a hand flat on the winery door, the way you'd lay a hand on a horse that came home without its rider.

narrator/42d30265b5884f9f.text: The trap's jaws close slowly on a stick. Its spring sighs, disappointed.

narrator/42e1cfb0f849c1e8.text: Dust, and dust under the dust. This altar has been forgotten more thoroughly than anything you've seen.

narrator/42e34402f7b5160a.text: Master, go. I'll hold the door. He's coming up the stair and he's laughing. Don't come back for me. I mean it. Corvina.

narrator/4306e065fa40bd7b.text: The note is still in the margin in faded brown ink. Silvain reads it again anyway, lips moving.

narrator/43071ea9f98135da.text: A flue lever hangs in the chimney's throat, rusted open. Under the grate, scratched into the stone, runs a ring of tiny letters.

narrator/432f3f078f95746f.text: The coffin maker jumps when the door opens, then pretends he didn't. He's a thin man sweating in a cold room, and he keeps his back to the storeroom door the whole time you're talking.

narrator/433b412f4172ba72.text: Grey steel comes out of grey scabbards with no sound at all.

narrator/4344346cf42950ff.text: The second stone is warm and smells faintly of smoke. Davian turns it over twice, looking for the tree in it, and doesn't find any.

narrator/434ddcc4cba70190.text: The lights come up out of the gorge like lanterns climbing a stair, and every one of them is still talking in somebody's voice.

narrator/4352c156c5284ddb.text: Each step is worn into a hollow in its middle. A great many boots have come up these stairs, all the way to the top, to look at a lamp that wouldn't light.

narrator/436f86eddad356b3.text: The front door is bricked up, and so is most of the window you came out of. Faintly, from inside, comes the sound of a trowel.

narrator/436fabf00edbd4ec.text: The watchman lets his spear fall. His festival ribbon has come loose and hangs from his breastplate like a wilted flower. 'All right,' he says. 'All will be well.' He doesn't sound as if he believes it.

narrator/4380b911332be7a1.text: The lake below is grey as a knife. On its island, a tower stands with one lit window, small as a spark. Somebody else in this valley is keeping a watch.

narrator/438790e6d1ae5f90.text: The two of them go down the stairs together, arguing in low voices about whose fault the last twelve years were.

narrator/43adbda461800e63.text: A round pavilion of white stone on six thin pillars, open to the weather. Under its roof stands a statue of a robed figure holding up a sunburst in both hands, worn so smooth by touching that the face is gone.

narrator/43d26f4f493a164e.text: The cages hang still. The girl has both hands on the bars, white at the knuckles. The boy is awake now, staring at the rocking chair, which has finally stopped.

narrator/43d5443d5bea6039.text: Someone has come halfway down the stair to see what the noise was: a lovely young woman with flour-white hands and a red ribbon in her hair, who looks over the wreck of the bakery with mild interest.

narrator/43fc3cf5404f8961.text: A thin young man hangs in silvered chains, his toes just clear of the floor. His lips are cracked back to the gums. He knows you at once.

narrator/440324155ec191df.text: Liriel opens her eyes. She gets up out of her blankets and crosses the camp to him barefoot over the cold ground, and her face is calm and quite empty, the way it is at prayer.

narrator/4417d2e1ec4f7d9d.text: One floorboard in the gallery is dark with rot and bows downward, like a sagging lip.

narrator/4422453f27ac0273.text: The bars are on the outside, held by simple iron pins. Anyone could let them out. Nobody has.

narrator/443904b55a80b77a.text: At a table stacked with books sits a stooped, pleasant-faced man in a scholar's gown, spectacles low on his nose, a cup of something steaming at his elbow. Nothing else in this library is warm.

narrator/444a1bb9bfc5554e.text: Behind the bar the casks are stacked three high, and when Arik taps the top one it rings hollow. Only one of them still sloshes.

narrator/444a9e771dc93f4a.text: Something small and warm comes home. Whichever of you paid Morgantha with a dream remembers it, all at once, and has to sit down.

narrator/4453b536a9190f2f.text: The road comes out onto a landing at the head of the bridge. Above the far crag something huge breathes in its sleep, slow as surf.

narrator/44618babf92e0649.text: It comes away easily, as if the hands had only been holding it until somebody asked.

narrator/448ba2af7ca31fe0.text: Straw beds, heaped together for warmth, with a few treasures tucked into them: a button, a spoon, a bird's skull, a scrap of ribbon.

narrator/449ccb690c2080ab.text: The house leans in to watch.

narrator/44be551c123bb671.text: You don't stay to see what the Vistani decide. You hear it, a little later, from the road.

narrator/44f37b21765a4007.text: The last of the druids' people sits down hard in the dirt, spent, chest heaving. Mud and berry juice streak the paint on his face.

narrator/44f654430eade8f8.text: Parriwimple is waiting at the gate with a shovel over his shoulder. He takes the foot of the coffin by himself and doesn't seem to notice the weight.

narrator/45091b829539843c.text: Lucian carries the bundle down to the crypt himself, holding it the way you would hold a sleeping child. You hear the lid of the sarcophagus grind home, and then his voice, saying the old words. Something in the air of the church settles, like a held breath let out.

narrator/450d1529924a1de3.text: You are at the tower on Lake Baratok, standing on its island like a finger raised for silence.

narrator/45199fa1583d3c1f.text: The carved lid slides back. On the champion's chest, under his crossed hands, lies something his watchers were never set to guard.

narrator/451ca730f756ba12.text: He gathers three books under his arm, nods politely and goes off into the stacks. You don't hear his footsteps, though the floor is bare stone.

narrator/4527b983528b9ae8.text: A narrow nook in the corner of the storage room, with nothing at the back but bare plaster. Bare, and oddly warm.

narrator/4530d5bf33fc58b9.text: Nobody plays the fiddle at Tser Pool again.

narrator/45394320dc52624a.text: Kip is writing a letter by the fire, slowly, crossing out more than he writes.

narrator/45481bae63979ef6.text: Kip doesn't sit down tonight. He stands at the edge of the firelight with his hat in his hands, facing out into the dark.

narrator/454b844dc2dbb31f.text: Sir Godfrey looks at each of you in turn: the slow, careful look of a man fixing faces in a memory that has failed him before.

narrator/45559211b2008150.text: Kolyan Indirovich, burgomaster, beside his wife. The earth is fresh and the candle on it is still burning, though nobody has been seen to light it.

narrator/4560bfa76f84e002.text: A young woman curls on the bed with her chin on her knees, licking the back of one hand and smoothing her hair with it. She watches you without blinking, and purrs when you come no closer.

narrator/4575a9646e328607.text: The wine is thin, sour and faintly purple, like a bruise you can drink.

narrator/459cff3b5f014e14.text: If the beacon burns tonight, they lie down tonight, and they won't march.

narrator/45a2002924fa1c16.text: You wait by the pens with the boy between you. The moon comes up full over the hills, enormous. The goats go silent all at once.

narrator/45a8a784390b3227.text: The crib is freshly made, the blanket folded neatly around nothing at all.

narrator/45b07995b36cc2c0.text: Dolls, puppets, tops and music boxes, every one of them carved with care and every one of them faintly wrong: a smile too wide, a bear with too many teeth.

narrator/45c5224db63f4edd.text: Somebody has laid out a pair of white slippers at the foot of the table, side by side, ready.

narrator/45e20c93fc8fc33b.text: Two cold weights lift out of two of you, like children climbing down from a cart.

narrator/45e90ec7cedb0623.text: Somewhere in the town a festival lantern goes out, and nobody relights it.

narrator/45f11ef7eee52e3e.text: He polishes a cup that doesn't need polishing and gives you nothing. He's done this before, to better questioners than you.

narrator/460127c1e2f22831.text: A deer, torn open and left. Whatever killed it didn't stay to eat.

narrator/461310f48445512f.text: They back away three steps, then turn and run, and never once look back.

narrator/4614f980a44d7112.text: Five gouges in the bark, higher than a man can reach, deep enough to lay a finger in. The pine is still alive. It does not look happy about it.

narrator/462c370a7308968e.text: The eating contest was Thistle's idea. Most things involving shouting are. It has been going on for some time, and Ratatoille has stopped cooking in protest.

narrator/4655b89bcb3c43ff.text: The east rows, where the grapes still hang: small, hard and purple-black, like a fist of bruises. A few of the leaves are green, stubbornly.

narrator/465d2b67e0976633.text: A girl of about sixteen sits on the edge of a curtained bed in a blue gown too fine for her, turning a ribbon over in her fingers. She jumps up when the door opens, and her face falls when she sees it isn't him.

narrator/466939b771cf0de1.text: Two children stand in the road where the cottages begin: a girl of ten with her chin up, and a small boy holding a stuffed wolf by one ear. Neither is dressed for the cold, and neither seems to feel it.

narrator/4682a1d2b2b698d1.text: Everything, sooner or later. Tonight, the town. Tomorrow, whatever he asks for next. She knows it, and she has decided it is a fair price, because she has decided she will never be the one who pays it.

narrator/46989a3229b72d61.text: A young monk in a plain brown habit is lighting the candles along the altar rail. He doesn't use a taper. He touches each wick with a fingertip, and each one lights.

narrator/46a1ef10a0dcd213.text: Hooves on the castle road behind you. Too early. A carriage lamp swings up out of the dark, and the black horse in the traces is coming at a gallop.

narrator/46ab9a0329d47f17.text: A long nave under a sunburst window, every candle lit, the altar dressed in white. The air in here is warmer than outside, and it isn't the candles.

narrator/46b9cf6c53210b6e.text: The bed is made. It has been made for a very long time. Nobody sleeps in it; he only likes to have it.

narrator/46c19ba2d16a57b2.text: A big grey wolfhound stands with his front feet against the mansion's side wall, under the boarded study window, and howls at the bricks. When you come close he stops, and looks at you, and goes back to it.

narrator/46d62b63674dbe57.text: It's a spell, not weather: a great one, cast once and left running, like a clock somebody wound and forgot. Whoever told the sky to strike here every evening never told it to stop, and the work is so good it hasn't faltered once.

narrator/46e948ae1137ed98.text: The three graves open from underneath. Ana climbs out first, and brushes the earth off her nightgown, and smiles at you with all her teeth.

narrator/46f195f5e2c2c601.text: The vault ceiling is cracked amber, hanging in shards as long as knives. One good shake would bring it down.

narrator/472e2569e8422e96.text: A cobbled yard between the house, the winery and the press house, with a well in the middle and a wine cart sitting on its axle by the gate. The winery door hangs open. Something inside is humming.

narrator/4733ebd44cd5cc4a.text: The hut turns its door away from you, the way a cat turns its back. There is no ladder, and the stump is slick as a fish.

narrator/4734a055e365432e.text: You open the cage. The raven comes out onto your arm, and shakes, and all at once there's a skinny boy of ten in its place, naked and blue with cold, holding on to you.

narrator/4736930e01064d33.text: The ticking inside him stops. Then it starts again, a little faster.

narrator/473d22f847b98058.text: On the jetty he coughs up half the lake and lies there laughing and crying at once, which seems fair.

narrator/47576042300db7ad.text: Old halberds, frozen to their rack. The wardens' guards left them here, and the cold has kept them.

narrator/47741998afcfa0a6.text: In the drowned house, on a peg above the waterline, hangs a heavy mantle that the flood never touched. Spells would slide off it like rain.

narrator/478388f75675b417.text: The floorboards ahead sag, grey and spongy. Something has been chewing them from below.

narrator/479139ef86d28d89.text: A stone stair turns up out of sight in the wall. Cold air comes down it, and the sound of wind.

narrator/47963a6ef0b1c2ce.text: Ireena wipes her face with the heel of her hand and stands up, and is herself again, mostly.

narrator/47a91867353f2871.text: He doesn't raise a hand. He looks at Ileana the whole time, and he is still looking at her when he goes down.

narrator/47ab27d3ef4cdf26.text: Hours later he reads the last line of the chapter, and turns the page of nothing, and there is nothing on the other side. He stops.

narrator/47af10dd80ed1937.text: The rocking slows. For the first time since you came in, she looks at you and not past you.

narrator/47d53f9ee2357a3b.text: A dollhouse taller than a child, painted in the same colors as the house around you.

narrator/47f22877639e9c29.text: Their marshal rides forward alone. His horse's ribs and his own have grown together over the years, so you can't tell where one ends.

narrator/47f5674bc9b1e528.text: Where the commander last stood, laid across a pair of empty gauntlets as carefully as an offering, is the thing he kept so that nobody would end the lord of the castle with it.

narrator/480378300043b8ab.text: The left-handed blaze, and the word under it. Thistle doesn't look at it again.

narrator/48055acde5971309.text: Alcoves cut into the walls, each with its relic: a goblin's hand, a knife of human bone, a rat's skull, a frog on a stick, a hag's finger. None of it is worth anything. All of it was precious to someone.

narrator/481b7c850aadf782.text: A watch brazier on a tripod, full of grey ash. It burns, though nobody feeds it, with a pale flame that gives light and no heat at all.

narrator/4827c2313b4c7a5b.text: Rose folds her hands at once, the way she was taught, and Thorn copies her a beat late. Halfway through, they both look up, puzzled, as if they have forgotten the words.

narrator/483742325cc788ce.text: At the foot of the stair stands a cask bigger than the rest, black with age, its hoops brown with rust. The druids' axes have been at every cask in sight but this one.

narrator/4844b06bb1ea8030.text: Every hearth on the floor exhales at once.

narrator/484d64d3368a8760.text: One stone at the foot of the cairn isn't part of it. It is smooth and marbled red and blue, and when you pick it up it leaves your hand to circle your head.

narrator/486cf2e3c027990e.text: A clerk's desk with a groove worn into the floor around it in a half circle: exactly the length of the chain.

narrator/488dc62c87721017.text: Something pale lies folded on the bottom step of the stair.

narrator/488e2b45771fd780.text: You rest among the flour sacks. Overhead, the rocking chair creaks and creaks, and never once stops.

narrator/48aee68b158e97d5.text: What's left of the Order's banners, rotted to grey lace on the house front. The device is still just visible: a silver dragon holding a lamp.

narrator/48b42fadbe1dd13c.text: He serves the rest without a word. Liriel looks at her hands, and then at the fire.

narrator/48b8747b90a33649.text: She doesn't write it down. She doesn't need to; you watch her remember it.

narrator/48c33f50af59f752.text: This crypt has no gate, only a wide arch, and the floor is scored with hoofmarks cut into the stone. It smells of smoke and a stable.

narrator/48ce6db9f83c5d33.text: The boards are off one window. Two cups by the stove, and somebody humming in the back room.

narrator/48d6f8c3c3ea5133.text: She snatches a jar from the shelf and shoves it at you. Something silver turns over inside it, slow as a fish.

narrator/48f0330b241029d6.text: When you look again, the chair is empty.

narrator/48ffcb7b01b0cdd6.text: Ireena looks at the doll on the offering stone for a long time, and doesn't touch it.

narrator/4922c2427b181f7c.text: Low rafters, warm air rising through the floor from the oven, and overhead the great gear of the sails, locked still. It smells of straw and sugar and something kept too long.

narrator/4925818ebf092b00.text: He doesn't answer. He screams, high and thin, like a kettle left on the fire, and behind the storeroom door something heavy shifts inside a crate.

narrator/4937d50561f4afc9.text: Behind the study desk, a panel lifts away. In the hollow sits a velvet box, and in the box a silver brooch, polished recently and never worn.

narrator/494206348ff9152f.text: A pale man with good manners, standing in the dark. Whatever he is underneath, he keeps it buttoned to the throat.

narrator/49471c32739c01fe.text: He pats his robe. He unpins a note, reads it, pins it back. He unpins another.

narrator/494e4d52a24b1b46.text: A wooden peg driven into the rock, and on it an iron key, its bow wrapped in rag. Kiril keeps it where he can see it from his bed.

narrator/49596c6a28bc798e.text: Broken stone and empty plinths. Only the guardians that never moved are still on the parapet.

narrator/497088ad08f072d5.text: Each place has a name card in faded ink. Some names are crossed out and others written in, over and over, on the same cards.

narrator/49965c1b53ed0334.text: Wolves come down the lane from both ends at once, in no hurry, because there's nowhere for you to go.

narrator/49b8f0a9b69bedc2.text: The altar step is only stone again. The dust has a faint warm colour to it still, if you look for it.

narrator/49be4ec67b627847.text: The lid isn't sealed. It's been opened and closed from the inside, many times; the dust on it has handprints.

narrator/49c1a539c3d612bd.text: A chamber hung with skeletons in rusty shackles. In an alcove at the far end stands a painted statue of a pale man in a black cloak, and the soot on the walls behind the skeletons is shaped like people.

narrator/49c2c159ebbcca25.text: For one breath the sweetness drains out of her face, and what's under it is older than the village.

narrator/49c71278acf4cc11.text: Inside the gate the bar leans against the wall, as thick as a man's thigh. The watch fire is kept high. Everyone who passes it puts out their hands to it, the way you'd touch a doorpost for luck.

narrator/49cb01657d89dd57.text: He rides on. Long after the hoofbeats fade, nobody wants to be the first to speak.

narrator/49e40e5e23593fd4.text: Three green moss agates wrapped in a handkerchief, worth about thirty gold to the right buyer.

narrator/49f1c99b24bd3011.text: Dire wolves, five of them, big as ponies, fanning out across the slope ahead. Behind them a man steps out from the trees, smiling, and starts to change.

narrator/49f6aa8c4fafdebd.text: He steps back from the bier. He doesn't look at you. He looks at her.

narrator/4a27cc043ed79663.text: Over each stall, a board with a name painted in a careful hand: Thunder, Brightmane, Old Faithful, Vesper. Under the boards, in the straw, the bones of the horses that answered to them.

narrator/4a5773133c83a8b1.text: The words are big and careful and underlined twice: ALDRIC ASHGROVE RODE FOR HELP. THE DRAGON SENT HIM. HE DID NOT RUN. DO NOT LET VLADIMIR TELL YOU OTHERWISE.

narrator/4a578dd6c70dded1.text: Shapes stand in the square, swaying like washing on a line. They turn toward you all at once.

narrator/4a5e0deddc28da25.text: He sees you looking, and his hand goes to the scarf, and then, slowly, he lets it fall. Under it are two marks, old and new, and more below those.

narrator/4a600e264a374770.text: Wren finds you on watch, which is not where Wren ever wants to be. He sits down, gets up, and sits down again.

narrator/4a663ecbe445448a.text: An old man sits on an upturned cask by the fire with a blanket over his knees: white beard, black eyes, and the bearing of a king who has mislaid his kingdom and expects it returned by supper.

narrator/4a7a3f8c02a0708d.text: A drum of black iron as tall as a horse, wound with chain, and a capstan with four bars worn bright by hands. The chain runs off it into a hole in the north wall, slack, moving very slightly, in and out.

narrator/4a7e42097374f8e1.text: The press house is empty and smells of rot and lamp oil. The great press stands where it always has, waiting for a harvest worth crushing.

narrator/4a7f5aee68e2b8f0.text: The rider rides away without a word. Dobre turns round, and sees you.

narrator/4a89abb90a63dce4.text: A long gallery of statues and portraits of knights. At the far end a narrow door leads into the tower, and the floorboards in front of it are worn pale, from people stopping there and not going through.

narrator/4aa2a3093897534a.text: A cot made up neatly, a lump of charcoal on the pillow, and the blanket worn through at the place where a big man sits every night to read a wall.

narrator/4aa4b5f2c0b30309.text: The head turns back toward the valley. Whatever it was waiting for, it wasn't you.

narrator/4aa8203bb31ee990.text: The chant has become a howl, and under it something heavy is dragging itself toward the stairs.

narrator/4ab9c49f34ac999c.text: The goat path comes round the gorge onto the north shoulder of the mountain, and the snow stops being snow: slush, then mud, then bare black rock that steams. At the top, set into the mountain, an iron gate, and warm air breathing out round it.

narrator/4abe48db6a1859f5.text: Five soldiers in old mail stand at their posts around the guardroom, grey as the stone behind them and a little blurred at the edges, like breath on a cold window. One of them steps out into the middle of the floor. He has sergeant's knots on his shoulder and no colour in him anywhere.

narrator/4af551f11ce07ea4.text: Fen arches in his chains and howls, and the howl breaks halfway and comes out as an old man's yell, and the fur goes, and the length goes out of his arms, and then there's only a skinny, white-stubbled trapper hanging from two rings, sobbing and laughing at once.

narrator/4b00a259922cf72d.text: Torn banners hang on the walls of a soldier's crypt, and a great sarcophagus sits under them like a general at a war table.

narrator/4b01b31a4ec0edb5.text: The chandelier lets go of the ceiling with a sound like a carriage-load of glasses hitting the floor.

narrator/4b1299ee1b0e0bbb.text: He steps back into the dark, and the dark keeps him. Ireena sags against the wall, blinking, herself again.

narrator/4b1f1645dfffb24a.text: The old words, said properly, in a room that has heard only one man's apologies for a very long time. The candle flames lean toward the tomb, and then stand up straight again.

narrator/4b275284c2bfd4fa.text: Plain pews, worn smooth. Somebody has carved small names into the back of each, generations of them, so the dead can still sit with their families.

narrator/4b3aa5890740a2ef.text: The man behind the bar has black hair, black eyes and the stillness of somebody who has been listening to the room since before you came into it.

narrator/4b61f9c95e646bc3.text: Clovin comes up beside you on the wall with a pair of old boots in his hands, soft grey leather, soles worn thin.

narrator/4b640d9192060409.text: Wolf blood dries on your boots. Ahead, two headless stone knights keep a gate that seems to be expecting you.

narrator/4b6842285036afee.text: A kitchen with a cauldron big enough to bathe in, and two small boys underfoot who vanish the moment you look straight at them.

narrator/4b7e2d9902804659.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Tarakamedes, the dragon in the grave. Its faithful went down into the earth to serve it. None came back up."

narrator/4b832db27b86d5b1.text: A stone in the cell wall moves under your fingers. Behind it, a prisoner's hoard: one stoppered healing draught, saved for a day that never came.

narrator/4b8b1d8827562831.text: Bricks fill the doorway where the front door used to be, and the tall window you came out of is half bricked over already. The house is mending itself, slowly, like a scab.

narrator/4b94c8e0ed06e64c.text: A narrow passage, two shoulders wide. The flagstones are worn smooth down the middle by a great many robed feet.

narrator/4b9d626ab408e0db.text: He is still shouting it when the passage turns.

narrator/4ba303794d1ff8f0.text: An old cask, and a great one. If it's hiding anything, it's better at hiding than you are at finding.

narrator/4ba8c913a08b1fb8.text: The portcullis rises before your hand touches it, smooth and quiet, and stays up.

narrator/4bb743bf43e84ef1.text: The lump of grey clay beside the dollhouse altar. It was never clay.

narrator/4bc357464c651fe4.text: A long hall of black stone hung with old banners runs the width of the keep. Tall doors open on a throne room to the north; a study, a trophy room and a clerk's office open off it; the grand stairs come up from below.

narrator/4bc976716ba0b0a2.text: Kip has unrolled a fresh sheet of paper on the log and is writing, very carefully, in his best market-day hand. When you lean over, he lets you look. It's headed PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT.

narrator/4bcb118167caca76.text: The vat's hoops go off like pistol shots, one, two, three.

narrator/4bda2c4726da538a.text: The undergrowth at the roadside stands up and walks. Behind it, two figures in bark-dyed robes are chanting, and the trees are listening.

narrator/4bdd717cd6790b00.text: Behind the chapel altar, a small silver reliquary in the shape of a dragon's claw. Inside lies a holy amulet, its chain still bright after four hundred years.

narrator/4befb82ac6a68e78.text: You tell him about a toymaker in Vallaki with a jester's cap and a monkey and no customers, who has wanted to meet him all his life.

narrator/4bf6d9164f928597.text: You bar the door and wait while the fire burns down to embers. Then, all at once, every board on every window begins to creak.

narrator/4bfef629b8e8af0d.text: An old well with a rope, a pulley and a bucket on a hook. Something down there is breathing in time with you.

narrator/4c125f9521d763a8.text: A thick ledger lies open on the table, a pen laid across the page.

narrator/4c2ef2b0f498af34.text: The salt goes in, a lot of it. Too much, maybe. The carcass is grey round the cuts and smells of the grave over the goat. You drag it along anyway.

narrator/4c38d68271095d2b.text: That night every window in the castle is lit, and music drifts down into the valley. Nobody in Barovia sleeps.

narrator/4c485228df6b74c1.text: You make the archway as the heap rises behind you, wet and enormous, its tendrils closing on the place where you stood a moment ago.

narrator/4c4854d32e72ca80.text: Grey light pours through the broken gate: men-at-arms, translucent, shields up, charging a line that broke four hundred years ago. You are standing where the line was.

narrator/4c5146ecb7728c73.text: Sergiu. My first. The siege winter, the thing at the window asked to come in, and he let it. He came back to us hungry. I could not do what had to be done. God forgive me, I could not. I have bricked him in with the garlic and his dog will not leave the wall.

narrator/4c5f9a20cb46c3c5.text: A round hall where the aisles meet. Names are cut into every inch of the walls, hundreds of them, and in its west side a stair of black stone goes down.

narrator/4c674316529d937b.text: Old pews of black wood. On one of them, the dust has been disturbed where someone sat recently.

narrator/4c6c7eaa8f27f949.text: The vault is long enough for a church, and it needs to be. Along the middle, on a raised stone bier, lies a skeleton with folded wings, as long as a ship, its neck ending in nothing.

narrator/4c6f43d633401fb6.text: A dais of new planks, painted yellow, with a carpet nailed down at the front where the Baron stands. The carpet is worn through in one spot, from turning to face the crowd.

narrator/4c70349074221c51.text: Water running downhill out of the slush, warm as a bath. Steam lies on it like breath on a window.

narrator/4c7293f5e0a5c8e3.text: A letter on the desk, in a big, generous hand that goes small and shaky by the last lines. It was never sent, and never finished.

narrator/4c780bc4ecf59399.text: A rotten jetty with half its planks gone. At the end, a mooring post, and a fresh rope tied to it with nothing on the other end.

narrator/4c7a909fd79cecac.text: Krezk laughs. Properly, the whole square, the kind of laugh that has been kept in a cellar for years. Children laugh because their parents are laughing. A goat leaves.

narrator/4cb718e19cd7ab3d.text: A long hall walled with skulls. Down the middle runs a table of bones with chairs of bones beside it, and over it a lamp of skulls burns green.

narrator/4cbc6b960165e89c.text: A statue of a young woman in white stone, standing on the only dry ground in Berez. The grass around her feet has been cut short, recently and with care. Nothing else here has been cared for in years.

narrator/4ccb05e1772e5764.text: She puts the crossbow down, which she hasn't done since you arrived.

narrator/4cd403bd45d9e1ae.text: The bottom drops away under you and you go in over your head. You come up spluttering, with the bow rope somehow in your fist, and tow her in while she watches with polite interest.

narrator/4ce548441a6a09f6.text: The mongrelfolk curls up small in a corner, a goat's ear folded down over a child's hand, and whimpers. 'Not the cells,' it says. 'Please. Not back in the cells.'

narrator/4ced36044a5d030d.text: The town square is swept, garlanded and full of people pretending to be in no hurry. In the middle stands a wooden dais, a pair of stocks, and a great wicker sun on a pole, as tall as a house and painted a desperate yellow.

narrator/4d012816fd2b23f8.text: A drum of black chain and a crank as long as a spear, and through the murder holes in the floor, the top of the portcullis, waiting.

narrator/4d114a52b29148b3.text: Grey stone, fitted without mortar by people long dead, three men high. Here and there are marks scored deep into the stones from outside, at about the height of a big dog standing on its hind legs.

narrator/4d193a23b404e9e4.text: You sleep by a fire that someone has lit with far too much magic. Your host stays up all night writing, and swears at his own handwriting.

narrator/4d208998d1805bd1.text: When the candles below it gutter, a thin line of light shows round its edge from behind, as if there were a second sun back there, smaller and closer.

narrator/4d227681650eb061.text: A board of servants' bells, one for every room upstairs, each with a painted label. As you watch, the bell marked Dining Hall twitches once.

narrator/4d57c46cf391c13c.text: A small wooden shrine at the water's edge, with candle stubs on its shelf and coins pressed into the wax. The candles face away from the pool.

narrator/4d728b8fa414580b.text: The house is silent in a new way: not the hush of something listening, but the hush after a long day's work is done.

narrator/4d7556af3fcb8cbc.text: A long nave of pews under a sunburst window, an altar on its step, a vestry and a narrow stair down to the crypt where St. Andral's sarcophagus waits.

narrator/4d8458d2c25c782e.text: In the ditch beside the road lies a peddler's pack with its straps torn through. No peddler. A long smear in the mud leads off into the trees, and stops.

narrator/4d8c194f72eacbcb.text: She says her own name under her breath, the way she did at the falls. Ireena. Then again, louder.

narrator/4d9f3007a2334d74.text: Davian takes the stone in both hands. Green light comes up between his fingers, the way sun comes through a leaf.

narrator/4da47e941ad1317f.text: Among the tokens left for the drowned, one is a pearl, and it hums against your palm like a held note.

narrator/4da7ed44ac9804b4.text: The winged figures at the corners of the slab unfold, stone grinding on stone, and drop to the floor.

narrator/4de04d32d0bd7aee.text: Inside the ring the ground is warm, like the flank of a sleeping animal, and every step you take is answered from somewhere deep under your feet.

narrator/4de1ad5626ad349a.text: The shutters are barred, but a candle burns behind them. When you look closer, it goes out.

narrator/4df035d7d63f0e77.text: The road at night: open fields, low walls, and a sky without a single star. Anything could cross those fields, and something is.

narrator/4df8f7beac537d6a.text: The buckets go down. The servants go back the way they came, a good deal faster. The sun sleeps dry.

narrator/4e06536ca42b5043.text: At her name her ears, if she had a cat's ears, would go flat. She opens her mouth, and what comes out is a long, low, perfectly made yowl.

narrator/4e15a0921c57e75c.text: A skeleton in shackles against the wall, in the remains of a keeper's hood. Whatever he did wrong, the others made sure he went on paying for it.

narrator/4e206610104fb170.text: Every eye in the square that isn't on the Baron is on you: the armed strangers. Whatever you do now, Vallaki will remember it.

narrator/4e22711e04f33867.text: The blow lands like a verdict.

narrator/4e2ed638f9e6452c.text: Four roads meet here, and none of them looks as if it wants you on it.

narrator/4e67e82948414448.text: He nods without looking up and opens his spellbook to a page he obviously isn't reading.

narrator/4e6b4c52db96ad12.text: The skull lamp tips on its chain and pours green fire across the chairs.

narrator/4e7699c13e0afc46.text: A small stone with a name on it, like the rest, and frost in the letters.

narrator/4e8ce49d1ee002b6.text: A wide stone hearth, cold and swept clean. Set into its back wall, where a cookpot ought to hang, is a rod of green copper as thick as a thumb, running straight up into the chimney.

narrator/4e8dc93aad40f557.text: Racks of casks run off into the dark, and bottles are racked to the ceiling behind them. The air is cold and smells of old grapes and older stone.

narrator/4e9103136ee5eefc.text: 'A body for the lord in the castle,' he says, 'a giant of earth and thorn on Yester Hill. It needs a heart. The stone from your vintner's vines is that heart. When the chant is finished, it walks.'

narrator/4e923189ded9d6bb.text: Three druids stand among heaps of dead brush that were blights until the tree on the hill burned. They have had a bad week, and they mean to share it.

narrator/4ea95a2e86f94264.text: The house is emptier without the coffin in it. Somehow the boards on the windows look less sure of themselves.

narrator/4eeb24fcd23813a0.text: A wall of trophies: a shepherd's crook, a hunter's cap, a Vistani boot with a fine buckle, a child's bonnet. The boot has a knife slash across the ankle and a dark stain down to the heel.

narrator/4ef2cf2e30deb5c9.text: The wall comes down into a short stair and a small dark room, and out of the dark comes a smell like a cellar full of old meat, and a thin grey young man with a burgomaster's jaw, who used to be somebody's son.

narrator/4ef9c8890c0aeb27.text: She unclasps the little sunburst she has worn since her first vows and presses it into the hand of whoever is nearest. It is still faintly gold, as if it had kept a little of the morning back for later.

narrator/4f06fef17c2362a7.text: He is not there any more. Out in the east, a long way off, something made of timber begins to scream.

narrator/4f0a6718ad3506a1.text: Bones, and the long white streaks of something enormous. You don't stay to look harder.

narrator/4f0e631f1c091ad9.text: Godrick sits down on the floor beside the old knight, and for a while neither of them says anything, and it is the most natural thing in the world.

narrator/4f10069cc727e07a.text: In the scree at the crag's edge, a little brass bell on a broken strap, the kind tied round a goat's neck, or a child's wrist.

narrator/4f1a295094c67b75.text: For a mile a grey wolf keeps pace with you just inside the treeline, never closer, never farther, never looking anywhere but at you. When the road bends, it is simply gone.

narrator/4f1bfc6f987f069c.text: The pool lies still as glass. Ireena has stopped walking. She hasn't noticed she's stopped.

narrator/4f2df2b5502af083.text: Nothing you can name. Only the feeling, as you stand over the pile, that the wood is paying attention to you.

narrator/4f34a843d6b7e5f6.text: Your blade goes through him like a hand through fog, and the fog is cold enough to ache.

narrator/4f3dee4288096075.text: Then Blinsky goes up the narrow stair to his workshop to fetch his best puppet, talking all the way, and Pidlwick goes very still at the bottom of the stair, looking up at the back of him.

narrator/4f3fcd7b86a6dcc9.text: The sigil under your foot wakes with a crack, and blue light jumps up your legs.

narrator/4f492a363b52882d.text: A landing at the head of the great stair. North, the dragon's study, its shelves half burned; west, a dormitory of beds nobody sleeps in; east, a long gallery of statues ending at the tower door. Two smaller rooms south: one bare, one covered in writing.

narrator/4f683f28f3b42a8d.text: Somewhere ahead, under the black water, a bell rings. Once, then again, slow, the way a chapel bell rings for a burial. There is no wind. There is no chapel.

narrator/4f720962f76b7426.text: She digs a new crow feather out of her hair, where she apparently keeps a few, and presses it into the cut next to the old one.

narrator/4fa13955385ddf18.text: A knight in dented plate waits on the broken front steps with his helmet under his arm. His face is grey and quite plainly dead, and he is doing his best to smile with it.

narrator/4faa2e6dabe937ab.text: Sir Godrick doesn't polish anything tonight. He sits with the ladle in both hands and looks at it a long while.

narrator/4fc1ccad6475d756.text: A spinning wheel, turning. The thread's coming on again, fine and even.

narrator/4fdd50d69a7af1b5.text: A small frightened boy who smells of goat. That's all you can tell.

narrator/4fed16f4ba8b8522.text: The quiet lasts a breath; then the hasty grave shifts, and every old grave around it answers. Unblessed earth, it seems, is an open door.

narrator/4ff03eb8e61e6ed2.text: It isn't your finest work, but it's warm, and Krezk hasn't had warm in a long time. By the end two children are sitting at the front, and their mother hasn't pulled them back.

narrator/50625ad13e169daf.text: 'The Baron's chair,' he whispers. 'She says the lord on the hill will give the town to the ones who stayed loyal. No more festivals. No more being told to be happy.'

narrator/5063512620f16f9f.text: Thistle doesn't say anything at all, which is the loudest thing she's done all night.

narrator/50672f83980e2a02.text: You break a seal stamped with a pointed hat. Somewhere, you hope, a wizard is not keeping count.

narrator/5074d421f1ba5009.text: Among the reeds, half sunk in the mud: a little leather bag of bone dice, and among them a smooth grey stone that is always warm. Somebody lost a game here, which is strange, carrying that.

narrator/507aa298f8797dc5.text: Ratatoille has drawn three circles in the dirt with a stick and is standing in the middle one, looking very pleased with himself.

narrator/507f854e27b1bc40.text: Low beams, a smoking hearth, a dozen tables and four drinkers. At the corner table, three women in bright skirts are laughing, which in this village is practically a crime.

narrator/5086a0e8e664d556.text: You sleep in turns on the dry end of the causeway. The marsh is full of small noises, and for once none of them are about you.

narrator/50b8f4be8fd1151c.text: Hedda is washing her hands in a pot of cold water, and has been for some time. They are very clean.

narrator/50c559062ee02ff6.text: Under the velvet he's sweating. He believes every word, and the belief is the only thing holding him upright. He is not a cruel man by nature; he is a frightened one, and he has found that cruelty is quicker.

narrator/50e84b02602528df.text: Soot on the plinth, old and greasy, in a long black smear like a lick from a tongue. The dark up here came in after the light went out, and made itself at home.

narrator/50ea768be7610c44.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Savnok, the locked mouth. Its keepers never told us what it wanted. They couldn't."

narrator/5107e81e9024d6b1.text: "Petitioner: Strahd, son of Barov, a prince of the western wars. He asks to stay young for as long as he wants anything, and to keep whatever he has taken. Brought before the one whose name we do not write."

narrator/5114a26cd0c0afd3.text: A deep well with a wooden lid. Someone has scratched a word into the lid, over and over, in a child's hand: HOME.

narrator/511598f490baccc4.text: He is out. Somewhere far above you it is night, and the night is his.

narrator/51229ba084fcf636.text: Ireena does not come down the road with you. You do not look back to see who stands beside her at the gate.

narrator/512381ef6446e897.text: Rings, pins and a lady's hair comb, every one of them old-fashioned and every one of them small.

narrator/516aee12be1811ac.text: Brick. Where the front door stood, there is only brick, still warm, still settling.

narrator/517b6692dc1eb072.text: Inside a ring of standing stones stands a tree with bark like a burnt hand. Beside it lies a man of earth and timber forty feet long, cloaked, with a face you have seen before.

narrator/517b87d606398d28.text: The chair by the fire is not empty. You would swear it was a moment ago.

narrator/51814c7e74c6118c.text: The spellbook is laid out like a cookery book. Every spell has its ingredients listed down the margin, its method numbered, and a note at the bottom headed "Serving suggestion". Fireball's says: "Do not serve indoors."

narrator/51876194037e998f.text: Grey coats on the backs of the chairs, a little bird on every shoulder. Every one has a number now.

narrator/51cb3f6a2ec24827.text: The words come out wrong, or the ice doesn't care for them. The lamp burns on.

narrator/51e7c3cb32d54a60.text: The drawer is shallower than the table. Under its false bottom lies a slim gold circlet set with a red stone, warm as a coal and twice as dangerous.

narrator/51fc34064ab97077.text: One old bird shrieks, and the shriek runs down the beams like a rumour. They know you. Ravens talk.

narrator/520ad1dbd58d1450.text: Izek lies at the foot of the dais. The fire in his arm goes out last.

narrator/52114cef993c0fcc.text: The shelf of snow before the temple doors is littered with amber, broken into pieces the size of shields. Neither colossus is watching now.

narrator/523dfed120249bbc.text: It takes the crust, considers it, and then, quite unmistakably, nods. It flies off west toward the vineyards beyond Vallaki, and circles back twice to make sure you saw which way.

narrator/524072115262469a.text: The floor gives way to the knee.

narrator/5247bdef26f86f03.text: The pole gate at the back of the den creaks open. A girl of about ten comes out first, holding a much smaller girl's hand, and three more children behind her in a line.

narrator/524b3ae9bc1c31bb.text: A narrow bedroom with a crucifix nailed over the bed and another nailed over the door, facing the storeroom.

narrator/52582eceb6a9ba75.text: Thistle sleeps outside the firelight tonight, on her own, with her back to you. It's the first time she hasn't slept within arm's reach of somebody.

narrator/525f255b95b0e434.text: A woman in a patched wool coat straightens up from a patch of purple flowers by the cave mouth, a knife in one hand and a fistful of stalks in the other. Her eyes catch what little light there is, the way a dog's do.

narrator/525fccda6efcfbe4.text: From the cavern below, a long breath in, like a forge's bellows, held.

narrator/5268322f387fef10.text: Kneading tables, cooling racks, and an oven big enough to walk into. There are no small shoes by the door. You check.

narrator/52690f3077f35df6.text: Iron gates on both sides, two rows of them. Behind some, nothing. Behind others, something breathing.

narrator/5277973ef0bbbc9a.text: And it is still tied to this place, by a thread as fine as hair that runs out of the mountain and down into the valley.

narrator/527f2ea6c325aa92.text: A plain iron strongbox, unlocked. The man who owns it trusts the room more than any lock.

narrator/5298c551900c2cd7.text: An elegant hall lit by oil lamps: a hearth with the family portrait over the mantel, and two suits of wolf-helmed armor standing guard by the library door, spears grounded.

narrator/52b7ef8fcb1fc492.text: The Abbot isn't looking at his bride. He's looking past her. At Ireena.

narrator/52bc578df9d7e173.text: He whistles once, as a man calls a dog, and the wolves go back into the trees with him.

narrator/52cb2b058dd8bc96.text: The altar is dressed in white again, and candles burn along its step in a row as neat as teeth.

narrator/52f6009ba3911963.text: Under the narrow bed, a little box of carved pine. Inside, on a bed of wool, a dusty rose stone that drifts up out of your palm and circles your head.

narrator/52fc5e6f1ff123ca.text: You walk her down to the village in the grey before morning. Goodwife Sarnov is on her step, waiting for nothing, the way she has waited every morning for twelve years.

narrator/5318f69d917310b0.text: Then the branches unfold, and the two in the good coats drop out of the pine like dropped coats, and land on their feet.

narrator/532329786bcad382.text: The hearth looks like a hearth. If anyone hid anything in it, they did it well, and they did it a long time ago.

narrator/532d6759ee6df59a.text: Hot skin, a racing pulse, a cough that rattles. You've seen fevers break, and you've seen them not. You can't tell which this is.

narrator/533397035e060b4b.text: Under the heap of offerings lies a staff of black wood capped in iron, left by someone who wanted something more than power. The amber took it anyway.

narrator/534064a5c254e7bb.text: These aren't the Martikovs' vines any more. Something has grown up into every rootstock in the row and is wearing the vines like sleeves. The wood under the bark is black and wet, and it's warm.

narrator/534800187ba6d7c0.text: Thistle does it quickly, with her knife, the way he taught her, and he is looking at her the whole time, and he isn't afraid.

narrator/53563f8cadb45661.text: The hut lies broken across its own roots, door open, shutters gone. It smells of cold soup and rot, and for the first time it isn't breathing.

narrator/535751c9dd57149c.text: He drops the slate. He picks it up, writes, rubs it out, and writes again.

narrator/53683852c36ac95a.text: Ireena has gone very still. Her hand has found her own sleeve and is gripping it hard.

narrator/5369414a64275f70.text: You sleep in shifts with your backs to the wall. The organ plays, very softly, until dawn.

narrator/536ceb68fbc5d4f7.text: An old woman in a flour-dusted shawl leans on a handcart heaped with glazed pastries under a cloth. Her smile arrives well before she does.

narrator/536fabfe71b7b18e.text: The cellar stair goes down into the right kind of cold, the kind that smells of oak and old wine. From somewhere at the far end comes a sound of scraping.

narrator/5373f274f9ededdf.text: A ring of good chairs, facing inward. The cushions are worn, but there isn't a book on any of them, and the candle stubs on the side tables are black ones.

narrator/537e225bccdebee0.text: Two stairs go down from here. One stops at the dungeon. The other keeps going, worn into a trough, toward the crypts and the cold.

narrator/538a8eaa5aee6f48.text: A young man in armour, carved from black stone, with a sword in his hand and a face full of plans. It is the only likeness under the castle that shows him smiling.

narrator/538aa1dfd23d447d.text: You knock. The tower considers the question and declines to answer.

narrator/5390b594a2d6de51.text: The end sounds wrong when you knock: higher, emptier, a door rather than a wall. The third hoop down turns a quarter-inch further than any hoop should.

narrator/5398ed9e5103d272.text: You step back. The drowned walk past you as if you were posts. They take Bluto at the end of the jetty; he doesn't fight them, in the end. They go down into the black water together, all of them, and the bell rings once, very loud.

narrator/53a5146745ce54cb.text: Little cots with names scratched on the frames: Ana, Tomas, the twins, Little Bird. On one, under the name, a smaller hand has added: I WAS HERE.

narrator/53a79dbb88e6834c.text: The vat bursts its hoops. What rises out of it is the winery's last harvest: skins, stems and rot, heaped into something the height of a man and still growing.

narrator/53afcc01adb17211.text: The cabinet glass is clean enough to show your face. The crossbows inside are oiled, as if the hunt is tomorrow.

narrator/53b4b2491e05ae8e.text: Wren does five minutes on Krezk's gate, and the goats, and the watchman's hat, and by the end someone at the back has laughed and been elbowed for it, and someone else has laughed at the elbowing.

narrator/53cd6950ddd86143.text: The last wine cart, loaded and never sent, sitting on its broken axle by the gate. The casks have been stove in. The druids made very sure nobody in the valley got a drink.

narrator/53d71843c4a821f9.text: A little man in motley and a cap of bells, painted laughing, with a child on each knee. A brass plate on the frame reads: PIDLWICK, FOOL TO THE HOUSE. Someone has scratched the eyes out of the frame's carved cherubs.

narrator/53ebe61f4cdf92f1.text: The frost on the window holds the shape of a long, patient head. When you look straight at it, it is only frost.

narrator/53ef5d3333426ca9.text: Rahadin sighs, the way a steward sighs at a stain, and draws a curved blade. The screaming around him grows louder.

narrator/53fa43a0fb4218ea.text: A spinning wheel with the wool still on it, stopped halfway through a thread a month ago.

narrator/541ee25f1a946b52.text: Not scratches: letters, cut with a fingernail or a tooth, over and over until they were deep enough to last. I SENT HIM. I TOLD HIM FLY. TELL FATHER. E.

narrator/542aef7cba0e4f65.text: They're gone into the rain. This time there's no crashing and no swearing. It goes very quiet out there for a long while.

narrator/543154c5c0b96afa.text: A hall of portraits and boarded windows, a staircase climbing into the dark. Somebody has nailed a plank across the front door from inside, and another, and another.

narrator/5439eced42a90075.text: East along the road a carriage lamp swings out of the mist. No horse snorts. No wheel creaks. Along the fences, every wolf in the valley has stopped howling at once.

narrator/54449fd83a579b03.text: Adrian is waiting by his father's chair when you come in, black sap on his cuffs, and doesn't look up.

narrator/546a2785820c19aa.text: Godrick takes his bedroll to the far side of the fire tonight and sits on it with his back very straight, and doesn't laugh at anything.

narrator/546b1d26c3e312cb.text: The druids pried up half the floor looking for something. Under the last board they didn't lift lies an emerald with a little green storm turning inside it.

narrator/547fa6d0291629bf.text: She sets the bowl down very carefully, and pushes it away with one finger.

narrator/5495e32c1343352e.text: Hedda doesn't pray tonight. She sits with the Holy Symbol of Ravenkind in both hands, the silver raven and its sunburst, and doesn't say anything for a long time.

narrator/54a45ffac723b4d5.text: One coin at the edge of the heap has a scratch across it, from a claw, maybe. Under the gold the scratch is dull grey. The next one too. The cup beside it has a dent, and the dent is grey.

narrator/54a7da7abc61600e.text: The organ stops in the middle of a phrase. The man at the keys closes the lid, gently, and turns on the bench.

narrator/54bbbb2ba8925f20.text: The watch hauls them off toward the stocks in the square, where the Baron's justice is very public and very cheerful. A watchman tips his helmet and pays the bounty.

narrator/54c0cd478e1e86cf.text: The palisade's south-east corner: a watch fire, a squat log lockup with one barred window, and a walkway where the watch can look out over the dark and see nothing at all.

narrator/54c0f5a548705101.text: Most of them are on the eldest's stone. The name on it is SORIN, and the dates make him nine.

narrator/54ea8df797ae35fd.text: It takes most of the watch. It's mostly the K in "knight", which he takes personally.

narrator/54ecddae11b6864c.text: Strahd turns his eyes on Ismark. Nothing more. Ismark's hand flies to his throat, and he goes down on his knees in the grave dirt, mouth working, blood running from his nose into his beard.

narrator/550aa93d1b5e8502.text: He keeps going. Three more about the Abbot. The square gets smaller somehow, people drawing in on themselves, and a woman near the shrine makes the sign against the evil eye, not at Clovin.

narrator/550f9e74e7c82617.text: Nobody sleeps. Somebody keeps humming, very quietly, and nobody admits to it.

narrator/552ff003b304e947.text: The stair is worn hollow in the middle by three hundred years of the same feet. Or so it feels. The creaking above you stops while you climb, and starts again when you stop.

narrator/55304d9a2d381c39.text: He bows to her, and to each of you, and is gone between the trees before the sun clears them. Ileana watches the treeline until it is full light.

narrator/5536bee6b7d6c243.text: You bring him down off the hill trail and in through the Blue Water Inn's kitchen door after dark, the way the Keepers do things.

narrator/553a3e5dfb8d0d41.text: You read him Markovia's letter, kneeling there, every word. He listens with his eyes shut.

narrator/554b1181672e9437.text: The burgomaster's grave is the only neat thing in the churchyard. Somebody has already left a candle on it.

narrator/55590faf2ffba83b.text: The little red-haired doll turns slowly on its thread in the heat from the hearth.

narrator/555c29b52baf3527.text: He gets up. He's an old man, and it takes a while. He goes to where his son is working, and they stand there, two men with the same black eyes, and neither of them is any good at this.

narrator/5575b287a638bb52.text: The rug lies in rags. Lief stares at it, then at you, then at the shackle, which opens easily now that nothing is watching it.

narrator/557e766009c5936e.text: Only clean flagstones now, as if the frost was waiting for a reason to leave.

narrator/558f60ad156b7366.text: The hedge on both sides of the road stands up and walks toward you, rustling.

narrator/55b191e409c7b08b.text: Little houses on wheels, carved and painted and hung with bells. Every door is shut. Every window has someone behind it.

narrator/55b68893ff43d0c3.text: Upstairs, the rocking stops for a moment, then starts again.

narrator/55d7d0f9683c45f4.text: The names of everyone who ever served the house, cut small, hundreds of them. The newest are near the floor, and some of them are only a few years old.

narrator/56097c4b87f16c71.text: Dolls with their eyes picked out, ranged along a shelf to watch the coffin. Someone has drawn smiles on all of them in red.

narrator/5619c62c20150401.text: You sleep in shifts, and whoever has the watch keeps one eye on Ireena's window. Twice in the night something taps on the glass, and nobody answers.

narrator/5620b2b31ccd220b.text: She comes out of the trees: twice a man's height, blue-grey and bent, with iron teeth and iron nails and a basket on her arm the size of a cradle. Grey dogs as big as ponies come with her.

narrator/563345b36109f9e7.text: You say what you can about a man you never met: that he held his door every night until his heart gave out. It's short, and Ismark nods as if it were the right length.

narrator/56369477aa0afe22.text: Rays. A sun. Gilt. If it means more, it's keeping the meaning to itself.

narrator/5651bac258f4c17b.text: Out in the east, a shutter bangs. A scream comes across the reeds, thin and rising, the scream of someone who has seen a light where no light should be.

narrator/566a46f76160cc07.text: For a moment you think he won't answer. Then he looks at the stair, as if he can see through it.

narrator/56700d61df99698c.text: A row of ravens on the ridge of the roof, all facing you. One of them tips its head as if it has a question.

narrator/567d91e4f370263c.text: He bounces off a will like a bird off a window and sits down hard, wailing. Rose holds him and glares at you over his head.

narrator/568d592c7801f70a.text: A row of narrow shops with painted signs. In the toymaker's window, a hundred wooden faces watch the street with perfect patience.

narrator/56bb079503853379.text: A full-length mirror in a carved frame. Cold air breathes along one edge of it, and the room behind you in the glass is a little darker than the room you're in.

narrator/56bbed44435e24fe.text: The weapons in the hall hang crooked on their hooks, trembling. The paneling creaks like something drawing breath to shout.

narrator/56d21fe4d7aebc74.text: Silver light comes down the stair from above, lying on every step like snow.

narrator/56e019003bf9420b.text: Ireena stands at the foot of the bier and doesn't move. The girl on it has her face, too.

narrator/56e1d793153ff9f6.text: The ring groans and holds. The chain rattles loud enough to wake the whole hill, and somewhere in the dark, something stirs in its straw and settles again.

narrator/56ea385c404ec7f7.text: Alabaster dancers stand along the mantel, caught mid-turn, every one of them facing the harpsichord.

narrator/56eef9f6fcbb1fe0.text: A wide wooden vat for treading grapes, stained purple to the brim with a hundred harvests. Something has been nesting in it.

narrator/5708f05c0f85ec94.text: Offalia is still snoring on the bakery floor. Whatever you mean to do about her, do it first.

narrator/570a7bfbf9099aca.text: Under the candle stubs in the offering box, someone left a scroll tied with white ribbon, its words written in a hand that shakes with fear and faith together.

narrator/570d0c42c822ffa8.text: Somebody starts pulling down the bunting. Somebody else starts taking the stocks apart, slat by slat, for firewood. Nobody tells anybody to smile.

narrator/5712891307814f10.text: They are quiet. They sit at opposite ends of the log for the rest of the night and don't look at each other once, which is somehow worse.

narrator/5726bebe272e5ddf.text: Vladimir is down on one knee among the scattered chairs. The wounds you gave him are already closing, slowly, with a sound like ice forming on a pond. He does not get up.

narrator/572ad463bb2bdd3b.text: St. Andral's stands on its rise at the north-east corner of the town, its bell tower leaning very slightly toward the castle, as if listening. Gravestones crowd its yard, and a fresh grave is being dug beside them.

narrator/572ec03348adf5bc.text: Ratatoille sits down, quite suddenly, on the nearest cask.

narrator/5738943940b4b918.text: The wall of Krezk is a darker dark against the mountain. There are lamps on the wall-walk, and every one of them is turned outward, toward you.

narrator/574091a3f814bc27.text: Scratches in rows of five on the inside of a cage bar, made with a fingernail. Two full rows and one more. Under them, smaller, a single scratch on its own, scratched out.

narrator/574c9c67f93aa8b9.text: Steel rings off amber. The colossus considers the scratch, and then it considers you.

narrator/57706731a8efb054.text: In the ashes under the witches' cauldron, a wand of blackened bone. Holding it, you feel your own heartbeat quicken, as if something behind you just breathed.

narrator/5777a4aa4c0b9779.text: The lock gives. Inside, someone small says: Mother?

narrator/57857f5c8e31b3b7.text: Two cages hang from the rafters on chains, each big enough for a child to sit in if the child doesn't stretch. There are scratches on one of the bars, in neat rows.

narrator/579155e14797465f.text: Ireena's face changes. Not fear. Something worse, and softer: recognition, coming up through her like a drowned thing finding the surface.

narrator/57957e14ae690bd0.text: You tell her. She listens without moving, and when you're done she lets out a long breath, as if she has been holding it for twelve years.

narrator/5796e0852a6e48b5.text: He steps back into the wall and is gone, and the doorway is only a doorway.

narrator/579c4b18b881659a.text: There's nothing in the hat but a goat's tooth, until Pavel empties his own pockets into it, and then Rodica from the well does, and then her neighbour.

narrator/57b2f7882a142a27.text: The fermenting hall is quiet. The mash in the vats has gone still and grey, like porridge nobody wanted.

narrator/57d257a862c4136a.text: Rations, torches, four gold pieces knotted in a sock. And a letter, half written, that begins: the road is safer than they say, my love, and stops there.

narrator/57e731d7a2460ee4.text: You watch him. He watches you watching, smiles, and you learn nothing at all.

narrator/57f113e0ecb4169f.text: You sleep in shifts with your backs to a crypt wall. Twice in the night a gate along the row opens and shuts, and nobody goes to see why.

narrator/57f30ac3ecc9fb6b.text: You sleep on warm rock under a cold sky, which is a strange thing. All night, through the stone, something breathes: in, and out, and in.

narrator/5822195a6337f430.text: For a moment the pretty face forgets to be pretty. Then it remembers, and smiles, and that is worse.

narrator/582e99ae26ce4cbd.text: Quiet, again. The house is already thinking about what to try next.

narrator/5837587f0189aa1a.text: Pipes, pedals and stops, all dusty, all silent. Whatever the organ hides, it keeps to itself.

narrator/58386217d34a3616.text: A yard of dead hedges and churned mud inside an iron fence. The mud holds paw prints the size of dinner plates, all of them pointed at the house.

narrator/5850eed2bcbdcfac.text: The vault is quiet now. Somewhere in the stone, very faintly, a sentry is still saying the challenge to nobody.

narrator/586d4e6f4ea722f1.text: A small square door with a brass button beside it. Behind it, ropes run up and down a shaft from the kitchen to the master's bedroom.

narrator/58743d89b382a3d5.text: No wound, no bruise, no poison's colour in the lips. Only, above her heart, a single red scratch, fine as a bramble's, that has never healed in all this time.
