narrator/587d609fdc442afd.text: The upper floor creaks under your weight, a long low complaint that travels ahead of you down the hall.

narrator/589903fe9b4c35f6.text: Fen's blaze, three notches and Thistle's fresh crow feather, still bright in the grey.

narrator/589aeecf75e5f89b.text: The glass holds one heartbeat too long. Behind you, the dining room's silver lifts off the sideboard with a sound like a breath let out.

narrator/58a058078b1db4a1.text: In the mud, the marks of a man's boots going down to the water, and between them a long smear where something was dragged, small and kicking.

narrator/58d29b4629e21110.text: The prayer catches on the brand like a match in lamp oil. Steaua screams, and the white flare runs out from the mark over her whole body and leaves it black.

narrator/58dddfd056704eae.text: Kasimir has stopped walking. He stands in the archway with his hands at his sides, as if he has forgotten what they are for.

narrator/58f0607f9b42aeaa.text: Things that were people once come scuttling from behind the sarcophagi, each with one great eye where a face should be. Two of the wardens' dead drift up through the floor behind them.

narrator/58fa3181c45fdfff.text: Scorched at the corners. The same small hand.

narrator/58fd132c86d97ed4.text: A reading table stacked with books on contracts, oaths and wagers, each one bristling with neat paper markers. The cup beside them is still steaming, though nobody has touched it.

narrator/5904290c1c3049d0.text: The cart stands where it stood, before the gate, its cage open and empty, and the gate breathing.

narrator/591ce0003712b098.text: Her hands are shaking too badly to hold a spell. She is not going to fight anybody. She is going to sit in the mud until it rises.

narrator/59206de75af0ce9f.text: Inside lies a heavy book bound in black leather, clasped in tarnished silver. Nobody wants to be the first to touch it.

narrator/5936a4f295326852.text: At the words "sent to keep", something old moves in his face, like a sleeper hearing his name in another room.

narrator/594052143dd02629.text: You say the words. When you look back from the next bend, the snow has covered them over gently, like a sheet drawn up by someone who loved them.

narrator/5949c8b8ed7e283d.text: The biggest house in Berez, and the only one with stone walls, which only means it took longer to fall. The burgomaster's chair is still at the head of a table under two feet of silt.

narrator/595a54119d026c87.text: Coins, teeth, a child's shoe, candle stubs. The wolves bring her what they value, and some of it is very strange.

narrator/595e75bbeb35fc1a.text: The gallery floor gives way with a long tearing groan, and the dark underneath comes up to meet you.

narrator/59633b1549e39ac5.text: Under the pines at night the road is a pale stripe in the black. Your lantern makes a small room of light, and the forest leans in to look.

narrator/5976b6e9cdce0c21.text: A handcart comes squeaking round the bend, heaped high under a white cloth, and behind it, pushing, a little old woman in a flour-dusted shawl.

narrator/5995d1a37859b9f0.text: The lower gallery is older than the rest. At its west end a narrower stair goes down again, into stone the colour of bone.

narrator/599cc26f59566346.text: The stand is empty, and this time it will stay that way.

narrator/59aa6116c6ee6a5b.text: You knock on it. It answers hollow, like a door with nobody home, and the bung comes away in your hand.

narrator/59aa8b0d89fc5d5f.text: The lockup warden spreads his hands. The lockup's empty, he calls, and somehow does not sound sorry.

narrator/59b4ad5e20f8df9d.text: The chest is empty now, except for a wooden horse with one ear and a faint smell of lavender.

narrator/59c0453dc3efad37.text: Shapes uncurl from the straw along the walls, and the cave is suddenly full of yellow eyes. Nobody told them you were coming. They are taking it personally.

narrator/59c7bff8786197e2.text: At the shrine, a woman in a patched coat is relighting candles that your fight has blown out. She does not turn round.

narrator/59d892d78c0f738d.text: Three grey wolves cross the trail ahead of you at a lope. The last one stops, looks at you for a long moment, and dips its head before it goes on. Emil's wolves know your smell.

narrator/59e376e5027b829f.text: The tent is as you left it. The five cards are back in the deck; the table remembers where they lay.

narrator/59f815da068b9601.text: A dead knight sits on the front step with his back to the doorpost and his helmet in his lap, facing the light, the way a man sits at the end of a long watch.

narrator/5a116250cc1c6983.text: The tunnel opens on a cavern, and the cavern is full of gold. A long slope of it, coins and cups and crowns, and lying across the slope, with a chain at its neck, a dragon.

narrator/5a21fbaafc0f4d77.text: A traveller sits against the inside of the doors, wrapped in a good cloak, chin on chest. They got past the colossi and in out of the wind, and then the cold finished what the climb had started.

narrator/5a275f784711e749.text: The dumbwaiter's shaft goes up into the dark. Soot comes down it. Nothing else does.

narrator/5a2de4402003b966.text: Two shapes unfold from the underside of the stair above and drop onto the steps, and the well fills with bats.

narrator/5a54882c61143a21.text: The causeway ends where Berez begins: broken walls standing up out of black water, reeds taller than a man, and the smell of a river that came indoors and stayed. Far off in the west a white statue stands on a dry mound. In the east, on a stump wider than a house, a hut is breathing.

narrator/5a552967e7124d5e.text: Heads on every wall: stags, bears, wolves, and things you don't have names for. At the far end, mounted like the rest, the long skull of a dragon.

narrator/5a5a893245c6f29c.text: You say nothing. Thistle notices her hand on his sleeve and takes it away, and then, after a moment, puts it back.

narrator/5a5e075639613914.text: Sir Godfrey comes down from the house with the Order's book under his arm, and a shield, and a pen that's been dry for centuries, and he writes for a long time.

narrator/5a777deeffce11f9.text: A fire pit of blackened stones, a spit across it, and something on the spit you decide very firmly is a deer.

narrator/5a818f79f9107c25.text: Old Barovian letters, from before the castle was built. Not a blessing or a warning: a single name, cut by someone who wanted it remembered. KHAZAN.

narrator/5a8beb43b4b4ed00.text: A priest kneels before an altar stripped of its cloth, as though the church were in mourning. He rises when he hears you, and his face rearranges itself into something welcoming, with effort.

narrator/5a97fab1ca903a67.text: The lids come up slowly. The three of them climb out into the grey daylight blinking and slow, like children woken too early, and very, very hungry.

narrator/5a98338792b29f5a.text: Tser Pool is black and perfectly still, though a stream pours into it from the north. The reflections in it are a beat behind the things they reflect.

narrator/5aa5992bf8d3573b.text: You touch the bell. For one breath Stella's face is entirely her own.

narrator/5aa6b1178898d6f3.text: A little way down the well, on a ledge where a squire once hid his treasures, a cube of ivory no bigger than a die. Every face is carved with a different shield.

narrator/5ab63eb205e87641.text: He doesn't make a sound. When the light reaches the step he is smoke, and then he is nothing, and she is holding her own hand.

narrator/5ac098aa77408e01.text: Glass, scorch marks and the smell of a storm that hasn't come yet.

narrator/5ac10e5e205a792c.text: For a moment the sparks in his sockets burn white. Then, very quietly, he begins to remember.

narrator/5ad6c00fffc5d7ae.text: He looks back at you with the flat patience of a man who hurts people for a living. Whatever he wants, it isn't to talk to you.

narrator/5ae0554ebe2907c0.text: The lullaby is still in your head. It will be for a while.

narrator/5ae3a2dce6a84caa.text: They come over the north wall in a bunch, lanterns swinging: the Abbot's Brutes, hairy and patched, and behind them tall shapes in rotted wedding white, stitched to walk. They have come to fetch a stray home.

narrator/5ae95be2bf7989d5.text: You lay a hand on the coffin and begin the words. Cold comes up through the wood into your palm. Then you see the marks.

narrator/5af2a5e2632c384b.text: Grey daylight, a long way down to the courtyard, and the wind tugging at you as if it has somewhere to take you.

narrator/5b03eabccc780ae6.text: He doesn't move until Ireena turns away. Then he watches her go, and goes on watching the place where she was.

narrator/5b1418d2ecb6cf4a.text: The inscription has been gnawed. By teeth. Small ones, patient ones.

narrator/5b15ea85d053fe6b.text: The great nest is a hoard: buttons, a spoon, a broken watch, a tin soldier, coins, a hand mirror with the glass intact.

narrator/5b1611b8abd2c86b.text: Dmitri looks at Ireena for a long while. Something in his face gives way, slowly, like ice on a thawing pond.

narrator/5b1d03f49d7eb497.text: A rented room turned into a travelling showman's dressing room: costumes, a lute, a stage moustache on the washstand. Under the bed, the corner of an iron-bound sea chest.

narrator/5b1e79ae4659ae86.text: Old Nistor comes out with his net still in his hands and sees them, and sees which way they're turning, and sits down on his step.

narrator/5b1f298f3686664b.text: A lamp post on Main Street, with a loose stone at its foot. Under it, folded small, a paper of names in a careful round hand.

narrator/5b20d3868f98f2cc.text: The captain's room. The strongbox chained to the wall is the only thing in the tower that seems to want your attention, and wants it very much.

narrator/5b2894c4596411bc.text: A courtyard of cracked flagstones and weeds, and the keep rising over it so high you have to lean back to see the top.

narrator/5b45b5c3fd6c5998.text: Wren turns his back on the chamberlain and walks away on his own two feet, not fast. It's the bravest thing you've seen anyone do in this house.

narrator/5b4956bb2bfa792c.text: He murmurs along with you, eyes closed. If he stumbles, you can't hear it.

narrator/5b557329a9fe51e4.text: Ratatoille is making a tart tonight, and making it badly: doing a step wrong, stopping, doing it right, as if he were arguing with somebody who isn't there.

narrator/5b5ac808ad26809a.text: The places are laid for exactly as many of you as there are. Not one more.

narrator/5b5bd87ed2ef159b.text: In the cradle, the root that was shaped like a baby has withered to a twist of brown, like a thing left too long in a cellar. The blanket is still tucked around it, very neatly.

narrator/5b5f8ec3fbf28e69.text: You dream of brick, climbing over your mouth course by course, and wake swallowing.

narrator/5b674ca282aaf537.text: Garlic braided with wolfsbane, nailed over a door, and a little mirror hung under it facing the street. Every door on this lane has the same, as if they all agreed on it one bad night.

narrator/5b6a044a4bb35e9b.text: A soot-streaked shawl lies on the bottom step, folded neatly, the way a servant folds things for the laundry.

narrator/5b73dcdf79791878.text: The goat track comes up from the south through switchbacks of pine. The hut stands in a yard to the east; the summit, with its cairn, rises to the north-west; a lookout to the west shows the lake below.

narrator/5b8987bbfa5e50ce.text: Your light won't settle on the lid. It slides off the letters as if the stone were wet with ink.

narrator/5b8b656b0186ffc0.text: Izek sits on his cot in the dark with a doll in his ordinary hand, turning it so the candlelight moves across its painted face. He doesn't get up.

narrator/5b9a03bc0869c963.text: The road leaves the village between two leaning posts and runs west toward the crossroads. Ireena stops at the last post and looks back once.

narrator/5babcc4c69f260d1.text: The bed is stripped. Someone has slashed the black velvet bows on the canopy to ribbons, very thoroughly, and left them on the floor.

narrator/5bb364b34f6f332d.text: Straw, a bucket, a ring in the wall. Every cell is furnished the same, and so is every prisoner.

narrator/5bbeba439b868fd8.text: A thin old man in ink-stained sleeves sits at a desk heaped with ledgers. An iron shackle on his ankle is chained to the leg of the desk, and the chain has worn a groove in the floor.

narrator/5bc8a949baf1fc5c.text: The hooded figure's hands are folded over its box, and the box is silent. It has nothing more to say to you. It has already said it.

narrator/5bd0f30d85224e6b.text: Elisabeth is already over the table.

narrator/5bd5d0da1cbd7a4f.text: The rope parts at the first cut. You lay him on the road, then dig beside it where the earth is soft, with blades and hands and whatever else will move dirt.

narrator/5bdc69fa34fabf08.text: She comes down off the step and takes each of your hands in turn, the way the novices do at the end of the morning hymn. Her fingers are warm, and they stay warm a long while.

narrator/5c10f95f3035d8c1.text: Coffins in every size, all well made. On the smallest, someone has carved a little sun, and then a little moon over it, as if unsure which would be kinder.

narrator/5c1231743e2de01e.text: The humming stops. In the silence, somebody at the back of the church begins, very quietly, to cry.

narrator/5c14e0f8174b677c.text: A howl from up the ridge, answered from below the road, and answered again much closer. The two at the front run on two legs.

narrator/5c209267190e24ed.text: A hearth with a green fire, a rocking chair worn pale on the arms, a table laid for more guests than she ever has.

narrator/5c28f57ac8b05321.text: The jar is warm, and it hums against your palm the way a cat does. Somewhere inside it, faintly, someone is arguing with himself about the correct way to open a door.

narrator/5c2a3d4e4b023609.text: A huge hearth with a black pot over a low fire. Something in the pot is bubbling. You decide, as a group, not to look.

narrator/5c37633b6279f7d5.text: You follow her painted gaze to the bottom of the frame. Something is wedged behind the canvas, exactly where she is looking.

narrator/5c4285b398676bc3.text: The frame gives under your hand and the whole portrait swings out like a door. Behind it a stair no wider than a coffin goes down into the dark, and up it comes the cold smell of metal.

narrator/5c463c6943f4f35b.text: A cord strung across the track, hung with bells, bones and little mirrors. Anyone who comes in from the road rings it, whether they want to or not.

narrator/5c524a792dfd0f67.text: She looks at each of your faces in turn, slowly, the way a cook reads a list of what's in the larder.

narrator/5c5be704e55f716f.text: The camp under the trees is struck, the tents folded, the fire cold. Only the cairn of river stones stays, and the ravens.

narrator/5c6181de11f9059d.text: You are in the tall house on Mournful Lane. It has been very patient with you so far.

narrator/5c625cf4f2f44b41.text: He takes the dress the way a priest takes a relic, in both hands, and holds it up to the candles. For a moment his face is so happy that it's hard to look at.

narrator/5c7fdcfe1f6b85c6.text: There is nothing frightened in her at all, which is rare in Barovia. What's there instead is patience, and faith, and a quiet appetite for the Baron's chair that she isn't troubling to hide.

narrator/5cb8d2be912b019c.text: The grey light makes every letter look the same. You give up before your eyes start to ache.

narrator/5cbff21739633cfb.text: A copper bath on clawed feet, bone dry. A bar of soap in the dish has gone hard as stone.

narrator/5cc360660fb7ff98.text: Steam, a green fire, a black pot as big as a bathtub, and the smell of something that was alive this morning.

narrator/5ce2689186338c24.text: Drawings pinned to the wall: a house, a sun, two children holding hands. Under every house, in the cellar, a black scribble with a great many legs.

narrator/5cf31f1800796276.text: A man and a woman are chained by the ankle to the cart's wheel, in their shirts, in slush that steams. They don't call out. They look at the gate, then at you, and shake their heads very slightly: not now, not while they're watching.

narrator/5d0b36af9791eec4.text: The black carriage again, waiting on the road with its door open, as patient as a stone.

narrator/5d10c84bccac4bd0.text: Wedged in the reeds, a waterlogged satchel: some fisher's knife, wrapped in oilcloth by someone who meant to come back for it.

narrator/5d467dddba173ff2.text: He sits on his hoard in a chair that has sunk to its knees in gold, turning one coin over and over in his fingers. Behind him a suit of armour with no one in it draws its sword.

narrator/5d4977774af5a714.text: Kiril's hoard: the purses, rings and good coats of everyone who ever walked the Krezk road at the wrong time.

narrator/5d4f69ea7b47baf5.text: A raven drops out of the dead oak and lands badly, the way old birds do. By the time it has straightened up, it is an old woman in a black shawl, brushing feathers off her sleeves like crumbs.

narrator/5d5c006bb25c3690.text: The tower's guardians lie in pieces on the floor. Nothing stands between you and the glass now.

narrator/5d5e20033cf6cf59.text: You sleep inside Van Richten's wards, on his floor, under his maps. For the first time in Barovia nothing scratches at the door all night. It turns out to be very hard to sleep without it.

narrator/5d8e027dd465d78d.text: You tell him what was scratched into the post of the last cage. Davian listens without moving, the way old men listen to weather coming.

narrator/5d9aa9d66a3ea073.text: In the oldest niche lies an old priest in rotted vestments. Round his neck, on a chain gone green, hangs a periapt of red stone that is still warm.

narrator/5da021db6d7da674.text: A wooden trapdoor in the ceiling, bolted from this side. The bolts slide, and still it won't lift: something heavy is sitting on it, the way the house sits on everything down here.

narrator/5da0dd570f346949.text: He steps off the end of the jetty, and the stones take him straight down.

narrator/5db4341cf6070b70.text: Steel comes out. Morgantha smiles at it the way a grandmother smiles at a child's wooden sword.

narrator/5dbedd0f3a4c815e.text: You find a way that keeps to the shadow: thorn, shale, a loose stone caught before it can fall. Take it, and nobody on the crown will know you're coming until you're there.

narrator/5dc0847fdee7080a.text: Ireena walks to the very lip and stands there, too still, the spray beading in her hair.

narrator/5dd2e1ccbf0b3e4c.text: Piccolo applauds, slowly, then reaches into the nearest purse and takes a coin. Admission, apparently.

narrator/5dd7cf28c2f5e7b5.text: A black iron pot sits in the coals, and has sat there long enough to have a ring of soot like a tree has rings. It smells of plums and pepper.

narrator/5df51a7534f4f284.text: Inside the palisade, Vallaki is all steep roofs, swept streets and festival bunting in a yellow that nobody here would choose for themselves. Every face you pass is smiling. None of the smiles reach the eyes, and several of them are watching you.

narrator/5df96ddbd6514b61.text: In the morning Petru's mother comes down from the south row with a basket on her arm and nothing to say. She stands in front of you for a long while. Then she puts the basket down and holds your hands, one after the other, all of you.

narrator/5e0580f85bb9a713.text: The frost has gone from the great window. The glass dragon curls around its lamp, and the lamp in the picture seems brighter than glass can be.

narrator/5e069166413fa6c9.text: She presses a small iron key into your hand. It is warm from her pocket, and the bow is wrapped in rag where it would touch the silver.

narrator/5e082b4c4474b838.text: Behind the host's chair stands a broad man in a grey coat under a crimson one, a little bird stitched on the shoulder. He keeps his eyes on the back of his master's head.

narrator/5e0fed181101bc7c.text: A howl from the pines ends in a word. Something tall comes down the lane on two legs, and the pack comes with it.

narrator/5e11e86b5ab8c6c3.text: Warm air comes out round the edges of it, slowly, and goes back in. The iron is warm to touch.

narrator/5e134558c6c97934.text: Under the dolls and the wooden horse lie two small bundles wrapped in faded blankets, tied shut with a child's careful knot.

narrator/5e2a196fbc310b56.text: You lower the flame. Vladimir watches it all the way down, then turns and goes back down the stair without a word, and his knights go with him.

narrator/5e2fc35abd7833e7.text: Old graves, tidy and close-set. The newest have little bells tied to them on strings that run down into the earth, just in case.

narrator/5e32c9f98c7c18b3.text: Then the gate is empty. The bell stops in the middle of a stroke. Ireena breathes out, slowly, for a long time.

narrator/5e331a0ea76b5078.text: Offalia drops the berries. Her hands are already longer than they were.

narrator/5e4866bea5e9ba86.text: For a moment the commander says nothing at all. Down the table, one of the dead knights sets his goblet down very carefully.

narrator/5e608cb626ddfdd4.text: The mist on the floor runs to the black stair and pours down it, slow as honey.

narrator/5e62f0165f88a826.text: You work the earring free. It is a little silver horse's head, warm from nothing at all.

narrator/5e63692e3bbd6502.text: Ratatoille corners you behind the supply packs, looking as though he's about to cast something difficult.

narrator/5e688224b485faf9.text: He makes a joke about the weather, and then another one, and goes back to his bedroll, and doesn't do a handstand in the morning.

narrator/5e840f4a76f110f1.text: Wintersplinter lies across the crown in splinters long as spears. In the split heartwood, where a heart would be, sits a green stone the size of a plum, pulsing faintly, like something trying to get its breath back.

narrator/5e8dedb3b115e286.text: The shuffling stops. Madam Eva looks past you at Ireena for a long moment, the way you might look at a house you lived in as a child.

narrator/5e94862bfe3b4da2.text: The lid comes down over his eyes. They stay open the whole way. He will not lie here for ever.

narrator/5e9584c2b6ab5b89.text: The lid is set square again, and the stone under your hand is faintly, stubbornly warm.

narrator/5e99708cc333c20f.text: A broad man in a leather apron stands behind a stall of blades, mail and coils of rope, with a ledger chained to the counter so nobody can walk off with the prices.

narrator/5e9dd40b38297af4.text: Frost has softened the lid's letters to dimples. You make out the name, and the word "crowd", and nothing kind.

narrator/5e9ed5b0ff05b1e2.text: In the crypt, under where she lay, are the things the count let her keep: a purse of old coins in a currency nobody in this valley has seen, and a short black rod with a brass cap, warm to the touch, that drinks the magic out of the air near it.

narrator/5ea1212d88cd86ad.text: The cook said the lamp over the Master's table drinks from this furnace.

narrator/5ea12a9ae29090cf.text: Bluto comes out of his shack with a lantern and sees them, and drops it, and runs for the jetty, for the boat, for anywhere. They turn toward him all together, the way a field of grass turns in the wind.

narrator/5ebf66fbe770c35f.text: The bridge, two strides wide over the cloud. The sky above it is empty now, and you find you can cross it without looking up.

narrator/5ec5ba21388b6371.text: Someone used to send guests down this way. You wedge the catch with an iron spike before you trust it.

narrator/5ece3898083da479.text: Godfrey says the oath. Half the table says it with him. Vladimir does not.

narrator/5ed6be98bd3bf4a5.text: A dragon's skull, silver-grey and longer than a man is tall, mounted on the wall among the stags. A brass plate under it gives a date and no name.

narrator/5eeba1e1a21056d6.text: The earth goes in fast and badly, and nobody speaks. Somewhere beyond the wall, something laughs, softly.

narrator/5efa33dd86292e8e.text: The cultist drops his blade and goes down on his knees, hands raised, eyes on the stones. 'I only came for the wine and the company,' he says. 'Everyone comes for the wine.'

narrator/5efb76a1d7c2753d.text: The glyphs are a sentence, and each waits for the next to be spoken. You find the grammar, and speak them all backward. The doors swing open, and nothing in the alcove beside them stirs.

narrator/5f1a7a7ed2024116.text: From the crest you can see the vineyards to the east, Lake Zarovich like a dropped mirror, and beyond everything, the castle on its rock. It looks back. It always does.

narrator/5f1b716cef3817e6.text: The cracks in the floor flare white. Something climbs out of the biggest of them, shaped like a man made of a bonfire and too big for the gallery, and skulls rise out of the ash after it, burning, and laughing.

narrator/5f210fcb95a5e648.text: There's a name piped on each pastry in burnt sugar, one per person, spelled wrong only once. Nobody mentions which. The supper sits warm in all of you right through the next day, like a hand on the back.

narrator/5f23a40bca296102.text: Then the window is empty and the night is empty, and her shawl lies on the floor where it fell.

narrator/5f2d1967dfc8e99c.text: A thin man in a threadbare vestment kneels at the altar, praying in a voice worn down to gravel. Beneath the floor, something answers him: a long, hungry cry.

narrator/5f4de43515b66dd6.text: The record of what he paid is here somewhere. The copper book on the lectern hasn't been opened in a very long time.

narrator/5f5b9e7d33620067.text: She catches your glance before it lands and tugs the scarf higher. Whatever is under it, she isn't sharing.

narrator/5f70d017903cf033.text: At "patience is how he feeds", the Abbot sits down on the altar step, as if someone has cut a string.

narrator/5f990d9565a92f5e.text: A palisade of sharpened logs rings the town. The Old Svalich Road comes in at the east gate and leaves by the west, past a Vistani camp outside the walls. The burgomaster's mansion, Wachterhaus and St. Andral's Church face the square from the north; the Blue Water Inn, the coffin maker and the lockup stand to the south.

narrator/5fa08aeaeda91871.text: Half an hour of scraping silt and pulling reeds bares a slab at the foot of the plinth with an iron ring in it. Under the slab, a stair goes down into the mound, perfectly dry, and somewhere below it a candle is burning.

narrator/5fc181fff200c0d1.text: A fine frame, a painted woman, a wall. If there is more to it, it is not giving itself up today.

narrator/5fc1effa680390c2.text: One chained book doesn't match its spine. Inside, page after page of exercises for the mind, and the chain falls open when you finish the first.

narrator/5fcde4e5bde25367.text: Half sunk in the mud by the trail, a pair of good boots. The hunter who wore them ran very fast, for a while.

narrator/5fd3d0bd448254b8.text: Horse bones in the stalls, still in their rotted harness, each under its own name: Briar, Thunder, Old Meg. The stablehands didn't leave them. The stablehands didn't leave either.

narrator/5fe34bee07845eb6.text: Under the hovel's step, someone keeps a scuffed leather haversack. It holds far more than it should and somehow always has the thing you reach for on top.

narrator/5fe54c9a539bd56a.text: The whole valley lies below you: forest, river, the village, all of it small. From here it looks like something you could own.

narrator/5fe55b1aec063288.text: A long table laid for a feast, the candles lit, the food steaming. There is a place set for each of you, and no host.

narrator/5ff62bc4881b998b.text: A sword lies in the weeds below the headless statues. When you lift it, the hairs on your arm rise, and you know without turning that the wolves are watching from the trees.

narrator/5ff9cf0215e37c9e.text: Aurel reads on by the fire, to the empty chair. He didn't notice you leave, or come back.

narrator/6014e371f1095d44.text: He looks past you at the rooftops, as if Izek might be standing on one of them, and says nothing.

narrator/6039647de1409dfe.text: Ravens, hundreds of them, on every beam. Every head turns toward you at once.

narrator/606b004123e8a0a0.text: Rows of narrow beds, all made with the blankets folded square at the foot. Nobody has slept in any of them. Somebody makes them every morning anyway.

narrator/607021d387a91846.text: Three locks on the inside of the door, a bolt, a bar and a padlock, all new and all locked the night Gertruda left. None of them was the one that mattered.

narrator/6077304d8b1703fa.text: He doesn't look up. His eyes are red to the rims, and his voice is hoarse and lovely and does not stop, not to breathe, not for you.

narrator/60afb2b6179ac47d.text: The long stair goes down and down, past the dungeon, toward the crypts. The air coming up it is colder than the cellar.

narrator/60ba2b097cb27af7.text: A crypt cut with the name Gustav Durst and the year of his birth, its slab set ready and never closed. Nobody ever got around to dying properly.

narrator/60cb7b7b42fd5fe0.text: The raven in your hands shakes itself, and all at once there's a skinny boy of ten in its place, naked and blue with cold, holding on to you.

narrator/610141688cacbf30.text: The lake lies black and flat to the far shore, reeds rattling at its edge. The jetty has rotted halfway out, and there are footprints in the mud going down to the water and none coming back.

narrator/610e0d6ed6d11f97.text: Tucked up under the wagon's step on a nail: a deck of playing cards. Run a thumb along the edges and some of them are a little rougher than the rest.

narrator/612be3e7d181a18e.text: Silence. Clovin nods to himself, as if he'd expected it, and steps down off the trough.
