Then the hounds come up the east road out of the dark: grey and long and silent, more than you can count, and behind them a long grey man in a hunting coat gone black with weather, with a boar spear over his shoulder.

narrator/69d7af6df6950ffa.text: The shades unravel into the dark, and the heap sighs and settles deeper into its sleep. Far above you, every lock in the house turns over, one after another, like a man cracking his knuckles.

narrator/69dab3386e520c9d.text: Grey shapes keep pace with you along the ridge above the road, and then, all at once, they don't.

narrator/69dee761fa04e605.text: A handcart tipped in the ruts with one wheel cracked through. The load is gone. Drag marks go off into the trees, and stop.

narrator/69e1e18655f40c72.text: Jars and bottles in neat rows, each labelled in a small hand: wolfsbane, garlic oil, grave dirt (three cemeteries), holy water (blessed twice), and one simply marked DO NOT.

narrator/69e2125c0b7994c9.text: You take their potions, their purse and their ropes, and you tell them, out loud, that you'll put it all to good use. It seems only polite.

narrator/6a0b0c0fc0e29493.text: Lake Baratok is small, cold and very still, held in the lap of the mountain like water in a cupped hand. In the middle of it, on a knuckle of rock, stands a round black tower with one window lit.

narrator/6a0eddfc5114986a.text: The Luna, slow and wide and the colour of strong tea. Downstream, half a church roof sticks up out of the water like the back of a whale.

narrator/6a16472f98febe12.text: The dining room, still laid for guests who never arrive.

narrator/6a1ef9846281181b.text: A big, slow, frightened man leaning on a spade. If he knows more, he's buried it deep.

narrator/6a2a17786326dac8.text: Under the floor of the last wicker cage, a prisoner hid a sword the druids never found. The blade is black and thirsty.

narrator/6a328bddce6ec2c6.text: The carriage lamp stops at the end of the lane. Its door opens on nothing, and a tall shape in a coachman's cape steps down, with the village dead shuffling behind it as if they've been called in to supper.

narrator/6a3b05a39a3a3318.text: A long stone house with a turf roof and a door with three bolts on the inside. Over the door, five little wooden suns are nailed in a row, and a sixth nail with nothing on it.

narrator/6a69f8f4e14ae528.text: The words come out in the wrong order, the way they do at a stranger's grave. Nothing answers. Nothing seems to mind, either.

narrator/6a751ac2397ef21a.text: He bends over the bowstring and doesn't look up again.

narrator/6a752fc4f02bc23b.text: The words go down into the grave with him. Behind the gallows, one of the old mounds settles, like a sleeper turning over.

narrator/6a7e4a0463904951.text: Her currant eyes find Ireena and stop there. For a moment the old woman doesn't breathe at all.

narrator/6a805d204c863b43.text: The chest at the coffin's foot holds coin and candles, and something wrapped in black velvet that he kept close.

narrator/6a9d30b3a76c7d6b.text: The track climbs out of the trees onto bare rock. The windmill stands at the top with its sails locked in a cross; smoke leaks from a pipe in its side, and the whole hill smells of baking.

narrator/6abb974f666ef2f6.text: You put the folded dress back in her lap. She runs her thumb along the lace, at the place where it was mended.

narrator/6ac34587561e5d54.text: You sleep on the shingle with your backs to an empty hut. All night the lake laps at the jetty, patient and steady, like something counting.

narrator/6ac6e08a6090ae76.text: The candles all lean toward her, every one, the flames lying almost flat. Vasilka, forgotten on her bier, turns her head to see what everyone is looking at.

narrator/6ad5fe54f1d312ac.text: A small crypt for a small man. The plaster on its walls was painted with juggling balls once, in colours now the shade of old bruises.

narrator/6aecbcb1ee7c6374.text: She unlocks the iron-bound chest behind her with a key she keeps on a cord round her neck, lifts out a bundle of oilcloth, and sets it on the table between the cards.

narrator/6af3e365927fcaec.text: You tell Krezk his name and step back. It is the quietest square you have ever stood in.

narrator/6b1d0b297a4cc270.text: They don't know; they are still waiting for a door to open, the way you wait for morning. Telling them will hurt, and not telling them will hurt longer.

narrator/6b2d746f2d2b12ec.text: A stair under the plinth comes down into one square room cut from the rock. The marsh is all around it and not a drop has got in.

narrator/6b4563d620d70128.text: A chasm with no bottom you can see, a drawbridge already lowered, a gatehouse with its portcullis up. Beyond it a courtyard of cracked stone and weeds, and the keep rising over it with one window lit.

narrator/6b4ccacfe00d472b.text: Behind the mill, out of sight of the road, a heap of bones is half sunk into the nettles. Sheep, mostly. Mostly.

narrator/6b519332dc384e30.text: Over the hearth, on a black thread, hangs a little doll of rag and straw with a head of real red hair. A tiny M is stitched on its breast. Through the M goes a long black thorn, pushed in and drawn out so many times the cloth around it has worn to lace.

narrator/6b5504cfcae3e20d.text: A handsome townhouse, freshly painted, its windows dark. It has the look of a house expecting guests, and looking forward to them.

narrator/6b691905728bb7fa.text: The smallest crypt in the row says Walter, and nothing else: no family name, no dates. It has never been opened.

narrator/6b7027f990924e81.text: Two children stand in the road where the cottages begin, as if they have never moved. The girl lifts her chin; the boy holds his wolf by one ear.

narrator/6b780de44b85d23b.text: The dust on the altar lies thick and even, except in one place, where it has been heaped over something.

narrator/6b8d5b548841929b.text: The portcullis hangs in its slot above you, teeth down. Nobody is at the winch.

narrator/6b99981f6acdd31d.text: Pull it now and the boy wakes screaming, and something in the yard wakes with him. The wood comes first.

narrator/6b9d41328a31290f.text: He looks at Ireena for a long time. She looks back and doesn't help him.

narrator/6bb035bd2abc0a73.text: The instrument cabinet has a false back. Behind it, on a black cord, a glass vial with something green and still inside.

narrator/6bb3be55e862a0a2.text: One board by the gear sits a fingernail higher than the rest, with no nail in it. Under it is the chute to the millstone.

narrator/6bcd1766ca7084f5.text: It tumbles into the ditch, struggles up and flies away low and lopsided, shrieking. From the trees on both sides of the road, a great many ravens shriek back.

narrator/6bdc21aa609e8fe2.text: Old war banners, black birds on red, rotted to lace at the edges. Their battles were won before your great-grandparents were born.

narrator/6bf23be937b1af22.text: Beside the cradle, the lamp-keeper's iron locker is bolted to the stones. When you nudge it with a boot, something heavier than lamp oil shifts inside.

narrator/6bf9194f55163b59.text: The board tips, and so do you, down the chute and onto the millstone with a sound the whole mill hears.

narrator/6bfe8506d30dc125.text: Words are cut over the stair: the house keeps its dead. Someone has added, below it, in a smaller hand: and its dead keep the house.

narrator/6c01149b1bc6283c.text: You dream of a long table laid with pastries, and everyone you have ever lost sitting round it, eating, too busy to look up.

narrator/6c0984c33d468c5e.text: The wine merchant sits among his bottles with his coat open and his ledger closed. There's nothing more he can sell anyone.

narrator/6c1163d4c01ebd08.text: Ireena slows at the crossroads and reads every arm of the signpost twice, as if it might have changed its mind about where things are.

narrator/6c161bec65686c45.text: Bluto looks back once, as if he'd expected someone to argue. Then he walks off the end of the jetty, and the stones take him straight down.

narrator/6c1c1687e0004ad0.text: St. Andral's stands on its rise, and the bell rings for the evening office as you come into the yard. It rings clean.

narrator/6c1eb5b5013686c7.text: Smoke, sour wine, and the low talk of people who have learned to talk low. Every head turns when the door opens, and then, one by one, turns back.

narrator/6c36a2fd5e347b4c.text: The seat of the throne lifts on a hidden hinge. Underneath is a shallow box lined with red velvet.

narrator/6c3858c0a7489954.text: The water comes up to your chest and the cold drives the breath out of you, but you get a hand on the bow and walk the boat back to the jetty like a reluctant horse.

narrator/6c3c278af479eb8b.text: She stops fighting the cord and stands, shivering all over, and lets you put a hand on her neck. Under your palm the hide is hot as a kettle.

narrator/6c55fa8b7d413a5f.text: Kiril's lair: a bed of good furs, a wolf-skin rug, an iron chest, and a wall of trophies. The trophies are not wolves.

narrator/6c6f2109ed335b04.text: Patrina is at her desk again, turning pages that crumble at her touch and re-form, and crumble.

narrator/6c798845e1a4f211.text: She ladles out a bowl without asking. It is hot, sweet and peppery, and it is the first thing in this valley that has tasted of anything.

narrator/6c82f55cc0b03bf5.text: Good horses, well kept, every one of them facing the lake with its ears back.

narrator/6c86838bc4c0ad25.text: Read together, they say what neither says alone. He didn't bargain to live forever. He bargained to stop growing older than her. Everything after was the price.

narrator/6c8bd84a3cc0a08d.text: Wren holds out a letter, creased soft at the folds, sealed in grey wax with a leaf pressed into it. Kasimir looks at the seal and stops breathing.

narrator/6c9dd40b5a4ee375.text: Ireena's hand goes to the scarf at her throat before she can stop it. He sees, and his smile widens.

narrator/6cac7b105b17848c.text: A cradle on rockers beside a copper tub. A mobile of little bones turns above the cradle, though there's no draught.

narrator/6cae8d78ccaa7d89.text: Round white goat cheeses set out on a board to firm in the cold, each pressed with a little sun on top.

narrator/6cc03d4ef84670d6.text: The words go into him like warm water. He shivers once, all over, and looks at you, and then down at his own wrist, and then, for the first time, back down the trail toward Vallaki.

narrator/6cc3543491d4dba8.text: He stands up, and up, and follows you down the lane to the burgomaster's house, stepping very carefully in your footprints so as not to wake anybody.

narrator/6cd5402746887f1a.text: The coffin holds a long drift of grey ash in the shape of a man, and a stake standing upright in it.

narrator/6cd8583b972be151.text: The room still smells of his mist. The heart beats on, a little faster than before.

narrator/6cdf0be29fe622a1.text: Forty beds, blankets folded square, pillows plumped. Somebody makes them every morning for men who never come up to sleep.

narrator/6d00d0d1a531bbbe.text: Ludmilla closes her book. Volenta claps her hands. Anastrasya turns her face to the wall and does not move.

narrator/6d117b287a378292.text: Cold stone and the smell of old candle wax. The floor of the vestibule is worn into two shallow hollows, side by side, where people knelt for a very long time.

narrator/6d23017c4d874f50.text: The wind hits you the moment your head clears the hatch. Below, the valley is black, with a few small lights in it that look very far away.

narrator/6d4a78859aa9966e.text: Rot is spread across the floor in a great slick. Lorghoth the Decayer has finally decayed.

narrator/6d4ac74c94619b2e.text: Black water, flat and quiet. Somewhere far out, a fish jumps.

narrator/6d4d71e8c837cdc1.text: His eyes go to your faces, one by one, and stop. Whatever the road has written on them, he reads part of it.

narrator/6d511655ff98fa5d.text: Last up the cellar stair comes a young corporal, who stops by Ilse just long enough to nod.

narrator/6d511c8f9ab7a4ed.text: The frost on the parapet melts all at once and runs down the stones like rain.

narrator/6d58549f436947ac.text: He tries to hold your stare and can't. With a sound halfway between a curse and a sob he kicks the hoops off the vat and bolts out of the back door, west.

narrator/6d6b29576f6ed797.text: Kip doesn't offer anyone an apricot tonight. That has never happened before. He sits with his hat in his lap and talks slowly, politely and very clearly, like a man reading out terms.

narrator/6d6b9dcd4bf98164.text: Far below, something chokes, and roars, and chokes again, and the floor under your feet shudders, and is still.

narrator/6d6dc949951a3a12.text: Somebody snorts. Then somebody else does, and is ashamed, and does it again. A child asks, loudly, which morning, and Clovin barks for her, and that's the first real laugh.

narrator/6d6defff1b7bd44e.text: A flat-bottomed rowboat, tarred and sound: the only boat on the landing that isn't rotting. Somebody still cares for it. Somebody who hasn't been home in days.

narrator/6d785f7f7b754117.text: Bones, bells, little mirrors, a dried bird's foot, a child's tooth on a thread. Each one is turning, very slowly, to face you.

narrator/6d7a7d5bcb58e2ac.text: The flame touches the old ash, and the beacon takes it like a long-held breath let go.

narrator/6d7bbb6f3328d26e.text: Cold air rolls up the steps from the cellar, smelling of grapes and stone.

narrator/6d81859fb86c2150.text: A stair hall at the foot of a tower. One stair winds up into the dark toward the spires; another climbs to the floor above, toward the sound of someone crying.

narrator/6d97536203d0beca.text: Nobody moves to fetch a book. You suspect nobody has for a very long time.

narrator/6da9c58a97c647bf.text: The balcony again, where one of the doors is breathing. You are fairly sure it's the nursery.

narrator/6daa6cd1f004a173.text: The attic again. The dust shows your footprints, and some smaller ones that aren't yours.

narrator/6dd63524b39bb8b1.text: She doesn't fall the way his spawn fall. She sits down on the edge of her crypt, and looks at her inky fingers, and is gone, a little at a time, like a page left in the sun.

narrator/6de23905a806a481.text: Bones gnawed clean and stacked, with a kind of tidiness. The tidiness is the worst part.

narrator/6de48418e8dc742a.text: Her eyes rest on Ireena a moment too long, the way a jeweller's rest on a stone.

narrator/6e02e1c87c0e030e.text: A drawer hides in the base of the toy chest, the kind a boy finds and tells nobody about. Inside, a grey cloth bag, and at the bottom of it something soft and warm, like fur.

narrator/6e1161ab614f660a.text: The rags are years old, many years. There's moss in the seams of his coat. But his face is a young man's, and his hands, and he's frightened in the plain way of somebody who has been out in the cold one night and wants his bed.

narrator/6e153f80776f5902.text: The altar is bare now, the dust brushed into the corners.

narrator/6e1bc24e3ee75526.text: Lady Wachter receives you in a parlour set with a ring of chairs, though only she is in it. She pours tea for each of you without asking how you take it, and gets every cup right.

narrator/6e1c4e0f47de4613.text: A hard man with a bow, and friends in the trees. That much was already clear.

narrator/6e2eeb5d3fee1cdb.text: The blanket is stretched so tight you could bounce a coin on it. It has been made every night for four hundred years, and never once unmade.

narrator/6e36e741e0ceef62.text: At the foot of the stair Vladimir Horngaard lowers his head, and his knights behind him do the same.

narrator/6e54a67ab872662b.text: Among the roots, half drawn into the earth, lie the bones of a young man in the rags of a black coat. At the throat is a wooden clasp carved like a raven, the twin of the one Davian wears.

narrator/6e5c1acba0205e3e.text: The watch closes in, spears levelled.

narrator/6e7b5c9492742bbf.text: Past midnight the boards over the windows begin to creak, then to split. Wolves throw themselves at the front door, and in the parlor and the wake room grey hands come through the gaps.

narrator/6e8270956dc884c6.text: You hang the sunburst back on its hooks. It settles with a sigh.

narrator/6e84ff21b0ae8d96.text: The spare bedroom. The rocking chair has moved.

narrator/6e9b59ee64026e83.text: The fiddle stops mid-note. Every knife in the camp comes out at once.

narrator/6ea99f3a3623aa67.text: The den is silent. The fire pit is ash, and the straw beds along the walls are empty, and they will stay that way.

narrator/6eae7e3f2956217e.text: Up to his thighs in the black water, a gaunt man in a sodden coat is wading out from the shore with a sack over his shoulder. The sack is kicking.

narrator/6eb17c0bc63a7eb1.text: Rope coiled to the same diameter, candles in rows of ten, lamp oil with every label facing out. The shelves are fuller than the village has any use for.

narrator/6eb743726092f3e2.text: She doesn't come with you. She's simply at the churchyard when you get there, standing beside the grave Mihail dug this week, waiting.

narrator/6ecf11211253ec21.text: She is black from muzzle to tail now, and her eyes are coals in a banked fire. She stands very still at the milestone, waiting for her new master, and doesn't look at you at all.

narrator/6ed2a5108e29a203.text: The faceless god looks down on the hall with nothing. You find yourself not standing directly in front of it.

narrator/6eebeafe2608610b.text: Grey shapes come down the scree above the road at a lope, spreading out as they come.

narrator/6ef23e5d3ad865ce.text: An arrow thumps into the road a hand's breadth from your boots. Up on the wall-walk, somebody you hadn't noticed is already nocking another.

narrator/6ef6bdec509e0a9e.text: Grave mounds, very old, sunk and grassed over. Something has burrowed into one of them recently, and not to get out.

narrator/6f07bb28954e2c84.text: Fen growls something low at her back, gentle, the way you'd settle a dog. She doesn't move an inch.

narrator/6f1dd4d259a056f9.text: The armor on the landing steps down off its stand.

narrator/6f200941cc701f3b.text: The altar is clean. The grooves are not.

narrator/6f2b2b90cce99b47.text: The tasting room: a long bar, a few tables, and a row of cups hung on hooks, every one of them clean. The druids haven't touched the cups. They don't drink, apparently. It explains a great deal.

narrator/6f2b4905360956a0.text: Liriel doesn't say anything at all. She has gone white to the lips, and very still, the way a candle goes still in a room where a door has just closed.

narrator/6f38a6ab433d132b.text: A foyer with a boot scraper, a coat stand and a sign in a round, hopeful hand: SMILE, YOU ARE A GUEST.

narrator/6f716294eb209f91.text: Emil gets up the way old men and old wolves do, in stages, and stands rubbing the black rings on his wrists.

narrator/6f7afe3e43ee725a.text: You pull the blanket off his knees. The chain runs from his ankle into the wagon's board, grey and wet, and where it goes into his skin, it has grown there.

narrator/6fab45aa2accfb0d.text: The last of them lets the weapon fall and shows you empty hands. Whatever they were paid, it wasn't enough to die for.

narrator/6fba81b68df38314.text: At the far end of the jetty stands Bluto, in the same sodden coat. His pockets hang heavy and lopsided. He has filled them with stones.

narrator/6fbe5394857720fd.text: Somewhere along the rows an iron gate creaks open, and does not creak shut again.

narrator/6fc01405e43b8e3f.text: A bronze plaque, green with age: the old king's champion, who never lost a fight. It lists the men he killed. It takes up the whole plaque.

narrator/6fc3e4380c3a74db.text: Thistle comes back to camp late, very pleased with herself, with powdered sugar all down her front.

narrator/6fd5fbbe5859c2ea.text: A cloaked woman with no face. Whatever she is, she is very old, and very patient, and she was here long before the wolves.

narrator/6fd749ea3014ae74.text: Holes, dozens of them, knee-deep and ragged, clawed rather than dug. In one of them something has given up and left its claws behind.

narrator/6fd949e0b2222d6d.text: Candles burn in the long hall with nobody to light them, and every flame leans the same way, toward the throne room doors.

narrator/6fdc25babfc620d4.text: The pines empty of bats all at once, and the dark comes down the lane like a flood.

narrator/6fe4eb8b1ecfa4a2.text: A grey mare is tied to the milestone by a halter of black cord. Smoke curls from her mane where it lies on her neck, and when she turns her head there are embers coming up in the backs of her eyes, like fire under ash.

narrator/6fea3f9952551fb8.text: The burial register: names, dates and causes in a careful hand. The careful hand gets less careful as the pages go on.

narrator/6fef9daff580e20a.text: The bunting is gone. Black ribbons hang from the watch's spears now, and the town is very quiet, the way a house goes quiet when someone important is asleep upstairs.

narrator/6ff4494b309f740a.text: The shutter stops swinging. The old woman goes so still that the hut, beneath her, goes still too.

narrator/6ffb0d833f9fcb6d.text: You find the ring's first letter and its last, and draw a line through both. The fire goes out like a held breath let go. Nothing in the hall stirs.

narrator/700b7c08c07ab50a.text: A windowless room behind the shelves, crammed with black-bound books on summoning and the dead. A heavy chest stands on clawed iron feet, and beside it lies a skeleton in leather armor that found this room first.

narrator/7024ceb6fe6a43fd.text: Every window is boarded from inside, and the boards are scored with claw marks on the outside of the wood. The house smells of candle wax, wet dog and grief.

narrator/70299f64f1b5da8b.text: Outside: the end of the road, the shut gate and its watchman, and a switchback track climbing toward the abbey. Inside: the burgomaster's house, the well and the square, goat pens, cottages, and the lane north to the shrine of the White Sun.

narrator/702d1ad115189387.text: Two centuries of Wachters, each in the fashion of their day, each with a small silver S somewhere in the painting: on a ring, a brooch, the clasp of a book.

narrator/702e58d4445536d1.text: The stair winds up inside the wall, every step worn into a hollow by four hundred years of boots that only ever went up to look at a dark lamp.

narrator/703dd62019a30c0f.text: Slush, then mud, then bare black rock that steams in the cold. At the top of the shelf, an iron gate set into the mountain, and warm air breathing out round it, slowly, in and out.

narrator/70446a55ebe7bcd5.text: The camp is empty. The fire has burned to a red eye in the ashes, and the wagons stand with their doors open. Only the great tent still glows.

narrator/704cf939138c68f2.text: The scholar takes off his spectacles, and his face goes with them: a jackal's head, black-lipped and smiling. The cold braziers light themselves with green fire.

narrator/7056c5d360f79f3f.text: Ratatoille butters his bread very carefully and eats it. Strahd watches him do it with every appearance of delight.

narrator/705acaee3b0c9e2d.text: The road west runs on into the mist. You have already said your goodbyes to this village; it didn't say any back.

narrator/705bc920b700d884.text: A painted sign over the gate: a wizard in a starry hat pouring wine into a cup held up by a raven. The paint is fresh on the raven and peeling everywhere else.

narrator/7071150e1ab1d742.text: A very small crypt at the end of the row.

narrator/7076246d38828cbf.text: A handcart lies tipped in the ditch with one wheel off. Beside it, sitting on an empty wine cask, is a stooped figure in a monk's cast-off habit, with one ear like a hound's and a hand that is mostly feathers.

narrator/7088b69c2186fb51.text: The inscription is there, and you read it, and a moment later you can't recall a word of it. You read it again. The same thing happens.

narrator/708f45b1fad3788e.text: You uncork the oil, and stop. Nobody has raked through the ashes at the back of that oven yet, and something about that oven nags at you.

narrator/7094e9084d9418b3.text: His eyes go to the dark line of the hills above the trees, once, before his smile comes back.

narrator/70b3a4b6d1aba0a0.text: The hearth at the end of the gallery is cold now, and the carved faces look at the floor.

narrator/70ba67c6f250f530.text: A high-backed chair half sunk in the drifts of coin. The seat is worn smooth. He comes down here to sit.

narrator/70be3577b4db767e.text: Tamsin closes the locket and puts it in Ireena's palm, and folds her fingers over it with his.

narrator/70e66ef952993601.text: Candles, benches, and a dozen people in their good clothes kneeling before a black-draped shrine, chanting softly. The chanting stops.

narrator/70ed8b11812c21c5.text: The chair stands still. It looks smaller than it did when someone was sitting in it.

narrator/7106e2e8dea13951.text: The bar is polished dark by hands and elbows. Behind it, a row of casks, and above them, three black feathers pinned to the beam in a row.

narrator/7116c89c6788b01e.text: She says it the way any other cook would say "not the rind".

narrator/71208554c6c36019.text: Lantern light on the abbey track, coming down the switchback fast. Sorin hears it before you do. He doesn't run; he puts himself between the lanterns and the little stones.

narrator/712571fbbb9415cc.text: The road runs on between its ditches, open fields on both sides and stone walls tumbled into the grass. Plenty of room to see what's coming. Plenty of room for it to come.

narrator/7131fed96a88ea0d.text: Small graves, kept tidy. Someone has put a candle stub on each one, and lit none of them.

narrator/713d3375ed15f732.text: She has thought about it every night for three winters. When she talks about the shutter her hand goes to the latch of her own coat, and stays there.

narrator/7151802fb03573d7.text: A doll with red hair, a green dress and a painted face carved with unusual care. A card reads NOT FOR SALE in a gloomy hand.

narrator/715ed8873a74482a.text: Your best story dies somewhere in the middle. A goat bleats into the silence. Somebody coughs, in a way that is clearly a review.

narrator/716ded291e969f79.text: Lines, arcs and glyphs, very neatly done. They mean something. They are quite certain of it, even if you aren't.

narrator/7189f0c51b4a2a8c.text: A square of mud around a dry well, and in the middle of it all a pastry cart, the only cheerful thing in the village. That should worry you more than it does.

narrator/718ed01aefebb7df.text: Then the water along the shore starts to stand up in the shape of people.

narrator/71cba5b8ab11543b.text: You are in the village of Barovia, where every shutter is closed and every door is listening.

narrator/71cbbf30574bc88a.text: A low vestibule, its floor worn by kneeling. One narrow doorway leads on into a long vault where a skeleton far too big for any tomb lies along a raised stone bier, wings folded, neck ending in nothing.

narrator/71ff3c5a76532a57.text: The crows come down before you have even cleaned your blade.

narrator/721c0568c30fbe8e.text: You find the joists under the rot and lay a path along them, and the old floor lets you pass.

narrator/7223c44f13494d82.text: The scarecrows lie where they fell, face down, poles snapped. Nothing is watching you from the reeds.

narrator/722c2524b2a541e9.text: The nuns' graves, small and neat, each with a sunburst cut into the headstone and a name: Sister this, Sister that. The last stone has no name, only the date the abbey emptied.

narrator/723288376c2d86c0.text: The dungeon is darker than it was and very quiet. The breathing has stopped.

narrator/72736c60d62e8c1d.text: Over the outer wall there is no ground, only air, and far below the tops of pines.

narrator/727e1e2734a174e0.text: He holds the doll up and smiles. His eyes, over the top of it, don't smile at all.

narrator/72c87550db3aed7c.text: A big raven drops onto your wrist, looks you over, and croaks once. The whole roost settles like a breath let out.

narrator/72d2fd545d42c6de.text: Strahd stands at the foot of his brother's tomb with one hand on the stone. He finishes what he was saying to it before he turns.

narrator/72eb1a771d0da235.text: One board under the card cabinet lifts at a touch. Beneath it, a silver medallion on a chain. Gustav Durst never lost at cards, and now you know why.

narrator/7317ffc976fb4faa.text: A ring of blackened stones where the fishers cooked their catch. The ashes are cold and wet, and something has dug through them looking for scraps.

narrator/732fd62c9d08fa3b.text: Godrick has been quiet all evening, which for Godrick is like a mountain being quiet. At last he puts down the sword he's been sharpening and clears his throat.

narrator/733d4c885afa1543.text: The track crests a rise, and there it is on its ridge to the north: the beacon of Argynvostholt, burning silver, laying a pale road of light across the treetops toward the castle.

narrator/73411567f60269cb.text: Kiril is dead. The wolves that are left go out of the cave mouth in a grey stream and don't stop running. Somewhere down the hill one of them howls, and none of the others answer.

narrator/73466e7085c1bad6.text: You find the place where the ward turns back on itself and pull. The colossus freezes mid-turn, head cocked, and stays that way.

narrator/735e1dc951c3d00e.text: A squat bell tower with no rope. The bell is still up there. On still nights, Krezk says, it rings anyway.

narrator/7363ae091f9063e4.text: Recipes, lists, warnings, a careful sketch of a duck. If the useful notes are here, they're under the useless ones, which are under the confusing ones.

narrator/73730eb6fb2f88e0.text: He says a word under his breath, and the door swings open. Then he lays his palm flat on the frame and murmurs again, and somewhere high in the tower something goes quiet, like a held breath let out.

narrator/738cec3c08d2fd91.text: A big grey wolf with an old arrow scar on its flank, set by the wall like a dog waiting to be let out.

narrator/739daa2069610f7f.text: The hut has been waiting for her. When you come instead, it stands up on its roots and screams through its door.

narrator/73eb641e4b0e6cdd.text: Another guardroom, and this one is not empty. Figures stand at their posts, coated in frost, perfectly still.

narrator/73f823705eaa1fa8.text: The inscription has been scratched over with tiny star charts. Someone sat here a long time, copying what the vestige told them.

narrator/740b28974a193f3d.text: Main street runs straight through town from gate to gate, its mud raked smooth. Bunting hangs between the eaves on both sides, so low you have to duck the sodden ends.

narrator/74127b0dc0b475eb.text: The press house is all height and shadow, built round the great wine press like a church round its altar. The air is thick with the smell of crushed fruit going bad on purpose.

narrator/741608db6fcaa10a.text: A narrow walk runs between the keep and the outer wall. The wind comes over the wall with nothing to stop it.

narrator/7429f6229057bb9d.text: A walled garden under frost. The poles along the north wall stand empty, and the snow beneath them is black with ash.

narrator/7459ce00d47a41bc.text: Black water to the far shore and the wolf hills above it. The fishers left a year ago when the nets stopped filling; only Bluto stayed. His rowboat is tied at the jetty's foot.

narrator/745e4c9041bcdb84.text: Low mounds ring the foot of the hill, old graves without stones. The track threads between them. Your boots, you notice, choose not to step on any.

narrator/74648de1935ef107.text: Rahadin draws a curved blade and settles on the top step as if he means to stand there for another four hundred years. The screaming around him grows louder.

narrator/746b9e94c2f366d6.text: A great round stone, white with dust. You run a finger through the dust and it isn't all flour: there's grit in it, and the grit is the wrong colour.

narrator/746d5f088284169f.text: You have two dresses: the one from the matron's trunk, and the one you brought up the mountain.

narrator/746e60ffd448266e.text: Flour, more flour, and jars you'd rather not open. The hags keep a tidy larder.

narrator/746f96ee339f2168.text: Stained glass of singers with their mouths open. In this light they could be singing, or screaming.

narrator/7480b9793675c17c.text: The captain's strongbox opens with a sound like a held breath let go.

narrator/74854425b7b1aa98.text: The black, sodden sun still stands on its pole. Lady Wachter has ordered it left where it is, as a reminder of what the Baron's light was worth.

narrator/748a4baec218215e.text: The road ends at a wall of fitted grey stone three men high, older than the trees around it, with one gate of iron-banded black oak. A watchman stands before it with a spear and the look of a man paid to say one word.

narrator/74929a707f26dbeb.text: The bridge is two strides wide over a gorge full of cloud. You remember the shadow on the ridge road, and find yourself looking up.

narrator/749bf970bf4936fd.text: The voice in the armour stops, and the wounds stop closing, and the armour is only armour.

narrator/74a07985779398b9.text: Half of Krezk is in the square by the shrine, because the burgomaster said they could come, and the other half is at the windows, because he didn't say they couldn't.

narrator/74d7b5bd9336d7a1.text: The man at the table by the hearth has a sword across his knees and a cup he isn't drinking. He watches you cross the room the way a sentry watches a road.

narrator/74d9f5dfe3ede1ad.text: And under the heap, where her belly lay, pressed into the rock by her weight: a coat of armour, every scale a hand across and silver, cold to touch in a cavern that's still warm.

narrator/74dc4a54444cad61.text: You can, now that you listen. Creak. Creak. Creak.

narrator/74f0fb074fec0ad7.text: The doll goes very still in his hand. He's been in enough fights to count yours before they start, and he doesn't like the total.

narrator/74f1bad64566a4fd.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Tenebrous, the last shadow. When the stars go out, this is what remains. We put it here to make sure it waits its turn."

narrator/74f59417a7e1964d.text: Down in the gorge there are lights: small, pale, drifting like lanterns carried by people who are taking their time. Under the roar of the water, somebody is calling.

narrator/751ae456398cf58d.text: A barrel under a brass spigot. The pipe runs up to a cistern on the roof; turn the tap and it coughs dust.

narrator/751b5e1ff7c16daa.text: The sigil under your boot wakes with a crack, and blue light jumps up your legs.

narrator/7528b07918734125.text: When you come up the last time, the water is flat and black and empty, and Bluto has gone, somewhere in the reeds. There is nothing in your hands but lake weed.

narrator/752c99ab0bfeddcc.text: A stone passage with a saint in a niche and a stair going down into colder air. Ahead, a pair of chapel doors.

narrator/75329bf14dee1d86.text: The jetty planks are slick and soft underfoot, and half of them give a little more than planks should. At the end, the water is very deep and very still.

narrator/75345226efc1f2ab.text: The landing, the empty shacks, the black water. Pawprints in the mud as wide as a dinner plate, going down to the lake and coming back.

narrator/753a83d526233713.text: One of you dreams of a warm kitchen, and an old woman at the table with her hands folded, watching you eat, and smiling, and smiling.

narrator/75494e8eb36cac3b.text: A crib, a mobile of tin birds, and a single candle that should have burned out years ago. Everything a baby needs, except the baby.

narrator/757bb658204d400a.text: Light flares white and a clap of thunder rolls down the road. The wolves scatter into the fog, and from somewhere farther off, a single long howl answers, as if passing on the news.

narrator/758b8b3ebecbc221.text: The stair down is narrow and the steps are glazed with old ice. Every voice in the temple is louder down here.

narrator/75b0eec4cf9f07ba.text: At the bottom of the stair the air is thick and warm and smells of rot. The chanting is very close now.

narrator/75dbe2d023f25e54.text: He weighs the heavier purse, grins, and tosses it over his shoulder to the nearest wolf.

narrator/7612df6cca821ffb.text: The chandelier lets go of the ceiling.

narrator/764223e0bd9c6ade.text: The house is only a house now, and the road at the village edge is only a road.

narrator/764763412a70797b.text: The field behind the gallows is a ruin of opened mounds. Nothing in it is getting up again, which is the most you can say for anywhere in this valley.

narrator/76546082c34208af.text: Somebody has already decided what to do with it.

narrator/7662a63dc41edff8.text: The road ends at the edge of a chasm, and the castle stands on the far side as if it grew there. The drawbridge is already down.

narrator/767288426831a5ef.text: The whole valley, laid out like a map somebody spilled ink on. Every road in it ends here.

narrator/76745d9a11fa08ba.text: It is quick. The hunger goes out of his face, and for a moment he is only a tired boy. Then he is dust in the chains.

narrator/768065885460e38d.text: A plain altar of oak on a stone step. The sunburst on its front has been touched so often by so many hands that the rays have worn smooth.

narrator/768b1637c81781ee.text: The crest is quiet. From here you can see the whole valley east to the castle on its rock, which seems, for once, a long way off.

narrator/768d72d8bbb5466f.text: A cell with a plank cot, no blanket, a stool and a ledger on a shelf. Nothing else. Whoever lives here doesn't sleep, or doesn't need to, or has forgotten how.

narrator/76a3e779d7b7fa1e.text: It isn't you they fear; it's the doubt, arriving all at once in a circle that never had any. One druid runs, then three. Ruxandra shrieks after them, gives you a look of perfectly polite hatred, and follows.

narrator/76a875538b9d6a61.text: A black carriage stands in the carriage house, polished and ready, with nobody to drive it. The horses in the traces do not blink.

narrator/76aada03b14a1367.text: The coffins are only boxes of earth now. You close their lids anyway.

narrator/76ae68c7483d7dc0.text: He rides on through the middle of you. The black horse never breaks its walk, and you find you have stepped aside without meaning to. The one who spoke has a thin cut across one cheek, neat as a quill stroke, and never saw the hand.

narrator/76aeba777bb1b046.text: They have heard promises in Barovia before. They don't believe yours.

narrator/76d97f25259b952d.text: Low rafters, warm air rising from the oven below, and the great wooden gear of the sails overhead, locked still. It smells of straw, sugar and something kept too long.

narrator/76e3dd5256a63661.text: They go round the bend, and the sound of them stops all at once, like a door shut on it.

narrator/76f6e0d8b4415ac3.text: By a painted wagon, a woman in a long dark coat sits fixing silver heads to crossbow bolts. Below her right knee, a brace of oak and steel; her left hand is bandaged, and she smells faintly of burnt hair.

narrator/770ac79e19cdb9b5.text: A low door in the tower's side, left of the gate, stands closed but not barred. A thin grey light shows under it, the colour of a lantern seen through fog.

narrator/771644254b21ca58.text: The water shivers and settles, and he is there beside her, the way he was at the pool.

narrator/771b31708a031f74.text: The floor of this gallery is cracked in long seams that glow dull red, and the air over them shakes. It's hard to breathe in here. It's very hard to think.

narrator/7736e9a4faa6a184.text: Mounds and more mounds, all the same grey under the grass. Someone with sharper eyes might tell them apart.

narrator/77483b1dd0035f5f.text: The hound heads on the chains in the amber all point the same way, at whoever carries the gift, the way dogs point at game.

narrator/7748b51e69b563fb.text: Three wooden balls appear from nowhere and he tosses you one. For a few minutes, on a stair in a vampire's house, you play catch with a clockwork jester, and he is very good at it.

narrator/7749e1c7be29bf3e.text: Ismark comes awake all at once, sees the empty window, and the colour leaves his face.

narrator/77533fc702383ea9.text: The light goes grey, then brown, then nothing. Out on the hill trail, a howl starts low and goes on getting louder for longer than anything's breath should last.

narrator/776543afed516f7e.text: It takes time. The crystal is hard, and it mends a little between blows. But the cracks spread, and at last, with a sound like a church window breaking, the heart comes apart.

narrator/7777692ea9c25d7f.text: The first pin comes out, and the whole row erupts. Starved things are not grateful. Starved things are fast.

narrator/7779ee026bcbff4f.text: The whole column lowers its lances at once, and the gate is full of bones riding at you.

narrator/777a1403b17bacbe.text: You sit with your backs to the wall. The wall, to its credit, stays a wall.

narrator/77813b9eee64de01.text: The grand stairs end in a landing of black marble. Beyond it a long hall runs away in both directions under banners nobody has dusted in a lifetime.

narrator/77897046e5fcb40e.text: You lay the bundle in the bottom, and Mihail takes the board with his sister's name on it and turns it over, and on the back, with his knife, he cuts ZINAIDA.

narrator/77a64cacdd25822e.text: A ledger ruled in red ink, every line squared off with a straightedge. Bildrath has not made a mistake in it in twenty years, and has corrected other people's mistakes in the margins.

narrator/77bd858685a95ce5.text: The colossus watches the valley below. When you come close, the light in its eyes brightens a little, the way a sleeper's breathing changes.

narrator/77d758080027e78f.text: Bones in the corner, cracked for the marrow. You count four skulls before you stop counting.

narrator/7837c2cf23ec2ed1.text: He goes out of the alcove on four legs, fast and low, and at the mouth of the cave he stops and looks back once, and makes a sound that might have been a laugh.

narrator/783d2b45dcc4d1b9.text: Under the house again, and the chanting hasn't stopped. It doesn't need to breathe.

narrator/78528d2a9c91950d.text: Somewhere far below, the thing you killed is already rotting back into its heap. The house will grow another; it can wait.

narrator/7867a17a95c326c8.text: You tell him: the kingdom his count came from has no name any more, the war that brought him here is four centuries done, and there's nobody left on either side of it but the count, and the valley, and the dead.

narrator/78a0f152d283b54d.text: Claw marks, sap and needles. Whatever climbed this tree, it didn't leave a note.

narrator/78a34fa2523675ce.text: The Blue Water Inn sits at the bottom of the town with its lamps lit and its door open, which in Barovia is the bravest thing a building can do.

narrator/78b082fd1afefb84.text: Liriel doesn't kneel this time. She stands in front of him with her hands folded, small and straight, the way a novice stands in front of her abbess, and asks very quietly.

narrator/78b9ae2e1a8ff6b3.text: Bella climbs the stair humming, steps over what is left of her mother without looking down, and settles into the rocking chair as if it had been made for her.

narrator/78c1adb38221c4c8.text: A fresh grave, very deep and very square, its spoil heap so tidy it looks measured. It was.

narrator/78c5b73ef6a3941d.text: Coffins, all empty, all waiting. Henrik's work is good. That's all you can say for it.

narrator/78cf5fdbc9d69515.text: A nail squeals slowly out of a lid. Then another.

narrator/78cfddf054328692.text: The brake's catch has been filed half through, neatly, on purpose. Let go of the handle with anyone in the cage and the cage goes straight to the bottom.

narrator/78ef89dc97d8a282.text: Near the head of it something pale moves and goes still: a druid on a rock, watching the gully. Somebody warned them.

narrator/78f6ee7c0cbd0c94.text: A young deer hung by its back legs from a branch, half skinned, with the hide pegged out on the ground beside it to scrape.

narrator/78f7f49b67f42974.text: Far below the window the valley lies under its mist like something drowned. You can see the road you came up.

narrator/78fd28f0bc7a416d.text: He reads with one long finger moving under the lines, humming, as pleased as a man with a good pudding.

narrator/79072a4d24a03440.text: He says it exactly the same way as last time. You suspect he has said it exactly the same way for centuries.

narrator/7914a04aa7b2d5d6.text: An emaciated shape in the amber, its ribs opened like a cage door with nothing inside. Its jaw works all the time, chewing nothing.

narrator/79398cf71e788ee3.text: Ruts in the rock itself, cut by iron wheels going up and down the same line for so long the stone has given in.

narrator/793c72952a08581d.text: The chalk lines flare white under your boots. For an instant you are everywhere and nowhere, and then you are back, and it hurts.

narrator/793d844124c97ca0.text: Equations in chalk cover the wall from floor to ceiling, beautiful and fluent, and every one of them stops halfway, at the same point, where the writer forgot what he was solving for.

narrator/794ab8a37ce85371.text: He looks at the holy symbol for exactly as long as a man can look at the sun. Then he looks at the floor, and keeps looking.

narrator/794ced451d7262c2.text: Kiril lies on the floor of his own den, and as he cools he forgets how to be a wolf: the fur goes, the snout goes, and what is left is a big, ordinary dead man.

narrator/795169d91bfe2a5b.text: The road east runs back toward the gates, and the mist lies across it like a held breath. Nobody has come in from that direction in a long time, except you.

narrator/7969c6464dc914c9.text: Above the archway, a carved crest: a wolf's head over a closed door. The Dursts were proud of this house.

narrator/796a436938e7a1f6.text: The gorge falls away into cloud. A stone kicked over the edge never makes a sound.

narrator/79702d708e450eb9.text: His knuckles whiten on the spear. Behind the gate, someone shouts a question; he shouts back an answer you don't catch, and it isn't brave.

narrator/797870ac6a14696e.text: Under your feet the hill's slow heartbeat stops, and then begins again, fast.

narrator/79832c71eb47c78b.text: Sorin is crouched among the little stones, putting the scattered toys back where they were, one by one.

narrator/79885af623af83a6.text: The mirror shows an empty room. You don't like what that says about the room.

narrator/798ced941e03d3cc.text: The dead come out of the trees on both sides of the road, slow and sure, still wearing the clothes they were buried in.

narrator/79965358d7e8903c.text: A scarecrow taller than the others, in a monk's old habit, with a sacking face and a mouth sewn shut with neat black stitches. Its arms are folded tight across its chest, as if it were holding something it was told to keep.

narrator/799a90b498888cb0.text: You don't argue. You tell him what you would want if it were your child, and what you would want if it were you down there, and he listens with his eyes closed.

narrator/79a03477395b9f8f.text: Under a recipe for ink and a list of the names of his own fingers, you find the wardens' word, written out in capitals with DO NOT FORGET beside it.

narrator/79b2071c5a4c793f.text: You hold out the brass key. He goes perfectly still, then turns his back to you and waits.

narrator/79cf02edcce70502.text: The men round the fire are big, bearded and painted green to the eyebrows. They see you, grin, and reach for their axes with something like relief.

narrator/79e88fec41cc48de.text: Red velvet seats, a folded blanket, and on the seat a card with a single letter on it, in a fine hand: S.

narrator/79f39ff2268d789c.text: He looks at you for a long moment, and then at the two young men behind him, and you can see him deciding which of them to shout at later.

narrator/7a0f0d36898909b3.text: Two cages hang from the rafters like birdcages for very large birds. In one, a thin girl with a set jaw and scraped knuckles. In the other, a small boy asleep against the bars, with crumbs on his chin.

narrator/7a15561c0edbb711.text: Bones under the black water, laid out in a neat row, as if someone tidied them.

narrator/7a2405326c9f844c.text: Down in the great hall, at the head of the table, a commander sits back in a winged chair and lets his sword lie.

narrator/7a27ef6bdafc7dd4.text: Three locks on the door, boards on every window, and a cold stove in the middle of it all. The weeping fills the house the way water fills a jar.

narrator/7a305faf32b8a2ed.text: The cobbler shakes your hand on the way past, very hard, without a word.

narrator/7a33cb9777b38b70.text: They go one at a time, the youngest first, like candles at the end of a long night. The sergeant goes last. He looks at the gate, and then at you, and nods once, as if signing something over.

narrator/7a59a9ddf5286151.text: The undercroft smells of old stone, old bones and something fresher. The dark here is very thick, and very attentive.

narrator/7a6201f411f6c315.text: A sparrow, a jay and a crow, hanging in the air at head height, wings out, frozen in mid-flight so perfectly you can count their feathers. They have been there a long time. Nothing has disturbed them.

narrator/7a7923fbd17bbeec.text: A parlour drowned in yellow cloth. Half-sewn suns, swallows and sashes cover every chair. It's the happiest room in Vallaki, and the most frantic.

narrator/7a80435b7c46cca8.text: The floor round the press is stained to the knee with what's left of the Mash.

narrator/7a86185301faac8f.text: A dead man with a spear. That's all you can make out in the dark.

narrator/7a89adcd14db0608.text: He turns his back and starts redrawing a line that didn't need redrawing, pressing so hard the chalk snaps.

narrator/7a930c49f083bca4.text: A stair without a rail climbs the inside of a tower so tall its top is lost in the dark. In the middle there is nothing at all: a well of black air going straight down.

narrator/7a964618f71e70d8.text: A short letter in an elegant, unhurried hand, signed with a single ornate S.

narrator/7aa3830cd66d004c.text: The roar arrives before the view does. Then the trees open on a gorge, and the River Ivlis goes over the edge in one long white fall.

narrator/7ace8a1ac69c1481.text: 'The Abbot is making a bride,' it whispers, 'for the lord on the hill. Sewn so beautiful. We are not to look at her. We look anyway.'

narrator/7aefc712ffc6bfc2.text: A raven drops onto a post at the side of the track and looks at you with one eye, then the other, as if checking its arithmetic.

narrator/7af1532d65cb1d38.text: Doors open a crack as Ireena passes and close again, and nobody calls out to her. A few people touch their foreheads, as if at a funeral.

narrator/7b00c41b2e9b28ed.text: Broken stone lies around the slab in wings and claws. The champion sleeps on without his watchers.

narrator/7b1733bbc52da23d.text: A pine as thick as a barrel lies along the edge of the road, felled long ago. Its upper side has been worn smooth by people sitting on it to rest, and by claws.

narrator/7b1a275594cb247e.text: A brick oven as big as a cottage hearth. Far at the back, through the glow of the coals, something catches the light in a way that ash and bone never do.

narrator/7b4a6497b54e1b55.text: A bed that hasn't been slept in, and a chair pulled up to the wall that adjoins her daughter's room. The plaster is worn smooth at the height of an ear.

narrator/7b58e031df288434.text: When the last man-at-arms goes down into the frost, the squires come forward from their stones, one by one, and each of them touches the banner and goes back.

narrator/7b81f772cece87d1.text: The air around the cairn claps shut like two great hands, and the summit rings like a struck bell.

narrator/7b8bdb4c569a8b0e.text: Ratatoille sends everyone away from the fire for an hour and won't say why. When you're let back, there's a cloth laid on the ground, and a supper on it that has no business existing in this valley: something roasted, something in a sauce, bread that's still warm, and a little pastry at each place with an apricot in it.

narrator/7b983bebd2ea32c9.text: The drive climbs between dead trees to a house that burned a long time ago and never quite finished falling down. Above it a square tower stands against the sky, with no light at the top of it at all.

narrator/7bc29dcd70baf44a.text: He holds your eye for a long moment, his painted face smiling the smile it was painted with. Then he wipes the slate very slowly and writes, small:

narrator/8cda0120382cdf25.text: Five long grooves in the bark, higher than a tall man can reach, and sap still beading in them. Fresh.

narrator/8cdfb3ea889758ac.text: A table older than the house it's in, by the look of it. Somebody has carved notches into the edge, in rows, the way you'd count days.

narrator/8cf3a12e76c9973b.text: A deep hearth with a fire that burns green and gives off far more heat than it should. The stewpot over it has never, you'd bet, been empty.

narrator/8cfaa78e76756fbd.text: A stone porch. Somebody has hung a sprig of dried flowers over the door, and it has been there so long it's the colour of the stone.

narrator/8d2e2d5abf7357fb.text: Black stalks in hard ground. One bed has been dug over recently, deep, and filled in again, and nothing has been planted in it.

narrator/8d44de3997a323c6.text: Something lies in the niche, wrapped in a nun's grey veil gone soft as moss. Whoever put it there meant it to wait. It has waited.

narrator/8d4654c3c8a0076d.text: She drops the roses on the Petrovs' step, one by one, very neatly, and goes up the wall of the house and over the roof like a spider. Toward the church.

narrator/8d473f6d74429301.text: She looks at the card for a long time, and does not touch it again.

narrator/8d513109a6f8b455.text: The ravens keep watch in the oak all night, and twice they all shout at once, at something you never see.

narrator/8d5cde2c8c681c7f.text: Lady Wachter wants it wet. Not now, in daylight, with the watch walking past it. Tonight.

narrator/8d677c3a469cc78c.text: Fresh earth, a board with his name burned into it, and someone's wildflowers already gone brown.

narrator/8d70e94da3ba7c3f.text: Haul her in on the drum before you take the meat down. She chokes on the collar for a minute, and a minute is long enough.

narrator/8d7f522de244914e.text: The crossroads at night: a signpost, a gallows, and a field of low mounds that the dark has gone very quiet around.

narrator/8d81bcae8d794623.text: He raises his cup to you, drinks from it for the first time, and winces.

narrator/8da4965aae7d1b0c.text: The cold takes your breath, and then, strangely, gives it back. By the time the water reaches your knees it feels like a summer pond at noon, though the snow is still falling on your shoulders.

narrator/8dbe6bd0b81b82e4.text: Twelve rays, for the twelve who marched with Markovia. One ray is shorter than the others, cut down later with a knife: for the one who turned back.

narrator/8dc05cf351edeafe.text: Pale lights hang in the doorways of the drowned houses, the way lamps used to.

narrator/8dc724982189aa2d.text: Under the sleeve, a bite: half healed, ringed in angry red, the marks of long teeth. She pulls the sleeve down fast and glares at you.

narrator/8dd21effed508cd3.text: The chain runs free with a long iron rattle, then stops. Somewhere ahead, the chant approves.

narrator/8dd549ef043ab138.text: The stair comes up into the loft between the rafters. Every board you step on announces you.

narrator/8df2f0d33f6d9ec1.text: The prayer is short and plain, and for once something in this valley seems to be listening. The red ring round the bite fades slowly, like a blush.

narrator/8dfaf1c77005161b.text: The three of them are back on the castle road, exactly where you left them, as if they've been standing there ever since.

narrator/8e045b14919ca85a.text: Grey shapes come through the pines at a run, low and fast, and the ones behind are already standing up on two legs.

narrator/8e16c7ea9a622864.text: Torchlight on the track ahead: a dozen dead knights of the Order on foot, swords out, standing around something that is still smoking on the ground.

narrator/8e290062edfbada9.text: Behind the wizard's casks, in a nest of old corks, a stoppered decanter. Pull the stopper and water runs out of it, and keeps running.

narrator/8e5a7368de3198f5.text: The servants' stair lets you down into low vaults that smell of smoke and onions, and of something under the onions.

narrator/8e64fc762825c20b.text: The rocking chair has stopped. The loft is only a loft now: straw, rafters, a gear and two empty cages, and a smell that will take a long time to leave.

narrator/8e67a6236f4ea313.text: A howl goes up close by, then another, and then grey shapes are pouring through the pines on both sides of the trail. Kiril's wolves are hunting, and tonight they've found something better than deer.

narrator/8e7a3a099d6ea902.text: Windows on every side, the grey sky, and the heart hanging in the middle of it all, beating.

narrator/8e7b5b4150a74234.text: You are among them before the chant can end. The effigy cracks too soon, and what drags itself out of its chest is half-made and furious.

narrator/8e80f94165612378.text: Round her throat is a black velvet ribbon tied in a neat bow, with a small silver bell on it that doesn't ring when she moves.

narrator/8e845df43fb34fd3.text: The door shuts behind you on its own. The carriage moves off with no word and no whip, faster than horses should, up into the mountains and the cloud.

narrator/8e97ffa580cd409e.text: The house is quiet now, with the stillness of something that has been fed. Every door you pass stands open.

narrator/8eab424ab32e22c6.text: The grace comes out steady. Every candle on the table leans away from the speaker at once, then stands straight again.

narrator/8eb55a06a1d1b64a.text: A cairn of flat stones by the track, each one carried up from the road by somebody going to the abbey for healing. The newest stone is a very small one, the size a child could carry.

narrator/8eccbc630c39d5f9.text: She crosses the hall to him. He offers his arm, she takes it, and the doors close behind them without a sound.

narrator/8edca335154d6b1c.text: Ilka looks at you a long moment, and decides to let you have the lie. It is the kindest thing anyone does in the mill today.

narrator/8edfb31315aea592.text: The courtyard is cracked flagstones and blown leaves, and running across the middle of it is a long pale scar where the stones look frost-bitten in high summer.

narrator/8eedf0192a3cdc3c.text: Among the bones the roc dropped on the shelf lies a traveller who almost got away: on his back, a folded cloak of black feathers that stirs in the wind as if it wants to open.

narrator/8ef6c534b8443992.text: Cairns mark the path where the snow would otherwise hide it. Some of them are old. Some of them are people.

narrator/8f013a2eee762d40.text: One small cask for every year, set by for a wizard who never came back to drink them. The oldest seal is cracked, and the cask beneath it is quite dry.

narrator/8f1eca552491b146.text: Bones on the shelf: an ox, a horse, and something that wore armour, picked so clean the mail is still on the ribs.

narrator/8f44f69827ff8165.text: Burial niches, row on row, each with a little carved sunburst. The oldest names are worn away entirely, but someone still dusts them.

narrator/8f462d06a6333e45.text: Vladimir is down on the stones by the stair, his body already trying to knit itself whole with a sound like ice forming on a pond. His voice comes from inside the armour, quite calm.

narrator/8f4d4add99017bac.text: The stair ends on an open platform under the sky, ringed by a low parapet. In the middle, on a stone plinth, stands a great iron cradle full of old ash, and the wind up here sounds like someone breathing.

narrator/8f59d3349211345f.text: Old bones, very large, very cold. If there's anything else here, it isn't speaking to you yet.

narrator/8f69152d293c802d.text: Afterwards she carries him out herself, and won't be helped, and buries him under a rowan on the hillside with a crow feather in the bark above him.

narrator/8f6f4cf2aa4666f0.text: An empty silver cage swings from the dead pine, door open. Nobody's watching it now.

narrator/8f75f1c24228ca65.text: Pines crowd up to the house's west wall. Nothing sings in them.

narrator/8f78df59b89063f8.text: Cold stone, dripping vaults and the sound of chains settling. Far off, a furnace breathes.

narrator/8f7c415d0038b21d.text: You leave him turning. Behind you, the rope creaks once, as if he has shifted his weight.

narrator/8fafd0277e0ac5ef.text: Plain crystal, smoky and cold, worth a few coins: the magic in this room isn't in the orb. It is in the soot on the walls, and the soot is waiting for someone to take the offering.

narrator/8fbccd8b09f2659c.text: The Baron's watch closes ranks around the dais, spears levelled at the crowd, and at you.

narrator/8fd0d28cc8c15a57.text: At the heart of the scarecrow field stands one that isn't like the others: twice a man's height, its body a heap of rotted silk and lace, white and yellow and grey, with faces in the stitching if you look too long.

narrator/8fdf9f88d7649046.text: A channel cut into the rock, dry, running from a stone gate in the wall to the cracks in the floor. Behind the gate you can hear water: the melt off the whole north face of the mountain, waiting.

narrator/8fee80e7d4987494.text: You pass the bread. Liriel takes a piece and tells him it's the best she's ever had, and Ratatoille says it isn't, it's a little dense, and looks as though he might float away.

narrator/8ff2aa269ffbe8b2.text: It could be anything. In Barovia, it usually is.

narrator/8ff338106be4a0a7.text: Three of the stone knights were never stone. They step off their plinths into the aisle, visors turning together.

narrator/8ff69692b8e5f7dc.text: The oven is cold. The cauldron has a skin on it. The bread on the table is going green.

narrator/8ffb5776160d82f9.text: The den erupts in yellow eyes and snapping, and the cave is suddenly much too small.

narrator/900d2178dc92a8a4.text: A rutted lane under dripping pines, the trees so close on either side that the sky is a grey stripe overhead. Cart tracks, footprints, and nobody.

narrator/90214c45b0605771.text: Lanterns on the road ahead, swaying in a line: a funeral procession, out at the one hour no living Barovian would walk. Mourners in grey carry an open coffin between them. It is empty.

narrator/90299703a92d97e6.text: And at the back, on the carver's doorstep, one old man is laughing so hard he has to hold the doorpost. Old Pavel, with tears running into his beard. He can't stop.

narrator/902f6f0170f7a631.text: Ratatoille asks, very formally, for the use of the kitchen. Davian looks at him the way he looks at weather, and waves a hand.

narrator/904311fb90d306d1.text: A crypt with Gustav Durst's name over it.

narrator/907de6813a663410.text: She takes the bags down herself, one at a time, and counts them, and her lips move as she counts.

narrator/908e23a35245f9c9.text: From somewhere out on the water, through the mist, a bell tolls once. Then again. There is no bell on Lake Zarovich, and no church on its shores.

narrator/908f357ce65d6687.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Yog, the unbroken. It outlasted everyone who worshipped it. That was the whole of its gift, and the whole of its price."

narrator/90a382f6a131f141.text: You hit the water running. Bluto swings at you with a fist like a wet stone and misses, and you have the sack before he can try again.

narrator/90acb9e9325b5180.text: The jar bursts on the flagstones. Among the shards, a dull grey stone splits in two. Across the room, Exethanter puts down his pen and sits very still.

narrator/90b80c63fd777550.text: The skeleton's finger gives up a plain gold ring. Inside the band, someone engraved a name too worn to read.

narrator/90bd4fac4199c851.text: The cuffs open with Emil's key. Thistle catches him before he hits the straw.

narrator/90c47f576c16839b.text: Ilka comes to the door and looks at the girl for a long time, and says, "You've got Toma's ears." Toma says he has his own ears.

narrator/90c95506188097f6.text: Cold air breathes out through a seam beside the firebox. There is room behind that stone.

narrator/90da9097bc76c09c.text: It happens all at once. The Baron is shouting for the watch. Lady Wachter steps out of the crowd with her chin up and armed men behind her. Father Lucian pushes toward the dais from the other side, hands raised, calling for calm.

narrator/90e2d437bd3a093c.text: A painted wagon, a horse hobbled in the reeds, a fire built small and hot the way hunters build them. Somebody here expects company, and has planned for the wrong kind.

narrator/90e8a7df1708acc9.text: A line of glyphs crosses the gallery floor, set by the wardens to keep the curious from the amber. They're still awake.

narrator/90fbe718e7aa1a42.text: Liriel is awake before anyone, kneeling at the edge of the camp facing east, where the dawn would be if this valley had one. Her lips are moving. After a while they stop.

narrator/91170db30a84139e.text: Then he goes to the west gate, which should be shut, and isn't. A rider on a black horse waits outside it with his hood up. Dobre holds out the last copy.

narrator/912ef281bf7920fa.text: A carved mahogany table laid with silver and crystal, eight high-backed chairs around it, and a ninth place set where there is no chair at all.

narrator/9134964b6c335095.text: She closes her eyes. Something in her face can't decide between laughing and throwing the spyglass off the mountain.

narrator/913a152cdd41a23e.text: A shed of grey boards. Through the gaps you can see rakes, a shovel, sacks. And on a nail, a sickle hung very carefully, blade inward.

narrator/91502d579e4d4309.text: A wooden box of candle stubs and a flint, for anyone who wants to light one. A slate beside it says, in chalk, TAKE ONE, LEAVE ONE, PRAY FOR KREZK.

narrator/91685aec1255689b.text: The antechamber stinks of the heap. It is coming.

narrator/9171d90f028e8418.text: An old man with a net in his lap, mending a hole he's already mended twice.

narrator/91789475781f6204.text: The first page is in a different hand, black and beautifully formed. She came for the silver's gold. Let her lie on it and never spend a coin. Keep her hungry and keep her hot, and feed her what I send. Her name is Sarkhaza. Don't say it to her face; she likes it too much.

narrator/917fbd76237cc056.text: Doru still clings to the ceiling above the cells, exactly where you left him. Only his eyes have moved.

narrator/91b163cf069677f1.text: Hedda stops at the foot of the altar and looks at the dust on it for a long moment. Then she kneels on the cold step, the way her chapel taught her, and takes out the silver raven.

narrator/91dd38e2925cdcc2.text: Among the chained books one has been read in the last year: the dust on its spine is thinner, and a strip of good paper marks a page near the end. The margins are crowded with a small, fast, educated hand.

narrator/91e2da0594dff2de.text: The broken cart's floor is a hand's width too high. Under the false boards, wrapped in sacking, lies a plain cloth bag that is much bigger on the inside than the out.

narrator/9206bb19b0e7cfda.text: His hand is flat on the table, pressing, as if the table might get up and leave.

narrator/92208adab43b7ab2.text: Sorin is sweeping snow off the stones around the pool with Kasha's broom, very carefully, round the little graves first.

narrator/92283de0f2c7f06f.text: The lane runs straight up between the rows. On both sides the dead vines rustle, though the air is perfectly still.

narrator/9228dcd44b941ba1.text: The dragon lies along the bier with his wings folded like a cloak, every bone in its place, except at the end of the long neck, where there is nothing at all. Frost furs the ribs and doesn't melt.

narrator/9229302cfccb3198.text: You reach in among the roots, and your fingers close on something that is not a root, not cold, and not yours.

narrator/92362376a1aec1b4.text: Nobody comes. The watch is already dead, properly this time. He keeps screaming anyway.

narrator/9241d98f2a9d02f6.text: A cart with a broken axle, half in the ditch, picked clean. The harness was cut, not broken. Whoever drove it left in a hurry, and on foot.

narrator/925174a8d2b71d1a.text: A real fire, banked high, with a kettle on the hook. It's the first fire in Barovia you've seen that someone made for comfort rather than defence.

narrator/925cbfd386c314ea.text: A crowded little shop: puppets, dolls, music boxes and wind-up creatures on every shelf, every one of them looking at the door. A curtained doorway leads back to the workshop.

narrator/92737cfd4b0dbfab.text: Clovin stands on his trough with his hat in his feathered hand, and doesn't say anything at all.

narrator/9279970ec80c4ec6.text: The parapet is old work, every stone fitted dry. Long scratches run across its top, in fours, as if something very large once landed here to see what it had caught.

narrator/92a66c41bd97e4d8.text: The last entry is a single name, Walter. Where the others say given, it says first.

narrator/92a69da30b28cb1e.text: It wants the dragon's fire, and you aren't carrying it. That waits in the mausoleum, in the frost on his bones.

narrator/92b7d587c671ec62.text: A net hung from a hook, sagging with meat gone green. Venison, you hope.

narrator/92b7fb73b3a21349.text: Steps cut into the ice by hands that have been dead for centuries, worn into shallow bowls by the feet of everyone who climbed up after them.

narrator/92d507c4262b0183.text: You say the names. Mihai. Old Dorota. The Lupescu twins. The ones worn smooth, as near as you can guess them.

narrator/92dd25ac3a2f2b76.text: Below, the woods and the far grey lake, and here and there a farmhouse with no light in it. Every one of them could see this tower once.

narrator/92e1695c84944cf7.text: He starts to hum, low and tuneless, and won't stop. It sounds like wind in dry branches.

narrator/92fc1b4234b6a201.text: The east wing is a ring of sarcophagi, each one a block of amber taller than a man, and each one has something in it. Something in all six of them is talking, softly, at once.

narrator/930e6f163a0fe505.text: The fermenting hall: eight great vats in two rows under the beams. The vats are full, and what's in them is breathing.

narrator/930ff09f13d27df0.text: Under the ledge, where the pilgrims left their bundles for the climb, there are nine purses of offerings for the temple, and the lamp-pole Mother Ecaterina carried up the pass, white with frost that doesn't melt.

narrator/932e21e05f354b34.text: A stag's head over the hearth, antlers dusted, glass eyes fixed on the door. The only thing in the den that isn't a wolf.

narrator/9343fcc9cafbca42.text: A trough frozen solid, with a goat's beard frozen into the top of it. The goat seems to have got away. Mostly.

narrator/93608b4799eb9c80.text: You tell him where she is. He smiles like a man who already knew, and only wanted to hear you say it.

narrator/93629bf095a18d00.text: You speak the old words for the dead, the ones every faith in the valley shares: rest, and be remembered, and let the living go.

narrator/9366fe20d895b162.text: The letter is read aloud in the middle of the square, every courteous word of it, down to the single initial at the bottom. When it's finished, nobody is looking at Lady Wachter. Everyone is looking at the castle on its cliff, and then at her.

narrator/936e42e03f2f26b3.text: She takes a child by each hand and goes down the stair with them, slowly, talking about soup the whole way.

narrator/93973d6f819a3c31.text: Low on the milestone, under a year of lichen, someone has cut a small bird with its wings swept back, and beside it four neat rows of ten strokes.

narrator/939e7b21cce82a91.text: A long cell with rusty shackles on every wall and stiff black robes on hooks between them. One prisoner never left: a skeleton in a tattered robe, a gold ring still on its finger.

narrator/93b3112ef9943ed0.text: The trail is worn smooth and wide, the way paths get when a great many feet use them. Some of the prints in the mud are boots. Most of them aren't.

narrator/93c5b812e88fb119.text: A narrow servery with a stair going down. Warm air rises from below, and the smell of bread.

narrator/93de204a5f988fc5.text: The tomb is quiet now. The braziers burn green and cold, and the coffin waits on its dais.

narrator/93ecb402759a1ecb.text: Lucian bars the doors and lights every candle he owns. You take your places in the nave. For hours there is nothing but the wax burning down and the priest's voice saying the long prayers under his breath.

narrator/93f1de9474d531e4.text: She stands between you and the cave mouth, but her eyes keep sliding past you, down the slope, west toward the Krezk road. She is listening for something coming home, and dreading it.

narrator/94041bfa32eeaf9a.text: The guardian's base is hollow, and something wrapped in oilcloth has been pushed right to the back of it, where no bird or rain could reach.

narrator/940e1ccbd37ed5be.text: The family in the portrait over the hearth keeps its eyes on the stairs. On you, specifically.

narrator/9413ad6a41c2e6cc.text: Morgantha unhooks a ring of iron keys from her apron and opens both cages, humming. The children don't move until she has sat back down.

narrator/9415627b438d9d8e.text: A tall iron case under a sheet. You lift the corner. You put the corner down again.

narrator/942252e9e57760e4.text: Soot is creeping out of the hearths along the floor, black and low, pooling in the middle of the hall.

narrator/942396b68326dcda.text: Her face gives you nothing but its scars. Whatever she feels about the castle, she has had a long time to bury it.

narrator/94391e3c18c9f21b.text: A milestone with the village's name chiselled off and a single word scratched in its place: TURN BACK. Under it, in a different hand: WHERE TO?

narrator/9450b1c3acb39e13.text: A vaulted hall on thick pillars. Chains hang from rings in the walls at the height of a man's wrists.

narrator/949cab62abc8b01b.text: Weeks of fasting, and his cheeks are fuller than yours.

narrator/94a60997f029ef39.text: The vines rise up off their trellises on both sides of the lane, and the vineyard comes for you row by row.

narrator/94dbeda1b872353f.text: The inside of the wagon is a hunter's armoury squeezed into a Vistani caravan: stakes, mirrors, bundles of herbs, and a neat little bed nobody seems to sleep in.

narrator/94dc1ea0a4387a1d.text: Rows of plain crypts for the people who ran the house: stewards, cooks, a master of horse. Their names are cut as neatly as their masters' were.

narrator/94e3448106486fc1.text: The boy is gone between one breath and the next. What drops from the ceiling is only hunger.

narrator/94efa484d505b429.text: Under the last cot, where a child once hid the best things in the world, a pair of gold lions no bigger than your thumb. They are warm, and one of them is purring.

narrator/94fa6b038d49763d.text: Two leaning posts mark where the village ends and the road west begins. Stop at them before you go.

narrator/950fa9e172bc6033.text: The carriage rolls over the drawbridge without slowing and stops before the keep. The doors are waiting for you.

narrator/95168178cc42dbd0.text: The amber drinks. You feel it, a tug at the wrist like a child pulling your hand, and then the doors are open and your hand is white and cold. In the alcove beside them, something tall wakes up hungry.

narrator/951915140d5baec8.text: He stops at the back gate of Wachterhaus, and a gloved hand takes another.

narrator/951bd03ac4e660af.text: The stove is cold and the pot on it is full of soup that set days ago. Two bowls wait beside it.

narrator/9531f57384285205.text: The furnace is black and dripping, and the sluice wheel is turned as far as it goes.

narrator/95364a758b84c5a2.text: Drying racks for fish, the poles grey with age and the nets on them stiff and empty. A few dried heads still hang from the top rail, picked clean by the crows.

narrator/9536f25c4b02639a.text: Two small punctures at her throat, under the collar, as neat as a seamstress's work. She did not die of age. She died of visits.

narrator/95401eea8a2934dd.text: The oven roars as if somebody had thrown open its door.

narrator/955f9681150e8cd3.text: You look up into the blank face, and for one long moment it looks back with every face you have ever feared.

narrator/9564e4698b803fac.text: He picks it up. His hands have stopped shaking. Ilse's haven't, quite, and he pretends not to see, which is the kindest thing a soldier knows how to do.

narrator/956c33de204eae46.text: Blades, mail shirts, rope, lamp oil and grain sacks, each with a price chalked on a slate in a hand that has clearly done this for years and has stopped apologising.

narrator/9570ef1022fd6bb6.text: Under it, in a different hand altogether, black and beautifully formed:

narrator/9572399fb89dde74.text: The heap in the corner is a crater now, a wet hollow the shape of something very large that has gotten up.

narrator/957a49bd2bc5c5f1.text: A drum of black chain as tall as a man, a crank as long as a spear, and a ratchet that has been oiled by nobody for a very long time.

narrator/957daa8be4a92d8c.text: The coffin is empty. A bed of dark earth lies in it, pressed into the shape of a tall man, and cold.

narrator/958144646b9b2e94.text: They aren't frightened of him. They're frightened of the abbey. Every one of those jokes is about the man who has their dead. Nobody in this square is going to laugh at the Abbot. They might laugh at a man who's had a hard time of it.

narrator/95817c4706e0ca3d.text: The jaw in the amber has stopped chewing. It is listening, hungrily, to whoever carries its gift.

narrator/9591de95dac36022.text: A trough of stream water for the horses, scrubbed clean. It is the only water in the camp that anyone drinks without thinking twice.

narrator/959ad729801b1f84.text: The family's floor is silent. Even the cold has gone out of it.

narrator/95af419bc03771a9.text: Hooves on the road behind you, a great many of them, coming fast. You get off the track just in time.

narrator/95bda2ca79555b1a.text: The last window in the house that isn't brick, and it is closing.

narrator/95ea40288ba2355f.text: You drag your boots through the chalk. The glow sputters along the lines and goes out, like a fuse that has been stamped on.

narrator/95f4c5fd24d3f425.text: She steps back from the edge, one pace and then another, and lets out a breath she seems to have been holding for a very long time.

narrator/95f4f7a9d10450e6.text: Nelu comes into the firelight a step behind you, filthy, shaking, alive. Big Tobar drops the wheel he's holding on his own foot and doesn't notice.

narrator/95f97887093def77.text: Lady Wachter sits in the Baron's great hall, in the Baron's chair, with her own tea service on his table. The festival portraits are stacked face to the wall.

narrator/a28836a434b756ce.text: Then the hunger comes back. But you have the moment, and you use it.

narrator/a2d9a64d02f4830f.text: You know whose wounds it drinks. Somewhere below you, a man is being spared every one of them.

narrator/a6b9cfbf5bd53a71.text: White, cold and patient. The road you came in on is somewhere inside it, and the mist would rather you didn't go looking.

narrator/a6bd7b962e301cc4.text: The mist does not lift. You have bought your lives, and you will spend them here, under a lord who wants nothing more from you.
