narrator/a77001a5e5501f76.text: It is quick, and it is quiet, and afterward none of you can remember who held the knife.

narrator/a77715e47dab38b0.text: You sleep in the lee of the crag. The ravens keep watch in the oak above you, and twice in the night they all shout at once, at something you never see.

narrator/a7967176ed2b79bb.text: One of the histories weighs nothing at all. Its pages have been cut into a hollow, and in the hollow lies a slim wand of black wood.

narrator/a7972d48165362c7.text: The Belview sweeps a clean path across the flags, looks at it, and sweeps it again. Snow is already falling on it.

narrator/a79ff67a4660527d.text: Up close the vines aren't dead, quite. They're waiting, like a man holding his breath under water. The grapes on them are small, hard and sour.

narrator/a7a13ad538d66f79.text: Fresh casks branded with a raven. The Martikovs' wine reaches even this cellar again.

narrator/a7a5642fd85bfeb9.text: Webs as fine as breath cover the lid. Under them the letters are there, but the webs move when you try to read.

narrator/a7b424bab585f8f1.text: After a moment the rider lifts a gloved hand in return. Then he closes it, one finger at a time, as if around something small.

narrator/a7e881d3f4740d20.text: Exethanter's sparks drop to whoever among you carries a gift, as if he could smell it on them.

narrator/a7f5f52ec785d15b.text: 'Two at each gate, changed at dusk and at midnight. The midnight pair drink.' He winces. 'Don't tell them it was me.'

narrator/a80dc5d18edaf1dd.text: A pine scored with claw marks far higher than a wolf could reach on four legs. Its branches start low enough to climb, if you don't think about who climbed it last.

narrator/a8153a9dec2f54a6.text: Gauzy drapes, upholstered chairs, stained glass of singers along one wall, little alabaster dancers on the mantel, and a harpsichord with its lid raised, as if someone has just stood up from it.

narrator/a81de9e1e60328a2.text: She tucks the arm inside her coat and turns her shoulder to you, and that's the end of that.

narrator/a83487f1b97c895a.text: He goes, limping, toward the hills. Whether he goes home or back to the chant, you can't tell.

narrator/a83a51c4c2734581.text: He finishes the song. Then, very carefully, in Anna's voice, he says the line that ends it every night through the shutters:

narrator/a843ea8b72857cda.text: Escher comes up out of the chair without seeming to use his legs.

narrator/a84e2f28d989f1ff.text: It is very quiet, and very cold, and the books smell of ice instead of dust.

narrator/a85304beade3e5bc.text: The lock gives. Inside, coin and a scroll, packed square, and nothing personal at all. Not one letter, not one keepsake.

narrator/a85911f4b637a339.text: A chalk board of what each regular owes the house. Most columns are short, but one, headed ISMARK, runs to the bottom of the board and carries on along the wall.

narrator/a85d85c9492a3a04.text: The walls of this crypt are scratched with sigils from floor to ceiling, as if someone wanted to be very sure about something.

narrator/a88da3fd50674970.text: Ilse opens the cracked book Jory carried in his drum: forty names in the captain's own hand. Merrow's eyes go to it and stay there.

narrator/a893d3082683622c.text: Godrick has tied his sword to his wrist with a bootlace. He has been sitting up with it like that since before dawn.

narrator/a8a19ce07cdd9539.text: The workshop smells of pine and varnish and nothing else. Henrik is whistling. Badly, but whistling.

narrator/a8c2f279fe68614e.text: The hut lies on its side in the mud like a dead ox, its root legs snapped and splayed, its door hanging by one hinge. The scarecrows lie face down in the reeds. Baba Lysaga sits beside the wreck, rocking.

narrator/a8c7ea721afb9f74.text: A fresh grave beside a headstone that reads only "Beloved". The earth is piled neatly, ready to go back in.

narrator/a8d73041f3e4ef4b.text: He twists a heavy ring off his finger and tosses it to you. It's worth more than most houses in the valley.

narrator/a8dfba906ac64a1a.text: Hoofprints in the slush, goats', all going up. None coming down.

narrator/a8f6d782be051802.text: They step aside, one to each verge, and let you pass. When you look back, the road is empty.

narrator/a8f99dfc6a5465b8.text: It's the oldest word between them, and it still works. His back straightens before he can stop it.

narrator/a8fce709f36b8bb5.text: She takes the ribbon out of her hair and lays it on the lid, over the stone sunburst.

narrator/a8fd7f994c1971d4.text: You dream of sails turning in fire, and wake with the smell of smoke in your hair.

narrator/a8ffaeaaf0bd42b8.text: Mandibles. Thousands of them, working at wood and silk, in the dark where Elisabeth meant to lie. Whatever is in there has been eating for years.

narrator/a902f3a23ac41da4.text: A hairline seam runs round one flagstone, and the wall beside it has a long, low slot cut in it at knee height.

narrator/a90c8de33d58e02b.text: A music box with a dancer who turns, and turns, and slowly comes to face you, though the tune has stopped.

narrator/a92a8a15bd07f1b5.text: You sleep in shifts on the hillside. All night the mill's one window glows, and the smell of baking drifts down the slope.

narrator/a930c74a8cc1e1e4.text: Open coffins stand in a row along the wall, and the earth in them is fresh.

narrator/a936f0463fc1caca.text: A gallery so narrow two people can't pass. Every door along it has something to say: claw marks, steam, a lock.

narrator/a93af930d5c09134.text: Stone stairs wind up inside the wall. Every room is tidy in the way of a man who expects to leave in a hurry.

narrator/a93d59ee74b9b8ab.text: A thin, cheerful girl with flour on her nose. That's all you see.

narrator/a94651f0c61abe6a.text: You tell her. She doesn't cry. She stands up, and the beans go everywhere, and she starts for the lane, and you have to tell her the rest: Granny, and the next dark night.

narrator/a94b7e83bdeb00f8.text: Dead knights stand at the broken gate now, faces turned toward the castle. They step aside for you without a word, the way sentries step aside for officers.

narrator/a96b0951e14b3b7b.text: One mound in the hanged men's field is newer than the rest, and shallow. Under a skin of earth, a pair of soft boots that make no sound when you set them down.

narrator/a9782313c984794a.text: A dragonchess board, three tiers of it, with a game in progress. Every piece on every side is carved from black stone.

narrator/a979bc1ccdf375f0.text: A scratch that never heals, over the heart, and no hand laid on her: that is the mark a doll leaves when a thorn goes through it. Somebody in this marsh knows how to make that kind of doll, and lives on a stump.

narrator/a98c5a96632681a5.text: Purple hooded flowers, planted in rows and weeded. Wolfsbane, a whole garden of it, at a werewolf's front door. Either somebody here has a sense of humour, or a plan.

narrator/a9a08c0900145487.text: She swallows, nods, and goes. You hear her bare feet on the stair for a long time, and then you don't.

narrator/a9e2878c65dc08e5.text: A tall black horse, saddled and bridled, tied short beside Arrigal's wagon. It is the only horse in the camp ready to leave at a moment's notice, and it knows it.

narrator/a9e5a5ebe0e2819e.text: The guardroom, empty. The table still has dice on it, mid-game.

narrator/a9ed3c1af8b6b8e8.text: The dragon's desk has a drawer a human hand would never find. In it, a wand of pale wood that twitches toward the door when you hold it.

narrator/a9f888d546aa5ca6.text: The attic stair shudders under you like a ladder someone is trying to shake loose.

narrator/a9f8e31fd9b82757.text: A throne room built for crowds and kept for one. The throne stands on a dais at the far end, and the floor between is worn smooth by people who were made to walk it slowly.

narrator/aa22710562bf9a49.text: Blades slide out of the paneling like teeth, and the house bites.

narrator/aa235159fe8b92b0.text: She is out of her chair before the words are finished, with a carving knife in one fist and green fire in the other.

narrator/aa2a97f73421d023.text: The cellar is quiet now except for the drip of a cask somebody cracked. The far end smells of turned earth.

narrator/aa56739943d9c5b0.text: At the bottom of the dry well, a coil of black rope that moves when nothing touches it. It has caught a rat already, and is in no hurry to let go.

narrator/aa5ccbee8dc73f39.text: Midnight. The carriage comes up the castle road with its lamp swinging and no hand on the reins: one black horse in the traces, and an empty harness beside it, waiting.

narrator/aa5db31ce5c21194.text: Ratatoille is cooking tonight, which is normal. He's cooking badly, which isn't. The stew has caught on the bottom and he hasn't noticed.

narrator/aa63cc35e94e74b5.text: A jester's grave: bells, a painted mask and a joke nobody remembers. Nothing else.

narrator/aa6c54ccb2c6b30d.text: She looks at you the way mothers look at children who have just said they didn't touch the honey.

narrator/aa8081362d43f717.text: He follows you for three spells, then loses the thread and gets angry, and the room fills with a short, furious snowfall that settles on everybody.

narrator/aa8e12d3a4571d83.text: A wine press as old as the winery, oak and iron, worked by a bar that takes four men to turn. The wood is stained purple to the grain, and smooth wherever a hand has pushed it for a hundred years.

narrator/aab04efc0d99d9a3.text: An old stump chewed to splinters, with a knot dead in its middle that is chewed worst of all. Two knives are still in it.

narrator/aab6b4d4b46eef40.text: Under the nursemaid's mattress, folded with care, lies a grey-green cloak that was never worn. Its edges blur when you look at them. A card is pinned to it, with a single initial: G.

narrator/aadb25fdfd2e5c67.text: A lovely figure lies curled in the clear amber as if asleep in a warm bed, one hand cupped as though holding out something sweet. When you look closer, the smile has a few too many teeth.

narrator/aaee01168bb00245.text: The lines flare white and you're torn loose from everywhere at once, and then slammed back, with a sound like a door blown shut in your bones.

narrator/aafcb995b78e8bc5.text: Davian opens his mouth to answer, and doesn't. He looks across to where Adrian is scrubbing a cask he has already scrubbed twice.

narrator/ab02b3d8cdec156f.text: A dead oak leans out over the slope, and every branch of it is full of ravens. None of them make a sound. All of them are watching you.

narrator/ab070d4ac641f837.text: The coffin waits on its trestles beside the fresh grave. Ireena stands at the head of it, very straight, as if guarding the door of a house.

narrator/ab2add4f7578ce34.text: A neat black wagon with silver trim and a small locked strongbox under the step. The window has a black curtain drawn tight.

narrator/ab51011be45301d7.text: An iron-bound door in a round tower of black stone, with no handle, no keyhole and no knocker. Under the moss on the lintel, letters have been cut very deep. The wood is warm to the touch, like a sleeping animal.

narrator/ab51f93e9fe47c3c.text: You keep to the logs. The bell follows you for a while, always just ahead, and then gives up.

narrator/ab5ba406993d60e1.text: In the water, beside her reflection, there is a second one: a young man in an old-fashioned coat with a sunburst at his breast. You look up. There's nobody beside her. You look down. He's still there.

narrator/ab62fe2eff167c21.text: Bolts of cloth in every colour, and yellow bunting by the yard heaped twice as high as everything else. The bolt of black at the back has not been touched in months.

narrator/ab6889c49fdd02f4.text: The pieces go off in the wind. The horses watch you do it. Then the carriage turns and goes, unhurried, like something that will be back.

narrator/ab705d88f58e92df.text: A howl ends in a word. Something tall comes out of the field on two legs, still wearing the shreds of a coat.

narrator/ab7ff980111b21a9.text: Something about the throne catches the light wrongly, the way a seat does when someone has only just left it.

narrator/ab95f21a6bfab139.text: The words aren't the ones this village uses, but they're said with care, and the earth seems to accept them.

narrator/abacefb8e7600d2f.text: Over the dress, his eyes go to Ireena, and stay there a heartbeat too long.

narrator/abae572e46c13e1d.text: A doorway with no house left behind it, and a horseshoe still nailed over it, points up for luck. It held, in its way: the doorway is the only part standing.

narrator/abc83b8fe66a0964.text: Thorn waves. Then there is nobody to wave at.

narrator/abe20f80174ac322.text: The pews are fuller than they were. People have started coming to church in Vallaki, now that it's the only place nobody bows to the castle.

narrator/abef1ff96fa07bf2.text: The woodpile stands up. It is taller than Grigore's house, logs for ribs and roots for fingers, and the little pale sticks of Bildrath's load come scuttling up the road to join it.

narrator/ac1a5b3523fd0755.text: The capstan turns half a bar. Then the chain is torn out of the drum's grip from below, so hard the bars spin and throw you off them, and runs out again into the rock, rattling, until it's slack.

narrator/ac1bbda686f84fce.text: The great stair arrives at a landing hung with smoke-stained hangings. Every door on the floor is shut except the one to the study, which stands a little open, the way a door does when someone left in a hurry.

narrator/ac1d08a060d609fe.text: A goat. A large, ill-tempered goat with one horn. It stares back until you look away first.

narrator/ac23378b38092f9c.text: The last entry is scratched into the copper in two hands. The first is a warden's. The second is very fine and very sure, and you have seen it before, on letters.

narrator/ac2beee170926a6c.text: Half the stair has become a ramp, nailed together out of crate lids. Blinsky has painted it with stars.

narrator/ac379c14e8b5cac1.text: It stands up off its post. It is much taller standing. Across the field, every other scarecrow lifts its head.

narrator/ac3e64b9228f4f14.text: Zinaida looks down at the grave, and then at Mihail, and says nothing at all. Then there's only Mihail, and the hole, and the spade.

narrator/ac4bc1492aa34ccb.text: You step aside. Ireena looks at you once, and then she stops looking at you at all.

narrator/ac5c4174e6a38908.text: The rope is old and slick with green, and halfway down your hands give. You go into the water to the neck, and it is so cold it hurts your teeth, and something down there brushes your ankle. You come up the rope faster than you went down.

narrator/ac6d98a537a75830.text: Yellow bunting by the furlong, every pennant hemmed by hand. On the back of one, very small, someone has embroidered: please.

narrator/ac6f54c15087a617.text: The road west runs out between the last houses, toward the crossroads. High to the south-west, on a cliff of black rock, a castle sits against the clouds and does not need to be introduced.

narrator/ac8140c67136588c.text: You dig into the drift of coin up to the elbow, and your fingers close on something that isn't money.

narrator/ac8fb756ed15ec40.text: The pin turns halfway and sticks. Ten minutes gone, and it will take another try.

narrator/ac92b7f55024010f.text: Ireena is sitting up, quite still, her eyes on him. Her hand is on her sword, and the hand isn't moving.

narrator/ac983f54d0da43bd.text: Liriel says the evening prayer in a whisper tonight, and when it's done she doesn't put her holy symbol away. She sits turning it in her fingers.

narrator/acbda818666f0d38.text: He is here. He lies in the coffin with his hands folded on his chest, as neat as a body laid out by good servants. His eyes are shut. He does not breathe; he has never needed to.

narrator/acbf223b88f57202.text: The door hums faintly under your palm, like a hive. Whatever it is waiting for, it keeps to itself.

narrator/acc2b143f344b02f.text: An armor stand with nothing on it, its pegs bent, as if something stepped off in a hurry.

narrator/acce8e1b2625f1de.text: At the bottom is a room with a tiny stone table, and beside it a lump of grey clay, shaped like a sleeping heap.

narrator/acebf3b9660dc221.text: Rose listens all the way through. When it's over she looks down at her hands, as if she has only now noticed she can see the floor through them.

narrator/acecaae171f016ee.text: The hatchet goes in and the log bleeds red, slow sap. The grain runs in rings the wrong way round, tightening toward the heart.

narrator/acfe1b28cc317f00.text: The Baron's watch throws down its spears one by one. Vargas Vallakovich stands alone on his dais with his sash crooked, until two of Lady Wachter's men take him by the arms.

narrator/acfecd0034009073.text: East, the road you came in on, small as a thread.

narrator/ad0081c9a8cef4d7.text: A narrow window onto the courtyard far below, where the mist moves in slow circles like water round a drain.

narrator/ad13761e311ff703.text: The same ruts as on the shoulder outside, worn into the floor by a handcart going down full and coming back empty.

narrator/ad25ec4a77d0f85b.text: Beside the furnace, an iron wheel works a sluice gate in a pipe as thick as a man. Water mutters behind it. The green fire roars on, unbothered.

narrator/ad270d37bc89d360.text: Three figures stand on the castle road, just inside the light: grey coats under crimson ones cut for bigger men. The one in the middle has a little bird on his shoulder, stitched in thread that used to be white.

narrator/ad2c7f55dee4a8a6.text: The snow near the edge has the wrong sheen: an overhang, not ground. Your boot finds the difference before your weight does.

narrator/ad3bc08880432967.text: A double set of stocks with a little roof over them, so that nobody in them gets rained on. The Baron is not a cruel man. He would want you to know that.

narrator/ad6d68dc8cb6fbf8.text: He nods slowly, as if you've told him something he already knew, and lies down with his back to the fire.

narrator/ad70b650d8480d1f.text: The vats boil over, and what climbs out of the mash has opinions about guests.

narrator/ad714bb3ad44e17b.text: His eyes find Ireena, and every candle in the chapel leans toward her, all at once, as if a door had opened behind her. Then they straighten.

narrator/ad8571fccbd704b3.text: The curse comes off him like a wet coat. One moment there's a goat in the gap of the pen; the next there's a big bearded man on his hands and knees in the straw, naked and shaking.

narrator/ad9c402f3dbc14e7.text: You come in under the branches one step at a time. The latch is silver and very cold. It opens. The raven drops into your hands, light as a glove, and doesn't make a sound.

narrator/ad9c5ef372669b84.text: She cups her hands and howls back. It's a very good howl. Nobody in camp sleeps for a while after it.

narrator/adc0252296a59ae0.text: Under the weeping she is perfectly clear-headed. She isn't mad; she's guilty, and grief is the only thing loud enough to drown it out.

narrator/adc1edc2ef341e00.text: You sleep in turns on the dry end of the causeway. All night, out on the stump, a hut shifts its weight from root to root, and something hums a lullaby.

narrator/ade3aa39953de712.text: Lady Wachter sits in the Baron's stocks with her back straight and her hair still pinned. People walk wide around her, and she watches each of them go as if writing down their names.

narrator/adead48561fb07ee.text: The footlocker opens on someone else's luggage: a mail shirt, a lantern, a coffer of red potions, a yellow-bound spellbook, a folded cloak. The cult kept whatever its guests brought.

narrator/adf6085845f1b3db.text: At the head, in a chair carved with a dragon's folded wings, sits the only one who turns his head.

narrator/ae068ed2edb87fd3.text: The devil's chapel. The sunburst over the altar has been turned upside down and nailed there, and the pews are full of nothing but cold.

narrator/ae2bdbcd1fd2e993.text: Sacks of coarse grey salt, damp and smelling of the grave. "LARDER" is chalked on each in a careful hand.

narrator/ae2e0fd87b6a3337.text: A long table runs the length of the hall under banners rotted to lace, and at it sit armoured figures, both sides, all the way down. Every one of them is facing the head of the table.

narrator/ae30e568b70f1320.text: The door gives with a dry crack, low down by the hinge. Lavender dust comes out to meet you.

narrator/ae39036717ad1673.text: Lead. Gilt lead, a mountain of it. The count spent good gold leaf on this, and it's the only gold he spent.

narrator/ae3d9c4e26913c99.text: A house with no roof and half its walls, the black water standing in its doorway. A child's shoe is nailed above the door frame, for luck, the way they do it here. It didn't work.

narrator/ae4f9d53ac20afb8.text: Three gowns, all the same size. Behind them, pushed to the back, a fourth in the same size with a stain at the collar.

narrator/ae5640d352878981.text: The rock here is glazed, black and glassy, like the inside of a kiln. Something very hot came out of the mountain once, a long time ago, and touched it.

narrator/ae632bad47124012.text: Morgantha's keys hang on a ring at what was her apron. The cages open at the second try, and the children climb out as stiff as old men.

narrator/ae6924c1d6032b5b.text: One stave of the founder's cask is a door. Behind it, packed in straw, a fat ceramic jug that sloshes, though when you look inside it's empty.

narrator/ae7ca459db0e6061.text: The tower holds up its light like an arm held up in a crowd: here, over here.

narrator/ae824118478904dd.text: Candlelight under the door, and the small clink of cutlery.

narrator/aebe66ea70d74cbf.text: Forty chairs down the long table, a grey coat over the back of every one. At the head sits a broad man with a captain's knot on his shoulder and nothing in his glass.

narrator/aed63682016ef118.text: Izek lies at the foot of the dais. The fire in his arm goes out last, ember by ember, like a lamp being turned down.

narrator/aee0fc30e626dc4b.text: You set the point over his heart and lean on it with all your weight. For a moment the wood will not go in. Then it does.

narrator/aee243c1e9885522.text: His eyes go to the castle the way a compass goes to north. And when the cloak slips, there are two small marks on the inside of his wrist, neat as a sewing needle's. Not enough to hurt him. Enough to listen through.

narrator/aee549f2710d39dc.text: Old Greytooth comes down the trail at a walk, with his pack spread out behind him like a hunt in the old days, and stops at the edge of the light to look at you.

narrator/aefd682cb1c96bcc.text: Ratatoille sits up, folds his blanket into a neat square, and walks to him across the camp with his face as smooth and empty as a clean plate.

narrator/aeff53adc5561ed8.text: The split colossus wears a warden's robe and hood carved in amber. Through the crack you can see right into it: hollow, and packed with old snow. Whatever moved it once has gone.

narrator/af05b3cf4d27017f.text: A workbench covered in wooden heads waiting for faces. One of them already has a face, and it's a red-haired woman's.

narrator/af0656dbb2da7e12.text: A chamber built round one thing: a great drum of black iron, wound with chain, and a capstan to turn it. The chain runs off the drum into a hole in the north wall. It moves, very slightly, in and out.

narrator/af07993682ad2580.text: Under the straw his nails are thick and dark, and there's a ruff of grey hair at the back of his neck that his mother has been cutting. He isn't sick. He's a wolf, nearly all the way, at eight years old.

narrator/af1081b722061fab.text: The grave-lamp still burns at the statue's feet, small and steady, in the middle of all that black water.

narrator/af17634dd2b2b5bd.text: On the rise behind the shacks, a bow creaks. You don't think much of it, then.

narrator/af18a1098d920952.text: The sparks in his sockets keep drifting toward the stair down to the vaults and away again, the way a man's eyes keep finding a door he has locked. Whatever he's forgotten, part of him is glad of it.

narrator/af20d2b40f86c31e.text: The light around him bends toward him the way water bends toward a drain. He is no man: something sent from far above, of the kind that stands behind the saints in old paintings. Something that has stood here far too long.

narrator/af24f134718afe05.text: A small vault behind the hearth, close and dry, with coin sacks against the walls and an iron box in the corner.

narrator/af2962cf5c46f4b3.text: A bell rings as the door opens, and somewhere a pencil starts moving. Every shelf is dusted, every label straight, every price outrageous.

narrator/af64e4553d7f082b.text: You lay the two small bundles in their two small crypts and slide the slabs home. The sound is final and, for once in this house, kind.

narrator/af6e5a7ff4f13be0.text: Crates of stock stacked to the beams, each one stenciled with its contents and its price. One is marked FOR THE BURGOMASTER, PAID, and has never been collected.

narrator/af81cef4dfe094ca.text: The tower is empty now, and just a building. Someone has left the guardroom swept.

narrator/af875bb73de59667.text: A doll in a lacy yellow dress, propped in the window box as if to watch the street. Someone small loved it, and then left it here.

narrator/afa5f88ba5eb8bfa.text: Three names near the end get no answer: the three on the cellar stair. Ilse marks them and doesn't look up.

narrator/afa84d93f53d332c.text: He stands up. He looks round at all of you, and visibly loses his nerve, and visibly gets it back.

narrator/afb513aec1247c9c.text: The small crate by the back wall is empty now. The altar cloth that was in it smelled faintly of incense, even down here.

narrator/afb973a97788a53d.text: Silt and reeds have buried the foot of the plinth. Something under your boots rings hollow.

narrator/afbef76463c86e57.text: The spade goes in easily. They've been digging their own way out every night, and the earth hasn't had time to settle.

narrator/afcb34a9eb01b19b.text: A row of soldiers' faces carved into the tower, each one different, each one stern. Under them, a line of letters: THEY KEPT THE ROAD.

narrator/aff308c54065a129.text: A copper tub full of something dark that has gone stiff at the edges. It isn't water. She is very old, and she does not look it.

narrator/affb294001628a4b.text: The dressing table in the corner stands empty. Morgantha glances at it once, and goes on smiling, and goes on shelling.

narrator/b02576172b5e5a92.text: Since Ireena knelt here, there is a little light low down in the water, like a coal under ash.

narrator/b02a18a913f84bc1.text: The burgomaster's diary said the candlemaker's girl died with a scratch over her heart, like a bramble's. It was never a bramble.

narrator/b038639d8d623f38.text: Green firelight leaks round the shutters, and the whole hut is humming to itself, like an old woman over washing.

narrator/b03b274a23e664c8.text: A square tower above the east wing, with an open lantern room at its top. Even from down here you can see the soot that climbs the parapet like a black tongue.

narrator/b0420b4d3071b00f.text: A rocking chair by the stove. It is perfectly still whenever you look at it.

narrator/b053aa3d47149834.text: He starts the prayer smoothly and then asks the dawn to wait. Every priest of the Morninglord asks it to come.

narrator/b062308b9733bf25.text: You look over. The well goes down past every floor of the castle and doesn't seem to stop.

narrator/b067995e290bc4e8.text: The chained books have titles like instructions. Some of the instructions are for things that should never be done twice.

narrator/b077625bdf9e0960.text: He takes the jar in both hands, carefully, the way you'd hold a bird. Then he looks around for somewhere to put it, opens his mouth, shuts it again, and tucks the jar inside his robe.

narrator/b09a958fe9c91e41.text: She ties it on with cold, quick fingers, and the smile goes out of her eyes for a moment, with relief.

narrator/b0b194724a8938f2.text: The smile is real, and it's held in place with both hands. Under it she's been afraid for so long that she's stopped noticing. She is the only person in this house who isn't afraid of the Baron, and the only one who's afraid for him.

narrator/b0be5e8286790cea.text: Off the path, half buried, a ring of tents has been crushed flat by old snow. Inside, a party of climbers sits where the cold found them, still holding their cups.

narrator/b0da6694bffef77e.text: Furniture under dust sheets, an iron stove, two trunks, and in the corner a bare nook where the plaster is warm to the touch.

narrator/b102ed0b09fca92b.text: The firebox is cold and black. A draught breathes through a seam in the stone beside it.

narrator/b1042148c608d713.text: Someone has to go in after it. The water is black and cold enough to stop a heart.

narrator/b11d2939ecd24ad2.text: She shrugs, as if your words were weather.

narrator/b128aa7afd5a2962.text: The desk faces the bookcase squarely, the way a guard faces a door. Now you know why.

narrator/b135afedc10e8e85.text: The prayer is long, and it costs. Warmth goes out of the caster and into the old man, and for a moment the frost on the chessboard melts and runs. Somewhere inside him, a lock that a witch closed decades ago turns over.

narrator/b13d2ce52ac9d6e8.text: A vaulted hall so high the candles don't reach the ceiling. Grand stairs climb into the dark, and somewhere an organ is playing.

narrator/b141dd8b0b83e071.text: A keeper, or the soot shape of one, flat on the floor beside the dry channel with his arm out toward the sluice gate. He didn't reach it.

narrator/b1592753b8ac8920.text: A long table laid for twenty with the best plate, every chair empty. It has been laid with great care for guests who are not coming.

narrator/b1660eb0adf099ea.text: The lever shrieks as it moves. The flue clangs shut, the fire chokes and dies, and every face along the hall turns to look at you.

narrator/b194ce1214e47791.text: The way out is open, and nothing in this house will stop you leaving now. Nothing in it needs to.

narrator/b197f4777527f67b.text: The top of the tower: windows on every side, a strongbox under the sill, a spiral of copper nails in the floor, now dull and quiet.

narrator/b19a70d1654b7289.text: Casks set aside for a wizard who never comes to collect them. Dust, and the smell of the vintage.

narrator/b19e941e9cf93d88.text: A long, low hall under the roof. Somewhere along it, a child is humming.

narrator/b1b86bca15649509.text: The chandelier over the hall is swaying gently, though there is no wind at all.

narrator/b1d43d4d9fd31e51.text: It comes out whole: a pale thorn as long as a finger, with a little white root on the end of it, still reaching. Luca opens his eyes.

narrator/b1db16a3b9121364.text: Gustav and Elisabeth in oils, younger, dressed for a ball. The dust on the canvas has settled thickest on her face.

narrator/b1e60c01571e2814.text: You walk him down the Old Svalich Road toward the village. He talks the whole way, about Aurica's fever and the doctor and the price of a cart, and every so often he stops talking and looks at the houses, which are all wrong, and starts again.

narrator/b1e83d30d7f6b9a1.text: You speak the word. The glyphs on the floor go dark one after another, like a row of lamps blown out, and the doors swing inward without a sound.

narrator/b1edbe4142d0782e.text: The figure in the clear amber has turned over in its sleep, toward whoever carries its gift, and its smile has grown a little wider.

narrator/b1f67221a82b3065.text: Empty armour, dented and patient. If any of it is hiding something, it's better at standing guard than you are at looking.

narrator/b1fb5a7aa4f63571.text: Torches go to the straw. You kept it dry through the night, and it shows: the wicker catches with a roar, and for a few heartbeats there is a sun in Vallaki, gold and enormous, and the faces in the square are lit with something very close to joy.

narrator/b1fda388150f7010.text: She steps sideways into nothing, cart and all, and the lane is empty. The smell of honey hangs in the air for a long while.

narrator/b213cd62f14d9ca0.text: Something in the cauldron turns over in its sleep. You decide not to stir it.

narrator/b22a86c5f31eaae3.text: Under the chalk circle, one board lifts. Victor hid his best tool where his father would never kneel: a wand of polished bone, warm from the floor.

narrator/b22cdb83ef6dd5f9.text: He looks at the coin, and at you, and then he laughs, a little, the first time all evening.

narrator/b2335a8e7bba459b.text: A carnival wagon in red and gold, with RICTAVIO'S WONDERS painted along the side and a padlock the size of a fist. From inside comes the slow, heavy breathing of something very large.

narrator/b242c47c0296409e.text: The queen lies in faded silk, and in her folded hands she holds something out to you, as if she had been waiting for her son's enemies.

narrator/b2444a223b12c294.text: The mist thickens at the gate, and then he isn't there.

narrator/b250c422232fdfef.text: For a heartbeat something old and very cold looks out of her eyes. Then she laughs, a dry sound like a deck being cut.

narrator/b276e77b65b93af6.text: You tell her about the woman who buys a pastry every morning, and a baby who died in its cradle the night the kind old pastry woman sat up with it, and the baby's name.

narrator/b295c1b995b48718.text: A hut of fitted stones without a speck of mortar, raised by somebody who knew exactly how and has since forgotten. The door is shut. Something inside is talking to itself.

narrator/b2a9a1b5998bb0ae.text: Thigh bones planed into chair legs, ribs bent into a backrest, knuckles waiting to be drilled for pegs. Fine work, and nobody's ever thanked him for it.

narrator/b2ab9555a4fab9dd.text: Grigor spits, nocks, and shouts a name. Arrows answer from three sides.

narrator/b2b2d9a3506ddde0.text: A well rope, tied tighter than a well rope needs to be. It's taut, as if something heavier than a bucket is hanging at the other end.

narrator/b2cf96d3762c044f.text: She turns a page. It crumbles. She turns it again.

narrator/b2ebb28790cf43e9.text: An arrow-slit. Through it, a sliver of sky and a long way down.

narrator/b2f33db5f5faa98b.text: Old headstones, their names worn to dimples. Several have been dug around recently, as if the earth was checking on them.

narrator/b2f707b679d6966a.text: The mouth cave is full of straw and the smell of animals, and every heap of straw could be a wolf, or a sleeping man, or both.

narrator/b30d709561e3cb87.text: Up the gully, under an overhang, a druid's cache wrapped in hide: dried herbs and a wand of yellowed bone.

narrator/b31c6c3f5264353e.text: Corvina stands up out of her crypt, and the iron gates along the row swing shut by themselves, one after another, like a house being locked for the night.

narrator/b322f1cd6722ded1.text: Heat, at last: a fire in a great oven, a cauldron muttering on its hook, and the smell of good bread over the smell of everything else.

narrator/b328144acdf60de0.text: They go on toward the village, the cart creaking, the boy pulling. The old woman's hands are folded very neatly. Nobody in this valley would think to look at her throat.

narrator/b33c381310856132.text: A broad vault, and in the middle of it a dais with two sarcophagi side by side: a king and a queen, carved holding hands across the gap between them.

narrator/b35c354b0e1803d7.text: Far below, the courtyard, the gate, and the road going away into the trees.

narrator/b35e3fdba4ed338d.text: A camp on the hill's shoulder: hide tents, a fire, a frame of poles hung with wicker cages. Bones are piled by the fire, picked and sorted, the way a careful cook sorts them.

narrator/b369662c051f3935.text: Behind the pole gate at the back of the den, a girl's voice says something you don't quite catch, and then nothing.

narrator/b3825eadf119a630.text: Krezk inside its wall: low stone cottages with turf on the roofs, smoke going straight up, and people who stop what they're doing to watch you pass and don't start again until you've gone.

narrator/b3997c1132110f0a.text: The words come out wrong, or the wrong way round, and the column doesn't move. The marshal's hand goes to his blade.

narrator/b3bf19fc1a626748.text: She lets go. She drops like a sack of grain, and the Belviews in the courtyard scream, and then the wings catch the air with a crack like a sail, and she is going up, and then along, and then away, very badly, in long lurching swoops, down the mountain toward Krezk.

narrator/b3c2c01f4ce1a0c6.text: An hour past midnight a raven comes down into the Seventh Row, and shakes itself, and is Adrian Martikov in his shirtsleeves, with his hat in his hand.

narrator/b3e2a01be8435d82.text: A suit of black armour steps down from its stand, as if someone had called the watch.

narrator/b3edebe36bfee106.text: She breaks the seal with her thumb and reads it twice, and then folds it very small and puts it inside her coat, against her chest.

narrator/b3fe4355fbdb4fb7.text: For a moment he's only a young man on a wall. Then he isn't there at all.

narrator/b4044ec95b0583d8.text: The road climbs south through dead pines toward the castle on its cliff. Every sensible part of you says: not yet, and not like this.

narrator/b429e04add7d3e90.text: North, the mountains, and on a ridge below them a cold silver light that doesn't flicker.

narrator/b4382fc1b565f139.text: She heaves herself out of the ditch and sets off up the lane toward the mill, humming. You may come to regret that.

narrator/b43a07f11dbd3fdd.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Fekre, the mother of fevers. She emptied a city by loving it. Wash your hands after."

narrator/b4437d8a311a251a.text: Charred poles and wet ash where the scarecrows stood. A sacking face lies in the mud, still smiling.

narrator/b4640ce966e85b77.text: The gallows rope hangs empty now, and the mound beside the road has settled. Crossroads are patient; this one will have another guest soon enough.

narrator/b47d5907f2f9fbef.text: Frost has had three hundred winters at the deep cuts. You make out a list of things the temple refuses to be, and no word at all.

narrator/b481e1714887241d.text: A crawlway hot as an oven, where a stoker once fed the furnace from behind. He is still here.

narrator/b483dd0bbc2324a3.text: Two figures in green-dyed sacking step into the road ahead, and the brush behind them steps out too.

narrator/b4917ae2836e5a55.text: Ireena takes the locket from her collar, opens it, and holds it up beside the portrait. The same face, twice. Three times.

narrator/b4bc0346e0a5a168.text: Vladimir stands. Down the long table the dead knights stand with him, and the sound of their armour is like a house settling. He lays his sword flat on the table, and one by one, so do they.

narrator/b4c4c112abba6682.text: Warm, floury and close. Everything is dusted white: the tables, the sacks, the floor, the millstone. The oven on the far wall breathes like something asleep.

narrator/b4e23356182242e9.text: The boards in front of the tower door sag a finger's breadth when you lean on the one before them. Rotten through, and only the carpet holding them.

narrator/b4e648786152a5d1.text: Plums, cellar dust, and something under them you can't name. Probably only age. Probably.

narrator/b4edb68c66bb43a3.text: The words come out in a rush: how many more are out there, where they sleep, which way they came. None of it is grand, and all of it is useful.

narrator/b50674bfb72b7b7a.text: Rails and hooks fixed under the ceiling for the bats. Someone polishes them. Someone polishes them often.

narrator/b50c987084187be6.text: Then he isn't there, and neither is the paper with Strahd's name on it.

narrator/b52563f6995ff27e.text: The man outside stands just past the reach of the firelight, hat in his hands: tall, very pale, his coat brushed and his collar buttoned to the throat. He bows to Ileana, and then, one by one, to each of you.

narrator/b5285e423af43802.text: Lamplight, a low fire, and the one window in the castle that never goes dark. By the fire a thin man in an ink-stained coat sits reading aloud to an empty armchair.

narrator/b53a51e43b1f3f82.text: The kindness goes out of his face all at once, like a lamp turned down. He stands, and the shackle slides off his wrist. It was never locked.

narrator/b54ebe6299d09ecb.text: A board of hooks, and on one a ring of heavy iron keys for every shackle in the cells. You take it.

narrator/b55857762bd0591e.text: He frowns at the lock for a long while afterwards, and then lets it be.

narrator/b56ae060615c1d30.text: The shackle opens. She rubs her ankle, stands, sits down again, and stands up properly the second time.

narrator/b5788e0c7b06f8fb.text: He salutes you with his blade, the old cavalry salute, and his two lieutenants walk their bone horses out of the column to his flanks. Nobody else moves.

narrator/b58fce678edef634.text: Someone is kneeling at the altar. He finishes whatever he was saying, rises, and turns. In the front pews, two figures who were praying stand up with him.

narrator/b5a1e01d55c16a29.text: The silver light runs out from the tower across the trees to the castle on its rock. Up there, a single window that was lit goes dark.

narrator/b5a393c824eac03e.text: The armour on its stand turns its helm toward the door. Behind it, three more suits step down from the wall pegs with nobody inside them.

narrator/b5aacf7cf78c4980.text: The words echo strangely in the low cave. The candles at her feet don't gutter; nothing answers. But nothing objects, either, and the air feels a little less close when you are done.

narrator/b5b0adab14d27d63.text: The altar is clean. That is the worst thing about it.

narrator/b5bbd9df7cbc918f.text: Two people are sitting by the fire on the shore, not quite looking at each other, passing a cup back and forth. The tower's window is dark for once.

narrator/b5c47df598a80f0a.text: Cosmin plants an old banner of the Order, a silver dragon on black gone grey, in the frozen ground at the head of the graves, and stands beside it with his wooden sword. The cold comes down off the ridge.

narrator/b5c6e433ed39c619.text: They bury Elvir at the end of the last green row, under the cairn they raised for him when there was nothing to put beneath it. Stefania sings. Davian doesn't. Adrian digs, and won't let anyone else hold the spade.

narrator/b5d27c3ff5f1fac8.text: A sigil on the bottom step wakes in white fire.

narrator/b5dc4e9930209639.text: A saint in a niche with her hands raised. Someone has hung a black cloth over her face.

narrator/b5e0ff45aebcaaec.text: The wicker sun towers over the crowd on its pole, waiting for its torch.

narrator/b5e2e9ed8bdcb3bf.text: Mary is on her feet before the door is fully open. For a moment neither of them moves. Then Gertruda says "Mother", very small, and Mary has her.

narrator/b5e6dfdd14e6a01e.text: A mound of rot and old rushes, taller than a man, steaming faintly in the cold. It rises and falls, very slowly, like something asleep.

narrator/b5f30bd9722f56c3.text: A well with its rope rotted away. When you drop a pebble, it takes a long time to land, and then something below says the word "thank you" very quietly.

narrator/b6082106a0df6314.text: The door of the hut slams itself. The fire in the hearth stands up tall and green, and the jars on the shelf begin to hum.

narrator/b60ce641bf9d954c.text: It smells of straw and something big and alive. A shape breathes under a tarpaulin at the far end of the wagon, slow and deep, and doesn't wake. Yet.

narrator/b61f06d1d09f9d67.text: You get the first line wrong, and the second line very wrong, and she corrects you both times without a flicker of impatience. The third line comes out right. She looks as proud as if you'd raised the dead.

narrator/b620450816f12127.text: A plain room with a cot and a chest, and every inch of one wall covered in charcoal writing, floor to as high as a big man can reach.

narrator/b64db76775b7f9c3.text: There's no warning, the way there's never any warning with Thistle. One moment she's sharpening her knife; the next she's standing over Wren with her hands on her hips.

narrator/b669dcc85dc04f5f.text: She doesn't answer. In the morning she's still with you, but a little farther off, the way a dog walks when it's been kicked and hasn't decided yet.

narrator/b687a41167bfb43d.text: You kneel by the bed and lay a hand on the boy's chest and pray. For a moment nothing. Then the warmth under your palm changes: not the fever's heat, but a cleaner one, like sun through a shutter.

narrator/b694babbc4056604.text: You leave them to the honey cakes. Later, someone notices they're sitting on the same side of the fire, her head on his shoulder, and neither of them has said a word in an hour, and neither of them seems to need to.

narrator/b696e72b6328a876.text: The door swings shut. The carriage turns in the road with great care and goes back the way it came.

narrator/b69e0ec9bfc0b193.text: Wooden heads waiting for faces, in rows. Blinsky carves the mouths last, he'd tell you, so the toys can't complain about the rest.

narrator/b6b25774e12a112a.text: Sorin is still by the stones, rocking slightly, humming in his mother's voice.

narrator/b6bf2cf6bf1b5a23.text: He is standing beside the heart with one hand resting on the glass, as a man rests a hand on a horse he is fond of. Every beat lights his face from below.

narrator/b6defb74395ad39e.text: One sigil is cut into the threshold instead of the wall, and its lines are a little too fresh.

narrator/b6f0f6fe6d1c7f3e.text: A handsome family in oils above the mantel: a broad, smiling man cradling a swaddled baby, a narrow woman looking at that baby the way you'd look at a stain, a girl of ten with her chin up, and a small boy holding a stuffed wolf by one ear.

narrator/b72a528aaa71822d.text: Whatever you carry out of Berez, you carry it on your backs for a long time. You find you are stronger for the weight.

narrator/b73d6af97ec9f6c8.text: Bones, polished by use. You try not to think about whose.

narrator/b76af35b11c7af62.text: Clutched in the frozen pilgrim's hand, a sword whose blade is rimed with frost that never melts. It kept him cold. It didn't keep him alive.

narrator/b76fd97e59e42fdb.text: A cramped room with a ladder going up to a hatch in the ceiling. You can hear the wind on the other side of it.

narrator/b7705fc86354088c.text: For a long moment nothing moves. Then the captain pushes back his chair and stands, because a sergeant has called the roll, and he has answered the roll every morning of his life.

narrator/b77f30b25b8d0b3b.text: Under the smell of oak there's something else down here: a cold that isn't the cellar's, pooling in the vaults like water.

narrator/b78269090b561bab.text: Inside the chest, wrapped in cloth, lie eleven dolls with red hair: one in a green dress, one in a grey cloak, one smiling. Every face is the same face, carved with terrible love.

narrator/b78a7ad15a8d4d78.text: Each of you came looking for something. None of you came looking for this.

narrator/b7b85f56df9ae20b.text: The grey gelding stops sidling and leans its whole weight on you, the way horses do when they've decided you are furniture.

narrator/b7c41611090233d5.text: The cold hits like a fist. You find him by touch, three fathoms down, already still, and you tear the coat off him and the stones go on down without him.

narrator/b7d874d77de6246c.text: He goes back to the fire and makes supper in silence, and it's excellent, and he doesn't eat any of it.

narrator/b7df212e2e4d2ba5.text: He's past you before the words are finished, a rush of cold air up the stair. Somewhere above, a door bangs, and the bell rope thrums once, as if something brushed it going over the wall.

narrator/b7e2fe9088f4f4c8.text: The winery smells of old wine gone to vinegar and of something else under it, green and wet, like a pond in summer. The floorboards have been pried up in rows, as if someone were looking for something.

narrator/b7ee1382417a2861.text: He presses his lips together and shakes his head. He is more afraid of her than he is of you.

narrator/b80e337389b13a84.text: The magic is in the ribbon, not in her: an enchantment woven into the velvet and knotted into the bow, and the little bell is its eye. It isn't looking at you. It's looking out of the window.

narrator/b82434fdf4405c6f.text: A high, cold antechamber before a carved archway. Through the arch: braziers, an altar, and figures in robes who are not quite there.

narrator/b824a6e82046f12c.text: The ward is still there, coiled in its ring of frost, but now you know where its edges are, and so does it.

narrator/b86c130fa12021e9.text: He laughs. He sits down in the straw again, folds his hands, and goes back to waiting.

narrator/b87480fcd100428e.text: You look over. The chasm has walls and mist, and no bottom you can see.

narrator/b875a47484280ae1.text: You sleep in shifts, and nobody sleeps much. The voices in the amber don't shout. They say your names, kindly, all night.

narrator/b875fcc50dd37a37.text: It takes a long time to wind him: forty turns, fifty. With every turn his ticking grows steadier.

narrator/b87ccd9f3d528bd4.text: Kiril throws back his head and laughs, and the laugh turns into a howl halfway through, and his loyal wolves come pouring up the passage behind him.

narrator/b8853d28398f3b1e.text: At the head of the table of bones, your host rises. Along both sides, the chairs stand up with him.

narrator/b88874cff77f5a1c.text: He takes off his spectacles, and his face comes away with them.

narrator/b8a67fc4c28dd511.text: Strong, glossy horses with plaited manes. One of them, a grey gelding, watches the road east and won't stop.

narrator/b8b7886f3b1ce8fd.text: You tell him about the pool, the young man in the water, and what Ireena remembered: the bride his lord truly wants ran from him once to her death, and given a second life, chose a dead man over him again.

narrator/b8c94713002b4ffb.text: From the crest you can see a green smudge on the hills to the east where the Martikov vines are. It's the only green in the whole grey valley, and it looks like defiance.

narrator/b8f351440be5839a.text: He takes the book as if it might be a trick. Then he opens it, and reads the flyleaf, and his lips move.

narrator/b8f439a29e8ba01c.text: The sparks in Exethanter's eyes go from candle to forge. Somewhere in the shelves, two skulls catch fire.

narrator/b916a098d5769ad6.text: The racks by Bluto's shack are heavy with fish nobody has salted, and the gulls have found them, and so has the smell.

narrator/b91a85a1dab8acdf.text: Under the strokes, smaller, in the careful capitals of someone who learned his letters late: NIGHT 1. ALL PRESENT. GUIDES SAY THE CASTLE IS TWO DAYS.

narrator/b923a58f47542734.text: It's very late. Liriel is awake, which isn't unusual. What's unusual is that she comes and sits beside you, and doesn't pretend she's praying.

narrator/b9257429865cdaf7.text: The warden's spear comes down, and the walls of the vault answer: grey men-at-arms step out of the stone on either side, shields locked, between you and the bones.

narrator/b92ed72d88576da6.text: In the cradle by the tub, under a crocheted blanket, lies a root dug out of the marsh and trimmed into the shape of a swaddled infant. Tucked under its chin like a rattle is a green gem the size of a hen's egg, glowing softly.

narrator/b9350d905d4d8e42.text: A stag with antlers like a winter tree, a bear with its lips pulled back, a wolf larger than any wolf. Every plate gives the same hunter's name.

narrator/b9407626648fcac0.text: A good silver mirror turned to face the wall. On its back, in chalk: DON'T.

narrator/b94ed3b5cea66135.text: Elisabeth Durst's crypt, the finest carving in the row, its slab still shut.

narrator/b95258f2d8ea7a14.text: A deep grave, square and clean, by the east wall. The board at its head says PETRA. Mihail is standing beside it with his hat in his hands.

narrator/b966e2b2c5991415.text: The pale figures on the shore move all at once, faster than anything dead has a right to.

narrator/b967cf876251d874.text: The boards split, and a leg goes through to the ceiling of the room below.

narrator/b9860ed9486d8ad6.text: Goat bones, picked clean and cracked, and a few that aren't goat. Something dropped these on the way in. Or on the way out.

narrator/b98a93fd3c707454.text: He knows something. He keeps looking at the well, and then at his sister, and his mouth works around a name he can't make himself say.

narrator/b995ae3671836e2c.text: Small bones, a great many of them: rats, mostly. They've been cracked open and sucked clean, and then arranged, neatly, by size.

narrator/b996d6a0de377719.text: Dead knights sit along both sides of a long table under rotted banners, armoured and unmoving, as if a feast was called four centuries ago and nobody has been dismissed.

narrator/b9a8dde3ae009c44.text: Two knocks on the shutter, soft as a knuckle on a cask to hear if it's full.

narrator/b9aec08ba189b4b8.text: Every bench in the refectory has turned to face the stairs, as if waiting for you to be served.

narrator/b9b580029dfd6777.text: She stops sweeping. She looks at Ireena for a long moment, and then, very slowly, makes the sign of the sun over her own heart.

narrator/b9b5f19bfaad01cd.text: You'll remember your apprentice's name when you need it, you said, when I asked you to stop calling me "girl". So I'm writing it at the bottom of every letter, in case you don't. Corvina. Corvina. Corvina.

narrator/b9d00a476bcc9550.text: Lysaga fills one more bowl, from a second, smaller pot at the back of the hearth, and puts it in front of Ireena with both hands, very kindly.

narrator/b9f57b57cf6095b6.text: You walk past slowly. The arrows follow you all the way to the bend in the road.

narrator/b9fe2474b08f4469.text: Pews worn smooth along the backs by armoured shoulders. In front of every one, the stone floor is dented where knees went down in plate.

narrator/ba05855727390082.text: Silver light lies over the whole ridge from the top of the tower, steady as a held note. The house under it is still a ruin. It looks like a ruin that has been forgiven.

narrator/ba1a40175219a356.text: Three small graves side by side at the churchyard's edge. The middle stone has a lamb carved on it and ANA in square letters. The earth on all three is loose, turned and patted down again, every night.

narrator/ba1d311212e0ad1b.text: She doesn't want revenge; she wants to hear him once more. She would know his song anywhere.

narrator/ba27a38cd9f869ec.text: In a small room downstairs, under a wall of charcoal names, a big knight in dented plate sits down on his cot and is still.

narrator/ba2bcf209e4bcdc5.text: The marks go up and up, north toward the rock face above the lake, and the prints beside them change, halfway, from boots to paws.

narrator/ba33dce111ff062d.text: At the very bottom of the temple, in a chamber of cold braziers, lies the largest sarcophagus of all, and it is empty.

narrator/ba4933da600d504a.text: A plain iron strongbox, unlocked, and under the holy water a bundle in oilcloth that the old man clearly didn't want to carry and couldn't bring himself to leave.

narrator/ba4e95e1c9ee1717.text: A thin grey mist lies along the floor of the aisles, all of it drifting one way: toward the middle, and down.

narrator/ba5754f36791560a.text: Shards of red glass on the dais, and the chains swinging empty in the draught.

narrator/bab55b7cc13a9b34.text: You push the dust aside with your sleeve. Under it the altar cloth is still white.

narrator/babdf31fa1869508.text: He mimes a ring of small people laughing, and himself in the middle, juggling. Then the ring fades away and he goes on juggling alone.

narrator/bac641f9346d7e16.text: The bones in the passage stand up, and some of them still have meat on.

narrator/bac7a7598ee905a9.text: Ismark takes the head of the coffin and Ireena walks in front with the lamp. The burgomaster is heavier than he looks, as grief usually is.

narrator/bb050db5493e0b34.text: Wedged deep in a nest of twigs and wire: a brass key as long as your hand, its bow shaped like a jester's cap with a tiny bell on every point.

narrator/bb099bdd2df7278b.text: The head of the stair, and a candle that never seems to burn down.

narrator/bb171fe96f6290d0.text: Four cages of woven willow, each big enough for a crouching man. The willow is still green. The druids grew them that shape, which is somehow worse than weaving.

narrator/bb2538ff47a95f85.text: Two figures in black plate stand in the middle of the track ahead with drawn swords, quite still, as if they have been standing there since before the trees. Their faces are grey. Neither of them is breathing.

narrator/bb45b47b77aab80c.text: A girl's bedroom with the bed pushed against the wall and scratches on the inside of the door, low down, at about the height of a cat.

narrator/bb463802f13cd809.text: A courtyard of worn flags round a well and a statue. Footprints in the snow go in every direction, and some of them aren't any shape that has a name.

narrator/bb7f0786d91e2488.text: Mouse has put on a clean apron and combed her hair with her fingers, and there's a candle in a hollowed turnip on the step of the hut. It's her birthday.

narrator/bb89789d3655289d.text: They gather their wounded and slip away between the wagons without a word. The Vistani remember a debt.

narrator/bba0957ae5680cb6.text: A rag doll, face down in the mud: a little stitched woman with a wool scarf and one button eye. Somebody small has loved it nearly to pieces, and then dropped it here.

narrator/bbb8955ab8538599.text: The ticking inside him stops, and starts again. He looks at the slate for a long while before he writes.

narrator/bbc9bfd536bd09b0.text: A great chair at the head of the table, carved with a dragon's folded wings. The arms are worn bright where gauntleted hands have gripped them, night after night, for centuries.

narrator/bbccb01ae6a8b68a.text: Around the cauldron, women in black rags look up all at once with the same wet smile. The brew heaves, and something black slops over the rim and keeps coming.

narrator/bc07d3c4cd8f0955.text: A good sword, well oiled, leaning where a hand can find it without looking. It has been used, recently.

narrator/bc14465461cc6758.text: Under the last stone, wrapped in oilcloth gone stiff with cold, lies a fat spellbook bound in grey leather, and tucked inside its cover two loose scrolls, written fast. The hand is strong and impatient. The capital letters all have a little hook.

narrator/bc43349d6caa0c1f.text: You say it aloud. The colossus lowers its head like a hound told to lie down, and the light behind its amber eyes sinks to an ember.

narrator/bc455a33d9eb7877.text: She smiles. She rocks. She shells. Whatever is under that smile has had a very long time to practise staying there.

narrator/bc66a1ced2c8187e.text: A cold bedroom hearth, the ash swept, a poker leaning at exactly the angle someone left it.

narrator/bc6ee748ed987e84.text: Dawn comes through the coloured glass. Real dawn, with real warmth in it, laid in red and gold squares across the dust and the broken pews and your faces.

narrator/bc833f76906023d1.text: The stone comes free with a small wet sound. It is warm, and it smells, impossibly, of grapes in the sun. In the cradle the root sighs and begins, very slowly, to wither.

narrator/bc89a65f20745c27.text: The foot of the stairs, its walls cut with little alcoves, each holding something strange: a dried hand, a bone knife, a hag's finger. Down here the chant is clear: they are praising the land, and the ancient one who is the land.

narrator/bcb8ac76a744680a.text: The lounge is empty. A book lies open on a chair; cards lie in a ring of patience with no queens in it.

narrator/bcdb12ffeb1d6c3c.text: The mist lets you in, holds you a moment like a host taking your coat, and hands you back to the road, facing west.

narrator/bced191433223d9f.text: The boards split, and a leg goes through to the ceiling below.

narrator/bcff5e94ba5c699e.text: He watches the windows more than the door. Each time a bird lands on the sill, he glances at it the way a man glances at a friend, and once you'd swear it nodded back.

narrator/bd39ba964e3d008f.text: A dead twig goes under somebody's boot like a snapped bone. Up in the pine, a hundred small heads turn.

narrator/bd47308377c02a17.text: Painted wood, good hinges and a lock you could pick with a hairpin. Arrigal's wagon looks too honest to be honest.

narrator/bd6347321eee478a.text: A painted statue of a gaunt man in a black cloak, holding out an orb of smoky crystal.

narrator/bd995daaeeb00f5f.text: Ilse is cleaning her greatsword by the fire, the same stretch of blade, over and over.

narrator/bda69dac6298aa2c.text: The candles lean, and stand straight, and the chair is empty. Ireena closes the locket. Her hand is steady.

narrator/bdabc825752d68e7.text: The carcasses turn slowly on their hooks in the heat. One hook is empty: you're carrying what was on it.

narrator/bdbefdf0d54ae21a.text: One empty coffin rings hollow under your knuckles. Under its false bottom, a pair of soft black slippers, their soles cold and faintly sticky.

narrator/bdc52e904bd826e8.text: Stanimir is not smiling. Two younger Vistani stand behind him with their thumbs hooked in their belts, close to their knives.

narrator/bdd1ccecd131c1b6.text: He goes into one of you like breath into a cold mirror; for a moment two sets of eyes look out of the same face, then only one. Somewhere inside, a small boy stops crying.

narrator/bdd68dc0984a180d.text: Scarecrows step off the poles along the track, one after another, as if somebody had called them in for supper.

narrator/bdf7b1a5182c0c0f.text: Cold candles, cracked windows and a sunburst over the altar gone grey with soot. Under your boots, faint through the floorboards, someone is weeping and someone is praying, and you can't tell which is which.

narrator/bdfca755d1a3eec9.text: A narrow gallery with doors on both sides. Somewhere a pot is boiling, somewhere bats are shifting, and behind one locked door somebody is humming.

narrator/be13b2f0356aa9e4.text: One room with a sleeping corner and a study divided off by a half wall. The hearth has never been lit; the cold doesn't seem to bother him.

narrator/be182d2ab1d7c12e.text: Blinsky sees what is standing behind your legs, and sits down on the floor of his own shop. Piccolo climbs onto his head to see better.

narrator/be30c2e30a708cac.text: The colossus steps down off its plinth, slow and stiff with ice.

narrator/be376fe313ce0a3c.text: The table has been cleared. Nobody cleared it.

narrator/be39a71dc42d5416.text: The track to the abbey goes up the mountainside in switchbacks, cut into the rock, so steep in places that someone has driven iron pegs into the stone to hold on by. Far above, a bell tower stands against the clouds.

narrator/be3e0233c3874b4c.text: The Baron reads the letter twice, moving his lips. On the second reading, the colour drains out of him from the forehead down.

narrator/be43b8614450cdce.text: Granny Ash comes across the lane with her dogs at her heels, and in the hag garden behind her the blights pull their roots up out of the beds.

narrator/be4aff61ca373aa0.text: Shut for the night. A slate on the door reads, in a neat hand: OPEN AT DAWN. BRING COIN.

narrator/be545a9a9ff2571e.text: The well is only a well. Down the shaft there's nothing but water, very cold and very clear, and your own face looking up.

narrator/be6c9d7114b34c26.text: The hidden stair lets you out into a little rock-cut room with an iron gate. The walls are warm here too, warm as skin.

narrator/be7d76678bf674d1.text: Exethanter looks up, blinks, and reads the paper pinned to his sleeve, his jaw moving with the words.

narrator/be8b894e9ecbbf06.text: The iron gate swings open with a long, thin screech: the only sound down here that isn't chanting.

narrator/be9a10ff0540851c.text: Lamplight, maps, the smell of cold tea. Someone has been working at the table very late, every night, for a week.

narrator/be9a392635ed83dd.text: The burgomaster's strongbox opens on dry velvet: he paid a good smith. Whatever he was saving for, he never got to spend it.

narrator/bea18572648d73a7.text: The village looks the same as it did, which is to say exhausted. A few more shutters stand open a finger's width than before.

narrator/bec0c36a08175d97.text: A lamp of skulls hangs low over the table, burning green, swaying though nothing touches it. Its chain runs up into the dark toward the furnace's noise.

narrator/bec6c0356b594566.text: Horses stamp on their line and the road runs back east to the gate. Somebody at the fire has noticed you, and gone to tell somebody else.

narrator/bedbca263f7b1594.text: A row of narrow cells with iron bars across their doors. Behind them, in the straw, shapes move: Belviews whose gifts didn't take, all elbows and fur and wrong-jointed legs, thin as winter. They watch you through the bars without blinking.

narrator/bede8d5d07e675ed.text: The portcullis is up, and the way is open. Ahead, candlelight and voices.

narrator/beff8e876a8b29bc.text: The amber in front of Ratatoille warms like a hearth. The voice in it is glorious and fond, a king's voice from a stage, speaking only to him.

narrator/bf0de607af3eb924.text: A fresh grave, half dug, the earth heaped neatly on a sack so the grass isn't spoiled. Nobody has died yet that you know of. The sexton digs ahead.

narrator/bf0ee40164f4e6f6.text: You sleep at the edge of the pines, and grey shapes keep watch on the slope above you all night. For once, they're watching for you, not at you.

narrator/bf1e6448defa9b36.text: A young woman in the horse pen looks up, and you know before she speaks that Stanimir has told her.

narrator/bf1eeb675dc2ca0a.text: The great press fills the middle of the floor, its screw as thick as a man's waist. Beside it stands a vat full to the brim, and the surface of the mash is moving.

narrator/bf43bde7635c6686.text: Mouse stops in the middle of the lane. Then she comes back, slowly, and stands behind you, and holds on to your belt with both hands.

narrator/bf4ae9c5caf5947b.text: You can see the whole Svalich road from here, and the village, and the lane to the mill. Anyone sitting up here would know who was coming long before they knocked.

narrator/bf555cebd62f8ade.text: A cold, frightened boy who wants his mother. That's all you see.

narrator/bf67d3be9ef04880.text: As Ezmerelda comes near, a thread of blue light runs round the door frame and crackles, like a dog lifting its lip.

narrator/bf87ab20283ee412.text: The door is oak, iron-bound and scored to splinters around the latch. Somebody has nailed a horseshoe over it upside down, and somebody else, or something, has bent it.

narrator/bf889722e1d72327.text: The bottom room was a wizard's hall once: you can see where the carvings were chiselled off the walls. Now it's a hunter's storeroom: crates of holy water, bundles of stakes, a camp cot made with military corners.

narrator/bf922e0c523fedaa.text: The hooks are empty. You already have the keys.

narrator/bfb3bfeb2744d04f.text: You rest with your backs to a wall that has seen worse. Somewhere a dog barks once and thinks better of it.

narrator/bfb402ee168e6767.text: At the milestone, Steaua stops shivering. When she lifts her head the grey has burned out of her, and her eyes are coals.

narrator/bfba04ff261c916d.text: He looks at you for a long moment before he speaks, the way you'd look at someone you have already heard about, and not kindly.

narrator/bfc3c00b168775ba.text: Davian doesn't take the third stone at once. He looks at it in your hand, then at you, and his face does something it hasn't done since you met him.

narrator/bfcd52f323ba57df.text: Eyes in the dark on both sides of the road, low to the ground, and more of them every time you look.

narrator/bfd148ce2569e1f5.text: When the hymn ends, the light goes out of the windows like a tide going out, slow and unhurried. It came, though. It came.

narrator/bfd2182ccc7781c9.text: Below you, the house goes quiet in a new way. Along the long table in the hall, armoured heads lift toward the windows and then bow, and the knights are only men sitting very still.

narrator/bfd90be78344ce4e.text: Places are laid for each of you. The silver is real, the food is hot, and nobody carries it in.

narrator/bff1cafde4721f7a.text: The amber is dark and cold. Whatever is inside is still there, but the wardens' seal holds, and for once it has nothing to say.

narrator/bff7215a940a6067.text: Beams, straw and a smell of old rain. If the barn hides anything, it is under more than you can shift.

narrator/bffc58403f70cfeb.text: The key turns stiffly. The cuffs open with a sound like a held breath let out.

narrator/bffd81a75638e82b.text: Something small comes down the stair toward you, one careful step at a time: a jester the height of a child, in faded motley and a cap of bells, with a painted porcelain face. Gears tick inside it.

narrator/c00138314d43ab34.text: The niches hold offerings: silver buttons, a ring, a child's carved dragon, candle stubs. The squires left what they had.

narrator/c00d33271a744727.text: The cold corner of the study is an open doorway now, with a short stair going down into a little room that has been swept, and a fresh grave in the garden outside its window.

narrator/c01058074af190e7.text: A big, generous fire built by people who don't have to worry about firewood or who sees it. Its smoke goes straight up, which in this valley counts as a miracle.

narrator/c014097fb0f8dfef.text: Figures are wading up out of the reeds, streaming lake water, with weed in their hair and their eyes gone white. The lake is giving back what it took, and it wants something in exchange.

narrator/c02c3c8e4b854bc8.text: At the back of the nook, behind the dust, a thin seam in the plaster, square as a doorframe.

narrator/c030994575e2cae7.text: Wedged under a root, a traveller's pouch, the leather gone black, with a stoppered vial inside that the water never reached.

narrator/c03339cf0ff48e92.text: The cairn has a grave beneath it now, the earth still dark. Someone has pushed a vine cutting into the soil at its head, and the cutting has put out a single green leaf.

narrator/c03ea176305dcbb0.text: Blinsky comes down safely with his puppet, chattering, and never knows how close the bottom step came. Pidlwick watches you watching him, and writes nothing at all.

narrator/c044230f1a116ab5.text: A tall, handsome house behind a rusted fence, its windows dark, its porch swept. It is the best-kept house in the village, and nobody will walk past it.

narrator/c046c19fc6de4226.text: Pidlwick II is juggling in the window, and there are three children outside watching him, which may be the most customers Blinsky Toys has ever had at once.

narrator/c04930774c090d73.text: Trodden into the mud beside the stocks, a silver ring. Whoever sat in the stocks last lost it, and it didn't protect them from the Baron.

narrator/c04c3f58997de4a4.text: When they come back, they come back slowly, side by side, soaked through, and they don't say who won. Thistle sits down next to Wren on the log, closer than she needs to, and leans on him, hard, the way she leans on people she trusts.

narrator/c06066dee5edb483.text: Where the logs of the causeway have rotted through, someone has mended the gaps with bones, laid crosswise and bound with reeds. Most of them are not animal bones.

narrator/c07335793b080194.text: Godrick doesn't kneel. He stands with the old sword across his palms and looks at it a long time, and then at the rest of you.

narrator/c083c491921f121a.text: The earth you blessed smokes under him. He came home to a bed that burns and lay down in it anyway, because there was nowhere else to go.

narrator/c08e86c3baedc2a3.text: At the statue's feet, among the offerings, something catches your light and holds it a moment longer than the rest.

narrator/c0910b759093a59c.text: The lid is so cold that your breath freezes on it, and the frost fills the letters before you can read them.

narrator/c0a228e5d90032ce.text: A hunting tapestry on an iron rod: hounds and riders in full cry after a single grey wolf. Look closer and every rider is smiling.

narrator/c0b02351b5315243.text: A shack of grey boards with a sail for a door and a lamp in the window. The kind of place where one man has been very lonely for a very long time.

narrator/c0b20154fc00d65a.text: There's nobody at the edge of the light. Then there is: a slim gentleman in a grey coat and grey gloves, a ledger under his arm, standing exactly where the firelight stops as if it were a line painted on a floor.

narrator/c0bc0f03bb363d7a.text: A bundle of legal papers, tied with string and heavy with seals.

narrator/c0c0dc514e6d7e34.text: A cold spare bedroom: a slender bed, a little iron stove, a writing desk and stool, a rocking chair, and in the window box a doll in a yellow dress.

narrator/c0ca1ed9596251fd.text: Letters, invitations and accounts, all in a neat, cold hand. If the desk keeps secrets, it keeps them from you.

narrator/c0cce3ba76ac3eb7.text: The contract in his ledger begins to smoke at one corner. Then the whole page catches, with a soft, polite sound, and burns down to his gloves, and he doesn't drop it.

narrator/c0ce08cf0389de86.text: You pull the rope, and the note that comes up out of the water is wrong: flat, angry. The water along the shore twitches. Better try something else, before it remembers what it was doing.

narrator/c0e0b5871fbd39d1.text: She lowers the spyglass at last and looks you over properly, the way a horse trader looks at a horse.

narrator/c0e174fa5cc9607d.text: A narrow boy's bed, made tight. Under the pillow, when you lift it, there's a stone with a hole in it, the kind children think lets you see fairies.

narrator/c0ecb3ef68fa46f9.text: The water goes into the flasks bright and stays bright, faintly, like the last of a sunset in a window.

narrator/c0fd55b701be9e3e.text: There's a scrabble of claws behind you, and Lupu comes through the study door like a grey storm and plants himself between you and the stair, and growls at the boy he used to sleep beside.

narrator/c10438a4de61021b.text: Tamsin is sitting with the locket closed in his fist, so tight his knuckles have gone white.

narrator/c107dd6a91c3b7fc.text: Just a house now, and a sad one. Whatever waited inside it has stopped waiting.

narrator/c10a4e83b76d3f79.text: Open the sluice before going down and shut it after, or the cracks will cook you where you stand. Andrei didn't. Andrei's still down there, in a way.

narrator/c118a5c8d9e75b61.text: Hoofbeats, unhurried, out of the fog ahead. A black horse with eyes like banked coals comes down the road at a walk, and the man riding it does not need to be introduced.

narrator/c124e9dc4b589352.text: The track comes out of the pines onto bare rock, and there it is: a windmill on the crag, its sails lashed still, its chimney smoking. The whole hill smells of fresh bread, and under the bread, of something else.

narrator/c13d0fd1b1ad6a54.text: Armour on the stair, coming fast.

narrator/c13d59e2462c8a0d.text: You have come farther into this house than most guests, and it has noticed. So have you.

narrator/c156a718742783bd.text: The hearth is cold. The green copper rod at its back has been drawn out of its socket, and the air in the tower no longer tastes of thunder.

narrator/c18174aae46813af.text: Iron jaws snap shut on a boot. Somewhere in the fog, a wolf yips, almost like laughter.

narrator/c18b49213dea7b93.text: You huddle in the lee of a boulder while the mountain screams over your heads. It passes, eventually. Everything up here passes, except the cold.

narrator/c18db05f75b058cc.text: An empty cage on a hook, at the height where you'd hang a bird. There's straw in the bottom of it, and a child's shoe.

narrator/c194d96e600b0a75.text: One brick by the taproom hearth isn't mortared. Behind it, a small black bead that is heavier than it looks.

narrator/c19e3f6640263461.text: Beams, nests, droppings, and eyes. A lot of eyes.

narrator/c1adebd9597606a6.text: The gold she lies on. Lead, under the leaf, all of it.

narrator/c1b6183aff36e2dc.text: The grey soldier at his post doesn't look at you. His eyes are on the door to the road, exactly where they have been for centuries.

narrator/c1d463da58692dd4.text: The lid slides back by itself. A young woman sits up in the crypt, grey to the lips, in the rags of a scholar's coat, with ink still on her fingers after forty years.

narrator/c1f4a9bc6011b253.text: The ring of glass where the lightning keeps striking. A letter-shaped hole in the ice at its edge.

narrator/c1f51c7d6b3bd358.text: The shingle shore of Lake Baratok. A stone causeway runs out from it toward the island, broad and solid until halfway, where the lake starts to win.

narrator/c1fd03b47cd1d273.text: He sees it coming and doesn't run. It is quick. Afterwards the fish go on flapping on the shingle for a long time, and then they stop.

narrator/c2013bea7102f17b.text: The slope is quiet. A grey wolf lies in the sun on the watch rock, sees you, and puts its head back down on its paws.

narrator/c2077779ba0691ab.text: The road runs west into darker trees, toward Tser Pool and, a long day beyond it, the walls of Vallaki.

narrator/c207bb5bacaa7ebc.text: You've been through them once already. They look no more organised for it.

narrator/c2159e0dc2feede6.text: He sees it coming, and for once he doesn't smile.

narrator/c21c31ddf5814870.text: He seems exactly what he says: a tired, frightened holy man, too gentle for this place.

narrator/c2258392eb691e66.text: The skull and coiled spine of a dragon fill the amber, packed so tight the bones have cracked. The amber is the dark red of old blood, and it is cold even to look at.

narrator/c22f7bd9c2dc1b5d.text: A woman with flour to the elbows looks up from a cauldron, takes in your boots and your weapons, and decides you can stay.

narrator/c23d242e981b6185.text: A table built from the bones of people who once stood against him: soldiers, rebels, hunters. He likes to have them at dinner still.

narrator/c23ff7a994761b97.text: A cot of bare planks. There's no hollow in the wood where a body would lie. It has never been slept on.

narrator/c2450233385c4a07.text: The shore is quiet except for the water running back off the stones. Far out and far down, the bell still swings. It isn't ringing. It's waiting.

narrator/c255b321999c970d.text: The sun rises over Barovia: a small, pale, ordinary sun. The valley stares at it the way a prisoner stares at an open door.

narrator/c258e182a7606482.text: The frost on the ribs glows faintly where you took the light, like a coal remembering it was once a fire.

narrator/c29c03a2f208355b.text: She doesn't hear you, or hears you from very far off, the way you hear a voice in a dream. She takes a step toward him.

narrator/c2a47d401cd4ddbd.text: She rocks, and hums, and scrapes the pot. If she is hiding anything, she has had a very long time to practise.

narrator/c3653bd7378e589b.text: Lights bob up out of the flooded houses, pale and friendly, and drift toward you at the speed of a walk. They are humming.

narrator/c36694a7a9fb582c.text: Off the end of the jetty, a little boat has slipped its rope and is turning slowly in the mist, a few yards out. In it, sitting very straight with her hands folded in her lap, is Arabelle.

narrator/c391bba879957634.text: It is exactly as Nadia said. She counted the chairs right.
