narrator/c3968f331436a4f5.text: A shadow the size of a barn roof slides across the bridge. Then the wind comes, and the scream, and the talons.

narrator/c3994f0decb05955.text: A narrow stair worn into a dip by centuries of trays. Grey livery hangs on pegs, waiting for servants who aren't coming.

narrator/c39c3f2aabd1d606.text: A low passage, the rock polished at shoulder height by bodies brushing past. Two kinds of shoulder: one at a man's height, one at a wolf's.

narrator/c39c50ac3fa4f9dd.text: Jars on every shelf, and some of them humming. Under the humming, from somewhere in the pantry, comes a quieter sound, steady and patient, like something that knows it's been found.

narrator/c3b502a4e024a896.text: A small square room at the foot of the stair, with three doors: a pale one carved with a sunburst, and two of bronze.

narrator/c3e75db5fd1b9b41.text: Then Kip takes an apricot out of his pocket, from habit, and looks at it, and makes a noise. There's a soft brown bruise on one side of it. It wasn't there this morning.

narrator/c3f2a34b21ecac7a.text: 'The mansion, mostly. He keeps a room up there nobody goes into. Nobody. The last man who knocked lost a finger for it.'

narrator/c42cabe8943547a8.text: A crest over the captain's bed: a sun over mountains, the arms of a crown that ruled this valley before the castle did.

narrator/c43912cd8ef092d1.text: Above the mansion door, the Baron's painted face beams at the square with his arms spread wide, as if about to embrace the whole town, whether or not it wants to be embraced.

narrator/c43bf96e555e4a4c.text: Casks of strong red wine with Luvash's mark burned into the staves. One of them is already mostly empty.

narrator/c43f5a4074707c90.text: A long bar, a crackling hearth and a dozen tables, most of them occupied by people who stop talking for exactly as long as it takes to look at you.

narrator/c4415b422d3c8104.text: The field is cold, colder than the night, and the mounds look less like mounds than like people lying very still with blankets pulled up.

narrator/c44dc8665b8f80de.text: Liriel is teaching the morning hymn to whoever will hold still. So far that is nobody, but she's undeterred.

narrator/c45877768e7251e1.text: She takes one step toward you and the next step into nothing, and she's gone. Far down the hill, a little later, something shrieks, and every raven in the oak goes up at once.

narrator/c48ef60a102ec325.text: Ludmilla closes her book. Volenta claps her hands. Anastrasya rises last, and slowest, and she is crying.

narrator/c49b7b13a6ec0d67.text: A wall of trophies. Ezmerelda stops in front of a Vistani boot with a fine buckle and stares at it for a long time, and says nothing at all.

narrator/c4a4503674d0d3b2.text: A map of the whole valley, closely annotated. A cave in the hills above Lake Zarovich is ringed in red ink with one word: WOLVES. Beside Vallaki, in smaller letters: R. The Blue Water.

narrator/c4af3582b47a9ae0.text: With the beacon burning, a niche you never noticed stands open at the foot of the bier. In it lies a shield worked with silver scales, left by the dragon for whoever would finish what his knights began.

narrator/c4b2e41022ffa986.text: The goat track climbs through dark pines into cold that comes too early for the season. Somewhere above, a small storm is waiting over the summit like a dog outside a door.

narrator/c4c64600c8b396fb.text: You find a dry doorway and watch Vallaki get ready to be happy. Bunting goes up, the watch counts heads, and somebody tests a bell and finds it loud enough.

narrator/c4ce92e2697c578e.text: Elisabeth's fork stops halfway to her mouth. For one moment the hunger leaves both their faces, and what's left is worse: two parents who have just remembered.

narrator/c4f1cd921d7dd835.text: Splintered wood, sap like old blood. If the heartwood hides anything, the tree is keeping it.

narrator/c5117b9c648c7956.text: The lane north narrows between cottages and climbs toward a gap in the wall, and the snow on it is swept, every flake, by somebody very old and very determined.

narrator/c52d98b4ed5bfc50.text: A dark marble hearth, laid and never lit. Whoever hung the family over it wanted them kept warm.

narrator/c53670e71cb4ecb7.text: The lock holds. Somewhere in the walls, something that might be laughter.

narrator/c53d73b6b1b8ab57.text: He's on a shelf of wet rock no wider than a cart, twenty feet down, soaked and shaking and three days hungry, with his knees pulled up and his hands over his ears.

narrator/c546f1c520c8a0ba.text: Adrian walks in beside you, black sap to the elbows, and stands in front of his father, and tells him all of it before you can.

narrator/c54816e5a9bb728a.text: The wind off the wings nearly takes you over the parapet.

narrator/c559db207d90249c.text: The abbey is quiet in a new way. The window that was always lit is dark, and the Belviews are out in the courtyard in the daylight, blinking at it.

narrator/c55fbddb00958568.text: Names chalked on a slate, a guest list. Most have been wiped away with a thumb. Near the bottom, newer: Nadia, lamplighter. And: the brother.

narrator/c56478096c7efe01.text: Escher's smile goes long in the teeth. The bats in the canopy of his bed come down like a dropped curtain.

narrator/c5665b8a3d5f4fdd.text: The lane runs straight up between the rows, and the vines stay vines. You notice yourself noticing that.

narrator/c5788f7b07485daf.text: Blankets and old sailcloth stretched between the trees. Inside one, a row of children's boots; inside another, an old man's wine-stained coat folded with great care.

narrator/c589650fcb0177a5.text: A burgomaster's study: ledgers, maps of the valley, a desk buried in papers. On top of the pile, one letter is written in a hand that grows shakier toward the end.

narrator/c591f8fc08c55347.text: A boy of fourteen or so sits wrapped in a horse blanket on the last of the squires' small graves, with a wooden sword across his knees and frost in his eyebrows. He gets up when he sees you, because a squire stands.

narrator/c5a7fa8dbad5744a.text: The corridor is quiet. For the first time, nobody is crying behind any of the doors.

narrator/c5b488c5fa619a46.text: The bridge has no rail, only a lip of stone a hand high. It has been enough so far.

narrator/c5d5afff9287a9f5.text: His fingers won't open. Not stiff: held, from the inside, like a fist around a secret. You don't get them apart without breaking one.

narrator/c5d6875a1e586c6f.text: The ceiling sheds a curtain of amber, every shard as sharp as glass.

narrator/c5d8fead6d765dd7.text: The candles in the old tombs are all leaning the same way, toward the stair, as if listening for something under them.

narrator/c6090068ca1c9dec.text: A rocking chair worn smooth, a bowl, a basket of knitting, and a footstool placed exactly where a child in a cage could see it.

narrator/c60f103e9044aa4e.text: They stand on the step together, her hand in his. In the east the mist does something it hasn't done in weeks: it thins, and one blade of true sun comes over the church wall.

narrator/c62070106411a0cf.text: The house gives something up. It doesn't like doing it.

narrator/c643db6cf195f534.text: Something lies cooling in the oven's ash: a squat iron brazier, still glowing, though nothing in it burns.

narrator/c64ce958ae649e23.text: The flagstone tips, and the dark beneath it is ten feet deep and full of spikes.

narrator/c660bfe0f5576df4.text: Hours in the thin sun, and prayers, and his eyes still go to the castle when he thinks nobody's watching.

narrator/c69e59e77a4deaf7.text: A long trench of torn earth and black splinters where the Seventh Row was. It smells of spilt wine.

narrator/c6b22a11c2caf294.text: A footpath climbs north through the pines to the lip of a gorge. The river goes over the edge in one long white rope of water, and the roar fills everything.

narrator/c6e0f2fa6b2ccb35.text: The roof beams groan as if the house is flexing its shoulders.

narrator/c6f0ce26c3e198a3.text: A small, straight-backed man in black waits in the middle of the long hall with his hands folded. Around him, faint as a draught under a door, many voices are screaming.

narrator/c6f802bf689d7ae9.text: In the alcove a big, grey-bearded man sits against the rock with his arms spread wide, chained by both wrists to iron rings. The chains are bright. Where they touch him, the skin has blistered black.

narrator/c7267dc9b5f64181.text: A low vault at the foot of a narrow stair. Coin lies on the floor in drifts, with chests and caskets sunk in it like rocks in snow.

narrator/c7845c859c0c0a02.text: A deep well with a stone lip worn smooth by buckets. When you drop a pebble, it takes a long time to hit the water, and the water, when it answers, sounds warm.

narrator/c78b1c61fe548122.text: A lane climbs between rows of vines the colour of a paper bag left out in the rain. At the top stand a house, a winery and a tall barn, all shut, with ravens on every roof.

narrator/c791c2d7d88a7ded.text: Wachterhaus is dark, except for a grate low in its wall, where candlelight flickers from somewhere under the ground.

narrator/c79fe30d1061b2d4.text: Offalia wipes her hands on her apron, and keeps wiping them as they lengthen into something with knuckles like walnuts and nails like a baker's peel.

narrator/c7ac8820a5f73e73.text: The mausoleum stands apart from the house, as if out of respect. Its door is shut and its stones are white with a frost that the sun doesn't touch.

narrator/c7aeaf4112a4568b.text: The wainscot has thin dark slits in it at ankle height, knee height, throat height.

narrator/c7bb813ee9aa2b68.text: A shop window full of toys. A jack-in-the-box. A wooden wolf on wheels. A doll with red hair, in pride of place, with a little card that says NOT FOR SALE.

narrator/c7bde819dc9fe239.text: Letters from Gustav Durst to the household's nursemaid, tied in blue ribbon. They begin politely and stop being polite.

narrator/c7c04e681897c5ad.text: Dead branches, a lot of them. It's hard to see much against the sky.

narrator/c9596f0167cac202.text: A drain in the middle of the floor. It is quiet for now.

narrator/c982ab7e92666981.text: Two narrow beds made with tight corners, two footlockers, uniforms pressed and hanging, and a small door in the wall with a brass call button beside it.

narrator/c98438d81ba43f83.text: In the middle, where the reflected sun lingers longest, your fingers close on something in the silt that has no business being warm.

narrator/c9e39c1a150507e6.text: Offalia snores on the bakery floor with crumbs on her chin, smiling at whatever she's dreaming. Now and then her fingers twitch, kneading.

narrator/c9e57b49cab5daa7.text: A shaggy draft horse hobbled in the reeds, cropping the thin grass with the patience of an animal that has pulled a wagon a long way. It watches the tower more than it watches you.

narrator/c9e765f6ce99e9f9.text: For the first time in years the chant falters. Knowing a story is a kind of power over it.

narrator/c9f56ff377cefed6.text: A puppet theatre with a little castle at the back and a little village at the front. All the villagers are on strings. So is the castle.

narrator/c9ff9b73464fdac9.text: The bar comes up with a groan. The gate opens a body's width, no more, and waits for you to fit yourselves through it.

narrator/ca0c49276f6cd23b.text: Grey salt, coarse as gravel, smelling of the grave. A scoop stands in each barrel, and the scoops are worn.

narrator/ca29294e4a420f26.text: A shuttered window with a candle burning behind the slats. The weeping comes from just inside, and it doesn't stop when you stop to listen.

narrator/ca33052a4734ccf2.text: The Gates of Barovia, and the mist, and nothing on the east road but the road.

narrator/ca360b30aea466c9.text: She ties a yellow ribbon to your sleeve with quick, cold fingers, and the smile goes out of her eyes for a moment, with relief.

narrator/ca41cbe07f779662.text: A bare room: a cot with a blanket stretched tight enough to bounce a coin, a lectern, a strongbox. Nothing on the walls. Nothing on the floor. A room kept by someone who has stopped living in it.

narrator/ca50f48fbb8d4ad0.text: The coin clicks into the niche beside the candle. The flame doesn't move, but for a mile after, the wind seems to be at your backs.

narrator/ca58d74fadde4b9b.text: Stone mourners walk in a line along the wall, heads bowed, every face worn smooth. One near the end has been recarved: it is weeping.

narrator/ca5dc4a3bb8b707b.text: The cairn stones lie where you set them down. The frost ring around them is melting, now there's nothing left to guard.

narrator/ca6d399a16f044be.text: He bows to Ireena, not to you, and the dark he stood in is only dark.

narrator/ca7fcdcf33249d54.text: Sorin is sitting in the hall carving, with Ilya leaning against his side giving instructions. There are wooden wolves on every shelf in the house.

narrator/ca898c708f791232.text: The reading hall is only cold now. The frost on the desks is thinner than it was, and nobody is weeping.

narrator/ca914e5cb2c592e8.text: The top of the watch rock is polished smooth by a great many patient bellies. There's a good view, and a fine collection of fleas.

narrator/cab192f865aa89a7.text: A dead knight in the courtyard is going through the motions of saddling a horse that isn't there, buckle by buckle, very carefully.

narrator/cad359f59ab37e23.text: Nobody moves for a long moment. Then a knight halfway down the table, whose name nobody has said for centuries, stands up. Then another.

narrator/cadd798f1156023a.text: The camp smells of horses, plums and pipe smoke. Every wagon is painted in colours the valley has forgotten: red, gold, a green like summer.

narrator/cb16a464af071b52.text: The bow comes down. A whistle, and three young men drop out of the trees, all with the same nose.

narrator/cb2b779378942bcf.text: A tall crypt with a stone slab at its heart, and on the slab a big man carved in armour. Winged things of stone crouch at its corners, facing out.

narrator/cb326601040ab373.text: A square of mud around a dry well. Two shops face it, one tavern and one mercantile, and both look as if they're waiting for customers who stopped coming years ago.

narrator/cb3b95acbde01719.text: Merrow looks to the walls for his company. Nobody comes. Down at the gate the drum is still beating "fall in", and behind the panels they stand where they fell in.

narrator/cb47ad7a789bd939.text: Something in the great nest in the middle of the roost catches what little light there is.

narrator/cb6526568d2ae896.text: A wardrobe full of coats, and behind it, cold air and a narrow stair.

narrator/cb6cdd606c63d7f3.text: The former Baron of Vallaki sits in his own stocks with his wrists through the holes and his gold chain gone. Somebody has hung his sash over the board, upside down.

narrator/cb81719d573088bf.text: Old mail, red with rust, every set the same. The dead men here keep their kit in order and nothing else.

narrator/cb92f62721910fc8.text: Downstairs, something heavy stops chewing. In the corner, a stool scrapes back. Three voices begin humming the same tune, and the loft is suddenly much smaller.

narrator/cbad616e1c41ba6d.text: At the bottom of the stair the mist has gathered and gone, and the air tastes of iron. Something here is lying very still.

narrator/cbb1397ec2896119.text: Splinters, a cracked axle and a smell of old turnips. Whoever drove this cart left nothing worth having. Or hid it well.

narrator/cbb9dcd1009caf87.text: Then they're calling you. Each of you. By name.

narrator/cbbea64b8a265535.text: He's across the hall before anyone can move, and Rahadin's sword is already out to meet him, as if it had been waiting four hundred years for exactly this.

narrator/cbd4b75ec6105124.text: His face is a shut door with good locks. Whatever is behind it, you won't have it today, and perhaps neither will he.

narrator/cbed3ded0bd6a9db.text: There. The house hid it well, but not well enough.

narrator/cbf8cef0d45ac4a9.text: Black water, rotten beams and the furniture of people who left in a hurry and never came back.

narrator/d4ec643821ddb098.text: 'The Abbot will be angry,' it sobs. 'He is always angry, since the bride.' It won't say more.

narrator/d510272c4814f215.text: A great iron cradle on a stone plinth, full of ash so old it has set like mortar. Soot climbs the parapet behind it in a long black tongue.

narrator/d5186ae4466f4f3c.text: You sleep in the cart shed with a watch at the door. All night, something walks the cloister in slow, even steps, and every hour it stops outside and listens, and goes on.

narrator/d5383bbc7da94213.text: A tall, mournful man in a patched jester's cap rises from behind the counter. On his shoulder sits a small monkey in a waistcoat, who looks at you with the same expression.

narrator/d54462d0168832d1.text: You rest. The village is a little quieter than it was; or you've grown used to it, which is worse.

narrator/d545e353bc98486a.text: No one moves toward the table. The chant waits, patient as stone.

narrator/d5554c5f99967204.text: The foot of the tower is a bare round room with a door back to the main floor and a stair going up the wall into the dark.

narrator/d5645c7ce730be68.text: She weighs it, and you, and decides a mill in the hand is worth more than a fight she might lose. The bags split under the knife like ripe plums, and something goes out past you, many somethings, all in a hurry to be elsewhere.

narrator/d56a098ed1738c56.text: Two iron rings set deep in the rock, and two lengths of bright silver chain hanging from them, with cuffs at the ends. The silver is blackened on the inside of each cuff, where it has been burning someone for a month.

narrator/d56fe8e361805ec3.text: The door with the carved hand swings open, and the chanting doubles.

narrator/d5755eb5e149400d.text: A pillared chamber around a stone altar, braziers burning on either side, and robed shadows turning toward you as one. In the corner, a heap of refuse breathes, very slowly, like something asleep.

narrator/d587fdd31352f977.text: A row of narrow cells behind iron bars. It's dark in there, and the dark is breathing, quick and shallow, from more chests than you can count.

narrator/d5ab605484524612.text: She turns, slowly, and looks out across the water at the tower with the one lit window.

narrator/d5af349c28ca4ac9.text: The book on the desk is closed now. It hasn't crumbled.

narrator/d5c827da4c93acb0.text: The Rag Queen steps down off her post, twice the height of a man, all rotten silk and lace and faces in the stitching. Two of the faces tear free of her and come screaming across the field in their wedding veils.

narrator/d5d06b74d50a2e9c.text: The mirror shows the room behind you in perfect detail: the bed, the hearth, the door, and you. The count stood here every morning for centuries and saw none of that.

narrator/d5d12025fb1aa84c.text: Two small crypts, side by side.

narrator/d5d6534a94cbf90e.text: Just below the well's lip, a coil of silk rope is tied off to an iron ring. It shifts in your hands, eager to climb.

narrator/d5e0d077d19b483e.text: Feathers still drift in the dark. The ravens that are left keep very still.

narrator/d60376a9d4d971f1.text: The shades boil up out of the floor between you and the stairs, hooded and hungry. They mean to hold you here until the heap can stand.

narrator/d60d90d1af46da11.text: A cook-fire, a black pot, a ladle, and a heap of carefully split wood. The Martikovs have been camping for three months and have made it look like a habit.

narrator/d61d24dd4ba0d8fd.text: She rocks, and weeps, and rocks. Whatever is under it, the weeping keeps covered.

narrator/d631557ff608b4e7.text: A broad stone hearth, the only warm thing in the village. Someone has carved initials into the mantel: a heart, two names, a date fifty years old.

narrator/d6335c65aa98a820.text: The camp dog trots after you for a few steps, decides you aren't carrying anything to eat, and goes back to sitting very hopefully beside the pot.

narrator/d637266d211f505e.text: Ribbons, roots and wishes. If the Vistani hide things here, they hide them where outsiders don't think to dig.

narrator/d638c8ae4d04a692.text: The peak of the north tower, crowned with stone guardians on the parapet: winged, crouching, faces turned in toward you.

narrator/d6627db08e226ebe.text: Heaps of dead brush lie in the vine rows where the blights fell when the tree burned, like scarecrows somebody forgot to finish.

narrator/d6635ac3152c1a02.text: You say so. The fight goes out of him all at once.

narrator/d6799c733e37fb7a.text: The bunting is gone, and the portraits are stacked face to the wall. The house smells of someone else's tea.

narrator/d68b30802831dcc2.text: He hits you square in the hip, hard enough to sit you down in the straw, and goes back to guarding the gap. Stelian, across the pen, very carefully doesn't laugh.

narrator/d6aa939eaf70d64d.text: From under the floor a young man's voice cries out, hoarse and eager: Father, who's there? I can smell them!

narrator/d6ac252011c31971.text: They look bored, mostly. Or cold. It's hard to tell in Krezk; it might be both.

narrator/d6be21e2c64659e3.text: You take the watch in turns beside the pole. Past midnight two figures cross the square with buckets, hoods up, livery buttons catching the lamplight. Wachterhaus livery.

narrator/d6c3db0fe6a84827.text: The stairs bring you up into a corridor of closed doors. Somewhere along it, always just out of sight, someone is crying very quietly.

narrator/d6dd483e0bb2f278.text: Two burning skulls rise from the coal heaps, and the fire in the furnace stands up on legs of its own.

narrator/d6df23f9ddcd2443.text: The cage door is easy to reach. That was the idea. As your hand closes on the latch, the branches above you unfold.

narrator/d6eec4f054ea0a1d.text: The statue's base is hollow. Inside, a twist of paper holds a pinch of grey dust that makes your fingertips hard to look at.

narrator/d706d54cf65ab05b.text: Two of Dobre's lads come round the corner at a run, and two more out of the guardhouse, and none of them are smiling now.

narrator/d709ddc48b5f12d0.text: The jester's sarcophagus has a false bottom. Under it, folded small, a red cape that smells faintly of brimstone and greasepaint.

narrator/d71165cf10cffb0f.text: Izek comes off the cot in one movement, and the arm that isn't his starts to glow like a coal someone has blown on.

narrator/d72f01e8b2601119.text: The east guardroom, its watch relieved at last. Shards of frost and mail lie where they fell.

narrator/d7330f7e21ceb15f.text: The square is packed shoulder to shoulder. The watch walks through the crowd with clubs, listening.

narrator/d73d2acf03451323.text: And the blanket over the tinker's knees hides a chain from his ankle into the boards, grey and glistening, that isn't iron.

narrator/d7580cfd19ff73eb.text: The blaze points up the slope, toward the hills above the lake where, at night, the wolves are loudest.

narrator/d764efa50c61ad9c.text: The bridge is a single span of stone between two towers, and the wind leans on it from one side, then the other.

narrator/d781d21855ef90f2.text: Doru drops from the ceiling without a sound. Whatever was left of the priest's son is gone behind his eyes.

narrator/d79e205d6521475f.text: She gets up the way the very old do, in stages, and goes down the far side of the hill without once looking round.

narrator/d7a539ef9c87b4ff.text: Thigh-deep in the cold, your boots find the bell where it fell: on its side in the silt, green with weed, its clapper still swinging. Wedged in the mouth of it, somebody's offerings from a long time ago, coins gone black.

narrator/d7e85e58499d577a.text: The barn's roof came down in one piece and lies in the lane like a ramp, beams and rotten thatch packed hard. Children have worn a path up it. From the top you can see over the back fences to the square.

narrator/d7f1875badabcede.text: The stair climbs the inside of the tower in long turns with no rail at all, and in the middle there is nothing: a black well of air going straight down.

narrator/d7f45f5ec025711a.text: Green-painted figures step out of the hedgerow on both sides of the road, and at their head walks an old woman you last saw among the roots of a black tree. The tree called her back, as she said it would. You let it keep calling.

narrator/d81c81ad56213833.text: The wardens' inscription, in our own plain words: "Zantras, who crowned beggars. Every king it made was pulled apart by the crowd that loved him. Do not look at it for long."

narrator/d836535755276b75.text: A slab of black stone, its grooved edges running to a drain. The drain is not dry.

narrator/d837addf2a956154.text: Dmitri Krezkov sends down what Krezk pays for a wolf that takes children: a purse, and a set of iron bands that have hung in the watch house since before his grandfather, for the wolf that never came.

narrator/d83eeedc7e01db8e.text: The family crypts, where the dead keep their own counsel. Most of them.

narrator/d85783053cb02d38.text: You raise the silver flame toward the cradle, and behind you, slow and heavy on the stair, comes armour.

narrator/d85fb37dfa14083b.text: For a long moment Izek's arm smokes at the knuckles. Then he turns his back on all of you and goes to stand somewhere.

narrator/d867567b8de44554.text: Warm, close and dark. Straw and furs, gnawed bones, the smell of animals that are sometimes people, and somewhere deeper in, small voices whispering.

narrator/d86bb575465ce86b.text: The road ends here, in a trampled half-circle of snow before the gate, as if it had walked all this way and lost its nerve.

narrator/d8b6b2968748df8d.text: Davian whistles two notes. Ravens come down out of the trees, off the eaves, off the roof of the press house, until the yard is black with them and every one is looking at you.

narrator/d8c852d3152e13a9.text: A hunter making a hunter's offer. If there's a hook in it, he's hidden it as well as he hides himself in a blind.

narrator/d8d35d34098bac57.text: A tripwire runs knee-high across the floor in front of the trophy cabinet, to a hunting crossbow on the wall above it.

narrator/d8db8148afafd6a5.text: The churchyard earth heaves. Old graves split along their seams, and the village's dead climb out to finish the funeral their own way.

narrator/d8eb2d28d5e78eab.text: Under the jetty's last boards, tied to a post below the waterline, a ring on a string. It is dry when you pull it up, though the string is soaked.

narrator/d928564dca821626.text: The trail climbs through pines and tumbled boulders. Through the trees, far below, the lake glints like a dropped knife.

narrator/d92cd73b5e3f6a5c.text: A cleft runs up the hill's west flank, choked with thorn and loose shale, out of sight of the camp on the shoulder.

narrator/d930c53210b6d2ac.text: The bunting sags. Somebody has turned half the Baron's portraits to the wall and then, out of kindness, turned a few of them back.

narrator/d945324250ae2595.text: Petru looks at you once. Then he walks out of the light toward the old wolf, and the old wolf puts its great head down beside his, and they go off into the dark together, the boy running on all fours before they reach the trees.

narrator/d945334955d7c2f3.text: She opens the captain's roll, finds a name near the middle of the page, and draws a small, neat line through it. Next to it she writes a number: 1.

narrator/d9501c47f4abecbb.text: The brand on her flank is still smoking. Whatever it's doing to her, it isn't finished.

narrator/d959aaa7b813d238.text: The blights lie where they fell, dead brush in heaps around their holes. Only the druid with the lantern is still digging, and he has a spade now, and opinions about who should use it.

narrator/d95d4b27b0d0866d.text: The racks are hung with fish now, rows and rows of them, silver going grey. Nobody is going to eat them.

narrator/d967f8bb67faeabb.text: Over the foot of the stair, two words cut deep and plain: HE RESTS. Nothing about peace.

narrator/d969f5ebdeb14a18.text: Cold stone, high vaults and dust, and somewhere an organ playing. Stairs climb, stairs descend, and every door is a little ajar, as if the house expects you.

narrator/d985650c5a11a19c.text: Escher's coats hang in the open wardrobe, beautiful and empty.

narrator/d9905004accfc2db.text: The headman's wagon: painted horses gallop round the sides. Inside, a child's bed, empty, its blanket thrown back.

narrator/d9a36cd29469f308.text: He closes his eyes, or the sparks dim, and when they brighten again he is smiling at you pleasantly.

narrator/d9b6c52ac25ac3c3.text: Ink, staves, a smudge that might be a tear. The notes refuse to become a tune, and the stand tips the music face down as if embarrassed for you.

narrator/d9b95e194ddb22bf.text: Stairs to the rooms upstairs. On the bottom step, a sign in Arik's square hand: ROOMS. LOCKS WORK.

narrator/d9c512721d22aa88.text: His eyes flick to Ireena, and back to you, and his smile goes stiff at the corners.

narrator/d9cf744c6ccddced.text: Coin from every reign the valley ever had, and some it didn't. Most of it has never been touched by anyone but a tax collector.

narrator/d9e7ec2b751b92a3.text: Empty crates, lids pried off, bottoms lined with grave earth. Somebody should burn them. Somebody will.

narrator/da359707965ffdbb.text: His eyes keep going back to her. Her hair, her hands, the line of her throat. Not hunger. Worse: the look of a collector at the one piece missing from a set he has spent his whole life completing.

narrator/da830cf16c0c1521.text: The silver goes soft and dark. The little painted woman curls up like a leaf.

narrator/da8eff6aa562f9ae.text: The lid lifts with a sigh of old air. Something inside was never his.

narrator/da9879970e7b7c89.text: The frost around the cairn lies in a perfect ring, and the snow that falls on the ring doesn't settle. Something here is waiting to clap.

narrator/da9e858b824a2896.text: Two burned-out candles and two empty trestles. The room still feels like it's holding its breath.

narrator/dadb80929a8918f2.text: The great hall again. The lamp has not burned any lower.

narrator/dae6ee95e33ec473.text: Sir Godfrey laughs. It starts low in the armour and keeps on coming, until his helmet rings with it and the dust comes down from the rafters, and he has to put a hand on the wall.

narrator/dafd44fe6303ce5b.text: She screams and throws her weight against the cord, and the brand on her flank flares white. When she comes down on all four hooves again there's no grey left in her at all.

narrator/db0c70754e28c16f.text: You shout. The others come up out of sleep with weapons in their hands, and there is nobody there. The fire has burned down to blue.

narrator/db116b65224bd4c7.text: A long gallery of fallen frames and torn canvas. Somebody has turned the few portraits still hanging to face the wall.

narrator/db4b90c25c75cc16.text: The cliff road is a ledge cut into the mountain's side, with the drop on your right getting steadily more interested in you.

narrator/db5065f9a9457c3a.text: He chatters on, pleasant and vague. If something lies underneath, he has hidden it from himself too well for you to find.

narrator/db5128298963606a.text: Swords come off the table and go back into scabbards that have not felt them in centuries. Somewhere in the house a door bangs open, and the cold that comes through it smells of horses that aren't there.

narrator/db555c980f202fa3.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Shami-Amourae, the honeyed hand. Its lovers died smiling. All of them."

narrator/db5c0b0bbdf5fbf8.text: A sweet old woman with flour on her sleeves. You find nothing else, and she watches you look.

narrator/db6459d54a65fde6.text: A great bowl of yellow bone by the door, with a pole for steering. It is the top of a skull, and the skull was the size of a cart.

narrator/db8bf48bb0386f84.text: Wren is doing his forms by the dead fire, very slowly, over and over, the same three moves.

narrator/dba605521e538c0b.text: The brand hisses like a doused coal and goes out. The embers in her eyes sink and go dark, and she is grey, all grey, and shaking, and very much a horse.

narrator/dba6b0e264778cce.text: Needle blights are scraping at the earth floor with their claws, and a druid with a lantern is telling them where.

narrator/dbc657f62f09bede.text: The lantern swings toward the ditch and stops. The lead mourner says three words, in a voice like a door that has not been opened in years: room for one.

narrator/dbe226af07b8ae86.text: All through the temple, the voices in the sarcophagi fall silent for a moment, as if a door had shut somewhere in a house they live in.

narrator/dbea4a18342c0329.text: Your voice catches his and carries it. He finds the next line, and the next, and the howling below fades under the two of you.

narrator/dc183daa56b4bae9.text: The inscription, in plain words: "Yrrga, the eye that opened outside. Its priests put out their own eyes. It was a mercy, and they knew it."

narrator/dc1c7db408212d31.text: A long day by the window in the light, with prayers every hour. By evening he's stopped watching the castle road, and is watching the bread instead.

narrator/dc26207e97616f7b.text: The room drops cold enough to hurt, and the boy flings himself at the nearest of you.

narrator/dc2673d6170ecb91.text: Cold ashes and a stone that won't move. The fishers who lived here took everything with them.

narrator/dc377b15b02455fa.text: The sigils run round the walls in one unbroken line, and every one of them points at the iron reliquary in the corner.

narrator/dc40e5c3d814024d.text: A dead pine by the trail, and a silver cage hung from its lowest branch. Inside, a young raven with every feather on end, beak open, making no sound at all.

narrator/dc4a2b4a313e7eba.text: He watches you reach for your weapons, and for the first time something crosses his face that isn't kindness. It looks very like grief.

narrator/dc526b8c95ba67ca.text: Paint, wood and the faces of saints nobody prays to. The statue gives you nothing.

narrator/dc58fd466b5dc611.text: His body comes apart into grey mist that pours away across the floor, through the cracks, and down. A vampire beaten goes home to its coffin. His lies under the castle, at the bottom of everything.

narrator/dc5ad64570090bb6.text: A clay pot of rendered fat, a skinning knife beside it and a basket of rags. Somebody here keeps a household, of a kind. The knife has been sharpened very recently.

narrator/dc634056f5df0de4.text: Blinsky comes down the stair with the puppet in his arms and listens to all of it: the first Pidlwick, the stair, the hundred years of sorry.

narrator/dc67628e140ea197.text: Rows of stoppered bottles, most of them labelled in a careful hand. You take the ones whose labels you can read.

narrator/dc67bb3bde191d4d.text: A tidy study: a desk, an inkstand, a bookcase of very old and very unread books. One of the shelves has no dust at its edge.

narrator/dc6d7df985ed015b.text: Pale lights bob out over the reeds, three of them, and drift toward you, swaying, the way a lantern sways in the hand of someone walking. Nobody is holding them.

narrator/dc760fe6cb67544e.text: He doesn't answer at once. The frogs stop. The wind stops. The flame in the grave-lamp, if it is lit, lies down flat.

narrator/dc8277d5f989ade7.text: The crest. The humming is very loud up here, and under it there's another sound: slow, deep, irregular, like something enormous learning how to have a pulse.

narrator/dc8ab1e4218c9baf.text: She is not afraid, and she is not resigned. She is waiting for nightfall, and for a visitor, with the calm of someone who has never once been let down by him.

narrator/dca6c9c517274a2e.text: The stair turns down into the dark. The bar has left fresh gouges in its brackets, and the bottom edge of the door is scored with marks like fingernails, from the other side.

narrator/dca7870ac751425d.text: At the bottom of the temple, beside a great hollow sarcophagus, a stooped scholar in spectacles is waiting, a book open in his hands as if he'd been reading by the amber's glow.

narrator/dcad90b15e548770.text: The valley has a new lord. It does not much matter to the valley which name it fears.

narrator/dcaf394fd46cfef9.text: Then she is gone, and Berez is empty at last, and the marsh goes on making its small wet sounds as if nothing has happened.

narrator/dcbf93ea1751387a.text: Painted wagons stand in a ring around a fire between the road and the black water of Lake Zarovich. Somebody is playing a fiddle very well, and nobody is dancing.

narrator/dcd01c531cb98574.text: The sails turn in the wind, creaking at every pass. A mill doing a mill's honest work, for once, even if there is nothing in it to grind.

narrator/dcddba734bfffcbb.text: Sausages, cheese, a sack of flour, and a smell of cloves. It's an ordinary pantry. That's the worst thing in the hut.

narrator/dce0a2850ea5242f.text: Figures stand in the lane ahead and behind, in the clothes of farmers and carters. One of them still has a pastry in its hand.

narrator/dd1d28d0de22ffae.text: The crypt is low and cold, lined with burial niches. In the middle, on a stone plinth, stands the sarcophagus of St. Andral, its lid pushed a hand's breadth crooked.

narrator/dd7ac4652c347e78.text: The crowd cheers. It's the first cheer of the day that nobody had to be prodded into, and the Baron very nearly weeps.

narrator/dd7e068abdbfefa6.text: The water in the well climbs the shaft on its own. She comes up out of it in her wedding veil, screaming, and the shadows in the square crawl toward her as if she's called them in to supper.

narrator/dd9ec0092cec3c2a.text: At the graveside Davian keeps looking at Adrian, like a man who has something to say and has forgotten the language it's in.

narrator/ddb572b25255b8f6.text: Ireena pushes through the crowd to you with her sword already belted on and her bag over her shoulder.

narrator/ddef136ef6bb532a.text: An old pine scored by claws, with branches low and thick enough to climb. Ten feet up, you'd see over the brush to both bends of the road.

narrator/ddf6e2b7814c3059.text: You stand before the altar. The cold is worse here, as if the stone remembers being prayed at and resents it.

narrator/de04244186a61c8d.text: Every frog in the marsh goes silent at once.

narrator/de08fe7fdd6c42c5.text: He looks at you a long while. Then he sits down on the edge of the grave and puts the spade across his knees.

narrator/de0e30ecf02db2d7.text: A bare room: a cot, a rack of curved swords, a ledger on a stand. A small man in black sits on the cot polishing a blade, and the air around him is full of faint screaming.

narrator/de15c0eabfbff0e8.text: The air turns cold enough to fog your breath. At the lych-gate, where nobody stood a moment ago, a tall man in a fine black coat waits, hat in hand, like a mourner who came late.

narrator/de2a940f033b671f.text: You find what shelter there is among the stones. The pool steams faintly in the cold. Long after midnight, something scrapes on the north wall.

narrator/de2edfea4b92d20e.text: She looks at you for a long moment, then pushes her left sleeve up. On the inside of her wrist is a mark like a thumbprint of jam.

narrator/de4eb1c41e807a5c.text: Captain Merrow draws his sword alone. Behind the panels his company stands in its ranks, and does not come.

narrator/de508fd4840e52b2.text: You kneel beside him and pray aloud. For a few breaths the voice under the floor stops, as if it's listening too.

narrator/de5650ca3a86625c.text: The bridge is older than the road on either side of it, and the river under it is the colour of strong tea. Something white turns over once in the current and is gone.

narrator/de73a1186336c69b.text: Three of the plinths are empty now, and their knights lie in the aisle in pieces that were never stone.

narrator/de990aca37339894.text: Thistle is lying on her back by the fire, looking up at the place where stars would be if the fog let them through.

narrator/de9b8e2937ff9613.text: You draw the sheet up over her face. It is the first thing in this house that has felt like a funeral.

narrator/dea65c7ffae754e8.text: Far below, deep in the castle, something draws a long breath, and the whole tower seems to listen.

narrator/deac40691b9b58b6.text: The big dog sniffs your boots for a long moment, decides you are not food and not trouble, and lies down across the square's best patch of sun.

narrator/ded75e3b016f9aa2.text: A heap of bones in a hollow, out of sight of the trail. Deer, mostly. Sheep. Further down, newer, the long bones of something that walked on two legs, cracked for the marrow.

narrator/ded82534aaee4533.text: The mountain exhales through a crack in the floor, and the breath is cold enough to stop yours.

narrator/dee5eb8b2f8548e6.text: He's off the wall before your weapons clear, laughing, and the laughter comes from the dark between the graves, where the earth has started to move.

narrator/deec05efa429cf50.text: He backs away, then runs, ribbon flapping. By morning he'll swear he was never on duty.

narrator/deee71f1bc11ab98.text: A long low kitchen gone feral: straw beds, a hearth with a black pot, bones in a pile, and a dozen Belviews of all sizes who stop what they're doing and repeat your footsteps back to you on the flagstones.

narrator/df03e3ca9647281a.text: In the belly of the wagon, among four years of pots and boots and bones, there's a purse heavy with travellers' money, and a gem the size of an eye, cold and clear, that the thing seems to have kept to see with.

narrator/df058b9cdc250bd0.text: Racks of weapons gone to rust, and a row of armour stands wearing nothing. Someone took the armour, and then someone else went on wearing it for four hundred years.

narrator/df0dccc6faefb158.text: Aisles of crypts run away into the dark in straight lines, each behind an iron gate with a name over it. The air is cold and very still.

narrator/df0f8a6f450f9fd3.text: A terrace of worn flagstones along the keep's wall. Past the parapet, the cliff falls away into mist, and the valley spreads out under it: the forest, the river, the lights of the village.

narrator/df1eeddea8d4e239.text: A young man in a robe of green-dyed sacking stands by the great press with one hand on the rim of a vat, as if he were comforting it. The mash inside shifts under his palm, and he doesn't flinch.

narrator/df2f1a9c6a42a2bf.text: A board of prices in neat black letters, each number roughly ten times what it should be. Underneath, smaller: "Browsing: free, for now."

narrator/df492ca2eeefa22b.text: She rocks the empty air one last time and is gone, the way breath goes from a window.

narrator/dfadaef52042938d.text: Long stacks furred with frost, books chained to their shelves, and a smell of ice instead of dust. Somewhere among the shelves, someone is humming a song they can't remember the end of.

narrator/dfb5909534bc8893.text: Black grapes. Too many. That's all you can tell.

narrator/dfbca9462290d8cc.text: A dead wolf hangs by one leg from a bent sapling, the snare bitten deep: silvered wire, tied with a neat, showy Vistani knot. More snares run off west, toward the little cold lake under the mountain.

narrator/dfc1cacf5bdb4021.text: A doll with red hair, a green dress and Ireena's face, exactly. Ireena looks at it for a long moment and says nothing at all.

narrator/e009bfeeb0a45a9e.text: A crow sits on a rain barrel and watches you with professional interest.

narrator/e037dd9b27a2672c.text: Powders, combs, a ring box with no ring in it, and a purse heavier than it looks.

narrator/e05d6606a69d405c.text: A ledge road with rock on one hand and a long drop on the other. The wind up here has opinions.

narrator/e0666914370f8dbb.text: Out of the house, into the open air, which turns out to be only slightly larger. Behind every shutter, someone is pretending not to watch you.

narrator/e0b2b6463d541028.text: The abbey's bell is ringing, slowly, though there's nobody in the tower. Somebody inside is still celebrating.

narrator/e0b47dfc1dacd6dd.text: The instruments are quiet. The drain is only a drain again, for now.

narrator/e0b8381af4b5a215.text: You tell her. She listens all the way through, holding the boy's hand, and her face does nothing at all.

narrator/e0c8b4e130c5edc5.text: It is wine. Very old, very good, and nothing else at all. He watches you work that out and looks pleased.

narrator/e0dba60de30ae5f6.text: The broom against the wall has opinions about visitors.

narrator/e0dba67c9951e639.text: The bunting is fresher than ever and the smiles are wider. In the square, a woman sits in the stocks with her back very straight, and the townsfolk walk wide around her.

narrator/e0dea8ada9a53c6d.text: Bluto stands among his drying racks up to the elbows in a net so full it has split, and silver fish flap all round his feet on the shingle. He is gutting them as fast as he can, and weeping while he does it.

narrator/e0e0c36914b1aa43.text: When it is over, the den is very quiet. Kiril, Emil, Zuleika and the last of the pack lie where they fell, and in death every one of them is only a man or a woman, and older than you thought.

narrator/e0ea0505fbc21ba6.text: A wooden shrine to the Morninglord at the crossing of two lanes: a carved sun, worn smooth by hands, and a ring of candle stubs that someone keeps lighting though they never burn for long.

narrator/e0f18967be6b0a1d.text: For a long moment he says nothing. Then he looks down at his hands as if they belonged to someone else.

narrator/e10d88f9b64745a1.text: She doesn't look up. She lifts a small loaded crossbow off her knee instead and points it at you.

narrator/e116a653b20fbdd6.text: The snow underfoot was never ground at all, only an overhang. It gives, and you slide toward the drop before your fingers find rock.

narrator/e1176fed3773aee1.text: For three hours the house smells of onions, thyme, browned butter and a great deal of muttering in another language. Stefania looks in once and is sent out again with a spoon to taste.

narrator/e117f2a8e14946f0.text: For a heartbeat the hunger leaves his face, and a scared boy looks down at you. Then it comes back.

narrator/e169749b94989958.text: Kip holds one out across the table. Strahd looks at it for a long moment, the way a cat looks at a moth, and takes it.

narrator/e16f3da8f7258c67.text: It is over quickly. It does not feel clean.

narrator/e16fe5c43be3df1c.text: Five deep gouges in the bark, higher than a tall man can reach, still weeping sap. Fresh. Something stood up tall here to sharpen its claws, and wanted you to see.

narrator/e179af035babdf15.text: The panel swings in on oiled hinges. Somebody wanted this closet kept, and kept quiet.

narrator/e185ece56e6f8871.text: Pidlwick II sits on the top step with his back to you. When you come close he shuffles along to make room, without turning round.

narrator/e18aeb36daf466e6.text: Her whole face changes. It goes soft and pink and dreadful, like a girl's.

narrator/e1994c1526e1c22c.text: A round window of colored glass, a rising sun in reds and golds. It's the brightest thing in the church, and it is the color of dusk.

narrator/e19e096a9be9aca1.text: The Grandsire comes over Krezk's wall in the moonlight with the old wolves of the pack at his heels.

narrator/e1c2f052c44dcdc3.text: A thin boy in a too-big coat is leaning over the well, shouting his own name down it to hear it come back.

narrator/e1c7727f45a664ee.text: For the first night since you met him, Tamsin falls asleep before anyone else, and doesn't wake once.

narrator/e1c813c3b9e3fbda.text: It scuttles away along the wall and is gone, out toward the mountain, faster than you'd think on those mismatched legs.

narrator/e1d7de9423ad06e7.text: The children from the road: the same faces, the same wolf. The varnish has gone brown with age, and the dust on the frame is thick enough to write in.

narrator/e1e479ffc09654eb.text: Patrina screams, and the frozen students at their desks lift their heads to scream with her.

narrator/e1e77789ec75a7bd.text: Then he isn't there. The firelight runs out to the dark and stops, and there's nobody standing where it stops.

narrator/e1f3cd9e70e6502d.text: She takes the silver horse's head, looks at it for a long time, and puts it in her own ear without a word.

narrator/e21401551947d6f0.text: Near the door stand new casks with a raven branded on each, still smelling of the Martikovs' yard.

narrator/e22582be408e4744.text: 'Set on you?' She laughs, then sees your face and stops. 'The lord on the hill pays well to know who walks his roads. Some of us take his coin. Not all of us. Not Madam Eva.'

narrator/e232b0fabd2f9886.text: A yard of frost around a stone hut. Birds hang in the air above it, mid-flight, frozen solid, and nobody has thought to take them down.

narrator/e233df85d560aab3.text: The house is quiet. It has the stillness of something that has been fed and is in no hurry for its next meal.

narrator/e2480cfadcb3b051.text: The parlour is cold. The ring of chairs has been turned to face the wall, and Lady Wachter sits alone in black, with no tea.

narrator/e249a5cd77865ecd.text: And under all of it, a boy's voice, hoarse from shouting: Da. Da, come down.

narrator/e25984857008d77d.text: Ireena stays on her knees a long moment. Then she stands, and wipes her hands on her skirt, and doesn't look back at it.

narrator/e2625250536a6dee.text: The planks of the drawbridge are old and black and sound under your boots. Below them the chasm goes down into mist.

narrator/e26763eb81d0488f.text: Tracks, and more tracks, most of them with claws. Nothing you want to follow.

narrator/e27535459f65d6cb.text: His boat is still tied at the foot of the jetty. Nobody will mind now if you take it.

narrator/e2870834d4edec97.text: The mirror is cracked clean across now, and a ribbon has been left tied round the crack like a bandage.

narrator/e2ae788bbaf5e8bd.text: You are in Vallaki, behind its sharpened palisade, where everyone is happy by order of the Baron.

narrator/e2b8a4d251c83b7a.text: A great vaulted kitchen gone to straw and bones. A dozen shapes look up from the hearth at once, and every one of them makes the same small noise you just made.

narrator/e2c1417ed0ea6057.text: Someone has kissed the lid so often that the inscription has worn smooth. The prints of lips are still in the frost.

narrator/e2c52883c2f045d0.text: A cold, frightened young man in a very old coat. Barovians don't throw anything away.

narrator/e2d0c2145cef604c.text: The ravens in the oak shuffle along their branches to make room, as if they'd like you to sit.

narrator/e2d28ae38c1b8d01.text: A tired woman in a grey hood, holding herself very straight. Whatever she means to do, she has had a long time to practise keeping it off her face.

narrator/e2f684bdbb9fd7f9.text: Godrick unbuckles the old sword from his back, the one he never draws, and holds it out across both palms the way a squire is taught to. The pommel is a griffin, worn almost smooth.

narrator/e3182e9f68cc10b5.text: His eyes go over you once, slowly, and stop at your hands. Whatever he sees there, he decides not to ask about it.

narrator/e321a23204a0f562.text: A thread of grey smoke still rises from the crown. Down here the dead blights lie in heaps along the track, like brush cut for a fire nobody lit.

narrator/e3295210a688fb3a.text: You knock. Inside, a chair scrapes, and a woman's voice comes through the wood, close and very steady.

narrator/e35ac154258e5256.text: The chest is full of oiled cloth, and in the cloth, two flasks of holy water and the Order's last pay chest, counted out to the coin.

narrator/e35d000b1449137a.text: You say it to the lid. The catacombs go very quiet, the way a room does when someone stops a clock.

narrator/e380415294f54b90.text: Out on the landing, where Rahadin can't see, he stops and leans on the wall and lets out a long, shaking breath. Then he looks at the rest of you.

narrator/e3834f8111612a0c.text: The river goes over the edge in one long white rope and vanishes into its own spray. The rock under your boots shivers with it.

narrator/e38f7424a9f137a9.text: The altar is a single block of grey stone with a sunburst carved into its face. Someone has scrubbed it so often that the sunburst is wearing away.

narrator/e396fd7190bacca5.text: Then there is only the night outside, and Ireena on her knees by the sill, shaking, herself again.

narrator/e3a2bd773af73762.text: One small cask for every year, set by for a wizard who never came. One of them, low on the rack, is colder to the touch than the rest.

narrator/e3b800b360b98daa.text: The old stump at the camp's edge is hollow. Inside, wrapped in a rag, is a corked flask that someone did not want Stanimir to know about. The cork is hot, and a thread of smoke leaks round it.

narrator/e3d2d434b65d4322.text: In one of the ravens' nests, among buttons and broken glass, a plain gold ring. When you take it, the ravens all look away, which is somehow worse.

narrator/e3d46c2deddf4a53.text: It takes a long time and both your faces go red, but her knuckles touch the log first.

narrator/e3eb435318d5eba3.text: Wooden soldiers, a top, a ball gone flat. Thorn's treasures, or most of them.

narrator/e3f1711ca78d1556.text: Steaua is in the pen when you come back, grey as river stone, with Luminita's face pressed into her neck.

narrator/e40f3433eb20927e.text: The causeway stones are slick and the water laps over them in places. Halfway across, the hair on your arms starts to stand up, all by itself.

narrator/e415e1c0804a2964.text: The great cave: a fire pit in the middle, furs and straw round the walls, a litter of bones, and a long scratched tally on the rock that nobody explains.

narrator/e428dadd25dfb22f.text: Izek's arm bursts into flame to the elbow. Most of the watch backs away from the priest; the ones who don't come with Izek.

narrator/e445a2a226c7095d.text: The lid has no inscription at all, only a keyhole carved in the stone with no lock behind it.

narrator/e45ac6065636a71b.text: Words cut into the archway in a plain, unlovely hand: one must die.

narrator/e4654aa893e8ff4c.text: Meltwater runs down the channel into the cracks, and the cracks hiss and steam and go dark one after another.

narrator/e46b9cc4eb9a340b.text: Black water, rotten boards and the smell of fish that aren't there anymore. Nothing else.

narrator/e46cbf7a79d6ce85.text: Broken stone wings lie where the gargoyles fell. Nobody has swept them up.

narrator/e48124cd9896ebe8.text: High above, on a shelf of the mountain, the abbey's bell tower and grey roofs. Even from here you can see that one window up there is always lit.

narrator/e4915dbe9cf78a67.text: A dark little bathroom: a wooden tub on clawed iron feet, a small iron stove with a kettle on it, and a barrel under a spigot that has been dry for years. The tub is full to the brim with water as black and still as a well.

narrator/e49b68dc919129b5.text: Pines, boulders, a trickle of meltwater across the path, and the lake glinting far below through the trees.

narrator/e4a31d28c85f98e1.text: Two cold presences step inside two of you and settle, the way children settle in the back of a cart. Someone is humming now, and none of you started it.

narrator/e4a8ee3f0791f987.text: The wire parts with a ping, the jar drops, and the night turns orange.

narrator/e4c686369bd9a272.text: Weeds, mud and broken stone. Something glints, or doesn't; the mist won't say.

narrator/e4cec26b563c1d50.text: Up here the stair narrows and the wind finds its way in through cracks in the wall. Some of the steps are missing.

narrator/e4d288a2e5446078.text: A girl with a basket of yellow ribbon and a pencil behind her ear. If she's hiding anything, it's hiding her.

narrator/e4de4e3faeca5000.text: A huge man in a red sash sits on the steps of his wagon with a bottle in each hand, shouting at the camp, at the lake, at the sky. The camp walks around him without looking.

narrator/e4e5db1520e048d9.text: The rod runs up the chimney and into the floors above, and it is humming, very faintly. It isn't for cooking. Something at the top of the tower is drinking from it.

narrator/e4e622dcfd54546e.text: The road climbs the last steep stretch to the tower. Faces are carved into the tower's stones, soldiers' faces, all looking down the road toward the valley.

narrator/e5017a8751e1fae8.text: Through the amber, blurred and golden, you can make out heaps of things inside. One of them is not like the rest, and it pulls at you.

narrator/e508f8cf06e2af6d.text: The hulk in the amber hasn't moved. It never moves. But the floor under your boots hums, once, like a pleased cat.

narrator/e5151069d099d458.text: The symbol catches the last of the firelight. He doesn't flinch. He looks at it the way one looks at a candle in a neighbour's window.

narrator/e536e19a0841e28a.text: A thick book chained to a stone lectern, its pages beaten from copper so that they would never burn or rot. The wardens kept their most important record where no flame could reach it.

narrator/e53c2f09f22f82c6.text: You tell their story back to them plainly, every piece the house let slip on your way down, and you do not leave out the ending.

narrator/e54424bef097c3f7.text: High in the claw-marked pine, a satchel hangs by its strap where something tore it from its owner. Inside, a pair of smoked-glass goggles that make the dark look like dusk.

narrator/e54f51a5f4f0b67e.text: The wheel slides off the axle twice, the second time onto a foot. Clovin watches with the air of a man whose day could not, in fact, get worse, and has just been proved wrong.

narrator/e55585b22caaaab1.text: 'I just hold the spear,' he says. 'Nobody tells me anything.'

narrator/e56693c2311f1f4c.text: The few ravens left keep to the far beams and watch you with flat black eyes. None of them comes near.

narrator/e589329066f53b3d.text: Wren comes back to the fire late, with his hands in his pockets, which he never does.

narrator/e5c1fbcb4688940f.text: Ilya opens his eyes, frowns at the ceiling as if it owes him money, and says he's hungry.

narrator/e5c8328f24ee71c9.text: She steps into another of you, apologizing as she goes. Now someone in the party is humming a nursery tune that none of you started.

narrator/e5d11c8106760b82.text: Trodden earth and fallen leaves. Pickers, probably.

narrator/e5d25c2f24162d8c.text: You say the old words, the ones soldiers say over the ones who don't march out with them in the morning. Down the column, one skull and then another bows forward over the pommel of a saddle.

narrator/e5d6c551e05fd481.text: A small office that smells of ink and tallow. Ledgers fill the shelves, the floor and most of the desk. The rest of the desk is an old man.

narrator/e5e86129fb47e418.text: Every blade on this floor has slipped its sheath. You can hear them in the rooms, testing the air.

narrator/e6064784406a10c7.text: Across the dark, one upstairs window of the Blue Water Inn stands wide open to the cold. You run.

narrator/e614799c82aab39a.text: The mirror has been turned round. Its owner looks into it, now and then, as if checking that someone is still there.

narrator/e618e314d7308f2a.text: Thorn starts to cry without making a sound. When you look back down the road a little later, the two of them stand exactly where you left them, and have not moved at all.

narrator/e61ac99813c852a7.text: When you let go of it, the bell stops. When you turn your back, it starts again.

narrator/e61d511a2e3d5388.text: One jar on the shelf is different from the others: blue glass, stoppered with wax, and inside it something silver turns over slowly, like a fish in a pool. The label is in a crabbed hand: THE CLEVER ONE ON THE MOUNTAIN, HIS REMEMBERING. DO NOT SHAKE.

narrator/e631fda729fffced.text: Inside the splintered heartwood, grown into the grain as if the tree made it, lies a staff of black wood that drinks the warmth from your hands.

narrator/e63264242abc0261.text: The oldest graves, along the north wall, sunk and tilted. Someone still sweeps them.

narrator/e64122d923d67cb1.text: A little wayside shrine to the Morninglord, its paint long gone. Someone has left a dream pastry on the ledge as an offering, still wrapped. Nothing has touched it, not even the crows.

narrator/e664418671dfa9a9.text: The vat's hoops are straining. The mash in it is the colour of moss, and as you watch, a bubble the size of a fist rises, bursts, and smells of the bottom of a pond.

narrator/e676854c4f19ada0.text: Prints, fog and old leaves, churned into one dark mess by something large, numerous and gone. Probably gone.

narrator/e6965365a4a1c4cc.text: Then she sees you, and smiles, and her smile has too many teeth at the corners.

narrator/e6a560c30cb1e609.text: Tamsin opens the locket once and says something to the painted face, too quietly for anyone else. Then he drops it into the fire.

narrator/e6a77eff433dc56f.text: Rahadin looks up from his blade. The screaming in the room rises a little, as if to see who has come.

narrator/e6b04c050885f41d.text: It's warm inside, too warm, and close, and the floor tilts a little as the hut settles its weight. Every wall is papered with drawings of the same handsome boy at every age, in charcoal, in the same loving hand.

narrator/e6c8cd903f0143fe.text: Out on the black water, a long way under it, a bell rings. Once. Again. Each time a little louder, as if it were coming up the slope of the lakebed toward you.

narrator/e6e51acfd67f963f.text: The cells empty all at once, and the noise is everyone's voice but their own.

narrator/e6e54221774e2308.text: The lights are gone. Under the roar of the water there's still one voice, hoarse and very real: "Da? Is somebody there? I can't climb it. I've tried."

narrator/e6e9355d9aa02725.text: The winch shrieks, the chain runs, and ahead the portcullis grinds up into the ceiling.

narrator/e6edeeed0d10d61c.text: From the top of the tower the whole tarn is laid out below, and the causeway, and Ezmerelda's fire, and far away to the east, small and black on its crag, the castle.

narrator/e6ee96a0760f7493.text: You dream of a lullaby sung through a floor, and a door that never opens.

narrator/e6f6b4445e64b7ad.text: Bundles of herbs hang drying from the roof: yarrow, valerian, and a great deal of wolfsbane. Each bundle is tied with a different coloured thread, in an order only one person understands.

narrator/e71200bf6712b051.text: Beside Tamsin's reflection there is a second one, though nobody stands beside him: a young man in an old coat with a sunburst at the breast, looking at the locket with an expression nobody should have to wear for three hundred years.

narrator/e75b8fa013c990c1.text: The marks lose themselves in pine needles. The woods are very quiet, in the way that means something is listening.

narrator/f08529a30cc77611.text: Something crosses the ceiling, quick and flat as a spider, and settles above you. A young man's face hangs upside down in the dark, smiling.

narrator/f0b3042d4038500a.text: He sits down on the step outside the shop with his back to the window.

narrator/f0c21fc79f9c18da.text: You walk for an hour and come back to your own footprints. By the time the snow lifts, the light has moved a long way across the sky.

narrator/f0deff67248e629d.text: A table with a dice game left in the middle: three bone dice, a pile of tin buttons for stakes, and one die still balanced on its corner.

narrator/f0eeffe11085a92d.text: The chant softens, almost kindly: the altar is waiting for one of you to lie down on it. Whoever does will not get up.

narrator/f0f0329b35e197cf.text: Two little beds, a rocking horse, drawings pinned to the walls, and a dollhouse so fine it seems to be holding its breath. The door was locked from the outside.

narrator/f119872b185685ed.text: Long crates with the lids nailed down from inside. Pressing your ear to one, you hear nothing at all: no breath, no heartbeat, the silence of something that doesn't need either.

narrator/f11c974eeb487ba0.text: Steel clears leather. The wolves were waiting for exactly that.

narrator/f146e9e1cd485a7d.text: Its eyes follow conversations, not movements. When someone says the name of the lord on the hill, every feather on it lifts at once. Whatever this bird is, it is not his.
