narrator/f14f65f7ca99f05c.text: The beam swings down like a door slammed in your face.

narrator/f15ee26b4b90989f.text: The track runs on logs across the marsh, with reeds closing in on both sides and black water winking through the gaps.

narrator/f1658ef78521778c.text: Every door on the lane is boarded over from inside, which means the people who live here nailed themselves in. Behind the boards, a child's voice asks a question and is hushed.

narrator/f1661bfbf23a2ed2.text: Sharpened logs, chest-thick, twice a man's height. Here and there a log has been replaced, recently, where something on the other side clawed it through.

narrator/f181625f52039028.text: A big, bearded man in a burgomaster's chain, painted glaring at the artist. Someone has hung a black ribbon across the corner of the frame.

narrator/f186e4098274ffb6.text: The cage hangs a foot below the landing, swaying on its chain, and the winch's brake is off. Nobody steps into that.

narrator/f1b1c7119399f69b.text: A hearth big enough to stand in, swept perfectly clean. Nobody has lit it since the night the house fell. Somebody sweeps it anyway.

narrator/f1bbdde080950d85.text: Velvet, dust, a canopied bed nobody sleeps in, and a mirror that shows the room without anyone in it.

narrator/f1c549178e3d9751.text: Old leather armor, cracked but whole, and three darts still lodged between the ribs. Whoever this was, the room was ready for them.

narrator/f1d8569bf0980194.text: He stands silent a long moment while the howling goes on. Then he finishes the prayer in a whisper, very fast, as if afraid it won't let him.

narrator/f1dce8e84ceacc77.text: He heaves the sack out into the deep water. It hits with a slap and sinks at once.

narrator/f1ed4b8a76193a27.text: You tell him about the pool. Ireena tells him the rest herself, in a flat, steady voice, about a wall, and a stair, and a morning full of white flowers.

narrator/f1f30ed35ef1ee9e.text: It's late and quiet, and Wren is lying flat on his back in the grass, perfectly still. It takes you a moment to realise he isn't asleep.

narrator/f218b8d6266f55b9.text: It looks at the leaf, then west toward Yester Hill, then at you, with great meaning, and goes.

narrator/f21f0cf396910cfc.text: The chest opens on three blank books bound in black leather, three rolled scrolls, and the smell of an old secret.

narrator/f22dc75821844d8c.text: Up close, the vines nearest the house have put out small, bright, absolutely unreasonable new leaves.

narrator/f241b7e1e10debb5.text: The empty plinth isn't solid. In a hollow under its top lies a silver ring, cold as frost. The dragon's hoard was carried off; this one piece, someone saved.

narrator/f2428f4a0e6dcab5.text: A tapestry so faded that the hunt on it is only shapes: riders, hounds, and something tall in the trees that none of them has noticed yet.

narrator/f255d49ed8f71ed0.text: At the top of the last turn the stair opens into a round room full of grey sky, and in the middle of it something red is beating.

narrator/f25c18f3e9a446d8.text: The west gate opens onto the lake road and a ring of painted wagons outside the walls. Music comes from the wagons, and the watch on this gate pretends very hard not to hear it.

narrator/f282a0b72c0ab6fe.text: The millstone sits in the middle of the floor under its hopper, and the floor around it is swept very clean. Nothing else in the mill is swept that clean.

narrator/f283df98925841e8.text: A standing harp by the hearth, every string still taut. One of them hums when you breathe near it.

narrator/f29f4f7bd879f0d1.text: The village falls behind you, shutter by shutter, and nobody waves. Somewhere ahead the road forks, and from its cliff the castle watches you choose.

narrator/f2b0e18a06063025.text: A hovel leaning against the palisade as though it's tired. A loaf on the sill, a big one, newly bought.

narrator/f2bf02b0ff58f291.text: A tool shed leaning against the garden wall, its door held shut with a loop of wire.

narrator/f2ce4610fee8c562.text: The figures in the frost turn their heads. Ice cracks off their mail as they stand.

narrator/f2d0efd7051eb18b.text: Two small cold weights slip out of two of you and away up the stairs, back to the attic where the house keeps its children.

narrator/f2d4b122676c64a2.text: A grey wolf stands square in the narrows, head low, while more shapes wait in the fog beyond it and something shifts in the trees behind you. None of them growl; they are waiting to see what you do.

narrator/f2d9ea2b0583e49f.text: Then he lies down in the furrow between the vines, and talks, very quietly, as if somebody were answering.

narrator/f30ab8c4b102f87a.text: Parriwimple steps between you and his uncle, very gently, like a wall that has decided to be polite.

narrator/f30f3632ecd37453.text: A long table scarred by knives, with three stools pulled up to it: one tall and narrow, one wide and sagging, one with a cushion on it.

narrator/f31dc3a990ab5cc4.text: As you come closer, its head turns all the way round to look at you.

narrator/f320ad25dffe543d.text: The pass, with its bridge and its tower. The portcullis stands up in its slot now, and the road goes on into the cloud.

narrator/f34b68a34fe9712e.text: Switchbacks of pine and scree, and on the trees, here and there, marks scratched at head height: names, crossed out, one after another.

narrator/f3504fef695f55ab.text: His face gives you nothing at all. It is a very good face for that. He looks back as if you were the one being read.

narrator/f35c50426af74022.text: Pidlwick II hops up the first steps ahead of you, then remembers his promise and drops back behind.

narrator/f37e44f762fb9096.text: Wachterhaus stands behind its own iron fence, older and better kept than its neighbours. The curtains are drawn on every window but one, and in that one, the curtain moves.

narrator/f3c00d3e47382748.text: The track comes up over the last switchback onto a shelf of the mountain, and there it is: grey stone walls, a bell tower, slate roofs furred with snow. It's very quiet. Then, from somewhere inside, something laughs in a voice that is almost a child's.

narrator/f3c1b85c3ac275b8.text: At the back of the cellar, a dark gap in the brickwork where a wine merchant sits among his bottles.

narrator/f3d19a90d82813f7.text: Stelian drops his crook. Somebody in the south row screams, and then laughs, and then can't stop.

narrator/f3e3090fa8f9f6bc.text: A rain barrel brimming with black water. Something has been drinking from it, and not with a cup.

narrator/f3e4bd25a620bed6.text: He takes a long time to stand up, and longer to put his coat on, and longest of all on the stairs. From the lantern room above, something hums and goes quiet as he passes the hearth rod: the ward is down.

narrator/f3e7b4c1b8f49f46.text: A dozen goats in a pen of split rails, and a billy with one horn who stands between you and the nannies and stares with absolute conviction.

narrator/f3ec691a50417f1f.text: The one-horned billy plants his feet in the gap of the pen and lowers his head at you. On his one horn, jammed down hard against the skull, is a thin silver ring.

narrator/f4031d4b4c6686b6.text: The lake path runs back east along the shore toward Vallaki's palisade and the bright wagons outside its west gate.

narrator/f40bacc4d3575ac4.text: A plain church, cold and quiet, with the sunburst above an empty altar. It feels, for the first time, like a room people could pray in.

narrator/f4133dcd7749b163.text: He bangs on the gate. The man who comes out through the wicket is broad and grey-bearded, wrapped in a sheepskin, with the face of someone who has buried more than he has planted.

narrator/f41e42df21da65a3.text: The blank books aren't blank any more. He has been writing in all of them at once.

narrator/f4236cce921faf01.text: She digs under the crocheted blanket, prises the green stone out from under the root's chin, and drops it into your palm as if it burned. In the cradle, the root begins very slowly to wither.

narrator/f42f57b03a5f3be4.text: He nods, very politely, and sits down on the top step with the slate in his lap. He doesn't write anything else.

narrator/f4326ce6388699ec.text: The cellar's far wall has been broken through, and beyond it the earth floor is a field of holes, as if something very large and very stupid has been looking for a coin.

narrator/f435637f5b62f704.text: The song falls flat somewhere around the chorus. Arik stops polishing a glass to watch it die.

narrator/f466f42eeac14581.text: A hunting crossbow on the wall swings round on its bracket and looses.

narrator/f473cbc44a42e252.text: Behind the third shelf of unread sermons, your fingers find a catch that the dust has been politely ignoring.

narrator/f482ba38643799ed.text: You tell him about the gallows at the crossroads, and the board, and the two words on it. He listens with his hands flat on the rail.

narrator/f498f4ccb8c931d2.text: The Penitent stands up out of the gorge wall, nine pilgrims fused in grey ice, and turns all its heads toward you.

narrator/f49e103e07e4cd36.text: Lake Zarovich, black and flat to the far shore. Fishermen's boats lie hauled up on the bank, all of them dry, all of them for a long time.

narrator/f4a048c4399fb391.text: A throne of bones at the head of the table, taller than the rest. The skulls on its back face outward, toward the guests.

narrator/f4ccf5207e3f5852.text: A guard post with arrow slits and an empty weapon stand. Whoever stood here left a long time ago.

narrator/f4db2f3db6a90b36.text: Four of the company step out of the walls, grey under crimson and hungry, and Merrow draws the sword he carried for twenty years.

narrator/f4e42bf61bb70ec9.text: It goes down like warm honey and lands like a kick. For a moment the valley feels almost like somewhere people live on purpose.

narrator/f4e8748a746a8402.text: In the corner of the little attic storage room, a panel no bigger than a fingernail hides a stair that winds down inside the walls, past every floor, below a cellar the house doesn't have.

narrator/f4f6ded809a6a833.text: Somewhere back toward the shrine, a woman's voice begins to keen, and keeps on, and then stops all at once, the way a door shuts.

narrator/f502ce3165969eef.text: Supper is a stew tonight, and Ratatoille has fussed over it for an hour. When he finally ladles it out, Liriel folds her hands over her bowl, as she always does, and says grace.

narrator/f5155f5acab07afc.text: A painted sign of a bunch of grapes dripping red into a cup: the Blood of the Vine. The paint has run in the damp, so the cup looks rather fuller than intended.

narrator/f528f51e3053edd3.text: A rocking horse with one glass eye, still rocking very gently.

narrator/f530a5d1865c74d3.text: Black robes on pegs, hoods up, arms hanging. From the corner of your eye, a row of people waiting their turn.

narrator/f5391522f58a9878.text: A long gallery of dark portraits. At its heart hangs the master of the house himself, painted life-sized, and his eyes are already on the door.

narrator/f53c537c7795d69f.text: A cairn of flat stones, each one scratched with a name. There are a great many names. None of them has been crossed out, which would mean someone came back for it.

narrator/f53fe4d1f1f788d8.text: It is this house, perfect down to the doorknobs: the hall, the den with its tiny stag's head, the nursery with its tiny crib. Someone spent years on it.

narrator/f544f31d363b555a.text: Three hollows in a heap of straw and rags, each the shape of a sleeper. One is very large. Above them, little bags hang from hooks in the beam.

narrator/f54e02841be8ef3c.text: A long table laid for a dinner party: silver, crystal, napkins folded into swans, a centerpiece of dried roses. Every chair is pulled out an inch, as if expecting someone.

narrator/f5536f74a36d1735.text: Hedda, at the back of the nave, puts a hand flat against a pillar and closes her eyes. For the space of one breath her face changes, as if someone has opened a door onto a warm room.

narrator/f56259fc5869a486.text: The candles along the altar rail gutter, all of them, at once.

narrator/f5641448d44b2ae7.text: The lane is already greening over. Nobody pushes a cart up here any more, and the ruts are filling with rain.

narrator/f57b9b955f9237c4.text: A game of patience laid out with no queens in the deck. It can never come out. It has been laid out a great many times.

narrator/f5887715a5c2de66.text: The lock fights back. The pick slips and skates across the silver, and Emil hisses through his teeth.

narrator/f59a3e9d200d2356.text: A piercing two-fingered whistle splits the air. Every bird in the trees leaves at once. Liriel lowers her hand, pink to the ears.

narrator/f59ec455d496e1b6.text: From the watch rock you can see the whole lake and the trail coming up from it, every bend. Nobody has climbed this hill unseen for a long time.

narrator/f5abfb2fd4c1c471.text: He listens. Halfway through, he lets go of Vasilka's hand.

narrator/f5f4481dd529a6ac.text: You don't give him a speech. You give him a place to start, and he takes it.

narrator/f612f31705ddd0d5.text: Everything in the hut has slid against one wall. The drawings of the boy hang sideways, and the stewpot lies on the floor where the hearth used to be.

narrator/f614f5b81353c5e5.text: Cart ruts climb the hill between scree and bramble, worn deep by somebody who comes and goes every week, in all weathers, pushing something heavy.

narrator/f619e524698e7352.text: You take the knife and the stick and show him: thumb behind the blade, little cuts, away from yourself. He watches with his tongue between his teeth. By the end of the watch the dog is a spoon, and a fairly good one.

narrator/f65f6430405ecc64.text: She means it. You think she means it. It's hard to tell with an eye that size.

narrator/f66725cbbbc6f732.text: Nine dry steps down into a vault of white stone. Behind you, Ireena counts them under her breath, and gets the number right before you reach the bottom.

narrator/f670a7cb5f6c825b.text: The light goes, all at once, as if a lid has been put on the valley. Then it comes back. High above the road something the size of a ship's sail banks over the ridge, turns its head to look down at you, and decides you are too small to bother with. Today.

narrator/f6712746e38b9e27.text: You sleep under the Krezkovs' roof with the shutters barred. Twice in the night you hear Anna singing upstairs, and once you hear Dmitri on the stair, stopping to listen, then going back down.

narrator/f67eabe9e0bb9875.text: It takes the better part of an hour. The wire comes out stitch by stitch, bright as the day he put it in, and Mother holds very still and tells you about every one of the nine gifts, in order, without once raising her voice.

narrator/f6839674bca8711b.text: He holds up his hands to show you he's harmless, and in the moonlight you can see the veins on the backs of them. They are dark, and they branch, like the leaves.

narrator/f6872b919f4ec0fb.text: A steep, narrow stair hidden in the walls, climbing into the attic. The steps are worn in the middle by small feet.

narrator/f68d09e778cb262b.text: The grey star's cold light leans toward whoever carries its gift, the way a plant leans toward a window.

narrator/f6a5aa2a75b34795.text: You are in the drowned ruins of Berez, the marsh up to every windowsill.

narrator/f6b0a3924b203447.text: The abbey stands silent on its shelf. Nobody lights the lamp at the gate any more. The Belviews have, though, for the first time, put washing out on a line.

narrator/f6b582f549604201.text: Away from the fire, on a stool by a wagon with its shutters closed, sits an elf with ash-dark skin and white hair, mending a net he will never cast. He doesn't look up until you are close enough to touch.

narrator/f6ba1c1bd2bcbdac.text: Another spare bedroom, as cold as the first: a narrow bed, a wardrobe, a stove nobody has lit in years.

narrator/f6c1a3a38847ce39.text: Stone, and the outline in the dust of whatever stood here. Nothing else.

narrator/f6c49033dea971b5.text: A boy's room, kept as he left it. You don't search it any harder than that.

narrator/f6c7e438a06992f1.text: You look for whatever looks back out of a man's eyes, and there is nothing there. Not cruelty, not grief, not boredom: a clean, empty room with the lamp left on.

narrator/f6e4a422d58cf978.text: The bricks come out one at a time. Behind them, in a rack's worth of space, a man in a good merchant's coat sits among his own bottles, long dead, with his ledger in his lap.

narrator/f6e5ec418fab90aa.text: You are on the road in the mists, and the mists have closed behind you like a door.

narrator/f6fe29c7058031b2.text: He nods once, as if that settles something. Then he shrugs out of the ragged trapper's cloak the wolf never quite tore off him and drops it round her shoulders.

narrator/f714c210bc2fb610.text: A bowstring creaks in the trees to the left, and another to the right. A grizzled man steps onto the road ahead with an arrow on the string, not quite aimed at anybody.

narrator/f71dcc0a65161193.text: The road west, out of the village toward the crossroads. The mud is printed with wolf tracks going both ways, and boot prints going one.

narrator/f734ec6a1529ed32.text: Behind the servants' hearth, one stone sits a finger's width proud of the others. Behind it, wrapped in a rag, somebody's careful little savings.

narrator/f739fe526b580d98.text: He picks the black grapes by feel, without looking, a whole hat full. He eats them standing there, one after another, with his eyes shut.

narrator/f74c0aaef80fb8cd.text: As you reach the gap, two small cold weights tear out of two of you and are dragged back into the dark, crying. The house keeps what it owns.

narrator/f77219d5e9da2756.text: The blade wakes in your hand, and so does he: the light finds his face and his eyes snap open, burning.

narrator/f77f3f8bb1a0280b.text: He's looking at his hands. Not the way a man looks at hands that ran away; the way a man looks at hands that did as they were told.

narrator/f7900f517ee81ffa.text: It stands, and keeps standing, until its top brushes the ceiling.

narrator/f797b8eaf7893182.text: Silvain kneels and puts the Tome of Strahd into the empty hands, real and heavy, open at the page he's reading. Then they close it.

narrator/f79a85414a24af69.text: A shrine draped in black velvet, with a silver S worked into the cloth and a crystal goblet at its foot, rinsed clean. There is a faint red ring inside it anyway.

narrator/f79bbd373e05c57b.text: The grief is real. So is the other thing under it, which isn't love so much as a collector's anger at a broken piece. He mourns her the way a man mourns a thing he owned.

narrator/f79eb7118095442e.text: Behind the frost on the cell wall, tally marks: hundreds of them, in rows of five. The last row stops at three.

narrator/f7a20baddb1c417c.text: Wine glasses in rows and a box of playing cards, the deck still in its paper. The Dursts were always expecting company.

narrator/f7d1e97ca0b3831c.text: A clay oven big enough to sit in. You decide not to wonder why that is the first thing you thought.

narrator/f7e9613319216ac6.text: In the meat of his palm there's a pale splinter, gone in deep and still going: the skin puckers round it as if it's being drawn in on a thread. The logs on the pile have all rolled a little closer to the pallet in the night.

narrator/f7f18c56dddb96c2.text: The one desk free of frost. A book lies open on it, its pages crumbling and re-forming, crumbling and re-forming.

narrator/f81a43bdb3c50446.text: The flagstone sinks, and a blade swings out of the wall at knee height with a sound like a breath drawn in.

narrator/f82bea445412f914.text: She rings a little silver bell by the bed, and somewhere far off in the castle a door opens and closes.

narrator/f83fac48facd06d0.text: Powders, brushes, a silver comb with long dark hairs in it, and a hand mirror turned face down. You leave it face down.

narrator/f87be0b4a18a22ba.text: He carries it to the nearest row and presses it into the soil with his thumb. For a moment nothing happens. Then the vine above it makes a small sound, like a cork easing out of a bottle.

narrator/f87d1c51d5a4fa1b.text: A stone well with a good rope and a sweet smell. The water is cold and clean. In Barovia that alone is worth a pilgrimage.

narrator/f87ef41d538f13a8.text: Stairs going down into warm dark. The chant comes up them like a tide.

narrator/f8840f78b7eae0d2.text: Exethanter sits very still at his desk, unpinning his notes one at a time and reading each before he lets it fall.

narrator/f884e84f5f3c09dd.text: A quilt pieced from a dozen old livery coats. Under the pillow, a wooden spoon carved into a crude little Belview, tusk and ear and hoof.

narrator/f890cfaeab12281e.text: The chanting stops. In the silence, the heap of refuse takes a long, wet breath.

narrator/f8a032963dbf3da8.text: A bed of furs, a chessboard, and a mirror with its face turned to the wall.

narrator/f8d3ba69bab0ed3a.text: The board is set for a game already in progress, and every piece on it, both sides, is black. He plays both, quickly and brilliantly, and always lets the same side win.

narrator/f90c6f3b5638753a.text: Candle wax, scorch marks and a smell like hot tin. Whatever they worship here, it isn't telling you where it keeps its money.

narrator/f916ae05670af23e.text: A square of trodden snow round a stone well, with a frozen trough and a few women filling buckets who stop talking when they see you, and start again, much more quietly, about you.

narrator/f91da359358e331a.text: A bookcase like the others, except that the floor before it is swept in a neat quarter circle, and one book has no dust on its spine.

narrator/f92615375b0c7959.text: Smoky crystal, cold as a winter window. Whatever it is, it doesn't want to be understood.

narrator/f92768351005511d.text: When you look again, the chair by the fire is empty. Nobody saw him go. Above the mantel the painted woman looks down at the ash.

narrator/f95b3032dabab2f5.text: The chanting has stopped. The silence it left behind is worse.

narrator/f95ef1a71111fb8c.text: The old surgery, scrubbed white. Instruments laid out in rows of shining patience. At the far end, on a long table under a sheet, someone lies very still.

narrator/f963a085f8f73799.text: Under the step of Arrigal's wagon, a drawer that only opens if you lift it first. Inside, a black dagger in an oiled sheath, and the sheath smells of something bitter.

narrator/f979986e711f65cf.text: Silt, cold stones, a child's lost button. Nothing the pool wants to give you, today. Your feet are warm all the way back to the shrine, which is gift enough.

narrator/f9bcf84c60b79b08.text: A squat log house with one barred window and a heavy door. A tin cup hangs by the window on a string, for passers-by to give the prisoners water if they're feeling disloyal.

narrator/f9c29cf716216502.text: He gets up, carefully, and walks away along the track without looking at the hill once.

narrator/f9c4c04a03666210.text: One board at the back of the shrine is newer than the rest. Under it, wrapped in oilcloth, a plain iron ring. Holding it, your thoughts feel like your own again.

narrator/f9e80da745c1853b.text: A rack of old mail shirts, oiled and hung. Oiled recently. By whom, you'd rather not think.

offalia_wormwiggle/20e7da63ef42be20.text: I looked all along the road and Mother wasn't there. Mother's cross with me. I can feel it from here.

offalia_wormwiggle/276cf3e7588a9987.text: I'm telling Mother you told a fib. Mother likes to know who fibs. She writes them in her book.

offalia_wormwiggle/36c95ac15a32725c.text: From the big stone, silly. You put things in the top and turn it, and it comes out the bottom soft as soft. Mother says you mustn't waste anything. Not the marrow. Not the teeth.

offalia_wormwiggle/3b09625d1e9fdbac.text: I'm not allowed to touch them. Not even the small one. Not yet.

offalia_wormwiggle/3b13dd900fd59654.text: Nobody tells me to step away from Mother's oven. Nobody. Only Mother.

offalia_wormwiggle/3de04b030ffc9e32.text: Dream pastries! Two hundred a week. Mother does the honey, Bella does the wrapping because she's got nice hands, and I do the flour. I'm best at the flour.

offalia_wormwiggle/3e597efff4555787.text: Mother's gone. I went home and the oven was cold. Nobody tells me what to do now. I've eaten all the hedges.

offalia_wormwiggle/490253deeabb8edd.text: No, you're just the right size for one. Mother would say so. Mother says so about everybody.

offalia_wormwiggle/78be41e75b1dc871.text: Back again! Did you want a pastry? They're still warm. They're always still warm.

offalia_wormwiggle/791f041096a114f2.text: You read Mother's book? Nobody reads Mother's book. Did you get flour on it? Please say you didn't get flour on it.

offalia_wormwiggle/872be9fcd4105758.text: The little ones? They're Mother's. Paid for and everything. They're upstairs, keeping. Mother says you don't touch what's keeping.

offalia_wormwiggle/9a8e80cf53e62366.text: Silly. Mother's upstairs. I can hear her rocking. Can't you hear her rocking?

offalia_wormwiggle/c41c7d59bdb854b5.text: Ooh, visitors! Are you deliveries? Mother never said there'd be deliveries. You're ever so big for deliveries.

offalia_wormwiggle/d82ca6a4f0c7b528.text: Really? She's not cross? Oh, thank you, thank you. I'll go straight home. I'll only stop at the good hedges.

offalia_wormwiggle/db480fed6086ba29.text: On the road? Mother never goes down to the road on a baking day! Is she cross? She sounds cross when she calls like that.

offalia_wormwiggle/f1c84ab0f03c0593.text: Everybody! The village. The farms. Folk on the Vallaki road. Mother writes them in her book with what they owe. Nobody can pay, after a while. That's the best part. That's when Mother goes visiting.

offalia_wormwiggle/f6efbd21c44c6106.text: You're the ones. You're the ones from the mill.

order_knight/033e22728e7133ad.text: We march when you march. Tell Godfrey his grey mare is ready.

order_knight/162ff0e6edbe59ad.text: Halt. This is the Order's road. State your business.

order_knight/20a0d62a0cf138db.text: The Order marches when you march. Until then we walk the roads. Go safely.

order_knight/42c4b4dc0d1e7437.text: The Order of the Silver Dragon. We keep the watch. Ask at the house.

order_knight/527eaa5478f78c97.text: He lives. We watch. Pass, oath-sworn.

order_knight/7c2422cea9d07664.text: One of his. It came down the road toward Vallaki carrying a message. It does not carry messages now.

order_knight/a0f966021f61271b.text: I had one. It was a good one.

order_knight/c3e2f872270d308f.text: Then go carefully. The commander does not care for guests. Sir Godfrey does. Ask for Sir Godfrey.

order_knight/c662a73180b691cc.text: The commander will wish to speak with you. He will not like what you say.

order_knight/fa328a6e48ee85ee.text: The old woman. She passed this way once, before these trees were tall. She asked us the time. We did not know it.

parriwimple/039c355d0915c72a.text: Hello. Uncle says to say welcome. Welcome.

parriwimple/092d288d50b4568c.text: I can carry that. I'll bring the shovel too, and dig. Uncle won't mind. Uncle will mind. I'll go anyway.

parriwimple/0ae41dd556cb9410.text: Me? In the cards? Nobody ever saw me in anything before.

parriwimple/183cb08da1ec5b5a.text: I dug it deep. Six feet. I measured with my arm, twice. Then I made it a little deeper, for the wolves.

parriwimple/244111178045b2fc.text: Uncle says my time costs money. Five gold an hour. You'd have to ask Uncle. He likes being asked.

parriwimple/3bee90f2e6a2402d.text: Days. Since the burgomaster died. Three. Nobody else counted, I think. Somebody should.

parriwimple/44f34ce2259222a6.text: The grave's ready. I put the dirt in a neat pile, so it goes back in neat. Uncle says neat is respect.

parriwimple/660e9fe6ad7ca559.text: Again. No. Don't, Uncle will charge you for the flour. But that was the best thing I ever saw. I'll remember you.

parriwimple/6eba26bc8bb3fdbc.text: I didn't like it. I carried the sacks fast.

parriwimple/86cca363b3e14c10.text: Hello again. I remembered you. I don't remember everybody.

parriwimple/b3d952e9db13ebbd.text: The pie lady. Uncle won't let me eat them; he says they cost money. She lives in the old windmill on the Vallaki road. I carried sacks there once. It smelled like bread. And like not bread.

parriwimple/c06b02821b9fe4ce.text: Thank you? I think? Uncle says people say nice things when they want a discount. There's no discount.

parriwimple/d7f113883d7f57b0.text: Nobody says that. Uncle says I'm a good lifter. That's nearly the same. Thank you. I'll remember you.

parriwimple/e4d1e28403f32437.text: Uncle says I'm not to leave the shop. Uncle says a lot. I can carry your packs. I can carry you, if you fall down. I'll count the days we're gone so he knows.

pastry_customer_man/0dae0db32326b89b.text: You're waiting too? No? Then step aside. They open when they open. The old woman knows I'm here. She always knows.

pastry_customer_man/1917a8c01e7c632c.text: One bite and I'm home, and my wife is alive, and the sun is out. Don't look at me like that. You'd come too.

pastry_customer_woman/be985d3814f61184.text: Just one for my husband. He can't sleep without them any more. Maybe two. Maybe I'll try one. Only to know what he sees.

patrina_velikovna/235ec244fd8e9dc9.text: I came up here to learn what the lord of the valley knew. Then I went down to his castle to learn the rest.

patrina_velikovna/262a4952877ba709.text: Go home, little brother. Don't bring me back. Don't make bargains. Be brave somewhere I can't see you; it will annoy me less.

patrina_velikovna/2e4ab0d3d3927b1d.text: ...There. That wasn't so hard. Three centuries, and it took you one breath.

patrina_velikovna/2ec5d645bb956a74.text: A student. I was the cleverest of my people, which was not difficult, and the only curious one, which was.

patrina_velikovna/37f2d353c06448db.text: You again. Have you come to stare, or have you finally brought me something worth reading?

patrina_velikovna/3842652def920bc1.text: Then let him be afraid a little longer. Get out of my library.

patrina_velikovna/490bd7d988c1bd5f.text: Rest. Everyone always wants me to rest. ...Perhaps I'm tired. Perhaps I've been tired for a long time.

patrina_velikovna/8a97bc7db45dceca.text: No. I've done my living. If Kasimir wants to do something for me, he can stop being sorry and start being brave. He'll know what I mean.

patrina_velikovna/8fc4e25ca41792b4.text: Living people. In my library. Do you know how long it's been since anyone in this valley had the nerve to climb up here and read?

patrina_velikovna/930cfcdadcb5a1de.text: The same page I was reading when I left. It's about him: how a prince became a lord forever. I thought if I understood it, he would see me as an equal.

patrina_velikovna/96a2897f2a623914.text: Of course. Stones, or steel. It's always one or the other with people like you.

patrina_velikovna/97a080cd5e4fa458.text: Bring me back. To what? To a valley that stoned me, a brother who watched, and a lord who has had four centuries to find someone cleverer?

patrina_velikovna/9d9968470de5c8b2.text: My people threw stones at me until I stopped moving. So I came back here. It's the only place I was ever free.

patrina_velikovna/9d9e7f8a9931259c.text: Then say it properly. Not to them. To me.

patrina_velikovna/b41a2e5df101027a.text: Your gods don't climb this high. Mine never did either. Don't preach at me in my own library.

patrina_velikovna/b71a9de1db00df29.text: ...Kasimir. You climbed a mountain. You. I'd have bet my bones against it, if I still had the use of them.

patrina_velikovna/c201c3c30a7aec91.text: He did, for a while. That's the trouble with being clever. Someone always finds a use for it.

patrina_velikovna/c2be372e39961435.text: Don't you dare. Don't you dare buy me back from a thing in a box, like a coat out of pawn.

patrina_velikovna/d8c4867d6e346934.text: Tell him I'm done waiting. Tell him the stones didn't hurt as much as the quiet afterward. He'll understand that. He was always very good at quiet.

patrina_velikovna/db39a3b0dc63a10f.text: ...Afraid. Yes. He always was. And he admits it now? That's new. That's very nearly brave.

patrina_velikovna/dceee58875d1fa3f.text: Kasimir. You've met Kasimir. Is he still mending nets by a Vistani fire and calling it penance?

patrina_velikovna/ddc662d44e0b15ce.text: Sorry. He's sorry. Three hundred years, and he sends strangers up a mountain to say it for him.

patrina_velikovna/de8dcd601de717a4.text: He stood at the back. Did he tell you? Everyone was throwing, and my brother stood at the back with empty hands, and watched.

phantom_warden/275fdea9032ac35a.text: None pass to the dragon's rest but the Order. Name your oath, or turn back.

phantom_warden/3cc82a5f8e69eca5.text: Godfrey. He was always letting strays in. Pass.

phantom_warden/4a200cf55cb8d764.text: The old form. Nobody has used the old form since... Pass.

phantom_warden/8055d46ae3684b28.text: Those are the words. Pass, brothers.

phantom_warden/a03d40932dbcd3a5.text: To tend it. ...Nobody has tended it since the squires died. Pass, and mind your feet by the bier.

phantom_warden/b8e696bbb505ae73.text: I opened the gate once. I'll not open this one.

phantom_warden/edbe75b624b08588.text: Not the words. I opened a gate once, to a voice that sounded right. I'll not do it twice.

pidlwick_ii/006a5dab5a3d4d0a.text: A PRESENT. I KEPT IT IN MY HAT FOR A HUNDRED YEARS. (He holds out a fly carved of black wood.) IT GROWS. DON'T TELL ANYONE.

pidlwick_ii/087dc2c436af5660.text: THEY LOVED HIM. NOT ME. SO I HELPED HIM DOWN.

pidlwick_ii/088be08de7db50a0.text: A TOYMAKER. LONG AGO. FOR THE CHILDREN OF THE HOUSE.

pidlwick_ii/169dfe53ac140ab7.text: (He tugs your sleeve and holds up the slate.) WHERE NOW?

pidlwick_ii/17f8d5b5ef47971b.text: HELLO. I AM PIDLWICK. THE SECOND.

pidlwick_ii/1f29129761655059.text: (He points up the stair, bells jingling.) TOP: THE GLASS HEART. HE GOES THERE WHEN HE IS HURT.

pidlwick_ii/220c6e41726e41e8.text: (He clutches his cap with both hands and backs up a step.) NO.

pidlwick_ii/2c7e8d95ee833ce4.text: (A deep bow, then the slate.) AGAIN? LATER?

pidlwick_ii/3a684c29eb092b59.text: (He spins on one toe.) THANK YOU. THANK YOU. THANK YOU.

pidlwick_ii/425c2ddcbe90f9fb.text: (He writes for a long time, and holds the slate up with both hands.) I WILL NOT PUSH. I WILL WALK BEHIND. ALWAYS BEHIND. PROMISE.

pidlwick_ii/46594210a38c161f.text: (He looks round the shop: the toys, the monkey, the two kettles, the tall sad man.) CAN I STAY?

pidlwick_ii/46b394869f19110e.text: (Last of all he points at the well, and then quickly away from it.) DO NOT LEAN.

pidlwick_ii/4df08695392c6f00.text: (He points across, toward the tower rooms.) SAD MAN IN THE LOCKED ROOM. STAIR BEHIND HIS CUPBOARD. UP TO THE BIRDS.

pidlwick_ii/4ea0a2cf738c8427.text: SHE HOLDS DOORS FOR HIM. ALL NIGHT. SHE HAS NO NAME ON HER BOX. (He taps the slate, very serious.) EVERYBODY HAS A NAME ON THEIR BOX. EVEN THE HORSE.

pidlwick_ii/53cac7ab463ec08b.text: (He wipes the slate and writes again.) HE NEVER ASKED ABOUT MY KNEES. NOT ONCE. I LET HIM LOOK ANYWAY.

pidlwick_ii/5a183659f60ca4d2.text: CAN I COME WITH YOU? I KNOW ALL THE STAIRS.

pidlwick_ii/5f601ac017cd8e4e.text: TICKING. MOSTLY. (He winds himself a little with a bent nail.)

pidlwick_ii/60e6de2a6852dff6.text: (He fetches a very small bag from behind a pillar, already packed.) READY. FOR A HUNDRED YEARS.

pidlwick_ii/68f6314fd2b22529.text: (He salutes with the wrong hand.) YES SIR.

pidlwick_ii/6c190a239c3ecf8d.text: I WIND MYSELF WITH A NAIL. IT IS NOT THE SAME.

pidlwick_ii/82e1dd9c7bfa4501.text: (He trots off toward the high tower.) ON THE STAIR. DO NOT FORGET ME.

pidlwick_ii/8ba8540d3e7af4d2.text: (He wipes the slate with his sleeve and writes again, quickly.) PLAY?

pidlwick_ii/8f0c3693d354e098.text: I WAS GOING TO. I DIDN'T. THAT IS NEW.

pidlwick_ii/9090a99fb6377007.text: THE BIRDS DO NOT LIKE ME. I TAKE THEIR SHINY THINGS. THEY TAKE MINE.

pidlwick_ii/98a20a509c304f8f.text: (He writes, and underlines it twice.) AFTER THE CASTLE. THE CARDS SAY I'M NEEDED. THEN I COME BACK.

pidlwick_ii/a83c757dc71a42a9.text: (He taps the slate, where it already says so.) BLINSKY. VALLAKI. I REMEMBER.

pidlwick_ii/b1763cc5f6d8512c.text: (He writes, rubs it out, writes again.) A LADY IN THE CELLARS. THE BIG CELLARS, WITH THE DEAD.

pidlwick_ii/c749c89f1bf26172.text: THE HEART IS QUIET. THE HOUSE IS LISTENING FOR IT. (He shivers, bells and all.)

pidlwick_ii/d41fbb862c7f0b1b.text: (He nods. He is used to it.) SAFE. YES.

pidlwick_ii/df60685752b7c6f9.text: (He comes out from behind you, step by careful step, and bows, very low.) HELLO. I AM PIDLWICK. THE SECOND.

pidlwick_ii/df7e321fca450550.text: SORRY. VERY SORRY. FOR A VERY LONG TIME.

pidlwick_ii/e2c127baacd58bbb.text: (He drops two of his three balls to wave at you with both hands, and doesn't mind at all.) HELLO. I WORK HERE NOW.

pidlwick_ii/e8784207a8e726b1.text: (He writes small, and shows only you.) TOYMAKER. NO. THEY OPEN YOU UP. TO SEE.

pidlwick_ii/e99e0cfb182870e1.text: (He wipes the slate.) OK. BUT HE ASKS ABOUT MY KNEES, I LEAVE.

pidlwick_ii/f0ba3ca7d1d04833.text: (He backs up a step and holds his cap on with both hands.) NO. TOYMAKERS OPEN YOU UP. TO SEE.

pidlwick_ii/ffe85d761306a855.text: KEY. THE BIRDS TOOK IT. UP UNDER THE ROOF.

pool_grave_keeper/933dafd1fee527ad.text: Stone suns, every one, so they face the morning. The snow pushes them crooked. I push them back. Between us we've kept it up for thirty years.

pool_grave_keeper/99718dfda231b070.text: The Krezkov boy, at peace in the water at last. I'll keep his stone straighter than all the rest. Don't tell the others.

pool_mourner/b67838152353c70e.text: Every morning I tell him the news. The goats, the weather, who's fallen out with whom. The water never freezes, not even in the deep of winter. That's how I know he hears.

rahadin/03f9451a0bdddf90.text: Everyone I have killed in his service. They do not leave me. It is the price of a long career, and I pay it.

rahadin/1a7992ed12daa83d.text: There are three rules. Go where you like. Take nothing that is not offered. Do not touch the girl.

rahadin/1a7dbb4d581dc3a4.text: I was. I am Rahadin. I keep this house.

rahadin/1cf507d3d96917ab.text: Guests do not usually come this far along the corridor. Those who do, I remember.

rahadin/212efa5e9490340c.text: As you wish. He will want to hear how it went.

rahadin/24413991626dddb8.text: I do not ask their ages.

rahadin/259e04d531a3327e.text: The master will be amused. She will come back on her own; they generally do. Mind the stairs.

rahadin/26145a41f08e8b1b.text: They are mine. I have collected them for a long time. You need not listen.

rahadin/3873274664ab3eee.text: In the house. He is always in the house, even when he is not. He receives when he chooses.

rahadin/4754171eb5d6b9d4.text: You came up the grand stair, so you are the master's guests. I am Rahadin. I keep this house.

rahadin/48cdac7153862eba.text: She rang for him an hour ago and told him what you said. He asked me to see her safely back upstairs. I always do what he asks.

rahadin/5a37e9e5e836a614.text: A guest of the master, in the rooms above. She is content. Leave her so.

rahadin/5ff57dccc0f57c2a.text: Then I will not keep you. Supper is at dusk, if the master remembers to serve it.

rahadin/603a5eaacb79d072.text: I keep accounts. Lipsiege keeps the master's money. I keep the rest.

rahadin/777c18ff4785429a.text: He wants to be amused. Amuse him, and you will live longer than most.

rahadin/a3975eaec99406d4.text: The youngest son ran. I let him. It was an oversight. I have not made many.

rahadin/a8dbbf58ad4f6f77.text: You are still here. Good. The master dislikes guests who leave early.

rahadin/b3cf2a013ceadd04.text: If an old woman has turned cards for you, you know more than I am permitted to say. Her cards are seldom wrong. It annoys him.

rahadin/c235ba415bf76a0a.text: The Velikovs. The mother, I think. She asked me to spare the children. I explained that there were no children, only the master's tenants, and that tenants who stone the master's guest are no longer tenants.

rahadin/d7a115f7f2a5e3a3.text: Since before this valley had his name. I served the man; I serve what he became. The house needs keeping either way.

rahadin/e225f1648d2ea2a9.text: You found my room before you found me. Most guests manage it the other way round. I am Rahadin. I keep this house.

rahadin/ebade3cbe94608a7.text: The master thanks you for returning what is his.

rahadin/f520d1942c11b622.text: I know the face. Everyone in this house knows the face. Her rooms have been ready for a very long time.

rahadin/f6440bb429cf9df8.text: I am Rahadin. I keep this house, and I keep its guests.

rahadin/fd9110d9094e2a6a.text: The girl is the master's guest. She stays.

ratatoille/00b08db7a0467323.text: Think first. Be kind second. Fireball third. In that order, always. Nobody listens to the order.

ratatoille/017e18a12c2d8953.text: I cooked for the Martikovs because they let me. I used to cook so that people would sit with me. This one I cooked because you're mine. That's different. I didn't know it was different.

ratatoille/022127cd12399fc3.text: That is, technically, correct. Split a coven and its magic curdles, like a sauce pulled off the heat too soon.

ratatoille/0377c6a91d71da63.text: No. It's what fear does when it's been in love too long.

ratatoille/03fd7a2d6bf3d6b7.text: It had a sword in its nest. Somebody marched up here armed to the teeth and became furniture. Bird furniture.

ratatoille/05b264cfc0825a75.text: That sample. Underworked crust, far too sweet, and one bite brought dreams all night. I want the recipe.

ratatoille/0605a3fc2b7fa04b.text: Just her. Something small. Bread, and the little honey cakes from home, and nobody else allowed to taste them. ...That's a terribly forward thing to do with honey cakes.

ratatoille/062744b993b2b4ae.text: My master died before my last lesson. I asked him what it was and he said it was in a letter I'm not allowed to read. I make jokes all day so nobody notices I'm not finished.

ratatoille/0682ede93af56339.text: The tree's in it. A little. Good soil and time will draw it out, I think. Or fire.

ratatoille/0811120694de8e5d.text: The wizard on the mountain played dragonchess against nobody for a year. The greatest wizard of the age, maybe, and nobody sat with him either. I've been thinking about that.

ratatoille/0a541acc7ad9771b.text: You'll want notes. I take very good notes.

ratatoille/0acb13c75fec662a.text: The hand in Lady Wachter's letter matches the one under the Durst house. Same loops, same patience. He writes to everybody.

ratatoille/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

ratatoille/0d31573aa2d994d2.text: That gem. The winery at the crossroads lost three like it. Their vines are dying.

ratatoille/0e39e939933c2bec.text: And the devil himself offered me a tower, and I told him I already had a table. I meant this one. I meant you.

ratatoille/0ef9d1ab4548905f.text: A primary source. The devil kept a diary. Of course he did.

ratatoille/1034006c69a4de03.text: Very well. I'll say something. I'll prepare remarks. Several drafts.

ratatoille/a4f56392491c1b25.text: They swung first. I'm almost certain. I was mid-incantation at the time.

ratatoille/a5b7801f46f88057.text: It's silent. Like the p in... no, don't, that'll make it worse.

ratatoille/a61f9517449df3a9.text: Give it here. It's like a recipe in a bad cookbook: all the important bits are in the method. Here. The way out. "A signature of the lord of the land of mists, freely given, in his own hand."

ratatoille/a6659245660c0f30.text: We've opened it going up. Whether anything comes down is, technically, a separate question.

ratatoille/a9b84e8456d01a2e.text: That's... that's actually the highest compliment a cook can receive. Use your hands. Use both hands.

ratatoille/aa3717c675756663.text: I can't read. Not proper. My name, and "ale", and "danger". Every letter we've had, I've said my eyes were tired and given it to someone else. My eyes are fine. I'm just slow.

ratatoille/ac4a8dad7f8559a1.text: A feud, then. The house hunted someone's wolves, and now someone's wolves hunt the house's guests.

ratatoille/acb49f71c5682533.text: A silver dragon, mounted between a bear and a stag like game. It's in the poorest possible taste.

ratatoille/b187dd0a2804a8f0.text: Or maybe they've read the same history of this valley I have.

ratatoille/b24a7924ebeb5748.text: I have heard songs about the dusk elves. None of them end like that.

ratatoille/b27beff1fb8432b7.text: May I see it? This is a very good ladle. Copper-bottomed. Somebody loved this ladle.

ratatoille/b2eff5f66061c3c5.text: Next time I sleep with the skillet. I want to see his face when I take him seriously.

ratatoille/b31bf51e9f5651f1.text: Urwin Martikov said those very words at the Blue Water Inn. With the same face. I notice these things. Diviner.

ratatoille/b3558d59b428987b.text: A vampire, then. The literature is unanimous on the name, if on very little else.

ratatoille/b45e7218942051a0.text: Yes. Of course. Eat. That's what it's for. It's only food.

ratatoille/b55b5056c02593f1.text: The portcullis is iron a hand thick, and it's warded. Nobody's lifting that from out here. The winch will be inside the tower.

ratatoille/b690bff2673bd2e3.text: A golem of earth with a magic stone for a heart. Ambitious. Badly sourced, but ambitious.

ratatoille/b6f28e9a90d06d89.text: Of course. Stirring. I'm very good at stirring and keeping quiet. I'd hoped to stop.

ratatoille/b7ddce138fe430b1.text: Liriel. She's a priestess. She's lovely and she talks to a god, and I'm a cook who learned fire so people would sit with him. What would she want with a cook?

ratatoille/b7fb9700c695354f.text: Refused. By "him", I take it. Nobody in this house will say his name.

ratatoille/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.

ratatoille/b904a217de8ad049.text: I'm going to go and stand behind that tree for a moment.

ratatoille/ba53728d9d520820.text: You can look. It's all right. Everyone's going to find out eventually.

ratatoille/ba5a6814854437dd.text: No. No, of course. I'd thought so. It's a very old order. Very particular.

ratatoille/bf9ef19d959a3b41.text: "Given." As if it were a pinch of salt. Mon dieu.

ratatoille/c151a3c27db1c997.text: That is not the point. You have entirely missed the... What would you like tonight?

ratatoille/c1acab3f495ba7d4.text: Clever girl. Very clever. When you are out, I will cook you anything you like. Anything.

ratatoille/c28694785f727534.text: I need a consultation. In confidence. I've tried divination. Divination says "obviously", which is very unhelpful, and also rude.

ratatoille/c433091e2bb955c1.text: It was... it was only bread.

ratatoille/c4623dff95a709ec.text: Her spread is crude, her technique unorthodox, and she is right. I can feel it. I hate it.

ratatoille/c4679484b2e80cb3.text: Twice, warden. Both times you admired my spellbook. Quite rightly.

ratatoille/c5ae8336905f9547.text: It isn't gone. It's in him, and still tied to its sarcophagus, and he's tied to the land. It's all one knot.

ratatoille/c6263baf8234cf21.text: I can foresee breakfast. Breakfast I will foresee, and it will be excellent, and you will all eat it. Sit.

ratatoille/c6c06c7873ad6b49.text: Fire from frost. That isn't how fire works.

ratatoille/c79d3c3f7219f9a0.text: At the academy I sat alone at meals for nine years. Nine. Do you know how long that is for an elf? It isn't long. It felt long.

ratatoille/c7b5e7e0cffea52b.text: I crossed the mists. I crossed the mists for a farm.

ratatoille/c7f6ffd3541b1313.text: I learned magic so people would sit with me. Then I found people who would. And now I look at the table and I don't know whether I want to sit at it.

ratatoille/cbc298482c170edc.text: It was a very well-informed yawn. Mon dieu. I yawned at Van Richten.

ratatoille/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

ratatoille/cca4661b36988332.text: He regenerates. Fire or radiance stops it, or so every treatise insists.

ratatoille/ce83f2849ba301e6.text: It's him. It's the Wizard of Wines. And he looks exactly like the woodcut in my third-year textbook of the greatest wizard alive, which is impossible, because that wizard would never talk to a rock.

ratatoille/cef29fc3769dbe53.text: The binding is cut. Every wound it was carrying for him, he carries himself now.

ratatoille/cf9a42b24d586cb7.text: He drew the castle from three sides, then walked up to read in its library. I admire him. I'd prefer not to be him.

ratatoille/d08d835564c9b8d4.text: Low on the wall. Right. Is that a riddle? I'm bad at riddles.

ratatoille/d14e77066a7bf864.text: Master Mordenkainen. Archmage. Sir. I am Ratatoille, Diviner of the... I'm Ratatoille. I've read everything you ever wrote, including the footnotes, including the footnote about the footnotes. I crossed the mists to become your apprentice.

ratatoille/d158beff82b2d560.text: ...Please don't tell the academy. Or do. No. Don't.

ratatoille/d16f262246e9dc11.text: Thistle. Think what the flour is ground from.

ratatoille/d1cb8246c46c5102.text: Yes. I know. That's the part I can't get past either.

ratatoille/d231b2f9562b61ee.text: That's because they haven't tasted it yet. Here. Taste this. No, wait. Now. Now taste it.

ratatoille/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

ratatoille/d2ceaa2d7bfe3d79.text: A gaoler, then, not a doorman. That is considerably worse.

ratatoille/d301b36df4c58e1f.text: Through! Everyone through! I shall go last. No, second to last. Go, go!

ratatoille/d39a76bddee278ee.text: Rule one: you do not draw anything on any floor without asking me first.

ratatoille/d44073018ef403d3.text: A windmill. A windmill means flour, and flour means bread. Not that I would... I am a wizard. Purely academic.

ratatoille/d4f022228ffe595e.text: The gears have stopped. Whatever that fire was driving, it isn't now.

ratatoille/d5a8be4c9aea0a41.text: The next day, people sat with me. A whole table of them. Asking about fire.

ratatoille/d672d216bb82270c.text: Somewhere in this fog is the Wizard of Wines. A master of the arcane and the table. He's going to be so impressed with me.

ratatoille/d737c61233bd7a34.text: Somebody warded this, and not for show. Look at the frost around it. It's in a perfect ring.

ratatoille/d8f2ca7da834acfb.text: We hurt the one creature in this valley that wasn't trying to kill us. Every augury I know calls that a bad sign.

ratatoille/daf9f5204dd53549.text: No, thank you, Your Excellency. I already have a table. They're sitting at it.

ratatoille/dcdd5d94d241c2bf.text: He's clockwork, Thistle. Clockwork doesn't smell.

ratatoille/dd106a9a7b943af9.text: An image, not a person. Whoever made it wanted us moved, not fooled.

ratatoille/dd22ab654557d9bd.text: Tomorrow I'll cook. Something simple. Bread. You can't lie with bread.

ratatoille/dd22c6bcbb9d9146.text: It's my grandmother's. She makes it every feast day, and every feast day she tells me I'm doing the crust wrong. I'm doing it her way tonight. I wanted to see if I could stand it.

ratatoille/e0221d3fa9d74a45.text: For what it's worth, I'd noticed. I didn't say anything. I'm not good at saying things. I'd have made you soup.

ratatoille/e12effcb522e0eb8.text: Thank you. Not that it's a secret. It's just private. There's a difference. One's for hiding, and one's for keeping.

ratatoille/e1f82129f39f7712.text: Not a speck of dust. Not one. I have never been so frightened by good housekeeping.

ratatoille/e30aaa62af6b27d5.text: My grandmother wore a collar like that in her portrait. She said it was embarrassing then, too.

ratatoille/e3c67df2e63d777f.text: Stanimir's story. The bride, and the brother. Mon dieu. He is the brother who died.

ratatoille/eb206c046933fcd4.text: An old trick. Effective, apparently. We're inside.

ratatoille/ed33ccb9facd4c52.text: Three stones that make vines grow where nothing should. Payment for one winter's lodging. That wizard either loved wine more than anyone ever has, or the stones were the cheapest thing in his pockets.

ratatoille/ed5abc1f44dfee9a.text: Technically, something always happens. But I appreciate the optimism. It's very undercooked. I like it anyway.

ratatoille/eee937adf2eb9eaa.text: A recipe. My best one. My grandmother's, actually, with improvements. Many improvements. She'd be furious. It's the bread.

ratatoille/eefc520f6c1d37c8.text: The venison's been hung a day too long and the sauce is hiding it. The bread's good. Who made the bread?

ratatoille/efc52d2c39b6cc8a.text: The barkeep. I tried to read him, the way one reads a sauce. There was nothing in the pot.

ratatoille/f04a66a1da393159.text: Godrick. About the reading. Letters are only a recipe for sounds. I could teach you, evenings. I'd be very patient. Probably.

ratatoille/f21db2639a0240ee.text: Non, non, non. Do not take the birds' side. I am having a crisis.

ratatoille/f25e60f26cfb7272.text: Thriving, thank you, Wren of the No Circle Whatsoever.

ratatoille/f2e385aede6e2d8d.text: That's a sword spell. A floating blade of force. It has a name in front of it, the way the great ones do. Mordenkainen's.

ratatoille/f3bec25674868bf1.text: I'll have you know I only want to study it. Professionally.

ratatoille/f5e4c6de7a85b0b3.text: They do not know us. They will never know anyone. That is... non. That is not right.

ratatoille/f763707f0cdbe87e.text: She does, doesn't she. Nobody ever did. Not even Maman. She'd say "eat it before it goes cold", which isn't the same.

ratatoille/f7ba33eb36dfde21.text: Revenants, almost certainly. They don't rest until their vengeance is done. One wonders on whom.

ratatoille/f7dab31eb4b08a08.text: Vampire spawn rest by day in the earth they were buried in, or near enough. Inert. Defenceless, the treatises say.

ratatoille/f8392d984006d0b8.text: Technically, I am a diviner. I foresee breakfast. Breakfast implies a morning. Voilà.

ratatoille/f9bbdd8c015ddc92.text: I'd like it noted that I've known a real knight since before he was one.

ratatoille/fccafa6a481ec30e.text: Yes, Master. Sir. Mordenkainen. Thank you.

ratatoille/fcd02d35d9fc5c93.text: That crust had bone in it. I know flour, and that was not flour. And her windmill sits on the Vallaki road.

ratatoille/fe49d15718175a52.text: Ratatoille. Cook. And wizard. In that order.

ratatoille/ffed7f898f994de7.text: I was sixteen once. Nobody sat with me either. Nowhere is not better, I promise you.

rictavio/06a35e1fc8575f1f.text: It's the only one I've ever seen work. Briefly.

rictavio/0905d1808a1eb359.text: The same as you, I expect, only for longer. I came to see whether the lord of this valley can be killed. I'm still deciding. I am also, I'm afraid, still deciding whether I care to survive the answer.

rictavio/090d2c6471f2f7e8.text: I told you once what I think of people who help this valley choose its masters. Words are cheap here. What have you done since?

rictavio/0c0cf141bffc4295.text: Take what will keep you alive, and pay what you can. I have outlived most of the people I armed. I'd like to outlive fewer.

rictavio/132578667bee3dfe.text: Ezmerelda. You went through the ward.

rictavio/1470fc1d27cecffe.text: Cards! Gypsy nonsense! Fortune-telling for the gullible!

rictavio/1724568071ef5a8c.text: Eva's cards again. And I hear five children walked down out of the wolves' hills because of you. That counts for something. It counts for a great deal.

rictavio/18c52cdfbd6fb32e.text: Someone has been in my wagon. No, don't deny it; I leave a hair across the lock. You're alive, so you didn't open the cage. Good. That was the most important thing.

rictavio/1a7edab3ec2e330c.text: Not that name. Not here. Rudolph van Richten made a great many enemies, and some of them have extremely long lives. Rictavio has none. I would like to keep it that way.

rictavio/1c811af458c80dc4.text: And if you can't, bar the church and stand in it. Holy water. Fire. Don't let them get behind you.

rictavio/209aeacce5720468.text: You're hunting a good night's sleep, I expect. So am I. Goodnight!

rictavio/25749d0b0678189a.text: That town chose its master, and I watched who helped it choose. I came home to think about whether anything in this valley is worth the trouble. I've been thinking for a week. It's gone very badly.

rictavio/262619061eaeec97.text: And you've read my journal, so there's no use in feathers.

rictavio/262852986a2603e9.text: ...Mirescu. Yes. He sat on the steps of my wagon and asked me, very politely, whether I believed a certain lord had written his own history. I asked who wanted to know. He said, "Everyone who's read the index."

rictavio/282b1f6c27de0792.text: You. How did you... Khazan. Of course. She found the name, and you walked in on it. I taught her to find things. I should have taught her to stop.

rictavio/30d8da1fbbdd500f.text: Very well. I'm too old to hunt alone, and you are much too young to be doing it at all. I'll come.

rictavio/3405d4e110a7ef94.text: Very well. I am too old to keep hunting alone, and you are much too young to be doing it at all. I'll come. The wagon stays; the beast in it is the only creature in Barovia I trust to guard my notes.

rictavio/3a1ced185966179b.text: Keep your voice down and your back to the wall. What do you need?

rictavio/3d168f305d47470b.text: I know. I can hear her. Everyone within a mile can hear her.

rictavio/467601bb062c58f9.text: Everywhere, and recently. I go where the audiences are. Here, there are no audiences, so I suppose I've come to rest.

rictavio/46d0bbe2f815ee20.text: Then come back when you have. I'll be here. I'm not going anywhere quickly these days.

rictavio/518f9a32f1fe99a8.text: And don't tell me what Eva's cards say. I know what they say. I won't stand beside people who handed a town to him, whatever the cards want.

rictavio/5742e59de32f4d11.text: Then he means to send his spawn for the church, and whoever is sheltering in it. They'll be close by, somewhere dark, somewhere nobody looks. Spawn sleep by day like anyone who works nights. Find their beds while the sun is up, and you choose the fight.

rictavio/59542027a13df3cf.text: It's a costume. It's a very good costume.

rictavio/5ad08290d8b1fc54.text: My audience returns! Twice in one week. In Barovia that's practically a following.

rictavio/60146b3c8d1d2613.text: Eva's cards again. And the ravens tell me two children came home from a hags' mill on the Vallaki road, because of you. Hags don't give anything back. That counts.

rictavio/634183adca5337c1.text: Both of them will get people killed. Vargas from fear, Fiona from faith. One of them only wants the town to be quiet. The other wants it quiet for him. I'd want neither in charge of a dog kennel.

rictavio/647e2132f89bfcd3.text: Friends! Strangers! Strange friends! Rictavio, at your service: teller of tales, singer of songs, proprietor of the most marvellous carnival wagon in seven valleys, which none of you may look inside!

rictavio/67c8323142be15b9.text: Have you now. A scholar. How dangerous for you.

rictavio/682ac7919ac1e224.text: The ward upstairs is down too. I'd rather not have to explain how I cooked my own guests.

rictavio/694bdd83070b02a3.text: Take these. I've more than I need, and you, I suspect, have less.

rictavio/76702cfc411af5eb.text: And this. The hat has been a great many people over the years. Let it be one of you for a while; I find I'm tired of being anyone else.

rictavio/78c5e6ef7f127522.text: Ah. My front door. Stand back, please; it's particular about company.

rictavio/834e14eb4f41ca75.text: Farewell, farewell! Tell your friends! Tell your enemies! Tell anyone, really; I'm not particular.

rictavio/85bdf7d3e419d3fd.text: I know that face. Thirty years older and wild as a goat, but I know it. Good God. They told me he was dead.

rictavio/85efc5a375448c06.text: A tale! There was once a hunter who chased a monster across the whole world, and caught it, and killed it. And do you know what he found? That there was always another monster. The end. It goes better with a lute.

rictavio/8639724b13d1db19.text: Eva's cards again. And there's a silver light on the ridge over Argynvostholt, where there's been none for four hundred years. Somebody lit it. That counts for a great deal.

rictavio/869b063e047979ad.text: Stay in the light where you can. And when you can't, stay together.

rictavio/87f684ff6f7259c2.text: A beast! A marvel! A creature that would eat a horse and then complain about the seasoning. I keep it locked away for its protection as much as yours. Mostly yours.

rictavio/8b856f84b424305c.text: Goodbye. I hope you find a better ally than your judgement.

rictavio/8f62deb6f19ebb49.text: She has made me promise never to key a ward to anyone again. I have agreed to nothing. She knows I have agreed to nothing.

rictavio/934ce88767b17b26.text: Clever. Patient. Bored, which is the dangerous part. He plays with people the way a cat plays, and like a cat he gets careless when he's amused. Keep him amused, and wait.

rictavio/95ea5aff4073a43b.text: If he was your friend, I'm sorry. He was the bravest coward I've ever met. Shaking the whole time, and asking his questions anyway.

rictavio/968243c1bd243bf6.text: Thank you. People rarely keep secrets in Barovia. It's not malice; it's that he asks so nicely.

rictavio/986c75af9159c72c.text: Forty years of hunting leaves a man with more weapons than hands. Blessed steel, a mace that unmakes the dead, draughts that keep a body breathing, and prayers I can no longer read without my spectacles. Buy what will keep you alive. I'd rather sell it than bury it with you.

rictavio/a46ff5184f738ba7.text: And you let it go. I understand. I did that once. It found me again eleven years later, and it remembered my kindness very precisely.

rictavio/a9e8b9803955e2fc.text: Still here. You've a talent for being where you shouldn't. I used to.

rictavio/af5e6687fda271c9.text: I'm going home to think: a tower on the little lake under the mountain, west of Zarovich. If you do something worth hearing about, come and tell me there. Bring proof. Not speeches.

rictavio/bb288d78f7331c27.text: Reasons. Old ones. I came home to think. I've been thinking for a week, and it's gone very badly.

rictavio/c1d9e833b4cbcc72.text: I keyed the ward to her because everyone I have ever taught is in the ground, and she is the last. If she can't get in, she can't follow me where I'm going.

rictavio/c330f89b47913b54.text: And you've been in my strongbox upstairs. Keep it. Where you're going, you'll need it more than I will.

rictavio/c5ebffa90d3a51d3.text: A bad bargain, and a pretty speech about it. I've had better speeches from vampires. Much better.

rictavio/ce2709ef2448e303.text: Everyone I have ever taught is in the ground, Ezmerelda. You are the last. I would like you to stay the last.

rictavio/d8846064ac542919.text: Eva. Of course it was Eva. That old woman has been shuffling me about this valley for longer than I care to count.

rictavio/dca72d665817cb97.text: This town has chosen its master, and I watched who helped it choose. I won't sleep another night under a roof that bows to him. I'll be gone by morning, wagon and all.

rictavio/e4e11422151775ac.text: He thanked me, beautifully. Then he asked the way to the mountains, because the index was kept in a temple of amber and he wanted to see the shape of the thing before he read it.

rictavio/e62b6f69eea2ff48.text: Hunting? I hunt applause, and rarely catch it.

rictavio/e8b09842c300913f.text: Eva's cards. I have spent thirty years refusing to be anybody's fortune.

rictavio/ec1e7fd812ba1882.text: ...Words are cheap in this valley. Deeds are what I'll watch. I'll come, and I'll be watching.

rictavio/f3c170910a886053.text: I told him to go home. I told him some books are written to be read, the way some doors are built to be opened, and he should ask himself who was holding the handle.

rictavio/f87e25a2c5cba2b3.text: And you put it down. Good. Every one of them was somebody. That's the part the books don't prepare you for.

rose/0852c0344261550c.text: You'll have to undo the knot. Thorn tied it. It's a bad knot.

rose/0ce2a9a25133f11f.text: Is it over? Is the noise over? Mother said she'd unlock the door when the noise downstairs stopped.

rose/1df65b026d662a0b.text: He was with Nurse. Then he wasn't, and Nurse cried, and then Nurse stopped crying.

rose/1fef71d2be3827ba.text: Mother hid her purse under the bottom stair in the hall, under the loose board. She said it was for emergencies. I think this is one.

rose/21237a1b174144b6.text: We hid in the toy chest when it got cold. Our bones are still there. Our crypts are downstairs, by Grandmother's. Mother showed us.

rose/2ef2fd666170284c.text: It's quiet in here. Thank you. Thorn, say thank you.

rose/3be2f79fa16bb885.text: Outside? We haven't been outside since the leaves were green. Mother won't let us.

rose/49bae72b3a377f8e.text: No, Thorn. I think everyone else is.

rose/526982f796781a4a.text: Please, you have to help us. Something horrible lives in our house, down in the basement.

rose/5c46e3fd14101047.text: Thank you. Thank you. We'll wait here. We're very good at waiting.

rose/68c81a7ca0c7754a.text: Our baby brother. He's down there crying, and we can't go back in. We can't. Please.

rose/6c38e3b84e91d468.text: The tall one just inside the village, by the dead tree, with the iron gate. Mother says it's the finest house in Barovia.

rose/7ec1a8f640b137df.text: They went downstairs with their friends and they didn't come back up.

rose/86d1ecd311e68b58.text: Everyone says that. Come back. Please come back.

rose/a36b0566b30c053d.text: Father made it for my birthday. He made it too well. It even has the stair they use at night. I found it with a hairpin.

rose/a755ddf229a065f9.text: We never saw it. We hear it, at night, through the floor. Like something heavy being dragged.

rose/acad79018e495021.text: We're always here. We're always waiting. Mother said to wait.

rose/bbd2d891e607370a.text: He's frightened. We both are. Please don't leave us.

rose/cc2b62a37fff4826.text: Oh. That's why we're never hungry anymore.

rose/ccda8d892cabb1bf.text: Mother and Father. The people in robes mustn't see us, they said, and we mustn't see them. They'd come back up when it was over.

rose/e8b4608e590e14fc.text: Thorn! Come out of there! ...Fine. Then I'm coming too.

rose/f05ac2cb9de1a4ce.text: Mother doesn't pray to the Morninglord anymore. She says he never answers, and the other one does.

rose/fcc9d4870ef4d655.text: Hold still. It doesn't hurt. Thorn, say sorry first.

rose/fdbae4415f24bdd8.text: Did you find him? Did you find Walter?

ruxandra/1a94fedd7e64c169.text: Then come and take it, children. Sing, all of you. Sing him awake.

ruxandra/371bb9ff9053f1d1.text: Guests. The hill gets so few guests. Mostly it gets offerings.

ruxandra/5926bc68b44d10b0.text: No. I don't think so. Sing, children. Louder.

ruxandra/5a66e6a4de2f1322.text: Kostin told us you'd come. He was ashamed. I told him shame is only fear that has been taught manners.

ruxandra/6183d26477f5b255.text: Cowards. It doesn't matter. He has heart enough for all of us.

ruxandra/631037fbbe90521a.text: Mercy. How like strangers. ...I'll go. The tree will call me back. It always calls us back.

ruxandra/7334cdec8e9cc2e5.text: Older than the castle. It grew from a stake pulled out of something that should have stayed dead, far away and long ago, and the mists carried the seed here, as they carry everything. It drinks. We give it to drink.

ruxandra/74b51618e039dd33.text: The black-eyed boy. Yes. He told his brother to fly, and the brother flew, and the boy laughed at us all the way up the hill. He stopped laughing, in the end. The tree is very thorough.

ruxandra/aba2cf9921f8dd05.text: We heard you in the gully, children. The hill hears everything. It's mostly ears.

ruxandra/b500006fc6512856.text: You broke him. You broke the heart. ...Well. The land will grow another. It always does.

ruxandra/e814434651f6f3b2.text: You've come for the bird-man's stone. It isn't his now. It's the heart of something better. Listen: you can almost hear it beating.

ruxandra/f9fb3eaebef59bec.text: The bird-man's son? He sent his brother away. Ordered him off like a dog. He was proud of it; he told the tree so at the end. The tree didn't care. Trees don't.

sarkhaza/01a1e5761bb42aa5.text: Then come here. I can't come to you. Not far.

sarkhaza/0d27ccfc06a9c6d2.text: Good. Forty years of salted goat and children and the count's jokes.

sarkhaza/13ce3d794fcb5db3.text: And you tried my chain. I felt you on the capstan. Weak little arms. I nearly felt sorry for you.

sarkhaza/1d94467702dfeef7.text: Thank you. Truly. And now, little things, I'm so very hungry.

sarkhaza/248c5be7e0decca0.text: Forty years. On lead. And he knew I'd count it every night.

sarkhaza/309f4a05ef3db01e.text: (She laughs, a long way down in her chest.) Lead. I've slept on this gold for forty years. I know every coin.

sarkhaza/370797f74edbdbe5.text: I smelled a dead dragon's hoard through the mists. A silver, killed by a man, his gold lying unguarded in a valley ripe for the taking. Do you know what that smells like to my kind? A feast laid out for nobody.

sarkhaza/5e3cc97bbeea153e.text: Grave-salt, packed in like mortar. Forty years I've eaten it. Did you think I wouldn't know the taste?

sarkhaza/701c3212148e4b2a.text: Visitors. Not keepers. Keepers come with a carcass and their eyes on the floor. You come with your eyes up. You've killed them, then.

sarkhaza/90bdd21331f7aec0.text: My name is Sarkhaza. Say it properly; you'll only get the one chance.

sarkhaza/a5a30f8b417a66c9.text: Take the pin out of my collar and I'll go up that valley to his castle and burn him out of it like a wasps' nest. You want him dead. So do I. That's an alliance. Pull the pin.

sarkhaza/ac18a11a609fb3c0.text: (Slower, now. Thicker.) That was a keeper's carcass. You salted it. The count's own grave-salt. Clever, clever little...

sarkhaza/bd5b75f9780a0b5b.text: I came through. He was waiting at the foot of this mountain with his hands behind his back, smiling. I don't remember the next part. I woke with this collar on, and iron through my wings, and the silver's gold under me.

sarkhaza/be2f2712d44c6f8c.text: Then there's nothing here worth keeping, and nothing worth lying down for. Come on, little things. Let's do this standing.

sarkhaza/ec7e22c882f9d006.text: You've read their book. I can smell the damp of it on your hands. So you know my name. Say it properly; you'll only get the one chance.

sarkhaza/f5774c19aa276361.text: Back again, little things. I'm still here. I'm always still here.

sergei_von_zarovich/15579638ad306abf.text: I gave it to her on a spring morning, at this water. She wore it the day she fell. My brother took it from the gorge, and he has used it as bait ever since.

sergei_von_zarovich/1e149fdd77586c69.text: Then be someone. That is all I ever wanted for her.

sergei_von_zarovich/211ce24dc51abb0a.text: Not this time. I know. Forgive me. I only ever had the one name for you.

sergei_von_zarovich/3f9b0cf17c7ef6cc.text: Keep it out of my brother's sight, Ireena. He wants it to remind you. Let it remind you of me instead.

sergei_von_zarovich/44b9b4f368f760bb.text: You needn't give it to me. It isn't mine any more. It is yours, or hers, or his, depending on what you do next.

sergei_von_zarovich/7e655b5e835c05f5.text: You kept your promise. So did I. I have waited a very long time.

sergei_von_zarovich/8aec54a73ae81db9.text: I am. I have had practice.

sergei_von_zarovich/904caeff223df67a.text: Thank you, thief. You are the first person in a very long time to steal something back for her.

sergei_von_zarovich/aa9f0ee6912c8b25.text: I know where he is. I have always known where he is.

sergei_von_zarovich/c1e9702b9403d74c.text: There is a pool at the top of the valley where the sun stays in the water. I can say more there. Here I am mostly bones.

sergei_von_zarovich/d172746476e3f7c5.text: Then carry her carefully. My brother will ask for her too, and he will not ask nicely.

sergei_von_zarovich/dbf257dc9a992de7.text: You came the long way round.

sergei_von_zarovich/e68f06756231ab31.text: The water is the only door I have. I cannot come out. You could come in. When you are ready. Not before. It will wait. I will.

sergei_von_zarovich/f08ccd92875ce202.text: No. Not this time. But you came to the water. You always did, in the mornings, before the bells.

silvain_aster/0377c6a91d71da63.text: No. It's what fear does when it's been in love too long.

silvain_aster/0682ede93af56339.text: The tree's in it. A little. Good soil and time will draw it out, I think. Or fire.

silvain_aster/0a541acc7ad9771b.text: You'll want notes. I take very good notes.

silvain_aster/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

silvain_aster/0d31573aa2d994d2.text: That gem. The winery at the crossroads lost three like it. Their vines are dying.

silvain_aster/0ef9d1ab4548905f.text: A primary source. The devil kept a diary. Of course he did.

silvain_aster/12220c0d7ff279e2.text: Cold fire. Technically impossible. I'll want notes. I'll want so many notes.

silvain_aster/1d4de962e0c91f56.text: That's not a storm. That's a reminder. Somebody set it to go off every night, like a bell.

silvain_aster/22374b43ca4ae77c.text: I wasn't going to. I was going to think it very loudly.

silvain_aster/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

silvain_aster/2c12359b655fa918.text: Everyone stand somewhere I can see you. I'm about to be very loud.

silvain_aster/2eea361f24f94d16.text: The boy is genuinely gifted. His circle is the finest piece of work I've seen in this valley, and it is a beautifully drawn door into nothing.

silvain_aster/2fbb9a7ad5bd54cd.text: Fire and radiance stop them knitting! Everything else is just a delay!

silvain_aster/36a380b9c2561ebb.text: A roc. They nest on high crags and take cattle the way an owl takes mice. The Tsolenka Pass is said to have one.

silvain_aster/36a7271ebb2abe37.text: Your binding arcs are lovely. Your destination glyph, however, describes the absence of a place. Very precisely. It's a beautiful description of nowhere.

silvain_aster/3df882d28bd80e9c.text: Everything I am is what I know. You're offering me a sword and asking for the hand.

silvain_aster/4307cef4f07886b9.text: A dragon who founded a knightly order. There's nothing about it in any library I know.

silvain_aster/466aff31017ea180.text: Yours is the one that worries them most.

silvain_aster/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

silvain_aster/4ff954f11491ede2.text: She was a bird. She was a bird a moment ago.

silvain_aster/512ff6ba0e0f2f42.text: The millstone will come through it. Stone always does. Nobody will ever grind anything on it again.

silvain_aster/536ebb066cce409e.text: He wrote this as if he had all the time in the world. I suspect he does.

silvain_aster/548dc45043c7f711.text: That isn't fog. That's a border, and it has opinions.

silvain_aster/5abdd30ccd56a2e4.text: A ward keyed to one person. You'd have to know her very well. Her voice, her stride, her temper. Months of work, out of love.

silvain_aster/5ae4b73d85ed6be4.text: Some birds in old places carry more than seeds. I'd follow it, one day.

silvain_aster/5e9044d861bf4930.text: You make it sound like a strategy.

silvain_aster/60c1a0ab292e942f.text: A wizard who never collects a debt is either very generous or very dead.

silvain_aster/666ef05503014122.text: A door that opens to a dead man's name. Elegant. Old-fashioned. It assumes nobody would ever be rude enough to say it.

silvain_aster/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

silvain_aster/6a5aabdc73c0fe93.text: Your phylactery. You've lost your own phylactery.

silvain_aster/6c32188c3f9ea623.text: A windmill on the Vallaki road, ground bone in the crust, and a smile that doesn't move. I have a hypothesis. I don't like it.

silvain_aster/74489df70b42b905.text: Everyone dies eventually. I assume they're in a hurry.

silvain_aster/77b2ab4eb620f5ef.text: There's an enchantment in it: old, patient, very simple. Grow. Whoever made it wanted nothing else from the world.

silvain_aster/80681d905be16c24.text: It was the living thing. Clever comes second, in this valley.

silvain_aster/82ecb0249114f105.text: There is no literature whatever to support that.

silvain_aster/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

silvain_aster/86209edb3f88a9d2.text: Memories that thin are rarely an accident.

silvain_aster/8a12f3790632191f.text: We killed a thing in the basement. I'd hesitate to call it the thing.

silvain_aster/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

silvain_aster/8d1820dc82b1631b.text: Will you fly with us, or above us?

silvain_aster/8e26cd67b2166068.text: Vampire spawn. Sleeping by day in boxes, like the books say. For once I'd have preferred the books to be wrong.

silvain_aster/91e5df5fb71b0ff8.text: Hedda. For the record, those cold prayers have kept me alive twice. I will take cold.

silvain_aster/a0155bc1b766b82e.text: Strength is strength. The devil didn't climb down from this mountain with good manners either.

silvain_aster/a13667424f7b860e.text: A lich. An actual lich. I have a great many questions, and I'm afraid of every one of them.

silvain_aster/a165b6e8a241410d.text: A flash in the attic window. That was the circle. He stepped into it the day his father fell.

silvain_aster/a3cae3809f75ef71.text: That's a mind. Most of one. I can hear it thinking.

silvain_aster/a6659245660c0f30.text: We've opened it going up. Whether anything comes down is, technically, a separate question.

silvain_aster/b187dd0a2804a8f0.text: Or maybe they've read the same history of this valley I have.

silvain_aster/b24a7924ebeb5748.text: I have heard songs about the dusk elves. None of them end like that.

silvain_aster/b3558d59b428987b.text: A vampire, then. The literature is unanimous on the name, if on very little else.

silvain_aster/b55b5056c02593f1.text: The portcullis is iron a hand thick, and it's warded. Nobody's lifting that from out here. The winch will be inside the tower.

silvain_aster/b690bff2673bd2e3.text: A golem of earth with a magic stone for a heart. Ambitious. Badly sourced, but ambitious.

silvain_aster/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.
