silvain_aster/b8f8be4ecbb20563.text: I won't pretend that isn't tempting. I will pretend it's beneath me, which is different.

silvain_aster/c5ae8336905f9547.text: It isn't gone. It's in him, and still tied to its sarcophagus, and he's tied to the land. It's all one knot.

silvain_aster/c6c06c7873ad6b49.text: Fire from frost. That isn't how fire works.

silvain_aster/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

silvain_aster/cca4661b36988332.text: He regenerates. Fire or radiance stops it, or so every treatise insists.

silvain_aster/d1cb8246c46c5102.text: Yes. I know. That's the part I can't get past either.

silvain_aster/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

silvain_aster/d2ceaa2d7bfe3d79.text: A gaoler, then, not a doorman. That is considerably worse.

silvain_aster/d39a76bddee278ee.text: Rule one: you do not draw anything on any floor without asking me first.

silvain_aster/d3eddbcfb12fd263.text: You said the dead have no shadows to be ashamed of. That's from the monographs. The ones on the walking dead, by the doctor from Mordent. I've read them twice.

silvain_aster/d737c61233bd7a34.text: Somebody warded this, and not for show. Look at the frost around it. It's in a perfect ring.

silvain_aster/dd106a9a7b943af9.text: An image, not a person. Whoever made it wanted us moved, not fooled.

silvain_aster/eb206c046933fcd4.text: An old trick. Effective, apparently. We're inside.

silvain_aster/ed33ccb9facd4c52.text: Three stones that make vines grow where nothing should. Payment for one winter's lodging. That wizard either loved wine more than anyone ever has, or the stones were the cheapest thing in his pockets.

silvain_aster/f2e385aede6e2d8d.text: That's a sword spell. A floating blade of force. It has a name in front of it, the way the great ones do. Mordenkainen's.

silvain_aster/f7ba33eb36dfde21.text: Revenants, almost certainly. They don't rest until their vengeance is done. One wonders on whom.

silvain_aster/f7dab31eb4b08a08.text: Vampire spawn rest by day in the earth they were buried in, or near enough. Inert. Defenceless, the treatises say.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/04587b68a62d27d6.text: Lord Argynvost lit it every night with his own breath. Silver fire, no heat in it. You could see it from every farm in the valley. It meant somebody was awake.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/0c1e15afe1aace24.text: It went out when he died. The commander won't hear it spoken of. If you want the rest, try the chapel. Something there still answers, some nights.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/15d82913cd5b5d0c.text: Then the Order knows your faces too. I've written worse things on that wall than "these were his friends".

sir_godfrey_gwilym/19d67deb1eddda5e.text: I follow the commander. I have since we were boys with wooden swords. And he's not wrong about Strahd. He's never once been wrong about Strahd.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/1ffae6d1c0606a2d.text: Keep it. It has a knight again, and a fellowship. That's all a sword was ever for.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/206b1f58eb5106ec.text: The horses are four hundred years dead, so we'll walk to war. We've walked further for worse reasons. Say the word when you go up to the castle.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/23501f153ff932a6.text: Ask the commander to call the muster. All of us at the table, the way it was. Say your piece to the Order, not to him. I'll stand up when you do. I promise, and I'll remember promising.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/2d5e96189dfa6421.text: Our patrol saw a black carriage at Vallaki's gate, bold as you like, by daylight. So the town bends the knee to him now. We'd have ridden out about that, once.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/2e3d3fc18b50344b.text: One thing, and then I'll stop fussing. Don't cross the courtyard after dark. Our men-at-arms are still fighting the last battle out there, and they don't stop to ask whose side you're on.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/2e610ef49b854b3d.text: Welcome to Argynvostholt. Mind the steps. The third one's gone, and the fourth, and honestly most of the house.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/3020aec7965cd09b.text: One more. I'll remember this light till then. That's an easy thing to remember.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/320eddff19d99170.text: Me? The old woman's cards wanted me? I'm the one who loses his boots. Some mornings I lose which foot they go on.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/3577239f45d852be.text: Let them go home. ...I heard that. I was lying beside them in the courtyard. I heard him say it, and Vladimir told me I'd heard wrong, and I let him tell me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/36462ddedb5ccc2d.text: That it mattered. Yes. I can hold on to that. The rest will come back or it won't, and either way I'll know which side of the door I'm standing on.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/3792fb6b0e103fbd.text: The patrol says Vallaki's quieter these days. Not frightened-quiet. Busy-quiet. I'd forgotten towns could sound like that.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/379360dd2a87e133.text: There's something about him on my wall. I wrote it down so I'd keep it. I can't remember what I wrote.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/385fd4d11100cec0.text: Or I could stay for one more ride. Your choice. I've made enough of mine.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/3c71e8eb10ee875b.text: One thing more, and then I'll let you up. A knight of the Order names his fellowship. Who stands with you, Sir Godrick?

sir_godfrey_gwilym/41b69637de903d95.text: Four hundred years. I let him tell me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/451a14960875f69d.text: I'll stand, Vladimir. I won't say it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/45c95d412678ee87.text: I'll be in my room with the wall. Come and fetch me when you need a big man in a lot of tin.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/4ab075c3efa98c54.text: I'll stand with you. I won't say it. I said it once already.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/4b35cc0d135b4ab1.text: Keep the watch. Shield the sleeper and the stranger. Lift the fallen. Take nothing not given. And when the light goes out, be the light. Rise, Sir Godrick, of the Order of the Silver Dragon.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/4c4aa0f51cb4f7c7.text: The Order of the Silver Dragon. Lord Argynvost founded us: a silver dragon who liked people enough to look like one at dinner. We kept a watch over the valley. Farms, roads, the passes.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/4f69014c1732e3de.text: The great hall, straight through. He sits at the head of the table, where he's sat since... I stopped counting at three hundred years. Be courteous. He isn't dangerous unless you mention the castle.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/580798fb44a8dc24.text: Go carefully. And if you hear singing in the chapel at night, don't worry. It's only the house, remembering.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/5b4ee3cef9e2a17e.text: Sit in his chair and add my name to the roster as absent. It'll be the first absence in four hundred years. He'll take it harder than a sword.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/5fafe414210f32f6.text: I am. It comes and goes, how much I mind.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/613a7a44b929395c.text: I'll put you down as the one who asked.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/623c392c50d4720d.text: Be the light. Not "hate the dark". We swore to be the light, and we've been sitting in the dark for four hundred years keeping score.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/6466086714787ecc.text: You'll mention the castle. Everyone does.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/64b6962d94bd738d.text: A night at the squires' graves, standing, with the banner. If the squires stand up for him, the Order can't say no. Not even Vladimir. The men-at-arms will come out of the courtyard for the living, though. They always do. He'll need people standing with him.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/65e468d579b3b605.text: Our squire's out at the gate. Living, would you believe. He talks to the men-at-arms as if they could hear him. I think some of them can.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/6775a32f41d84d4e.text: The Lantern Company. Twenty men we sent over the passes for help, the week before the end. They came back too late, and the young lord's archers were waiting on our own road.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/680211b15b8b5493.text: Ioan. Ioan. (He shuts his eyes, which doesn't seem to help him much.) A thin lad with big hands. He cut stone for his father before he came to us.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/695d41359906052b.text: Then a young lord came over the mountains with an army. We lost. We died. We got up again. That last part wasn't in the oath.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/702ee54db7f0181e.text: The oath's still there. I checked this morning, the way you'd pat a pocket for your purse. Still there.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/709d74e8c14f9640.text: Still here. Still me, mostly. What do you need?

sir_godfrey_gwilym/714d00242d5dceaf.text: Vladimir. Please. Look at what's in their hands.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/752c2eaad350e279.text: They ride home every night. They never get here. I go down to the gate sometimes, to see if tonight's the night.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/770fe3b8db864418.text: And St. Andral's has its saint back, I hear. Good. I was christened under that roof, I think. Or one very like it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/78bf3ad9d57d5dc1.text: He wants the oath. Vladimir won't give the living the oath, and he's right, in his way. But the oath was never the first thing a squire swore. First was the vigil.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/78d594322991decc.text: Cold. You lot are warm, though. I'd forgotten people were warm. I keep standing too close; tell me if I do.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/80aeaea89647f757.text: I've written all your names on the inside of my gauntlet. In case. You don't mind?

sir_godfrey_gwilym/8265c7d332b834ae.text: Stand easy, Piet. They're with me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/8586775214697027.text: And the mists came down behind him, and no help ever came, and Vladimir called him a coward at the table, so the rest of us would have somebody to hate who wasn't the dragon.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/91ac9a3cee42dfd7.text: The light's still pulling at me, very gently, like a child at a sleeve. I don't mind. It means it'll be there when I'm done.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/93ef9a11b4a2ce42.text: And I let him. I wrote it on the wall so I wouldn't, and then I forgot the wall.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/98f82c5559f6a3eb.text: Do you think so? I've wondered.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/9b729f9939018753.text: Then don't. An oath's no good from a man who can't say it yet. The Order's very good at waiting, lad. Come back when you can.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/a0ca13cff01065fa.text: But some nights I can't remember why we swore what we swore. I remember that it mattered. I've lost the words for the rest.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/a6599f07edbc7b01.text: Ioan: rode with my lord's last word, on my horse, on my order. And under it, Cosmin: stood the vigil. Squire. (He blows on the page.) Vladimir can argue with the squires if he likes. I wouldn't.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/a978e5f906771a20.text: A ladle. Oh, that's the best thing I've heard in four hundred years. Then you were already a knight, lad. I'm only the witness. Let's witness it properly.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/a9e1740e3e4c4cd4.text: Back again. Good. The house is better with somebody breathing in it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/b8dfbcc5bd698daa.text: The Order's steel waits in the vault, polished by dead hands for a war we forgot. Take what you need for the castle. We ask only enough coin to light candles for the fallen. We have no other use for it now.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/baffb1d75728c777.text: I'm with them, Vladimir. Put me down as absent.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/bc547a14b75e2348.text: And when the house had fallen Vladimir wrote "fled" against his name, and I let him. I forgot. Four hundred years I let a boy be a coward in our book because I forgot.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/be5eeb50ffb1307d.text: I put the ones that mattered most down low. So I'd still be able to reach them, at the end. Read it to me. My eyes have gone the way of the rest of me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/bfe4b45b4b29c2cc.text: I'll write it on the inside of my gauntlet. I write everything down now.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/c16699f3157481b9.text: Who knighted you first, lad? Somebody did. You stand like it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/c548bc165733edc4.text: I know that name. It hurts, and I don't know why it hurts. That's how I know it's one of the important ones.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/c5496e50f2dcc0a2.text: Four hundred years, lad. Still at our posts, though. Mostly.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/c553ecd0a172c9cc.text: He went. That night. I'm sure of that and nothing else. Whether he ran or rode, I can't find it. It's in here somewhere. (He taps the side of his helmet.) Most things are.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/c9ab46f3276c7bb3.text: Then I'll come. I'll tell the commander myself, so he hears it from me and not from the hall. He'll say I'm a fool. He's said it before. It has never once stopped me.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/cae45f233069c797.text: There wouldn't be. The young lord kept the libraries, after.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/cd15f7bf23fd175f.text: Let them go home. That was the word. My lord said it in the courtyard with his last breath, and somebody had to carry it down to the valley, because the knights wouldn't. I sent him. I sent Ioan. On my horse.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/d2639688c06f08b6.text: Brothers. Hear them out. I did, and I remember things I'd lost.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/d5498737744e9e15.text: And take my armour. Not the rust I'm wearing: the good plate, in my chest upstairs, that I kept polished for a war that ended four hundred years ago. A knight of the Order should wear it, and you said the oath better than I did.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/dcbacc496a0af82b.text: You swore his oath. I heard you. I'm not angry. I swore it too, once, and it took me four hundred years to hear what I'd said.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ddc2da278151928f.text: Thank you. Tell the old woman her cards were right about me, and that I was very tired.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/de2279e9c60b9863.text: It's calling. It's warm. ...Not yet. I promised somebody a ride. I'll come when the castle's done, and the light will still be here.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/de58c19c92cfbddc.text: Teodor. The pears were Teodor's. I've been remembering his pears for years and thinking they were mine.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/e78f6c2d8d6823b7.text: "Remember the oath." I wrote that for tonight, I think. I just didn't know it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/e79ed6320a8d6c75.text: The night before the end. Argynvost called Aldric up to the tower and sent him out over the passes for help, because he had the fastest horse.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/e8c1ee3b4ed48cd2.text: Pears. I remember pears very clearly. And a grey mare who bit everyone but me. And my sister Gwenllian, who laughed like a goose. I've lost her face. I've still got the laugh.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ea3825a5f90eda63.text: The cards. The old woman's cards wanted me, didn't they? I can feel the light pulling. I could go now. I'd like to.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ecb56e1681c0e431.text: The town with the festivals? The patrol says the singing carries all the way up the ridge. It isn't happy singing. It's very loud singing.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f12b0ac7fe20f875.text: This was Ioan's. He left it at the gate the night he rode, because a shield slows a horse. It's caught every arrow that's come at the Order's gate for four hundred years. Take it. Our squire has a wooden sword and the right idea, and that'll do him for now.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f142b3dabe87e177.text: It's kind of you. It isn't enough, not yet. Find me the words, if you can. They're carved somewhere in this house. I used to know where.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f1aef10f5444ceec.text: Keep the sword. Aldric would want it to go on being carried by someone who comes back.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f1e0a7cf699b8485.text: So he said he'd wait until he wasn't. He sleeps out there on the stones. It's very cold. He means it, I think. I'd have meant it, at his age.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f3943f3c6235ef4a.text: I'd go. I'd go tonight. But I'd be half a knight. I've lost the oath, and a knight without his oath is a man standing in a great deal of tin.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f681f11517f970f3.text: The road patrol said you'd be coming. They said you were polite. That's rare enough that they mentioned it twice.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f787802f1769b31e.text: Sir Godfrey Gwilym, of the Order of the Silver Dragon, or what's left of it. You'll want the commander. Everyone does, eventually. Then they wish they hadn't.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/f9a8192c10360585.text: Interesting. Yes. There's a boy out on the squires' graves. Living. Came up the ridge a week ago and asked to swear the oath. Vladimir told him the Order doesn't take the living.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ff1d9e99538c454f.text: Kneel, then. No, the other knee. That's it.

sir_godfrey_gwilym/ff475f0e82e94b5e.text: Something new. I haven't had anything new since... well. Since.

sorin_krezkov/5d9b54022ee9a5ab.text: Sorin. Sorin, come in, it's dark.

sorin_krezkov/75d7de4a3e84bbbc.text: Mama, it's dark. Mama, I want to go home.

sorvia/0761c60ad36005ab.text: What? They'd work it out. They're not stupid. Look at them; they're nearly clever.

sorvia/0d8ea912cc4195c5.text: He knows you're here, you know. The lord. He knew before you did. He always does, because we...

sorvia/3339c34a6a372e78.text: You'll meet a tall, dark stranger. Everyone here does. Only once, usually.

sorvia/52a35ec7daedbe25.text: She's nice. She mended my horse's bridle once and wouldn't take a copper. I hope... nothing. More wine?

sorvia/5d1bad293f552b24.text: And he hasn't finished with you. He's hardly started.

sorvia/6c73533c3182b24a.text: So many lines. You've read too much. One day a book is going to read you back.

sorvia/88240be161c12010.text: You'll do. Here, take this. Our uncle won it, and lost it, and won it again. The pictures lie better than Mirabel.

sorvia/b741e43ad4a77925.text: A line of faith straight down the middle, and a crack right across it. Don't worry. Cracks let the light in, Grandmother says. Also the wind.

sorvia/bd375fb97ce9012d.text: Your life line is long. It's just that something keeps trying to cut it. There, see? Teeth marks.

sorvia/c154b9df358683f5.text: This hand has been in a great many pockets. One of them belonged to someone very, very old. My advice? Give it back. Mirabel's advice will be to sell it.

sorvia/d753fabffbc9ae01.text: Oh, yes! Give it here. Not you, Mirabel, I know yours; it says you'll die of being rude.

sorvia/d9de2be2b1d0cd8e.text: Your boots have walked farther than boots should, in this valley. Sorry. I notice things.

stanimir/08d8095dca3571c5.text: Nicu. My sister's boy. He rode to Vallaki to sell a horse, and he came home by the crossroads after all.

stanimir/11f32c37b78ea0c0.text: He wears the Baron's ribbon now, I hear, and somebody else's name. Be kind to him, sergeant, or be quick. He has been both to himself already.

stanimir/1f6dc2ade61dc2df.text: Pay her what she asks. It is never only money, and it is never more than you can spare. Usually.

stanimir/20cf33fb024316a7.text: Madam Eva has been old since my grandmother was a girl. She reads the cards for whoever the road brings, and the road brings whoever the cards want.

stanimir/20d74d2a834eca05.text: Everyone knew your father. He shouted at me for an hour once, about a horse. Best conversation I had that year.

stanimir/23d69df75df8c44b.text: You showed the old woman your teeth in her own tent. I play the fiddle at my fire, friends; I don't play the fool. Mind your manners in that tent.

stanimir/24b63ff492a7a1ba.text: He walked again? This land won't even let our dead lie down. Then you gave him his rest the hard way. That is still a gift.

stanimir/2dd3b841515f12d9.text: To the fire, the fiddle and Madam Eva, in that order on a good day. On a bad day, to my wife.

stanimir/2df3d7f82af3096b.text: And you bring the burgomaster's girl, out past the crossroads. Well, well. Sit near the fire, lady. Not too near the trees.

stanimir/2e9120f8158888dc.text: Forty. You owe me ten and a true word, and I will never see either. Sit if you must. The wine is not free tonight.

stanimir/34856537d2650912.text: Into the trees at night, following what they took for a woman singing. My people sat by the fire with their hands over their ears. That is what we are good at.

stanimir/40d102ff30549c17.direction: [storyteller by the fire, slow and theatrical]
stanimir/40d102ff30549c17.text: Once there was a prince who won this valley with his sword, and he had a younger brother whom everybody loved. The brother was to marry a girl as lovely as a spring morning. The prince wanted her.

stanimir/46fb27e2b93e8421.text: Madam Eva is in the big tent. She has been expecting you. Don't ask me how; I stopped asking forty years ago.

stanimir/4d160909b05c9ec8.text: Plum wine, from plums that grew in a summer before any of you were born. Drink! It won't hurt. Much.

stanimir/50c17e74018ab9a9.text: Good. A guest who takes and then gives back is still a guest. Barely. Sit, but sit where I can see your hands.

stanimir/5c47e000b4185b6d.text: One came back. Half a moon later, down the castle road, alone, barefoot, a drum on his back and no sticks for it. He wouldn't sit by our fire. He asked the way to the town with walls.

stanimir/5f8f847ec37419fe.text: Back at my fire! Good. Sit, drink, tell me lies about the road.

stanimir/63d2d28c28e41789.direction: [hushed, then bursting into a hearty laugh]
stanimir/63d2d28c28e41789.text: His own guards filled him with arrows. He did not die. He has been not dying ever since. Drink! It's a wedding story. It should end with a drink.

stanimir/67dd75b7bf3b345d.text: Soldiers. Grey coats, a little bird on the shoulder, forty of them, singing songs I would not sing in front of my mother. Yes. We camped them here.

stanimir/6e79103f570fa6cc.text: And listen. Somebody in this camp will send word up the hill that you passed this way. That is how it is with us. It will be me, and I will tell him you went east. Small thing. Big thing. Both.

stanimir/7e8ace48cceba5f7.text: My strongbox is lighter by forty gold, and you are the only strangers in my camp. I will ask once.

stanimir/9d04d5231e027a2d.text: With words said over him, even. I don't know your gods. I hope they knew him.

stanimir/a6f01617ed66eb42.text: You lie the way I play the flute: loudly and badly. Give it back. And ten more, for making me listen to it.

stanimir/aeed4839f49ba7ee.text: As you like. Nobody robs my fire twice.

stanimir/b03a394720d0a087.text: Forty for the box, ten for the flute solo. Sit, but sit where I can see your hands. And nobody sings.

stanimir/b262fde593dc3157.text: Sit, friends. Sit. The fire is still free, and for you the wine is too.

stanimir/b52b74ba165bca60.text: A pleasure! Come again. Bring more gold and less mud.

stanimir/b6654653d0bffdbe.text: Silver earring shaped like a horse's head? Black hair, too long? A laugh like a donkey falling downstairs?

stanimir/b8eda7ce1ae81f2d.text: Guests! Off the road, out of the dark, into the light! I am Stanimir. The fire is free, the wine is cheap, and the music is the best in Barovia, because it is the only music in Barovia.

stanimir/bc3f5c81f4495245.text: We answer to the road and the cards. And a little, yes, to the man on the hill. He lets our wagons through the mist. A dog doesn't bite the hand that holds the gate.

stanimir/bf96c970957f2faf.text: You cut him down. Strangers, and you stopped and cut him down, when nobody else on that road would slow their horse.

stanimir/c6fe845ec66f764c.text: Luminita must hear it from me. Not from you. From me.

stanimir/c80ad6548de76012.text: Still hanging, then. I'll go myself, tonight, with a knife and a good horse, and bring him home.

stanimir/d0cb02acc88db549.text: Then we will play something cheerful. Something very loud and very cheerful.

stanimir/dcfa1aca3285e0ee.text: The castle paid in gold that was very cold to hold. I won't tell you we didn't take it. We took it. We always take it. That is what he keeps us for.

stanimir/e94af3ae1ec34e08.text: Then one of my own owes me an apology. Sit. I'm sorry I asked.

stanimir/f34fda4152450da2.text: On the wedding day, the prince made a bargain with something under the world. He killed his brother. The bride ran from him, and the castle wall was high, and the gorge below it was very deep.

stanimir/fb60780a3216d6a6.text: Rope, oil, food that keeps, blankets that keep you. Two potions, very dear, because they are very dear to me.

stanimir/fbe7d9a6c9c954e1.text: You put a knife to the old woman's throat in my camp. Walk through, if you must. Don't stop, and don't sit.

stefania_martikov/1b9bf20ed8e19014.text: I think my brother would have died for Elvir without stopping to think. So something stopped him. I'd give a great deal to know what.

stefania_martikov/2e7fd705dadd764a.text: You're the ones Adrian found. Good. Sit, eat, and don't feed the children; they lie about being hungry. Mirela, out of that tree. I'm Stefania. I keep this family alive, mostly by shouting at it.

stefania_martikov/31bdebfa1ec34472.text: And Adrian told you something, didn't he? He never tells me anything. ...Good. Better you than nobody.

stefania_martikov/58d205c0ba965cae.text: Sleeping in beds again, which they're furious about; they'd got used to roosting. Viorel bit his cousin yesterday in raven form. I've told him that's twice as rude.

stefania_martikov/660bb8df68c294dc.text: No. He won't. Last spring Father sent Elvir and Adrian to watch Yester Hill. The druids' things caught them in the bracken. Adrian came home alone, all blood and feathers, and said "I flew." Nothing else. Not then, not since.

stefania_martikov/738e2137fdbecd8f.text: They think it's an adventure, which is the only mercy in it. Toma has decided he's going to kill a druid. He's seven. I've told him he finishes his porridge first.

stefania_martikov/83cf9bd4bb06bac7.text: If a single coin goes missing in this camp, I'll know who to shout at.

stefania_martikov/99c5dbc7d7581fd0.text: A roof! Walls! A floor nobody's growing things through! I've scrubbed the kitchen twice and it still smells of druid. What can I do for you?

stefania_martikov/99fa795956c4b0fa.text: Home. Get in here. You stink of smoke and you've torn your good coat. ...You're all right? Good. Good.

stefania_martikov/a9899a90731becbe.text: I have. And a floor, and a door that shuts. Here, take this; it was Grandmother's. Press it to a wound and the wound closes, which is more than I can say for my brothers' mouths. You'll need it more than we will now.

stefania_martikov/b367fe39c990d358.text: Bring Father the truth. He can't argue with the truth; he's never had the practice. Elvir was taken up that hill. If anything of him is left, it's up there.

stefania_martikov/bf23adc9d151af59.text: The cart came back from Vallaki empty and the driver came back drunk. Urwin sent a note, three words: "About time, Father." Father laughed until he had to sit down.

stefania_martikov/dbe2564f1d08689a.text: Father's standing right behind you and you're telling me? He'll love that. Go on, then, both of you.

stefania_martikov/dc122e1d11cb715d.text: Elvir was the youngest. The loud one. Father raised a cairn for him with nothing under it, and he's hardly said a kind word to Adrian since.

stefania_martikov/e1036118bf4b256b.text: The cart came back from Krezk. They opened the gate for it, and the burgomaster counted the casks in himself. He sent us back a pear tree. I don't know what to do with a pear tree.

stefania_martikov/e818bb5d09d33bb1.text: The cart came back from the village under the castle. They rang the church bell when it rolled in. The driver says nobody there had heard it ring for anything but a burial in years.

stefania_martikov/f6f5166e9cd4a259.text: Back again. There's soup. There's always soup.

stella_wachter/083c19cdfec9337f.text: I sleep with the shutters open now. Father Lucian thinks it's for the air.

stella_wachter/15db90dec32632b9.text: And Mother knew. Mother tied the bow every morning and told callers I was delicate.

stella_wachter/1e5e22f172318d4a.text: Father Lucian has given me a cot behind the vestry and a great many blankets. He keeps asking if I'm cold. I'm not cold. I'm furious.

stella_wachter/25439494ce90a20e.text: Mother's book club meets in the cellar, under the study. The way down is a panel behind the bookcase: push the third shelf, not the second. They don't read. They pray. To him.

stella_wachter/2612bb0681c1462d.text: Come and find me there. I'll have something for you, when I've stopped shaking.

stella_wachter/322b3eb3c296f25d.text: He looks out of my eyes. Every day. Mother ties the bow fresh every morning, so it's neat for him. Get it off. Get it off me.

stella_wachter/62cff71bf07997bc.text: I'm free of him. I'm not free of her. I'm going to Father Lucian. I know the way; I've watched it from that window every day for two years.

stella_wachter/70a108f5c6748ddd.text: And this. He sent it for my sixteenth birthday, with a card that said "for flying". I never put it on. You should. Let him see it on somebody who isn't afraid of him.

stella_wachter/a5a63518041dd189.text: And this was my dowry. Mother would only spend it on him. Take it.

stella_wachter/c2fd0f2d8f771edb.text: I told him I'd follow him like a cat follows cream. At Mother's party. I was laughing. He said: then you shall.

stella_wachter/cf547801361efa3d.text: The third shelf, not the second. Did you look? Don't tell me what's down there. I've heard them singing.

stella_wachter/e3db437f2ce4e95e.text: Two years. Two years I've sat at that window and watched the square for him. Who went into the Baron's. Who went to church. Who looked up.

strahd/0100fd8e9f96e190.text: A dusk elf taught you to stand like that. I know the stance. I knew a whole people who stood like that.

strahd/018e867e11182fc3.text: Come, my dear. This house has waited a very long time to hear your step.

strahd/01d86d1b4eb88cad.text: How brave, and how thin. Another night. There are so many nights.

strahd/021fbb56d36133fe.text: I built it to be seen from everywhere in the valley. I have been looking out of it ever since.

strahd/02c747913bd13643.direction: [cold fury, the courtesy dropping, low and sharp]
strahd/02c747913bd13643.text: You do not say no to me. Not you. Not again.

strahd/02ce2bc8628a9310.text: Patient, my dear. There is a difference. You will learn it.

strahd/034b4d7b4bb43fe6.text: I know what you are carrying, little merchant. I can smell the ink from here. Some assessor with a ledger and a grey coat has his hand in your pocket, and you want my name to pay him with.

strahd/0514b6ddbd8fb7b4.text: The little monk. My chamberlain tells me you have a teacher's manners. He did not enjoy them. Nobody has unsettled Rahadin in two hundred years.

strahd/0786fac98fe1a6d0.text: Freely given. In my own hand. Your assessor will hate it. Give him my regards.

strahd/07d2e1a9dbdd22c5.text: Here is my price. I will name it once.

strahd/0926b6152e0d0675.text: My guests. You do get everywhere. I am not sure I like you being here, of all places.

strahd/0a0c10bfbcc85ebc.text: Ireena. You came to see her. Of course you did.

strahd/0ac66905aabf4ae2.text: Well said. The last man who shouted at me is in that grave. Allow me to return the courtesy.

strahd/0b46b36fc75cf06d.text: Under your protection. Kolyan said the same, from his doorway, with a lamp. It held for a month. Let us see whether yours does better.

strahd/0bf5992e35745ebf.text: As you wish. The chair will wait. It is good at waiting. So am I.

strahd/0dbfdb15415714e5.text: Then you have done my work for me without asking, which I will forgive once. Do not let it become a habit.

strahd/0ecba6fc74e18089.text: Do come to dinner. She will be there. She has always been there.

strahd/0f37d7a3c1ac7e34.text: Leave Ireena with me, freely, and walk out of my house with your lives. The mists will even let you go. I can be generous when I am happy.

strahd/0f5e25038c140b4f.text: Off my road. In my land. Under my sky. Let me show you whose road it is.

strahd/0fdc90b4b676f77b.text: Do not get up. We have not been introduced. I am Strahd von Zarovich, and you are sleeping in my house. All of this is my house.

strahd/1249e9f743e68b56.text: You had my letter, I trust. You read it twice. You thought I would not know.

strahd/16653043e2159990.text: Silvain. Scholar. Come here. You may take notes, if you like.

strahd/18a10370b192cd62.text: Your friends may keep their candles in the cellar. I find them touching, the way a dog is touching when it brings home something dead.

strahd/18a66b14ce08559c.text: For whoever came. You came. I am grateful, and I am not often grateful.

strahd/18c2b6e5893de28a.text: Splendid. Do not die too quickly. I should have to find new guests, and the valley is so short of them.

strahd/19877930fb6c28fd.text: Dead. Lysaga. And you tell me she did this.

strahd/1c1f484a080b380b.text: Since you ask it, my dear. You see how easily I give you things, when you ask.

strahd/1c405d08001d31de.text: Because you are the most interesting thing to happen in my valley for a very long time. And because I wanted to see you up close. Before.

strahd/1f317c6729a24191.text: Thank you. That was courageous, and very foolish, and I shall remember both. Now go home, all of you. I have to see to my house.

strahd/1f3762f9593e2da4.text: What is mine. Ireena knows the way home. She has always known it; she has only forgotten. I will remind her, one night at a time.

strahd/1f9fd14b0e2bd099.text: Not tonight, then. I can wait. I have had a great deal of practice.

strahd/23bcf96224094e90.text: Liriel. Wake up, priestess. Come here and kneel. You know how; you do it every morning.

strahd/2533a4980ffacb58.text: Or I could buy your contract from him instead. Then you would owe me, and not a stranger. I am a much better landlord than a devil. Ask anyone in the valley.

strahd/26217337ca5f3783.text: Walk where you like tonight. Some doors will open for you and some will not. That is true of every house.

strahd/26a17e9541e62d37.text: Afraid? Of a box of bones and a tired priest? I am disappointed in you. I had thought you clever.

strahd/26d5a340ae88f8aa.text: Go where you like. Every road is mine, and every door you knock on opens on a house that pays me rent. When you are ready, we will dine. Until then I remain your host, and your landlord, Strahd von Zarovich.

strahd/28f23544b94930f9.text: There. You're mine now, a little. Don't look so worried. I'm very patient with the things I own.

strahd/2b6586bdb3398d5a.text: You found your way out of the house on the hill. Most do not. I listened for your screams. There were fewer than I had hoped.

strahd/2c2b4a9816ead25b.text: Not on the road. The road is for travelling. We will do this properly, in my house, when you are ready. You are not ready.

strahd/2c9d5b84214a6330.text: My quiet guests. You said nothing at the graveside. Let us see whether the road has loosened your tongues.

strahd/2fe7ad289c11dc72.text: Yes. You did well in that house. Let us see you do well here.

strahd/3002bc09bbb0689e.text: You have read my book. Then you know I was not always this. Do not pity me for it. I never pitied anyone.

strahd/324aab210d00e5ef.text: Tell her I asked after her. She will pretend not to care. She always did.

strahd/32a41a7ff8985412.text: Baba Lysaga is dead. She held me when I was born. Whatever else she was, that was hers to keep, and you took it.

strahd/34d2bfc386b1a2d3.text: Holy ground. Bones in a box. You will not stay inside a church forever, my dear. Nobody does.

strahd/37ffbfb835ab5970.text: Then I will send my carriage for her tonight. Go home, if you can still remember where that is.

strahd/38821d945454a325.text: Perhaps you are. Let us find out.

strahd/3a98352f4a9464ee.text: You haven't given me any apricots.

strahd/3ba8b481b243316d.text: Gallant. Do you know how many gallant men have stood exactly there? I stopped counting them. I did not stop killing them.

strahd/3cebfdb52efbb4ae.text: You quarrelled with the Vistani. A pity. They are so useful, and so easily frightened.

strahd/3d2eb6b4c8425d1d.text: Thank you. Truly. Now go, before I remember how much you have cost me.

strahd/3f7f03c780f75854.text: You did once. You will again.

strahd/40757887e6e92fc8.text: You carry my brother's sword. It did not save him either.

strahd/41dc67a265221d6b.text: Keep me interested. In this house, it is the only thing that has ever kept anyone safe.

strahd/41e59d89c83f3d27.text: Ah. The ones who drew steel at a funeral. I keep the memory the way one keeps a pressed flower, or a debt.

strahd/4480f3fce954e3f4.text: Upstairs. I will not say where. Finding it is half the pleasure.

strahd/45310951d389a74a.text: Do not get up. I only came to see how my guests are sleeping. Badly, I see. I have taken some trouble over that.

strahd/47388ab03dc973ff.text: You have put Ireena behind a wall and a door. I have always admired walls. They tell me exactly where to look.

strahd/477c885df7895c47.text: I owe you the truth about Marina. I do not often owe anyone. Consider it noted.

strahd/47b50f535e0f44fa.text: Then I will ask again. I am very patient, and you will have to sleep some time.

strahd/48a38a58a64974c6.text: The old priests' sun. I remember the last man who carried it. I remember how he sounded at the end.

strahd/48f10a4b34bf1842.text: Keep your trinket. It will not keep her.

strahd/49f70e1190190c06.text: Good evening. You will be the strangers my wolves keep telling me about. I am Strahd von Zarovich, and this is a private grave.

strahd/4a05403878f7424e.text: And the large young man who calls himself Sir. I have met a great many knights. None of them smiled so much, and none of them lasted.

strahd/4bed6a75f0bed572.text: Ireena is resting upstairs. She will not join us tonight. It has been a long week for her.

strahd/4cba81e4c4892779.text: You drew steel at a funeral. Tonight, I hope, you will settle for the cutlery.

strahd/4e04e85040c28023.text: My wolves have a new leader. They will want to make a good impression.

strahd/4eaf2d6b56c9032e.text: Ireena is welcome, of course. Her room has been ready for a very long time.

strahd/4efffff63895c9cb.text: The valley and I have an understanding. I keep it, and it keeps me. You would find the arrangement suits you less.

strahd/4f624c84b5b7aed0.text: Sir Godrick, of the Order of the Silver Dragon. The last recruit of an order that died in my courtyard. I hope they gave you a good sword. They never had much else.

strahd/4fb752e823e76e5c.text: You broke my heart in the tower. A poet would make something of that. I will make something of you.

strahd/5136da5733270938.text: You stood between Tatyana and me at her window. I remember every face that has done that. There have not been many, and they did not stay long.

strahd/52e9243e1617ed00.text: How gallant. She hardly needs you; she has been refusing me on her own for centuries. It has never once saved anyone who stood where you are standing.

strahd/576e5a270de8ad8a.text: Ireena. They have you walking in the mud like a pedlar's wife. Let them. Every road in this valley ends at my door. I had them laid that way.

strahd/5c2dfe614cce729e.text: Poison would be so impolite. And so dull.

strahd/5e009408355d4f2b.text: I have left a fight with you before. You may have taken it for weakness. It was manners.

strahd/5ed251ecfd924b1c.text: Steel, at a funeral. Here, then: something you are allowed to kill. They were this village's grandmothers once. Do be gentle.

strahd/60915f440c5b066b.text: Ireena, stand aside, please. This is between your friends and me.

strahd/620998afa79b9f16.text: My guests. You came. Sit, please. I trust the carriage was comfortable.

strahd/626e96f79f62a3a1.text: And a scholar. My library would delight you. You must come up and see it. The last scholar who came is up there still. He has stopped asking to leave.

strahd/62ec74282f72eaec.text: Want? That is a merchant's word. I want nothing from her that she does not choose to give.

strahd/63535b920f4a28a6.text: You bleed well, all of you. Keep her, for now. I enjoy the way you hold on.

strahd/63f5674c666aed37.text: Hedda. Healer. Come here, and bring your hands.

strahd/6412ec79a9dc9dc8.text: Good evening. You will be the guests my wolves keep telling me about. I am Strahd von Zarovich. This is my road, those are my wolves in the trees, and the mist behind you is mine as well. Do enjoy the walk.

strahd/6482f78f6089eb43.text: The little priestess of the dawn. You sing to my windows in the mornings that aren't mornings. I hear everything in my valley. A lovely voice, and a hopeless task.

strahd/64ea66cdbc52ec27.text: My guests. You came. I did wonder whether you would, and I am so rarely made to wonder.

strahd/66041225379637bd.text: My guests. You have grown remarkable, and I have grown curious. Dine with me tonight at Castle Ravenloft. The carriage knows the way.

strahd/66519f11ad10d538.text: You bled me at her window. I have thought of it fondly since.

strahd/671eaa628055719b.text: You saw me on the ridge. You looked thin. Do eat. I prefer my guests well fed.

strahd/699397fff128913d.text: Manners. Good. You will need them at my table, and my guests do not always leave it. We will speak again. Ireena. Leave the window unlatched tonight. I should hate to break the glass.

strahd/6a4424c891eeea09.text: A priestess of the dawn, in my valley. How brave. How very late.

strahd/6b2a15b2216a1466.text: You are most welcome. It has been a charming evening. I so rarely get to use the good silver.

strahd/6e1038f429867171.text: Ireena. Candlelight suits you. Sit beside me. No? Then sit wherever you like.

strahd/6f1e78e030739f71.text: Pity. You would have made a very good monster. You have the attention to detail.

strahd/72122db4c5f9bb00.text: And the wild one. My wolves speak of you. Run with them tonight, after supper, if you like. I will show you a forest no axe has ever touched.

strahd/73a3a4edb413a3b9.text: The offer stands until you leave my house. Then it falls, like everything else.

strahd/73aedbff2bd90a8a.text: One of you has been up the mountain, to the temple. I can tell. We have more in common than you would like.

strahd/7675f8f71ce241d9.text: Godrick. Up, squire. Your lord is calling you.

strahd/7822a07e807a3482.text: Close the lid. Walk away. Come back in a hundred years and we will do this again. It will be the most interesting thing that ever happens to any of you.

strahd/7a220416eaa457e2.text: The little thief carries her portrait. Keep it close, child. When I want it back, I will come for it, and for the hand that holds it.

strahd/816daf00c48a3f21.text: Beneath me. Yes. You are learning how I think, and that is the first step to being mine. Another night, then, with better light.

strahd/8359c15ebdc7b1de.text: You will find the valley very quiet without me. Very small. You will go home, and nothing there will ever be as large as I was.

strahd/83af0e9ec2bb5465.text: I promise you nothing. Perhaps one evening I will come to dinner. Do not trouble to set a place for me. I will choose my own.

strahd/840f52bc09a90b09.text: My brother's sword. I threw that sword as far as a man can throw anything.

strahd/868dacd5aaa0cb01.text: He always did take what was meant for me, and thank whoever brought it.

strahd/86cdbd7d27b55b80.text: Welcome to my house. I am Strahd von Zarovich, and you are very welcome in it.

strahd/8780459f2aaf106d.text: And the soldier who kept my invitation. I am touched. Your company asked after you, you know. Near the end.

strahd/87dd7cca9a33e625.text: My guests, on my road. The ones who told me no across a graveside. I have thought about it every night since. I think about very little else.

strahd/8860b09fd454bb02.text: I have been a generous host. I can be other things. Consider this the last of my courtesy, and consider it carefully.

strahd/88f99f4ab9012b13.text: You did, once. It changed nothing.

strahd/8a8eaecd19012b56.text: Ah. My guests. You are just in time to say goodbye.

strahd/8af73a06da70e687.text: Bring your weapons, by all means. I forgive the business by your fire. A host must.

strahd/8ce8bec982aafb5c.text: Wise. So few of my guests are. Go down into my valley and live there, for as long as you keep me amused.

strahd/8d90fc09b768fd53.text: My guests. I have kept a list. It is a habit of the old, and of the patient.

strahd/8e5662047770418e.text: And you carry my brother's blade. Sergei never could hold on to anything that mattered.

strahd/8e5fed758cb49c1b.text: Brave. They are always brave. It never changes how the story ends.

strahd/8e9f1600f3f37744.text: Ah. And the evening was going so well.

strahd/8ed8d9920f90bf37.text: You fought well on my road. Come and let me thank you properly.

strahd/8f043a8ca283bc07.text: Or kneel, and serve me, and live a very long time. Or refuse, and we will finish this.

strahd/8f61bec8faaa8ba6.text: And the merchant who paid his devil with my name. I am told your assessor is still furious. I have not laughed so much in a century.

strahd/92f40a6a9481e401.text: No harm will come to you under my roof before the meal is over. You have my word, and my word is older than your kingdoms.

strahd/96017b442e1e6f42.text: You kept my first letter. I noticed. I notice everything that concerns you.

strahd/9b0961e14ff822ac.text: How brave. Your god has not eaten at this table in a very long time. Do tell him the soup was excellent.

strahd/9c2d46aa64bc5af9.text: Tamsin. Bring me what you stole, little thief.

strahd/9cbc2a75938be3d8.text: In a man's own house. I will remember that. Sleep, if you can. I will be watching to see which of you does.

strahd/9d106733b2d0fbdd.text: Do. And mind the lamp, if you lit it. She never liked the dark.

strahd/9d9512da62455342.text: Better than I hoped. Not yet what you will need. Do keep practising.

strahd/9fa4f17f36a01da1.text: And a merchant, with ink on his soul. I can smell it from here.

strahd/a3e17d0de5c32d99.text: You stare, guest. Is something the matter with my face?

strahd/a48bc16895566681.text: Ireena. You came all the way down. You always did come, in the end.

strahd/a49730ad057f29ef.text: And you, who watched me all through the meal. I hope you found what you were looking for.

strahd/a5a531b368f479af.text: You drew on me once, on this very road. I said not here. I have changed my mind.

strahd/a6213dcc0b0755ee.text: You have refused my carriage. I am told it was a fine evening for a drive.

strahd/a924142741fa02f4.text: Silence. Keep it. It will be all you have left, in the end.

strahd/abb4e2d87a25dd31.text: You carried her home, thief. All that way, and you never once dropped her. Now give her to me.

strahd/ac626d122eb7d773.text: Silence. Wise. Keep it; I will learn what you love without asking. Ireena. Latch the window, if it helps you sleep. It will not stop me.

strahd/aec7473885b2d040.text: And you, merchant. You smell of brimstone and apricots. Someone already holds your paper. I wonder what they would take for it.

strahd/afbf796e53140a7d.text: Wren. Little monk. Your master is not here to tell you no. Come.

strahd/b17fe32796769947.text: You gave my first letter to a devil. I am told he was very cross. I can't remember when I last enjoyed a piece of news so much.

strahd/b33ddb4ad8a6a6de.text: Beneath me? Everything here is beneath me. That is the point of a castle. Begin.

strahd/b3b191b6c6674995.text: You gave it to my brother. How very like him to accept.

strahd/b5630eb8d7c0f8dc.text: Well said. There are other windows in this town, and other people asleep behind them. I wonder which I will visit instead.

strahd/bbdf977c74200841.text: You burned my tree on Yester Hill. It was older than your nations. I do not expect you to understand what that means; I only want you to know that I do.

strahd/be145f942680b5db.text: My guests, on my road, and still so well mannered. Good. Polite guests are the easiest to keep.

strahd/c08600511b9b27c2.text: Good. I should have been so disappointed. Begin.

strahd/c1092dc049ca657b.text: Someone lit the old dragon's lamp on the ridge. I watched it from my window. It is very pretty.

strahd/c5462e9fa151b6b8.text: And my thanks for the boy from under the church. He came home to me starving, so I let him have the first family he passed on the road. He was very grateful.

strahd/c6df5d37f10fe48e.text: Sergeant Varga. Fall in. Your company did, at the end.

strahd/c7cca6e507559fe8.text: You have left Ireena with a priest and his saint. How touching. Saints are so rarely at home.

strahd/c8007678585d04ef.text: Your father held his door for a month with a lamp, Ismark. You could not hold a cup.

strahd/c847f17d49251a7e.text: Do not stop on my account. Kolyan shouted at my wolves from his doorway every night for a month. Let him have a little quiet now. He had none at the end.

strahd/c8e3a9ff9856aea6.text: You have Ireena with you. Keep her warm and keep her close. I should be desolate if anything happened to her that I had not arranged.

strahd/c97a30d88e01134b.text: Keep it lit. It is the only light for a mile, and every hungry thing in my woods can see it. Good night.

strahd/cbed612c9fcf2c4b.text: The village hid her from me, and in the morning she was dead in their chapel. So I sent the river to ask them why. It is still asking.

strahd/ce9085c451735a65.text: Tonight? To learn you. Which of you sleeps lightly. Which sleeps with a hand on a knife. Which one the others would die for. I will need to know that, later.

strahd/ceb7d39518763d21.text: Kip. Merchant. Come here. I want to inspect the goods.

strahd/cec6c8d8354e7454.text: In my own bedroom, at this hour. You might at least have knocked.

strahd/cf194c6cc0938b69.text: Ireena. Come out. The night is fine, and the company in there is very old and very dead.

strahd/d0a613e713a8f98a.text: The old woman at the pool has told you a story about me. She tells it to everyone. It always ends the same way.

strahd/d1c46a595b78f7cf.text: A critic at my table. How refreshing; my staff are all too frightened to tell me anything. You are the cook among my guests, I think. And a diviner, they tell me.

strahd/d6285a55bdb2add7.text: And a little monk who stands like a dusk elf. I knew a whole people who stood like that. There are very few of them left. I saw to it.

strahd/d65b6b807ca064de.text: Good evening. I hear you are becoming formidable. I like to see such things for myself. Indulge me.

strahd/d68534b991118c9e.text: There. Civilised. We will dine together, one evening. I insist, and I am not used to being refused.

strahd/d7d86cccffdde693.text: We have met on the road, of course. You and my wolves. I have not had a better evening's exercise in years.

strahd/d9895eff9e060709.text: Ah. There it is. I had forgotten what it looked like.

strahd/da5b747519fac5b3.text: Ask the old woman at the pool. Or ask me, over dinner. Good evening, Ireena.

strahd/da72cfd89efbe428.text: Ireena. Such late hours. Shall I wait while you decide whether to scream?

strahd/da9777ca32523a98.text: You have been to see the old woman at the pool. Did she tell you where to dig? Dig, by all means. I have outlived everyone who found something.

strahd/e036fa57fcb31948.text: Before whatever you are planning. You are planning something. Everyone who sits at this table is.

strahd/e108de1ead6741e2.text: As my guests wish. I only wanted her to hear the bell. Bells are for funerals, Ireena. Listen to it, and wonder whose is next.

strahd/e2b2aa83d431dc9e.text: Ratatoille. Come here, little cook. I am told you wish to be taken seriously.

strahd/e46fe5dfd42d2e73.text: You see? We understand each other already.

strahd/e4a3330df2417bf2.text: Kneel, then. There. You see how easy it is? Everyone kneels in the end. You have only done it sooner.

strahd/e60a70ef50ddafc9.text: You wear the Morninglord's trinket where I can see it. I have seen it before. I watched its last bearer's light go out.

strahd/e7aecb0f62bbb1fd.text: I came to welcome you to my land, all of you. You have been busy since you came, and I know every door you have knocked on. Stay as long as you like. The mists will see that you do.

strahd/e85b87b64212da26.text: A candlemaker's daughter, which is to say nobody, which is to say someone I had looked for over a very long time. She was frightened of me. They usually are, at first.

strahd/e8c116666a4391ff.text: Well. Here we are. I confess I had imagined this room with more candles.

strahd/e910968dfb96fe53.text: I am at the gate, my dear, as a guest should be. Everything past it is mine: the yard, the grave, the man in it. And you. Keep the scarf on. I know what is under it. I put it there.

strahd/eb5e32eb7da0574b.text: My dear guests. Forgive a host for writing when he might call. My nights are spoken for, and my days are not my own.

strahd/ebda8d9d52f21219.text: Gustav. You write again to offer me your devotion, as if it were a coin I had dropped. I did not ask for it, and I do not owe you for it.

strahd/efe4734935ec7eec.text: Stay. Cook for me, or conjure for me, as you prefer. I will give you a title older than your family and a tower of your own, and every person in this valley will stand when you enter a room. I don't make that offer twice.

strahd/f3de91d181fca112.text: You. The one asleep nearest the fire. Come here.

strahd/f46bf620d8da2ef8.text: She sang to me, when I was small. She was the only one who did.

strahd/f9a1d7a48e209f7e.text: Do keep looking. I am told I am worth it.

strahd/f9dea76ba605c1d7.text: My soul is not mine to sell. It was sold long ago, at a better price than your devil could imagine. So my name costs me nothing. I'll give it to you.

strahd/fae1039500bf8ef1.text: Ireena is upstairs, dressing for dinner. She asks after you. Less than she did.

strahd/fcbfb8ec0b6b9baf.text: There. That is how little it takes. I wanted you to see it, before you decide to fight me.

strahd/fe8fb04432964b55.text: The guests who told me no across a grave. And here you are at my table. I find that deeply satisfying.

strahd/ff615843e4d63811.text: The house is yours tonight. Do not let me keep you.

szoldar/0c1e4ef01455c0e1.text: Szoldar Szoldarovich. Hunter. That's my boy Yevgeni, who is meant to be mending his bowstring and is instead staring at you. Sit, if you're the strangers everyone's been not talking about.

szoldar/1167cebc8a21eb0b.text: Dusk, at the landing. I'll be on the rise with the bow, pointed the right way. You have my word, which you've already had to buy once.

szoldar/3eb47df87e8da1fd.text: Go, then. I'll drink here, where it's warm, and the castle can count its wolves itself.

szoldar/5bab45feea1f7cbc.text: Who told you that? ...Yevgeni. Of course.

szoldar/60d5854027b83f3c.text: I can find him. I can't kill him; not with the boy. You can, by the look of you. We split it down the middle.

szoldar/68d2d3eddd7d4b47.text: Urwin says a great deal for a man who pours drinks. He's right, though.

szoldar/776cf5873d9079bd.text: The wolf, then. God help me. If the castle asks, the wolf ate me.

szoldar/8619746701fad43c.text: The landing at Lake Zarovich, where the fisherman's shack is. Dusk, any day you like; he comes down to drink when the light goes. I'll be on the rise with my bow. You stand on the shore and look like dinner.

szoldar/9fa2932783d5047a.text: Threaten me in the Baron's town with the Baron? Go and tell him. He'll put you both in the stocks for spreading gloom.

szoldar/b6755399b75f1974.text: The Baron pays a copper an ear for wolves. He pays three hundred gold for one wolf in particular. Old Greytooth. Big as a horse, grey to the gums, and he's had two shepherds and the lakeshore goats since spring.

szoldar/b71dbc2d32729bed.text: Three hundred gold and an empty purse from Arrigal. The boy says that's a good trade. The boy's soft. He's also right.

szoldar/bf1e58cf4b907e6d.text: Yes. Arrigal pays. A purse for every strong stranger I bring to the lake at dusk, and the wolf does the rest, and the castle learns what you're made of. You think I had a choice? You think anybody in this valley has a choice?

szoldar/d735fbc1f0bd47ec.text: Dusk. The landing. Don't keep him waiting; he isn't patient, and nor am I.

tamsin_tealeaf/04b0e6cca8e5330e.text: I knew it. I knew you liked him.

tamsin_tealeaf/063a160f89bddceb.text: They were shouting at each other for an hour. I think that's the happiest I've seen anyone in this valley.

tamsin_tealeaf/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

tamsin_tealeaf/0b7ea79d6e955117.text: A tower in a lake with a lamp in the window and a Vistani with a crossbow on the doorstep. That's either a love story or a siege.

tamsin_tealeaf/0beb7508f0a87fe2.text: Locks on the outside of a children's door. Whoever fitted those knew exactly what they were for.

tamsin_tealeaf/0e5b2fcc9a38705c.text: Because you'll put it right yourself, one day. Won't you?

tamsin_tealeaf/0e6449791f8235a9.text: You keep the password to the vault pinned to your coat.

tamsin_tealeaf/0fccad7ce9481828.text: A council. Arguing about lamp oil. Out loud. I think that might be the happiest thing I've seen in Barovia.

tamsin_tealeaf/14eb34d1e51bb283.text: I think we just got a letter.

tamsin_tealeaf/166b8dc2fc9ced73.text: Nobody's eating anybody. That's a promise, and I'm very good at promises.

tamsin_tealeaf/1ff6886be66073b8.text: So Berez didn't kill the girl. The nanny did. And the whole village went under for it.

tamsin_tealeaf/20b68775a28dfac8.text: Odd coin, she said. I like odd coin.

tamsin_tealeaf/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

tamsin_tealeaf/27f7a1b10f9c7a74.text: The women in the village tavern were counting us. Heads, blades, purses. I knew it.

tamsin_tealeaf/2be6f021cd2b7ee7.text: Kept it where, exactly? Purely professional interest.

tamsin_tealeaf/2d861e6639fc8351.text: We're keeping a vampire hunter's secret, in a valley where the vampire reads everyone's letters.

tamsin_tealeaf/33228c2a00300ee9.text: Urwin Martikov said those same words at the Blue Water Inn. With the same face, too.

tamsin_tealeaf/35e971d20f303ef0.text: Stanimir's story. The bride and the brother. He's the brother who died.

tamsin_tealeaf/38ba9e9ca3eb7177.text: No wine coming from the vineyard, no word from the vintner. In Barovia, that's not a supply problem. That's a story nobody's finished telling.

tamsin_tealeaf/4092e31b920290f8.text: So we're siding with the priest, the innkeeper, and everyone who isn't in charge?

tamsin_tealeaf/4200c477f38f25fa.text: That much? For one potion? I've stolen less. In theory. Hypothetically. Never mind.

tamsin_tealeaf/4264125c64784793.text: Home. You mean the burgomaster's house. You mean Ireena.

tamsin_tealeaf/42ae4b37bcf47247.text: She means the locket. The woman in the locket. Doesn't she?

tamsin_tealeaf/4363dcd0014be1b6.text: What a lovely, sturdy counter. Very... sturdy.

tamsin_tealeaf/45dc84869bec8fd2.text: Not bread? What does "not bread" smell like?

tamsin_tealeaf/4a446a650340d322.text: There's a raven on the roof again. It's the same one. I'm sure it's the same one.

tamsin_tealeaf/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

tamsin_tealeaf/4f55ded5d7f571b3.text: He offered me a book. Free. Nobody gives you a book for free. Not even in a library. Especially not in a library.

tamsin_tealeaf/522302aa0765cf5d.text: She said one of us is going to lie to the man in the castle, and he's going to like it.

tamsin_tealeaf/54e8017e906daaaf.text: Something a hag won't touch. I want it already.

tamsin_tealeaf/552ba17bfe031130.text: She pinched my cheek. Like she was checking a melon. Like she was checking a melon for later.

tamsin_tealeaf/59006e8846030289.text: That's the better half to keep, honestly.

tamsin_tealeaf/5bb8440a241c388d.text: Hello. We're very glad you're not drowned.

tamsin_tealeaf/5cd67e6dd2f9ab19.text: The tavern in the village of Barovia is out too. The barkeep said the deliveries had stopped.

tamsin_tealeaf/5d1af1ad60916c9e.text: Hinges on the inside. Whoever built this didn't want to be followed.

tamsin_tealeaf/5d7afe5a8402b450.text: We're Festival Marshals. For life. Every week.

tamsin_tealeaf/64bc930b6f3b9b81.text: You were the raven. On the road. You walked beside us for a mile.

tamsin_tealeaf/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

tamsin_tealeaf/6ebff3aaf066c14d.text: How long ago was this painted? And how are they still that age outside?

tamsin_tealeaf/7256304ec44aef5e.text: I keep thinking about the eyes one. Not to take it. Just thinking about it.

tamsin_tealeaf/74d924461aec3a2e.text: "Nothing comes down." They kept that sign up for centuries. And we've just opened the gate.

tamsin_tealeaf/7662363db22bfb6c.text: At the falls she remembered a wall and a gorge. This is the same look. The same distance in it.

tamsin_tealeaf/76b962aad4c8cd23.text: I'd fit in that dumbwaiter, you know.

tamsin_tealeaf/79bc41f2ac220adb.text: Stanimir's story by the fire had a prince, a brother and a bride. It left out the box.

tamsin_tealeaf/7a84780e0bcdd418.text: The one she took a dream from. Do you know what it was?

tamsin_tealeaf/7bcd41f3c329c2ce.text: It's warm. It's warm like a hand is warm. I don't love that.

tamsin_tealeaf/8132725c1725869e.text: Does it do anything? Heal? Bless?

tamsin_tealeaf/830239a393a1a16b.text: Every Vistani wagon in Barovia is our wagon now. Do you think that includes the cooking?

tamsin_tealeaf/830cd608888fe7aa.text: Raven-eyed innkeeper in Vallaki. She meant Urwin, didn't she? The whole family's birds, I'd bet.

tamsin_tealeaf/83115adafc2d5fef.text: The crow's fresh. Somebody keeps replacing it.

tamsin_tealeaf/83146f35ef731846.text: That's what every dog says about the man with the leash.

tamsin_tealeaf/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

tamsin_tealeaf/840ca66572103c92.text: She's looking at me like a ham again.

tamsin_tealeaf/8417d0709c85d41f.text: Alcoves full of other people's keepsakes. The cult robbed its dead and kept the pieces like relics. I'm not taking any of those. Not those.

tamsin_tealeaf/866688ce722aff99.text: Borrowing. This is borrowing. We'll bring it back. Probably.

tamsin_tealeaf/8b35fb6cb5026e2e.text: She's looking at me the way my aunt looks at a ham.

tamsin_tealeaf/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

tamsin_tealeaf/8f73c688564aa3aa.text: Bells don't ring underwater. Do they? They shouldn't.

tamsin_tealeaf/8fe094e58cfa5972.text: Sweet dreams, Offalia. Honestly meant. Mostly.

tamsin_tealeaf/905235e0915e192c.text: I said I'd fit. I didn't say I'd go. ...I might go.

tamsin_tealeaf/91d69a2ae21332f6.text: He had a saddled horse by his wagon. Night and day. Who keeps a saddled horse for nothing?

tamsin_tealeaf/932cb5a5eeaae6fb.text: First real wine in this whole valley, and we're the reason. I'm going to be insufferable about this.

tamsin_tealeaf/9373ac437d72d23b.text: Does it... hurt? Being on a wall?

tamsin_tealeaf/9a78980226254e5c.text: Because he was bored. We're the entertainment. I've had worse jobs. Not many.

tamsin_tealeaf/9b560c7ced879577.text: Somebody out here hunts wolves for a living, and hunts them well.

tamsin_tealeaf/9cf72c580ee51e0a.text: I can smile. I'm smiling now. Look.

tamsin_tealeaf/9d001c491e75b13d.text: Oh, that's beautiful. Nobody ever checks the jar that tells you not to.

tamsin_tealeaf/9da1f716315e2888.text: That's the nicest thing anyone's said about me in this whole valley.

tamsin_tealeaf/9f114331655b9d50.text: Could the books say once and a half?

tamsin_tealeaf/a42490e6c47bae4f.text: Put me down as the handsome one.

tamsin_tealeaf/a53db035d004680c.text: That raven nodded at us. A bird nodded. And then it flew off toward the vineyards like it wanted us to follow.

tamsin_tealeaf/a61bb7cff4233e60.text: Ireena. The man in the water. Do you want to talk about it?

tamsin_tealeaf/a67404ba152a29f9.text: I could teach them a coin trick. Purely for morale.

tamsin_tealeaf/a8936679b47340aa.text: Hello again. You're much drier than last time.

tamsin_tealeaf/a9b0874d94de6807.text: Whatever you told the old woman, you don't have to tell us. But you could. If you wanted.

tamsin_tealeaf/ab04309e119ba554.text: I don't think it's that kind of prophecy.

tamsin_tealeaf/abc4372830a5770e.text: Paper says it's ours if we want it. Paper says a lot of things.

tamsin_tealeaf/b1a07ba7f4c29eaf.text: We'll find it for you. There's a wall upstairs with hundreds on it.

tamsin_tealeaf/b78eec077623c945.text: Do you think their mother will buy pastries again?

tamsin_tealeaf/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.

tamsin_tealeaf/bb49ff6e54aa8dd4.text: That's Stanimir's story. The prince, and the bride, and the wall.

tamsin_tealeaf/bfbb254312389c3a.text: Or he's coming back for the casks.

tamsin_tealeaf/c0c6c3339380e63d.text: We drowned a sun. I've never said that sentence before. I don't think anyone has.

tamsin_tealeaf/c3a174b770ef27f6.text: I miss the eyes one a little.

tamsin_tealeaf/c5680a4a80e281b4.text: They didn't, though. You've still got your boots.

tamsin_tealeaf/ca93628aa7fa6cc6.text: Did you see the boy? Shouting his own name down the well. I want to do that.

tamsin_tealeaf/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

tamsin_tealeaf/ccc08da381838727.text: Those weren't monsters. They were people he'd been practising on.

tamsin_tealeaf/d0202b8dcb105b15.text: The Belviews repeat everything you say. Everything. I said "hello" and got it back in my own voice from six directions.

tamsin_tealeaf/d1a1e9b81b1cc6ba.text: Hello there. No, we're not your mother. We're the next best thing. Probably.

tamsin_tealeaf/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

tamsin_tealeaf/d2ac8841cfa07bab.text: Maybe you're just good at stairs.

tamsin_tealeaf/d3ebdff0573871cf.text: Would you... would you like to come down to Krezk, one day?

tamsin_tealeaf/d547f13df0c28ded.text: I'd have said it on the first day. I say everything on the first day.

tamsin_tealeaf/da75156af2725def.text: A whole lake and not one fish in a year. Where do fish go? Do they have somewhere better?

tamsin_tealeaf/dab311e7f7ced9d5.text: Remembered. It was a very good lock, though.

tamsin_tealeaf/dae27c6ee4d82a91.text: Maybe nobody. Maybe that's the point. You go anyway.

tamsin_tealeaf/df2192dcf7d936a8.text: I'd like the recipe. I'd like the recipe very much.

tamsin_tealeaf/e19c29ac632ce7f5.text: A forty-foot statue of the man in the castle, made of mud. Does he know? Do you think he's flattered?

tamsin_tealeaf/e3c2916f4cc8954e.text: Walking up walls is a terrible idea, and I'd use it every night of my life.

tamsin_tealeaf/e7655b467249c8e9.text: A windmill with the sails tied down, and the chimney going full blast. What's it grinding, if the wind isn't turning it?

tamsin_tealeaf/efd7e3912b74c886.text: I like Sir Godfrey. He's the only dead person in Barovia who's apologised to me.

tamsin_tealeaf/f1459783b58f62e0.text: The locket. It's her. It's always been her. And that's him, the one she was meant to marry.

tamsin_tealeaf/f1823e4a81c15188.text: I was hoping you could tell me. She's been calling my name in my sleep for three months.

tamsin_tealeaf/f394e15b0ac1b37e.text: For what it's worth, I'd have stayed in bed too. I'd have stayed in bed for a week.

tamsin_tealeaf/f587a723d18c831e.text: I'm going to start leaving out bread for every bird in this country.

tamsin_tealeaf/f6441e489c6441c7.text: So that's who the Vistani tell their stories to.

tamsin_tealeaf/f711a570edb4d33e.text: Did one of them just wink at me?

tamsin_tealeaf/fae6304d53cbafbf.text: Locks that work! That's the best news I've had since the mist.

tamsin_tealeaf/fb4f214668abd926.text: No keyhole. I take that personally.

tamsin_tealeaf/fe7f4ccd567f4721.text: We're just going to leave the coffin there? In the road? All right.

teodor/028dc4837d57ab3e.text: I'll knock, now and then. You needn't answer, my heart.

teodor/0a7577f15cb28990.text: Before I forget, and I have been forgetting things: the grave Mihail dug for me, by the east wall. I filled it with what I couldn't give back. Purses off the road, mostly, from people I reached too late.

teodor/0cd67ae371a93130.text: My master wants a door in this village. Not broken: opened, from the inside, by somebody who asks him in. One door in, and he can walk to any door he likes. The burgomaster's, for instance, and the girl behind it.

teodor/0e942643d1cab24d.text: And a shield. A traveller carried it all the way from the mists, and it didn't help him. It might help you.

teodor/133de77b10aee055.text: Teodor Cozma, cooper, of this village, formerly. Forgive me for not coming in. It isn't that I don't want to.

teodor/27cef8b276a2c9ed.text: I went to the crossroads for a barrel, and a gentleman in a carriage offered me a lift home. I said yes. That's all it takes, in this valley: one yes.

teodor/3070341980d9fa8e.text: Yes. I thought one of you might. You've the look of people who've walked a long way and would like something to show for it.

teodor/327be77e4f1e1c93.text: To tell her the news. And to stand here.

teodor/457576c75f7e2b1c.text: He did. And he keeps me, the way you keep a dog you haven't decided to drown yet.

teodor/561c02d371f7cc4a.text: It's coming up. I can feel it in my teeth, like frost.

teodor/567b8b47de407d02.text: They're very rude, wolves, and nobody misses them. I can't recommend the flavour.

teodor/6414cdaa02c62bb9.text: You'll have noticed the dead walk this village after the second bell. Perhaps you noticed they never scratch at this shutter. They know whose door it is. So does everything else that walks at night.

teodor/827142fa63c3df44.text: The grave Mihail dug for me. Look in it. I filled it with what I couldn't give back.

teodor/8fcc74d0c66e17b6.text: Dead. Hungry. Polite. In that order, most nights, though I work hard to keep the third one at the front.

teodor/9386a6ff00bf934a.text: At your backs? I've stood politely at the back for three winters. Very well. One more night of it.

teodor/afabfaf3d66aa6c0.text: Good evening, my heart. You have company. Good evening to your company.

teodor/b08be85393a6981e.text: He'll know I failed, my heart. That's rather the point. I came to say goodbye.

teodor/b65a79ff034fc2d9.text: I'll be warm. It's been three winters.

teodor/c956985c40ad9290.text: As you like. I'll be at the churchyard wall, being no help at all. I've become quite good at it.

teodor/e4e1e588b274377e.text: Ileana. The sun's coming. I'd like to see one more, if you'll stand with me while I do.

teodor/ecab052bafb1370d.text: I haven't had anyone at my back since the cooperage. Mind the bats; they bite low. And if I go for a throat tonight, it will be one of theirs. You have my word, for what a dead man's word is worth.

teodor/f39fd24305e037a7.text: It was never the garlic, my heart. You never once hung it up.

teodor/f6abc76ed358dcda.text: I won't fight you in front of her. But hear me first, because there isn't much night left, and none of it is mine.

teodor/fee1c59e0538c0fe.text: The woods, then. The wolves will be pleased; they've missed me.

teodor/ff83ef19908b28ec.text: He gave me three winters to get Ileana to ask. Tonight he sent word that he's done waiting. If I don't bring him a door by morning, he'll send someone who doesn't knock.

the_grandsire/49a6d5ba29486433.text: (In a voice like a grave being dug.) The runt. Mine. Mine by the moon, mine by the bite. Give him back to the pack.

the_grandsire/4d31f93a5719bee3.text: Give me the runt and the pack takes no more Krezk children. Not one. Not for as long as I hold the pack. You have my word. Wolves keep their word. It's men who don't.

the_grandsire/4d56336f7c396b05.text: (It sniffs the air, and its lips come back from its teeth.) What have you done to him. What have you done to my runt.

the_grandsire/97739e849b76c795.text: Then the pack will have him back over your bones.

thistle/01e81a8f5565a344.text: You keep breaking the second one.

thistle/031048f8aa383ff9.text: Hounds that never lose a scent. In my trade that's not a gift. It's a curse on a leash.

thistle/032a1e85fd9e4b1d.text: Grandda's dogs never heel for strangers. Never. I did.

thistle/03528000bc23c381.text: Sunbeam. Scared of the dark. Here, of all places.

thistle/039938d209fe2350.text: No. Daft's when you stop wanting things.

thistle/040ac416f4519389.text: Big. Carry me. My feet are tired.

thistle/0440c24ab38aaedf.text: We told him. He'll go for her now. Good. She eats babies.

thistle/044c09864f30eed5.text: Your god's like a deer, Sunbeam. You go quiet and still and wait, and they come out. Grandda says.

thistle/062744b993b2b4ae.text: My master died before my last lesson. I asked him what it was and he said it was in a letter I'm not allowed to read. I make jokes all day so nobody notices I'm not finished.

thistle/07c50e0bb377cbcf.text: She said he had teeth already. Grandda says you can tell a biter from the first day.

thistle/0879c5aacfbcc336.text: Welcome, Sir Godfrey! I'm Thistle. Don't forget it. I'll check.

thistle/088f7dc7d4572816.text: Their mam sold them. Her own pups.

thistle/08b5dd4658a38d71.text: You. Arm-wrestle. Now. Big's asleep and I need to win something.

thistle/09eae08ceaec7ab0.text: Look at it! Every farm in the valley can see that. Somebody's opening a shutter right now. Bet my boots.

thistle/0b2b60822a72b1e3.text: "To whoever keeps this house after me. Tomorrow I take the bell-ringers, the gravediggers and the two old soldiers who still remember how, and we go up the road to his door."

thistle/0c7d035a20936822.text: Grandda says never take a hungry thing's word. Hungry things say anything.

thistle/0ec7672f477170b4.text: Crows hold them too. Grandda's crow sulked at me a whole winter.

thistle/0fc132954f8fe905.text: Whole village shut up tight. In the daytime. Smells like fear and cabbage.

thistle/103b64c808d1f3e9.text: It's for Grandda. For when we go to Krezk. He likes things with feathers. He'll pretend he doesn't.

thistle/10fa577879aeeb76.text: You smell like a dog, Grandda. You smell like a wet dog.

thistle/11e734f643ae8632.text: Rematch. Now. To the dead tree and back. In the dark.

thistle/1215e74a60b33ed3.text: Draw. It was a draw. He's lying if he says different.

thistle/1384d959e4e7eb11.text: Grandda says rocks endure too. Never met anybody who wanted to be a rock.

thistle/13c4948055ab1de5.text: You did a handstand on the edge.

thistle/184df692ccff4fa0.text: Grandda says a wolf that walks like a man is two kinds of trouble and one kind of sad. You're the trouble kind. I've got a pack. Mine don't eat kids.

thistle/187826536981ea70.text: Why are you so happy about a rotten apricot?

thistle/19ad805802ef92ea.text: That's them. The road ones. Same wolf. That paint's older than Grandda.

thistle/19b17a6d8251cb56.text: Bye, Toma! Bye, Ilka! Whistle like this if anyone bothers you!

thistle/19b34938f25e4b80.text: SUNBEAM! Told you! Fingers in, tongue back, push!

thistle/19b64c988684e61a.text: He was hurt. He was hurt bad. And he still stopped to cut me a blaze.

thistle/1a499c45d7a685be.text: Don't. Don't touch him. Not you lot. Not the way you've been.

thistle/1aa0a4745cbb31c1.text: Right. Read it. I can do that. I'll read it tonight. I'll read it tomorrow. I'll definitely read it.

thistle/1bc0866db6c23e07.text: Never been outside? Then she walks to the prettiest thing she sees. And the castle's pretty. Bark and bones.

thistle/1dd1ff2f41301ff4.text: Then I'll carry it. I've carried it this far.

thistle/1f0de559d14676c6.text: Big room full of gold, and he never spends any. What's it for? You can't eat gold.

thistle/1fb6626db9c59e7b.text: They put the box down and walked off into the fields. Like they were going home.

thistle/21ab08aff30abd5b.text: Same face she had at the falls. Like she's gone a long way off.

thistle/23f0e307fe040ea9.text: The locket. I'm good, but I'm not that good. Nobody leaves a coach that easy to rob. I think somebody put it where my hand would find it, so I'd carry it here.

thistle/27f748dd83e1c4e9.text: Course we will. You're mine now. Both of you.

thistle/2ce4cb4059e16f7d.text: You let me. Don't let me. Grandda never let me, not once. That's how I knew he thought I was real.

thistle/2e917bcfc201dde2.text: Four hundred years. Master Sorrel always did take his time with the post.

thistle/306beec52eafb50c.text: Thinking about the word. On the tree. Run.

thistle/3320c1b10aa660a6.text: Yours. I know your tracks now. I'd know them anywhere.

thistle/34c77b1cab605ddf.text: The big soft one from the shop? He gave me a biscuit. He's good. He smells like flour and sad.

thistle/34da2d2b37748f4a.text: A wife, stitched out of dead girls, to make him gentle. Grandda tried that with a mean dog. Got it a friend.

thistle/363582f679211e1d.text: GRANDDA! That's his! That's his mark!

thistle/384fb07f7d699ee9.text: No high places. No still water. Easy. I'll watch her feet.

thistle/393eea79ee9957fc.text: Not your pack tonight. Maybe not tomorrow.

thistle/3a066bcc41e85bbb.text: I like towns. Bit. Beds. The little cakes. People singing in the big room at the inn. And I don't fit in them, and I don't fit in the woods any more either. I don't fit anywhere.

thistle/3a692c0ebc129222.text: I know. I want to win again. It was good.

thistle/3b26a3551172cdb5.text: Tracks this big. Last wolf this big took Grandda's hounds. He went after it.

thistle/3b2e8d5e52899f69.text: "Cared for." That's a lie. I can smell a lie on paper.

thistle/3b867430406b8a99.text: Raised by a trapper and two hounds. And a crow. The crow did most of it.

thistle/3ba7d22e9bbf0232.text: No. I'm a wolf. Wolves heel once, maybe. Then they bite the hand.

thistle/3df370c1032ee8a7.text: Go on. Run. No more cages. Run till you can't see the walls.

thistle/42574131dfe30c08.text: Fen. Fen Burley. Not my real grandda; he found me in a fox's den when I was this big. Said the vixen didn't want me and he didn't either, but somebody had to.

thistle/4562c9afc5965b36.text: A year old. Maybe more. Clean cuts, right hand, not in a hurry. He was fine here. He was following something big and he was fine.

thistle/45cdb9bd736a264f.text: My dad sent the devil away from our gate. Told him we'd manage. I went after him down the lane and signed behind Dad's back. I came home and said the orchard came back on its own. He went to temple and gave thanks for it. I've been lying to him for two years.

thistle/45d2da253af31a9c.text: I'd rather cook than cast. I always would. I learned magic so people would sit with me, and I'm good at it, and I'd still rather be in a kitchen. That's a terrible thing for a wizard to say.

thistle/45e6c424a573496e.text: He isn't here. I know. That is what faith is for. You need none; you are right here. That is how I know you are not him.

thistle/46392174d30fe717.text: I'll find him. I can track a moth across a frozen lake. I'll find him.
