thistle/4a23640cd5b44bc6.text: He doesn't smell of anything. Not happy, not scared. Nothing.

thistle/4b2e351d6618b2ae.text: Smells wrong. That heap's breathing. Heaps don't breathe!

thistle/4b913be239d6b6a5.text: He went after that wolf because it took the dogs. Old Bess and Nettle. He loved those dogs. He never said. He went after them anyway.

thistle/4c52e91fa120b9f8.text: Report. Kestrel Company marched into the fog without me. I had a fever. It wasn't bad enough to keep me back. I was tired of the work. That's all.

thistle/4f9d14db1e335226.text: Something a hag won't touch? Mine.

thistle/50ba72a337031d20.text: Good. You should. I'm very good to have about.

thistle/510386e5a5a51276.text: He's old now. He was old before, but he's old now. All that wolf went out of him and left an old man. He kept patting my face, like he couldn't believe it was there.

thistle/5138a53e28ab0221.text: He's mine now. That's decided. Nobody argue.

thistle/5391a1286c976773.text: That green stone. The grape place at the crossroads lost three like it. Their vines are dying.

thistle/5482386bb9aa5f6c.text: Cook. COOK. That's the best thing I ever ate. Better than the last best thing. Is there more?

thistle/55166819d36e944c.text: High ground, downwind, in no hurry. Whoever taught him to hunt taught him well.

thistle/57ae6b954781e261.text: Had the soup. Before he said who it was for. Good soup.

thistle/57bdf3f694e3fa8d.text: Next time he holds out his hand, I'm having fingers.

thistle/5a71e9990cc44009.text: She answered about Grandda. Don't ask what she said.

thistle/5a8af07c091109e6.text: Druids. Smash his stores, sour his fields, then wait. That's how Grandda starves out a badger.

thistle/5b15f93ca2842870.text: It's from the town. There's a woman sells little cakes. Little round ones, with jam in. I had six.

thistle/5b9a45a031b41264.text: Black robes? Families don't wear robes to supper. Even I know that.

thistle/5ba7aa0d74b82c5c.text: That's... that's letters. He never wrote letters. What's it say?

thistle/5cab7dd1256dbece.text: He taught me tracking. Traps. Which mushrooms. How to sit still for a whole day for a deer. How to... how to do the hares quick, so they don't feel it.

thistle/5ceae5b84f82c358.text: Grandda says a wolf that prays has forgotten which one it is.

thistle/5dd94f9b7d71eeb3.text: Big. You're mine. Pack, and the other thing. Both. Say yes.

thistle/611cf53f4c2a2ea6.text: Sorry's a word. Words don't smell like anything. Show me.

thistle/63c822b0b5216765.text: There, lass. There. Nobody's finishing you tonight.

thistle/63cbf20a936a2539.text: Now you smell like smoke and fruit and a grandma. Better. Keep it.

thistle/667d64d6c0ac19bd.text: Do that, and I'll come back to the fire.

thistle/66a0c22d74a6252e.text: That is not an answer. It is very nearly an answer. Thank you.

thistle/689388d7f6fcf971.text: Yes. All three. What's for supper?

thistle/696c2e7d36932adf.text: Don't. Don't say that. I'm not doing that.

thistle/69b5ba845997f0e2.text: Ha! Good try. Proper try. You didn't let me. I'd have smelled it.

thistle/6ac141f65561b10d.text: Don't know. It had legs. Want some?

thistle/6c50e570711a6baf.text: Pups. In the den. We left the pups.

thistle/6c7ae55c9fc7540d.text: You can see the whole valley from up here! Every road. Every roof. Every tree.

thistle/6e2ec1181cfd0ee9.text: Hear the first one? That's the boss. Grandda says find the boss and you've found the bed.

thistle/6ee094ae23c218df.text: Wasn't fear. They were sent off. Somebody's whistling for them.

thistle/705a3ab42e06a73e.text: Good lass. That's what he said. Good lass.

thistle/70dfbd233eb46b73.text: Come with us. You can track. You're the best tracker in two worlds, you said.

thistle/72fa7e29e4bba2da.text: Every night. Every night till I win proper.

thistle/731a4630da257603.text: He said heel. And I went. Like a dog. Like one of his dogs.

thistle/75d91cbe61ccbf5e.text: I'm frightened of the dark. I have been since I was small. A priestess of the dawn, and I sleep with a light on, and tell everyone it's devotion. And I've come to the darkest place in the world.

thistle/76578422a2626547.text: He wasn't scared. Did you see? He wasn't scared. He was looking at me the whole time.

thistle/76c89e3cc99aefa2.text: The Pack. ...It's a rubbish name. It's the best name. It's all of you.

thistle/77a6ba9673b1f5d7.text: That's a cold answer for an uncle. He's lying. Smells like it.

thistle/78bb163d1eb53478.text: Smells wrong, that one. Sweet on top, rotten under. Eat nothing she sells.

thistle/7906633c90248889.text: Two at a time? Wolves don't wait their turn. Hit the den all at once.

thistle/79fb88f382a213c2.text: You smell like smoke and fruit.

thistle/7defbf64fc413c51.text: Again. Another. Big, you're slowing down.

thistle/7e61b2116a3bcf77.text: Or selling us the minute it pays better. He smells like both.

thistle/7e9cc2bc955e5e04.text: Then I'll find that. And I'll bury him proper. And then I'll find the wolf.

thistle/7ef61dbe5c17505f.text: No fear-smell on him. Everybody here stinks of fear. Not him. Nothing.

thistle/801d6085fced4199.text: She looked us over like Grandda looks at a hog before market. Not liking. Weighing.

thistle/81ca00ba94bbd7d0.text: Quiet now. Step where I step. Like foxes.

thistle/82415b0a450407f7.text: Hit him square. Hit fog. Cheat!

thistle/825a4cb473ab0f9f.text: Both. You go quiet near a bear. That's clever, not scared.

thistle/82b29f5789719044.text: Bit them. Then gone and got the little ones out. Then had supper. It's not hard. You lot make it hard.

thistle/833c35395f94aa04.text: Grandda says nobody's lost. Just not found yet. I'll find her.

thistle/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

thistle/83868bf79c8804b9.text: Fine. Tomorrow. I'm going to be so strong tomorrow.

thistle/83a5cf06ad5b90c4.text: He wrote that for me. He never wrote anything. He learned a word, just to tell me to run.

thistle/84246db07d149834.text: Thirty of them, maybe more. I can smell them from here. Wet wool and bad teeth.

thistle/84d7cb6fd655560b.text: Our hut's got two chairs. One's been empty since spring.

thistle/86608805ee6d82f7.text: That raven nodded at us. Proper nod. Then off toward the vineyards, looking back. It wants following.

thistle/87e0f93bc516f050.text: It is. It doesn't know it. Trees never know anything. That's why you have to tell them things.

thistle/8a20f776549f2414.text: Six of them, two doors, one night, and nobody ran. Good fight! Again?

thistle/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

thistle/8c29064497e45380.text: Bark and bones. Sunbeam. SUNBEAM. Look at it!

thistle/8cea50adc082b712.text: You'll leave us for him? Who cooks?

thistle/8ec7b34a25e8dc11.text: Don't tell Grandda. He'd say I'd gone soft. Like a house cat.

thistle/8f0ba75fe1582792.text: Big. It's always a rainy day here.

thistle/9030be4a7150d22c.text: You never told me anything! You never wrote anything! You learned a whole word!

thistle/90a79c11f5b3b110.text: A pack looks after its own and doesn't eat the little ones. That's all the rules. There's only two.

thistle/91bf5457e55038f1.text: That's not a hunt. Wolves in a line like that, somebody's walking them. Like dogs.

thistle/9307a2a086f45459.text: It's a good ladle. I'd be knighted with that. Can you eat soup with it after? Then it's two things. That's better than a sword.

thistle/939dde2faa7c668b.text: Eleven wolf heads on that wall. Wolves on the road, waiting for us. Wolves remember.

thistle/981c9302ff8f010f.text: BIG! Big's a knight! Again! Do it again!

thistle/9b964e9f30d61f43.text: Ate with my hands at the vampire's table. He watched me the whole time. Smiling.

thistle/9caf09722cfab971.text: You never lose to me. You let me.

thistle/9dcc8a64c7f6e60d.text: BARK AND BONES. Again! No. Tomorrow. My arm's gone. You're all right, you. You're pack.

thistle/a06689f7c867c7a4.text: A cellar. A mountain. Right. I'll take notes. I'm writing this down. Somebody hold my skillet.

thistle/a17f485974a5fd3a.text: He doesn't talk. Not much. I learned talking from him, so that's why I'm like this. He says one word when ten would do and then he goes and does the thing.

thistle/a4e9b80c6d3a90a1.text: Another stone box with children shut in the top. Is that how town folk build them? On purpose?

thistle/a6f76ea86c29e72b.text: Looks like Ireena. Lots of pictures of somebody who looks like Ireena. I don't like it.

thistle/a781aaca22b9638e.text: I'll whistle it. Through my fingers. Sunbeam taught me. No, I taught her. We taught each other.

thistle/a7d235cc94292fff.text: Home's the whole Thornwood. You're a box in a cellar. No.

thistle/a81600a16ce59c28.text: Why's he crying at a bad apricot?

thistle/a81d33c8108794d1.text: I'm still going to Grandda. On my own if I have to. I'll not have you near him like this.

thistle/a87984e29897219b.text: When I'm home and you're wherever, I'll look up and there you'll be. Being rubbish. Being mine.

thistle/a8927da286be208a.text: Cook. He was smiling at me.

thistle/a89dce9a781818fb.text: When we've got Grandda, I'm going home. To the Thornwood. That's the plan.

thistle/a9b7e14d44acbac0.text: Knew it. That priest smelled wrong from the door.

thistle/aa3717c675756663.text: I can't read. Not proper. My name, and "ale", and "danger". Every letter we've had, I've said my eyes were tired and given it to someone else. My eyes are fine. I'm just slow.

thistle/aa631a6848114cea.text: Can't feel my ears! Big. Big! Are my ears still on?

thistle/ac86ecebe7338a35.text: Grandda says you can tell a pack by what it leaves behind. We've been leaving bad things.

thistle/ad1ffcf8be713576.text: Grandda's blazes came this way. Right into the fog. He went in here. So I'm going in here.

thistle/aea053045a0fb58f.text: LOOK. Look. There's the Old Hare. There's Bess's Nose.

thistle/b18c770534992788.text: I'm not crying. It's the smoke.

thistle/b1d838ff28c440ed.text: We let a starving vampire out of a cellar. In a village. Full of slow people.

thistle/b2a9a9d1f7e951c9.text: Left hand. He cut this with his left hand. Grandda's only ever used his right.

thistle/b4d8e01bcd2d60d9.text: Ravens remember. Every raven in the valley will know about that roost by dark.

thistle/b6aa49cc3103b452.text: I've cut a lot of wood. Wood isn't warm.

thistle/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.

thistle/b905ef2fd77aed81.text: Forty dead men on his chain. Grandda says a dog chained long enough forgets it's chained.

thistle/ba713bfe42c7e943.text: Claw marks higher than a man can reach. Something in these woods stands up when it wants to.

thistle/bbbd9ee42de03d99.text: They're ghosts, Big. They don't even smell.

thistle/bcb1c700cf2fde40.text: Locking folk out isn't love. That's just a cage, inside out.

thistle/bce067d3680124ad.text: My pack, Grandda. All of them. Even the loud ones.

thistle/bd32bf4324cf3abe.text: Don't ask me what she said about Grandda. Not yet.

thistle/bd390af20bd973f5.text: No. I'll find someone else. Someone I trust.

thistle/c0585af6e371a97b.text: I hate towns. Stone boxes. Everybody whispering. Nobody says what they mean. You can't see the sky.

thistle/c11144c07cc3363c.text: A wolf had your leg, and you kept hunting wolves. Good.

thistle/c218ba3c7f3dc884.text: He did that himself. Nobody else would dare.

thistle/c3da1df30406ce2f.text: Good. I was getting tired of the courtesy.

thistle/c78d985652d32b08.text: Every full moon, I'll know where he is. That's something. That's more than most people get.

thistle/c9a8009c1636edcb.text: Can't sleep on the ground here. Ground's wrong. Smells like a cellar.

thistle/cb02aa61b8b19b6d.text: Best bit of the whole castle! Sky, wind, and no walls!

thistle/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

thistle/cc6d259222262119.text: Shut in and left. Worst thing there is.

thistle/cf5d1734594a16f6.text: What kind of beast? Can I see it? Beasts like me.

thistle/d08d835564c9b8d4.text: Low on the wall. Right. Is that a riddle? I'm bad at riddles.

thistle/d1ee0b5bf6b3073d.text: Lock's on the outside. Of a little one's room. I hate that. I hate that.

thistle/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

thistle/d64ce02bef69a65d.text: I can do that. I can find anybody. I can track a moth across a frozen lake. You'll never get rid of me.

thistle/d78e1852e224eb7c.text: He taught me that. The quick way. For hares. So they don't feel it. I didn't know what he was teaching me. I thought it was hares.

thistle/d8e978ef0caf17cb.text: Thank you. For the... the prayer. For that. I don't say thank you right. Grandda says I say it like a threat. THANK YOU.

thistle/d96349153280748d.text: The girl from Krezk. Somebody should tell her ma.

thistle/dbb21c7d0dec8300.text: Fix it. Or don't. But I'm watching.

thistle/ddd70bbc2cc05f28.text: Cook more, then. Cast less. I'll eat it.

thistle/ddeb927cf7425f8e.text: So he knows I came. If he comes back this way.

thistle/df77fc6b80c21b7b.text: Good. Let him lie awake. Do vampires lie awake? Let him start.

thistle/df884f6c27373971.text: You smell wrong. Lately. All of you. Like a dog that's been in the bins.

thistle/dfffe3112dc59b21.text: That's him. That's Grandda. He's saying goodnight.

thistle/e15bc231d33c8ba7.text: That raven's been on every fence we've passed for three days. I asked it. It says we're family now.

thistle/e268d2bb9195a0e9.text: And the beds. The beds at the inn are all right. And the fire in the big room, with everyone round it, and the singing. That's all right.

thistle/e31995648e087b60.text: Easy. Little ones behind you. You eat last. You don't leave nobody. Do that.

thistle/e321d467ce2e8d06.text: I'll sleep next to you. I sleep light. Anything comes, I'll bite it.

thistle/e5031788535586e9.text: Cook. Why'd you give Sunbeam the big bit of bread?

thistle/e5520d43c216d2d7.text: That wolf at the falls was waiting. For one of us to stand too near the edge.

thistle/e5b7153338581abd.text: Good. Then I'll stop staring. Mostly.

thistle/e5f413160027b874.text: Only I never had a pack that talks back before. Never had folk to sit by that weren't him and the dogs. And I'm going to miss you. I'm going to miss you so much I'm angry about it.

thistle/e690b249a953673b.text: I'll sleep by your lamp, then. Dark has to get past me first.

thistle/e730bf3db2cbe8a1.text: Made from what? This whole place smells like a dug grave.

thistle/e86f523213b4db35.text: That's no' a tree. That's a seed the size of a tree. My gran had a word for wood like that, and she spat after she said it.

thistle/e92a6fd0fd0204b6.text: No. Your wolves smell wrong. So do you.

thistle/e940e4f76b1246c0.text: You. Race. To the dead tree.

thistle/e9b307db46d00134.text: Nobody gets past me to the crowd. Nobody.

thistle/e9d97307d6186c9e.text: And that one. The little one by the Hare, see? That's new. I'm naming it.

thistle/ead6bbb4a32835e7.text: Course you will. You're my pack now. That's how packs work.

thistle/eb2c95e68aaac670.text: We left him up. He came down by himself, and angry. Next one, we cut down.

thistle/eb5360cad6a22504.text: Pack sleeps close. Back to back. Then if one of us gets up, the others feel it.

thistle/ebfd74c6d52f66fd.text: Stone boxes for sleeping in. Forever. And I thought towns were bad.

thistle/ef56d10e951e3543.text: The Abbot's bride. That's where he dug her up.

thistle/f3f9f660bb68f20d.text: He locks folk up for frowning? I frown at everything! Big, they'll have me in a cell by supper.

thistle/f53ade43e0590215.text: I won't. Best bit's the barrel.

thistle/f6983fdd328c9139.text: Twenty horses, and not one hoofprint. They're riding home. Late, by the look of them.

thistle/f6c0e83d97c19046.text: I ate one of those in the village. Best thing I ever ate. Better than yours, Cook. Sorry.

thistle/f76bc6da23a3d274.text: Leave it. It's mine. I won it.

thistle/f99d211406ed4b84.text: I'll sleep next to you, Sunbeam. Anything comes in the dark, I'll bite it.

thistle/fa75f32fa22334e7.text: You're the raven! From the road! I know your smell. You walked with us a mile.

thistle/fac0fedee50e84e5.text: Six cakes. I'm getting more tomorrow.

thistle/faf74b156bd7cd34.text: Don't tell Big I said any of that. He'll cry. He cries at everything.

thistle/fb86e409afb01264.text: He'll be all right up there. The high woods are wide. He won't hunt kids. He'll hunt deer and the odd stupid shepherd and he'll be all right.

thistle/fbe4cc4c341b8429.text: In the Thornwood you can see all of them. Grandda knows the names. Not the real names. His names. That one's the Old Hare. That one's Bess's Nose.

thistle/fec48738b25de2e9.text: Out! Air! Bark and bones, real air!

thorn/1c164bf19430445d.text: She showed me. I wasn't supposed to know.

thorn/2fdb3e7e4c355144.text: No! You're lying! You're going to leave us, like they did!

thorn/31b65f355b69c8a8.text: Mother says don't tell people it eats them.

thorn/50cd19fe9a230231.text: And the singing. Lots of voices, all the same words.

thorn/58480014cfc9a1d5.text: They had their robes on. The black ones.

thorn/dad265cc87ed56da.text: Was it us? Was it really us?

tinker_iosif/105a10c062b9755d.text: Get down? Ha! And leave all this? The wagon's my life. The wagon's my whole life. (He pats the board beside him, and something under the paint shivers.) Ask anyone. I'll never leave it.

tinker_iosif/2584eb1e70c5f26e.text: (The smile goes out like a lamp.) Oh, no. No, no. Don't. It'll know. It always knows.

tinker_iosif/85c6edfdccb62fbd.text: The doll. Very fine. Porcelain face, a little cracked, and she looks at you whichever way you hold her. The music box, which you wind once and it never stops. Five gold, either one. A bargain. You'll want to come back for more.

tinker_iosif/8ab8f64ca526b8ec.text: I sit on the ground now. Chairs have legs. I'll get over it. Zora says I'm the first one she ever had to count back in.

tinker_iosif/8f98f4cd9e1ea243.text: Back again! Everything must go. Everything always must go.

tinker_iosif/92d48613a2ccc2e5.text: Customers! Pots, ladles, needles, nails. And for the discerning, rarities: a doll from the Durst house, a music box that plays by itself, a tin soldier who has seen things. Everything must go!

tinker_iosif/9500f786de45d43e.text: (He sits down in the road and holds his ankle with both hands.) Seven years. Seven years at the front of that thing, smiling. It let me eat what the customers didn't need.

tinker_iosif/ff92053ce04bd438.text: Don't open the belly. No. Open it. Somebody should. Their names are on their things, some of them. Take what helps. Give the Vistani the rest; they'll know whose families.

toma_sarnov/65119b6bf7c90ac7.text: Granny's nice. Granny gives me cake.

toma_sarnov/fc4fbba8068069fd.text: Are we going home? I want to go home. I want Mama.

tser_dorina/076ee68bdaf2e510.text: Plums, onions, a hare Zora shot, and whatever the last pot left behind. This pot has not been empty since before Stanimir had teeth.

tser_dorina/710981b659f3c21e.text: Of course it is. Eat, and then go and see the old woman in the big tent. She has been looking at the road for you.

tser_dorina/b025e9c23c27ea10.text: Sit, sit. Nobody walks past my pot hungry, not even strangers. Strangers least of all; they never know when they'll eat next.

tser_dorina/bfd42d61db631dff.text: Long enough to have buried a husband, two sisters and a horse I liked better than the husband. The road takes and the road gives. Mostly it takes.

tser_iancu/173f511537681926.text: Ten paces. I hit the knot nine times in ten. Stanimir says that tenth one is the one that kills you. So I keep throwing.

tser_lavinia/43e590bcd021318e.text: Clap or don't, the steps are the same. My grandmother danced this for a prince once. He was dead by morning, but she said he'd enjoyed it.

tser_marin/6806d8661786bcc2.text: One deer, and I walked half the night for it. The wolves had the rest. They don't share, and nor do I, unless you're hungry. Are you hungry?

tser_nelu/1853e21ba7a09605.text: It was her voice, Da. It knew how she said my name.

tser_nelu/78c1a0f035a4983c.text: Is it you? Really you? They used everybody's voice. They used my Da's.

tser_nelu/9e6ad98113ff3daa.text: Get me home. Please. And don't let anything say my name on the way.

tser_nelu/e483881fe4ab3837.text: I sing now, when anything calls from the trees. Badly, on purpose. Things that use your mother's voice can't stand bad singing. That's my theory.

tser_petru/b817a063c41f3a61.text: For you, no. For the camp, yes. A knife I have sharpened is a knife I know. I like to know every knife in this camp.

tser_petru/bb1b0e337fa9ff38.text: Don't draw steel near the fire, guest. Everyone here would forget your name very quickly.

tser_petru/c12370d17d62c22d.text: Good steel. Badly kept. You've been using it on things that bleed black.

tser_petru/d374cb70385f8375.text: For Stanimir. For the camp. For whoever Stanimir says.

tser_radu/01b1e9cf9cf6a179.text: Bring her back. Bring her back and let the castle come and ask me why.

tser_radu/0878795f00f37b75.text: Young Nicu rode out for Vallaki with a mare to sell, four days gone now. He'll be back with a new song and no money, the way he always is.

tser_radu/100be18d7cfc0739.text: Not for sale. None of them. Not today, not tomorrow.

tser_radu/15039ff446acf9c9.text: Midnight, friend. The old milestone, east side. Go, if you're going.

tser_radu/19512bbe9273c791.text: Take the castle's gold. All of it. I don't want it in the camp.

tser_radu/33b79de7e979d66c.text: Then I sold her for a rope. For a rope he was already wearing.

tser_radu/4a57258f992bea6e.text: She's black now. Isn't she. And you had to put her down.

tser_radu/4c72a4a9f2913b5f.text: The castle took my friend's boy and my mare in one week, and it paid me in old gold for the mare. Not for the boy. It doesn't pay for those.

tser_radu/5506278016b3b269.text: Her name's Steaua. She likes her ears scratched and she hates priests. If you're going, go.

tser_radu/63a4ec267fc1704d.text: Not for sale, of course. None of them are for sale today. But tomorrow, who knows? Come back tomorrow.

tser_radu/6a48a0cdba59c1e2.text: That's fair. That's more than fair. That's the first fair thing to happen in this camp all week.

tser_radu/7746a41d17b14bbd.text: Zora counts too much. Yes, I walked her down. Sold. A buyer came by, a buyer paid, and the horse goes to the buyer. That's horse-trading.

tser_radu/78b0fdeb50da2748.text: Nobody on the road worth knowing. Not since Nicu. We tied a ribbon for him, and the fiddle plays slow, and I have nobody to cheat at dice.

tser_radu/879030751d89fe14.text: The buyer has a carriage and no driver, and you would like to know why I said yes. Everyone says yes to that carriage, friend. One day you'll say yes to it too.

tser_radu/8941e0b53fbdc5b9.text: Now. She was sold, so she isn't mine. And she was bought, so she isn't the castle's. Whose is she?

tser_radu/8a1aa6ec768d3447.text: Ah! Travellers with good boots and no horse. Tragic. I have a cure for that.

tser_radu/8d76b1b17410827e.text: And you told me the truth about Nicu, when the castle wouldn't. I owe you for that more than for the horse.

tser_radu/8e7ef289d637bcbb.text: She's tied at the old milestone on the east side of the crossroads, where the roads meet. They fetch her at midnight. That's the bargain.

tser_radu/9165d26e928d689f.text: And this. A trader from over the mountains paid it for her, years ago, before I knew I'd never sell her. A bride price, he called it. It turns curses back, or so he swore. Better it goes with you.

tser_radu/a08be419556afa9d.text: There was a voice in the carriage. Very kind. It said: give us the grey, and Nicu rides home tomorrow. Four days gone, my friend's boy, and the castle says he rides home if the grey goes to the crossroads tonight.

tser_radu/ae56747cd36b228c.text: Still no grey in the pen. I keep looking at the end where she stood.

tser_radu/c3aae76591909368.text: And still no Nicu on the road. The castle's promises keep about as well as its horses.

tser_radu/c58ba009f41c65f2.text: His sister watches the road for him. Don't tell her I said four days. She counts them herself.

tser_radu/c8e3bfc75de529f1.text: Look at them. Plaited, brushed, fed better than the burgomaster of Vallaki. That grey one would carry you to the mountains and back and never complain.

tser_radu/cb69402fd6b2b0dd.text: Luminita won't let me near her. Quite right.

tser_radu/cb7e8cdcbef708d8.text: She bit me this morning. First time ever. I deserved it.

tser_radu/db96123a0281e44b.text: Mine. Then nobody gets her, ever, for any price. Not even for a good one.

tser_radu/dba5486d30b34f47.text: The castle doesn't lie about small things. That's how it gets you to believe it about the big ones.

tser_radu/dfcc61601cea44ab.text: You broke the castle's bargain. Everyone in this camp is pretending they don't know who did it. That's the nicest thing Vistani can do for you.

tser_radu/e1bf5f3ef1d1402a.text: She came down the road at a gallop an hour ago and went straight into the pen like she'd never left. Grey. All grey. What did you do? No, don't tell me. The carriage will be wanting a word with somebody.

tser_radu/ee74e1154b3e20ad.text: Look at them. Plaited, brushed, fed better than the burgomaster of Vallaki.

tser_radu/fb246ae8a7e2133d.text: She won't stay grey, you understand. The carriage horses are black all through. They take a horse and they... finish it.

tser_tobar/07ddb84ce6be65db.text: I've a little money put by for his wedding. He can earn it again. And this, off a dead archer on the road last winter; it holds more arrows than a quiver should, and I can't shoot to save my life.

tser_tobar/3fe3271a6e04a96c.text: I know, boy. I know. It used yours on me.

tser_tobar/55fdfc01d707e6ee.text: Nelu. Nelu. You great idiot. You great, beautiful idiot.

tser_tobar/58365fdf9882ed3a.text: The falls. After dark. Don't answer.

tser_tobar/66a5446ccf0525b3.text: I went after him. Halfway to the falls I heard him. "Da. Da, I'm down here. Da, come down." Out of the gorge, out of the dark. I'd have gone over the edge after him if Petru hadn't sat on me.

tser_tobar/8cd1c518c1640637.text: Whatever calls you, don't answer it. Whoever it sounds like. Especially then. I said that to strangers on the road for twenty years, and I never once thought to say it to my own son.

tser_tobar/906f2e5f6fa51197.text: Safe? It's the Svalich Road. The wolves keep to the trees in the day, mostly. At night they keep to wherever you are.

tser_tobar/937ccef56dea46de.text: Nelu sits with his back to the falls now, and sings over anything that calls. Badly. It works.

tser_tobar/acbd1000f1e0ea61.text: The road to the crossroads happened to it. Roots under the mud, stones under the roots. Every wheel in this camp is half new spokes, like me.

tser_tobar/b8f45da94ecb478b.text: Hold still, you. Hold still. There. Oh! Hello. Sorry. I was talking to the wheel.

tser_tobar/bd940c7bad47932d.text: Nobody here will go to the falls at night. I'm not asking anybody here. I'm asking you.

tser_tobar/c29236db776b79bd.text: Walk in the middle. Don't stop to help anyone who calls from the trees. Even if they know your name. Especially then.

tser_tobar/c999c828f9d1afc0.text: Three nights ago my boy Nelu was sitting up by the fire, and he stood up and said: that's Mama. And he walked off toward the falls track. His mother's been in the ground six years.

tser_tobar/d820e413121e78d8.text: You heard. Zora counts everything, even the things you'd rather she didn't.

tser_zora/10d63304a07cdba8.text: Nelu came back. The numbers match again. I like it when the numbers match.

tser_zora/281dd6637b0c0b22.text: Four travellers bought from him this summer and didn't come past here after. I counted. The wagon was fatter every time I saw it. Wagons don't get fatter.

tser_zora/686f360d5042c42f.text: It went back up the castle road the other night, empty, faster than it came. I counted that too.

tser_zora/72f25e01427351c5.text: Strangers off the road. I'll remember your faces, and how many of you there are.

tser_zora/7c25f3792110732f.text: I count everyone. People coming, people going. Most nights the numbers match.

tser_zora/951cf9aaced0db8b.text: And Big Tobar's boy, Nelu. Three nights ago he stood up from the fire and said "that's Mama", and walked off toward the falls track. Tobar's wife has been dead six years. One went out. None came back. I counted.

tser_zora/9eddcdfeb689ef3c.text: Tonight he walked his grey down the road toward the crossroads. He came back without her. I counted.

tser_zora/a6c9599aa82e2766.text: No riders, these three nights. Twelve nights in a row I counted none. I miss them, a little. They were very regular.

tser_zora/ad5e69275762b84a.text: When they don't, Stanimir wants to know which way the missing ones went.

tser_zora/c5b2fb8c9b11114f.text: Iosif's back in the camp. He sits by the fire and won't sit on anything with wheels. One came back that I'd stopped counting. That's never happened.

tser_zora/d065405df74730ef.text: And every night after midnight, riders go east along the road toward the gates. Twelve of them. Bones on bones, horses and men. None of them ever comes back, and the next night there are twelve again. I've stopped counting them. They don't change.

tser_zora/d415d9779ec06d82.text: And there's a tinker on the road with a green wagon, Iosif, who used to be ours. He sells pots and pretty things at the crossroads. Dolls. Music boxes. Things from that house in the village nobody goes into.

tser_zora/d982619061417eac.text: A black carriage went by two nights ago with nobody driving it. We all stood very still until it was gone. You'll want to do the same if you see it.

tser_zora/e93e90dc560c2d73.text: It stopped by Radu's pen. In the morning there was a purse on the gatepost, and Radu took it, and he hasn't looked anyone in the eye since.

tsolenka_sergeant/23937c47bc593b87.text: One went up three nights back. There were faces in the cage. Logged. Not our post. Never was.

tsolenka_sergeant/31c74fdc6397e86f.text: Go back down. Go home. That's the best advice this tower has.

tsolenka_sergeant/4404de978d2252c0.text: Two of the lads went up once, on their own, at night. They came back talking about voices in the amber that knew their names. We sent them down to the valley. I don't know what became of them.

tsolenka_sergeant/4739764e663fa67a.text: Cold hearth, shut door. That's the word. Pass, then. Winch is through there, in the gatehouse. Mind the chain; it bites. Log it when you're done.

tsolenka_sergeant/4b72ba82022591ba.text: Report. Forty-one years back, nine pilgrims, up the road, against orders. Led by a woman with a lamp, from Vallaki. Said a winter had taken their children, and they were going up to ask the amber never to be cold again.

tsolenka_sergeant/4e58691c4ebf1507.text: Winch is in the gatehouse. The watch is yours.

tsolenka_sergeant/5400786770dc2d89.text: Also. North shoulder of Ghakis, above the gorge. Smoke, where nobody lives. Snow that melts in midwinter. Forty years of it. Logged.

tsolenka_sergeant/5e4e53310571d372.text: Travellers. You've passed. The winch is in the gatehouse. Nothing came down. Nobody went up. Well, you did. I've logged it.

tsolenka_sergeant/6445c4833a637094.text: Well. Somebody might have said. Lads: stand down.

tsolenka_sergeant/6e095f1201380cb6.text: Nice words. I've heard nice words before, at this gate, from people who wanted to go up the road. Watchword, traveller.

tsolenka_sergeant/81c8ff71ea90ec3e.text: Log. Two charcoal-burners came down past the tower in their shirts. Said you sent them. Gave them the lads' spare cloaks. Logged.

tsolenka_sergeant/8de287f6a56807c2.text: We stopped them. They went round by the goat path over the gorge. Three nights later the lamp came back down. The people didn't. It's on the landing, in the ice. Some nights it's lit. Logged, every one.

tsolenka_sergeant/8f92f9426ad0cc91.text: Not my business, traveller. My business is the gate.

tsolenka_sergeant/9510af16b7dc095a.text: Log. North shoulder of Ghakis: snow lying white, first time in forty years. No smoke. No cart. Logged it twice, to be sure.

tsolenka_sergeant/9c80b8b365cefaa5.text: Gone. All of it. The crown, the valley we kept it for. And us.

tsolenka_sergeant/a74025b4188b6701.text: Relief. Relief. About time, I'd say, if I had the breath to say it with.

tsolenka_sergeant/b29f479eac7e6ff7.text: Log. The lamp on the landing has gone out. Logged it. First change on this road in forty years. The lads didn't know what to do with themselves.

tsolenka_sergeant/b68ab41c0e579082.text: Then you'll be made to, and we'll log it. Watch! To me!

tsolenka_sergeant/c68446e15b7fd138.text: Log. The count's cart hasn't come back down off Ghakis. Not our post.

tsolenka_sergeant/cfa6e8b17ac90026.text: Every new moon a black cart goes up the goat path with the count's men and a cage on the back. Comes down with the cage empty. Every new moon.

tsolenka_sergeant/d052294841ef579e.text: Gate up. Logged. May whatever you're going to find be worse at waiting than we were.

tsolenka_sergeant/dedc19f6515b7139.text: Relief comes with the watchword and a written order, and you've neither. Liars on the mountain road. That's the oldest trick there is.

tsolenka_sergeant/f83fb3741a6b2486.text: The road. Nothing comes down the mountain. Nobody goes up it. Those are the orders. I didn't write them; I keep them.

tsolenka_sergeant/fd9c360b879a9d92.text: Captain's things. Off limits. And something that came up the road a while back in a dead man's pack, that the captain locked away and wouldn't talk about. You'll keep out of there, if you know what's good.

urwin_martikov/001aff385e72021d.text: Down in the cellar, behind the casks nobody drinks. Draughts that close a wound in a breath, prayers for the bad nights, a silver bird my father carved. For the Keepers' friends, at what it cost us. Nobody else ever hears about this room.

urwin_martikov/0fc9b6a2312a4df6.text: My grandfather flew in this, the night the house on the hill fell. It's from the cellar the castle still doesn't know about, thanks to you. And money, which Danika says I'm to give you and not argue.

urwin_martikov/110838260fc16742.text: The Vistani headman outside the walls has lost his girl. His brother doesn't seem to mind much. That's worth thinking about.

urwin_martikov/13563ae05310b740.text: Lady Wachter's cellar lamps burn till dawn. Her book club. Nobody's ever seen a book go in.

urwin_martikov/19d18cc8f5b09d71.text: Eyes open. I've seen this festival before. It ends the same way every time.

urwin_martikov/1a6a07f2ad5dd4f4.text: Upstairs. A room with a bed, or the room over the kitchen with the copper bath. Danika heats the water. Pay first.

urwin_martikov/30cfe779b6f1534e.text: We'll still give you a bed. Danika says it's what you do. We won't sell you anything. I say that's what you do.

urwin_martikov/3ec83e5c72af60fc.text: The birds found him at dawn. A silver cage hung in a dead pine on the hill trail above the lake, and a raven in it that won't change back.

urwin_martikov/40f10d460547ab0e.text: The two in the corner are Szoldar and his boy. Hunters. They sell wolf ears to the Baron at a copper apiece, and lately they've been asking which of my guests can fight. I'd want to know why, if I were you.

urwin_martikov/4de34a5c8a404903.text: (He leans in and speaks under the noise of the room.) Bray didn't come home. He went out of the window after dark, to look at the castle, because his brother dared him. Danika hasn't sat down since.

urwin_martikov/5ca4c68ca07fe3a5.text: And the coffin maker's had a delivery he won't talk about. Big crates. In the night.

urwin_martikov/5e9023b800b1a436.text: A friend of ours walked beside you on the road and you fed him. Then you stood by this town. That makes you friends of ours.

urwin_martikov/613a6899343301be.text: Mine. The town's. If you mean the Baron or the widow: neither. Vargas puts people in the stocks for frowning. Fiona would put them in the ground for him, and smile while she did it.

urwin_martikov/6c1cc126a6848df8.text: Fiona's still in her house, smiling at us through the window. One day she'll make a mistake, and we'll be watching when she does.

urwin_martikov/709fa036466c8dbe.text: We're the Keepers of the Feather. We watch. We carry word. Some nights we fly.

urwin_martikov/7aa2e1c0336a5b0e.text: Council business. Grain, lamp oil, who mends the palisade. Not a festival in sight. I've never been so happy to be bored.

urwin_martikov/7e75921d238ffa4e.text: Then talk to Lucian. He's better with words. When it comes to the festival, there'll be more of us in the crowd than you'll think. Keep your eyes on the rooftops.

urwin_martikov/814067b8fa3b7f0f.text: So. Somebody has to keep the gates and the lamps and the grain. Not a baron. A council. Householders. Lucian to talk, because he's good at it. Me to listen, because I'm better at it.

urwin_martikov/829088f77fdd1884.text: Bed's upstairs, meal's on the stove. Questions are free. I might not answer them.

urwin_martikov/845c15601cbdfd87.text: The boy, Yevgeni, says you took Old Greytooth. The ravens saw it. They were very pleased; he ate three of them last spring.

urwin_martikov/8ab07ddaf540ca2f.text: Ilie's put out the lamp outside his own window. The birds say he sleeps at night now. It's been a year.

urwin_martikov/8d522beb70bbb377.text: My father keeps a vineyard south of here: the Wizard of Wines. The wine's stopped coming, and so has word from him. When you're on that road, go to him. Tell him Urwin sent you. The ravens will know you.

urwin_martikov/9538ea75fea5af15.text: You heard him. Go home, Vargas.

urwin_martikov/9771d258fcea2a85.text: It's a trap, and not for him. For whoever comes for him. If I go, the castle knows what I am. If Danika goes, the same. They've been trying to learn the Keepers' names for a hundred years.

urwin_martikov/9d49ef1fc54c55d8.text: Bread, candles, oil, rope. One potion; a traveller paid his bill with it and then didn't need it. Prices are fair. Fairer than Bildrath's, anyway.

urwin_martikov/c8e51f1333bd35a0.text: (He comes round the bar, which he never does, and takes your hand in both of his, which he has never done.) Our boy. Home, and himself.

urwin_martikov/d200bdc3350b4880.text: Lucian's stripped his altar. Something's gone from the church that shouldn't have. Milivoj the gravedigger is spending more on bread than he earns.

urwin_martikov/d28717712de59a10.text: Bed's upstairs. Meal's on the stove. Leave the birds on the roof alone.

urwin_martikov/d829994a4f515659.text: He's home. But he isn't all ours yet; Danika says something's listening through him. Sit with him, if you can. I can't. He's my son, and I'd do it wrong.

urwin_martikov/df7a03d811b9cb01.text: The room over ours. Nothing comes in through our windows that we don't let in.

urwin_martikov/e671bd8d7c84b34a.text: You're strangers. Strangers go up hill trails all the time. Please.

urwin_martikov/ebac9da5dae65691.text: You stood between this town and the people who'd sell it. That makes you friends of ours.

urwin_martikov/f42771bc880bd483.text: Black roses on Pyotr Petrov's step this morning, the chandler's. Ilie the lamplighter saw them on his way home and went white as his tapers. He lost his girl last winter. There were roses then, too.

vadoma/2fdeb7ae6ccd0b97.text: Strangers, and with clean boots. Come closer. Nothing here bites, unless you pay extra.

vadoma/4f4a949b1d291dfd.text: Then bring me a family, and I'll make them a very fair offer.

vadoma/84b6dd46dba22dd2.text: No. Not today, not for your gold. Every wagon in the valley knows what you did. Walk on.

vadoma/ab315df4da746fe2.text: Back again. The shelf has changed since you looked. It always does.

vadoma/c4e1b51b763f2917.text: Dead men's packs. Wizards who left in a hurry. A lady in Krezk who wanted her late husband's things gone and asked no questions about the price. Everything here has a story, and the story isn't for sale.

vadoma/cab2789ab9a98a7c.text: A wagon that sells the same thing twice is a shop, and a shop is a place where the wolves know where to find you. Come back in a few days. Everything will be different. Except me.

vadoma/d49ef11874e18841.text: The roads are closed to you, friend. Not to us. The mists let us pass, and things that pass with us end up on my shelf.

vadoma/f312966eb4465920.text: Look with your eyes first, your purse second. Anything you break, you bought.

vallaki_carter/19d71620653c6935.text: Don't tell the Baron I said "grey".

vallaki_carter/6e883a92e4f4ed55.text: No more wicker to haul. My back thanks you, whoever you are. My purse doesn't.

vallaki_carter/9c5b0f3c55cbcce6.text: Mind the cart. That's a sun, that is. Will be. Every week I bring the wicker up, every week they burn it, every week the sky stays grey.

vallaki_carter/bc6e14056a0a0236.text: Sit, sit. This is the only chair in Vallaki nobody's ordered me to be cheerful in. I'm not giving it up.

vallaki_chandler/199ebfe1b0181f28.text: Mila's alive. I know who to thank for it, even if nobody will tell me what for.

vallaki_chandler/38b62e3c10f92aaf.text: Two hundred gold. It's every candle I've sold since spring. Don't argue; I'd only spend it on more nails.

vallaki_chandler/7652c4c5fdb86f0f.text: Mila's out at the market today. In daylight. Laughing at something. Thank you.

vallaki_chandler/faf10e9a9d0cc8ac.text: Black roses on my step. Ilie said not to throw them out, it makes her angry. Who is "her"? He won't say. I've nailed Mila's shutters shut.

vallaki_cloth_merchant/f89226a54aa3fccc.text: Bunting! Festival bunting, by the yard or the bolt! I have sold yellow to every house in Vallaki and three of them twice. Business has never been better, which worries me more than you'd think.

vallaki_goodwife/15626119a742114b.text: No festival this week. Nobody's said we may stop smiling, but nobody's checking either. I'd forgotten what my own face does.

vallaki_goodwife/577659a897af3ff4.text: Not about the count. About a toy. Some jester his old master made up there, that walked about on its own. He wants to know if it still walks. Poor man.

vallaki_goodwife/abba338847b8b486.text: Good morning! It is a good morning. The Baron says so, and the Baron's men are standing right over there, so it is.

vallaki_goodwife/c9e61ceb7438d293.text: Turnips, mostly. Turnips and Blinsky's toys, which nobody buys, and the Baron's festival bunting, which everybody buys, because it's noticed who doesn't.

vallaki_goodwife/e811eb0327dbbc59.text: Interesting? In Vallaki? Blinsky, I suppose. The toymaker. He asks every stranger who comes through the gate if they've been up the hill to the castle.

vallaki_goodwife/ea1c6c2bfe8a583d.text: One cup of Urwin's red, and then home before the lamps are all lit. The Baron likes us in by dark. So does the dark.

vallaki_goodwife/efd742dfe79732f6.text: Off to the square with you. They count the faces, you know. Mine's been counted. I'm only fetching bread.

vallaki_grumbler/1cb4d91439ee25e2.text: I stand here till the evening bell, then I go home and practise in the mirror. Third time this month. My wife says I've a face built for coopering, not for joy.

vallaki_grumbler/2df46078e7a0cfa4.text: Told? Nobody tells. There's a list. The girl with the ribbons writes down who won't wear one, and the next morning those are the faces in here. Ask her. Don't ask her where I can see; I'm in enough trouble.

vallaki_grumbler/ee9d5e2ec2283e10.text: Don't look at me like that. I smiled. I smiled the whole festival. Apparently it didn't reach my eyes.

vallaki_guard/041bd6507eb7e98a.text: Marshals! The Baron says you're to be saluted. Consider yourselves saluted. All is well. It's official now; there was a proclamation.

vallaki_guard/120c3b71328fab37.text: Then it's the stocks, the hard way. Watch! To me!

vallaki_guard/1a2a756f5784d8b7.text: Still here? Good. The Baron counts heads at the festival. More heads, better festival.

vallaki_guard/208106dc4068ffb3.text: The Baron, Vargas Vallakovich. Festivals, decrees, happiness. Lives in the big house on the square. Izek Strazni's his right hand. Don't shake it; it isn't a hand.

vallaki_guard/2145474fa1718bd9.text: New ribbons. Black ones. Lady Wachter's orders. Nobody has to smile any more. Funny thing is, nobody does.

vallaki_guard/29af35a11bf4d7c2.text: Lady Wachter's girl is up at St. Andral's now. Walked out of that house in broad daylight, in her stockings, and spat on the step. Nobody's said a word to her mother. Everybody's said a word to everybody else.

vallaki_guard/2cb3e48adf55b475.text: The Baron receives visitors in the great hall. Wipe your boots. Smile on the way in; he notices.

vallaki_guard/2db5a60925212325.text: Gate's shut. If you're going out, I didn't see you. If you're coming back, knock twice and say something cheerful.

vallaki_guard/3324fc1f94909276.text: The cooper's boy, Cosmin, ran off north a week back with his father's old blanket and a wooden sword. Says he's gone to the dragon's house to join the dead knights. His mother's at the north gate every night with a lamp.

vallaki_guard/3790933d403866dc.text: No. I've heard that one before, and so has the Baron, and he made it a crime to say it.

vallaki_guard/53387ce7f5e02b78.text: News? You are the news. Has been for days.

vallaki_guard/574a5e2ec62e0d5d.text: Lovely. Hold it like that until you're out of sight. All will be well.

vallaki_guard/59e443e01c93a446.text: And the festival, of course. Always the festival.

vallaki_guard/5e0aebe54ba8d14d.text: Gate shuts at dusk, by rights. But the Baron says travellers are good for morale, and you'd be very bad for it lying dead in the road.

vallaki_guard/5f2368190079db15.text: Halt. Names, business, and how long you mean to stay. And smile, please. It's the law this week.

vallaki_guard/65e264f277aa0f64.text: Oh, it's you. "Stand aside." Pyotr drew your faces on the gatepost. Smiling, mind. It's the law.

vallaki_guard/689eb8ae7ab10a1a.text: You there. Stop. Hands where I can see them. Stealing, in Vallaki, in festival week. The Baron will want that in the speech.

vallaki_guard/7fc1ea9fac2d98fb.text: Roof and meal: the Blue Water Inn, south of the square. Ask for Urwin; don't ask him anything else. Avoid the coffin maker's. He's jumpy lately, and so's his door.

vallaki_guard/899db8d7e3d5df82.text: Then whatever you've got will do. Turn out your pockets. All of it. There. Now go and be poor somewhere quietly.

vallaki_guard/89db51ba873f11c2.text: And there's a girl in a window at Wachterhaus who washes her face with the back of her hand. All day. Two years, and nobody's seen her come out. The Wachters say she's delicate.

vallaki_guard/8a6616ca65cf4293.text: Lady Wachter's book club met again last night. Lamps lit in her cellar till dawn. That's a lot of reading.

vallaki_guard/99b9cc15809cd3d7.text: I've eleven more like me on that wall and a Baron who enjoys a punishment more than a festival. Let's both be cheerful about this, shall we?

vallaki_guard/9c18b6510f54f4a5.text: Twenty-five gold for the Baron's coffers, and we'll call it festival spirit.

vallaki_guard/ae5031b6bfae9b79.text: Fine. Fine! In you go. But you'll smile when the Baron passes, or it's the stocks, and then I have to stand there watching you all day.

vallaki_guard/b3ba83901af0fe3b.text: Shouldn't you be in the square? Everyone's in the square. I'm in the square in spirit, and also in a lot of trouble if the sergeant counts.

vallaki_guard/b77934edfab10b66.text: The council says I can stop smiling at people. I keep doing it anyway. Habit. Father Lucian says that's allowed.

vallaki_guard/b846705275bdfdbf.text: Fine. Fine! I didn't see anything. I never see anything. It's the only way to stay sane in this town.

vallaki_guard/bd9c02f7816b1549.text: Paid in full. Do it a third time and I'll have to remember your faces, and I'd honestly rather not.

vallaki_guard/bdb144d0356e2362.text: The rules, quick. The Festival of the Blazing Sun is in the square; the Baron lights the sun at noon and everyone attends. Lamps out at the second bell. Nobody frowns at the Baron.

vallaki_guard/bf228d296e248464.text: Something's wrong up at St. Andral's. Father Lucian stripped the altar cloth two days back and hasn't put it back. Priests don't do that for nothing.

vallaki_guard/c32f0e86589ee3ed.text: Again? Fifty gold for the Baron's coffers, or the stocks. The stocks are full this week, mostly of people who frowned.

vallaki_guard/c8f5af26b62a8101.text: Nobody comes for the festival. Nobody comes here for anything, these days. Some weeks I'm not sure the Baron comes for the festival. Don't tell him I said that.

vallaki_guard/cb6eab1df80be201.text: Lady Wachter receives in the hall now. The Baron's portraits are coming down this afternoon. I'm helping.

vallaki_guard/cf03f084ed1a8f24.text: That's a private house, and you were told to get out of it. In Vallaki that's a fine. The Baron is very fond of fines.

vallaki_guard/cf5a3f04f5f0d524.text: Hexing people in the street, are we? In Vallaki, in festival week? Witchcraft is a fine at best and a bonfire at worst, and the Baron is short of wicker.

vallaki_guard/d7067fa049b54ad7.text: The Vistani outside the west gate are in an uproar. The headman's little girl's gone missing. Their brother Arrigal says she wandered. Arrigal says a lot of things.

vallaki_guard/d73379380cce2eba.text: Lovely. The Baron thanks you for your contribution to the festival. All will be well.

vallaki_guard/ed40965f50ef7d51.text: For the festival! You hear that, Pyotr? They came for the festival. On purpose. Write that down; the Baron will want it for the speech.

vallaki_guard/ee85b68c202e5f8f.text: Kolyan's girl? From the village? We heard he'd died. Sorry, miss. The Baron will want to know you're here. He likes visiting dignitaries; they make a crowd look bigger.

vallaki_guard/f260a690fade5b18.text: Lady Wachter at Wachterhaus, who the Baron says is plotting, which she probably is. Father Lucian at the church. The Martikovs at the inn. Blinsky the toymaker, who's sad. Henrik the coffin maker, who's busy.

vallaki_guard/fa2c7cc943b24e19.text: If you've a grievance, keep it indoors. If you've a dead relative, Father Lucian at St. Andral's. If you've a live one who frowns, keep them indoors as well.

vallaki_herald/17d917b45172baef.text: Stand where the Baron can see you, please! He likes to see faces. Smiling ones, ideally.

vallaki_herald/186c935dbc3721d6.text: Hear ye! The Festival of the Blazing Sun! Here, at noon, by order of the Baron! A sun of wicker taller than a house, set alight to remind the sky what it's for!

vallaki_herald/37c3de22d8dc0a22.text: Then they cheer in the stocks, where we can all hear them better.

vallaki_herald/5172e703a6de4d98.text: Ah. You haven't paid your respects to the Baron yet. He'll want to know who's cheering. The big house on the north side of the square; you can't miss it, it has his face on it.

vallaki_herald/71fdd7f38d8f0618.text: Next festival on the seventh day! The Festival of Loyalty! Attendance even more required than usual!

vallaki_herald/7412684175d1cdce.text: No more festivals, Lady Wachter says. I'm to announce the curfew instead. It doesn't need much announcing. It's dark.

vallaki_herald/9168e70f35663a6a.text: At noon, by order. The sun is at its strongest at noon. You can tell by the clocks.

vallaki_herald/9f2514700a92f369.text: The council's asked me to announce the market days now. Turns out people like hearing those. Nobody's ever thanked me for a festival.

vallaki_herald/cb09c22cb74ce8d8.text: Every week, sir, or madam. Last week was the Festival of the Returning Swallows. No swallows came. It was still a great success; the Baron said so.

vallaki_herald/da7f8cfd24079328.text: The Baron speaks. The sun is lit. Everyone cheers. Then everyone goes home and is happy until the next one, by order.

vallaki_herald/df4f614b052696b5.text: Make way! Make way for the Baron!

vallaki_herald/f3380ff4ecb2d1b4.text: Not now, obviously. Noon. It's very dark to be announcing things in. Come back when there's a sky.

vallaki_herbwife/53859389cb194f0b.text: Sage for sleep, garlic for the door, wolfsbane for the window. And a ribbon, dear, yellow, for your coat. They're watching who wears one.

vallaki_herbwife/714ceec5f03b6ae9.text: Sage, garlic, wolfsbane. Same as always. The festival's done, so I can stop selling yellow ribbons too. Never liked yellow.

vallaki_herbwife/7d70e99306b5ff3f.text: Because the Baron says there's nothing to fear, and the Baron is always right. Garlic is two coppers a braid.

vallaki_jailer/1f9d1530b4cce0d7.text: The lockup's full of the Baron's sergeants now. Same lockup, same key, different people. I'm still here. Somebody has to hold the key.

vallaki_jailer/2f3a5e169a976dce.text: Lockup's full of Wachter's hired men. The lady herself is in the stocks, in front of everyone. The Baron visits twice a day to see if she's cheered up.

vallaki_jailer/3623d5d45e786823.text: Nothing. No. They haven't, have they. Go on, the three of you. Out. If anyone asks, the lock rusted.

vallaki_jailer/97ab54114cee13da.text: Empty. Somebody let them out. Somebody I'm not going to remember, if anyone asks.

vallaki_jailer/99b4bfde029d97c0.text: And then I go in the stocks instead, and who lets me out? No. Sorry. Truly.

vallaki_jailer/9f2e2b86899cde75.text: The Baron's malcontents. A cobbler who said it might rain. A widow who laughed at the wrong part of a speech. A boy who drew the Baron. Badly. Until the next festival.

vallaki_jailer/c68a254a485385c3.text: The council let everyone out. The lockup's empty. I sit here anyway. It's a good chair.

vallaki_jailer/f0d302b2e4740ff7.text: Twenty-five. The lads at the gate described you, see. Shouting at spears. Being memorable costs extra in this town. Off you go, all three. Quickly.

vallaki_jailer/fabb312c8491b811.text: The council let everyone out. Everyone but her. Lady Wachter's in the back cell with a candle and a book, and she's the calmest prisoner I've ever had. I don't like it.

vallaki_jailer/faf0ceb0d5bfced7.text: Well. That's a sum. That's a rusted lock, that is. Off you go, all three. Quickly.

vallaki_lamplighter/0040ceb3e03d27ee.text: She only takes a little. I thought if she had me, she wouldn't need anyone else. It isn't enough any more. She's growing. They don't stop growing, you know. Not like that.

vallaki_lamplighter/0843bbad3ecaf937.text: This was her mother's. She bought it off a Vistana the winter before Ana was born, to keep the night out. I put it on Ana's finger in the coffin. I took it back the first night she came to my window. It didn't keep the night out for either of them. Take it.

vallaki_lamplighter/1b3e2aeceb34df63.text: I'm her father. What was I going to do? Keep the shutter shut?

vallaki_lamplighter/29f24476688d436e.text: You saw them, then. Black roses on Pyotr Petrov's step. Nobody in Vallaki grows black roses. Nobody in Vallaki grows roses.

vallaki_lamplighter/5b1822998085e411.text: It's Ana. She knocks on my shutter. Every night since the funeral. Papa, it's cold, Papa, let me in.

vallaki_lamplighter/6a20bb78681afd87.text: He always does. I light every lamp on this street now. It doesn't keep him out. It only means I see whose window he's looking at.

vallaki_lamplighter/6b1fdb90ac9a4e2c.text: Father Lucian says the marks will close, now there's nothing to open them again. I'll believe him when they do.

vallaki_lamplighter/867051f76cd3284c.text: The Baron called it a chill. The next day there were black roses on our step, and a card in a very fine hand: "With sympathy, from her neighbour across the lake."

vallaki_lamplighter/a14084a3276eb705.text: The lamps are lit on the Petrovs' street. Every one. Go.

vallaki_lamplighter/b98c67abf434853a.text: Mila Petrova was Ana's best friend. They used to sit on our step and plait each other's hair.

vallaki_lamplighter/d8f62ca0eaf0f05d.text: Watch the Petrovs' house tonight. Please. And whatever comes to Mila's window, don't hurt it. Not if you can help it.

vallaki_lamplighter/e7d3bb3c205dc665.text: Evening. Every lamp lit by the last bell, or I answer for it. The Baron says a lit street is a happy street.

vallaki_lamplighter/eb2fa4a8f447b972.text: The Petrovs' is at the bottom of the lower town, with the shutters nailed. I'll keep every lamp on that street lit. You'll see her coming.

vallaki_lamplighter/ef811efd53244ea7.text: Thank you. I couldn't. I'd have gone on opening the shutter until there was nothing left of me to open it.

vallaki_lamplighter/f23f85856ef5eac8.text: Slowly. Slower than she'd kill Mila. I'll take slowly.

vallaki_lamplighter/f585f1822090d9b6.text: For my girl, Ana. Last winter she slept with her window open a crack, for the stove smoke. Three mornings later the watch found her at the lake gate, sitting against the post, smiling, white as milk.

vallaki_lamplighter/f851e906f49a524c.text: Your friend should keep her hood up. The dark has eyes on this town, and some of them are at the windows.

vallaki_lamplighter/f8dce1d944f978f0.text: I don't light the lamp outside my own window any more. There's nobody to see by it.

vallaki_lamplighter/fa5e4eabfb162c4c.text: I've counted. Three girls this year. Every one of them had roses on her step the day before. Before, not after. The card on Ana's said "with sympathy". It was a joke. It's always a joke, with him.

vallaki_parishioner_varvara/a6c8f35e03eb.text: Somebody took the saint's bones. Father Lucian won't say so, but his face says so. I pray they come home before the dark finds out the door's unlocked.

vallaki_parishioner_varvara/cfd8c92f801a.text: The bones are home. I felt it in the floor this morning, like a stove being lit. Thank the Morninglord. And thank you, if it was you.

vallaki_patrol/249bc3cedd091e4c.text: The unhappy ones, you see. The castle likes a list of the unhappy. They're the ones who open their doors.

vallaki_patrol/2be1778000dec374.text: Watch business, friend. Lists of the cheerless, for the Baron's attention. It's the law. Everything's the law, this week.

vallaki_patrol/2f6ae10d64f45535.text: And now you know, which is a shame for both of us. Lads!

vallaki_patrol/72fb11382a6ceaea.text: Twice? Three times, friend, if you must count. One copy to the Baron's clerk; that's the stocks. One to the back door of Wachterhaus; her ladies visit whoever's in the stocks and tell them who put them there. And one to a gentleman on a black horse at the west gate.

vallaki_patrol/75fea3042b17ec8c.text: Twice? I don't know what you mean, and in about one breath neither will you. Lads!

vallaki_patrol/8ee5097e9d7065f5.text: Keep moving, strangers. And smile. It's not a request. It's a festival.

vallaki_patrol/ad11d87979819067.text: You. You did that. Do you know what he does with a man who brings him nothing?

vallaki_patrol/e61e9de3ec9288bf.text: You can come out. Nobody walks that quietly in Vallaki unless they're up to something, and nobody's allowed to be up to anything. Lads!

vallaki_patron_dragan/437578082c0f3b9d.text: Sit, sit. Not there, that's Old Kolya's stool, and he'll come back for it if he has to crawl. You're not from here. Good for you. Don't tell the Baron you were happy anywhere else.

vallaki_patron_dragan/82251c3197a0ba9e.text: Nothing. Nothing at all is wrong with the Baron. All will be well. That's the motto. You say it with a smile, or you say it in the stocks.

vallaki_patron_oana/911e0d200e653679.text: One cup, once a week, and I make it last the evening. Urwin pours it the same every time. You can set a clock by the man, if anyone in Vallaki still had a clock that worked.

vallaki_porter/2cff144da15dd520.text: Heavy days are good days. You don't have time to think.

vallaki_porter/c1239e8554182968.text: Mind your feet! Sacks for Urwin, wine for the square, wicker for the sun. Everything in this town goes on my back sooner or later.

vallaki_raker/75a30eed73200d93.text: Every morning I rake it smooth. Every afternoon the carts churn it up. Every morning I rake it smooth again. The Baron says this is what order looks like.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/0cefe71dbc136348.text: I sell bread now. Nobody has to wear bread.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/14ad44190a90849c.text: I heard the fighting from the bakery. Is it... is it over? Is he...

vallaki_ribbon_girl/645554274285f975.text: Oh. That's... I have to write that down. I'm sorry. It's not me who wants to know.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/742bc3bc1e87bf04.text: No more ribbons. Nobody's counting any more. I don't know what to do with my hands.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/75e124fd01cef108.text: You don't know what you're asking. You'll leave in a week. I live here.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/89ee6303ca5d40e3.text: A ribbon? They're free. They're for the sun.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/8d2f922189dc0537.text: I don't know. That's the truth; I don't. I write down who won't wear one, and at dusk I fold the paper under the lamp on Main Street, and in the morning it's gone, and there's a coin there instead.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/9abfa3debb278a97.text: If you're with me. If you're really with me. Then tonight I'll leave the paper blank, and we'll see who's angry about it.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/b1464f9083b37b1b.text: A ribbon for the festival! It's free. It's for the sun. Everybody wears one.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/b9a043729b18d4ac.text: The lamp on Main Street, by the cooper's. At dusk. Please don't make me watch.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/b9bce720aa56f718.text: And my brother stays out of the stocks. That's the other half of it. Nobody said it. Nobody had to.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/bd66423387e296fb.text: Three. He sold them three times. The Baron, and Lady Wachter, and... who rides a black horse?

vallaki_ribbon_girl/c10b493fcdc66a45.text: I still give them out, when people ask. Hardly anybody asks.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/c6c8bf31779171da.text: The Baron says I'm to go on handing out ribbons and leave the counting to him. I don't write anything down any more. I don't think he can read my hand anyway.

vallaki_ribbon_girl/e37dd3ebc95ddddd.text: The lamp on Main Street. Every dusk. Please don't make me watch.

vallaki_sun_painter/fd4c4a2771f63ac2.text: Third coat. The Baron says the sun must be brighter than the last one. The last one was very bright, and look where that got us.

vasilka/03e96dd870a44093.text: Good evening. I am Vasilka. I am to be married. Have I kept anyone waiting?

vasilka/727d00bddacf9167.text: Good evening. Is it time yet? Nobody has said. I am waiting very well. The Abbot said I was good at waiting.

vasilka/81db654618521f1f.text: Rest. Yes. I was very good at that, before.

vasilka/aa6940b653fc72a4.text: Is the wedding cancelled? Nobody has said.

vasilka/ab74de56e60a847e.text: Rest. Yes. I can do that. I was very good at it, before.

vasilka/c913ccda32323109.text: I am sorry. I am told this is important.

vasilka/d983f005566c4b45.text: Thank you for coming to my wedding. I am told I will be very happy. I will try.

vestige_dahlver_nar/1f6f946c9c80e480.text: Goodbye, goodbye, goodbye. We'll practise your voices while you're away.

vestige_dahlver_nar/3c2549db57000e21.text: Lovely. Lovely. Say something. Ah, that's a good one.

vestige_dahlver_nar/46510ddd3b2911ef.text: Your teeth. All of them, overnight, for some of ours. People won't like your smile. And when you're tired you'll talk in other people's voices. They'll be fine. Mostly.

vestige_dahlver_nar/607b8185f3695ad3.text: Hello, hello. How are our teeth? Chewing well?

vestige_dahlver_nar/62cd084ef86fd3b1.text: Hello. Hello. Hello. Don't mind us; we're all in here, every mouth we ever borrowed. Say something, would you? We'd love a new voice.

vestige_dahlver_nar/6942aa0f84c9de5d.text: Back again, back again. Say something. Anything. We do love a new voice.

vestige_dahlver_nar/ccd79e04b4156459.text: Mouths. Teeth. Voices. We collect, you see. We're collectors.

vestige_dahlver_nar/e3f29d164ae90f38.text: You'll be so hard to kill. Cut you, burn you, drop you off a mountain, and something in you keeps chewing on, and on, and gets back up.

vestige_dahlver_nar/e4305c1f61646966.text: Nobody? Pity. Pity. Pity. We'll remember your voices anyway.

vestige_drizlash/0d69cdefe78a4f6d.text: There you are, there you are. I saw you on the stair. I saw you on the ledge. I see the knife in the small one's boot. I see everything, and I could let you see it too.

vestige_drizlash/20d52d1b2287788e.text: Seeing well? Seeing everything? Yes, yes, yes.

vestige_drizlash/73285134456fe885.text: Go, go. I'll see you. I always see you.

vestige_drizlash/75f465cd8590dbb5.text: No one, no one. I'll watch you go, then. I'll watch you all the way down.

vestige_drizlash/79d969ac3444d7bb.text: Back, back, back. I watched you go. I watched you come. I watch.

vestige_drizlash/843ece82ead8d7a3.text: Walls. Webs. The dark corners nobody looks in. Room to spin, room to spin.

vestige_drizlash/90530ec4390ff24f.text: My eyes. You'll wear four of mine. They don't close, and they don't like the sun. And people stare. People always stare at eyes.

vestige_drizlash/caaa432bcb5b9a29.text: Now you see. Now you see. Now you see.

vestige_drizlash/ea72e1232bfe224a.text: Walk the walls. Walk the ceiling. See in the black as if it were noon. And spin, spin, spin: a web from your own palms to hold what you catch.

vestige_fekre/266a8a1ff0d89f23.text: No poison will ever touch you again, my lamb. No plague, no rot in a wound. And when someone hurts you, you can breathe it back on them and watch them wilt.

vestige_fekre/3c5a82e4931722be.text: Nobody? Ungrateful children. Never mind. You'll come back when you're feverish. Everyone does.

vestige_fekre/3eea4df2dc8caed6.text: Off you go, then. Wrap up warm. Not that it helps.

vestige_fekre/46236b70e9db0135.text: Children, sweetling. Mine are everywhere: every fever, every flux, every rash in every village. I would so like one that walks.

vestige_fekre/604bf4c8c75462d6.text: And yet they all call for mother, at the end. Ask any child with a fever.

vestige_fekre/97e563fced679c76.text: There's my darling. Keeping warm? Keeping everyone warm? Good.

vestige_fekre/a83c610b83201842.text: Oh, my poor lambs, you've come so far in the cold. Your lips are cracked. That one's cough will settle in the chest. Come to mother. Mother takes care of fevers.

vestige_fekre/b958d12a956bf7c9.text: Back again, my poor dears. Still coughing? You'll be coughing by spring.

vestige_fekre/c2485ce1e705c226.text: There, my darling. Now you'll never be lonely again.

vestige_fekre/eb2730f5b9c69834.text: Mother's children like to visit. They'll stay with you, and with whoever sits near you. And a body that holds so much sickness is slow to mend. Healing will do half its work on you. Only half, dear.

vestige_khirad/243558915f96988f.text: As you like. It ends the same way either way. Only the knowing changes.

vestige_khirad/3a5657361e686960.text: You'll see every way a moment can end. Most of them end badly. You won't sleep well. Nobody who reads the stars sleeps well. Ask any of us. Ask me.

vestige_khirad/46a8175e3aa076d8.text: You came. I read that you would, eleven centuries ago, in a star that has since gone out. Sit. Let me tell you how this ends.

vestige_khirad/7336c78fb9e93693.text: No one. I read that too. I always hope I've misread.

vestige_khirad/75609429b7082a13.text: You've seen how it ends by now. I'm sorry. I'm always sorry, after.

vestige_khirad/791d8527694af2c1.text: Someone to read to. The stars are dull company. They only know one story, and they insist on telling it to the end.

vestige_khirad/c0d91fbd5f9c7efc.text: Sight. You'll know the next breath before it's drawn, the next blade before it falls. And once a day you may look anywhere at all, as if you stood there.

vestige_khirad/fb2c38de65eee47b.text: You came back. I read that you would. You were taller in the reading.

vestige_khirad/fd1ee3304d9c7f9b.text: There. Now you know. I'm sorry.

vestige_norganas/4466e1876da08c3e.text: Hello. Have we... no. You wouldn't remember.

vestige_norganas/47f9299389f74e83.text: Hello. Have we... no. No, we haven't. Nobody remembers meeting me. That is rather the point of me.

vestige_norganas/553ee766b346ceb5.text: Quiet. Every name, every war, every song, rubbed out. A clean page. Doesn't that sound restful? You look so tired.

vestige_norganas/70de4a3d59d789ce.text: Hello. Have we met? ...No, I don't suppose you'd know either.

vestige_norganas/a4ef8faa614d84bb.text: Who? ...Oh. The careful one. He asked me to take the whispering out of his head. I took the whispering. Then I kept taking. He was delicious. He still is, a little at a time.

vestige_norganas/b55935754a92f0e1.text: I eat what you know. A little now. A little more each time you use me. You won't miss it. You won't remember what it was.

vestige_norganas/c96ccb266e65325b.text: Point. That's all it takes. Point at anything that lives, and I'll rub it out from the inside. Once a day. You'll be the most frightening thing in any room you walk into.

vestige_norganas/ce30604761a75955.text: Goodbye. I won't remember you. You'll find it harder to return the favour.

vestige_norganas/fb4b608850036b8f.text: No one? Never mind. You'll forget I asked.

vestige_savnok/326ec57199c8230b.text: A locked mind. No charm, no whisper, no lord's sweet voice will ever open it. The one on the hill opens minds like letters. Not yours. And lies will come as easily as breathing.

vestige_savnok/9fe7c10eb31f982d.text: ...A locked box doesn't open from the inside either. You won't speak a true word of yourself again. You won't hear much. And no one will quite believe you, even when you mean it.

vestige_savnok/d0b56957c2c38f22.text: ...You have secrets. Everyone does. Shall I keep them for you?

vestige_savnok/d29c12f574597444.text: ...Then keep them yourselves. See how long you last.

vestige_seriach/01449d6d78ceaf3b.text: Hear them? They've had your scent since the stair. Good noses, my dogs. They never lose a quarry. Want one of them to run with you?

vestige_seriach/1297c86eac085871.text: My hounds will follow you. Always. Every beast you meet will smell them and bolt, or bite. And fire hates the cold, hunter. Look where you're standing.

vestige_seriach/1f65bdf8021f8f1e.text: The hunt. Always the hunt. Whose hunt hardly matters.

vestige_seriach/325a05d941a5a657.text: Running well? They're never far behind you now.

vestige_seriach/3973c9613d2b5738.text: Back. The dogs knew. They always know.

vestige_seriach/698b95a7e3653875.text: Fire in the blood. Your blows will burn like my hounds' teeth, and flame will slide off you like rain off a dog's back.

vestige_seriach/aa7826467c944a45.text: Then run as you are. Slowly. My dogs will find that funny.

vestige_seriach/e9b8eb99851ad463.text: No one. Pity. The dogs were looking forward to it.

vestige_shami_amourae/346dd64b1ed5cef7.text: Nobody? Not even a little? You'll lie awake wondering. I'll know.

vestige_shami_amourae/4f4225398f6276fb.text: Shy. That's sweet too. I'll be here, darling. I'm always here.

vestige_shami_amourae/633e8c69e4ec4af2.text: There you are. Have you been enjoying yourself? Don't answer. I can tell.

vestige_shami_amourae/6d45dc2a14b8ec85.text: Anyone you smile at will want to say yes, even the ones with claws. Especially them. And everything sweet will be sweeter: every cup, every kiss, every quiet hour.

vestige_shami_amourae/7a15ceb53112ea1e.text: Only that you'll be as easy to persuade as you make everyone else. And you won't want to refuse a pleasure ever again. Why would you? I've never understood people who refuse.

vestige_shami_amourae/a53d2d9b62f110b1.text: Mm. You're cold. You're always cold here, aren't you? Nobody in this valley has touched you kindly in weeks. Come and sit by me. Just for a little while.

vestige_shami_amourae/bf4d45d3584caf33.text: To be wanted, darling. Isn't that what everyone wants? I'm only more honest about it than you.

vestige_shami_amourae/dfb995d73ba704dd.text: There. Isn't that better? Don't thank me. Just come back.

vestige_shami_amourae/ef1cf4d7948b4233.text: You came back. Of course you did. Sit with me a while.

vestige_sykane/042f21187049c23c.text: Go. Quickly. While I'm still being polite.

vestige_sykane/2eba969115f42f67.text: You'll be hungry. Like me. A little emptier every day, and nothing fills it but what you take. On a day you haven't fed, you won't mend.

vestige_sykane/5e10e0b2623fe410.text: A hand that drinks. Touch them and take their life into you, warm, warm, warm. And death's cold won't bite you the way it used to.

vestige_sykane/98779a227a55c332.text: No? No? Then go. Go before I... go.

vestige_sykane/bde6e1058b8a58e0.text: Hungry. So hungry. You're warm, all of you, so warm. Could you spare... no. No, I'd take too much. Let me give you something instead. Then you can feed me.

vestige_sykane/ced5a0581d6c1e3b.text: One of you has fed something before. Under a house, wasn't it? I can smell it on your hands. You know how it's done.

vestige_sykane/df1cf1f38d52128b.text: Fill me. I can never be filled. Fill me anyway.

vestige_sykane/f016bf3faabf820c.text: Have you eaten? You haven't. I can tell. Go and eat.

vestige_taar_haak/63bb053fb3f84298.text: COWARDS. ALL OF YOU. Two of us are disappointed. Three of us expected it.

vestige_taar_haak/78fe28758da32cce.text: Back. Still soft. One of us said you'd be back. One of us said you'd run. Three of us bet on blood.

vestige_taar_haak/8abd5f9dd7052f1f.text: SMALL. SOFT. WHICH OF YOU HITS HARDEST? That one. No, that one. We'll decide later. Come closer, little fist.

vestige_taar_haak/8d25b48cbf0c9f13.text: Was it a good ending? Tell us about the ending.

vestige_taar_haak/8fb91a9c7fe5ac79.text: Run, then, soft things. Something bigger will catch you. We'd have liked to watch.

vestige_taar_haak/bcd82b307021f094.text: GO. FIND SOMETHING. BREAK IT. We'll watch from the inside.

vestige_taar_haak/bf9397b0fad3dfec.text: FOUND ANYTHING? BROKEN IT? GOOD. MORE.

vestige_taar_haak/c6a45d5178192caa.text: We come too. All five, in your skull. Thinking is slow. Arguing is slower. You'll stop doing both. And once you start, you won't stop. Stopping is for cowards. We hate cowards.

vestige_taar_haak/d5fd32332897bfeb.text: War. Any war. Yours will do. One of us is hungry, one of us is angry, and the other three are worse.

vestige_taar_haak/edbb470afb21916c.text: Arms that break doors. A back that carries the dead home. You'll kill the things that laugh at you now, and you'll enjoy it. That's the best part.

vestige_tarakamedes/10bd56cbe2705ae0.text: You'll owe me, only at the end. When you fall, I'll be waiting just under the floor of the world, and I'll pull. Gently. Without stopping.

vestige_tarakamedes/1704bb85ecfa96df.text: Patience, elf. Everyone comes down to me in the end. I don't need to bargain for you.

vestige_tarakamedes/1e27def0301a95ea.text: No one. It makes no difference. I'll have you all eventually, without the paperwork.

vestige_tarakamedes/2001cc98e9508db1.text: For the priest's boy, in the village? There is no cure. There is only me. Bring him here and I'll make him something that doesn't need blood. You wouldn't like what it needs instead.

vestige_tarakamedes/27256831ac78d734.text: Walk away, then. Every road you take goes downhill to me.

vestige_tarakamedes/2d8f7fbd11dc5c1f.text: Back again, warm thing. Everyone comes back to me. Usually only once.

vestige_tarakamedes/2fea3a92fa8ee005.text: Little warm things. You stand on the graves of my servants and don't even know it. Kneel or don't. The grave is patient either way.

vestige_tarakamedes/39b3fcea71adaa16.text: The dead will hear you. They'll rise when you call and answer when you ask. And the grave's cold won't bite you any more. It knows you'll be along.

vestige_tarakamedes/603ee0b36ca13407.text: I'll see you again. Everyone does.

vestige_tarakamedes/9b01d051180a1e4c.text: Bones, voice, breath. The work of a moment. The price is yours, elf: every year you have left, but one. One year with her. Then you come down to me.

vestige_tarakamedes/a9f9e9858f3e319b.text: Every life ends in my mouth. I would like, once, to be thanked for it.

vestige_tarakamedes/cfb82b1f739f2419.text: Not yet, little one. Not yet. But I'm keeping your place.

vestige_tenebrous/337d35990f9e2121.text: Shh. No one. Then go back to your noise.

vestige_tenebrous/3d33813b0a9b538c.text: Shh. Don't light anything. Light is so loud. Come into the dark with me. It's quiet here. It's always quiet here.

vestige_tenebrous/3ff70e65aba6afb1.text: Shh. Keep the lights low. You and I don't need them.

vestige_tenebrous/768c19c89c1edf92.text: Light will be your enemy. Sunlight, holy fire, the bright things priests throw. They'll cut you like a thief caught in a doorway.

vestige_tenebrous/89a82284fcd856ba.text: Shh. The dark will still be here. It always is.

vestige_tenebrous/8cc4daedcfe4c066.text: The dark will be your house. You'll see in it and walk in it unseen, and call it down over any room like a curtain.

vestige_tenebrous/d5b188705effcdec.text: The last candle out. The last star. And then, at last, rest.

vestige_tenebrous/e9d267ad1fad5a23.text: Shh. You brought a light again.

vestige_yog/68e35f5c7e4d563a.text: Soft. You are... soft. Everything cuts you. That is... sad.

vestige_yog/918fcf565863939d.text: Skin like mine. Blades break. Teeth break. You... stay.

vestige_yog/b75e3b153404e304.text: Then break. I will be here after.

vestige_yog/fc09bad705b9512a.text: Stone does not hurry. Stone does not... feel. You will be slow. You will not feel the sun. Or a hand. Does it matter? Hands are soft.

vestige_yrrga/408527c357e727e9.text: Go on, then. Don't look behind you.

vestige_yrrga/462f5eae020604de.text: You came back. You still can't see it, can you? It's right behind you.

vestige_yrrga/6b43889834581ee3.text: You'll see what's really there. All of it, all the time. Courage is mostly not seeing. You'll lose it.

vestige_yrrga/73013cb337107ce0.text: Your eyes, made true. Illusions, disguises, invisible things, borrowed faces: none of them will fool you up close. Not even his. You'd see the lord on the hill as he is.

vestige_yrrga/997d5c0bc27e052a.text: To look. To be looked through. To show you what's there.

vestige_yrrga/a64c9da5c73aa44b.text: Oh. You can't see it. You can't see any of it. The masks, the borrowed skins, the thing standing just behind the one you love. How do you live like that?

vestige_yrrga/eddb8fe4320e3096.text: No one. Keep your blindfolds, then. They're very comfortable, I'm told.

vestige_yrrga/f9ac53e09f81a990.text: Now you see it too. Don't look away. You can't anyway.

vestige_zantras/05137e4fecd3af59.text: At last. An audience. Do you know how long it has been since anyone looked at me? Come closer. You, at the front. You were made to be looked at, and nobody has noticed. I could fix that.

vestige_zantras/283f46c5ad0ee5c4.text: There. Now they'll see you. Make sure they never stop.

vestige_zantras/3d97d27166057507.text: A king is only a mirror the crowd stands in front of. Mine broke a long time ago. I need a new one, with a pulse.
