vestige_zantras/4bb2c7a00704122a.text: Then give it to one of them. Gifts can be passed along, you know, if you're generous.

vestige_zantras/68cd9c687a7e4d45.text: Hardly worth the mention. You'll need them to keep looking. Every hour. And people who aren't looking at you will stop being interesting. What use were they anyway?

vestige_zantras/749c54e1c7b00e90.text: Then go back to being furniture. I'll be here when you tire of it.

vestige_zantras/7dfa8d248d239477.text: No one? A crowd of nobodies. How fitting. Off you go, then. Nobody will notice.

vestige_zantras/aaa6be5856cdc0cc.text: My audience returns. I knew you couldn't stay away. Nobody ever can.

vestige_zantras/e5a7c866359d318e.text: Furniture. You'll be furniture again by morning.

vestige_zantras/e7cc095ddeacca8a.text: When you walk into a room, it will turn. When you speak, people will lean in. Kings will stammer beside you, and you will never again be the one nobody remembers.

vestige_zantras/f5b6dc95d0d32f92.text: And you, my dear. You already have it, don't you? Everyone looks at you. Strangers, wolves, lords on hills. Do you hate it yet?

vestige_zhudun/05042fe9323a438d.text: My light, under your skin: cold, and untouched by the holy fire your priests throw. And once a day, a door into the black between the stars, opened in your enemies' midst.

vestige_zhudun/1224123075c483c8.text: No one. Then stay in your little dark. I'll go on shining at nobody. I'm used to it.

vestige_zhudun/1c992720fd7f9a47.text: You're shining. Faintly. It suits you.

vestige_zhudun/268a176e0597a9e6.text: No. But you haven't felt your dawn since you came through the mist, have you, little priestess? Not once. I can feel how cold you are. Let me be your light. I'm right here, and he isn't.

vestige_zhudun/2ba5dad49a2c2621.text: Go and look for your dawn, then. Tell me if you find it.

vestige_zhudun/58df8f1066ab3185.text: You came back to the light. Even a cold one.

vestige_zhudun/722849824b9b77e7.text: A dead star is cold all the way through. You'll be frailer, slow to warm, and fire will find you like dry kindling. And you'll glow in the dark, always, just a little. Grey.

vestige_zhudun/af2a4d8d9a13bbba.text: To shine again. On someone. Anyone.

vestige_zhudun/de4a928c4e85b09c.text: I was a sun once. Worlds turned around me. Now I am a cinder in a jar. Come closer. I still have a little light.

victor_vallakovich/0eceb349212e0e5b.text: Get out. Get out of my attic. I hope you're stuck here forever. I hope you are.

victor_vallakovich/1c3280e049461701.text: I know how many. I can count. I'm the only one in this house who can.

victor_vallakovich/27b0d5cad34f9ea4.text: Finally. Somebody who understands. I'm close. A few more nights. When it's done, I'll be gone, and nobody in this house will ever make me wave at anything again.

victor_vallakovich/283b1119c57d70b2.text: No. Go and break someone else's life's work.

victor_vallakovich/3e23a60e29d0ad38.text: That's... no. That's not... let me see.

victor_vallakovich/4143f4184a9aaa78.text: Still here. Still not stepping in it. Happy?

victor_vallakovich/59466ee577de47fa.text: Six weeks! Six weeks of work! Do you know how hard it is to get chalk in Barovia?

victor_vallakovich/601431e03ebb5fd8.text: Fine. Fine! I won't step in it. I wasn't going to anyway. Not today.

victor_vallakovich/623193513c4a8723.text: With you? You told me I'd die in my own circle. I'm still alive. Out of spite, mostly.

victor_vallakovich/66c24fafb0692528.text: He's in the stocks. My father. Every day. People walk past him to get to the well. I hate him and I want to kill all of them.

victor_vallakovich/6c59028406631792.text: Come to scuff something else? There's a nice candle over there. Very breakable. Go on.

victor_vallakovich/7301c7b16b0fd1b7.text: Fine. Bribery. At least it's honest.

victor_vallakovich/7505f788167b79ea.text: Do you know what it's like being his son? Every week a festival. Every week I have to stand on the dais and wave. I'd rather be nowhere.

victor_vallakovich/8360de276b936e7b.text: A door. Out of this house, out of this town, out of this valley. A teleportation circle, from a book that was never meant for this town. It's nearly right.

victor_vallakovich/8c11763ff4be9d0d.text: It didn't take them anywhere. There was a flash. Then there wasn't anyone. Father thinks they went to Krezk. I let him.

victor_vallakovich/9a8a723bd0d340fb.text: Take this. I copied it out of the book. It's the only spell in there that ever did what it said.

victor_vallakovich/9ff74d6d1bcb6ef9.text: Grigor and Mirela. They volunteered. Mostly. I told them it would take them somewhere warm, with sun.

victor_vallakovich/a078648a2aa254fe.text: Then there's nowhere. It isn't broken. There's just nowhere for it to go. There's no way out of here at all.

victor_vallakovich/a5338c74b9d5e6e0.text: That fortune-teller's cards named me, didn't they? Lucian told me. Fine. There's nothing left here for me to hide from.

victor_vallakovich/ab2b5f9a6e83d255.text: Out. Out of this attic, out of this house, out of his festivals. With a party of armed lunatics and a fortune-teller's blessing.

victor_vallakovich/b0644a4effd84833.text: With you? You ruined six weeks of work with your boots.

victor_vallakovich/b9c05ddd5309203c.text: And you've been reading my notes. Those are private. They're private calculations.

victor_vallakovich/d18b20a62bc7f8d5.text: You sound like Mother. Get out of my attic.

victor_vallakovich/e122a6bf5ebf1d97.text: Ten gold of chalk. That's... that is actually a great deal of chalk. The Vistani sell it by the stick.

victor_vallakovich/ea10e0b011c86bde.text: ...Fine. I'll leave it. Until I've worked out what's wrong with it. Which might be a while. Which might be never. Are you happy?

victor_vallakovich/f0b97d5669b0135a.text: He took the book. He took the book and he locked it in his desk with the festival ledgers. I hope you're very proud.

victor_vallakovich/f1b68036b50b3f4e.text: She hanged him. In the night. Mother hasn't spoken since. If the circle still worked I'd take her through it, even into nowhere.

victor_vallakovich/f1ce98ff6abde1d8.text: Yes. Obviously yes. I'll get my book. Don't tell Mother until we're past the gate.

victor_vallakovich/f4c3e0d4fe1998c0.text: Out. Did Mother send you? Tell her I've eaten. Tell her I'm practising scales. Tell her whatever keeps her downstairs.

victor_vallakovich/f7c2c5470bc5fd0f.text: You stepped in it. You actually stepped in it. Grigor at least had the excuse of being told to.

victor_vallakovich/fc880d46376ade47.text: We leave at dawn. Father's packing bunting. Bunting. I may walk into the lake on the way.

vistana/297fd3048013eced.text: Sit, if you like. Don't touch the horses. Don't ask about the fortunes; I'm off duty.

vistana/31c0ad546a2efda5.text: I saw a man on the shore last night, after the moon went down. Bluto, the fisherman from town, the one with no fish. He had a sack over his shoulder, and the sack was moving.

vistana/a7fbb1f182cfaff3.text: The girl's home. Luvash is sober. Two miracles in one week. We'll have to move camp; the luck won't last.

vistana/ff6bbda19bcae9dd.text: I told Arrigal. Arrigal said fishermen carry sacks. Go north to the water. Hurry.

vladimir_horngaard/0452a8ffac2906e8.text: You wish to speak to the Order. Very well. They will not listen. They have listened to nothing but me for four hundred years, and they have been content.

vladimir_horngaard/06738fbc77ba0605.text: The Lord Argynvost founded us to keep the watch over this valley. We kept it. When the army came over the mountains we held the passes, then the road, then this house. We held the house one night.

vladimir_horngaard/0b5a0194ed2c8a31.text: Every knight of this Order died at his post. Every knight but one. Ashgrove saddled the fastest horse in the stable the night before the end and rode away over the pass, and we died, and he did not.

vladimir_horngaard/145c7d7206f500fc.text: Oathbreakers. In my own tower. I should have seen it in your faces; the living always look like that when they mean it.

vladimir_horngaard/1770432b6f2cd0e4.text: Then you will fail, or you will succeed and let him go free. I do not know which I would hate more. Good night.

vladimir_horngaard/1967f31061061e6d.text: One of mine will stand as my second, so that it is a contest and not a lesson.

vladimir_horngaard/1cd199acbe31f01a.text: End him. Everyone who climbs this ridge wants to end him. You will not manage it, and if you could, the Order would not let you.

vladimir_horngaard/1ee38ce6e2169629.text: What he would want. You sound like Godfrey. Go, before I start to find it persuasive.

vladimir_horngaard/24fc6a6f84d59ee1.text: So that is what it looks like from up here. In four hundred years I never once came up to see.

vladimir_horngaard/27c4a09ac4caad9d.text: Godfrey writes a great many things on that wall.

vladimir_horngaard/382afcfe81885124.text: Go, then. The gate is where you left it. It usually is.

vladimir_horngaard/41bb100b548083bb.text: They follow Godfrey now. Take them. Somebody must keep the hall, and it was always going to be me.

vladimir_horngaard/459f65dd3d4ea067.text: The red-haired one. I know the look the castle wears when it thinks of you; I have watched it from this ridge. He wants you forever. We know something about forever.

vladimir_horngaard/45b29ee7edfacfb9.text: Words. I have heard four hundred years of words. Draw.

vladimir_horngaard/49d53f888b2c4e32.text: Then it rides. Godfrey will lead it; he was always the one they liked. I will keep the hall, as the beaten keep things.

vladimir_horngaard/4a583e7f9de7e9b2.text: He fell in the courtyard, in his own shape, with forty of us around him. They took his head to the castle to hang on a wall where guests can admire it. I am told he is much admired.

vladimir_horngaard/4e2685dbfd6caf56.text: The Order marches when you march. Do not keep us waiting. We have done enough of that.

vladimir_horngaard/55f2d40b2f3f9b42.text: You have met him. Then you saw it: he is bored. Imagine an eternity of that, in a valley that hates him, watched by men he cannot kill. That is my gift to him.

vladimir_horngaard/5accd5074488a346.text: I will be up again within a day. I always am. Unless you light that.

vladimir_horngaard/5b39fac311a283fe.text: The Order's law stands. I yielded. I will not pretend I enjoyed it.

vladimir_horngaard/5f1a538d112abe62.text: It is a cage. The only question is who holds the key.

vladimir_horngaard/69168df13b7ae7ca.text: Yes. It came to this house long ago in the hands of a hunter who meant to end him with it. The hands died at our door. I have kept it since, so that nobody would.

vladimir_horngaard/78a6987b0fe56e08.text: Then you are what he is. Oathbreakers.

vladimir_horngaard/7a0c666523d9aa36.text: He said it. "Let them go home. Do not keep them for me." I held his head and heard him, and then I stood up and swore you all to this instead.

vladimir_horngaard/7bb50773f69f84ed.text: If that burns, the Order goes out like a row of candles, and he sits in his castle with nobody left, living or dead, who hates him properly. I will not let you give him that.

vladimir_horngaard/7f4daf162055990b.text: Fine words. The young lord had fine words too, the night a voice at the gate asked for it to be opened. The Order defends its house.

vladimir_horngaard/81111d1401f87efe.text: Yielded. The Order's law is the Order's law, and I wrote most of it. The stronger arm commands. Command, then.

vladimir_horngaard/83fa43b9c3276809.text: Absent. There has not been an absence in four hundred years. I shall need a new column.

vladimir_horngaard/84b5b5f2c4045621.text: He told you. Of course he told you. He never could keep a thing to himself.

vladimir_horngaard/91377a9780109ace.text: Say it after me. He lives. He suffers. We watch.

vladimir_horngaard/9325708715af5ee8.text: Let them go home. He said it with his last breath, and I took them to war instead.

vladimir_horngaard/9588346c008685fb.text: Light it. I will stand with you while it catches. I owe him that much.

vladimir_horngaard/95e58c02d05c2772.text: Then you know how a hall sounds with forty empty chairs. Mine are not empty. I have seen to that.

vladimir_horngaard/9804909ddc012d9c.text: You swore an oath at my table. Break him. Do not end him.

vladimir_horngaard/a4fc2a455ea01ec2.text: I held his head and he said it, and I could not bear to go where he was going and tell him I had lost his house. So I kept them here, so that none of us would have to.

vladimir_horngaard/a8bca075c83f98d7.text: Fine words. The young lord had fine words too, the night a voice at the gate asked for it to be opened. The Order does not ride.

vladimir_horngaard/a916537106fd4e33.text: Words on a stone. Go, then, all of you who want to. Follow Godfrey to the castle and die a second time. I will keep the hall.

vladimir_horngaard/a9e481e0353456f2.text: You bring his sword into this hall and ask me for an accolade. The Order does not take recruits, boy. It takes revenge.

vladimir_horngaard/aa66f5cf1498fe1b.text: Go on, then. I can feel it waiting. So can he.

vladimir_horngaard/aaad1beec00c87f1.text: I am Vladimir Horngaard, commander of the Order of the Silver Dragon. State your names and your business. Godfrey will enter you in the book of guests.

vladimir_horngaard/ad3468bf3c809cc4.text: Because it is his light, and if it burns it will call us after him. The Order would go out like a row of candles.

vladimir_horngaard/adefe8148dcf9f41.text: The Order rides, then. Not to watch him. To finish it.

vladimir_horngaard/af961c4eed9a01b7.text: The Order's law: the stronger arm commands. Your company against me, and I will not complain of the odds. I have had four hundred years of practice, and you have had breakfast.

vladimir_horngaard/c105c824ad33b315.text: You may have it on the Order's terms, or by the Order's law. Not otherwise.

vladimir_horngaard/c28a175cfe555abc.text: Light it, then. Quickly, before I remember why not.

vladimir_horngaard/ca1612dc61b348f9.text: Be the light. I had forgotten it said that. I had forgotten a great deal, it seems, and called it discipline.

vladimir_horngaard/cba26924b37259a8.text: Death is a door for him. I will not hold it open.

vladimir_horngaard/cc038dcb4888c5f6.text: Not for hate, then. For the valley, as he would have had it. One last march, and then home. I will lead it, if the Order will still have me.

vladimir_horngaard/cda81a25237d0ee4.text: Take it. Use it to break him. If you use it to end him, the Order will know, and the Order will come.

vladimir_horngaard/cf6cb97658b57a97.text: Living. In this hall. You will forgive me if I do not rise. I have been rising for four hundred years, and I find it overrated.

vladimir_horngaard/d01e6ac4cf7bab96.text: Where a thief would have to go through me. Purely professional advice.

vladimir_horngaard/d15c2f237dce580e.text: Company. ...Four hundred years in the front row, and he has never once looked up at us.

vladimir_horngaard/d1d0e2f5bffea9a7.text: Then the Order defends its house.

vladimir_horngaard/d584eb5a1f0b9628.text: You again. State your business. The living spend so much breath.

vladimir_horngaard/da633fd405b09283.text: Swear it, and what I keep is yours, and the Order's war chest besides, and no dead thing on the knights' road will trouble you. And we will be there at the end, to see the oath kept.

vladimir_horngaard/dde8c0aac3dbfb7f.text: The Order's war chest, what there is of it, and the chaplain's water. Spend it getting to his door.

vladimir_horngaard/deeb94bf8a66c33e.text: Swear the Order's second oath with us. When you reach him, you will break him and not end him. Take his castle, his servants, his sleep, his bride. Leave him alive in the ruin of it, forever.

vladimir_horngaard/defa1d9e9c562cb6.text: It is warmer than I remembered. He always said it would not be, and it always was.

vladimir_horngaard/dfb97a04a823be7e.text: Death is a door. He would walk through it, out of this valley and away from us. We want him here. In the room. Forever. Death is a mercy, and the Order is not merciful.

vladimir_horngaard/e1f14b9c20faf884.text: I could not go where he went and tell him I had lost his house. So I kept you here, so that none of us would have to.

vladimir_horngaard/e2a7ac2d652b8f7d.text: And he would sit in his castle with nobody left in the world who hates him properly. I will not give him that.

vladimir_horngaard/e4436f960ca4a4c3.text: Audience. ...Yes. That is what we are. Four hundred years in the front row, and he has never once looked up at us.

vladimir_horngaard/e82f2f0b817645bb.text: Every knight of the Order died at his post. Every knight of the Order is still at his post. That is the whole history. Godfrey tells it with more pears.

vladimir_horngaard/ea2d885d644efdee.text: Four hundred years. A long marriage. We have not quarrelled once.

vladimir_horngaard/ebedfa860c1989e3.text: You remember your oath. Good. He lives, he suffers, and we watch. That is all the Order asks of anyone.

vladimir_horngaard/f0f57c7d73377ea9.text: Then you know nothing. Godfrey will show you out.

vladimir_horngaard/f4c99cd0f990bcdb.text: Do it, then. And afterwards I will take my knights home.

vladimir_horngaard/f79b3f19c98d5a10.text: Take it. I kept it so that nobody would end him. It seems I was keeping it for you.

vladimir_horngaard/fc4296ca3f1b2da0.text: Very well. The Order rides. I will lead it, since somebody must keep Godfrey from forgetting which end of the sword to hold.

volenta_popofsky/0c8e7c98cf8553c0.text: Visitors! Ludmilla, look, visitors with pulses. May I keep one?

volenta_popofsky/1878eb1fbcde2ca8.text: He's in the house tonight, you know. He likes to watch new people. He's watching now.

volenta_popofsky/2ecce89ce8ee06fb.text: He never says for how long, though. He never, ever says that.

volenta_popofsky/3890170a4c023b53.text: Oh, you're brave. I love brave. Brave lasts longer.

volenta_popofsky/450b74a62f1c89e7.text: You came back to play. I knew you would. Everybody comes back to play eventually.

volenta_popofsky/471ea7c40ad1a4e5.text: I always win. It's the trying that's fun.

volenta_popofsky/b1ffba277fa9a7eb.text: Patience. I'm very patient. You'd be amazed. Shall we play something else? I count to a hundred and you hide. If I find you before dawn I win.

vosk/07b7ec32c315ae6b.text: Ah, visitors. Vosk, a scholar of the temple. I've been expecting someone for a while, and here you are.

vosk/0b084ab7e40808ad.text: That was in the warden's notes. I told him to burn those. He forgot. Of course he forgot.

vosk/1728a0b9262c0152.text: Oh! Company. Forgive me, I've been reading so long I'd forgotten other people were real. Vosk. Master Vosk, if you're formal. A scholar, like yourselves. Well. Like some of you.

vosk/1847cd10c5b8bacc.text: The oldest are in the vaults. And at the very bottom there's a sarcophagus with nothing in it at all, which is the most interesting of the lot. I'm going down there myself, presently. Do come and find me.

vosk/19892fb6dc58475b.text: Oh, you must listen to them. Everyone should, once. You'll never meet anything so honest. They tell you exactly what they'll give you, and very nearly what it costs.

vosk/26c3353a81bd8458.text: Coin. How quaint. Thank you. I'll put it with the others.

wren_featherfoot/81ee8ab3f2c75574.text: Right. Yes. Good. I'm going to do a handstand now, to cope. Don't watch. Watch a bit.

wren_featherfoot/81f7f03d392e8b0f.text: She's looking at me like a ham again. Rude.

wren_featherfoot/835124060a9cd105.text: I tell everyone I want the book for the scholarship. I want it because Aurel went after it, and I would like to know whether my friend is alive. There. Somebody write that down.

wren_featherfoot/83bbd643a7d81958.text: Shove over. I've read a lot of contracts. Mostly upside down, across a desk, while someone wasn't looking. Here. "A signature of the lord of the land of mists, freely given, in his own hand."

wren_featherfoot/840ca66572103c92.text: She's looking at me like a ham again.

wren_featherfoot/8784df8d61d08cbe.text: Don't. Don't, I'll cry, and then you'll all have to watch a monk cry, and it's not a dignified sight. We cry with our whole bodies. It's all the flexibility.

wren_featherfoot/878f6efbeb25576a.text: Master Sorrel took me off the street because he thought there was something in me worth the trouble. Lately I've been wondering what he'd make of the company I keep. I don't like the answer.

wren_featherfoot/8931982e076851a8.text: Did he say how long before?

wren_featherfoot/89c6948e5e4d83e8.text: No more dream pastries anywhere in the valley. A lot of folk are going to wake up tomorrow and remember they're sad.

wren_featherfoot/8a682597180455f8.text: Rude. I'd have let us in.

wren_featherfoot/8af3b0f55403b681.text: So Berez never killed the girl. His old nanny did. And the whole village drowned for it.

wren_featherfoot/8b35fb6cb5026e2e.text: She's looking at me the way my aunt looks at a ham.

wren_featherfoot/8b3ccdc7c36d8e71.text: "Some sicknesses are cured by tenderness. Others only grow fat on it. Keep this house open to the hurt and shut to him. If I do not come back, don't come looking. Light a candle and go on."

wren_featherfoot/8d43e38110c281e5.text: Yeah. Yeah, you're right. Probably for the best. Bad time. Vampires. Very busy.

wren_featherfoot/8de33b8a8b163289.text: Keys, locks and things unsaid. Has somebody been going through my pack?

wren_featherfoot/8e6bca5dc4f1a68b.text: Wall side, Kip. Hand on the stone, eyes on my heels. Not the drop. My heels are much nicer.

wren_featherfoot/8f0c6595e8b892ae.text: Thank you. That's all we needed to hear.

wren_featherfoot/8fa23bbbbb0defa1.text: Three halflings, then. I'm only trying to help.

wren_featherfoot/905235e0915e192c.text: I said I'd fit. I didn't say I'd go. ...I might go.

wren_featherfoot/914cde5d2caf92ca.text: Lovely castle. Bit drafty. Bit evil.

wren_featherfoot/91d0466cd50bcbdc.text: Just tell her. Plainly. Like an idiot. ...She does like plain. She hates it when people go round the houses.

wren_featherfoot/93e7643113c49f80.text: Godrick, you've polished that same buckle for an hour. Thistle's not even looking. ...She's looking now. Polish faster.

wren_featherfoot/94f42a386c0bdc0d.text: Race her for it. Winner says the thing. ...That's either genius or how I die. I'll take it.

wren_featherfoot/96799e0c937fdc04.text: She pinched my cheek and said I'd keep. Keep for what, madam? Keep for what?

wren_featherfoot/97deee0dcbcdfdc9.text: Can I tell you the real thing? I'm scared I'm a clown with good knees. That I'm tricks all the way down, and if you took the jokes out there'd be nothing left but a halfling doing a handstand.

wren_featherfoot/9936f2272ddffa4d.text: Huh. Part of me. Like a nose. A nose isn't a trick. A nose is a nose. I'll think about that.

wren_featherfoot/9a2482a62436b42a.text: Easy, then. Be kind when it's stupid to be. Be kind when nobody would know. That's the trick.

wren_featherfoot/9a636cb387be2feb.text: It was a draw. ...She won. Don't tell her I said.

wren_featherfoot/9ec23f9fba98e530.text: Until someone asks me a question I don't want to answer. Then I fall over. It's very convenient.

wren_featherfoot/9f4274e6562fb20e.text: Just so everyone knows, I'm the bite-sized one.

wren_featherfoot/9f85f50f023b34c5.text: I let her win. ...I didn't. She won. I'd have let her, though. That's the bit that's new.

wren_featherfoot/a06689f7c867c7a4.text: A cellar. A mountain. Right. I'll take notes. I'm writing this down. Somebody hold my skillet.

wren_featherfoot/a187572abbf73419.text: Spoilsport. Here. It was getting heavy anyway; what have you got in there, a brick?

wren_featherfoot/a2919a1acaafb7f0.text: I'm still learning it myself. We can be terrible at it together.

wren_featherfoot/a754ce4b5479a22a.text: Held a house a month with one sword. If that's lesser, I'd love to meet the greater.

wren_featherfoot/a922432ff2f91b33.text: Keep saying it, Rat. One of us will believe it.

wren_featherfoot/a9981f253c708217.text: Not the builders, love. The landlord.

wren_featherfoot/aa3717c675756663.text: I can't read. Not proper. My name, and "ale", and "danger". Every letter we've had, I've said my eyes were tired and given it to someone else. My eyes are fine. I'm just slow.

wren_featherfoot/aafbac89e111999a.text: Rat. There's a table made of bones under that lamp. Admire it quieter.

wren_featherfoot/ac942809bac12c0c.text: What if you died for a minute? Just a minute. Technically void.

wren_featherfoot/acf23c2be9d237e4.text: Had no body to go with.

wren_featherfoot/ad5fe26cef96b9da.text: Worth a go. They don't strike me as the haggling sort.

wren_featherfoot/aed0452ddc631742.text: Funny how Pidlwick always ends up behind me on the stairs. I've started going down them backwards.

wren_featherfoot/aff20c0394976fe3.text: Evening. Don't look for your boot; it's in the air. Watch this.

wren_featherfoot/b197b3920046a261.text: I used to tell him everything. Every stupid thing. He'd just nod. I thought he didn't have anything to tell.

wren_featherfoot/b1e22aa081bfca82.text: ...That was a thirteenth joke, that you just did. That was mine. Give it back.

wren_featherfoot/b34e26c35f906fef.text: Didn't look ironic, Kip. Looked like you were about to offer him a sample.

wren_featherfoot/b8114e4e72bad700.text: Only music in the whole valley, and we stopped it. Nice work, everyone.

wren_featherfoot/b8971b4db3eeab47.text: A doll of red hair over her hearth, with a thorn through its heart. She kept it. She still handles it.

wren_featherfoot/b8f22ab7981b7937.text: Kasimir. The last line. Read her the last line he wrote. Not the bit about me. The bit before.

wren_featherfoot/bb993e02d8dee948.text: The old woman knew, though. She looked right at me. Nobody looks right at me.

wren_featherfoot/bbd19099f1faaee9.text: Noted. Sorry's a good start. Master Sorrel would say the leaf apologising to the wind changes nothing. Then he'd make tea anyway.

wren_featherfoot/bbefd4a38eab5df7.text: Good thing none of us is the type to stand near edges.

wren_featherfoot/bcc3cb7a9f2735da.text: She could. She did. You can stop counting now, love.

wren_featherfoot/c296c6798f36a1d3.text: And now you want to go up a mountain and argue her back.

wren_featherfoot/c48965af524ff55a.text: It's the vinegar. Whole place reeks of it. That's all this is.

wren_featherfoot/c67f642014134163.text: There. Somebody sang it for you. Sorry it took so long.

wren_featherfoot/c7236eb245dc7d44.text: Don't know. That's the trouble with dead masters. You have to guess, and you always guess the hard one.

wren_featherfoot/c7285f87aeb19787.text: He left. He wasn't losing. He moved his sleeve out of the wine and left. Rude.

wren_featherfoot/ca7e7b7b783bfcca.text: I don't remember walking. I remember the cold, and his fingers on my neck, and thinking: this is it. This is the last lesson. Don't get up when the wrong voice calls.

wren_featherfoot/caa526429d14d7fb.text: A book club with no books. I knew clubs like that back home. They were always worshipping something. Usually gin.

wren_featherfoot/cc161b8394b2d2bf.text: "They tell me to reason with him. That he was a prince once and could be again, if someone were patient. I have been patient. Patience is how he feeds."

wren_featherfoot/cf0b3a16f5e26c40.text: I would. That's why I'm saying it.

wren_featherfoot/cf203c278df1ca58.text: All I'm saying is, I won. Once. Fairly. In front of witnesses. History will record it.

wren_featherfoot/d08d835564c9b8d4.text: Low on the wall. Right. Is that a riddle? I'm bad at riddles.

wren_featherfoot/d0ce7ace15cdd17a.text: Godrick, why did the skeleton stay home from the ball?

wren_featherfoot/d0e4d187c402c569.text: Bet they'd have done you a good price.

wren_featherfoot/d1d747bb538541d8.text: Right. One of us has a lodger. Hands up? Nobody? Lovely.

wren_featherfoot/d23e09383048cde9.text: Since we crossed the mist, I have not felt my god. The prayers still answer. They answer cold. I have told no one, because a healer who doubts is a healer nobody lets near the bed.

wren_featherfoot/d26fef5dd4836683.text: Master Sorrel told him not to. He wrote it down and posted it across the mountains. Let her rest. And we got it there, and it wasn't enough.

wren_featherfoot/d31fdd566ebbc1bd.text: Nobody make a joke. Not even me.

wren_featherfoot/d3273e9c135c8e2a.text: Nobody said a word to him. Was that brave, or were we terrified?

wren_featherfoot/d59bde222e2cfff0.text: I'll allow it. ...Thanks. That was the sincere bit. Don't get used to it.

wren_featherfoot/d94ae7452192855b.text: Only when I'm sad. So, no. Never. Look at me go.

wren_featherfoot/d9aa1cd4092e2bb0.text: Tell him, and something horrible happens to someone horrible. Master Sorrel never covered that one. Shame. I'd have listened.

wren_featherfoot/daf59bc42c710289.text: She was waiting for the right hands, Kip. Keep yours on it, not on a price.

wren_featherfoot/db6091a5bc97a1f5.text: Master Sorrel says every nursemaid thinks the baby's hers. He never said what to do when the baby's a vampire.

wren_featherfoot/dbcb23c4bdd0b27c.text: Real man, real letter. Easy. Walk up, hand it over, done.

wren_featherfoot/dc1c2d2aa6ddcc77.text: Bet you checked the corners anyway.

wren_featherfoot/dc8bf63a15145e6d.text: I'm not joking now. Nobody lies down on that. Nobody.

wren_featherfoot/dd3c0f6d185d54ff.text: Wasn't me. ...They are very nice buttons, mind.

wren_featherfoot/df2192dcf7d936a8.text: I'd like the recipe. I'd like the recipe very much.

wren_featherfoot/dfc6b90bd51bdd15.text: What if you were two halflings in a coat?

wren_featherfoot/e0ace4db3efa716b.text: Have you? What does it look like? No, don't tell me. I'd only make a joke about it.

wren_featherfoot/e2cd671a6702e165.text: I know. That's what's so frightening about you lot. Everywhere else, being funny's the fee for being let in.

wren_featherfoot/e48890fa8c12837c.text: I tried to pick his pocket. Big market day, old elf in grey, looked half asleep. He caught my wrist without turning round. Didn't even stop walking. Just walked me out of the market by the wrist, like a dog on a lead.

wren_featherfoot/e601f5442115c3cb.text: No blood. Just light, and then nothing. What was that, that we killed?

wren_featherfoot/e660fb9c313f7569.text: Those Vistani women were counting us. Heads, blades, purses. I know that look. I used to wear it.

wren_featherfoot/e7216467fb73651b.text: You're scarier than you look, you know that?

wren_featherfoot/e9e371e978b44ec6.text: Look at him. Putting his coat on to go and get shouted at by his student. ...Lucky old man.

wren_featherfoot/ea362206e8d8c54f.text: He was bored, so he sent for the entertainment. I've played worse rooms. Not many.

wren_featherfoot/ed1f15d9d388f13a.text: I know. I've seen you. That's the worst part. I've got nobody to blame for this but all of you.

wren_featherfoot/eee2b07eda965f19.text: I'm going to say this once, plainly, because I don't do plainly and I want you to notice.

wren_featherfoot/f28c02cbcf8e77a6.text: Something about bats. There's definitely something about bats. Give me a day.

wren_featherfoot/f2ce2e98a5f9b946.text: Right. Quick one. I'll keep it short; I know you're all very busy being heroes.

wren_featherfoot/f511809bdece3ac7.text: Morning, Diviner of the Third Circle. How's the circle?

wren_featherfoot/f5310e9f047a1b3d.text: I'm telling everyone. No, I'm not. Yes I am. No, I'm not.

wren_featherfoot/fab70def4b77c969.text: Every night it is, then. I'll need new knees. Worth it.

wren_featherfoot/fbb896b2d23f64fb.text: The fiddler's telling the castle we went east. That's a man sticking his neck out for us.

wren_featherfoot/fdbe52fae4dc3ecb.text: Master Sorrel had a saying. "Watch what your hands do when nobody's grading them." Lately our hands have been doing some things I'd not want graded.

wren_featherfoot/ffada2b4e1408f82.text: Borrowing. This is borrowing. Master Sorrel taught me the difference. Mostly.

wren_featherfoot/ffb5f6063a6d8a77.text: Lovely. We've upset the one bird that holds a grudge.

yevgeni/3951b1f08fc043db.text: Father will be on the rise with his bow. He says he'll shoot the wolf. He's said that before, and he never has.

yevgeni/3bc8900105b7e808.text: Don't go to the lake at dusk. Or go, but go early, and not where he tells you to stand.

yevgeni/5913665f5cce6cac.text: He chose his side, up on that rise. I chose mine, too late to help him. This was his horn. He blew it once, in the hills, and men came out of the air to fight beside him. I'd rather you had it than the castle.

yevgeni/76de579d7223281d.text: Father ran when the wolf went down. Toward the camp, toward Arrigal's fire. He left his horn on the rise. I think he meant to. He blew it once, in the hills, and men came out of the air to fight beside him. Take it.

yevgeni/7b29e704cf71ee74.text: Go early. Choose your ground. And if you see my father on the rise with his bow, please don't kill him unless you have to.

yevgeni/8077811cf3408ef8.text: And this was Father's horn. He blew it once, in the hills, and men came out of the air to fight beside him. He said it was for the end of the world. He says you've seen more of that than he has. He wants you to have it. He'd never say so.

yevgeni/a8c2cbdad32f3ca4.text: You did it. The Baron's clerk paid out on the ears without even looking at me. Here: the whole three hundred. Father says half; I say all of it. Father isn't here.

yevgeni/aea757381f6c705d.text: Father does the talking. I mend the string.

yevgeni/cb88a207518441ba.text: I go out with Father again now. We take wolves, ordinary ones, a copper an ear. It's honest. It's very boring. I like it.

yevgeni/d9a4a143c706c5e7.text: A man from the Vistani camp pays him. Arrigal. A purse for every strong stranger who goes down to the landing at dusk. The wolf isn't ours to hunt; it's the castle's. The castle wants to know how you fight.

zinaida/52c1f4d2e2184d88.text: A grave. Mine. With my name on.

zinaida/c41d83332098a595.text: That's mine. That's mine. Put it back. Don't give me to him. Don't give me to HIM.

zinaida/caa66d0d6110621b.text: Liars. You came from the carriage. Everybody comes from the carriage.

zuleika_toranescu/0213b26030ccd87f.text: Those were Kiril's favourites, most of them. You've saved me a job. I'm Zuleika. My husband Emil hangs in chains in the west alcove because he told Kiril no.

zuleika_toranescu/028f5d6fe75c9ba7.text: Free my husband. Let him howl his challenge, and when Kiril comes home to answer it, stand beside Emil. Do that, and the children go home.

zuleika_toranescu/02cbdb795d8e6d2f.text: And you've brought the Vistani butcher. She has killed two of ours this month. Tell her to keep her silver in its sheath, or this ends here.

zuleika_toranescu/03e2bd5fb9b0db4b.text: Here. My own brewing: the same thing that keeps the pack sleepy when I want them sleepy. Don't ask what's in it. Drink it when you're bleeding.

zuleika_toranescu/08b08c290206fe2a.text: Then come. Walk behind me, keep your hands away from your weapons, and don't look anyone in the eye for long. The ones inside are mine, or near enough. They'll let you pass if I say so.

zuleika_toranescu/0a9ca395729679a5.text: Go carefully. These hills are full of people who used to be people.

zuleika_toranescu/13595bf8de375372.text: Five, from the farms under Krezk. The ones who live through their first moon will be wolves. The others will be supper. That's Kiril's arithmetic, not mine.

zuleika_toranescu/159b8e3dfc40afdf.text: Then you'll have six wolves between you and the sky. Don't.

zuleika_toranescu/172eda6638fdd6ad.text: Are tired, and frightened, and they listen to me. Mostly.

zuleika_toranescu/354bbb31a8404ea8.text: I am one of them. That's why. I know exactly what Kiril will turn those children into, because he turned the pack into it first.

zuleika_toranescu/423c2a213a4d3bb3.text: I mean bring yourself back in one piece. Or most of the pieces.

zuleika_toranescu/4db9e735639afeb2.text: Someone left a thing at her feet last winter, wrapped in oilcloth. Not one of us. We don't touch what's given to Mother. You aren't one of us.

zuleika_toranescu/516d2e336c34397e.text: Kiril finds it funny. Kiril finds most things funny, until they bite him.

zuleika_toranescu/6523869a1776e089.text: Back again. Have you decided, or did you climb all this way to admire the view?

zuleika_toranescu/66cb2eda5bd919e2.text: He's out. I heard him howl; the whole hill heard him. Go to the great cave and stand where Kiril can see you. Don't make him come looking.

zuleika_toranescu/67711ce9ce2933d4.text: Then go back down the hill and don't come up again. The ones inside won't be as polite as me, and Kiril won't be polite at all.

zuleika_toranescu/760a3cd272337e62.text: I'll take them down the stream path to the Krezk road at first light. And the eldest has a bite on her arm she thinks nobody saw. I saw.

zuleika_toranescu/7aa73728d9180e32.text: You've still got him, then. Feed him properly. He sulks when he's hungry, and he bites when he sulks.

zuleika_toranescu/7d765af050724fd2.text: Wolfsbane and the right words, three nights running. By the moon it'll be a scar and a story. Nothing worse.

zuleika_toranescu/7fe5e772b95d47a7.text: Then your books were written by day.

zuleika_toranescu/88f4131e2df9a2ab.text: Wait. Take this. Emil gave it to me the winter we met: a ring no chain can hold. I've worn it every day he wore silver. I won't need it now.

zuleika_toranescu/896c10b9ef310d76.text: The children got home. All five. The eldest scolded the Krezk gate guard for keeping them waiting.

zuleika_toranescu/8d239ef147d1ab31.text: Then go. I held this den with you in silver. I can hold it with you out for a walk.

zuleika_toranescu/94eba7297b7f2b6b.text: Emil is in the alcove off the great cave, to the west. Here: the key to his chains. Kiril trusted me with it so I could watch him suffer. He has never once understood me.

zuleika_toranescu/aa65f52aaf0d980d.text: The pack's mending fences. Literally; I have them mending the pen into a woodshed. Wolves hate mending things. It's very good for them.

zuleika_toranescu/ba07d68e52d39d57.text: Somebody drew you a map. I'd like to know who, one day, so I can thank them properly.

zuleika_toranescu/bf56d01a80a5c325.text: Emil said no, in front of everyone. Kiril's favourites held him down. Kiril and those favourites are out on the Krezk road now, hunting. They'll be back.

zuleika_toranescu/bf694533b85963e8.text: You smell of Dragan, too. Dragan liked to wait at the falls for travellers. He was one of Kiril's. I won't pretend to miss him.

zuleika_toranescu/ca733d278f64254f.text: Kiril Stoyanovich runs the pack now, and Kiril runs it for the castle. The castle wants more wolves. So Kiril has started bringing home children.

zuleika_toranescu/cccc18a470b0ef44.text: I feed them when he isn't looking. It won't be enough. The moon comes in eleven days.

zuleika_toranescu/d05a29cc95fcd98f.text: Mother Night. The Barovians call her the Morninglord's dark sister and lock their doors on her nights. We just call her Mother. She keeps the dark kind to things that live in it.

zuleika_toranescu/d893c150ee315821.text: That's far enough. You've walked a long way uphill to be eaten. Most people only manage it once.

zuleika_toranescu/e11571319e0cd056.text: Free him. Let him howl. Stand beside him when Kiril comes home. Then the children go home too.

zuleika_toranescu/f786d1e45ef93a00.text: Still here? Emil is in the west alcove. He isn't going anywhere, which is rather the problem.

zuleika_toranescu/f9de5e5bb9b09c39.text: I do. Kiril gave it to me so I could watch him suffer. Here. Wrap the bow in something; the silver runs right up the chain.

zuleika_toranescu/febd1838d3b62f7e.text: Zuleika. Wife to Emil Toranescu, who led this pack for nineteen winters, and who is hanging in the back of that cave in silver chains because he said no to the wrong wolf.
